title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling and Molecular Evaluation of Centella asiatica Extract for Neuroprotection Against Experimental Cognitive Dysfunction
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
011f72f6c4b5850fec4e4c39ff3bf5c5724e5c50.abstract: <jats:p>The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. The plant material was subjected to pharmacognostic evaluation, physicochemical analysis, preliminary phytochemical screening, and chromatographic profiling. An ethanolic extract of C. asiatica was subsequently investigated in a scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction model in rats. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, while biochemical and molecular parameters associated with neuroprotection were evaluated. The extract showed characteristic pharmacognostic features, acceptable physicochemical parameters, and the presence of triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolics, saponins, and other secondary metabolites. Illustrative results showed that treatment with C. asiatica extract improved spatial learning and spontaneous alternation behaviour, reduced brain acetylcholinesterase activity and oxidative stress, and enhanced antioxidant defence. Molecular evaluation indicated improvement in BDNF expression together with attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings suggest that standardized C. asiatica extract may exert neuroprotective effects through complementary cholinergic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic mechanisms.</jats:p>

title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics
container-title: Cognitive Neurodynamics
06090e0d49c5226d4872ceacfa8c8d6d2e0b71d2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber–Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron’s centrality—quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure—we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting. Remarkably, centrality determines the nature of the synchronized attractor: motifs in which the tonic neuron has low centrality synchronize into tonic spiking, whereas highly central tonic neurons drive the network toward synchronized bursting. Moreover, the networks exhibit nontrivial collective behaviors, including large-ISI “stairway-to-heaven” structures, partial firing death characterized by the coexistence of spiking and subthreshold neurons, and remote synchronization in the star configuration with the tonic neuron at the hub. While the present study focuses on the Huber–Braun model in four-neuron motifs, excitability and electrical coupling are features shared by many conductance-based neuronal models. This motivates the hypothesis that analogous structure–dynamics relationships may also arise in other neuronal models and small network motifs, highlighting the potential role of local structural control in shaping collective neural rhythms.</jats:p>

title: From Diagnosis by Accumulation to Diagnosis by Layers: Cognitive Psychiatry and Iatrogenic Risk in an Adolescent with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report and Narrative Review
container-title: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
64b593cb9865a450df79cb5a14e983d428eb6e0d.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may show overlapping behavioural descriptions arising from neurodevelopmental features, psychiatric syndromes, environmental stressors and medication effects.
Objective: To illustrate a layered psychiatric formulation using the clinical course of an adolescent with ASD, self-harm, restrictive eating, atypical experiences and prolonged psychopharmacological exposure.
Methods: Clinical material supplied by the treating team was synthesised as a case report, with a complementary structured narrative review of literature on diagnostic overlap, pharmacotherapy, puberty, safety and feeding. The main PubMed/MEDLINE search covered January 2023 to September 2026, with a subsequent targeted update; evidence selection was purposive rather than systematic.
Case Presentation: A 16-year-old adolescent experienced school and adaptive difficulties, sensory sensitivities, food restriction with occasional self-induced vomiting, self-injury and suicidal ideation. Clinical records described sequential exposure to several psychotropic agents. A reduction in lithium dose from 450 to 300 mg/day during the September 2026 admission was followed by improvement in reported hygiene, food variety and family interaction, but later by distress and an urge to self-harm. Co-occurring psychotherapy, environmental changes and uncertain clinical measurements prevent causal attribution.
Discussion: The proposed eight-layer framework considers constitutional traits, temperament, neurodevelopment and cognition, psychodynamics, relationships and environment, superimposed syndromes, somatic factors and treatment effects. The concept is heuristic, not a validated diagnostic instrument. Feeding symptoms warrant assessment of sensory selectivity, body-image concerns, compensatory behaviours and nutritional consequences. Evidence associating adverse childhood experiences with neuroimaging measures in autistic samples is relevant context but does not substitute for individual assessment.
Conclusion: Longitudinal, risk-sensitive formulation may help identify competing explanations and measurable intervention targets. The clinical sequence does not establish that medication, family circumstances or any single intervention caused the observed outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Associations between cognitive reserve, glymphatic function and cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
c9c11c975e0f61b55daf14543da03e25f7117ac9.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the association between cognitive reserve (CR) and glymphatic function in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to examine whether the relationship between CR and cognition is mediated by glymphatic function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>113 MCI individuals and 91 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled to assess the glymphatic function by using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), perivascular space (PVS) ratings, and choroid plexus volume (CPV). Cognitive reserve index questionnaire (CRIq) was employed to evaluate the comprehensive CR of participants in both groups. The glymphatic function was compared between the two groups and Spearman correlation analyses were performed among the CR, glymphatic function and cognition. Mediation analyses were further conducted to explore potential mediating effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The MCI group had significantly lower bilateral ALPS index and mean ALPS index than the HC group, while the bilateral CPV, basal ganglia (BG)-PVS and centrum semiovale (CS)-PVS scores were significantly higher in the MCI group than the HC group. After controlling for age and sex, bilateral and mean ALPS index were positively correlated with MoCA, MMSE, and VFT scores; mean ALPS index and left ALPS index were positively correlated with AVLT-immediately performance. BG-PVS was negatively correlated with MMSE and VFT scores, and right CPV was negatively correlated with VFT scores. Meanwhile, CRIq was positively correlated with bilateral and mean ALPS index, but was negatively correlated with BG-PVS, and mean ALPS partially mediated the association between CRIq and cognition in the MCI group.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Mild cognitive impairment individuals exhibit reduced glymphatic activity relative to HC. Comprehensive CR is associated with cognitive function in MCI, with the mean ALPS index statistically mediating a portion of the CR–cognition association.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:p>Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI.</jats:p>

title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
2b5bbc241b06a03ff17faa558df753c72b75e4ac.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      CD62L
                      <jats:sup>low</jats:sup>
                      neutrophils and a reduced frequency of CXCR4
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      TREM-1
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      CCR2
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). This was accompanied by elevated soluble TNF receptor 1 (sTNFR1) and decreased sTNFR2 and CXCL12. In the TP2 cohort, PMN-MDSC levels were comparable between REC and PASC groups, alongside increased emergency granulopoiesis regulators IL-3 and IL-6. Multivariate regression revealed significant associations between PMN-MDSC signatures, granulopoiesis-related markers, NC scores, and cognitive test scores in either the TP1 or the TP2 cohort. These results represent cross-sectional observations in participants assessed within the respective post-infection intervals, rather than longitudinal evidence of persistence. The results show that dysregulated granulopoiesis and neutrophil maturation are present even at 18 and 36 months in PASC individuals, potentially associating with overall symptom severity and cognitive impairment.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Development and Validation of A Cost-effective Passive Avoidance Apparatus for Assessing Memory Impairments in Mice
container-title: Indian Journal of Animal Research
64797322e7d050c812518a49ac307812dddfa35a.abstract: <jats:p>Background: The passive avoidance (PA) test is commonly used to evaluate memory performance in rodents; however, the high cost of commercial apparatus limits its accessibility for neuroscience research. Methods: This study aimed to develop a cost-effective PA apparatus integrated with custom software for automated step-through latency measurement. To validate the system, a scopolamine-induced amnesia model was established using repeated regimens (1 mg/kg, i.p.) daily for six consecutive days. Result: A total apparatus development cost is approximately 450 USD, with the integrated software enabling heatmap visualizations of animal movement. During the retention trial, scopolamine-treated mice exhibited significantly shorter step-through latencies than saline-treated controls, indicating impaired memory retrieval. The automated measurements were consistent with manual timing, suggesting the accuracy and reliability of the apparatus. Histopathological analysis revealed marked cell loss in the hippocampus of scopolamine-treated mice, accompanied by reduced brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression. These findings confirmed successful induction of neurodegeneration and supported the memory deficits detected by the apparatus. Overall, the developed PA system offers a reliable and affordable platform for memory assessment in laboratory mice, particularly in resource-limited settings.</jats:p>

title: Comparison of ChatGPT-Generated Patient Information on Testicular Cancer Across Two Assessment Periods: Clinical Accuracy, Response Quality, and Citation Support
container-title: Urology Research and Practice
c93eb8feb9c99f0cdaf287bfd045672a3550f06c.abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: The aim of this study was to compare clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation characteristics of ChatGPT-generated testicular cancer information across 2 assessments 20 months apart.
Methods: Sixty-one patient-oriented questions derived from European Association of Urology (EAU) Patient Information were submitted to ChatGPT-4o in December 2024 and repeated unchanged using ChatGPT-5.6 Luna in August 2026. Two urologists independently assessed accuracy against contemporaneous EAU guidelines and rated quality using the Global Quality Score (GQS) and modified DISCERN (mDISCERN). Citation quantity, source quality, and source-to-claim support were evaluated. Only the first response was retained; repeated-generation variability was not assessed.
Results: Fully accurate responses were 86.9% (53/61) in 2024 and 93.4% (57/61) in 2026 (P = .125). Of 8 clinically relevant inaccuracies in 2024, 4 were corrected, 3 improved but remained misleading, and 1 persisted. GQS increased from 3.75 ± 0.77 to 4.82 ± 0.41 and mDISCERN from 30.37 ± 4.65 to 36.80 ± 1.93 (both P < .001). Citations per response decreased from 5.97 ± 3.53 to 4.79 ± 1.19 (P = .042), while high-quality unique sources increased from 77.4% to 96.9% (P < .001). Fully supported sources were 80.1% and 86.4% (P = .050); 6 sources (2.6%) in 2026 did not support the claims.
Conclusion: Response quality and the use of high-quality sources were greater in 2026, whereas changes in clinical accuracy and source-to-claim support were less clear. Clinically meaningful errors persisted in guideline-sensitive topics. Because different model versions and interfaces were assessed, the findings represent model- and interface-specific snapshots, not a controlled head-to-head comparison.
Cite this article as: Ekenci BY, Altan M. Comparison of ChatGPT-generated patient information on testicular cancer across two assessment periods: Clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation support. Urol Res Pract. 2026;52, doi: 10.5152/ tud.2026.26067</jats:p>

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
8ceeae83917828c5b1e08cdb8fa3ca811cbe8ee6.abstract: Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: Practical Bedside Tests for Assessing Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction (POCD) in Anesthetized Patients
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
e86136c3ac2f46b0b3b08a72d66be50e2049d437.abstract:
<jats:p>Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD)—characterized by deficits in memory, executive function, and processing speed—is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized complication of surgery and anesthesia. POCD is associated with protracted recovery, diminished quality of life, and adverse long-term outcomes, particularly among elderly and high-risk populations. While early detection via bedside cognitive tests is vital for optimizing postoperative care, more comprehensive gold-standard neuropsychological batteries remain largely unfeasible in routine clinical practice due to significant time, cost, and resource constraints.
This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of practical bedside cognitive assessments for identifying POCD. Commonly employed tools—including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test (TMT), Digit Span, Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS)—are critically appraised regarding their sensitivity, limitations, and suitability for the perioperative environment. The review specifically addresses feasibility in acute postoperative settings, accounting for confounding factors such as age, literacy, and sensory or motor impairments. Furthermore, the necessity of establishing baseline cognitive status and the urgent need for tool validation within surgical cohorts are highlighted.
No single bedside instrument offers a sufficiently comprehensive assessment for POCD. Rather, a multimodal approach—integrating high-sensitivity tools like the MoCA or TMT with rapid screening instruments—represents a more robust and clinically viable strategy for early detection. Future research must focus on standardizing assessment protocols and validating these tools across diverse surgical populations to ultimately enhance the quality of postoperative cognitive care.</jats:p>

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
b447a82291c817794bca34b6c506bac2ac66c2cb.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From Pre-Bolshevik Baku to the Post-Soviet Camp:  Emigree Post-memory in the Works of Banine and Gunel Movlud
ბოლშევიკებამდელი ბაქოდან პოსტსაბჭოთა ბანაკამდე: ემიგრანტული მეხსიერება ბანინესა და გიუნელ მოვლუდის შემოქმედებაში
container-title: სჯანი
890d876d7ae2c07c98267b9bc701a0001c20a99e.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper explores Azerbaijani émigré and refugee literature through the prism of memory, violence, and trauma. It focuses on two women writers separated by nearly a century: Ümül Banine (Baninee), who left Baku after 1920 following the collapse of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and settled in Paris, and Günel Mövlud, who fled her native Jabrayil in the 1990s as part of the displaced generation of the Karabakh war. These two figures frame two historical moments that mark, respectively, the beginning and the end of the Soviet era. Their literary works are examined through the lenses of collective and individual memory, trauma and post-trauma, pre- and post-bolshevik historical rupture, and the neurobiology of violence.
Alongside them, the paper briefly considers a third voice – Dilbar Axund­zadə – whose memoir of life with the repressed poet Mikayıl Müşfiq reflects a different con­dition: not exile, but internal survival under Soviet repression. Although connec­ted to the same cultural space, these women represent distinct historical periods and modes of displacement, revealing how personal destinies are shaped, remembered, and narrated under radically different political regimes. While Banine’s narrative preserves an episode of internal displacement experienced by her mother in 1905, during the early phase of the Armenian–Azerbaijani conflict in Baku and other Azer­baijani territories, Mövlud’s narrative presents a different configuration of violence and memory: not cosmopolitan exile but internal displacement in the post-Soviet period.
Research methods:
Both individual and collective memory are selective and interpretive; they are never static but always reconstructive. Émigré and refugee literature foregrounds this process with particular clarity. Banine’s Days in the Caucasus transforms childhood upheaval into an ironic and reflective narrative, while Mövlud’s The Camp fragments refugee experience into intense sensory episodes – mirroring neurobiological re­search on trauma, which shows that violence imprints memory in sharpened yet dis­continuous traces. Stress hormones heighten certain recollections while disrupting nar­rative coherence, and adolescence, as a period of neural plasticity, renders such memories especially enduring.
Banine’s memoir reveals generational tensions within a multicultural household: her grandmother’s conservatism, her father’s cosmopolitan aspirations, and the coexistence of German, Russian, and English alongside Azerbaijani tradi­tions. Christmas trees stand next to Novruz celebrations, and a German governess introduces Christian rituals into a Muslim family home. At the same time, the text ex­poses darker layers of postmemory: the Armenian–Azerbaijani clashes of 1905 and 1918-1920 resurface in children’s “games” played with their half-Armenian friend Tamara. What adults leave unspoken, children reenact symbolically. As Marianne Hirsch defines it, postmemory transmits trauma to those who did not directly experience it but nonetheless inherit its emotional weight.
While Banine’s narrative preserves an episode of internal displacement ex­perienced by her mother in 1905, during the early phase of the Armenian–Azerbai­jani conflict in Baku and other Azerbaijani territories, Mövlud’s narrative presents a different configuration of violence and memory: not cosmopolitan exile but internal displacement in the post-Soviet period. Her camp narrative depicts weddings reduced to survival strategies, improvised libraries in cramped “kletka” rooms, and mosques built by foreign sponsors. Here, the rupture is not between generations but between two historical conditions – the stability of the Soviet past and the fragmentation of post-war displacement. Trauma becomes embodied: Mövlud describes a paralyzed girl repeatedly abused while others avert their gaze. This scene resonates with trau­ma theory’s “freeze response,” in which neither fight nor flight is possible and the bo­dy and psyche enter a state of paralysis.</jats:p>

title: ETALON: Verified Execution and Persistent Research Memory for Agentic Computer-Aided Drug Design
a1ef09a90238f52ae133f226f04cc5136b61674d.abstract: <jats:p>Language-model agents can coordinate computational drug discovery, but adapting a campaign to new evidence requires scientific software that supports flexible workflows, consistent modeling, and continuity across research sessions. Here we present ETALON, a harness that equips a general-purpose coding agent with an integrated environment for computer-aided drug design. Three independently usable systems supply its scientific operations: MolQuarry for chemical and biological evidence, MolCascade for molecular preparation, screening, and docking, and PRISM for molecular generation and physical modeling. Each exposes configurable procedures with explicit scientific requirements, so the host can revise its research strategy while retaining consistent preparation and evaluation practices. Operations registered with a common execution layer are checked before dispatch, and their outputs carry separate records of completion, verification, and admission, so that an incomplete computation is not recorded as an unfavorable molecular result. A persistent research graph links evidence, judgments, experiments, and results across sessions, and candidate method revisions are compared with frozen baselines under criteria declared in advance.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Computing at the Edge: Lag Analysis and Neural Network Forecasting for Fishery Landings in the Colombian Caribbean
16b4b0ed8f381dcf53065fa4831dbe408bb25394.abstract: <jats:p>Fishery-dependent indices in data-limited fisheries are short and incomplete, which raises the question of when adaptive learned models, including cognitively inspired ones deployed at the edge, are justified. We analysed monthly landings per unit effort (LPUE) of pink shrimp (Penaeus notialis) in the Gulf of Morrosquillo, Colombian Caribbean: 65.7% of values are missing and the longest continuous segment has 28 months. Naive, trend, autoregressive (AR), echo state network (ESN), LightGBM and LSTM models were compared in rolling-origin experiments with training-only preprocessing, and their cost was measured on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. One-step-ahead errors were 5.1–5.7 kg per trip for the trend, the AR(2) and the learned models, against 7.6 for persistence; no learned model showed a robust out-of-sample improvement over a linear trend or an AR(2). An exploratory model incorporating river flow at a data-selected lag achieved the lowest RMSE (4.2 kg per trip), but its improvement over the statistical baselines was not statistically conclusive and was not consistently reproduced when lag selection was restricted to the training data at each origin. Backcasting was worse than persistence. A fit took 8 ms (AR) to 3–9 s (LSTM); the double-precision ESN execution process showed the largest peak memory footprint (1.7–4.1 GB of 8 GB). The limit is the information in the series, not the platform; under these conditions a linear trend or an AR(2) is a sufficient reference.</jats:p>

title: Capacity Limits in Cognitive Processing Reflect the Curse of Generalization
65a5e431acc5d0a8d2c5143f2e9ef4740d73e2de.abstract: The striking constraints of some human cognitive processes stand in stark contrastto the near limitless capability of others. While we can acquire and flexibly use vast amountsof information, the amount we can process at any one time is often stiflingly limited: forexample the number of items we can hold in working memory or the number of tasks that canbe performed at once. Here, we integrate ideas from information theory, cognitive science,and neuroscience to offer a unified account of why processing is often so limited. We arguethat this reflects a fundamental tradeoff between generalization—how effectively existingrepresentations can be used in novel settings—and how many distinct representations canbe processed in parallel. Representations that best promote strong forms of generalization— a characteristically human cognitive strength — come at the expense of surprisinglystrict limits in the number of items that can be processed at once, an equally characteristichuman weakness. We refer to this as the “curse of generalization.” We formulate this first ininformation-theoretic terms, and then in process models, including a neural network modelof classic tasks used to demonstrate strict limits in human processing capacity. This tensionoffers a potential explanation for a range of phenomena — from performance on the tasks onwhich we focus, to representational learning and skill acquisition more broadly — as wellas the performance of modern machine learning architectures that exhibit generalizationcapabilities comparable to humans.

title: Large-Eddy Simulations Modeling of High-Lift High-Work Low-Pressure Turbine Blades: Validation and Application
container-title: Journal of Turbomachinery
c2a5abd9a2ff1806b534f5d813fc3ec103397ac0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Over the years, computational fluids dynamics (CFD) has matured to such a state so as to be indispensable in turbine design. In the past two decades alone, significant advances in turbine design have been made through the use of CFD—in particular, through the use of Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) simulations. Currently, turbine design is RANS-driven; however, significant gains in performance and efficiency are becoming more difficult to achieve using RANS. For this reason, the turbomachinery CFD community is moving toward Large-Eddy Simulations (LES). In the design of low-pressure turbine (LPT) blades, LES is particularly beneficial owing to its ability to capture accurately both transition and separation. In this paper, LES is used to characterize a new family of high-lift high-work LPT blades—designated the LXFHW-LS family—designed at the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL). LES simulations are conducted in accordance with the methodology outlined in Part I of this paper. The purpose of this paper is twofold: (1) to use LES to predict the performance of the LXFHW-LS family and compare it to measurements in a low-speed linear cascade and, in doing so, (2) to illustrate how LES may be used in LPT design as it evolves from RANS-driven to LES-driven. For each blade in the family, the loading distribution and loss coefficient are computed for 16 separate Reynolds numbers. Computational results are validated using detailed experimental measurements from a low-speed linear cascade wind tunnel. Experimental measurements include blade loading distributions, total pressure loss, and particle image velocimetry (PIV) measurements. In comparing computational and experimental results, particular emphasis is placed on the evolution of the suction surface (SS) separation bubble (if one exists). A variety of techniques are used to visualize the extent of the separation bubble, including machine learning.</jats:p>

title: Experiment-based calibration in psychology: foundational and data-generating model
896e44a978cf20bc63251037fbc18b086cf21d92.abstract: Experiment-based calibration is a novel method for measurement validation, which – unlike classical validity metrics – does not require stable between-person variance. In this approach, the latent variable to be measuredis manipulated by an experiment, and its predicted scores – termed standard scores – are compared against the measured scores. Previous work has shown that under plausible boundary conditions, the correlationbetween standard and measured scores – termed retrodictive validity – is informative about measurement accuracy, i.e. combined trueness and precision. Here, I expand these findings in several directions. First, Iformalise the approach in a probability-theoretic framework with the concept of a standardised calibration space. Second, I relate this framework to classical validity theory and show that the boundary conditionsin fact apply to any form of criterion validity, including classical convergent validity. Thus, I state precise and empirically quantifiable boundary conditions under which criterion validity metrics are informative onvalidity. Third, I relate these boundary conditions to confounding variables, i.e. correlated latent variables. I show that in the limit, calibration will converge on the latent variable that is most closely related to thestandard. Finally, I provide a framework for modelling the data-generating process with Markov kernels, and identify sufficient conditions under which the data generation model results in a calibration space. In sum,this article provides a formal probability-theoretic framework for experiment-based calibration and facilitates modelling and empirical assessment of the data generating processes.

title: Large inversions in Lake Malawi cichlids are associated with habitat, lineage, and sex determination
container-title: eLife
b641d8a47331fdefe6b0f48a514a41a05aa8f4a4.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic
                    <jats:italic>Diplotaxodon</jats:italic>
                    group into
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    ancestors at the time the
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.
                  </jats:p>

title: Large Language Models for Cyber Security: A Systematic Literature Review
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
b0bc58efd35742a0df2f019162f0c83912291f16.abstract:
<jats:p>The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened up new opportunities for leveraging AI in a variety of application domains, including cybersecurity. As the volume and sophistication of cyber threats continue to grow, there is an increasing need for intelligent systems that can automatically detect vulnerabilities, analyze malware, and respond to attacks. In this survey, we conduct a comprehensive review of the literature on the application of LLMs in cybersecurity (LLM4Security). By comprehensively collecting over 40K relevant papers and systematically analyzing 185 papers from top security and software engineering venues, we aim to provide a holistic view of how LLMs are being used to solve diverse problems across the cybersecurity domain.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Through our analysis, we identify several key findings. First, we observe that LLMs are being applied to an expanding range of cybersecurity tasks, including vulnerability detection, malware analysis, and network intrusion detection. Second, we analyze application trends of different LLM architectures (such as encoder-only, encoder–decoder, and decoder-only) across security domains. Third, we identify increasingly sophisticated techniques for adapting LLMs to cybersecurity, such as advanced fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and external augmentation strategies. A significant emerging trend is the use of LLM-based autonomous agents, which represent a paradigm shift from single-task execution to orchestrating complex, multi-step security workflows. Furthermore, we find that the datasets used for training and evaluating LLMs are often limited, highlighting the need for more comprehensive datasets and the use of LLMs for data augmentation. Finally, we discuss the main challenges and opportunities for future research, including the need for more interpretable models, addressing the inherent security risks of LLMs, and their potential for proactive defense.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Overall, our survey provides a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in LLM4Security and identifies several promising directions for future research. We believe that the insights and findings presented in this survey will contribute to the growing body of knowledge on the application of LLMs in cybersecurity and provide valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners working in this field.</jats:p>

title: CryoDECO: disentangling compositional and conformational heterogeneity in cryo-EM with foundation-model priors
1cbc6edf26ff53ee4978d8584f04c0294216609c.abstract: <jats:p>Cryo-electron microscopy has transformed macromolecular structure determination, but heterogeneous biological samples contain multiple complexes and conformational states that remain difficult to resolve. This difficulty reflects a circular dependency among particle separation, pose estimation and structure reconstruction. We developed CryoDECO, a prior-guided framework that enters this coupled inference problem from structural representations learned from large-scale cryo-EM data rather than from random initialization, and that reduces manual tuning. CryoDECO separates simulated mixtures of up to 100 structures, resolves experimental and native-derived mixtures into populations suitable for high-resolution refinement, and captures continuous motion together with local density differences within a shared trajectory.</jats:p>

title: Judges of Empire
The first uniform rail passenger fare model in Europe: Hungary's late 19th-century reform and its foreign judgement
container-title: Hungarian Studies
9f113d3a0ce5f82ca3c2c5368e0e16d06a94f6e4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The advent of the railways had a profound impact on the fates and economies of nations, transforming nearly every aspect of society and culture throughout the 19th century. Despite a somewhat late start, Hungary developed a large and sophisticated rail system. This system was revolutionized in 1889 with the introduction of the zone tariff system by Gábor Baross, which greatly simplified ticket pricing and made rail travel affordable for the average Hungarian. Though few believed it would be sustainable, the Baross system had a substantial international impact. Experts from across Europe traveled to Hungary to study the reform. This paper examines the impact of the unified zone tariff system—the first of its kind in Europe—and explores its reception abroad and the extent to which it served as a model for other nations, drawing on both Hungarian and international historical literature on railway and tariff policy, as well as primary sources.</jats:p>

title: MLLM-Driven Autonomous Driving: Closed-Loop Decision-Making with Language-State Alignment and Human Instruction Integration
container-title: ACM Journal on Autonomous Transportation Systems
d800c7e114eb4db4826982c6e016151dc7d88ec1.abstract: <jats:p>The core challenge of autonomous driving is achieving real-time decision-making and safety control in complex, dynamic environments, especially in long-tail scenarios where conventional systems often fail due to limited adaptability, poor human-vehicle interaction, and low interpretability. This article introduces MLLM-CLAD, a closed-loop decision-making framework powered by a multimodal large language model, which addresses semantic gaps and feedback limitations through a co-optimization strategy that integrates behavior-state alignment and language instruction fusion. MLLM-CLAD integrates three core modules: (1) The Mapping-Enhanced Language-State Alignment Module employs a deterministic mapping pipeline from language instructions to control signals, which enables highly accurate mapping from LLM semantic outputs to executable control signals. (2) The Hierarchical Dynamic Instruction Integration Module robustly categorizes and dynamically prioritizes human language instructions into different semantic types. (3) The Multimodal Fusion Module leverages a lightweight spatiotemporal Q-Former to jointly encode images and LiDAR point clouds, aligned with language in latent space for improved temporal reasoning and cross-modal consistency. Evaluated in the CARLA Town05 Long, MLLM-CLAD achieves a 78.3% Driving Score and reduces collision rates by 35% in safety-critical scenarios. On the LangAuto benchmarks, MLLM-CLAD attains a 78.5% long-tail scenario pass rate. Furthermore, the end-to-end latency is reduced to 128 milliseconds. This work establishes a scalable path toward safe, low-latency, and interpretable autonomous driving in simulation, with a clear roadmap for real-world extension.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
