title: Disruption Forecasting and Predictive Analytics With Machine Learning Approaches
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
17c3410fca5d52334564908f9163fcfe7cb92222.abstract: <jats:p>This research addresses predictive analytics for proactive risk identification and management across sectors. Using time series analysis, ML algorithms, and Chi-square testing, the study found that financial forecasting models are accurate, with credit scoring models being 85% accurate. The study reveals that predictive analytics-based frameworks considerably improve an organization's resilience. To boost forecast accuracy, businesses should integrate real-time data, use adaptive algorithms, and customise models for their sector. ML-based predictive analytics can forecast, plan for, and reduce these issues. This chapter discusses ML in predictive analytics and how firms may leverage data-driven insights to become more resilient and ready for anything. ML approaches including supervised learning, unsupervised clustering, and DL architectures are examined for disruption prediction. Real-world examples demonstrate how things work, and discussions of challenges and trends encourage research and industry use.</jats:p>

title: AI Crisis Simulations for Strategic Supply Chain Resilience Engineering
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
efa3bdd3f378e0abf94485b4112923a7db9e1877.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the integration of Scenario Intelligence (SI) in supply chain resilience engineering, leveraging AI-powered simulations for crisis management. Traditional risk management approaches are increasingly ineffective at addressing modern, unpredictable disruptions, whereas SI, through dynamic AI-driven simulations, enables proactive, real-time decision-making. Theoretical frameworks like complexity theory and resilience engineering—evolving from robustness to antifragility—are central to understanding the adaptability of supply chains in crises. The chapter covers practical applications of AI simulations in predicting and managing natural disasters, pandemics, and geopolitical risks, demonstrating how AI enhances decision-making in volatile environments. It also highlights the role of policy frameworks, industry innovations, and global governance in fostering AI adoption for resilience. Despite its potential, challenges such as data privacy, integration complexities, and governance issues remain significant barriers.</jats:p>

title: AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility Health Crises, Geopolitical Strife, and Cyber-Sabotage
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
4614f38b11f4dc792498ad9446a4ebd70c22f00e.abstract: <jats:p>The threat of unparalleled disruptions of international supply chains caused by health crises (example, COVID-19), geopolitical and geo economic tensions, and an increase in the risk of cyber-sabotage is growing. The conventional risk management strategies are not sufficient in handling the multi-dimensional nature of supply chains today. This chapter explores the potential uses of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in securing, stabilizing and future-proofing supply chains in the face of volatile conditions. By combining predictive analytics with blockchain, machine learning-driven anomaly forecasting, and the use of AI-driven decision-support tools, companies can also ensure resilience against uncertainty, cyberattack, and breakdowns in logistical operations. The chapter also examines how the incorporation of AI and supply chain governance connect in terms of ethics, and how to protect data security. By integrating a set of conceptual frameworks, real-life industry case studies and best practices within global supply chains</jats:p>

title: Cybersecurity in Digital Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a2d591ae29b63d49c8f5b0f24754dec3ea764c2d.abstract: <jats:p>With ever-increasing exposures of interconnected networks to threats and complex vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity of digital supply chains acquires importance. The principle of zero-trust architecture is, never trust always verify. An implication of this is that stringent authentication must be validated, real-time acknowledgment and monitoring must be ensured at all points, and the least-privilege access must be granted to all the users and devices. An undeniable fact is that blockchain guarantees security in transactions through its decentralized and tamper-proof record. Thus, building a truly trust less infrastructure in logistics and supply chain, blockchain and smart contract-based applications can be employed to automate business processes, remove intermediaries, and prevent fraud. For a quantum computer, post-quantum cryptography becomes an answer to preserve secrets in view of any threat of decryption; it thereby replaces classical ways of encryption with one that resists quantum attack.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Supply Chain Security
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a9fac601cba8221d0a0ca6b6ee0491173add368e.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are the backbone of global trade, yet they face unprecedented risks in the digital era. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into supply chain security has emerged as a transformative strategy to manage complex risks, enhance cyber defenses, and build resilient networks. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of how AI is reshaping supply chain risk management, from predicting disruptions to automating responses. It discusses how AI-driven tools bolster cybersecurity in increasingly digital supply chains, identifying threats and safeguarding critical links. The chapter also examines the ethical challenges—such as data privacy, bias, and accountability—arising from AI integration, along with governance measures to ensure responsible use. Policy and international cooperation aspects are explored, recognizing that global supply chains require harmonized regulations and collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Architecting Antifragile Supply Chains With AI, Digital Twins, and Zero Trust Architecture
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
633ea892d6852074e94cf9336e159d7797152a41.abstract: <jats:p>In an era defined by perpetual disruption, traditional supply chain models have proven dangerously fragile. This chapter introduces the “Sentient Shield,” a novel framework for architecting antifragile supply chains that benefit from disruptions rather than merely withstanding them. The framework integrates three critical technologies: AI driven predictive analytics for precognition, Digital Twins for hyper realistic visualization and simulation, and Zero Trust Architectures as a foundational security posture. Through detailed case studies of the COVID 19 vaccine distribution, semiconductor trade wars, and the SolarWinds cyberattack, this chapter demonstrates how the Sentient Shield creates supply chains that learn from disruption. The chapter concludes with practical implementation principles and discusses governance challenges, providing a comprehensive blueprint for C suite leaders, government strategists, and researchers seeking to build self-improving supply networks in an increasingly volatile global environment.</jats:p>

title: Securing Supply Chain Data Integrity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
6ae06d7ba4e33764ea4e2c6baf465dcb9f47235f.abstract: <jats:p>The digitization of global supply chains has enhanced efficiency but simultaneously expanded the attack surface for cyber-sabotage and insider manipulation. Ensuring data integrity across interconnected entities has become a strategic necessity for operational resilience. This chapter presents an AI-driven multi-layered framework integrating machine learning, deep learning, federated learning, and explainable AI to strengthen data authenticity and transparency. The framework detects behavioral and contextual anomalies, preserves privacy through decentralized intelligence, and supports auditability via interpretable decision outputs. Analytical case studies from pharmaceutical and semiconductor domains demonstrate adaptability across heterogeneous supply environments. The study further outlines future research directions involving quantum-safe architectures, sustainable AI, and ethical governance, positioning artificial intelligence as a cornerstone for secure, trustworthy, and resilient supply chain ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: The Convergence of National Security and Supply Chain Sovereignty
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
44cb6bda4d1590b2dfc8114ac6a80fe1ec18625f.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in global supply chains has reshaped how organizations and governments predict, detect, and respond to security threats. Yet, this transformation has produced both notable successes and critical failures. This book explores real-world adoption cases, best practices from multinational corporations and defense agencies, and the regulatory, ethical, and technological challenges influencing AI integration. It also projects the future of supply chain sovereignty in 2040 and beyond, highlighting risks such as technological dependency, data monopolization, and geopolitical fragmentation. By combining insights from policy, industry, and technology, the book offers a comprehensive framework for securing supply chains and provides guidance for academics, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to align AI innovation with resilience, ethics, and long-term security.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse in Supply Chain Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
09f40adbf7cb76bff382bbf6d92aec1c8a0bac82.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the concept of the industrial metaverse in supply chain management, highlighting its role in enabling AI-driven virtualization, collaborative decision-making, and sustainable transformation. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital twins, IoT, and immersive interfaces create integrated, real-time, and interactive supply chain ecosystems. The study emphasizes the shift from reactive to predictive and autonomous supply chains through simulation, optimization, and data-driven intelligence. It further discusses the role of the industrial metaverse in enhancing multi-stakeholder collaboration, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability through circular economy practices. A comprehensive framework is proposed to integrate technological, organizational, and strategic dimensions. The chapter contributes by offering insights into building resilient, intelligent, and sustainable supply chain systems.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse and AI-Driven Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
47d3e0515c13fda1af2da5950b7c6fa396315d15.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how agriculture and food logistics are being transformed through artificial intelligence and Industrial Metaverse-enabled supply chain systems in emerging economies. It examines the shift from traditional linear food systems toward immersive, data-driven, and phygital ecosystems integrating digital twins, blockchain, IoT, and AR/VR technologies. Using a qualitative multiple-case study approach, the research analyzes India, China, Brazil, and Russia to understand how policy reforms, technological adoption, and infrastructure development influence food security and resilience. Findings show that AI-enabled forecasting, real-time monitoring, and immersive simulation improve supply chain efficiency, reduce food waste, and enhance sustainability. However, challenges such as infrastructure gaps, digital inequality, and limited workforce readiness persist. The study emphasizes the importance of integrated policy frameworks and education systems to enable next-generation resilient food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Recognition
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
8d55c03606f397dfebd690ec5704784da2344f3c.abstract: <jats:p>Current e-learning systems are still not well-suited to learn in real-time as individuals' emotional and cognitive state. The chapter presents AIALE (Affective Intelligence Adaptive Learning Engine), a multimodal system capable of embedding facial coding, bio signals, keystroke dynamics and eye-tracking in a single pipeline and with sub-500ms inference latency. The AIALE's three-tier architecture consists of a deep learning-based effect inference, a reinforcement learning-based curriculum control and a pedagogic intervention broker. AIALE was tested with 214 university students from four disciplines and led to statistically significant increases in knowledge gain (31% above that of a knowledge-adaptive baseline) as well as to an increase in engagement duration and a balance of cognitive load, compared to a knowledge-adaptive baseline and a non-adaptive control. An ablation analysis shows that the most significant affective dimensions for adaptive interventions' quality are confusion and cognitive load detection. The chapter also introduces five research gaps and explores emerging research avenues such as generative AI tutoring agents and explainable affective adaptation.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI as a Catalyst for Intelligent Transformation in Higher Education Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
666d4eec1099228678f9ba6af74a13a32a982a4f.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of higher education administration has exposed the limitations of fragmented, rule-based systems that struggle to support timely and data-driven decision-making. This chapter examines agentic artificial intelligence (AI) as a catalyst for transforming administrative ecosystems into adaptive, intelligent, and coordinated systems. Moving beyond traditional automation, agentic AI introduces autonomy, context-awareness, and continuous learning, enabling real-time data integration, predictive–prescriptive analytics, and workflow orchestration across core domains. Drawing on frameworks such as multi-agent systems, decision intelligence, and socio-technical systems, the chapter analyzes how agentic AI reshapes institutional processes and decision structures. It also highlights key challenges, including data silos, governance complexities, and ethical concerns. Ultimately, the chapter argues that effective implementation requires systemic integration, robust governance, and strong human–AI collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Decision-Making Augmentation in Higher Education Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
4753ec1853130197948d90a206fa4f559f31bc1c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid digital transformation of higher education has intensified the need for more adaptive, data-driven administrative decision-making systems. This chapter examines the emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative approach that extends beyond traditional analytics and generative models by enabling autonomous, goal-directed, and context-aware decision processes. It outlines the conceptual foundations of agentic AI through intelligent agent theory, decision intelligence, and socio-technical systems, and analyzes its core capabilities, including perception, reasoning, planning, and action. The chapter further explores its applications across key administrative domains and highlights its potential to enhance efficiency, predictive capacity, and institutional responsiveness. Despite these benefits, critical challenges related to governance, ethics, data fragmentation, and human-AI collaboration are emphasized, underscoring the need for balanced and responsible implementation.</jats:p>

title: Decision Intelligence for AI-Enabled University Governance and Data-Driven Administrative Transformation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
1ea21bd12f81b110514bb8aff08dc36ff1204ee4.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming governance and administrative processes in higher education institutions. Traditional systems relying on manual operations and fragmented data are increasingly inadequate. This chapter proposes an AI-driven decision intelligence framework for efficient, data-driven, and policy-aligned governance. The framework integrates data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, and predictive analytics within a unified architecture, where institutional data from student, financial, and human resource systems are analyzed using machine learning models to generate insights. These are refined through policy-based decision mechanisms to ensure transparency and compliance. Results show improved decision accuracy, operational efficiency, and reduced processing time, supported by dashboards for real-time monitoring. Ethical concerns such as data privacy and bias are also addressed. A case study from Tamil Nadu demonstrates the framework's applicability as a scalable model for AI-enabled governance.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI as a Governance Partner in Higher Education Leadership
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
57435d97d2fd69fae64c511686c94b37c80641ef.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter advances the argument that agentic artificial intelligence should be theorized as a governance partner in higher education leadership rather than as a mere administrative tool. As universities operate within intensifying accountability, datafication, and audit regimes, agentic systems increasingly participate in enrollment, budgeting, accreditation, and research decisions, reshaping institutional decision architectures. To address this shift, this chapter proposes the Strategic Agentic Governance Framework, a feedback-driven model linking data intelligence, normative framing, decision orchestration, accountability, and adaptive institutional learning. Drawing on distributed leadership, institutional agency, algorithmic governance, and socio-technical systems theory, the framework reconceptualizes leadership as meta-governance, the deliberate design of hybrid human and machine decision systems. The chapter also examines accountability diffusion, algorithmic bias, and data sovereignty, and offers testable propositions and a maturity continuum for future research.</jats:p>

title: Digital Catalytic Leadership for Governing Agentic AI
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
a7a2f25db22c009ea70fb3c60ff8c7c5966288e7.abstract: <jats:p>The evolution of agentic AI is transforming higher education administration beyond simple automation. This chapter examines the governance challenges of AI integration in universities and proposes Digital Catalytic Leadership (DCL) as an adaptive governance framework. The study finds that while agentic AI can improve administrative effectiveness, it also creates challenges related to accountability, data security, and human–AI relations. This chapter argues that DCL is important for building adaptive, ethical, and human-centered higher education governance in the AI era.</jats:p>

title: From Paperwork to Predictive Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
59ed15c0f7f338ea6f034d707cac8523fbdf31f4.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a Cambodia-specific framework for implementing agentic AI in higher education administration, converting bureaucracy and paperwork into a predictive, evidence-based governance model. Cambodia's higher education faces accountability, accreditation, student expectations, and limited admin capacity. AI adoption is fragmented, causing delays, duplicate reports, and inconsistent services. The chapter suggests agentic AI can act as an orchestration layer for institutions by integrating systems and enhancing decision-making in Admissions, Enrolment, Scheduling, Finance, HR, Research Administration, and Quality Assurance. It highlights key use cases such as coordinating student services, automating accreditation evidence management, forecasting queues, and identifying compliance gaps. The chapter aims to provide a pragmatic policy synthesis based on practice and resource constraints in Cambodia. The chapter's main contribution is a practical model to facilitate the adoption of responsible agentic AI that aims to improve administrative efficiency and transparency.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Budget Allocation and Predictive Financial Analytics Using AI in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
811b776505e2e740c926ee67de48c35b2159227e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter considers the potential use of an agentic AI in changing the face of financial planning and budgeting in higher education organizations characterized by uncertain funding, unpredictable enrollments, and increasing accountability. This chapter criticizes the conventional approach to incremental budgeting and advances a governance-centered model in which AI functions as an agent for enhancing collaboration in financial decision-making rather than taking control from people's hands. Informed by Dynamic Capabilities theory, the contribution illustrates the role of AI in improving the capabilities for sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring at institutions for adaptive management. This chapter further develops the concept of a four-step RACT model for implementing AI in responsible ways. The contribution is enriched through institutional case illustrations with emphasis on the advantages gained through AI adoption. The challenges associated with the application of AI in financial management are discussed, alongside mitigation approaches. Research gaps are clearly stated.</jats:p>

title: A3 Model in Indian Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
c1ad93ee7e0991c260ac643de8c3fa1e55541ddd.abstract: <jats:p>The appearance of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Indian academic spaces has ushered in a wave of revolutionary changes, bringing new tools like intelligent automation, supporting governance, intelligent data-based decisions, and the like. This subchapter attempts to bring out a framework, A3 Model, where Agentic AI, Administrative Resilience, and Educational Excellence are offered within one overarching design from a more applied framework. The chapter goes on with an empirical inquiry where mixed methods and PLS-SEM are used on data from Indian universities, focusing on how Agentic AI shapes institutional responsiveness and academic performance. The results show that there exists a strong and positive connection among the capabilities of AI, the existence of an agile organization, and the realization of desirable academic outcomes, but most significantly, the interaction of those effects in the context of escalating and fostering the productive and efficient administration within the higher education system.</jats:p>

title: Administrative System Transformation Through Agentic AI in Enrollment and Admissions Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
19d4c9a3cbac21418f82ad721e79494df8fa79eb.abstract: <jats:p>Administrative challenges are increasing in higher education establishments in light of the rising enrollment pressures, changing student needs, and heightened demands for accountability. Agentic AI, with its capacity to self-directly perceive, plan, act, and learn, opens up avenues for a novel way to revolutionize enrollment and admissions management. This chapter provides an overview of the ways in which agentic AI is transforming the enrollment cycle, including the engagement of students, admission applications, prediction and planning, decision-making, and yield management. Based on the recent research and practical experience of various educational establishments, the potential, as well as possible difficulties associated with automation, ethical issues, privacy concerns, workforce transformation, among other issues, are discussed.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI in Enrollment and Admissions Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
00d998159a5393674028a10b076cd1fb8a858ea4.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in transforming enrollment and admissions management within higher education institutions. The chapter discusses the evolution of admissions systems from traditional manual structures to intelligent, data-driven administrative ecosystems supported by predictive analytics, workflow automation, applicant screening, and conversational AI. The study highlights how AI-enabled systems improve enrollment forecasting, communication responsiveness, institutional coordination, and operational efficiency while reducing administrative delays and inconsistencies. Empirical findings from multi-institutional analysis demonstrate measurable improvements in applicant engagement, screening accuracy, workflow synchronization, and fairness in admissions processes. The chapter further explores governance, ethical considerations, explainability, and human-AI collaboration frameworks necessary for responsible implementation of intelligent admissions systems in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI in Higher Education Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
cf8cf6f3740adc256c5ee8a80e0a1c1edcb0aaeb.abstract: <jats:p>Higher education institutions are increasingly transitioning from traditional rule-based automation toward autonomous, goal-directed agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems within administrative environments. Unlike conventional automation tools, agentic AI systems can interpret context, plan actions, utilize external tools, and adapt dynamically to changing conditions. This chapter examines the opportunities and risks associated with these systems in student support services. It discusses benefits such as improved responsiveness, continuous service availability, and reduced administrative workload, while also evaluating risks including algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, decision opacity, and the potential reduction of human-centered support. The chapter further proposes a governance framework based on Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) oversight models to support responsible and transparent AI deployment in higher education administration</jats:p>

title: ESL Classrooms in the Age of AI
container-title: Examining Gender Dynamics in English Language Development
9ec5be19b6f57cc824ddd32998fbae5b92f230e2.abstract: <jats:p>Between 2020 and 2025, EFL and ESL classrooms have undergone rapid platformization, with AI writing tutors, learning management systems, and online proctoring becoming central to instruction and assessment. This chapter examines how these AI-mediated technologies reshape gender dynamics in language education, with attention to learners outside the traditional gender binary. Combining a critical narrative review (2020-2025) with a structured walkthrough of ten platforms evaluated against a three-criterion Gender-Inclusivity Audit, the chapter finds uneven patterns: while flagship generative AI has improved its handling of gender-neutral pronouns, legacy writing-evaluation tools, learning management systems, and biometric proctoring continue to enforce binary, Western-normative baselines. The chapter contributes a comparative theoretical synthesis, empirical evidence on algorithmic bias, and a five-step practitioner framework, arguing that educational equity requires gender-responsive, decolonially-grounded design rather than superficial gender-neutrality.</jats:p>

title: Media, Information Literacy, and Digital Inclusion
container-title: Designing and Implementing Literacy Ecosystems
85d8685daef775e3add303b6478de7ce0dff10c3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter intersects media, information literacy (MIL), digital inclusion and community informatics in rural Zambia. The development of digital technologies, media platforms and information systems has transmogrified how people access information, communicate, participate in civic life and contribute to socioeconomic development. Notwithstanding these advancements, noteworthy digital inequalities persist between urban and rural communities, predominantly in developing countries. There, access to information and communication technologies (ICTs), digital skills and information resources remains uneven. Besides brining out disablers, the chapter argues that MIL is a critical enabler of meaningful participation in contemporary information societies and a prerequisite for reducing digital exclusion. The chapter proposes an integrated framework linking media access, information literacy, community empowerment and sustainable rural development. It concludes with policy and practice recommendations for strengthening digital inclusion and community transformation in rural Zambia.</jats:p>

title: Coexistence of AI Nurse and AI-Simulated Patient in Nursing Education Using a Bidirectional Fine-Tuning Pipeline: Development and Content Analysis Study
container-title: JMIR Biomedical Engineering
83be49219b02021add3414e1cbea9cacaa7c21ab.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Simulated patient systems are essential in nursing education but face actor scarcity, instructor burden, cost, and disrupted continuity where in-person simulation cannot be sustained. Existing large language model (LLM)–based systems address these issues but treat the dialogic partner—the AI nurse—as a static prompt or unspecialized model, compromising data collection quality and pedagogical applicability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We report (1) the construction of 2 specialized fine-tuned models, NURSE-ONE (AI nurse) and PATIENT-ONE (AI-simulated patient), via a 5-step bidirectional fine-tuning pipeline; (2) their evaluation using Berelson content analysis validated by independent human coders; (3) an exploratory third-party evaluation by nursing faculty; and (4) the design of a coexistence simulation ecosystem supporting 3 operating modes, including offline disaster preparedness applicability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>On a single consumer-grade graphics processing unit (NVIDIA RTX 4090; 24 GB video random access memory), the multimodal base model gemma4-E4B-it was fine-tuned via low-rank adaptation in five steps: (1) a 251-scenario base from 29 institutionally authored nursing care plans and 20 items from the 115th Japanese National Nursing Examination; (2) a provisional dialogue system (AutoGen v18, maxmsg=25) to collect training dialogues; (3) NURSE-ONE fine-tuning across 3 training volume conditions (245, 735, and 1225 cases); (4) 4-condition Berelson comparison; and (5) PATIENT-ONE fine-tuning on NURSE-ONE–generated dialogues with a 3-condition comparison. Interrater reliability was confirmed by 2 independent nursing experts (196 blinded utterances, κ=0.770) and corroborated by 2 LLM raters (κ=0.742). Ten nursing faculty evaluated 3 coexistence modes in a working web user interface (21-item rubric; item-level content validity index=1.00).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Four-condition Berelson analysis (
                      <jats:italic>χ</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      <jats:sub>15</jats:sub>
                      =42.0,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001) identified the 735-case nurse-side condition (open question rate=21.5%) as NURSE-ONE; information collection rate reached 15.5% (~4× baseline) at 1225 cases. PATIENT-ONE A/B/C analysis (
                      <jats:italic>χ</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>

                      =11.8,

                      =.30) showed no significant category shift but the lowest response length variability (SD 24.5) and highest information-providing rate (47.9%) at 735 cases, adopted as PATIENT-ONE. The 2 adapters appeared to operate on different axes—qualitative questioning style on the nurse side and quantitative response stability on the patient side—a preliminary observed pattern we term functional asymmetry, pending replication. Third-party evaluation rated the AI-simulated patient, AI nurse, and dyadic interaction at 90.3%, 69.0%, and 84.8%, respectively, with role maintenance at ceiling (mean 5, SD 0). All 3 modes met the prespecified 3-second latency threshold.

                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 5-step bidirectional fine-tuning pipeline produced 2 specialized models whose joint deployment constitutes a design pattern for nursing education simulation. The preliminarily observed functional asymmetry between qualitative nurse-side variation and quantitative patient-side stabilization appears to underwrite the system’s coherence, supporting 3 operating modes on consumer-grade hardware and deployable offline in disaster preparedness contexts. Third-party evaluation confirmed exploratory educational applicability, with all evaluators rating the system as usable, providing a foundation for future learner outcome studies.</jats:p>

title: AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Foundations of AI Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
9f630b63700f2df7c972c28e264e05e6ceddde77.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence governance has emerged as a critical imperative in contemporary digital societies, demanding comprehensive frameworks that balance innovation with accountability, human rights, and democratic values. This chapter examines the foundational principles, institutional mechanisms, regulatory approaches, and ethical considerations that constitute effective AI governance systems. Through analysis of global governance frameworks including the EU AI Act, risk-based regulatory models, and international cooperation mechanisms, the chapter explores how legal norms are being transformed to address AI's unique challenges. Key governance dimensions examined include algorithmic accountability, transparency requirements, human rights safeguards, and the integration of democratic oversight into AI systems. The chapter provides empirical insights from recent governance initiatives across jurisdictions, analyzing both regulatory successes and persistent governance gaps.</jats:p>

title: AI Governance Foundations
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
2b28db33bf306c935f211bfca2b70402877fdf38.abstract: <jats:p>Government Artificial intelligence altering the governmental systems and substituting the traditional e-government models with the more algorithmic system of governance, where the decisions are increasingly mediated by the automated systems and processes based on the data. This has created challenging legal, ethical, and regulatory challenges of responsibility, accountability, transparency and fairness. The governance principles of AI involve the establishment of legal definitions, framework and standards to define responsibilities, scope and rights of AI usage in government and civil service. System regulation, risk reduction and protection of the right of the citizens demands definite legal definitions of AI, automated decision-making, and algorithmic accountability. Efficiencies can be opened up by making e-government, centered around digital service delivery, to become algorithmic governance, with incorporation of AI tools to analyze policies to distribute resources, predictive services, and make administrative judgments.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI and Foundation Models
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
c1f53c26084dcc82007fb1323a246abfe7791ac5.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence and foundation models represent a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, raising unprecedented governance challenges. This chapter examines the intersection of these technologies with democratic institutions, legal frameworks, and ethical norms. It analyzes emerging regulatory approaches including the EU AI Act and OECD principles, explores algorithmic bias and accountability mechanisms, and investigates tensions between innovation and rights protection. Through systematic review of recent scholarship and policy developments, the chapter identifies critical challenges in transparency, intellectual property, and algorithmic decision-making legitimacy.</jats:p>

title: The New Social Contract
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
22bdcab34bf4ce9285fa937f0a7ef9efba76e478.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the transformation of democratic accountability in the age of artificial intelligence through legal, institutional, and political analysis. It examines how algorithmic decision-making reconfigures authority and responsibility, emphasizing the need for a new social contract integrating AI within constitutional frameworks. Focusing on India, the chapter proposes participatory, rights-based, and accountable governance models to align technological innovation with democratic legitimacy and public trust.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Constitutional Law in Structuring AI Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4b4b0de7a68d19261bb75753772840e30a18eec7.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the foundational role of constitutional law in structuring artificial intelligence governance frameworks. As AI systems increasingly influence democratic processes, individual rights, and societal structures, constitutional principles provide essential constraints and guidance for regulatory design. The analysis explores how fundamental rights doctrines, separation of powers, democratic accountability mechanisms, and rule of law principles shape AI governance approaches across jurisdictions. Drawing on comparative constitutional frameworks, including the EU AI Act and emerging international instruments, the chapter demonstrates how constitutional law bridges normative values and technical regulation. Key challenges include algorithmic accountability, automated decision-making impacts on fundamental rights, and the tension between innovation and constitutional safeguards.</jats:p>

title: A Conceptual Shift in Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
ab477729de01bf724d4e82f352be4fc70e322edf.abstract: <jats:p>Today, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an integral part of governance. This chapter examines the paradigm shift that is necessary for the governance of AI, which includes four key components: legality, transparency, accountability, and respect for human rights. By referring to global instruments like the European Union AI Act and the UNESCO's Ethics of AI as well as the respective national laws, it is proposed that the governance of AI should not only be about the technical but rather the rethinking of public law in light of human rights. The chapter conducts a conceptual analysis of the gaps between the regulatory framework and the actual implementation of AI in practice, particularly in high-risk industries. An Integrated Governance Framework (IGF) is proposed, in which all four pillars are interrelated.</jats:p>

title: Principles of Good Governance in the Age of AI
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
f1bf41b5e570221d1d030fc576b518faa6ad2712.abstract: <jats:p>The concept of artificial intelligence is becoming a part of the governance, artificial administration, and even the decision-making process in legal administration, which prompts serious questions about the quality of democracy and institutional control. With the impacts of algorithmic systems becoming a regulatory enforcer and in policy outputs, the opportunities of risks linked to transparency, discrimination, and lack of accountability escalate. This chapter discusses the ways in which the rule of law and democratic practices should be supported by relying on the principles of legality, transparency, and accountability in governing AI. It examines issues like black box problem, diffusion of responsibility and algorithmic discretion and suggests a normative model entailing the combination of legal protection, oversight and transparency norms to guarantee responsible and trustworthy AI usage.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive Regulation, Sandboxes, and Experimentalist Approaches
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
7e11bfc9418f4605cdb5f5a63e9b3f499236e89e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence technologies presents unprecedented challenges to traditional regulatory frameworks and democratic governance structures. This chapter examines how adaptive regulation, regulatory sandboxes, and experimentalist governance approaches are reshaping the social contract between citizens, governments, and technology corporations in the AI era. Through comprehensive analysis of emerging regulatory models across multiple jurisdictions, this study demonstrates how experimentalist approaches enable responsive governance while maintaining democratic accountability. The chapter evaluates the effectiveness of regulatory sandboxes in balancing innovation with risk management, explores the theoretical foundations of adaptive regulation in complex technological environments, and proposes a reconceptualized framework for the social contract that accommodates algorithmic decision-making while preserving fundamental rights.</jats:p>

title: Legal Ontologies as Semantic Infrastructure for Normative Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
f174114117b770c5b4a90db645fc80ad53f70442.abstract: <jats:p>The future challenge in AI & Law is not merely computational performance or post-hoc interpretability, but the translation of legal meaning into forms that computational systems can process without downgrading the normative structure of the Law into statistical correlations. This chapter introduces the philosophical argument that legal ontologies should be treated as semantic infrastructure for normative governance, that is, a mediating layer between legal texts, institutional practice, and AI-based decision support. Legal ontologies as computational artefacts that encode legal knowledge in a machine-understandable way, make explicit the conceptual commitments that enable systems to qualify facts in legally relevant terms, align conclusions to rules, exceptions, and principles, and generate explanations that simulate legal justification. Synthesizing the literature on legal ontologies (i.e., scope, engineering methodology, applications), this chapter focuses on developing a theoretical description of legal ontologies as semantic infrastructure for accountable AI in legal domains.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Economic Development, and Human Rights
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4ee6296fcf5b904bf56fa2f91c3f8be35f78cd19.abstract: <jats:p>Over the last century, the world witnessed unprecedented technological advancements and economic growth. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been a major technological breakthrough, decisively transforming economic interactions in various sectors. With their unique characteristics of speed, accuracy, and efficiency, AI-enabled systems enhanced innovation, increased productivity, and advanced economic growth. However, current experience affirms that the benefits of AI-empowered economic development are not equitably shared. It results in rising poverty, economic inequality, and human insecurity worldwide. Developing countries experience them most severely due to the increased digital divide. The human rights of millions of people are directly or indirectly denied on account of the biased interplay between AI and economic development that primarily favors advanced countries. From this perspective, this chapter, using the qualitative methodology's narrative synthesis and critical analysis tools, examines the correlation between AI and economic development through the lens of human rights.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Accountability and Protection of Fair Procedure Rights in AI-Driven Public Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
a83d8cfd752d0d873913a4e386493a38c0794f36.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyzes the paradigm shift from human-based bureaucracy to data-based governance and the tensions between algorithmic logic and fair procedure rights. The authors argue that automated decision-making in public administration triggers algorithmic procedural erosion, where traditional legal protections fail to address “black box” opacity. By identifying research gaps in how administrative law handles algorithmic discretion, this chapter explores the realignment of state power from officials to code developers. The authors propose reconstructing legal norms through an “Accountability by Design” framework, integrating procedural rights such as notification, intelligible explanation, and human intervention directly into AI architecture. Furthermore, this chapter advocates for independent algorithmic audits as legal evidence in judicial reviews to bridge information asymmetry. Finally, the authors conclude that normative redesign is essential to ensure digitalization strengthens democratic sovereignty and the rule of law, rather than creating an unaccountable technocracy.</jats:p>

title: The “Legitimate Interest Trap” in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
2e9944fcddef72768c2ae829a9e0e2ec444ccbc0.abstract: <jats:p>As organizations accelerate the deployment of AI systems, many default to the “legitimate interest” lawful basis for processing personal data. This move appears attractive because it avoids consent friction and accommodates broad operational goals such as security, fraud prevention, or service optimization. In practice, however, AI amplifies the evidentiary and governance burden embedded in legitimate interest, namely controllers must show a specific legitimate purpose, prove necessity (no equally effective, less intrusive alternative), and demonstrate that the interest is not overridden by individuals' rights and freedoms. Drawing on the European Data Protection Board's Guidelines 1/2024 on Article 6(1)(f) and the EDPB's Opinion 28/2024 on AI models, this chapter argues that “legitimate interest” becomes a trap when treated as a rhetorical justification rather than a structured test that must be operationalized through technical and organizational safeguards. The chapter proposes an “LIA-by-design” approach, that aligns privacy assessments under the EU AI Act.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Governance and Due Process in India
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
588dcb96d6cae7a2831ce0b99703c07178f2e3ab.abstract: <jats:p>The expansion of digital governance in India has embedded algorithmic systems within welfare administration, particularly in identity verification, eligibility determination, and benefit delivery. While these systems are justified on grounds of efficiency and scalability, they raise significant concerns for due process and administrative fairness. This chapter examines how core procedural safeguards notice, hearing, and reasoned decisions are affected by automated decision-making frameworks. It argues that algorithmic governance introduces opacity, limits avenues for contestation, and weakens accountability. The integration of digital identity further conditions access to welfare on technological compliance, increasing risks of exclusion. The chapter concludes that algorithmic systems fundamentally reshape state citizen relations and require recalibrated legal safeguards.</jats:p>

title: Digital Sovereignty and Legal Pluralism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
0e1ac7826c5e0fc071b7288b1558bb3f5df99b2a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving concept of digital sovereignty through a comparative analysis of the European Union, the United States, and India within conditions of legal pluralism. It explores how democratic systems negotiate authority, rights, and regulation across overlapping legal, technological, and market domains. The European Union's rights-based constitutionalism, the United States' market-oriented digital order, and India's developmental-democratic model reveal diverse strategies for governing data, platforms, and infrastructure. Drawing on secondary data from 2020–2025, the chapter analyzes regulatory frameworks such as the GDPR, DPDP Act 2023, and the U.S. FTC's enforcement regime. It identifies convergences in recognizing data as a strategic resource and divergences in institutional design, enforcement capacity, and global influence.</jats:p>

title: The Adoption of International Artificial Intelligence Frameworks in Latin America
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4701fb43814a97a05be3830c6acecafd8a990cf2.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines emerging AI regulation in Latin America through qualitative comparison of countries participating in the Council of Europe's Framework Convention on AI—Argentina, Mexico, Uruguay (Group 1)—versus influential non-participants—Brazil, Chile, Colombia (Group 2). It contrasts international soft law with the first global binding treaty, highlighting its universal openness and risk-based approach. Group 1 shows proactive adherence (Uruguay pioneering signatory, Mexico active observer) through ethical yet fragmented national strategies, while Group 2 prioritizes sovereignty via advanced risk-based legislative projects, indirectly aligned with Council of Europe standards through EU AI Act and UNESCO guidelines. The study concludes that the globalist-national dichotomy is converging toward risk-based governance and proposes the OAS as a strategic forum for an Inter-American AI Declaration to harmonize both groups, standardize supervisory mechanisms, and catalyze Council of Europe adherence, strategically positioning Latin America within global AI governance frameworks.</jats:p>

title: Digital Illiteracy and Accounting Compliance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
5efe409d16d9b3864a79a51144be26f5f26411d2.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how digital illiteracy affects accounting compliance during the transition to mandatory e-invoicing in Greece. A quantitative approach was employed using data from 220 enterprises located in the Prefecture of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace. A structured questionnaire measured digital skills, awareness of e-invoicing procedures, and perceptions of state support. The results reveal that educational level and gender significantly influence the effective implementation of e-invoicing tools, while age has no significant impact. Despite gradual improvements in digital competence, digital illiteracy remains a key barrier to full compliance, especially among SMEs. The findings highlight the need for targeted digital training programs, simplified e-invoicing platforms, and policy incentives aimed at strengthening SMEs' technological capacity. This research empirically links digital literacy to compliance behavior in an emerging economy context, offering actionable insights for policymakers, tax authorities, and accounting practitioners.</jats:p>

title: Educating Citizens in the Algorithmic State
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
c36db21603c573e6fb9e8bf58f69f40ba2fba2e3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines ethical AI awareness as a necessary form of civic competence in the algorithmic state. As AI systems increasingly shape public administration, healthcare, welfare, education, local governance, public safety, and democratic communication, citizens need more than basic digital skills. They require the capacity to understand how AI may affect rights, equality, transparency, accountability, inclusion. The chapter presents a curriculum for ethical AI awareness designed to educate AI-aware citizens and stakeholders on the ethical foundations of AI, bias and discrimination, sources of algorithmic harm, mitigation strategies, ethical frameworks, transparency, accountability, policy advocacy, and collaborative problem-solving. It argues that such education should be accessible, interdisciplinary, participatory, and inclusive, addressing not only citizens but also public officials, policymakers, educators, developers, civil society actors, and professionals.</jats:p>

title: Smart Resilience
container-title: Strategic Planning and Adaptation of Resilient Agri-Food Systems in a Changing World
1daef2626367c084bc117f883f6ea817c3e58afb.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated with strategies for adapting to climate change in the planning of the agricultural and food sectors. The goal is to make food systems more resilient and ensure long-term food security in the country. As climate change, resource shortages, and social and economic inequalities exert increasing pressure on global food systems, the utilization of data and flexible planning methods presents new opportunities for change. This chapter demonstrates how AI tools, such as machine learning, predictive analysis, and geospatial data, can facilitate climate-smart farming by enabling better decision-making, mitigating risks, and enhancing productivity. Examples from India, the Netherlands, and Kenya show how AI has been successfully used to build climate resilience worldwide. The chapter also introduces a new framework, the Data-Driven Strategic Planning Matrix (DSPM), to help match new technologies with fairness and sustainability objectives.</jats:p>

title: AI- and IoT-Driven Sustainable Smart Farming Through Modernizing Traditional Rice Machinery
container-title: Strategic Planning and Adaptation of Resilient Agri-Food Systems in a Changing World
1d19d443915e719ae530b58cbd9a0addd601cbb2.abstract: <jats:p>The combination of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) into the established works in rice farming is a radical change in the direction of sustainable and climatically adapted agriculture. By retrofitting traditional machinery with modular sensors, microcontrollers and edge/cloud AI, real-time data on soil moisture, temperature, crop health and nutrients is available. Intelligent irrigation, intelligent fertilizer prescriptions, and intelligent pest control maximize inputs, minimize labor, fuel, and chemical expenditures, and improve productivity. The chapter relies on secondary data and theoretical analysis, which limits its scope for empirical study. Bangladesh, Indian and Chinese case studies show that real efficiency, cost savings and yield stabilization are achieved. Adoption requires digital literacy, inclusiveness of services, and favorable policies; future research activities must focus on multi-season testing, interoperable systems, and gender-sensitive and sustainable deployment.</jats:p>

title: Explainable AI and ESG-Driven Decision Intelligence for Strategic Leadership in the Creative Economy
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
d8b4eafefe49e40a437d889529cb8c99644dca1c.abstract: <jats:p>As ESG principles and cutting-edge digital innovations intersect in the creative economy, strategic leadership is changing in ways never before imaginable. This chapter discusses the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in supporting ESG-driven decision intelligence by allowing a leader to make transparent, accountable, and data-informed decisions. Based on the Resource Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the chapter advances a conceptual framework that combines explainability, ESG performance measures, and strategic leadership capabilities. The conversation focuses on the benefits of explainable AI for governance, stakeholders' trust, sustainability, and organizational resilience in the creative sector. The chapter also provides future research directions in the context of responsible human-centric AI leaders in the changing digital and sustainability landscapes.</jats:p>

title: Navigating India's ESG–Digital Nexus Through AI-Driven Ethical Transformation
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
22f3457abdf2fffb7ebe5401b54c2f7bc15f8c5c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how India's creative economy might navigate the ESG–Digital Nexus via an AI-driven ethical shift, not just tech for tech's sake. It draws on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Stakeholder Theory, and basically looks at how AI-Driven Digital Capability, Big Data and IoT Integration, Ethical Digital Transformation, Strategic Leadership Agility, ESG Performance, and Sustainable Creative Economy Development connect together. The study uses survey data from 412 professionals, and it then analyses the whole thing with PLS-SEM. The outcome of the study is that AI capabilities and digital integration really do improve ESG performance, but they do it through ethical digital transformation. Strategic leadership agility tends to reinforce these effects, while ESG performance in turn supports sustainable creative economy development. Overall, the chapter stresses that technological experimentation has to be matched with ethical governance and sustainability objectives if India wants long-term competitiveness and responsible digital expansion.</jats:p>

title: Human-Centered Leadership in the Age of AI and Automation
container-title: Evolving Societies and Contemporary Workplace Issues
80fd311f525faf8dbdb5cda66118e610c171be8c.abstract: <jats:p>In the age of AI and automation, organizations need leadership that combines technological advancement with humanity. Human-centered leadership emphasizes empathy, ethics, and inclusiveness to ensure that innovation enriches and does not undermine the human experience at the workplace. As digital systems further impose decision-making, leaders will need to navigate complex ethical dilemmas, facilitate workforce development, and drive trust, culture, flexibility, and psychological safety. This approach requires open communication, equal access to opportunities, and anticipatory action in response to algorithmic discrimination and digital exclusion. This paper, based on international case studies and cross-cutting expertise, considers how leaders across the public, private, and nonprofit sectors are evolving their practices in response to the challenges of digitally reshaping workplaces. This study ends with actionable frameworks, policy guidance, and research directions.</jats:p>
