title: A TOE–RBV–TBL Integrated Model of AI-Enabled Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
40d1fa5cdd6cd6c42b1d66704eea0c7b9caed768.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping food logistics by enhancing operational efficiency, reducing waste, and promoting sustainable supply chain practices. This study develops and validates an integrated Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE), Resource-Based View (RBV), and Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework to examine the determinants and outcomes of AI-enabled sustainable food logistics. Primary data were collected from 312 professionals in India's food supply chain and analysed using CB-SEM. The findings reveal that technological readiness, organisational capability, and environmental pressure significantly drive AI adoption, while AI capability positively influences environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The study offers a comprehensive theoretical framework and practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to build resilient, intelligent, and sustainable food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Cold Chain Optimization for Reducing Food Loss in Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
f7b19d3fb02e51972e9a5e5f799a5064e20516bb.abstract: <jats:p>With the combination of IoT-based monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making, AI-powered optimization of cold-chains increases the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of perishable chains. Sensors can provide real-time data, therefore, monitoring the temperature, humidity, and logistics status continuously and predict risks of spoilage and optimizing routing, storage, and inventory control with AI models. In case studies in dairy, seafood and fresh produce, there has been a substantial decrease in the spoilage and increased efficiency in work. Traceability and compliance are additionally improved with the help of the blockchain integration. In general, cold-chain systems with AI will help minimize food waste, advance food quality, and sustain logistics in complicated supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Quality Monitoring and Food Safety Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
2f988859afeb8045e1f8933ad6d0b777eed57974.abstract: <jats:p>AI has transformation in the area of food quality inspection and safety management due to the capabilities that have been introduced in rapid, precise, non-destructive and predictive assessment of food quality through the production process, processing, storage, transport, retailing and consumption. These techniques are applicable in fast monitoring and quick intervention in areas of dairy products, meat products, seafood, fruits and vegetables, cereals, beverages and ready to eat meals. This chapter discusses the principles, technologies, applications, benefits, challenges, and future prospects of AI-based food quality monitoring and safety management, with particular emphasis on intelligent sensors, real-time contamination detection, automated inspection, shelf-life prediction, process optimization, traceability, and predictive risk management across diverse food sectors.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Predictive Analytics for Sustainable Demand Forecasting in Agri-Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
ae908a7d83acc41af9c9be1d1de1a65faa9f8570.abstract: <jats:p>Predictive analytics, which is an AI technology, is changing the logistics of agri-foods by enhancing sustainability and demand forecasting. The conventional predictive approaches do not normally reflect their dynamic aspects, including weather fluctuations, market behavior and consumer behaviors, resulting into inefficiencies and food wastage. This chapter describes an AI-based framework that combines multi-source data, machine learning models, and decision support systems to come up with correct and real-time demand forecasts. The strategy facilitates optimal inventory control, effective distribution strategy, and minimized environmental concerns. There are enormous evidences of case studies showing enhancement of accuracy in forecasts, reduction of wastes, and efficiency in the operations. The results address the possible opportunities of AI assisting the resilient, adaptive, and sustainable food supply chains in the fast-changing global food system.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Innovations in Agri-Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
700ec2c44d31bcf14cea8b84c21efb4ae0bd8c73.abstract: <jats:p>Algorithms and other AI tools are increasingly being used to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and resilience of the Integrated Agri-food Supply Chain (IASC) across several areas of the agri-food sector. Innovations enabled by using AI technologies in agri-food systems referred to in this chapter are the ones that will achieve the best production, processing, distribution and consumption. The predictive analytics, machine learning, and intelligence-supporting tools are all about ensuring that requirements are always checked and predictable, resources are deployed,, and risk minimisation is done in real time. AI and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain platforms, and automated logistics are explored, and the potential for creating transparent, traceable supply chains that adapt to fluctuating demand and supply is investigated. Case studies have been presented that show successful applications and improvements in productivity, waste minimisation,, and operational costs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Driven Real-Time Route Optimization for Dynamic Food Logistics and Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
a3d254406bb275561bb5d6e8d0065c094ec34437.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter describes how to use real-time data analytics and machine learning to automatically simulate and execute alternative food logistics routes to predict supply chain bottlenecks (such as supplier failures or natural disasters) before they occur. Based on academic publications from 2024 to 2026, the chapter uses a systematic review and thematic content analysis. The findings show that AI and data analytics are transforming food logistics and supply chains into sustainable, efficient, and creative transportation. Traditional logistics systems suffer from poor order consolidation, low truck capacity utilization, static route planning, and significant environmental impacts. Efficiency losses increase operational expenses, delay supply, and increase carbon emissions, threatening sustainability. Cloud-based data platforms and reinforcement learning optimize logistics and route planning. Logistics sustainability demands data-driven decision-making and clever automation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
1ca0d752e991777e60571046cca42e7e93889d3a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of agri-food supply chains through artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing sustainable food logistics, resilience, and human resource management (HRM). It highlights how AI-driven technologies such as machine learning, IoT, and predictive analytics enable real-time decision-making, demand forecasting, and supply chain optimization, thereby reducing food waste and improving efficiency. The study integrates sustainability dimensions—environmental, economic, and social—with resilience strategies to address disruptions and uncertainties. Furthermore, it explores the critical role of HRM in facilitating workforce transformation, human–AI collaboration, and organizational change. An integrated AI–Sustainability–HRM framework is proposed to enhance adaptability and long-term performance. The chapter contributes to theory and practice by presenting a holistic, data-driven approach to building intelligent, resilient, and sustainable food logistics systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Food Waste Reduction in India's Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
fc88c02780841f38b3f41c69dae42b101d38d76a.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we focus on the role that AI-driven predictive analytics can play to assist with forecast accuracy, cold-chain orchestration, quality monitoring and speed of response upstream and downstream through the farm-to-market flows to abete food loss and waste in India´s perishable supply chains. It relies on a systematic secondary empirical synthesis of India-centric studies, policy papers, and analytics research on global experience pertaining to high perishability classes of vegetables, dairy, fish, and other fresh fruits. The chapter proves that besides infrastructural hurdles, food waste challenges of India is also a challenge of timing, visibility and coordination. Evidence from India reveals how much of the loss occurs is seasonally driven, how losses are correlated with harvest volume, storage, transport reliability, and the quality sorting and practices. This chapter presents a predictive analytics framework for agri-logistics, suggests how Indian firms and policymakers can implement the approach, and claims that digital traceability.</jats:p>

title: Predictive Business Intelligence Architectures for Cold-Chain Logistics Mitigating Food Waste Through AI-Driven IoT Sensor Integration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
791f2efff6e75d93d6ead2cbd5779a343d5628c2.abstract: <jats:p>Food loss and waste in cold-chain logistics result not only from refrigeration failures, but also from fragmented data, delayed responses, and weak coordination across supply-chain actors. This chapter presents an IGI-style conceptual and implementation framework for predictive business intelligence (BI) in cold-chain logistics. It argues that waste reduction is more effective when Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, event-driven data integration, and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics are designed as a layered architectural capability rather than as stand-alone monitoring tools. Drawing on literature in cold-chain management, food quality, wireless sensing, BI, predictive analytics, AI-enabled supply chains, and digital twins, the chapter shows how variables such as temperature, humidity, location, door events, shock, dwell time, and product condition can be transformed into risk scores, dynamic shelf-life estimates, prioritized exceptions, and closed-loop decisions. It also proposes architecture and seven implementation workstreams for deployment.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Cold Chain Management Using AI and IoT
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
60daab0ba3149ca77331fc247ab25917cceed633.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is fundamentally reshaping cold chain logistics, enabling unprecedented levels of precision, transparency, and sustainability. This chapter examines how intelligent sensing, predictive analytics, blockchain-based traceability, and digital twin simulation collectively address the chronic inefficiencies of temperature-sensitive supply chains. Drawing on recent empirical and review studies, the chapter presents an integrated framework that links real-time data acquisition to AI-driven decision-making and blockchain-anchored accountability. Key themes include spoilage prevention, carbon footprint reduction, regulatory compliance, and consumer trust. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on challenges and emerging directions for scalable, equitable, and ethically grounded cold chain transformation.</jats:p>

title: Regularization by noise for the energy- and mass-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equations
container-title: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
8c206c60a6a005a074ded0a75dccaaae5de060d8.abstract: In this article we prove a regularization by noise phenomenon for the energy-critical and mass-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equations. We show that for any deterministic data, the probability that the corresponding solution exists globally and scatters goes to one as the strength of the non-conservative noise goes to infinity. The proof relies on the rescaling transform and a new observation on the rapid uniform decay of geometric Brownian motions after short time.

title: Thinking Through Mixed Realities
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
7e2a004df4a83c1b92fd39dd0f7d5d36604859f2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter explores knowledge of and in mixed realities and uses tools from epistemic justice discourses to think about ways our environment is made more intelligible or less so. As Mixed Reality technologies embed more knowledge into our environment in new ways, decisions must be made about what and whose knowledge is included and what interactions with the environment are made easier or harder. The chapter also looks at the ways in which Mixed Reality can be used by companies to gain knowledge about the world to train up AI agents, and the ways in which MR and AI tools can be used by those with the resources to employ them to understand the world, and the implications of both. Finally, the chapter looks at how forming knowledge of partially or fully virtual entities and worlds is different from a fully material environment.</jats:p>

title: Digital Skills and Professional Judgment in AI-Driven Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
fa94d39fbd808cc46e56a32eb78b60762c9d5124.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping financial decision-making by altering how information is analyzed, interpreted, and translated into professional judgment. This chapter examines the role of digital skills in determining whether AI strengthens or undermines the quality and accountability of financial decisions. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature, the chapter conceptualizes digital skills as cognitive–governance capabilities that extend beyond technical proficiency to include critical interpretation, calibrated reliance on AI, explainability, professional skepticism, and ethical judgment. Particular attention is given to automation bias, accountability risks, and the organizational conditions that shape human–AI interaction. The chapter concludes that responsible AI-enabled financial decision-making depends not on algorithmic capability alone, but on the alignment of digital competence, professional judgment, and effective governance.</jats:p>

title: From Financial Accountant to Digital Finance Architect
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
301bb7a811700c54a3c8f72796dd343a397ed320.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyzes the digital transformation of the finance function as a structural reconfiguration of processes, decision-making logic, and governance. It demonstrates how automation, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and RegTech are shifting traditional job profiles from process execution to the architectural design of digital financial systems. On this basis, the Digital Finance Competency Architecture (DFCA) is developed, integrating technological, data-analytical, governance-related, and strategic-cognitive competencies. The analysis illustrates that effective performance in digital finance environments requires systemic competence, i.e., the ability to translate data, models, and regulatory requirements into coherent decision-making architectures. Finally, implications for education, organization, and governance are discussed, and the Digital Finance Architect is established as a new professional role model.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Financial Decision Support for Handicraft Artisans
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
1d34157c42ec302960b797359d16b132c9fe0d28.abstract: <jats:p>Handicraft artists play an important role in conserving cultural and social history while also contributing to the growth of their respective economies. It contributes four to five percent to the world economy and creates a huge number of job opportunities in the neighbourhood. Handicraft workers contribute to societal innovation in the shape of innovative work methods, techniques, and so on. This area sheds light on the hidden talents and abilities of craft workers. However, their salary and economic situation do not allow for this. They are frequently confronted with issues and obstacles such as limited market access, intense rivalry from major companies, a lack of technology, and a communication gap. The article focuses on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to solve difficulties for the handicraft industry. Primary data were acquired from 120 handicraft workers for the study using a structured questionnaire, including demographic information, production costs, profit from their company, and numerous problems they encounter.</jats:p>

title: AI and Predictive Analytics in Performance Monitoring
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
6734ced4b1406c8f7437d78ac9138a400a2eaba5.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics have revolutionized supply chain performance monitoring by enabling real-time visibility, proactive risk management, and data-driven decision-making. This chapter examines the integration of AI technologies—including machine learning, deep learning, and advanced analytics—into supply chain performance measurement systems. It explores how predictive models enhance forecasting accuracy, optimize resource allocation, and improve sustainability outcomes while maintaining compliance standards. Through systematic analysis of current research and practical applications, the chapter demonstrates how organizations transition from reactive compliance monitoring to proactive competitive advantage through intelligent performance systems.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
95a62b89e12f29ec2d10ee4b3bff78918b9670c6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical communication skills are a core yet complex competency in medical education and practice. However, early-stage medical students often struggle to apply communication frameworks in practice due to limited opportunities for structured simulation training. Generative AI (GenAI)–supported training has the potential to offer a scalable and innovative approach for clinical communication skills training.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined the longitudinal development of medical students’ clinical communication skills over 1 academic year and investigated whether AI-powered simulation contributed to differential improvement relative to conventional training. In addition, the study explored motivational, behavioral, and affective mechanisms associated with communication skills development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A nonblinded randomized controlled design was used at a medical school in the United Kingdom, with students assigned either to the control group (n=28, 56%) or to the AI group (n=22, 44%), who practiced with SimPatient, a patient-simulator chatbot accessed through a web browser. Communication skills performance was assessed using standardized objective structured clinical examinations (OSCE) scores relative to the pass marks to enable comparison across time points. Paired t tests and difference-in-differences (DID) analyses were conducted between groups and over time to examine changes in communication skills. Latent change score modeling was used to identify predictors of communication skills change. Sentiment analysis was conducted on 6120 comments from AI-student conversations. Finally, a system quality survey was used to assess participants’ feedback on the AI-powered simulator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Latent change score modeling showed that gains in intrinsic motivation and behavioral learning were significant predictors of students’ communication skills change. The AI group showed a greater descriptive increase in communication skills than the control group, yet the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Within the AI group, consultations whose lexical tone trended more strongly toward resolution (consultation tone) were descriptively associated with communication skills improvement; given the small subsample (n=17), this finding is reported as exploratory. The AI group’s confidence level in AI use was negatively associated with communication skills improvement, while the group nevertheless reported a generally high level of satisfaction with the system.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, medical students’ clinical communication skills increased over the academic year, with this development most strongly associated with their motivation and behavioral engagement; the AI-supported group did not differ significantly from conventional training. The simulator responded appropriately and provided a usable environment for practicing foundational communication behaviors but was limited in capturing the affective complexity, vulnerability, and narrative unpredictability of real clinical encounters. In conclusion, this study suggests that GenAI holds promise for supporting foundational clinical communication training and providing positive practice environments, thereby fostering motivation and behavioral engagement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Reconnoitring Yogic Peace of Mind and Transient Happiness With Their Perceived Psychological Correlates
container-title: The Neuroscience of Happiness
2a08909a0d86148aae4b34a85733003e4a4fe6d2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter discusses yogic peace of mind as a complex, self-reported psychological construct and looks into its linkages with perceived cognition, emotional regulation, meditative consciousness, and well-being. The empirical part of the research is a pilot cross-sectional study conducted only using data collected via questionnaires; it did not include measurements of brain activity, neurotransmitter levels, the autonomic nervous system, or any other biological parameters. Consequently, all neurological hypotheses are discussed as interpretations based on existing neuroscience literature and not on the findings of this particular research. Some preliminary findings of factor, regression, and structural modeling analyses will be used to evaluate the proposed theoretical links between the concepts. There is evidence of correlations between long-term yogic practice, reported peace of mind, and positive psychological outcomes; however, there is no proof of causation or physiological changes. Further large-scale longitudinal studies are required to verify the hypothesis.</jats:p>

title: Cult of Personality or Lack of Competition? Determining Trump’s Sway Over Republican Partisans on a Critical Case
container-title: Public Opinion Quarterly
0b620bb854060710d7831a6d8b3c0a56a45e26a0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>It is well established that partisans follow their leaders. While this potentially has important implications for political accountability, studies of opinion leadership rarely examine accountability directly. We test whether partisans are able to hold a dominant leader accountable under favorable conditions using a critical case: Trump’s position on the Epstein files. Two preregistered experiments, fielded before the release of the Epstein files, show that partisans follow Trump and do not hold him accountable when he is unopposed or contested by the Democrats. However, when Trump faces opposition from within his own bloc—especially countermessaging from right-coded media elites—both issue-specific and overall approval decline substantially, and following is halved. Our results have two important implications. First, opinion leadership does not imply the absence of political accountability. Second, meaningful political competition in polarized societies may need to originate from within ideological blocs. While Trump is powerful, credible opposition can make him accountable.</jats:p>

title: The application of an artificial intelligence–enhanced virtual reality cognitive behavioral therapy tool is feasible and acceptable in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: A multicenter mixed methods pilot study
container-title: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
34e53c5af6594279fbcef7d176c277418b8c6c44.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently experience anxiety, pain, and reduced quality of life. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective for anxiety, but access may be limited. We evaluated the feasibility and explored the potential clinical impact of an artificial intelligence–powered virtual reality CBT-based application (XAIA [eXtended Reality Artificially Intelligent Ally]) in patients with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This was a multicenter, mixed-methods pilot study recruiting adults with IBD from the University of Chicago and Cedars-Sinai medical centers. Participants completed a single 30-minute session with the XAIA conversational avatar. Pain and anxiety were measured before and after the session using a visual analog pain scale and State–Trait Anxiety Inventory, respectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted after the session to assess acceptability. Quantitative analysis was completed using paired t tests, and interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-four participants (median age 34 years, 71% women, 59% with Crohn’s disease) participated in this study. Qualitative analysis revealed high acceptability, with participants reporting feelings of safety, validation, and improved coping. Participants valued the immersive environment, conversational avatar, and ability to discuss sensitive topics without judgment. As an exploratory outcome, participants reported a statistically significant improvement in pain (−0.46; P = .011) and anxiety (−10.65; P &lt; .001) immediately following a single session.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A single artificial intelligence–driven virtual reality CBT-based session in patients with IBD was feasible and well accepted and demonstrated preliminary evidence for acute reductions in pain and anxiety scores. Immersive digital behavioral health interventions may represent a scalable adjunct to traditional mental health support among adults with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Health Tool Implementation in Clinical Practice Settings: Umbrella Review
container-title: JMIR AI
ed6b7c7bd88c542620745d58d7720ce6fb1ecaf8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI has the potential to improve clinical decision-making, efficiency, and patient outcomes, yet adoption in routine clinical practice has been slower than anticipated. While prior studies have identified factors that influence AI implementation, a comprehensive synthesis grounded in implementation science frameworks is lacking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to qualitatively and comprehensively describe barriers and facilitators to AI implementation in clinical care settings using an implementation science determinants framework, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), and to identify AI-specific determinants not fully captured by CFIR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted an umbrella review of reviews examining determinants of AI implementation in clinical practice. In accordance with the PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews) reporting guidance, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for English-language reviews published between January 2013 and July 2025. Reviews were included if they addressed barriers to and facilitators of implementing AI-enabled digital health tools in clinical care settings. Determinants were deductively mapped to the updated CFIR and inductively analyzed to identify emergent AI-specific constructs. Review quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklist, and overlap among primary studies was evaluated using the GROOVE (Graphical Representation of Overlap for Overviews) tool.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-two reviews published between 2021 and 2025 were included, encompassing studies conducted from 1990 to 2025. Reviews varied in design, including systematic, scoping, rapid, narrative, and literature reviews. Overall review quality was mixed, with 9 (41%) reviews rated at 100% quality and 4 (18%) at 50% or lower. Primary study overlap was slight, with a corrected covered area of 0.4%. Determinants of AI implementation were identified across all CFIR domains. Prominent barriers at the innovation level included limited evidence of clinical impact, poor interpretability, complexity, lack of adaptability, and insufficiently representative data. Facilitators included perceived relative advantage, co-design with clinicians, and evidence of local clinical benefit. At the implementer level, low AI literacy, limited confidence, time constraints, and concerns about professional displacement were common barriers, while training and technical support facilitated adoption. Inner setting barriers included inadequate infrastructure, limited resources, poor workflow compatibility, and weak governance structures. Outer setting barriers included unclear policies, laws, and liability frameworks, whereas partnerships and cross-sector collaboration were frequent facilitators. Inductively identified AI-specific determinants included transparency, trust, accountability, model bias, data governance, model maintenance, robustness, generalizability, existential threat, and concern about loss of the human element in care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI implementation in clinical settings is shaped by complex, multilevel, and AI-specific determinants that extend beyond traditional digital health considerations. Implementation science frameworks can be adapted to incorporate these constructs. Tailored, theory-informed strategies addressing technical, organizational, psychological, and regulatory factors are essential to support safe, equitable, and sustainable integration of AI into clinical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Stimulation for Delirium Prevention in Older Surgical Intensive Care Unit Patients With Cognitive Impairment: Protocol for a 3-Arm Randomized Pilot Trial
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
6a0305024bfe7ca8c2a7ec25512ab1521c9d9887.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative delirium is common among older adults after major surgery, especially those with cognitive impairment, and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, functional decline, mortality, and subsequent cognitive deterioration. Nonpharmacologic delirium-prevention strategies are recommended but are difficult to deliver reliably in high-acuity environments because they require repeated staff-intensive interactions, consistent patient engagement, and integration into complex intensive care unit (ICU) workflows.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, usability, safety, acceptance, and adherence of ReCognitionVR 2.0, an immersive virtual reality (VR)–based cognitive stimulation intervention designed for older surgical ICU patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This is a single-center, 3-arm, parallel-group randomized pilot trial. Ninety adults aged 65 years or older undergoing major surgery with expected postoperative ICU admission and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 15 to 24 will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to ReCognitionVR 2.0 cognitive stimulation, passive VR control exposure, or standard-of-care nurse-led reality orientation. VR sessions will be delivered once daily for up to 20 minutes on postoperative days 1 through 3 when participants are calm and alert. The primary outcomes are feasibility metrics, including recruitment, outcome completion, safety and tolerability, usability, acceptance, and adherence. Secondary outcomes estimate preliminary changes in attention and executive function using the Months Backward Test and NIH Toolbox Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test. Postoperative delirium incidence is an exploratory clinical outcome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was funded in September 2025. Participant recruitment and data collection are currently ongoing. Preliminary data quality assessments and exploratory reviews of the collected data are underway. Formal statistical analyses of the trial outcomes will be conducted after participant enrollment is completed and the study database has been finalized and locked. As of July 29, 2026, we had enrolled 18 participants. Early operational experience informed the refinement of exploratory VR performance metrics and the documentation of protocol deviations. Following an oxygen-connection near miss, we added a preintervention oxygen/readiness checklist as an operational safety safeguard. Enrollment of 90 participants is projected to be completed in 2027 if the current recruitment pace is sustained. Results are expected to be published in winter 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This protocol will generate data on feasibility, safety, usability, adherence, digital performance, cognitive assessment, and delirium measurement, all needed to optimize ReCognitionVR 2.0 and to design a future multicenter efficacy trial of VR-enabled delirium prevention in critical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Beyond binary AI text detection: Partial authorship, source-text similarity, and an integrated threshold model of detectability
container-title: International Review of Applied Sciences and Engineering
acc924b3d1c0e2463fe1a308d503fda2a23b1d77.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study investigates AI text detection under conditions that more closely reflect real-world writing practices than conventional binary human-versus-AI benchmarks. Rather than treating authorship as a dichotomy, detectability is examined as a function of partial AI authorship, source-text similarity, and generator heterogeneity. Ten pre-LLM, human-written English scientific abstracts were used as reference texts, from which four authorship states (H100, AI50, AI75, and AI100) were constructed through controlled rewriting and paragraph-level mixing. AI-generated content was produced using four large language models: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and LLaMA. Detection outputs from Turnitin and GPTZero were evaluated using non-parametric statistics, correlation analysis, and logistic threshold modeling. The results demonstrate that fully human and fully AI-rewritten texts are statistically distinguishable: median AI scores increased from 0 in H100 to 53 in AI100 for Turnitin (
                    <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>
                    = 49.5,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001) and from 0 to 11 for GPTZero (
                    <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>
                    = 61.0,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001), although AI-generated texts did not constitute a homogeneous class. Detectability also varied significantly across the four nominal authorship states for both Turnitin (H = 30.39,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001) and GPTZero (H = 21.77,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001), and systematically with source-text similarity and the generating model. Turnitin showed greater sensitivity than GPTZero to changes in nominal AI proportion and transformation intensity, particularly under mixed-authorship conditions. Significant generator-dependent differences were also observed, with Gemini outputs generally receiving higher AI-detection scores than ChatGPT or LLaMA outputs. The main methodological contribution is the Integrated Detectability Threshold Model (IDTM), which represents detection probability as a joint function of nominal AI proportion and transformation intensity. Within the present sample, the model identified a similarity transition range of approximately 63–66%, below which Turnitin-based detection became more likely than non-detection. These findings support a shift from binary AI classification toward a threshold- and risk-sensitive interpretation of AI text detectability.
                  </jats:p>

title: Should quantum physics be approached with mathematical formalism in school? Effects of instructional approach on functional understanding under cognitive and affective controls
container-title: Physical Review Physics Education Research
6493f05b70eb976685bab6227f1a5b655fc3ff28.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Evidence from physics education research suggests that the introduction of mathematical formalism in quantum physics instruction can support the development of students’ conceptual understanding, particularly by promoting functional ways of reasoning about quantum phenomena. However, empirical findings on the effectiveness of such approaches at the secondary school level remain inconclusive, and little is known about the extent to which learning outcomes are shaped by instructional design as opposed to learners’ affective and cognitive characteristics. This study addresses this gap by investigating the relative influence of instructional approach on students’ understanding of single-photon states, while controlling for prior knowledge, cognitive load, situational interest, and physics self-concept. A quasiexperimental pre-post design was implemented with
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mi>N</a:mi>
                      <a:mo>=</a:mo>
                      <a:mn>172</a:mn>
                    </a:math>
                    upper secondary students, comparing a qualitative instructional condition with an approach supplemented by a reduced Dirac formalism. Learning outcomes were assessed using the framework of Functional Fidelity and Fidelity of Gestalt. A multivariate analysis of covariance, followed by univariate analyses of covariance, was conducted to examine the contributions of instructional and learner-related variables. The findings indicate that affective variables emerge as strong predictors of functional understanding and suggest that learning in quantum physics is driven less by instructional format than by learners’ affective and cognitive prerequisites. In particular, fostering interest appears to be a key mechanism for supporting the development of functional understanding. The results highlight the importance of integrating affective dimensions into instructional design and provide a basis for future research on the interaction between instructional approaches and learner characteristics in quantum physics education.
                  </jats:p>

title: PGP-FD: A Lightweight Phase-Guided Generative Graph Process for Resource-Efficient Edge Fault Pattern Recognition in Fire-Protection Valve Sensing Systems
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
e8c77c8dfb0acb232d4d72b81bf0990419bebb53.abstract: <jats:p>Edge fire-protection sensing systems must recognize latent valve faults under limited computation, memory, and energy budgets, although fault samples are scarce and operational responses are strongly phase-dependent. This paper proposes PGP-FD, a lightweight phase-guided generative graph process for event-driven edge fault pattern recognition. Each valve operation or inspection is represented as a compact response window. A depthwise temporal encoder captures local dynamics, a monotonic phase gate models the ordered evolution of standby, actuation, transient, recovery, and settling phases, and a compact measurement graph learns hydraulic-mechanical coupling among pressure, valve motion, and event context. To reduce class imbalance, a fault-conditioned stochastic process generates rare events during training under range, phase-order, and valve-pressure consistency constraints. The training-only posterior and offline synthesis branches are removed during deployment, while confidence-uncertainty prefix inference avoids unnecessary continuous computation and retains full processing for difficult cases. Experiments on real fire-protection valve data show that PGP-FD improves recognition quality, response speed, and online model compactness over representative baselines. The results demonstrate a practical integration of lightweight pattern recognition and mechanism-consistent generative learning for resource-efficient industrial edge intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
488230a323f4a1db95fece744265b1e2765b04ec.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer have substantially improved survival, resulting in a growing population of survivors of childhood cancer who may experience long-term treatment-related sequelae. Cognitive late effects are an important long-term consequence of childhood cancer and can affect cognitive functioning, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Digital health interventions offer accessible and flexible approaches to managing cognitive difficulties among children with cancer. However, the existing evidence has not yet been comprehensively synthesized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to map and synthesize the existing evidence on digital health interventions for cognitive management among children with cancer; characterize intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components; and identify evidence gaps and priorities for future research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O’Malley framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist. Six academic databases, including PubMed, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, were systematically searched for relevant studies published between January 2010 and August 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the population-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Screening was performed independently at the title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved through discussion and, when necessary, consultation with a third reviewer. Descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis were used to synthesize the findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 5371 records were identified through the literature search. Following screening, 19 publications representing 14 independent study samples and involving 566 children with cancer were included. Four digital health modalities were identified: computer-based interventions, internet-based interventions, mobile apps, and neurofeedback training. Computer-based interventions were the predominant modality. Across these modalities, working memory and attention were the most frequently targeted cognitive domains, while feasibility, acceptability, and adherence were the most commonly assessed implementation-related outcomes. However, relatively few interventions incorporated coach support, telephone-based communication, or educational components, and none evaluated economic outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health interventions that combine cognitive training with supportive care, education, monitoring, and communication. Multicenter randomized controlled trials should subsequently evaluate these interventions using clinically meaningful outcomes, with comprehensive assessments of safety, adherence, implementation, and health economic outcomes to establish their effectiveness, feasibility, and sustainability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

53a8b9399dccecdf1d6c3cc1543b58d05b5ccf4c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and digital service systems within the hospitality sector has ushered in an era known as Hospitality 5.0. title: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists
container-title: JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies
c5049fe9025dc797144b0755cc5c8f46a237bd87.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
fe8ffd10b2aac6d85d74d4e0e162424399ee26ab.abstract:
<jats:p>As technology continues to evolve rapidly, the future of small business holds immense promise and potential. Though uncertainty and risk are key issues for both large companies and small businesses, in recent times applying new technology may allow for a better characterisation of uncertainty and reduce risk in small business decision-making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The curated chapters cover topics including: business models, social innovation, green innovation, firm resilience, industry 5.0 and many more. The diverse chapter authors from around the world provide in-depth information on innovative behaviour and future trends in eco-innovation, frugal innovation, and AI innovation by entrepreneurs and small business and gather academic recommendations from research on innovation adaptations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The series Emerald Studies in Sustainable Innovation Management aims at exploring the advancements of innovation management in turbulent times with a special attention to the transition towards a sustainable economy. The practice of innovation management is evolving rapidly as a consequence of positive phenomena such as digitalization and the green transition and negative ones such as crises and global emergencies.</jats:p>

title: Exploring the Impact of Sustainable-Oriented Innovation Practices on Competitiveness of Listed Indigenous Small Businesses in West Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
58c0bfabdb27354497e128f229483d2ad85bd894.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In the current landscape, where businesses are propelled by fast changes, their survival relies on their capacity to engage in sustainable development via innovation. Sustainable-oriented innovation practices have sparked significant academic and research interest because it is a vital pillar. Therefore, the objective of this study is to examine the impact of sustainable-oriented innovation practices on the competitiveness of listed indigenous small businesses in Nigeria. The descriptive survey design was used, and the study population comprised staff of listed small businesses in Nigeria. A closed-ended questionnaire was designed and administered, and 421 were retrieved, representing a ninety-five percent (95%) response rate. The hypothesis was tested which showed the relationship between variables and define the effect of sustainable-oriented innovation practices on competitiveness. The findings show that sustainable-oriented innovation practices of listed indigenous small businesses impact their competitiveness. Specifically, the results showed that sustainable-oriented innovation practices contribute significantly to the competitiveness of listed indigenous small businesses in Nigeria (β = 0.465, t-statistics = 2.698 &gt; 1.96, p-value = 0.000 &lt; 0.05). The path coefficient of 0.465 implies a moderate and positive correlation between sustainable-oriented innovation practices and competitiveness. This study recommends that listed indigenous small businesses should foster an organizational culture that values creativity, experimentation and lifelong learning. In this scenario, sustainable-oriented innovation practices become a strategic priority for competitiveness and businesses seeking to achieve a competitive advantage.</jats:p>

title: Embracing Circularity: How Indian Small Businesses Are Redefining Sustainability
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
388e1a6a49f44beb29afa76ae81569d60c6bed87.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>On account of resource insufficiency and polluted environmental situations, companies in India have adopted the principles of circular economy to gain sustainable development. In the present study, an attempt has been made to investigate the practice of circular economy principles by small companies in India by emphasizing more on the pros and cons of the concept. For the purpose of this chapter, case studies of the companies that have adopted circular economy practices were considered. The outcome of this study provides guidelines about the integration of the principles of circular economy model into their business operations. This research also gives suggestions about the support required from change agents in order to make this framework a sustainable economic model.</jats:p>

title: Climate and Digital Transitions Among Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in Africa: The Role of Development Finance Institutions
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
8b27d253570775e220ff4e8a070d64f9459a0838.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this chapter, the authors examine the role of Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) in enhancing climate and digital transitions among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The authors iterate the crucial role of these transitions in achieving resilience, competitiveness and sustainability among MSMEs’ amid evolving global challenges. Additionally, the authors explain the importance of DFIs in providing critical financial and technical assistance, enabling MSMEs to adopt climate-smart technologies and embrace digital transformation. The authors also highlight case studies illustrating successful DFI interventions. This chapter concludes by emphasising the need for DFIs to prioritise outreach to marginalised communities, balancing developmental goals with financial sustainability and capacity building to scale their impact.</jats:p>

title: Understanding the Adoption of Renewable Energy Among Small Businesses in Africa: Evidence From Nigeria
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
b689d46e93f9663cc17810b561c17cc8034a38eb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The adoption of renewable energy technologies has gained growing attention in Africa due to increasing electricity shortages and rising energy costs. This chapter investigates the drivers and barriers to solar energy adoption among small businesses in Nigeria as a lens to understand the broader African context. The study used cross-sectional data collected from 150 small enterprises located across major cities. The authors found that only 22% of small businesses have adopted solar energy, with income identified as the primary driver of adoption (Z = 2.12, p = 0.034). As the firms had an estimated business value of ₦750,000 ($625) and an average workforce of four employees, the average monthly revenue was found to be ₦277,000 ($231), while the average monthly expenditures of ₦17,420 ($15) and ₦20,608 ($17) were incurred on electricity and fuel, respectively. Financial constraints emerged as the major barrier, highlighted by 82% of respondents. To address this challenge, the respondents (77%) recommended government-subsidized solar energy initiatives to accelerate solar energy transition among small-scale enterprises in Africa. These findings underscore the potential of financial incentives to enhance solar energy adoption. This chapter provides critical insights for policymakers aiming to promote renewable energy adoption in developing economies.</jats:p>

title: Disruptive Technology and Market Performance: The Role of Market Capability and Resource Orchestration Capability in Small Business
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
19aafbbeb67a23759acb6e57352235f544a24704.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter explores the role of disruptive technologies in enhancing the market performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This chapter also investigates the mediating effect of the market capability and resource orchestration capability (ROC) on the disruptive technology-market performance. Through a positivist lens, this chapter employs the deductive approach in data collection and analysis. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was employed to analyse data from 327 SMEs owner/managers. Results reveal that disruptive technologies significantly and positively influence market performance in emerging markets while both market capability and ROC mediate the relationship. SMEs in emerging markets need to improve their marketing and resource orchestration capabilities, as these are essential mediators in the interaction of disruptive technology and market performance.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Disruptive Innovation and Business Performance in Small Businesses in Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
3c4517a910cdfaf09c7b5b7cd9e6af10f41d05cb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examined the impact of disruptive innovation on the business performance of small businesses in Africa, with a focus on Southwest Nigeria. This chapter adopted a descriptive quantitative survey research design. Primary data were collected through a structured, closed-ended questionnaire distributed online. The population of the study, which also serves as the sample size, includes 282 owners and managers of small businesses in the southwest Nigeria. The purposive sampling technique was adopted, and the data were analyzed using a multiple regression analysis. The findings of this chapter show that there is a significant positive relationship between disruptive innovation and business performance (r = 0.52, p-value &lt;0.05, Sig 0.000). Also, there is a significant impact of market competitiveness on business performance (β = is 0.518, p-value &lt;0.05, Sig 0.000). This study concludes that small businesses need to prioritize investing in market competitiveness and technology adoption to maintain a competitive advantage in the global market. This chapter also recommends that small businesses should prioritize the adoption of technologies and market competitiveness to enhance operational efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Disruptive Technologies and Small Business Innovation Efficiency in West Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
4070bc2b188e534881e72bcf35de3b1a3949cc06.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examined the impact of disruptive technologies on small business innovation efficiency in West Africa. Guided by three objectives, this chapter identified the drivers and enablers of technology adoption, assessed the impact of disruptive technologies on innovation efficiency and analyzed the barriers to adoption. A qualitative approach included a literature review and case study examination. The collected data were from several sources, including government reports, industry research and peer-reviewed publications. The results showed that government policy, market competitiveness and digital infrastructure were significant accelerators for technology adoption. Case studies from Nigeria and Ghana showed how favourable settings helped mobile platforms, artificial intelligence and blockchain usage, enhancing operational efficiency, cost savings and service delivery. Adoption was hampered, especially in conventional industries, by high implementation costs, lack of technical knowledge and data security issues, among other obstacles. Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations Theory clarified adoption trends by stressing the need for external facilitators to overcome impediments. Although disruptive technologies might significantly increase innovation efficiency, this chapter found that more widespread adoption relied on strategic government assistance and competitive marketplaces and enhanced digital infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Implications of Green Technology Innovation in Sustainable Organizational Environment
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
84a25cde6e843092039826c464fcb47a0566a551.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The integration of green technology innovations in organizational practices is a critical driver of sustainability in today’s business landscape. As environmental concerns intensify, organizations are increasingly recognizing the need to adopt green technologies to reduce their environmental footprint while ensuring long-term economic viability. This study is aimed to analyze the implications of the green technology innovation on the sustainable organizational environment. It is assumed that a sustainable organizational environment can be affected by the promotion and development of green technology innovation. The methods used are meta-analytical, reflective, and descriptive based on the review of the conceptual, theoretical, and empirical literature. It examines how adopting energy-efficient systems, renewable energy solutions, waste reduction technologies, and eco-friendly production processes can enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and improve corporate reputation. Furthermore, this chapter discusses the role of green technologies in driving innovation and fostering a culture of sustainability within organizations. The analysis concludes that there are direct implications between the green technology innovation and the sustainability of the organizational environment. The implications of green technology adoption extend beyond environmental impact, influencing organizational behavior, stakeholder engagement, and long-term strategic planning. By embracing green technologies, organizations can align their business goals with global sustainability objectives, positioning themselves as leaders in the transition toward a more sustainable and resilient economy.</jats:p>

title: Human Socialization (and Dis-Socialization) by AI and Robotic Companions in Educational Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
21e354c94bb2573462d54359bd698db08de31a01.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter interrogates how AI chatbots, social robots, and ambient agents function as companion technologies that reconfigure human socialization and dis-socialization in educational ecosystems. Drawing on socialization theory, ecological systems, sociocultural mediation, sociomaterial assemblages, and posthuman subjectivity, it constructs a multi-level lens spanning micro interactional dynamics, meso institutional architectures, and macro political economies. The chapter develops typologies of companion configurations, maps learner needs to companion affordances, and analyses interactional quality through constructs such as social presence, parasociality, and epistemic justice. It then articulates normative, rights-based, and governance frameworks that distribute responsibilities across learners, educators, institutions, vendors, regulators, and civil society. The chapter positions humane companionable education as an agenda that seeks to harness machine companionship for inclusion and flourishing while resisting surveillance, stratification, and civic erosion.</jats:p>

title: Emotional and Social Intelligence in AI Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
6a2e01dfa5708795013bf97dce0351890b7ec891.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence increasingly engages emotional and social dimensions of human life, its ability to recognize and respond to emotion raises important ethical and philosophical concerns. This chapter examines the development of emotional and social intelligence in AI, highlighting the shift from rational computation toward affective interaction. Drawing on cognitive psychology, affective computing, and moral philosophy, it explores whether machine empathy reflects genuine understanding or performative simulation. The discussion addresses risks such as emotional surveillance, manipulation, dependency, and cultural misrecognition, while acknowledging benefits of emotionally responsive AI in education, healthcare, and assistive contexts. To address ethical gaps, the chapter proposes a Computational Compassion Framework (CCF) integrating moral intentionality, transparency, human oversight, and contextual sensitivity into AI design. It argues that the future of emotional AI lies not in humanizing machines, but in embedding ethical responsibility within technological systems.</jats:p>

title: Attention, Obligation, and the Rootedness of Human Identity in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
e4417ce1339c12cc05dc70011ea7ae674c983fe8.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how the AI renaissance is reconfiguring fundamental anthropological conditions of human existence and how Simone Weil's ethics of attention, obligation, and rootedness can provide a normative framework for understanding these transformations. Methodologically, the analysis combines conceptual reconstruction, philosophical-hermeneutic updating, and critically reflected conceptual engineering to translate Weil's categories into contemporary AI contexts. The analysis identifies three interconnected transformations: AI-mediated environments can reshape the conditions for sustained attention; distributed human-machine agency can create responsibility and obligation gaps; and digital infrastructures can weaken the conditions for social, economic, and political rootedness. The chapter develops a Weilian governance framework that deepens human-centered AI by identifying the anthropological conditions that underlie rights, human oversight, accountability, and participation.</jats:p>

title: Human Rights in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
b6cc6cdaede90b65d88551af1e19e431b12e7088.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is an innovation that is fast changing society, economy, and government structures. Although it is extremely advantageous, it also triggers the issue of human rights, fairness, and accountability. This chapter focuses on the discussion of the manner in which human rights will be protected in the ascendancy of AI. It raises the red flag over perilous algorithms, the absence of transparency and surveillance technologies proliferation. Legal frameworks and considerations that can be used to steer innovation towards dignity, equality, and justice are also addressed. Healthcare, employment, policing case studies gives an example of how AI affects the basic freedom. The chapter proposes a right based regulation of AI, stating that innovation should be moderated and should not harm people and society. It concludes with the policy suggestions that can make AI advocacy to social justice and maintain human freedoms.</jats:p>

title: Construction and Case Study of a Quality Evaluation Model for Intelligent Information Systems in a Generative Artificial Intelligence Environment: The Case of Bilibili
container-title: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
c7d63252644539de3df39bb8cce6761d736c89be.abstract: <jats:p>After generative artificial intelligence (AI) was embedded in search, content generation, and user interaction, traditional information system quality evaluation faced new boundaries. Based on the DeLone and McLean (D&M) Information Systems Success Model, this study adopts literature research and a single-case study, takes Bilibili as the case, and constructs and applies a six-dimensional evaluation framework based on public materials, observations of platform functions, and publicly available user feedback. The findings show that system quality, information quality, and service quality can still explain basic platform operation, information output, and service support, but they cannot fully cover AI’s semantic understanding and task completion, the trustworthiness of generated results, and continuous human-computer interaction. Therefore, this study introduces AI intelligence quality, trustworthiness quality, and interaction quality on the basis of the three traditional dimensions and clarifies the boundary of each dimension. The Bilibili case shows that the framework can identify both basic capabilities and AI-specific quality, thereby helping to avoid conflating technical performance, content quality, intelligent capability, and trust issues. The study provides a structured analytical framework for evaluating the quality of intelligent information systems in a generative AI environment and a reference for platforms to optimize AI functions and governance mechanisms.</jats:p>

title: Exploration of the mechanism by which quorum sensing signals AI-2 and AIP enhance ethanol tolerance of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei 5
container-title: Food Science and Human Wellness
dcc785851cee11e3f907af2e094a4b78d8d567f7.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lacticaseibacillus paracasei (L. paracasei) plays an indispensable role in food fermentation and probiotic formulations. Nonetheless, its industrial utilization is frequently limited by its low tolerance to ethanol. Given that biofilm formation constitutes a critical survival mechanism for bacteria under stress conditions, this study sought to examine the impact of exogenous autoinducer-2 (AI-2) and autoinducing peptides (AIP) on the biofilm formation of L. paracasei in the presence of ethanol stress. The findings revealed that both AI-2 and AIP substantially enhanced biofilm formation, increased membrane fluidity, and augmented exopolysaccharide (EPS) production under ethanol stress conditions. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed distinct regulatory mechanisms: AI-2 primarily upregulated genes encoding ABC transporters (e.g., potABCD, phnCDE, oppABCDF), which support ATP-driven uptake of compounds essential for cellular homeostasis under ethanol stress. In contrast, AIP mainly activated genes involved in the phosphotransferase system (PTS) (e.g., BglF, MtlA, CelB, CelC), facilitating carbohydrate uptake and central carbon metabolism to meet the biosynthetic demands of EPS and biofilm matrix assembly. This work would provide important insights into the stress adaptation mechanisms mediated by quorum sensing (QS) in L. paracasei 5.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Green AI-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Improved Industrial Metal Surface Defect Detection
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS  COMMUNICATIONS & CONTROL
7cb4bdcba33492ba6826438a8e4421a4967bef1a.abstract:
<jats:p>Defect detection of industrial metal surfaces is often limited by the scarcity of annotated data and the high cost of manual labeling, which limits the performance of data-driven inspection systems. This paper presents a Green AI-driven framework for synthetic data generation that efficiently augments industrial defect datasets while minimizing computational and annotation costs. The proposed approach employs a deterministic procedural pipeline to generate synthetic defect images together with aligned segmentation masks at the pixel-level, providing accurate supervision without the computational overhead of deep generative models. The framework is evaluated on the Kolektor Surface-Defect Dataset 2 (KSDD2), which is extended into a hybrid dataset through synthetic augmentation followed by human-in-the-loop validation, to ensure the realism and reliability of the generated samples and annotations. A lightweight state-of-the-art anomaly detection model, SuperSimpleNet, is trained under controlled ablation settings on both the original and hybrid datasets using identical test splits for fair comparison.
Performance is evaluated using both image-level and pixel-level metrics, including AUROC and average precision. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid dataset consistently improves defect detection and localization performance while substantially reducing the need for costly data acquisition and manual annotation. Unlike computationally intensive generative approaches based on GANs or diffusion models, the proposed procedural framework synthesizes defects directly within predefined regions, enabling automatic generation of pixel-accurate ground-truth annotations without human intervention. The resulting hybrid dataset improves all evaluation metrics, achieving the largest gain in anomaly localization performance, with AP-loc increasing by 5.3%, while image-level AUROC increases from 0.9840 to 0.9907. By combining efficient synthetic data generation with precise automatic annotation, the proposed approach provides a resource-efficient solution that aligns with Green AI principles.</jats:p>
