title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling and Molecular Evaluation of Centella asiatica Extract for Neuroprotection Against Experimental Cognitive Dysfunction
container-title: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
011f72f6c4b5850fec4e4c39ff3bf5c5724e5c50.abstract: <jats:p>The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. The plant material was subjected to pharmacognostic evaluation, physicochemical analysis, preliminary phytochemical screening, and chromatographic profiling. An ethanolic extract of C. asiatica was subsequently investigated in a scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction model in rats. Behavioral performance was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, while biochemical and molecular parameters associated with neuroprotection were evaluated. The extract showed characteristic pharmacognostic features, acceptable physicochemical parameters, and the presence of triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolics, saponins, and other secondary metabolites. Illustrative results showed that treatment with C. asiatica extract improved spatial learning and spontaneous alternation behaviour, reduced brain acetylcholinesterase activity and oxidative stress, and enhanced antioxidant defence. Molecular evaluation indicated improvement in BDNF expression together with attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings suggest that standardized C. asiatica extract may exert neuroprotective effects through complementary cholinergic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic mechanisms.</jats:p>

title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics
container-title: Cognitive Neurodynamics
06090e0d49c5226d4872ceacfa8c8d6d2e0b71d2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber–Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron’s centrality—quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure—we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting. Remarkably, centrality determines the nature of the synchronized attractor: motifs in which the tonic neuron has low centrality synchronize into tonic spiking, whereas highly central tonic neurons drive the network toward synchronized bursting. Moreover, the networks exhibit nontrivial collective behaviors, including large-ISI “stairway-to-heaven” structures, partial firing death characterized by the coexistence of spiking and subthreshold neurons, and remote synchronization in the star configuration with the tonic neuron at the hub. While the present study focuses on the Huber–Braun model in four-neuron motifs, excitability and electrical coupling are features shared by many conductance-based neuronal models. This motivates the hypothesis that analogous structure–dynamics relationships may also arise in other neuronal models and small network motifs, highlighting the potential role of local structural control in shaping collective neural rhythms.</jats:p>

title: From Diagnosis by Accumulation to Diagnosis by Layers: Cognitive Psychiatry and Iatrogenic Risk in an Adolescent with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Case Report and Narrative Review
container-title: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
64b593cb9865a450df79cb5a14e983d428eb6e0d.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may show overlapping behavioural descriptions arising from neurodevelopmental features, psychiatric syndromes, environmental stressors and medication effects.
Objective: To illustrate a layered psychiatric formulation using the clinical course of an adolescent with ASD, self-harm, restrictive eating, atypical experiences and prolonged psychopharmacological exposure.
Methods: Clinical material supplied by the treating team was synthesised as a case report, with a complementary structured narrative review of literature on diagnostic overlap, pharmacotherapy, puberty, safety and feeding. The main PubMed/MEDLINE search covered January 2023 to September 2026, with a subsequent targeted update; evidence selection was purposive rather than systematic.
Case Presentation: A 16-year-old adolescent experienced school and adaptive difficulties, sensory sensitivities, food restriction with occasional self-induced vomiting, self-injury and suicidal ideation. Clinical records described sequential exposure to several psychotropic agents. A reduction in lithium dose from 450 to 300 mg/day during the September 2026 admission was followed by improvement in reported hygiene, food variety and family interaction, but later by distress and an urge to self-harm. Co-occurring psychotherapy, environmental changes and uncertain clinical measurements prevent causal attribution.
Discussion: The proposed eight-layer framework considers constitutional traits, temperament, neurodevelopment and cognition, psychodynamics, relationships and environment, superimposed syndromes, somatic factors and treatment effects. The concept is heuristic, not a validated diagnostic instrument. Feeding symptoms warrant assessment of sensory selectivity, body-image concerns, compensatory behaviours and nutritional consequences. Evidence associating adverse childhood experiences with neuroimaging measures in autistic samples is relevant context but does not substitute for individual assessment.
Conclusion: Longitudinal, risk-sensitive formulation may help identify competing explanations and measurable intervention targets. The clinical sequence does not establish that medication, family circumstances or any single intervention caused the observed outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Associations between cognitive reserve, glymphatic function and cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
c9c11c975e0f61b55daf14543da03e25f7117ac9.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the association between cognitive reserve (CR) and glymphatic function in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and to examine whether the relationship between CR and cognition is mediated by glymphatic function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>113 MCI individuals and 91 healthy controls (HC) were enrolled to assess the glymphatic function by using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), perivascular space (PVS) ratings, and choroid plexus volume (CPV). Cognitive reserve index questionnaire (CRIq) was employed to evaluate the comprehensive CR of participants in both groups. The glymphatic function was compared between the two groups and Spearman correlation analyses were performed among the CR, glymphatic function and cognition. Mediation analyses were further conducted to explore potential mediating effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The MCI group had significantly lower bilateral ALPS index and mean ALPS index than the HC group, while the bilateral CPV, basal ganglia (BG)-PVS and centrum semiovale (CS)-PVS scores were significantly higher in the MCI group than the HC group. After controlling for age and sex, bilateral and mean ALPS index were positively correlated with MoCA, MMSE, and VFT scores; mean ALPS index and left ALPS index were positively correlated with AVLT-immediately performance. BG-PVS was negatively correlated with MMSE and VFT scores, and right CPV was negatively correlated with VFT scores. Meanwhile, CRIq was positively correlated with bilateral and mean ALPS index, but was negatively correlated with BG-PVS, and mean ALPS partially mediated the association between CRIq and cognition in the MCI group.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Mild cognitive impairment individuals exhibit reduced glymphatic activity relative to HC. Comprehensive CR is associated with cognitive function in MCI, with the mean ALPS index statistically mediating a portion of the CR–cognition association.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:p>Spinal cord injury (SCI) often causes partial or complete sensory and motor loss, disrupting the afferent integration needed for accurate mental body representations (MBR, i.e., body awareness and visuospatial body map). MBR deficits compromise sensorimotor recovery and contribute to neuropathic pain in about 69% of adults with SCI. Medications for neuropathic pain are often ineffective and can cause adverse reactions. Our previous pilot clinical trial showed that Cognitive Multisensory Rehabilitation (CMR), a physical therapy that restores MBR, produced significant, lasting reductions in neuropathic pain, improved sensorimotor function, and enhanced brain function. Building on these results, we examined feasibility and whether 8 weeks of CMR or adaptive fitness (1) improves sensorimotor function and reduces pain; (2) increases sensorimotor- and MBR-related brain activity and connectivity in adults with SCI.</jats:p>

title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
2b5bbc241b06a03ff17faa558df753c72b75e4ac.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      CD62L
                      <jats:sup>low</jats:sup>
                      neutrophils and a reduced frequency of CXCR4
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      TREM-1
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      CCR2
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). This was accompanied by elevated soluble TNF receptor 1 (sTNFR1) and decreased sTNFR2 and CXCL12. In the TP2 cohort, PMN-MDSC levels were comparable between REC and PASC groups, alongside increased emergency granulopoiesis regulators IL-3 and IL-6. Multivariate regression revealed significant associations between PMN-MDSC signatures, granulopoiesis-related markers, NC scores, and cognitive test scores in either the TP1 or the TP2 cohort. These results represent cross-sectional observations in participants assessed within the respective post-infection intervals, rather than longitudinal evidence of persistence. The results show that dysregulated granulopoiesis and neutrophil maturation are present even at 18 and 36 months in PASC individuals, potentially associating with overall symptom severity and cognitive impairment.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Development and Validation of A Cost-effective Passive Avoidance Apparatus for Assessing Memory Impairments in Mice
container-title: Indian Journal of Animal Research
64797322e7d050c812518a49ac307812dddfa35a.abstract: <jats:p>Background: The passive avoidance (PA) test is commonly used to evaluate memory performance in rodents; however, the high cost of commercial apparatus limits its accessibility for neuroscience research. Methods: This study aimed to develop a cost-effective PA apparatus integrated with custom software for automated step-through latency measurement. To validate the system, a scopolamine-induced amnesia model was established using repeated regimens (1 mg/kg, i.p.) daily for six consecutive days. Result: A total apparatus development cost is approximately 450 USD, with the integrated software enabling heatmap visualizations of animal movement. During the retention trial, scopolamine-treated mice exhibited significantly shorter step-through latencies than saline-treated controls, indicating impaired memory retrieval. The automated measurements were consistent with manual timing, suggesting the accuracy and reliability of the apparatus. Histopathological analysis revealed marked cell loss in the hippocampus of scopolamine-treated mice, accompanied by reduced brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression. These findings confirmed successful induction of neurodegeneration and supported the memory deficits detected by the apparatus. Overall, the developed PA system offers a reliable and affordable platform for memory assessment in laboratory mice, particularly in resource-limited settings.</jats:p>

title: Comparison of ChatGPT-Generated Patient Information on Testicular Cancer Across Two Assessment Periods: Clinical Accuracy, Response Quality, and Citation Support
container-title: Urology Research and Practice
c93eb8feb9c99f0cdaf287bfd045672a3550f06c.abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: The aim of this study was to compare clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation characteristics of ChatGPT-generated testicular cancer information across 2 assessments 20 months apart.
Methods: Sixty-one patient-oriented questions derived from European Association of Urology (EAU) Patient Information were submitted to ChatGPT-4o in December 2024 and repeated unchanged using ChatGPT-5.6 Luna in August 2026. Two urologists independently assessed accuracy against contemporaneous EAU guidelines and rated quality using the Global Quality Score (GQS) and modified DISCERN (mDISCERN). Citation quantity, source quality, and source-to-claim support were evaluated. Only the first response was retained; repeated-generation variability was not assessed.
Results: Fully accurate responses were 86.9% (53/61) in 2024 and 93.4% (57/61) in 2026 (P = .125). Of 8 clinically relevant inaccuracies in 2024, 4 were corrected, 3 improved but remained misleading, and 1 persisted. GQS increased from 3.75 ± 0.77 to 4.82 ± 0.41 and mDISCERN from 30.37 ± 4.65 to 36.80 ± 1.93 (both P < .001). Citations per response decreased from 5.97 ± 3.53 to 4.79 ± 1.19 (P = .042), while high-quality unique sources increased from 77.4% to 96.9% (P < .001). Fully supported sources were 80.1% and 86.4% (P = .050); 6 sources (2.6%) in 2026 did not support the claims.
Conclusion: Response quality and the use of high-quality sources were greater in 2026, whereas changes in clinical accuracy and source-to-claim support were less clear. Clinically meaningful errors persisted in guideline-sensitive topics. Because different model versions and interfaces were assessed, the findings represent model- and interface-specific snapshots, not a controlled head-to-head comparison.
Cite this article as: Ekenci BY, Altan M. Comparison of ChatGPT-generated patient information on testicular cancer across two assessment periods: Clinical accuracy, response quality, and citation support. Urol Res Pract. 2026;52, doi: 10.5152/ tud.2026.26067</jats:p>

title: Digital Technology Use, Cognitive Engagement and Perceived Learning Effectiveness Among Adult Learners in Non-Formal Education in Uzbekistan
8ceeae83917828c5b1e08cdb8fa3ca811cbe8ee6.abstract: Although digital technologies are increasingly embedded in adult education policy, evidence from post-Soviet Central Asia remains scarce. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined how digital technology use relates to two proximal indicators of learning processes – cognitive engagement and perceived learning effectiveness – among adults in non-formal education programmes in Uzbekistan. Survey data from 312 learners nested in 26 programmes across three provinces were analysed with two-level random-intercept models, followed by semi-structured interviews with 22 learners and two facilitators, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. After adjustment for age, gender, educational attainment, urban–rural location and programme type, digital technology use was positively associated with cognitive engagement (β = .38, 95% CI [.27, .49]) and perceived learning effectiveness (β = .35, 95% CI [.24, .46]). Between 17% and 18% of the variance in each outcome lay at the programme level. Four qualitative themes – socially produced digital self-efficacy, peer-mediated learning, institutional culture and structural barriers – helped to explain these patterns. Interpreted through self-directed learning theory and the capability approach, the findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends on the social and institutional conditions in which adults use them. The cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report preclude causal inference.

title: Practical Bedside Tests for Assessing Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction (POCD) in Anesthetized Patients
container-title: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand
e86136c3ac2f46b0b3b08a72d66be50e2049d437.abstract:
<jats:p>Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD)—characterized by deficits in memory, executive function, and processing speed—is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized complication of surgery and anesthesia. POCD is associated with protracted recovery, diminished quality of life, and adverse long-term outcomes, particularly among elderly and high-risk populations. While early detection via bedside cognitive tests is vital for optimizing postoperative care, more comprehensive gold-standard neuropsychological batteries remain largely unfeasible in routine clinical practice due to significant time, cost, and resource constraints.
This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of practical bedside cognitive assessments for identifying POCD. Commonly employed tools—including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test (TMT), Digit Span, Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Abbreviated Mental Test Score (AMTS)—are critically appraised regarding their sensitivity, limitations, and suitability for the perioperative environment. The review specifically addresses feasibility in acute postoperative settings, accounting for confounding factors such as age, literacy, and sensory or motor impairments. Furthermore, the necessity of establishing baseline cognitive status and the urgent need for tool validation within surgical cohorts are highlighted.
No single bedside instrument offers a sufficiently comprehensive assessment for POCD. Rather, a multimodal approach—integrating high-sensitivity tools like the MoCA or TMT with rapid screening instruments—represents a more robust and clinically viable strategy for early detection. Future research must focus on standardizing assessment protocols and validating these tools across diverse surgical populations to ultimately enhance the quality of postoperative cognitive care.</jats:p>

title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
b447a82291c817794bca34b6c506bac2ac66c2cb.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From Pre-Bolshevik Baku to the Post-Soviet Camp:  Emigree Post-memory in the Works of Banine and Gunel Movlud
ბოლშევიკებამდელი ბაქოდან პოსტსაბჭოთა ბანაკამდე: ემიგრანტული მეხსიერება ბანინესა და გიუნელ მოვლუდის შემოქმედებაში

890d876d7ae2c07c98267b9bc701a0001c20a99e.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper explores Azerbaijani émigré and refugee literature through the prism of memory, violence, and trauma. It focuses on two women writers separated by nearly a century: Ümül Banine (Baninee), who left Baku after 1920 following the collapse of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and settled in Paris, and Günel Mövlud, who fled her native Jabrayil in the 1990s as part of the displaced generation of the Karabakh war. These two figures frame two historical moments that mark, respectively, the beginning and the end of the Soviet era. Their literary works are examined through the lenses of collective and individual memory, trauma and post-trauma, pre- and post-bolshevik historical rupture, and the neurobiology of violence.
Alongside them, the paper briefly considers a third voice – Dilbar Axund­zadə – whose memoir of life with the repressed poet Mikayıl Müşfiq reflects a different con­dition: not exile, but internal survival under Soviet repression. Although connec­ted to the same cultural space, these women represent distinct historical periods and modes of displacement, revealing how personal destinies are shaped, remembered, and narrated under radically different political regimes. While Banine’s narrative preserves an episode of internal displacement experienced by her mother in 1905, during the early phase of the Armenian–Azerbaijani conflict in Baku and other Azer­baijani territories, Mövlud’s narrative presents a different configuration of violence and memory: not cosmopolitan exile but internal displacement in the post-Soviet period.
Research methods:
Both individual and collective memory are selective and interpretive; they are never static but always reconstructive. Émigré and refugee literature foregrounds this process with particular clarity. Banine’s Days in the Caucasus transforms childhood upheaval into an ironic and reflective narrative, while Mövlud’s The Camp fragments refugee experience into intense sensory episodes – mirroring neurobiological re­search on trauma, which shows that violence imprints memory in sharpened yet dis­continuous traces. Stress hormones heighten certain recollections while disrupting nar­rative coherence, and adolescence, as a period of neural plasticity, renders such memories especially enduring.
Banine’s memoir reveals generational tensions within a multicultural household: her grandmother’s conservatism, her father’s cosmopolitan aspirations, and the coexistence of German, Russian, and English alongside Azerbaijani tradi­tions. Christmas trees stand next to Novruz celebrations, and a German governess introduces Christian rituals into a Muslim family home. At the same time, the text ex­poses darker layers of postmemory: the Armenian–Azerbaijani clashes of 1905 and 1918-1920 resurface in children’s “games” played with their half-Armenian friend Tamara. What adults leave unspoken, children reenact symbolically. As Marianne Hirsch defines it, postmemory transmits trauma to those who did not directly experience it but nonetheless inherit its emotional weight.
While Banine’s narrative preserves an episode of internal displacement ex­perienced by her mother in 1905, during the early phase of the Armenian–Azerbai­jani conflict in Baku and other Azerbaijani territories, Mövlud’s narrative presents a different configuration of violence and memory: not cosmopolitan exile but internal displacement in the post-Soviet period. Her camp narrative depicts weddings reduced to survival strategies, improvised libraries in cramped “kletka” rooms, and mosques built by foreign sponsors. Here, the rupture is not between generations but between two historical conditions – the stability of the Soviet past and the fragmentation of post-war displacement. Trauma becomes embodied: Mövlud describes a paralyzed girl repeatedly abused while others avert their gaze. This scene resonates with trau­ma theory’s “freeze response,” in which neither fight nor flight is possible and the bo­dy and psyche enter a state of paralysis.</jats:p>

title: ETALON: Verified Execution and Persistent Research Memory for Agentic Computer-Aided Drug Design
a1ef09a90238f52ae133f226f04cc5136b61674d.abstract: <jats:p>Language-model agents can coordinate computational drug discovery, but adapting a campaign to new evidence requires scientific software that supports flexible workflows, consistent modeling, and continuity across research sessions. Here we present ETALON, a harness that equips a general-purpose coding agent with an integrated environment for computer-aided drug design. Three independently usable systems supply its scientific operations: MolQuarry for chemical and biological evidence, MolCascade for molecular preparation, screening, and docking, and PRISM for molecular generation and physical modeling. Each exposes configurable procedures with explicit scientific requirements, so the host can revise its research strategy while retaining consistent preparation and evaluation practices. Operations registered with a common execution layer are checked before dispatch, and their outputs carry separate records of completion, verification, and admission, so that an incomplete computation is not recorded as an unfavorable molecular result. A persistent research graph links evidence, judgments, experiments, and results across sessions, and candidate method revisions are compared with frozen baselines under criteria declared in advance.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Computing at the Edge: Lag Analysis and Neural Network Forecasting for Fishery Landings in the Colombian Caribbean
16b4b0ed8f381dcf53065fa4831dbe408bb25394.abstract: <jats:p>Fishery-dependent indices in data-limited fisheries are short and incomplete, which raises the question of when adaptive learned models, including cognitively inspired ones deployed at the edge, are justified. We analysed monthly landings per unit effort (LPUE) of pink shrimp (Penaeus notialis) in the Gulf of Morrosquillo, Colombian Caribbean: 65.7% of values are missing and the longest continuous segment has 28 months. Naive, trend, autoregressive (AR), echo state network (ESN), LightGBM and LSTM models were compared in rolling-origin experiments with training-only preprocessing, and their cost was measured on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. One-step-ahead errors were 5.1–5.7 kg per trip for the trend, the AR(2) and the learned models, against 7.6 for persistence; no learned model showed a robust out-of-sample improvement over a linear trend or an AR(2). An exploratory model incorporating river flow at a data-selected lag achieved the lowest RMSE (4.2 kg per trip), but its improvement over the statistical baselines was not statistically conclusive and was not consistently reproduced when lag selection was restricted to the training data at each origin. Backcasting was worse than persistence. A fit took 8 ms (AR) to 3–9 s (LSTM); the double-precision ESN execution process showed the largest peak memory footprint (1.7–4.1 GB of 8 GB). The limit is the information in the series, not the platform; under these conditions a linear trend or an AR(2) is a sufficient reference.</jats:p>

title: When shorter lasts longer: Rapid induction of configural memory in Lymnaea stagnalis
container-title: Journal of Experimental Biology
033d5517cb4c35741a59d899f701233b11fcced4.abstract: <jats:p>Configural learning in the freshwater pond snail Lymnaea stagnalis is a well-established model for investigating higher-order associative learning. When snails simultaneously experience an appetitive food cue and predator cue, they form a configural association in which the food cue no longer elicits its normal feeding response but instead elicits a fear-associated suppression of feeding. The established conditioning procedure uses 45 min of simultaneous exposure to food and predator cue and produces a configural memory expressed 3 h after conditioning but not 24 h later. Here, we report the serendipitous discovery of a substantially shorter conditioning procedure that produces a more persistent memory. During experiments using carrot slurry (food cue) and crayfish effluent (predatory cue), individual snails were simultaneously exposed to the two cues for only 7 min. Unexpectedly, animals conditioned using this procedure showed suppressed feeding not only 3 h later but also at 24 h, demonstrating long-term configural memory. We therefore characterized the specificity and robustness of the 7-min procedure. Exposure to carrot slurry or crayfish effluent alone did not produce the persistent change in carrot-evoked feeding, demonstrating that the effect required the combined presentation of both cues. We also tested this using fish-conditioned water and shell clipping, which mimics predator attack and gave rise to the same results. Thus, a rapid 7-min conditioning procedure reliably induces long-term configural memory across chemically and physically distinct forms of predator-risk information. These findings establish a rapid and broadly applicable procedure for inducing long-term configural memory in L. stagnalis.</jats:p>

f1cb21a987aaeb2b6deed5283b42f7a1f7b161dc.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes an adaptive robust fading memory filter (ARFMKF) to accurately track impulsively maneuvering spacecraft under heavy-tailed measurement noise. The ARFMKF is capable of simultaneously suppressing the adverse effects of measurement outliers, heavy-tailed measurement noise, and impulsive maneuvers. First, the Huber robust M-estimation methodology is investigated to mitigate the influence of measurement outliers and heavy-tailed measurement noise, enhancing the filter’s robustness to measurement model uncertainties. Then, an adaptive fading factor is incorporated to improve the maneuver detection sensitivity of the proposed filter and is used as a weighting coefficient for covariance inflation to compensate for the dynamics model errors caused by impulsive maneuvers. In addition, a discrimination index is designed to effectively distinguish impulsive maneuvers from measurement outliers, ensuring appropriate covariance inflation in the presence of maneuvers. Simulations show that the proposed ARFMKF outperforms the comparison filters in terms of maneuver detection sensitivity, discrimination capability, and overall tracking performance, particularly in scenarios involving multiple impulsive maneuvers and frequent measurement outliers.</jats:p>

title: Does it matter if agentic AI is an author? effort and Nigerian Copyright Law
container-title: The Journal of World Intellectual Property
e91841117471418443cd0df1711f16c39758b7d8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Agentic AI complicates copyright by unsettling the basis on which authorship is attributed, particularly where effort bears on originality and protection. This article asks what makes effort legally authorial, examining Nigerian copyright law, whose originality threshold requires effort to give a work original character, alongside comparative doctrine. That formulation reflects a common‐law tradition attentive to labour, skill and judgment, distinct from the European emphasis on the author's own intellectual creation and free and creative choices. The article argues that neither the quantity of labour involved in production nor the operational agency attributed to an AI system establishes authorship by itself. What matters is the relation between the claimed effort and the determination of copyright‐relevant expression. This difficulty is especially apparent where systems generate music with limited human intervention. Agentic production thus exposes a broader problem of legal attribution. Copyright may continue to seek an author even where production no longer coheres around one. The article describes the unsettled condition surrounding this shift as nescience, arguing that it counsels legal restraint rather than inaction. Where no qualifying human authorial contribution to the resulting expression can be established, copyright protection should be withheld, leaving fully AI‐generated expression in the public domain.</jats:p>

title: Former versus current smoking among older adults living with Alzheimer's disease, related dementias, and cognitive impairment
container-title: Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease
e74c6c985074e65f48c1666ddc9c3e2c6cb93529.abstract: <jats:p>Smoking is a major modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD), yet smoking status among older adults with ADRD or cognitive impairment, not dementia (CIND), remains poorly characterized. Using pooled 2010–2020 Health and Retirement Study data, we examined former versus current smoking among US adults aged ≥55 years with lifetime cigarette smoking. In weighted analyses of 13,595 participants, adults with CIND (AOR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74, 0.92) and ADRD (AOR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65, 0.99) had lower odds of former smoking than cognitively normal adults. Findings highlight the importance of understanding smoking cessation needs in cognitively impaired populations.</jats:p>

title: Metamemory-guided retrieval and memory revision for long-term conversational memory
789558e33fa80ea09af789aead659892ecca38d2.abstract: Relevant information in long-term conversations is often scattered across sessions. Even when a system finds evidence that supports its answer, it may omit other information needed to address the question. To address this problem, we propose a framework for metamemory-guided active retrieval and memory revision (MARR). The framework organizes historical conversations into a heterogeneous memory graph, connecting records across sessions through entities and topics while retaining original messages and temporal information for later inspection. When answering a question, the system checks whether the evidence is sufficient in light of what it has already answered and uses the actual retrieval trajectory to determine where to search next. Information obtained through supplementary retrieval informs revision proposals, which the Writer checks against the original text before deciding whether to accept them, reducing unsupported changes. Evaluations on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S show that the framework recovers some omitted evidence and improves question-answering performance. Further analysis finds that some answer errors can be corrected by reexamining material already available, while continued retrieval yields more pronounced benefits for multi-hop questions with incomplete evidence. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of long-term conversational memory depends both on finding relevant information and on the system's ability to understand and use it adequately.

title: Differences in Translators' Cognitive Load under Generative-AI Post-Editing: An Eye-Tracking Study of English-Chinese Scientific Texts
container-title: Future of Social Sciences
7793a603db2a8f408a2d3da40407434bb0b16b52.abstract: <jats:p>{'en': 'Generative artificial intelligence has entered the translation workflow faster than evidence about its effect on the translator has accumulated. This study asks whether working from a large language model draft lowers cognitive load or merely redistributes it. Thirty-six translators, twenty translation trainees and sixteen practising professionals, rendered nine English popular-science and technical passages into Chinese under three within-subject conditions. These were unaided human translation (HT), post-editing of a static neural machine translation draft (NMT-PE), and post-editing of a GPT-4o draft with an interactive prompt pane (GAI-PE). Pupil diameter change, fixation duration, gaze distribution, keystroke logs, NASA-TLX ratings and MQM scores were recorded. GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. These observations are consistent with an increased demand for verification, though the generative condition also gave access to an interactive prompt pane, so the differences cannot be attributed to the model alone.'}</jats:p>

title: Chicago: Myth, Memory, and Reform
container-title: Journal of Urban History
e6ae047f808d1d7524859f2c90c6e8c292268e42.abstract: <jats:p>This essay argues that Chicago’s exceptional status in American history stems from both its urban history and civic mythology. It explores how Chicago is an important case study for examining intertwined histories of labor, urban geography, and social reform and identifies opportunities for scholars to better integrate gender, age, and sexuality in the study of Chicago’s cultural landscape. This essay questions celebratory narratives of Chicago’s progressive reform movement by highlighting how the prohibitionist impulse of many urban reformers created political contradictions in the modern state.</jats:p>

title: Memory of Textile Crafts
container-title: FormAkademisk
e5e43fb8da57f05ea2df0bb189fd95e46ad20090.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents the development of and first experiences in teaching practice with ‘Memory of Textile Crafts’, a memory game-like learning game to facilitate discussion around textile techniques in (textile) design education. In the game, students are asked to collaboratively find matches of four technique cards representing one of seven specific textile techniques and to further discuss the techniques through general construction logics, qualities and contexts. The learning game is introduced in different contexts, whereof two cases from teaching are described and discussed here. Here we see its agility to combine with exercises and integrate it in teaching to address different cognitive levels of learning. Furthermore, the article proposes a Compass of Textile Logics to frame textile techniques as transformations between levels and logics.</jats:p>

title: Epithelial inflammatory memory in ulcerative colitis: molecular mechanisms and translational implications
container-title: Frontiers in Immunology
e6c1b37c70eb2c5bb9d9f470ef95108f634b4fc9.abstract: <jats:p>Ulcerative colitis (UC) can relapse after clinical and endoscopic remission, raising the question of whether previously inflamed epithelium retains altered responsiveness. Patient-derived colonic organoids and lineage-resolved colitis models show that inflammation-associated chromatin accessibility can persist after removal of the original environment and influence subsequent epithelial behavior. Basal inflammatory transcription, however, can return toward normal during organoid expansion. These observations distinguish ongoing inflammatory output from latent regulatory competence; transcriptomic normalization alone neither establishes nor excludes functional memory. Differences between paired colonic regions and persistence across molecular layers support spatial and molecular heterogeneity. Exposure history, treatment, and patient characteristics are plausible modifiers whose independent contributions remain unresolved. This Review focuses on the evidence for epithelial inflammatory memory in UC and its implications for regeneration and mucosal healing. We examine how stem and regenerative lineages could retain prior experience, with emphasis on enhancer accessibility and the supporting evidence for histone, DNA-methylation, and metabolic mechanisms. Persistent epithelial states are distinguished from continued niche stimulation, reversible adaptation, fixed injury, and somatic clonal selection. Altered recall can accelerate repair while coexisting with deficient differentiation, barrier function, or regenerative reserve, making functional recovery more informative than inflammatory output alone. Translational opportunities include targeted biopsy assays linked to organoid recall, longitudinal sampling during remission, and interventions that restore mature epithelial function. Stepwise assay validation and treatment testing could connect these mechanisms to clinical outcomes, although no epithelial memory assay or memory-directed therapy is currently validated for routine UC care.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive and Computational Mechanisms of Multi-Agent Task Allocation in Digital Environments
container-title: Zamonaviy dunyoda ilm-fan va texnologiya, Vol. 5, No. 32 (2026)
a4977d530dd3c977736917d4c95b2d2167e0f6cc.abstract: <jats:p>Digital environments transform multi-agent task allocation in terms of computational load, utility optimization, and allocation of attention. Based on distributed systems theory and reinforcement learning, this study will combine empirical evidence in artificial intelligence, software engineering, and information systems studies to determine the impact of digital stimuli (prompt complexity, resource constraints, and algorithmic task routing) on agent cognition and neural-inspired valuation processes. The paper constructs a conceptual Multi-Agent Task Allocation Model (MATAM) based on bounded rationality and multi-agent reinforcement learning theories using secondary data synthesis. The effects of computational overload, the activation of reward circuitry, and dynamic personalization in multi-agent environments are summarized in three integrative tables of documented empirical evidence. The results indicate that online agent frameworks reinforce decentralized processing, reward optimization, and dynamically restructure preference formation. The paper enriches software engineering theory because it incorporates computational and cognitive-inspired processes in adaptive multi-agent systems.</jats:p>

title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: Brain Sciences
da193c91691df6e6a71c2550f7730fd91e939587.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = −0.389, 95% CI −0.773 to −0.005), inattention (g = −0.415, 95% CI −0.749 to −0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = −0.366, 95% CI −0.658 to −0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.</jats:p>

title: Visual search as a cognitive marker to discriminate progressive supranuclear palsy from Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Brain Communications
fb0b2ca40289de871a2b5bcf1b1dc0020f6521ff.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Early and accurate diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is a high priority for both patients and clinicians. Nearly half of individuals with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy are initially given an alternative diagnosis—most commonly Parkinson’s disease—and the correct diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is delayed by an average of three years compared with Parkinson’s disease. Problems with cognition arise early in the progression of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, including profoundly disturbed visual search. This search deficit is likely caused by a combination of oculomotor, visuospatial, attentional and executive dysfunction, which is not observed in Parkinson’s. Since assessment of visual search is not routinely included in clinical testing for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, it may represent a promising method for differentiating these movement disorders. However, few studies have systematically compared visual search in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Parkinson’s disease, so the extent to which search deficits can reliably differentiate the two diseases is unknown.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To address this issue, patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (N = 28), Parkinson’s disease (N=28) and age matched controls (N=27) completed four tests of visuospatial attention: an easy feature search task, a difficult feature search task, a conjunction search task and a paper-and-pencil cancellation task (the Bells test). We measured perceptual sensitivity (d prime), search time and detection accuracy. Search efficiency in the Bells test was also modelled using Quality of Search score. In addition, patients completed tests of oculomotor system integrity, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire 25.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>As predicted, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy was associated with a profound search deficit: search was slow and highly disorganised on all tests. Furthermore, reflexive orienting along the vertical axis was impaired on the easy feature search. Critically, Receiver Operator Characteristic analyses revealed that the Quality of Search score derived from the Bells test classified Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with a sensitivity of 82%, a specificity of 96%, and Area under the Curve of .90. Given the Bells test is fast to administer (∼5 mins), free, relatively simple to score and already widely used in neuropsychology assessment, it has the potential to be a highly effective addition to the battery of tests used in the differential diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy</jats:p>

title: Occupational Types, Working Hours, and Cognitive Trajectories
container-title: Work, Aging and Retirement
65536a8deef74fc867f672ab5b60911cfee63e16.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The relationship between work and cognitive function in later years has gained attention recently. However, information on occupational types, working hours, and cognitive function based on longitudinal cohort studies from developing countries remains limited. This study utilizes data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and employs group-based trajectory modeling to depict the heterogeneous changes in cognitive function over time among middle-aged and older adults and specifically examines the associations between occupational types (agricultural work, non-agricultural employment, non-agricultural self-employed or family business), working hours, and cognitive trajectories. Our findings indicate that agricultural work is associated with poorer cognitive trajectories compared to non-agricultural employment and non-agricultural self-employed or family business. Compared to individuals working 40 hours or less per week, those working 41–55 hours had a higher likelihood of experiencing a “rapid decline” cognitive trajectory. Furthermore, working over 55 hours per week was associated with an increased likelihood of belonging to both the “rapid decline” and “persistently moderate” trajectory groups. We did not observe a significant multiplicative interaction between occupational types and working hours on the cognitive trajectories. These results enhance our understanding of the relationship between work-related factors and cognitive function, providing a scientific basis for developing targeted intervention measures in the context of developing countries.</jats:p>

title: Programmer expertise classification using cognitive load and transfer learning
container-title: Discover Computing
fd7d35f3693ec5876c0a6c12b79c6a1d1736a370.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Context</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Evaluating a programmer’s performance by considering both technical and cognitive skills is indispensable in many software development tasks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Problem</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Technical skills are relatively easy to assess, whereas non-technical skills, such as long-term memory, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence, are often overlooked while measuring the performance of a programmer.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Aim</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The primary objective of this work is to propose a reliable framework for classifying programmers into five framework-derived proficiency ranks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Participants are given an assignment with both technical and non-technical questions. A cognitive load index that combines technical and non-technical skills is used to analyze performance and stratify it into five ranks. The proposed framework was evaluated using CatBoost and TabNet classifiers in a transfer-learning setup. It used the source dataset (Another researcher’s dataset) for pre-training and the proposed programmer dataset for fine-tuning. Extensive experiments, including confusion matrix analysis, 5-fold cross-validation, sensitivity analysis, and ablation studies, confirm the framework’s effectiveness and robustness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The fine-tuned CatBoost model outperformed the TabNet model, achieving an impressive 87% accuracy, a significant improvement over the pre-trained model’s 31%. The findings demonstrate that combining technical skills with non-technical aspects greatly enhances the accuracy of classifying programmer expertise. This offers a dependable method for assessing programmers in software engineering education. The study develops a robust framework for evaluating programming performance that incorporates both technical and non-technical skills, and it can be adapted for other cognitive and skill-based evaluations across different fields.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Immune Memory: Contradiction Filtering at Write Time for Long-Term LLM Agents
f5520afab274d96e48ccde3a1765dc4b8cada69b.abstract: <jats:p>Long-term memory for LLM agents, as implemented in systems such as MemGPT and Mem0, is optimized for retrieval and scaling but lacks a systematic mechanism for preventing the accumulation of contradictory statements at write time. We formulate the admission problem as separate from storage and retrieval and propose IMMUNE MEMORY, a lightweight layer orthogonal to any existing store. Analogous to innate immunity, which recognizes self/non-self patterns before an adaptive response is launched, the layer intercepts an incoming statement before commit and routes it into one of three categories: ADMIT, QUARANTINE, REJECT. The decision is based on a consistency signal computed against the current memory state and on external verification for sources not marked as trusted. The architecture requires no modification of the store and is compatible with MemGPT, Mem0, and graph backends. This is a position paper: we define the layer interface, a taxonomy of contradictions, a quarantine metadata schema, and a validation protocol on LoCoMo with controlled contradiction injection; the concrete implementation of the consistency signal and the judge prompt are left out of scope as engineering details.</jats:p>

title: Confronting deliberative failures after extremist attacks: Memory activism and democratic resilience
container-title: Political Studies Review
dde457d37674af1e02a95245a2d98aeefdcdec4b.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines the role of memory activism in the wake of far-right extremist violence and identifies the conditions under which it can strengthen democratic resilience. Combining insights from memory studies and deliberative democracy with an illustrative case of memory activism following the 2020 far-right attack in Hanau, Germany, the article identifies an overlooked democratic function of memory activism: exposing and addressing deliberative failures in the public sphere. It highlights four such failures – hegemonic listening, inattention to difference, epistemic injustice and tokenistic engagement – and shows how memory activists contest them through public acts of remembering while calling for a deeper, more inclusive democratic public sphere. It further argues that memory activists’ capacity to repair deliberative failures and contribute to democratic resilience depends on the institutional and cultural uptake of their claims and narratives across the broader public sphere.</jats:p>

title: Exploring the Relationships Between Auditory Processing, Language, Cognitive, and Speech-in-Noise Abilities in School-Aged Children
container-title: Ear & Hearing
9af30a4b81ce81a45b4858e624167bf0904d1cf3.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Understanding speech in noise and reverberation requires the integration of auditory, language, and cognitive abilities. Many children experience listening difficulties in such environments which, if persistent, can affect long-term academic outcomes. However, relative contributions of underlying processes remain poorly understood. This study investigated how nonspeech auditory processing, language and cognitive abilities contribute to phoneme identification and sentence understanding in noise in a representative sample of school-aged children.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study included 221 primary school children aged 6 to 11 yr (88 boys, 133 girls), all with normal peripheral hearing. Participants completed measures of nonspeech auditory processing, phoneme identification, and sentence understanding in noise and reverberation, as well as language ability, attention, nonverbal intelligence, and memory. Using structural equation modeling enabled us to consider the influence of multiple predictors simultaneously.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A complex pattern of relationships emerged. Bottom-up nonspeech auditory processing supported phoneme identification, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language ability had a direct top-down influence on sentence understanding. Memory and intelligence contributed indirectly through their influence on language. Minimal associations were observed between cognition and nonspeech auditory processing, supporting a conceptual distinction between auditory and higher-level processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that bottom-up and top-down abilities make distinct contributions to listening and identify direct and indirect pathways underlying children’s listening in adverse conditions. Auditory processing contributed to phoneme perception, which in turn supported sentence understanding in noise. Language abilities exerted a strong independent influence to sentence understanding in noise, while nonverbal intelligence and memory affected performance only indirectly through language.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Effects of Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation over the Left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex on Executive Function During Sustained Simulated Flight Operations: A Randomized Crossover Study Using a Flight–Cognitive Dual-Task Paradigm
container-title: Bioengineering
0d51663564d3f91f1ccc57c496c03743d27146d9.abstract: <jats:p>Sustained flight operation load may compromise executive control in complex human–machine interaction environments. Intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) holds potential for modulating executive function, yet its effects on different executive components under sustained operational load remain unclear. This study employed a randomized, balanced, within-subject crossover design, enrolling 25 healthy male participants. Each participant completed three intervention conditions: Active iTBS, Sham iTBS, and No-stimulation. Each experimental session consisted of stimulation delivery, a 60-min cruising simulated flight, and a 30-min flight–cognitive dual-task phase. Primary outcomes were behavioral performance on the Go/No-Go, 3-back, and number-rule switching tasks; EEG microstates and prefrontal relative oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) changes during the dual-task phase served as exploratory neurophysiological indices. Results showed that condition differences were concentrated in working memory updating and rule switching: compared with No-stimulation, Active iTBS shortened 3-back reaction time and reduced switch cost; compared with both No-stimulation and Sham iTBS, Active iTBS improved 3-back accuracy and number-rule switching accuracy; the switch-cost difference between Active and Sham iTBS did not reach significance (pBonferroni = 0.055). No significant condition effect was observed for the Go/No-Go task. EEG microstate analysis revealed task-specific changes: under the Active iTBS condition, the occurrence rate and temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the 3-back task; temporal coverage of microstate D increased during the number-rule switching task; no significant microstate changes were observed during the Go/No-Go task. Exploratory fNIRS analysis indicated that left-hemisphere and all-channel prefrontal HbO under Active iTBS was higher than under Sham iTBS in planned pairwise comparisons (pBonferroni < 0.03), but the corresponding condition main effects (p ≥ 0.065) and condition × hemisphere interaction (p = 0.919) were non-significant, and channel-level effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction. These findings suggest that, within the flight–cognitive dual-task paradigm, Active iTBS over the left DLPFC is associated with improvements in working memory and rule switching performance, accompanied by changes in microstate temporal organization during certain tasks. The microstate and fNIRS results provide exploratory neurophysiological observations and cannot establish causal relationships with the behavioral improvements.</jats:p>

title: A Verifiable Agentic Framework for Sequential Multimodal Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Progression
container-title: Bioengineering
6139e574fe257ad3d9cd5f4a73efa8d28c9688a8.abstract: <jats:p>Multimodal models can predict progression from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but most evaluations assume that every modality is immediately available. We developed a retrospective framework using only the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) that separates statistical risk estimation, sequential evidence acquisition, language-model explanation, and deterministic verification. Participants with baseline MCI were assigned state-specific landmarks using information visible within a +/−90-day window. The primary simulation cohort included 425 participants with clinical/cognitive, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) evidence; 153 converted to AD within 36 months after the landmark. Calibrated elastic-net models were evaluated with 10 repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. In the common-landmark cohort, adding MRI-derived and CSF features improved the Brier score from 0.158 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.141–0.175) to 0.138 (0.122–0.155) and the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 0.837 (0.802–0.871) to 0.878 (0.847–0.908). A sequential policy used cross-fitted estimates of individual Brier-score gain to decide whether to request MRI or CSF. The fixed-threshold exploratory analysis requested 40.6% fewer simulated tests than an all-tests policy while meeting the prespecified Brier and AUROC noninferiority margins. Under fully nested threshold selection, the policy requested 46.9% fewer tests and met the AUROC criterion, while narrowly missing the Brier criterion (difference 0.00546, 95% CI 0.00090–0.01003; margin +0.01). In a 40-card-per-model engineering audit, local Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B models copied probabilities and cited supplied evidence correctly in 40/40 cards but matched the deterministic action in 16/40 and 15/40 cards, respectively. Execution authority therefore remained with the deterministic policy. Here, agentic refers to the orchestration of modular evidence states, policy checks, verification, and explanation; it does not imply autonomous language-model control. As a retrospective simulation, the framework does not establish prospective clinical utility, real-world cost savings, or external computational reproducibility.</jats:p>

title: Electrophysiological Evidence of Cognitive Dysfunction After tSAH: An ERP Study Based on Three Different Stimulation Paradigms
container-title: Brain Sciences
8d238e46231e1ce5c166fe7d44664f6c6b11a4bb.abstract: <jats:p>Objectives: This study aims to investigate the characteristics of event-related potentials (ERP) in patients with traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (tSAH) during the clinical stable phase, with the aim of obtaining neuroelectrophysiological indicators that can objectively assess cognitive dysfunction caused by this injury. Methods: A total of 16 healthy volunteers and 33 tSAH patients in the stable phase were recruited. Demographic and clinical data were collected, MMSE assessments were completed, and EEG data for P300, mismatch negativity (MMN), and contingent negative variation (CNV) were recorded using a 32-lead ERP system. ERP analysis was performed by comparing the tSAH group with the healthy control (HC) group and by further dividing the tSAH group into a cognitive impairment subgroup (CI, n = 18) and a normal cognition subgroup (NC, n = 15) based on MMSE scores, with a focus on the mean amplitude and peak latency within specific time windows and their correlation with cognitive behavioral measures. Results: The results showed no significant differences in demographic characteristics between the two groups, while the MMSE scores of the tSAH group were significantly lower than those of the HC group. Compared with HC, the mean amplitude of P300 in response to the target stimuli was significantly reduced in multiple brain regions in the tSAH group and attenuated the negativity of mean CNV amplitudes across multiple brain regions, while no significant differences in mean MMN amplitudes were detected across electrodes and no significant differences were observed in peak latencies of P300 and MMN. The CI group was slightly older than the NC group; after controlling for the effect of age, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores of the CI group were significantly lower than those of the NC group, but no significant differences were found between the two groups in mean amplitudes and peak latencies of P300 and MMN or in mean CNV amplitudes. Conclusions: This study indicates that tSAH may be one of the relevant risk factors for post-traumatic cognitive dysfunction. ERP findings suggest that the allocation of relevant cognitive resources is attenuated in this population, but no differences were detected in the temporal sequence of neural processing. No significant abnormalities were observed during auditory deviance detection corresponding to the MMN time window, and no significant differences in ERP characteristics were found among the subgroups. This study found that tSAH can cause selective cognitive electrophysiological impairment, but ERP electrophysiological changes do not fully match cognitive impairment classified based on clinical scales.</jats:p>

title: From post-editing to prompting

df83e9cf6827c8467cf5e40f234bf447875f35ec.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study compares traditional translation and post-editing with generative-AI-assisted translation in Arabic–English translation education. Drawing on 68 task records completed by 58 undergraduate students through EduApp, it examines observable effort, textual intervention, and implications for translation competence. The findings indicate that AI-assisted tasks involved significantly more written or entered characters and a higher length ratio, but no statistically significant difference in task completion time. Qualitative analysis suggests a shift from local correction to broader reformulation, including more formal institutional phrasing and syntactic restructuring. The study concludes that AI-assisted translation redistributes rather than eliminates student effort and requires evaluative and interactive skills alongside established translation abilities.</jats:p>

title: Stepped-Care Internet Cognitive Behaviour Therapy for Childhood and Adolescent Anxiety: Parent Perspectives
container-title: Clinical Child Psychology and Psychiatry
92ec3cbd09a5da6393ce0202a35a4aa802e8a51b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By exploring parental views, we can better understand how stepped-care models with internet cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) interventions are experienced by young people and their families. A qualitative approach was used to understand parents’ perceptions of the acceptability and appropriateness of a stepped-care ICBT intervention. Specifically, what elements were effective, what barriers existed and how treatment expectations could inform adjustments to enhance overall outcomes for young people.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty parents of children and adolescents (aged 9-16 years) who completed the BRAVE Stepped-Care randomised controlled trials for anxiety participated in semi-structured interviews informed by Proctor et al.’s implementation science framework. Data were analysed using deductive reflexive thematic analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Four overarching themes were identified, (1) comfort with stepped-care approach, (2) desire for support that feels personalised, (3) parental involvement perceived as helpful and (4) importance of family flexibility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The self-directed component of ICBT was well received, particularly with parental involvement. Parents valued personalised support, especially via videoconferencing, and the flexible stepped-care ICBT approach suited busy family schedules. Finding suggest that stepped-care ICBT can be effectively implemented in routine care when parental engagement and flexible, personalised support are prioritised, potentially improving adherence, outcomes and scalability.</jats:p>

title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults
container-title: JAMA Neurology
58dc5bdf70917b19fd999f920eeed4070a884131.abstract:
<jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-4">
                    <jats:title>Importance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-5">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-6">
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-7">
                    <jats:title>Exposure</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-8">
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-9">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-noi260073-10">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Effects of mind-body exercise on cognitive function in patients with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
container-title: Aging Clinical and Experimental Research
1f4dc16d35f5a0b2c857d9e29b1101f23ddc7455.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This investigation carried out a systematic review and network meta-analysis to assess how different forms of mind–body exercise influence overall cognitive performance in patients with MCI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic search was conducted across eight Chinese and English databases (up to April 2026). A frequency-based network meta-analysis was performed to estimate the standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals, with interventions ranked by SUCRA values.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 44 RCTs (3,189 patients with MCI) were included. The network meta-analysis showed that, for the MoCA outcome, Baduanjin, Tai Chi, Qigong, and dance were all significantly superior to the control group (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.05). For the MMSE outcome, all three exercise types except Qigong were significantly superior to the control group. SUCRA rankings indicated that Baduanjin ranked first for both the MoCA (91.6%) and MMSE (88.3%). Subgroup analyses suggested that Baduanjin was most effective for short-term (≤ 12 weeks), high-frequency (> 3 times/week), or short-duration (< 60 min) interventions, while Tai Chi was more effective for long-term (> 12 weeks), low-frequency (≤ 3 times/week), or long-duration (≥ 60 min) interventions. The sensitivity analysis results were robust, and the risk of publication bias was low; however, the certainty of the evidence was generally low.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Baduanjin, Tai Chi, dance, and Qigong may be beneficial for global cognition in individuals with MCI. Baduanjin ranked highest in the SUCRA analysis. Tai Chi showed a potential advantage in longer-duration interventions. Given the low certainty of evidence and reliance on indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Generative AI dependency and perceived learning outcomes among university students: an indirect association involving effort regulation
