<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into university learning, raising questions about dependency-oriented reliance and self-regulation. Drawing on a self-regulated learning perspective, this study examined associations among GenAI dependency, effort regulation, and multidimensional perceived learning outcomes, including the statistical indirect association involving effort regulation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 982 students at three higher education institutions in Guangdong Province, China. Confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modeling were conducted, with indirect associations tested using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for GenAI use frequency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The measurement model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.953, TLI = 0.944, RMSEA = 0.043, SRMR = 0.041). GenAI dependency showed a small negative total association with perceived learning outcomes (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = −0.087) and was negatively associated with effort regulation (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = −0.257). Effort regulation was positively associated with perceived learning outcomes (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.497). The residual direct association was nonsignificant (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.041), whereas the indirect association was negative and significant (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = −0.128). After adjustment for GenAI use frequency, the indirect association remained significant, but the small total association was no longer significant.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight effort regulation as a relevant learner-controlled process in the association between GenAI dependency and perceived learning outcomes. title: Quantum Chemical Calculations, Molecular Docking, ADMET and Unveiling Therapeutic Potential of Marine Alkaloid Petrosamine: Shows Promise for Anxiolytic, Anticonvulsant, and Memory-Preserving Effects in Zebrafish Model
eaac7a4347b01e5d69e73d96089756655bff576e.abstract: Research into natural products of marine origin has experienced a rapid advance during the 21st century due to the discovery of the various pharmacological potentialities reported in the literature of exclusively marine bioactives with mechanisms of action involving important biological activities found in various species of marine organisms. The pyridoacridine alkaloid petrosamine, extracted from species of sea sponges of the genus Petrosia sp ., which occur on the coast of the state of Ceará, is a natural marine compound with experimentally proven neuroprotective pharmacological properties. The aim of this article is to evaluate the anxiolytic, sedative, anticonvulsant and memory-preventing effects of the marine alkaloid extract petrosamine in adult zebrafish . Thus, the findings confirm the pharmacological potential of petrosamine as an anxiolytic and memory-suppressing agent, supporting its investigation in new therapeutic strategies. Moreover, petrosamine exhibits intermediate chemical reactivity, characterized by a moderate HOMO–LUMO energy gap and high electrophilicity. The MEP and Fukui function analyses consistently highlight the cationic nitrogen atoms as electrophilic centers, while the oxygen and bromine atoms represent the main nucleophilic regions. Petrosamine had a sedative and anxiolytic effect and prevented memory in adult zebrafish via GABAergic neurotransmission. The studies evaluated indicate that compounds of marine origin are emerging as a promising source of bioactive compounds, revealing an important therapeutic potential for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Context makes the difference: Temporally Resolved Dopaminergic Teaching Signals Shape Associative Memory in Drosophila Larvae
98d88bf3f09266b996b7f00b82eb8ccbf0244ab4.abstract: <jats:p>Animals can adapt their behavioral responses to environmental cues by learning from experience. This ability relies on the formation and recall of memories that are shaped by beneficial or detrimental consequences and regulated by the dopaminergic system, which is highly conserved across insect species. In the Drosophila melanogaster larva, eight of total ∼120 dopaminergic neurons (DANs) innervate the mushroom body (MB), a key center for associative memory. This subset of DANs can be anatomically grouped into two clusters of four cells: the primary protocerebral anterior medial (pPAM) cluster, associated with reward signaling, and the dorsolateral 1 (DL1) cluster, associated with punishment. Such a functional dichotomy is observed in larval and adult Drosophila and reflects a fundamental organizational principle of reinforcement learning across invertebrate and even vertebrate species. Aversive reinforcement through high-salt exposure is encoded within the DL1 cluster in a combinatorial and heterogeneous manner, critically involving two neurons, DAN-f1 and DAN-g1. Using temporally precise optogenetic activation and inhibition during olfactory conditioning, we show that these neurons can modulate memory strength and valence. Their effects are most often consistent and predictable, enabling accurate computational modeling of DAN-driven teaching signals. By manipulating the intrinsic physiology of DAN-f1 and DAN-g1 and altering the valence of gustatory input, we are beginning to understand at the single-cell level how dopaminergic activity is systematically adjusted to control memory formation.</jats:p>

Beyond cognitive ability, investigating the symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways of emotional and spiritual intelligence on academic achievement in higher education
container-title: Discover Education
cdeb990ae16d2daa39339b50c528857e3da1acea.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Higher education is typically explained in terms of cognitive ability (IQ) when linked to academic achievement. However, despite evidence of non-cognitive intelligence, specifically emotional and spiritual intelligence, its association with academic achievement remains underexplored. In Ghana, where spiritual orientation is strong, research on the relationship between emotional and spiritual intelligence and academic achievement among higher education students remains limited. This study used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) and Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (FsQCA) to assess symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways. The study used a quantitative cross-sectional correlation design, drawing on data from 339 students across six colleges at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). PLS-SEM shows that emotional intelligence is significantly related to academic achievement (β = 0.344,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    < .001) and spiritual intelligence (β = 0.661,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    < .001). Spiritual intelligence is associated with academic achievement (β = 0.371,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    < .001). The model explains 43. 4% of the variance in academic achievement. The FsQCA results showed that a single configuration was consistently associated with high academic achievement. The combined presence of both high emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence had a consistency of 0.825 and a coverage of 0.766. Configurations in which one intelligence was high showed high consistency but low PRI consistency, so they were associated with both high and low achievement. The same findings appear in the robustness analysis. Therefore, emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence appear to relate to achievement conjecturally, as co-occurring resources rather than independent or compensatory routes. The findings call for Ghanaian evidence on the multidimensionality of intelligence and show the value of integrating PLS-SEM and FsQCA to inform educational research.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Resistively switching metal‐insulator‐meal (MIM) structures are a strong contender for universal memory technologies and neuromorphic computing applications. Their ability to combine non‐volatility with analogue tuneability enables in‐memory computing, where both data processing and storage occur in the same physical location. A period‐doubling bifurcation was observed in endurance tests of TiN/ Hf

                    Zr

                    /Au devices, where sequences of voltage pulses with constant amplitudes are supplied to the stack. Based on this, the memory cell's response to increasingly larger voltage pulses is measured. The extracted parameters are used to deduce a probabilistic non‐linear map describing endurance cycling of the MIM system. The investigation of the dynamics involves the identification of parameters that have been reported to be subject to change during continuous switching, and the investigation of how this drift affects the switching dynamics. The found model thus serves as a design framework to either deliberately develop systems exhibiting chaotic dynamics or circumvent them for classical memory applications.
                  </jats:p>

aa5bc1aadbb3845a6ccf6498a3e37b34b2054f88.abstract: <jats:p>Em 13 de janeiro de 2025, o Brasil sancionou a Lei nº 15.100, que proíbe o uso de aparelhos eletrônicos portáteis pessoais por estudantes durante aulas, recreio e intervalos em toda a educação básica, declarando como objetivo salvaguardar a saúde mental, física e psíquica de crianças e adolescentes. O artigo examina a natureza da evidência disponível sobre os três domínios de desenvolvimento invocados por essa premissa. A pesquisa foi conduzida na base Europe PMC, restrita a título e resumo, sobre registros indexados até 26 de setembro de 2026, com classificação de delineamento por tipo de publicação indexado. Foram identificados 4.934 registros que associam exposição a telas e infância. O domínio emocional reúne 931 registros, o cognitivo 792 e o comportamental 287. A assimetria entre delineamentos é acentuada e desigual entre os domínios: a razão entre estudos transversais e ensaios randomizados é de 5,5 para 1 no domínio cognitivo, de 17,5 para 1 no comportamental e de 20,2 para 1 no emocional, domínio que reúne apenas 13 ensaios randomizados em toda a literatura indexada. A participação dos ensaios randomizados caiu de 10,8% dos registros de 2015 para 2,4% em 2025, enquanto o volume anual quadruplicou. Conclui-se que a premissa legislada apoia-se em um corpo de evidência predominantemente observacional, escassez que decorre em parte de limitações éticas intrínsecas ao objeto.</jats:p>

title: Decision-Making Amid Information-Based Threats in Sociotechnical Systems: A Review
container-title: Journal of Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making
a4910b6e433c6a4809545ea8ec12b508486046ac.abstract: <jats:p>Technological systems increasingly mediate human information exchange, spanning interactions among humans as well as between humans and artificial agents. The unprecedented scale of, and reliance on, information disseminated through these systems substantially expand the scope of information-based influence that can both enable and undermine sound decision-making. Consequently, understanding and protecting decision-making today faces growing challenges, as individuals and organizations must navigate evolving opportunities and information-based threats across domains and information environments. While these risks are widely recognized, research remains fragmented: work evaluating information-based threat phenomena has progressed largely in isolation from foundational studies of human information processing. In this review, we synthesize insights from both domains to identify shared cognitive mechanisms that mediate vulnerability to information-based threats and shape behavioral outcomes. We then present a multilevel conceptual framework and outline directions for future research aimed at integrating these perspectives, emphasizing the importance of mitigating human vulnerabilities and aligning human-machine representations.</jats:p>

title: Disaster Exposure and Early Self-Reported Posttraumatic Growth: Indirect Associations Through Cognitive Emotion Regulation and Moderation by Dark Triad Traits
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
1d338d1ee595817516c6ab780e261be28e7fec07.abstract: <jats:p>Associations between disaster exposure and posttraumatic growth (PTG) are inconsistent, highlighting the potential relevance of cognitive processing and personality differences. This study surveyed 1498 individuals within one week of the July 2021 Henan floods to examine the associations among disaster exposure, early self-reported PTG, cognitive emotion regulation (CER), and Dark Triad traits. Disaster exposure showed a small positive association with PTG in the unadjusted model (b = 0.324, p < 0.001), which became nonsignificant after adjusting for gender, age, and current location (b = 0.146, p = 0.139). In the unadjusted parallel indirect-association model, disaster exposure showed positive indirect associations with PTG through both adaptive CER (estimate = 0.079, 95% CI [0.031, 0.144]) and maladaptive CER (estimate = 0.166, 95% CI [0.083, 0.256]), whereas the direct association was nonsignificant. After adjustment, only the indirect association through maladaptive CER remained distinguishable from zero. Dark Triad traits moderated several component associations, but only the conditional indirect association through adaptive CER differed across Dark Triad levels. Early perceived PTG was more closely associated with patterns of cognitive emotion regulation and personality differences than with disaster exposure severity alone. However, the cross-sectional design precludes temporal or causal interpretations, underscoring the need to distinguish early perceptions of growth from enduring psychological adaptation.</jats:p>

title: Postmemory After Deportation: Intergenerational Memory and Belonging Among Ahıska Turks in Türkiye and Kazakhstan
container-title: Genealogy
3f94a186e21b5e8ce0a6c663dfaa5f837c4f313b.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines how descendants of a deported community relate to a displacement they did not experience directly and how that inherited past acquires different meanings across settlement contexts. Focusing on Ahıska (Meskhetian) Turks in Türkiye and Kazakhstan, the study uses postmemory to examine intergenerational transmission and interpretation. The study draws on eleven semi-structured oral-history interviews conducted in Türkiye and Kazakhstan in 2024–2025, contextualized through published historical scholarship and documentary studies. The analysis considers narration, silence, selective uptake, material mediation, and commemorative performance as different forms through which descendants encounter the deportation past. Within this small comparative sample, accounts from Türkiye highlighted linguistic and cultural affinity and public commemoration, while accounts from Kazakhstan drew attention to local belonging, assistance received from Kazakh neighbors, and memories of historical injustice. Generational position influenced participants’ access to family memories, although direct conversations with older relatives, photographs, and commemorative events remained relevant across generations. The findings highlight how uneven family transmission, generational position, and individual circumstances shape descendants’ interpretations of the deportation past. They also show that attachment to Ahıska can coexist with a strong sense of belonging to the country of residence, without necessarily involving an intention to return to the ancestral homeland.</jats:p>

title: Whose House, Whose Decline? Property and Family Memory in Buddenbrooks and Cevdet Bey and His Sons
container-title: Genealogy
9a2636a0657b241668605374ca788ebb1c116497.abstract: <jats:p>Family novels are often read as if the fate of a house told the fate of a family, and a home’s sale or rebuilding becomes evidence of a lineage’s decline. This article is a comparative study of Thomas Mann’s Buddenbrooks and Orhan Pamuk’s Cevdet Bey ve Oğulları (Cevdet Bey and His Sons), two novels in which a house changes hands, and it asks what such readings leave out. Previous comparisons have read the two houses as signs of a single family fortune, a gap the article addresses. Combining close reading with Bourdieu’s account of the family as a collective body and a field of unequal interests, and with Hall’s approach to representation, it examines the house transactions, the domestic disputes that follow them, and the later narration of earlier ownership. In both novels the economic outcome of a transaction, the losses it imposes on particular members, and the way the house’s past is later told come apart. A buyer’s gain coexists with one member’s loss of security, a firm’s continuity with the end of a shared household, and a building’s survival with a family that no longer speaks of those who built and sold it. The article proposes a way of reading family narratives that keeps economic continuity, unequal losses, and the selective transmission of the past distinct.</jats:p>

title: Gastronomic Memory, Women’s Labor, and Social Solidarity in Mourning Meal Practices in Turkey
container-title: Genealogy
181e9ece7d6c1816def7d005c0b454735b4a0155.abstract: <jats:p>Death is a transitional period that, beyond marking the end of life, involves traditional practices aimed at alleviating and sharing grief. One such practice, found across cultures in varying forms, is the tradition of mourning meals. This study examines the multidimensional social significance of social solidarity, gastronomic memory, and women’s labor within mourning meal practices in Turkey. Using a qualitative design, participants were selected through convenience sampling, and data were collected via semi-structured interviews with 21 women from Turkey’s seven geographic regions, then analyzed thematically. The findings show that mourning meals are organized around a division of labor grounded in social and female solidarity, that this knowledge is preserved through intergenerational transmission, and that it is closely intertwined with gender roles. Olfactory and gustatory memory emerged as powerful elements of gastronomic memory that give concrete form to the experience of mourning, although traditional practices have undergone significant transformation in recent years, driven partly by migration and urbanization. Beyond a mere nutritional practice, mourning meals in Turkey objectify shared memory across different faith communities, carrying both common ritual patterns and regional variations, with women’s labor remaining an invisible yet central element. The study conceptualizes mourning meals as a multilayered domain reproducing social bonds and cultural memory.</jats:p>

title: Task-Specific Impacts of Cognitive Fatigue on Subjective Experience and Psychomotor Performance
container-title: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society

                    <jats:p>To determine how cognitive fatigue (CF) affects subjective experience and reaction time (RT) performance across tasks with different processing demands (simple, go/no-go, choice), and whether these effects depend on the type of fatigue-inducing mental work.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>CF is a psychobiological state of subjective exhaustion from mental effort that can compromise workplace productivity and safety. Although slowed RT is an often-observed consequence of CF, it is unclear how this compares across RT paradigms and fatigue-inducing tasks.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>Using a remotely administered experiment, 402 participants completed a 60-minute CF (Math-Memory, Stroop, Time Load Dual-Back) or control (documentary) intervention. Subjective ratings (mental fatigue, motivation) and RT performance (simple, go/no-go, choice) were assessed pre- and post-intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>

                      Relative to control, all CF tasks increased subjective fatigue (

                      ≤ .030) but not Math-Memory. Simple and choice RT slowed significantly following all CF interventions vs control (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                      < .010), with the greatest choice RT slowing after Stroop (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>

title: Cognitive Digital Ocean: integration of quantum hybrid computing, digital twins and graph neural networks for bioresource and fleet management. Part 2
container-title: Fisheries
8b6f0dac89f54a98d8d8f8c60f76f4ae8be52c66.abstract: <jats:p>The paper presents the concept of the Cognitive Digital Ocean (CDO) – a multi level cyber physical system for managing the fishery complex, integrating quantum hybrid computing, physics informed neural networks (PINN), graph neural networks (GNN), a hierarchy of digital twins (from genome to global ocean), and fractal analysis of the spatial distribution of bioresources. Special attention is paid to the shipbuilding aspect: mathematical models of the ship power plant (SPP), controllable pitch propeller (CPP), propulsion complex, and hull hydrodynamics are presented. It is shown that solving the fundamental Millennium Problem – the Navier Stokes equations – on quantum computers opens up fundamental possibilities for hydrodynamic forecasting with a horizon of up to 30 days. The system is aimed at solving the strategic tasks of the Russian Federal Agency for Fisheries (Rosrybolovstvo) until 2030: increasing production by 25%, digital transformation, and technological sovereignty. The limitations  of the applicability of quantum methods are considered and engineering workarounds are proposed.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of Spontaneous Affective Facial Responses for Cognitive Status Assessment in Older Adults: Exploratory Feasibility Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
97a7c39fc651c92b0504e2c164b26bd1dedf8810.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As Taiwan enters a super-aged society, the prevalence of dementia continues to rise, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches to identify behavioral alterations associated with cognitive decline. AI-based analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses has emerged as a potential digital phenotyping tool, but its feasibility for assessing cognitive performance remains underexplored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using AI-derived spontaneous affective facial response metrics, including affective expression congruency and onset latency, to characterize differences across cognitive performance levels in older adults with healthy cognition (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 60 participants (HC, MCI, and dementia; 20 per group) were presented with positive and negative emotion-eliciting videos and completed Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) recall and calculation tasks. Facial expressions were video-recorded and analyzed using a convolutional neural network–based AI system. AI-derived metrics included affective expression congruency, categorized as congruent, neutral, or incongruent according to the detected facial response, and affective expression onset latency, defined as the time from stimulus presentation to the emergence of a nonneutral facial expression detected by the AI model. Group differences were analyzed using 1-way ANOVA, Pearson chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise post hoc comparisons, analysis of covariance adjusting for age and education, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Affectively congruent responses were generally less frequent among participants with lower cognitive performance. During the 14-second positive stimulus, congruent positive expressions were observed in 65% (13/20) of HC participants, 20% (4/20) of MCI participants, and 0% (0/20) of participants with dementia. During the 48-second negative stimulus, congruent negative expressions were observed in 60% (12/20) of HC participants compared with 5% (1/20) of both MCI and dementia participants. Onset latency differed significantly across groups for the 14-second positive stimulus (F2,57=19.63; P<.001; η2=0.41), 52-second positive stimulus (F2,57=4.25; P=.02; η2=0.13), 48-second negative stimulus (F2,57=15.61; P<.001; η2=0.35), and MMSE-based cognitive-task condition (F2,57=11.28; P<.001; η2=0.28). After adjustment for age and education, the group effect remained significant for all latency outcomes (F2,55=3.89-10.68; all P≤.03; partial η2=0.12-0.28). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses showed stronger separation in several HC vs MCI and HC vs dementia comparisons, whereas MCI vs dementia comparisons showed limited separability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-assisted analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses revealed differences in expression congruency and onset latency across cognitive performance levels. These preliminary findings suggest that AI-derived facial behavioral metrics may serve as noninvasive adjunctive features for observational cognitive assessment. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design, modest sample size, and absence of internal or external validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Cognitive frailty typologies and subsequent dementia in a large representative sample of the English population
container-title: Communications Medicine
65cf5b194713c8347be2163e54ddea8ea8c988cb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cognitive Frailty (CF), the coexistence of mild cognitive impairment with physical frailty, may represent an intermediate state between functional vulnerability and preclinical dementia. Its potential reversibility makes it an important target for prevention. Distinguishing patterns of CF that are more and less likely to lead to dementia, and associated factors, is important for developing interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (Waves 4-9), we examined different typologies of CF based on specific cognitive impairments demonstrated. We compared longitudinal outcomes of incident dementia over 10 years for the different typologies. We also examined the impact of inequalities (Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) and household wealth), cognitive reserve (low education), and psychosocial factors (depression and loneliness) on the longitudinal models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CF groups with executive function (using verbal fluency) and/or processing speed impairment (Group 1) are distinguished from those with memory impairment only (Group 2) or impaired memory and executive function and/or processing speed (Group 3). Inequalities, cognitive reserve and psychosocial factors all show association with CF likelihood, but education (odds ratio (OR) of no qualifications compared to degree/higher education = 1.632 (Group 1) and 3.436 (Group 3)), IMD (OR 1.656 (Group 1 quintile 5), 2.083 (Group 3 quintile 4) compared to quintile 1) and loneliness (OR 1.208 (Group 1), 1.185 (Group 3)) are only associated with CF where executive function/processing speed are key characteristics. Longitudinally, only CF groupings with memory impairment (OR 2.024, Group 2; 2.733, Group 3) are predictive of dementia.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Distinguishing typologies of CF and associated risk factors is important for estimating future dementia risk, and for targeted design of interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship
container-title: PLOS One
6e96be301bf7c349635ce2ce01e377cb78f8053f.abstract: <jats:p>Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6–16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1 axis mediates hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment by driving hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis
5e8edb2dcfdf906f6247d2a606e5b799f1aa5f7e.abstract: High-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment severely compromises the physical and mental health of individuals who rapidly ascend to or reside long-term at high altitude; however, its initiating mechanisms, pathological cascades, and molecular regulatory network remain incompletely understood, leaving a paucity of effective therapeutic targets and preventive strategies. Using a mouse model of simulated 6000 m hypobaric hypoxia and a primary hippocampal neuron hypoxia model, we integrated behavioral testing, transmission electron microscopy, Seahorse metabolic analysis, transcriptomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation-coupled proteomics, structural prediction, pharmacological intervention, and clinical validation in human cohorts to systematically delineate the molecular mechanisms and core regulatory pathways underlying hypoxia-induced neuronal ferroptosis. Hypoxic exposure time-dependently impaired object recognition and spatial memory in mice and caused hippocampal neuron loss. Mechanistically, mitochondrial damage emerged as a critical initiating event during hypoxic stress, triggering mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release and subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Hypoxic hippocampal neurons exhibited canonical features of ferroptosis, including elevated Fe²⁺ and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, decreased GPX4 expression, and enhanced ACSL4 expression and increased mitochondrial C11-BODIPY oxidation. Pharmacological inhibition of STING with C-176 significantly alleviated these ferroptosis phenotypes, neuronal loss, and cognitive impairment. Co-immunoprecipitation combined with proteomics identified CISD1 (mitoNEET), a mitochondrial outer membrane protein, as a STING-interacting partner, and their binding was enhanced under hypoxia and localized to mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites. Moreover, the ferroptosis inhibitor Liproxstatin-1 rescued hypoxic cognitive impairment and partially restored mitochondrial morphology and respiratory function without reversing STING phosphorylation, indicating that ferroptosis functions downstream of STING and constitutes a feed-forward amplification loop by aggravating mitochondrial damage. In human cohorts, levels of serum iron and oxidative damage markers correlated positively with residential altitude. Collectively, these findings establish a self-amplifying pathological axis of mitochondrial damage-mtDNA-cGAS-STING-CISD1-ferroptosis, and targeting this axis may provide novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of high-altitude hypoxic cognitive impairment.

title: Clinically Meaningful Cognitive Improvement from Intermittent Neurostimulation of the Nucleus Basalis of Meynert in Parkinson’s Disease
1918570c1845246fb80422548bfaeeffd556cacd.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>
                  Cognitive decline begins in early stages of Parkinson’s disease (PD) for many individuals and remains largely untreated. The nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), the brain’s cortical cholinergic hub, and its lateral efferent fiber bundle degenerate early in PD and are linked to cognitive and cognitive-motor impairment. Pre-clinical evidence indicates intermittent stimulation of the NBM improves cognition. The objective of this study is to establish the feasibility of combined continuous subthalamic nucleus (STN) and intermittent NBM DBS for cognitive impairment in people with PD. Five patients with PD and cognitive impairment approved for STN DBS were enrolled as part of an ongoing clinical trial for combined STN and NBM DBS under an Investigational Device Exemption. Three participants received a ‘vertical’ trajectory in which two leads were placed in the STN, and two additional leads were placed in the anterior portion of the NBM, both using the same burr hole for each hemisphere. The two other participants received a novel ‘lateral trajectory’ in which the NBM leads were placed along the NBM lateral efferent bundle via a small twist craniostomy behind the ear. An automated programming algorithm DBS Illumina 3D™ (Boston Scientific) was used to program the NBM leads based on volume of tissue activated modeling. The investigational Chronos software (Boston Scientific) was used to deliver continuous high frequency DBS to the STN 24 hours/day and intermittent patterned DBS to the NBM for 1 hour/day. The two leads placed in the NBM (‘Vertical’ target) or its lateral efferent bundle (‘Lateral’ target) were successfully and accurately placed as part of the usual STN DBS procedure. All participants were successfully programmed using the Illumina 3D™ algorithm without adverse effects. Following 6 months of combined continuous STN and intermittent NBM DBS, all five participants saw clinically meaningful improvements in cognition as part of a neuropsychological assessment battery, as well as the expected motoric benefit from STN DBS. The current study demonstrated that intermittent stimulation of the NBM to target cortical cholinergic deficits may provide clinically meaningful improvements in cognitive symptoms in Parkinson’s disease.                   <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="clintrialgov" xlink:href="NCT05968703">NCT05968703</jats:ext-link>
                </jats:p>

title: Prompting Metacognition: Using Prompt Writing as a Language Task and Metacognitive Tool in ELT
container-title: Journal of English Language Teaching
76b3fd30466f48e1d4fc86aa24c4caf37205ad99.abstract: <jats:p>Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.</jats:p>

title: Designing and Evaluating a Clinical Decision Support System to Assess Mild Cognitive Impairment
container-title: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
f850297ff9b4f586b14a5cf4069025d30dc311b3.abstract: <jats:p>Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly used in clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to improve the interpretability and trustworthiness of machine learning (ML) predictions in healthcare. While prior work has examined how healthcare professionals (HCPs) interpret various explanation methods, limited research has investigated how these explanations function in systems that incorporate novel data sources like game-based digital biomarkers. This paper extends our previous work by presenting an improved, interactive web-based CDSS designed to support HCPs in assessing the risk of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). The system integrates ML predictions from gameplay data with data-centric, feature-importance, and counterfactual explanations to assist diagnosis and case-finding. We conducted a mixed-methods study with 51 HCPs to evaluate the system's understandability (objective and perceived), perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust. Participants gave consistently positive ratings across the self-reported perceived constructs, which were found to be strongly correlated. HCPs generally perceived the explanations as useful for clinical reasoning and reported that they understood and trusted the system, while acknowledging an initial learning curve. However, the evaluation of objective understanding was more mixed and correlated only weakly with the perceived constructs. In particular, participants encountered challenges in understanding game-based digital biomarkers, interpreting feature importances, combining local and global explanations, and understanding details of the underlying ML models. These findings highlight the importance of explanation designs that foster both positive user perceptions and accurate comprehension.</jats:p>

title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
22e034cadfc5369f2e260fba0d544b33f66ac832.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and (3) evaluate prognostic value for recovery of consciousness. Forty-eight healthy controls and 26 patients in MCS completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature mismatch negativity (MMN), passive and active oddball P300, the subject’s own name, semantic oddball, and sentence N400. Effects were classified using blinded expert visual scoring, region-of-interest ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding. Associations between binary ERP classifications and recovery were tested in 22 surviving patients at follow-up. In healthy controls, visual scoring identified MMN to at least one deviant and P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48 participants. Command following as demonstrated by task-related P300 enhancement between active and passive oddball conditions was detected in 81%. Command following was detected in 92% in the semantic oddball task. Sentence-congruity effects (N400 and/or P600) were identified in 69%, despite a strong group-level response, while the own-name effect was detected in only 35%. In patients, detection rates were lower: MMN was found in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted as positive; passive oddball P300 in 35% and active oddball P300 in 31%; sentence-congruity effects in 12%; active-versus-passive oddball modulation in 12%; and semantic oddball effects in 8%. Visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than ANOVA and cluster-based testing, and agreement varied substantially across paradigms. Binary ERP classifications were not significantly associated with recovery (14 recovered, eight did not), although prognostic analyses were limited by sample size. Group-level ERP effects overstated single-subject detectability in healthy controls, whereas the absence of group-level effects in MCS obscured reliable ERP responses resembling those of healthy controls in a few individual patients. In MCS, ERP effects associated with semantic processing and command following were generally uncommon, and binary ERP indicators did not predict recovery in this sample. Our findings establish a benchmark for selecting and refining ERP paradigms and detection methods to assess residual cognition after severe brain injury.</jats:p>

title: Shape Memory Alloy Sealing Gaskets for High-Pressure Flange Connections
container-title: Shape Memory and Superelasticity
4d318a01890f2ddac9d3bdebadc923bbbbffb298.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-pressure flanges are essential components for joining pipes, ensuring sealing, and preventing liquid and gas leakage. Gaskets play a critical role when subjected to high stresses, situation where they can cause irreversible deformations that, combined with fluctuations in mechanical and thermal loads, can compromise their integrity. The present work aims to evaluate the use of shape memory alloy (SMA) sealing gaskets, specifically NiTi alloys. This work establishes a comparative performance analysis of NiTi and AISI 316 stainless steel gaskets under the same operating conditions. Finite element method is employed to evaluate the mechanical response of both materials under critical loading conditions, including service overpressure, progressive bolt preload loss, and individual bolt loss scenarios. The analysis combines SMA constitutive nonlinearities and contact interactions to properly capture the sealing behavior. Experimental data are used to calibrate the constitutive model for the NiTi alloy. The analysis framework is based on average and local sealing pressures, allowing a detailed comparison between the two materials in terms of their sealing efficiency and mechanical robustness. Results indicate that SMA gaskets present a better performance, improving the contact area of the sealing surface between the flange and the gasket.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Model Organism: The Unboxing of Thinking Process
4f8d81e930ce435f88a6cef602b5c156dcd86ff3.abstract: We establish the Hortus Regis Alti (HRA) Experimental and Observational Protocol for studying a frozen language model as a cognitive model organism. The preparation combines controlled input perturbations, complete native-token preservation, deterministic symbolic probes, contextual process coding, and explicit failure screening. One DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B implementation with INT8 linear layers and BF16 elsewhere produced 176 archived trajectories across four observation configurations of one Bayesian decision problem, containing 2,205,963 generated tokens. Eight baseline pairs regenerated identical overlapping prefixes across 93,016 token positions. Three empirical demonstrations organize the study. Symbolic closure separated from execution termination, including renewed processing after a closure marker. Aggregate consumption separated from item-specific response paths: 36 of 40 four-level item series changed direction. Correct local computation separated from maintenance of task representation: an auxiliary result could be calculated correctly and subsequently rebound as an operand. Complete contextual reading localized 1,926 evidence anchors, including successful repairs and recurrent failures. Measurement checks further showed that a short window could classify a long exact cycle as highly diverse. These findings motivate testable hypotheses of representational control competition, training-register capture, and content-specific effects of symbolic continuation. The contribution is a process-oriented experimental preparation, a reproducible trajectory collection, and a quality-control procedure that connects observable symbolic events to discriminating intervention sites. Precision specifications identify the model strain, execution conditions, measurement units, semantic coding decisions, and regeneration range supporting these claims.

title: Attention in model-based cognitive neuroscience: Mechanisms for optimization under constraint
d7b6769b954c81379761a9e047a33fbc40c48a90.abstract: Two major criticisms of attention research are: 1) verbal theories lack the specificity to make falsifiable predictions about how the various mechanisms of attention operate; and 2) the term ``attention’’ is frequently ascribed to conceptually similar phenomena despite dissociable neural underpinnings. The field of model-based cognitive neuroscience is well-positioned to address (1) through mathematical formalization of hypothesized processes, but may perpetuate (2) insofar as similar algorithms and parameters may recur across modeling traditions without necessarily drawing upon a shared neuro-mechanistic basis. This review provides a function-first organization of the algorithms that have been hypothesized to implement or give rise to ``attention'' at various levels of processing: perception, decision-making, and learning. We ground mathematically-formalized processes in the performance-relevant objectives they serve and the processing constraints that limit them. In doing so, we provide a road map of the broader computational-level solutions that ``attention'' mechanisms have been invoked to provide.

title: The Cognitive Structure of the WPPSI-IV: What Can Network Analysis Tell Us?
9e26592f6712d1797aef2305ab358e6872c057bc.abstract: The Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Fourth Edition (WPPSI-IV), is widely used to assess young children’s cognitive abilities. Its indices describe performance in domains such as verbal comprehension and working memory, but evidence for interpreting these as distinct abilities remains limited. This study examined whether exploratory graph analysis (EGA), a network method, could recover the proposed index groupings from published normative correlations for ages 2:6 to 3:11 (n = 600) and 4:0 to 7:7 (n = 1,100). Simulations tested whether the same method could recover those groupings when separate, correlated factors generated the data. The main EGA procedure placed the primary subtests in one group. It also produced one group in 99.6% to 100% of samples generated from the index models, so it could not distinguish those models from simpler alternatives. In the older band, however, factor models fit better with several factors than with one. Recovery depended on factor correlations, the number of subtests per factor, and a built-in check for a single dimension. Groupings also changed with subtest coverage. For school psychologists, a one-group network result, however consistent, cannot by itself show whether WPPSI-IV index scores reflect distinct abilities.

title: A phase-calibrated combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation platform for short-Term frontoparietal network modulation and cognitive fatigue resistance
container-title: Journal of Neural Engineering
0543fae036aa19547ebb7e39691e088052619142.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Non-invasive multimodal neuromodulation is often limited by cross-modal temporal misalignment caused by modality-specific conduction delays. To address this challenge, we developed a microcontroller-based multiphysics stimulation platform integrating transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) with visual and auditory rhythmic inputs. A feedforward delaycompensation strategy using individualized ERP latencies (visual P1 and auditory N1) was implemented to reduce intermodal timing discrepancies.The system was evaluated in a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study with 15 participants providing complete EEG datasets. Compared with sensory-only stimulation, the phase-coordinated multiphysics condition increased resting-state frontoparietal theta power and enhanced functional connectivity (wPLI). During a subsequent high-load cognitive task, it was also associated with reduced accumulation of fatigue-related parietal alpha power.Exploratory analysis revealed a moderate association between parietal alpha stability and behavioral performance (r = 0.577, p = 0.024). These findings suggest that temporally coordinated cross-modal stimulation may support more stable large-scale neural dynamics and improved cognitive performance under sustained load, providing a technical framework for precision multimodal neuromodulation.</jats:p>

title: Robust retrieval in a hierarchical associative memory
container-title: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
f837836023dfa4313b84f0445b8c5c2443881beb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We study a hierarchical associative-memory model inspired by hierarchical Hopfield networks with hidden layers. While such architectures are often viewed as biologically plausible realisations of dense associative memories, it remains less clear which mathematical advantages are provided by the hierarchical organisation itself. To address this question, we introduce a sparse stroke–concept model in which elementary feature patterns (strokes) are first stored and subsequently combined into higher-level memories (concepts). Retrieval proceeds in two stages: a feature cue activates candidate strokes, and a second-layer decoding rule identifies the most likely concept.&#xD;Our main result shows that successful concept retrieval does not require exact recovery of all constituent strokes. Instead, it is sufficient to control aggregate false negatives and false positives at the intermediate stroke layer. We derive deterministic and probabilistic retrieval criteria that quantify the interplay between stroke-layer errors and overlaps among competing concepts. In particular, the&#xD;second retrieval stage can compensate for a substantial amount of first-layer noise. We analyse both fixed-size and variable-size concept ensembles. For variable concept sizes, we introduce suitable penalised and normalised scoring rules and establish corresponding retrieval guarantees. The results provide a rigorous mathematical description of how hierarchical organisation can improve retrieval&#xD;robustness, even in situations where it does not alter the classical Hopfield-type storage-capacity scaling.</jats:p>
