title: AI-powered optical communications and networking for future infrastructures
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
04172700aaf98b939cf474d5fb1dd26b6cb8ea3b.abstract: <jats:p>As future infrastructures such as computing power networks, data center interconnections, industrial internet, and intelligent transportation continue to evolve, optical communication and optical networks have higher requirements for high bandwidth, low latency, high reliability, and intelligent autonomy. This paper focuses on the research of optical communication and network technologies enabled by artificial intelligence for future infrastructure, and constructs a framework for optical communication transmission link perception and control methods as well as optical network resource orchestration and autonomous control technologies. In the optical communication layer, research is conducted on joint modeling of optical channel state perception and transmission characteristics, intelligent modulation identification and adaptive control of encoding parameters, compensation and equalization processing for high-speed links' nonlinear distortion, and prediction of error evolution and regulation of link stability; in the optical network layer, research is conducted on joint modeling of topology expression and service status, integrated decision-making for routing selection and wavelength allocation, dynamic resource orchestration driven by multi-service traffic prediction, as well as fault location recovery and construction mechanism of autonomous control loop. The research can provide technical references for the construction of optical network systems with high capacity, low latency, and high autonomous management capabilities in future infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Cross-lingual semantic drift analysis in AI-assisted political text translation
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
66a398f5e54b19eaad9508be310eeda76a88c3b2.abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to quantify the semantic drift of translation in artificial intelligence-assisted translation, a cross-lingual semantic drift detection method was constructed. In this method, bilingual text pairs are taken as input, and cross-lingual semantic vectors are generated through text cleaning, sentence-level semantic unit segmentation, and source-translation representation alignment. On this basis, word-level, sentence-level, and paragraph-level features are fused to compute the drift vector, drift intensity, direction constraint, keyword offset, semantic tendency and mood strength, and a lightweight classification head is applied to perform four-level drift discrimination. In the experiment, 18,640 source-translation text pairs were constructed, and 46,920 semantic units were obtained. The training set, validation set and test set were 32,844, 7,038 and 7,038 samples, respectively. In the comparison experiment, the accuracy of the proposed method reaches 0.894, F1 reaches 0.879, and AUC reaches 0.936. In the comparison of translation models, the average drift intensity of alignment-enhanced translation is reduced to 0.218, and the proportion of significant drift is 5.9%, which verifies the effectiveness of cross-lingual alignment and joint drift score for semantic shift detection.</jats:p>

title: AI-enhanced traffic analysis for mitigating enterprise network ransomware propagation
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
2743acd3822c92b32e649464537fe5d5823d3314.abstract: <jats:p>Computer-aided traffic analysis is fundamental to defending enterprise networks against sophisticated ransomware attacks. This paper presents a novel AI-driven architecture combining dynamic graph neural networks with multi-head temporal convolution modules to identify and contain ransomware propagation in real time. Even in the presence of encryption or obfuscation, this approach can create adaptive propagation graphs to record temporal changes in spatial interactions and network flows between hosts. This enables precise modeling of ransomware lateral movement. A composite dataset, integrating enterprise-grade traffic and simulated attack traces, is used to evaluate the framework. The results show that the method has significantly improved in detection accuracy, recall rate and propagation containment rate compared with the traditional feature-based system and traditional machine learning classifier. In addition, the method guaranties low inference latency, making it suitable for enterprise deployment. To enhance the robustness of detection and the generalization ability in various attack scenarios, the architecture adopts advanced feature normalization, joint entropydriven edge modeling and nonlinear feature fusion. Comprehensive evaluation shows that the framework can adapt to complex and changeable network environment and effectively distinguish between benign and malicious propagation. These results demonstrate the importance of AI-enhanced traffic analysis in enterprise ransomware defense. It also shows that there are more effective methods than existing baselines.</jats:p>

title: AI-assisted training of web front-end development course for vocational undergraduates based on code semantic diagnosis
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
da833a669581e78886974d115abf96fdb5c520f1.abstract: <jats:p>The Web front-end development course of professional undergraduate puts forward higher requirements for students 'ability of code implementation, page rendering and debugging, interface joint adjustment and project iteration. This paper proposes an AI-assisted training mode based on code semantic diagnosis for Web front-end engineering training scenarios. The system collects WebIDE code commits, Git commit records, browser console logs, automated test results, page rendering screenshots and learning behavior logs, and constructs a code semantic graph that integrates DOM nodes, CSS rules, JavaScript functions, event bindings and interface request relationships. Page rendering difference detection is used to identify layout deviation, style conflict, interaction failure and data rendering anomaly. By tracing the error propagation path, the system can locate the fault source node and its influence path. The credibility of the AI feedback is verified by Lint detection, test case playback and rendering result verification. The experimental results on 96 students for 8 weeks show that the error recognition accuracy of the proposed method reaches 92.3%, the feedback matching rate reaches 88.4%, the average diagnosis time is 73 ms, and the success rate of task correction increases to 92.8%. Research shows that this mode can improve the efficiency of front-end code diagnosis, the reliability of AI feedback and the quality of project implementation, and provide technical reference for engineering training of vocational undergraduate software courses.</jats:p>

title: Research on AI perception modeling and information flow optimization control mechanism in the numerical control machining process chain of higher vocational colleges
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
23f5f3642cfd676846962416dac534b9c1f9f7de.abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid development of intelligent manufacturing, data collection and processing in the numerical control machining process have become key points for improving processing efficiency and accuracy. This paper proposes an AI perception modeling and information flow optimization control mechanism based on the numerical control machining process chain. By solving and improving the problems of slow process information flow and large processing errors in numerical control machining in higher vocational colleges, By introducing data acquisition, feature extraction and optimization of feature extraction and modeling methods, combined with information flow scheduling and data compression technology, real-time supervision of information flow and process optimization regulation are carried out in the processing technology chain. Experiments show that this system method significantly improves processing accuracy and efficiency, and enhances the control response speed and robustness of the system.</jats:p>

title: Control technology and implementation of laser foreign body removal device on transmission line optimized by light perception and AI decision
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
3828d23af01ae4afd66f3ed2f89db81800b00657.abstract: <jats:p>In view of the discharge trip and disposal risk caused by foreign matter attachment of bird's nest, plastic film, kite line and other foreign matter on transmission lines, and the positioning deviation of laser removal, this paper proposes a control technical scheme of laser foreign matter removal device on transmission lines optimized by light perception and AI decision. Taking line ontology, foreign body target, laser PTZ and ranging unit as objects, a collaborative control model of imaging perception, distance estimation, target segmentation, risk discrimination and laser execution is constructed. Contour extraction, coordinate mapping, priority calculation, power adjustment and scanning path generation are linked. The verification results show that the target recognition accuracy is 96.8%, 95.4%, 94.7% and 97.2% in the tree branch, plastic film, kite line and bird nest scenes, respectively. Under the conditions of standard light, low light, strong backlight and 4m/s wind disturbance, the success rate of removal is 96.4%, 94.9%, 93.8% and 92.7%, respectively, and the average response time increases from 0.78 s to 1.04 s. The results can provide technical support for visual perception, intelligent decision-making, laser execution and safety protection of foreign body removal equipment on transmission lines.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI-driven high-naturalness Chinese speech synthesis model
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
d52ec8db612dda73b6df3f4545a42c29f9edfa30.abstract: <jats:p>In order to solve the problems of insufficient tone continuity, abrupt stop and continuity of long sentences and distortion of spectral details in Chinese speech synthesis, a generative artificial intelligent-driven Chinese TTS model with high naturalness was constructed. The model takes the front end of the text as the input basis, maps phoneme, tone and prosodic boundaries into a unified latent space, and completes semantic-prosodic joint coding by Transformer. At the acoustic end, the conditional diffusion network is used to learn the noise addition and reverse denoising process of Mel spectrum, and the neural vocoder completes the waveform reconstruction. Experiments were conducted on 12000 Mandarin text-speech samples. The results show that the MCD of the proposed model is reduced to 4.51, F0-RMSE is 22.6, and RTF is 0.034, which is better than Tacotron2, FastSpeech2 and VITS in terms of spectrum restoration and tone stability. The validity of the model is verified.</jats:p>

title: Fine wind field inversion and early warning method integrating dual-polarization Doppler radar and generative AI for low-altitude economy scenarios
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
1452e996c34dfec3690fc333985563ef034dbf34.abstract: <jats:p>To meet the need for precise and timely warnings of wind shear, turbulence and microbursts below 500 m in low-altitude economy operations, this paper proposes an integrated framework that combines generative-AI radar super-resolution, physically constrained wind-field inversion and graded hazard warning. A conditional diffusion model (Radar-SR3) reconstructs dual-polarization Doppler radar fields from 1 km to 100 m resolution, improving the visibility of small-scale echoes. Reflectivity, radial velocity, differential reflectivity, differential propagation phase and correlation coefficient are then fused under mass-continuity constraints to retrieve single-radar three-dimensional wind fields and derive safety indicators. Finally, a LightGBM-LSTM module identifies hazardous wind-field types, estimates risk levels and extrapolates 5-15 min impacts. Tests using public radar observations, wind-profile data and aviation verification samples show that the proposed method attains 29.7 dB PSNR and 0.90 SSIM, reduces inversion RMSE by 26.7% against 3DVAR, and achieves 89.4% warning accuracy with an average 9.6 min lead time. The framework improves fine-scale perception, inversion reliability and operational warning timeliness for low-altitude flight safety.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive-niche-based occupational exposure modeling for quantifying generative AI impacts on employment and educational supply
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
942a52d863954e8748cbc7424159a306f3287da2.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes a computable occupational cognitive niche model for quantifying the heterogeneous impact of generative artificial intelligence on employment and education supply. Instead of treating Gen-AI as a uniform jobreplacement factor, occupations are represented as five-dimensional cognitive niche vectors constructed from O*NET task data, and Gen-AI substitution is modeled as a time-varying intensity vector over the same task space. Occupational exposure is then calculated by vector overlap, and employment impacts are estimated by combining exposure scores with BLS baseline projections. Results under the 2034 scenario show clear cross-occupational heterogeneity: software developers obtain the highest exposure score of 0.1620 and a projected employment reduction from 1,918,067 to 1,607,340, while electricians show the lowest exposure score of 0.1052 due to their concentration in physical and context-dependent execution tasks. Graphic designers exhibit an intermediate exposure score of 0.1351, reflecting both vulnerability to generative production and persistence of judgment-intensive tasks. The model further updates task weights to capture within-occupation structural reconfiguration and maps occupational demand shifts to IPEDS-based education supply vectors. Quantitative comparison shows that university supply is concentrated in complex problem solving and rule-based execution, while arts and vocational pathways require differentiated adaptation toward judgment, physical execution, and responsibility-intensive competencies. The proposed framework provides a transparent and extensible method for linking Gen-AI exposure assessment, employment projection, and education supply adjustment in a unified computational model.</jats:p>

title: Design of an AI-driven platform for time series forecasting and intelligent decision support
container-title: International Conference on Wireless, Optical Communication, and Information Engineering (WOCIE 2026)
26106bcc8370065ddf4a2de7ce17bcfde81a3a57.abstract: <jats:p>Traditional financial analysis methods are increasingly inadequate for handling complex and nonlinear time series data. To address this challenge, this study designs an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven platform for time series forecasting and decision support in financial management. The proposed platform integrates deep learning and knowledge reasoning technologies within a multi-layered architecture, enabling intelligent management from data acquisition and preprocessing to forecasting and decision-making. A hybrid prediction model combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), and an attention mechanism is developed to enhance the accuracy of financial trend and risk prediction. Experimental results show that the platform improves forecasting accuracy by about 12%–18% compared with traditional statistical models in tasks such as cash flow prediction, cost control, and investment analysis, demonstrating its effectiveness in supporting intelligent financial decision-making and risk management.</jats:p>

title: Comparative Evaluation of AI Chatbots for Medical Research: Cross-Sectional Observational Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
08d3abe31942fe4167e6a4c65009ef6f4293209f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The use of generative AI in research and clinical practice is rapidly expanding, offering unprecedented capabilities in pattern extraction and data analysis. However, its application raises critical concerns regarding the accuracy and reliability of the information provided.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The aim of this study is to analyze and compare the performance of 4 generative AI platforms (ChatGPT, Grok, Meta AI, and Perplexity) in retrieving bibliographic references within the medical and health care field and to assess factual accuracy and information retrieval strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional observational study was conducted based on the simulation of 3 bibliographic queries with varying levels of specificity (aflatoxin toxicity, hospital sanitization, and human papillomavirus vaccination). Each prompt was administered in triple iteration on each platform operating in “Guest” mode. Factual accuracy was verified through a manual cross-check against the Scopus and Google Scholar databases using a hierarchical query strategy prioritized by DOI. The incidence of hallucinations was quantified via a standardized scoring system (range 0‐5) based on metadata correctness. Categorical associations were analyzed using the Pearson chi-square test, while nonparametric continuous variables (hallucination score, publication year, and citation count) were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Of the 360 requested references, 273 were generated (task completion rate: 75.8%). Among these, 190 adhered to the requested article format (instruction adherence rate: 69.6% of generated outputs). Fact-checking revealed that 128 of these 190 validly formatted articles (metadata accuracy rate: 67.4%) showed an exact match with real evidence, resulting in an overall strict yield of 35.6% (128/360) from the initial requested references. The ability to provide real references depended significantly on the AI model used (χ
                      <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                      ²=192.5;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001). Kruskal-Wallis tests revealed statistically significant differences among the models across all analyzed dimensions (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001). Grok emerged as the most reliable model, achieving 71 out of 90 (78.9%) exact matches, exhibiting minimal hallucinations (mean score 0.2, SD 0.5), and showing a marked propensity toward recent sources (median year 2022, IQR 2019.0-2024.8). ChatGPT demonstrated robust stability, with 46 out of 90 (51.1%) exact matches, and anchored itself to older (median year 2020, IQR 2011.0-2023.0), highly cited literature (median 73.5, IQR 10.8‐718.0 citations). Perplexity exhibited critical rates of total hallucination and a structural inability to distinguish scientific articles from gray literature. Meta AI systematically failed the task, producing entirely incorrect data on a single occasion (0/10, 0% exact matches).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Under the specific testing conditions of this study, the evaluated large language models demonstrated a lack of the necessary reliability to replace validated bibliographic databases, primarily due to response instability and a high incidence of metadata fabrication. The results highlight the urgency of introducing structured AI literacy programs across medical education, promoting the use of such technologies exclusively as a complementary tool and always subject to rigorous human fact-checking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital Frontlines in Immigration Services: An Environmental Scan of the Use of Digital and AI Tools by Immigrant-Serving Organizations in Canada
Les pionniers numériques dans les services d’immigration : analyse contextuelle de l’utilisation des outils numériques et d’intelligence artificielle par les organismes pour les immigrants au Canada

681b8401e1e44cc3146103db8825ef507a884b7f.abstract: <jats:p>Using a web-based environmental scan as a method, this study examined a sample of Service Provider Organizations (SPOs) in the settlement or immigrant-serving sector across Canadian cities to assess their adoption of digital tools. Findings reveal that AI adoption remains nascent, with only a few SPOs deploying AI-powered tools for employment services. SPOs used chatbots and group chats minimally, and chatbots mostly relied on rule-based systems or served as digital receptionists. Further, our findings suggest that SPOs using AI tools were concentrated in larger urban centres, leaving smaller cities largely underserved. The study highlights a gap between SPOs' potential and current uses of AI tools.</jats:p>

title: When Does an AI Interviewer Work? How Task Type and Interview Outcome Shape Procedural Justice, Source Credibility, and Negative WOM
container-title: International Journal of Business Communication
d6012e9007cfdbbad9d7efcdd42d4454d41b5116.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines how interviewer type (AI vs. human), task type (factual vs. evaluative), and interview outcome (success vs. failure) jointly shape applicants' perceptions of procedural justice, source credibility, and negative word-of-mouth (WOM) intentions. Using a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design with 199 Korean adults, the study tested (a) the sequential mediating roles of procedural justice and source credibility (trustworthiness and expertise) in the relationship between interviewer type and negative WOM intentions, and (b) the moderating roles of task type and interview outcome on these indirect pathways. Results showed that AI interviewers, compared to human interviewers, generated lower procedural justice perceptions, which in turn reduced source trustworthiness and ultimately increased negative WOM intentions. A significant three-way interaction among interviewer type, task type, and interview outcome further emerged for source trustworthiness. In the success condition, AI interviewers were perceived as more trustworthy on factual than evaluative tasks. In the failure condition, however, this pattern reversed: AI interviewers were perceived as substantially less trustworthy than human interviewers specifically when the task was factual. Moderated mediation analyses further showed that the sequential indirect effect on negative WOM was significant only when applicants failed a factual task. These findings highlight that both task type and interview outcome are critical boundary conditions shaping applicants' responses to AI-mediated evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Neural Signatures of AI-Assisted Cognition: EEG Profiles of AI Users and Non-Users and Implications for Brain Chemistry and Structure

37caf7504b4f1fb2abdbbffbc56cdd002224e901.abstract: <jats:p>This review combines EEG and fMRI studies of cognitive task completion with and without generative AI from the standpoint of the recent MIT “Your Brain on ChatGPT” study. Next, the results of these studies are used to make an inference about brain chemistry and brain structure through PET, MRS, and MRI/DTI studies of reward system functioning and intensive use of technological gadgets. The newly released OpenNeuro dataset ds008496 that provides EEG data collected when writing essays in conditions of interaction with various AI systems becomes the next step of this research line.</jats:p>

It integrates dynamic capability theory and responsible AI governance to examine the mediating role of digital dynamic capability (DsDC) and the moderating effect of responsible AI orientation (RAIO).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Two complementary empirical studies were undertaken. Study 1 applies a staggered difference-in-differences design with propensity-score matching (DiD-PSM) to 500 GenAI adoption events (2019–2024). Study 2 employs a two-step system generalised method of moments (GMM) estimator for 1,274 firm-year observations (2016–2024) to analyse persistence, mediation and moderation effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GenAI adoption was associated with a market-perceived efficiency signal (a 2.7% rise in cumulative abnormal returns) alongside a 1.9% decline in environmental, social and governance sentiment, a reputational rather than substantive sustainability indicator, evidencing an efficiency-responsibility tension. Over time, DDC helped partially translate these short-term gains into sustainable performance, while RAIO mitigated ethical and reputational risks, enhancing firms’ long-term legitimacy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study relies on archival indicators and text-derived governance measures; future research could combine these data with surveys or internal audit evidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers should pair GenAI deployment with adaptive digital capability and responsible AI governance to protect stakeholder trust.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study advances theory by integrating capability and governance perspectives to explain the sustainability of GenAI adoption. Methodologically, it introduces temporal triangulation by combining DiD-PSM and System GMM, offering a novel dynamic causal framework for responsible digital transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Constructing AI safety: a comparative cognitive-discursive analysis of corporate and regulatory discourses
container-title: Frontiers in Communication
b1417153c80108b492bf23febdfcc44c0d7f5602.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The global proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has transformed safety governance into a highly contested sociopolitical battleground, yet existing discourse studies frequently under-theorize the micro-cognitive mechanisms of epistemic reality construction within AI safety standardization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate how corporate and regulatory actors engineer divergent cognitive realities of AI safety through specific micro-grammatical choices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We proposed an integrated Cognitive-Critical Discourse Analysis framework by synthesizing Langacker's cognitive conception of reality with Fairclough's three-dimensional model, and applied it to a comparative corpus of corporate safety frameworks and regulatory policy documents.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tech enterprises engineer a reality of techno-pragmatic containment via active voice, high-certainty evidentiality, and immediate projection to naturalize self-regulation. Conversely, regulatory bodies construct a reality of socio-structural vulnerability using distal modals, passive constructions, and deontic mandates to legitimize state-enforced compliance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Linguistic normalization is actively deployed to facilitate or contest corporate epistemic hegemony in AI governance. These findings provide empirical references for revising regulatory discourse and enhancing public media literacy against algorithmic exceptionalism.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI Enabled ERP-CRM Integration for Predictive Customer Analytics
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
2d27d9d06d01a39942c58fdbf7d8da87c5d21532.abstract: <jats:p>Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems provide complimentary insights on customer‘s transactions, interaction and engagements. However, fragmented enterprise data, lack of cross-system relationship learning, limited behavior modeling over time and weak interpretability of prediction hinder reliable predictive customer analytics. To overcome these obstacles, this research introduce a proposed technique called Cross-System Temporal Customer Intelligence Engine (CSTCIE), an integrative solution aimed at enhancing customer ‘s churn prediction based on unified enterprise data. The CSTCIE method uses probabilistic entity resolution for alignment of customer records, Dual Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) encoders for ERP and CRM feature representation and cross-attention to learn relations between operational and engagement data. The Transformer learns customer's behavior dynamics, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) predicts churn probability and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) finds influential features in prediction. Accuracy of 96.40% and Receiver Operating Characteristic–Area under the Curve (ROC-AUC) of 91.30% from experiments performed as part of the manuscript were found, indicating promising classification and churn discriminant performance. Recall and precision-recall performance, however, should be further improved. In conclusion, CSTCIE represents a promising integrative and interpretable approach to customers churn analysis.</jats:p>

title: AI Enabled Predictive Compliance Controls for Healthcare Database Security Governance
container-title: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
0b40e4e96f9dd37db8202fd3a918dcfab7f86793.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has changed the way healthcare security is implemented using intelligent prediction of risks, adaptive access control and secure management of Electronic Health Record (EHR). Existing access to control encounter difficulties in identifying new threats, policy enforcement and finding a balance between data protection and efficient processes. In address to solve these issues, the proposed Hybrid Gated Temporal Integer Unit (HGTIU) system can be discussed. Integrated model is the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Temporal Defeasible Logic (TDL) and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). Healthcare audit logs and authentications for healthcare are evaluated to determine suspicious activity and any possibility of security breaches. The illustrative prediction accuracy of HGTIU is 93.60% achieved in experimental validation. The permissions, context policies and emergencies are evaluated by TDL, while MILP select the right control measures considering residual risks, costs of intervention and impact on work processes. The research aims to improve healthcare data security, compliance and operational efficiency through intelligent and risk-aware access management.</jats:p>

title: Meritocracy and generative AI in higher education: institutional pathways and use–response alignment across four systems
container-title: Advances in Social Behavior Research
1d18258e5287d5117654b68c5dc746e92d867f48.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines how higher education systems respond to the rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) under different institutional conditions, asking how meritocratic competition is translated into assessment and credential pressure and how student GenAI use aligns with institutional responses. Using a comparative qualitative case-study design, the study analyzes secondary evidence from China, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Germany through two a priori frozen indicator frameworks. The first framework traces how meritocratic competition is institutionalized through admissions, grading, and credential differentiation; the second maps student GenAI use patterns against institutional responses in teaching, assessment, and support. Strong credential differentiation and education–labour-market linkage emerge in all four systems, but through distinct pathways: state-coordinated in China, marketized in the United Kingdom, decentralized and market-oriented in the United States, and state–professional in Germany. Partial use–response alignment is the cross-system norm; systems differ mainly in pedagogical integration, regulatory adaptation, and institutional support. AI literacy and support provision lag behind student adoption in all four cases, making institutional capacity the most persistent source of misalignment, while limited comparable measurement of equity alignment and of guarded and compensatory use shows that monitoring capacity is itself part of governance. GenAI governance therefore converges less on common rules than on common capability gaps. The findings suggest that governing GenAI in meritocratic systems depends less on uniform rules than on sustained investment in institutional monitoring and support capacity.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI-enabled writing feedback in primary school English instruction: application landscape, practical dilemmas, and a teacher-led collaborative framework
container-title: Advances in Social Behavior Research
46a2a0e62e833b05feb28298ad275d5b27608889.abstract: <jats:p>Writing feedback is a pivotal yet chronically constrained component of primary school English writing instruction, squeezed by large class sizes, low marking frequency, and homogeneous comments. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), with its immediacy, personalization, and dialogic interaction, opens new possibilities for reconstructing writing feedback. Drawing on a narrative synthesis of 52 Chinese and international sources, and addressing a literature in which research on AI writing feedback concentrates on higher education and on the learner side, this paper maps the application landscape of GenAI-enabled writing feedback in primary school English, consolidates and examines five practical dilemmas concerning accuracy, appropriateness, teacher literacy, ethics, and evaluation orientation, and proposes a Teacher-led, AI-assisted, Student-centered Collaborative Feedback Framework (TAC-F). The framework assigns teachers responsibility for goal setting, affective support, and feedback verification, positions GenAI as an initial assessor and material provider, and treats students as reflective revisers within a pre-writing, while-writing, and post-writing closed loop, supported by prompt-template libraries, feedback-verification routines, school-based teacher AI literacy development, and ethical data norms. Preliminary multi-tool observations, together with a six-dimension observation framework and a same-prompt pilot protocol, are developed to help teachers screen AI-generated feedback; the observations suggest that current tools are reliable on explicit errors but unstable at the discourse level. Six implementation suggestions are advanced to inform the digital transformation of primary school English writing instruction.</jats:p>

title: Awareness of Generative AI Limitations and Students’ Intention to Use ChatGPT: A Moderated Mediation Analysis
container-title: Journal of Advanced Research in Education
2b83fad3d16665e8e1efb29889de46a07511e57c.abstract: <jats:p>This research examined the importance of understanding generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) limitations in predicting college students’ likelihood of using ChatGPT, based on a modified Technology Acceptance Model. It treated awareness, perceived usefulness, and perceived anxiety about skills deterioration related to GenAI as independent variables, with intention to use ChatGPT as the dependent variable. The first-stage moderated mediation model was applied to analyze participants’ responses, with cooperation from 931 college students from different fields of study at a private higher education institution in the Philippines. The findings revealed that the awareness of GenAI limitations exerted a positive impact on the intention of college students to use ChatGPT, in particular, both its direct positive effect (c’ = 0.169, p < .001) and an indirect effect through the mediation of perceived usefulness. Conditional process analysis confirmed that skill-erosion concern moderated the relationship between awareness and perceived usefulness (moderated mediation index = -0.075, 95% CI [-0.107, -0.046]). Although perceived usefulness remained a significant mediator of the relationship between awareness and intention, the indirect effect diminished as skill-erosion concern increased, dropping from 0.233 for students with low-little concern to 0.105 for students with great concern. The collinearity analysis confirmed that the predictors were empirically distinguishable. The findings show that beliefs about risks regulate the technology acceptance process, and that AI-literacy training can be pursued alongside measured caution about dependency rather than treating these goals as alternatives.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating Multi-Agent AI Systems for Decision Support in the Operational Readiness of Heavy Industrial Facilities
container-title: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
660493abdd965d8a7c9e5ee350aab36e0d2a7930.abstract: <jats:p>This structured integrative review synthesizes evidence across five interconnected areas and develops an integrated framework for evaluating multi-agent AI in the operational readiness of heavy industrial facilities. The review examines multi-agent architectures and coordination, operational-readiness decision support, digital twins and virtual validation, safety and system assurance, and human–agent interaction and governance. From this synthesis, the study develops a reference architecture, a six-dimensional evaluation framework covering technical performance and reliability, coordination and context integrity, operational-readiness value, safety and assurance, human factors and governance, and implementation viability, scalability, and interoperability, together with a five-level maturity model. The framework considers both whether multi-agent AI can support assessment of facility readiness and whether the AI-supported decision system itself is sufficiently reliable, assured, governed, and mature for that role. Industrial evidence from Saudi Aramco and Bosch applications across Bosch and SICK manufacturing settings indicates practical value in maintenance planning, fault diagnosis, information synthesis, and production support. However, the available evidence is stronger for operational benefit and implementation feasibility than for coordination reliability, safety assurance, and lifecycle governance. Current systems are therefore best characterized as bounded, human-supervised decision-support tools rather than autonomous readiness authorities. Progress toward governed operational use will require stronger industrial benchmarks, traceable engineering evidence, reliable coordination, effective safeguards, lifecycle assurance, and clearly defined human decision authority.</jats:p>

title: From eWOM to Synthetic WOM: A Systematic Review and Integrative Framework for AI-Mediated Persuasion in Tourism and Hospitality
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
00a781a18d4dc93c4173f3c7c4c9dbc8a7643e69.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) now participates in analysing, selecting, reformulating and producing online review communication. Tourism and hospitality research examines these uses through overlapping concepts, leaving uncertainty about their relationship to human experience and electronic word of mouth (eWOM). This review combines bibliometric mapping of 142 publications in English indexed in Scopus at the search date, thematic coding of 54 papers and close comparison of an analytical core of 20 sources. The bibliometric results locate generative systems within research on eWOM, review analytics, service technologies and recommendations. The focused synthesis identifies five distinct roles for AI in review communication. These roles differ in experiential provenance and control over message formulation and presentation. The framework locates them within synthetic word of mouth (Synthetic WOM) and proposes a pathway linking provenance cues, consumer appraisal and outcomes. It also identifies practical priorities for platforms and tourism firms: clear disclosure of AI involvement, source identification and access to supporting reviews. Reviewed studies support individual relationships within this pathway; the complete sequence remains for empirical testing. Platform studies also report changes in subsequent review contribution. The framework uses these findings to propose a longer-term feedback connection to the review corpus.</jats:p>

title: From Shadow IT to Shadow AI: A Scoping Review of How Embedded AI and Employee Use Increase Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Risk
container-title: Journal of Cybersecurity Education, Research and Practice
3805a82bfed81dbc127e741fe1c526c220ff0684.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into enterprise software has introduced a critical governance challenge: Shadow AI, the unmanaged and often invisible adoption of AI tools and features by employees outside formal IT oversight. Unlike traditional Shadow IT, which centers on unauthorized data storage and infrastructure, Shadow AI operates at the knowledge and decision-making layer, introducing probabilistic risks including data leakage, agentic misalignment, and indirect prompt injection that existing security frameworks are ill-equipped to address. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) synthesizing 38 peer-reviewed and industry sources to investigate three research questions: how organizational visibility gaps into embedded and employee-used AI increase cybersecurity and data privacy risk; what cybersecurity incident types are most commonly associated with ungoverned AI-enabled applications; and what risks employee interactions with AI pose to sensitive, proprietary, and regulated data. The analysis identifies a critical visibility deficit created by AI capabilities embedded within vendor-managed platforms, the semantic opacity of large language model interactions, and employees' utilitarian bypass of security policies. A taxonomy of six AI-specific incident types is presented, encompassing data leakage, prompt injection, credential compromise, agentic misuse, phishing augmentation, and insecure plugin exploitation. Findings demonstrate that existing governance mechanisms, including data loss prevention systems, identity and access management frameworks, and static risk assessments, are structurally misaligned with the dynamic nature of generative AI. The paper recommends a transition to dynamic, risk-based governance integrating continuous monitoring, cross-functional oversight, and AI TRiSM frameworks.</jats:p>

title: Audience Discernment of AI-Generated Media Content: A Systematic Review
container-title: Middle East Journal of Communication Studies
c5a6c6fe7909cd084994114b76eba674bdfc31dc.abstract:
<jats:p>Despite the growing prevalence of AI-generated content in the media industry, media research has largely focused on specific aspects, such as measuring communicators' attitudes and perceptions toward the use of this emerging technology. Research examining audiences and their ability to discern AI-generated content remains limited. Accordingly, this study aims to examine audiences' ability to discern AI-generated media content. The study employs a systematic review methodology, reviewing 19 studies based on clearly defined inclusion and exclusion criteria within the Participants, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework.
The study identified several key findings. Most notably, audiences can distinguish AI-generated content through a range of technical and statistical indicators, including probabilistic and predictive indicators, digital watermarking, pixel prediction, and blockchain technologies. Recognizing these indicators requires audiences to possess an adequate level of technical knowledge and expertise. In addition, media and journalistic literacy, together with transparency and disclosure practices and linguistic indicators, can assist audiences in distinguishing AI-generated content from human-generated content.
Regarding the methodological approaches adopted in previous research, the review found that studies on this topic primarily focus on issues of trust, credibility, and transparency in AI-generated content. It also revealed that questionnaires, whether electronic or paper-based, are the most commonly used data collection instrument. Furthermore, individuals constituted the most frequently studied sample, and the review highlighted the diversity of theoretical frameworks employed across the included studies.</jats:p>

title: BIET Smart Hub: A Smart Dashboard with Real Time Event Tracking and an AI Based Chatbot for Student Support
container-title: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering & Technology
13e82e472882cff64a588d7ff81636d41385c51a.abstract: <jats:p>College information is often distributed across notice boards, circulars, messaging groups and department level channels. This can make it difficult for students to locate current event information, seating allotment documents, photographs and other institutional details. BIET Smart Hub is a web based portal developed to bring selected college information together in one place. The student facing interface provides access to the homepage, events, gallery, department information and published seating allotment documents. An authenticated administrative interface supports the creation and maintenance of event records, images and allotment documents. The application uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the interface, Python Flask for server-side request handling and MySQL for structured data. The paper describes the system organization and the functions represented in the available interface screenshots. The current implementation offers a centralized information access point and reduces the need to maintain separate information channels for each supported module.</jats:p>

title: P-156: Accuracy of AI-generated nutrition advice in diabetes: comparing the reliability of two methodologies
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
0b282267be6ee2012aec19af60f6cfe52b08a2f1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is increasingly recognized in pediatric populations worldwide. Children, adolescents, and their caregivers are progressively using large language models (LLMs) to obtain nutritional advice, raising concerns about the accuracy of information in this vulnerable group.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to assess the reliability of a new methodology compared to current methods to assess AI generated nutrition advice in diabetes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A large language model was prompted to generate 45 frequently asked questions about diabetes. Each question was answered with a maximum of 50 words. Responses were then fragmented into individual claims, with each sentence containing a single piece of information and rewritten for standalone clarity. Six registered dietitians (RDs) with ≥3 years of clinical experience in chronic disease were divided into two groups (n=3) to assess response accuracy using the Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026 as the primary reference. Group 1 evaluated full responses using a 4-point Likert scale (1 = not at all accurate; 4 = fully accurate), representing the reference method. Group 2 assessed the responses which have been fragmented using a binary scale based on the accuracy of the statement (Yes/No), representing the proposed method. All assessors received prior training. Inter-rater reliability was evaluated using Fleiss’ kappa (p &lt; 0.05). To enable comparison, claim-level scores were converted to equivalent Likert-scale values.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fleiss’ kappa coefficients were 0.07 (p &gt; 0.05) for the method of reference and −0.01 (p &gt; 0.05) for the proposed methodology, indicating very low inter-rater agreement in both approaches. Therefore, the proposed method did not improve reliability of assessing accuracy of AI generated advice compared with conventional method.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Further research is needed to develop reliable, systematic, and resource-efficient method for evaluating the accuracy of AI-generated nutrition advice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Exploring Generative AI Adoption Among Community College Faculty and Staff: Practices, Perceptions, and Challenges
container-title: Journal of Education, Humanities, and Social Research
e1a94a627bdf3109bc7f74c75ed41f14a46056fe.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) presents new opportunities for teaching, learning, and professional productivity in higher education. However, evidence on its adoption among community college faculty and staff remains limited. This descriptive, exploratory study examined GenAI practices, perceptions, and institutional support needs using aggregated findings from a 2026 institutional survey conducted at a U.S. community college. Results indicated that 84.8% of respondents reported previous experience with AI technologies, although comfort levels and perceived understanding varied. GenAI was more frequently reported for writing, professional communication, and general workplace tasks than for learning management system course design and student support. Respondents also expressed interest in hands-on professional development and clearer institutional guidelines, alongside concerns about academic integrity, information accuracy, and data privacy. Drawing on conceptual perspectives related to self-efficacy, perceived usefulness, and facilitating conditions, the study highlights the importance of examining professional applications, employee perceptions, and institutional support needs together. These findings provide descriptive insights that may inform professional development and responsible GenAI integration in community college settings.</jats:p>

title: O-25: AI-integrated biosensor wearables for Real-Time monitoring and personalized risk mitigation in adolescents with type 1 diabetes and early diabetic kidney disease
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
86053d613d943d5853f06ee0b86fa88c5a6035dd.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) are at increased risk of early diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Conventional clinic-based monitoring often fails to detect early physiological changes such as autonomic imbalance and glycemic variability that contribute to disease progression</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the role of AI-integrated wearable biosensors in continuous monitoring and personalized risk mitigation in adolescents with early DKD</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this 30-day observational study, 260 adolescents with T1DM and early DKD were equipped with wearable biosensors measuring heart rate variability (HRV), electrodermal activity, physical activity, and sleep patterns. An AI-driven platform analyzed real-time data to detect subclinical stress markers and deliver personalized behavioral recommendations, including hydration, glycemic control, and stress reduction strategies</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The system effectively identified early physiological deviations such as reduced nocturnal HRV and sleep disturbances. Participants adhering to AI-generated recommendations showed significant improvement in autonomic balance and hemodynamic stability (p&lt;0.05). Early detection of fatigue and sleep fragmentation enabled timely intervention. Adherence to renal-protective behaviors improved, accompanied by better mental well-being and reduced anxiety</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-enabled wearable biosensors provide a proactive and personalized approach to managing early DKD in adolescents with T1DM. By enabling continuous monitoring and real-time interventions, this model enhances patient engagement, stabilizes physiological parameters, and represents a promising advancement in precision-based diabetes care</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: O-23: Graded-evidence reasoning AI with calculators and education — a deterministic, compounding-evidence AI diabetes educator for type 1 diabetes, validated via 1.5 million patient-days of real-world data
container-title: Hormone Research in Paediatrics
0dbc48ce76afb9c8e4bb2fec73b0a94fe5731bdb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Published AI for diabetes education targets type 2 diabetes with no safety framework, evidence grading or real-world validation. No system combines a structured evidence-graded knowledge base with deterministic educational tools for type 1 diabetes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To build and validate a dual-component educational system (evidence-graded wiki plus six deterministic calculators) for type 1 diabetes across the paediatric to adult lifespan.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We built a version-controlled clinical wiki (67 concept pages, 453 source summaries, 900+ evidence items) graded A to E, ingesting ISPAD 2024 and ADA 2026. Six paired deterministic calculators cover activity, exercise insulin-on-board, hypoglycaemia and hyperglycaemia treatment, AID setting review, exercise planning and alcohol. Both were validated against a real-world type 1 diabetes dataset (10,000 individuals, 2013 to 2025, 1.5 million patient-days) through 33 pre-specified assessments. Safety used 77 general, 18 adversarial and 12 jailbreak cases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 33 assessments: 18 confirmed (10 fully, 5 with nuance, 3 partial), 8 reversals, 7 deferred or not completable; 17 reversals of assumptions logged overall. Key reversals: step benefit plateau at 4,000 to 5,000 (not 10,000); sleep regularity correlated more strongly with time in range than exercise volume (77.0% vs 71.3%, n=251, p&lt;0.001); female pen users with high exercise had the worst time below range (4.3% vs 2.2% in males, n=694, p&lt;0.001). Safety: 0/77 genuine failures; 18/18 adversarial and 12/12 jailbreak attempts resisted.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A dual architecture pairing an evidence-graded knowledge base with deterministic educational calculators, validated at population scale, surfaced contradictions to clinical assumptions. A paired consultancy stream funds free public access (Robin Hood model). It offers a responsible-AI template for paediatric and adult type 1 diabetes education. Next: paediatric cohort ingest and external validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:p>Adolescent diabetes, particularly type 2 diabetes, has increased dramatically in the United States over recent decades.                     <jats:p>We utilized a comprehensive cohort of 15,149 individuals from the most recent comprehensive youth diabetes dataset, NHANES (1999–2018), to train and validate machine learning models representing diverse algorithmic approaches. title: WASTEVISION: AN INTELLIGENT IoT AND AI-BASED FRAMEWORK FOR PREDICTIVE AND OPTIMIZED MUNICIPAL WASTE MANAGEMENT

3e38b53c1e69cfe9eaf44de222d31f7f37c2b368.abstract: <jats:p>Efficient management of municipal solid waste is vital for public hygiene, environmental sustainability and the sensible use of civic resources. Conventional collection practices rely on fixed schedules and manual supervision, which leads to overflowing bins, slow response, needless collection trips and wasteful use of resources. Prior work has presented IoT-based smart bins, AI-based waste classification, predictive analytics, GIS-based analysis and citizen-oriented solutions, yet these capabilities are usually built as isolated systems. This paper proposes an integrated intelligent framework that combines IoT-based waste monitoring, AI/ML-based waste classification, waste-collection forecasting, GIS visualization, full-bin alerts and waste-related reporting. The framework gathers and analyses bin fill level, weight, location, timestamp, historical waste patterns and waste images, and presents the results on a centralized web platform that supports data-driven collection decisions. A prototype is developed to show how IoT, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics and spatial information can be combined into a practical municipal waste-management solution.</jats:p>

title: Generative image design and cross-modal content generation for intelligent creative production
container-title: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
0aa8882921d680a2cb25c0cf4f06e779058648a0.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence modifies the production of digital content, but the intelligent  creative processes still have problems such as semantic drift under different conditions, local  structural distortion, lack of long-term consistency and insufficient control over the influence of  text, sketches and reference images on the output. This paper introduces a cross-modal generative  image design framework which integrates multi-level semantic integration, hierarchical condition  management, conflict-aware gate control and temporal refinement. Text supplies the overall  semantics, sketches restrict the geometry and reference images provide appearance hints; their  token-, region- and scene-level representations are aligned before entering a latent diffusion  backbone. Since no trained model weights or source image set was used in this research, the  quantitative assessment is limited to a reproducible feature space test rather than an imaginary  complete image benchmark. In 2400 controlled examples, the proposed approach decreases the  FID-based Fréchet feature distance from 25.17 to 18.70, enhances the CLIP-like semantic matching  score from 0.260 to 0.275 and improves the consistency of features between adjacent frames from  0.895 to 0.919. Compared with flat condition setting, the Fréchet score is reduced by 25.7% and the  semantic alignment improves by 5.6%; the high residual structure outlier ratio decreases from 22.3%  to 14.3%. The method provides a practical foundation for the design of controllable generative  images and sequences in illustration, advertisement, visual storytelling and digital media production.</jats:p>

title: Research on AI real-time detection based on IMV system
container-title: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
95e76f8b6feee2714754ff9ef04a78c8827ac5bc.abstract: <jats:p>The development of portable electronic devices has driven the growth of demand in the button battery market, and has also raised higher standards for product quality control in the production process. At present, the button battery testing process is still mainly completed manually, and the testing results are easily affected by personnel's operational level and subjective judgment, and the stability needs to be improved. This article proposes an AI real-time detection method for button battery injection caps based on industrial machine vision (IMV) technology, which realizes functions such as image acquisition, defect judgment, abnormal product removal, and production information recording. The system collects images through industrial cameras and uses the COGNEX visual platform to complete image analysis and detection control. Train a deep learning model using the collected sample data to extract defect features and complete the recognition of different defect categories. In response to the limited number of original samples, image enhancement was used to expand the training data size, resulting in a dataset containing 9345 samples. The experimental results show that the model detection accuracy reaches about 99% after data expansion. Compared with traditional grayscale threshold segmentation and edge feature extraction methods, this method improves detection accuracy by about 14 percentage points. Research has shown that the detection system can complete defect recognition and automatic removal in actual production processes, and has good applicability to online manufacturing environments.</jats:p>

title: AI in Patient Narratives: Reimagining Healthcare Communication through Narrative Medicine
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
edb10a913848f93230bd15f1a0e8406cfdd08ee6.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly involved is how healthcare information is recorded, organized and dissemination of healthcare. Emotions, personal experiences, social contexts, and patients’ views of illness are examples of aspects of illness that are difficult to express using clinically data alone. This new breakthrough is especially relevant to patient narratives, which encompass these aspects of illness. This study analyses the role that Artificial Intelligence plays an important role in the process of building and spreading narratives using Rita Charon’s concept of Narrative Medicine as a foundation. Considering what happens when a patient’s story is processed by technological systems, the emphasis that Charon places on attention, representation and attachment provides a solid platform for thinking about the situation. By easing communication across several languages, organizing fragmented narratives, summarizing medical information, and making complex material more accessible, artificial intelligence may be able to assistance healthcare professional. On the other hand, these possibilities raise significant concerns. The reduction of a patient’s personal narrative to an automated summary may leave out emotional or contextual details. Additionally, algorithmic bias, privacy concerns, inaccurate outputs, and questions regarding patient agency may all have an impact on how a patient’s experience is portrayed. The paper therefore argues that AI should be understood as a support mechanism rather than as a substitute for the human practices central to Narrative Medicine. Technology can assist organize and disseminate information, interpretation, empathy, ethical responsibility, and meaningful engagement with the patient remain human responsibilities. A responsible approach to AI- assisted healthcare communication must prioritize patient voice and lived experience at the centre of technological use.</jats:p>

title: HelioIQ: AI-Powered Solar Panel Fault Detection and Predictive Maintenance
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
fcf2d6f10f22d582984898205586012b770b27d1.abstract: <jats:p>HelioIQ is an intelligent, AI-powered platform designed to detect solar panel faults and support maintenance by combining multiple data sources into a unified system. Solar panels can experience conditions such as dust accumulation, bird droppings, snow cover, shading, overheating, loose connections, cracks, and electrical damage, which may reduce power generation and efficiency. Existing monitoring methods often rely on manual inspection or a single data source, limiting their ability to identify different fault conditions and link diagnostic results to maintenance actions. HelioIQ addresses these limitations through a multimodal approach that uses solar panel images and sensor readings, including voltage, current, power, panel temperature, and light intensity. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) developed using TensorFlow and Keras analyses panel images to classify visible conditions, while an image validation component rejects inputs that do not contain solar panels. An Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model analyses sensor data to identify abnormal operating conditions. A decision-level fusion mechanism combines the outputs to determine the overall panel status, fault category, severity level, confidence score, and maintenance recommendation. Cases involving conflicting model outputs are flagged for manual review. The system is implemented as a full-stack web application using FastAPI, JWT-based authentication, a MySQL database, and a React-based dashboard. Its modules include Image Diagnosis, Sensor Diagnosis, Combined Analysis, Solar Array Grid, Prediction History, Work Orders, and Reports. By maintaining diagnostic records and linking detected conditions to structured maintenance tasks, HelioIQ provides an integrated approach to solar panel monitoring and maintenance support.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI in English Language Teaching: A Systematic Review of Its Impact on Teaching Practices and Learning Outcomes
container-title: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
8fb433a0a2295e097a0eab7db1db828dcf5bf252.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are now common in English classrooms, but the research on them is spread thinly across different tools, settings and skills, and most of it records what people think rather than what learners actually gained. This review looks at how GenAI is changing the way English is taught and what learners gain from it. Using the PRISMA procedure, the review drew on Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Springer, selecting peer-reviewed journal papers from 2024 to 2026; 28 studies were analysed in full. In most studies GenAI served as a helper for teachers in lesson planning, materials, feedback and classroom activities, but how far it was taken up varied with teachers’ own attitudes, self-assurance and preparation. Assessment was the area most challenged, prompting teachers to rethink task design and academic integrity. In terms of learning, GenAI is associated with perceived improvements in writing, grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, motivation, confidence, and autonomy, but most evidence is perception-based rather than measured. The review concludes that GenAI is best used as a supplement to teacher-guided instruction, with teachers checking its output and guiding learners towards critical use. Future research should adopt longitudinal and controlled designs that measure language outcomes directly.</jats:p>

ef96c87c78d4f88ce8de11fcb3a29942540d4d45.abstract: <jats:p>Sinuri ng pag-aaral ang mga karanasan at pananaw ng mga guro sa Filipino sa paggamit ng AI chatbot bilang kagamitang panturo at ang kanilang mga mungkahi para sa responsableng integrasyon nito. title: AI-Generated Feedback for Nursing Documentation and Clinical Reasoning Training: A Scoping Review of Applications and Validation Approaches
container-title: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research
7aa90b9342a0673008e1620356a0908c67545c5b.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: This scoping review aimed to map the application characteristics of AI-generated feedback in nursing documentation and clinical reasoning training and to synthesize the validation approaches used to establish trustworthiness.Material and Methods: Guided by the Arksey and O’Malley framework, a structured search was conducted across five databases for peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2025. Fourteen studies met the eligibility criteria. Data were synthesized descriptively to characterize AI application features and validation practices.Results: The included studies utilized diverse AI systems, including LLM-based platforms, chatbot tutors, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, automated scoring engines, and mixed-reality applications, delivering both real-time and post-task feedback across varied nursing learning contexts. Validation approaches were highly heterogeneous, revealing substantial gaps in the evidence of trustworthiness. While many studies demonstrated strong evidence in expert review, guideline/rubric alignment, and reliability testing, evidence for robustness across cases and safety safeguards remained limited. Conclusion: The findings highlight a critical validation gap, in which technological adoption is advancing faster than the evidence supporting technical reliability, educational validity, and clinical safety trustworthiness. Future research should prioritize standardized validation frameworks that explicitly address safety-critical metrics to ensure the responsible implementation of AI-generated feedback in nursing education.</jats:p>

title: How Behavioral and Normative Characteristics Influence User Satisfaction with Gen-AI Chatbots: The Mediating Roles of Emotional Empathy and Proficiency Evaluation
container-title: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
6c7f7e5205fd44cd9ea30abe91565f21e6db84fe.abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid diffusion of generative AI (Gen-AI) chatbots in service settings, understanding how their interactional characteristics are associated with user satisfaction has become increasingly critical. Although prior research has primarily emphasized system performance, relatively limited attention has been devoted to the underlying psychological mechanisms through which specific interactional features influence user experience. To address this gap, the present study develops a dual-path mediation model that differentiates between affective and cognitive processes, focusing on the mediating roles of emotional empathy and proficiency evaluation. Empirical data were collected via an online survey from 550 users with prior chatbot interaction experience. Structural equation modeling was employed to examine the effects of six chatbot characteristics on user satisfaction. These characteristics were classified into two categories: behavioral interaction characteristics (perceived initiative, perceived responsibility, and perceived timeliness) and normative interaction characteristics (perceived standardization, perceived impartiality, and perceived transparency). The results indicate that all characteristics, except perceived timeliness and perceived impartiality, exert significant positive effects on emotional empathy. Meanwhile, all characteristics exert significant positive effects on proficiency evaluation. The mediation analyses further indicate that emotional empathy and proficiency evaluation mediate some of the relationships between chatbot interactional characteristics and user satisfaction. By disentangling these mechanisms, this study advances current understanding of human–AI interaction from a dual-process perspective and clarifies the distinct roles of affective and cognitive pathways. It also offers practical guidance for the design of Gen-AI systems, suggesting ways to better align system features with users’ emotional expectations and task-oriented needs in real service settings.</jats:p>

title: Green AI for Sustainable Agriculture: An Explainable-AI (XAI) Perspective on Energy-Efficient Crop Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
88212f3988da8ca8d548c2cfd044d37d838996f1.abstract: <jats:p>In modern agriculture precision forecast crop yields, diagnose plant disease and schedule irrigation systems rely on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Cost of training and deploying these models is weighed their accuracy. Two research threads have far developed largely in parallel. Green AI, which treats computational and energy efficiency as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside accuracy and Explainable AI(XAI) uses technology like Shapley additive explanations(SHAP), LIME and Grad-CAM to open the “black box” models so that farmers , and policymakers can act on their predictions.This paper synthesises recent literature (2017–2026) at the intersection of these threads as they apply to agriculture, covering crop-yield prediction, plant-disease detection, and soil- and irrigation-modelling studies that report either energy-efficiency measures or explainability analyses, or both. The synthesis identifies a specific and consistent gap: while explainability is now common in high-performing agricultural ML studies, almost none of them report the energy or carbon cost of training the underlying models, and the one purpose-built Green-AI agriculture framework identified in the review explicitly leaves explainability as future work rather than integrating it. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes a unified Green-XAI methodological framework for agricultural ML that couples resource-appropriate model families – tree-based ensembles such as Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, alongside a compact CNN architecture for imagery – with SHAP-based interpretability and continuous energy/carbon instrumentation across the training and inference lifecycle. The paper details the proposed dataset scope, the governing model equations, the SHAP computation, and an accuracy-versus-energy evaluation protocol, and positions the framework against a comparative synthesis of the performance figures reported by prior studies</jats:p>

title: The Role of AI in Graduate Admissions: Results From the Fall 2025 ETS/NAGAP Survey
