441e7e8de8fd308cf96d6a4ec93745b07c7bc0cd.abstract:
<jats:p>As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to gain prevalence, its use is gaining acceptance in graduate enrollment management (GEM), as professionals begin to think beyond its use for chatbots or recruitment materials to imagine how it can increase efficiency. At the same time, AI’s effects on how GEM professionals perceive traditional application components are beginning to become clearer. GEM professionals have begun to question the value of the traditional personal statement essay and indicate that other elements of a holistic admissions process may consequently gain significance moving forward, including interviews, campus visits, and proctored writing samples under controlled conditions. Here we detail results from the Fall 2025 ETS/NAGAP survey of graduate enrollment management professionals, sharing their experiences of AI’s impact on graduate admissions processes, and conclude by looking forward to how processes and practices are likely to change based on emerging norms and consensus on best practices.
Suggested citation: Gooch, R. M., & Haviland, S. B. (in press). The role of AI in graduate admissions: Results from the Fall 2025 ETS/NAGAP survey (Research Notes). ETS.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Authority in Practice: Generative AI, Decision-Making, and Accountability in Public Administration
container-title: Digital Government: Research and Practice
6291947077e9efdb21bd80154ec49341dcbca7e3.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping public sector decision-making, yet empirical understanding of how it reconfigures governance remains limited. Drawing on 24 semi-structured interviews with public officials in Kenya, this interpretive qualitative study examines how GenAI reshapes decision-making authority, accountability, and trust in human-centred governance. The findings identify three interrelated mechanisms: the concentration of epistemic authority in generative outputs, strongest among officials lacking the technical or situated knowledge to interrogate them; a structured pattern of default compliance and selective override, where organisational norms place the burden of justification on deviation rather than compliance; and a diffusion of accountability through system-based attribution for co-produced outputs, reversible where organisations maintained clear review and documentation. GenAI’s fluent, narrative outputs, unlike the scores and flags of earlier systems, appear to lend a persuasive authority we interpret as theoretically significant rather than formally demonstrated. Officials perceived that resulting opacity and diffused responsibility could strain institutional trust even where performance improves, reflecting their accounts rather than direct evidence from citizens. The study contributes a process-oriented, GenAI-specific analytical framework, empirically grounds hybrid discretion in organisational practice, extends emerging accounts of GenAI-specific accountability entanglement, and offers a theoretically informed account of officials’ perceptions of GenAI’s implications for institutional trust.</jats:p>

title: Secure Communication and Coordination System for Military Operations Using AI and Real-Time Monitoring
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
c53ffd5e2c250b9c36603665c85769cd6df781e4.abstract:
<jats:p>Effective military coordination, information management, and operational decision-making hinge on secure and reliable communication. Unfortunately, systems that depend on fragmented channels and manual processes often face delays, limited visibility of information, security risks, and challenges in coordinating activities among authorized personnel. This paper introduces a Secure Communication and Coordination System for Military Operations that leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Real-Time Monitoring. Our proposed system features secure user authentication, encrypted information exchange, role-based access control, centralized communication management, and real-time activity monitoring—all within a single digital platform. By integrating AI, we enhance capabilities like message classification, information prioritization, anomaly detection, and spotting unusual communication patterns. 
The research follows a design-oriented approach that includes requirements analysis, system design, implementation planning, and thorough functional and security evaluations. Our architecture prioritizes confidentiality, integrity, availability, accountability, and controlled access to sensitive data, while ensuring human oversight of AI-generated recommendations to mitigate risks tied to automated decisions. Ultimately, we aim to provide a structured framework that boosts the security, timeliness, and organization of military communication, facilitating better coordination among authorized personnel. To validate the effectiveness of this system, practical implementation and systematic testing under realistic operating conditions will be essential.</jats:p>

title: Students’ Positions towards Generative AI Technologies:  Strengths and Challenges in Higher Education
container-title: Journal of Educational and Social Research
0e92692b1ed4305609b5bc62447b9cd15693ce42.abstract:
<jats:p>The current study examined the attitudes of Arab students toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education, focusing on their self-reported awareness of its limitations and risks, readiness to use these technologies, concerns, and recommendations for effective integration into teaching and learning. The study employed a mixed-methods design involving 337 undergraduate and postgraduate students from a teacher education college in Israel, recruited through convenience sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire comprising closed-ended and open-ended questions. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and independent-samples t-tests, while qualitative responses were analyzed thematically. The findings revealed an overall mean of 2.91 (SD = 0.783) for students’ self-reported awareness of GenAI limitations and risks and a mean of 3.53 (SD = 0.865) for readiness to use these technologies. Readiness was positively correlated with previous use (r = 0.408, p < 0.001), but not significantly correlated with self-reported familiarity (r = 0.031, p = 0.571). Male students reported significantly higher readiness than female students, t(335) = 2.326, p = 0.021, whereas no significant difference was found by academic level. Students’ concerns had an overall mean of 3.06 (SD = 0.872), with the potential negative effects of overreliance on generic skills emerging as the highest-rated concern. Concerns did not differ significantly by previous-use group, gender, or academic level. The qualitative findings showed that students recommended using GenAI to support research and academic tasks, integrating it into courses and learning activities, verifying the accuracy of generated information, and providing appropriate training and instructor guidance. The findings highlight the importance of a balanced and responsible approach to GenAI integration that combines practical support with critical evaluation, academic integrity, and the preservation of independent thinking.

title: Self-Efficacy as a Mediator between Passion for Using AI Applications and Internet Addiction among Egyptian University Students:  A Structural Equation Modeling Approach
container-title: Journal of Educational and Social Research
a18a3df85e87f08687155b23d6ba56af971791e0.abstract:
<jats:p>The study aimed to examine the mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between passion for using artificial intelligence applications and internet addiction among university students using structural equation modeling. The study sample included two independent samples, selected from students of the Capital University in Cairo, the psychometric verification sample (N=653) and the main sample (N=730). Participants completed three main scales to assess passion for using artificial intelligence applications, self-efficacy, and internet addiction. The results showed a negative effect of harmonious passion for artificial intelligence applications on internet addiction, both directly (?= -0.111) and indirectly through self-efficacy (?= -0.240). The results also indicated a positive effect of obsessive passion for artificial intelligence applications on internet addiction, both directly (?= 0.164) and indirectly through self-efficacy as a partial mediating variable (?= 0.273). The structural model demonstrated a high fit with the data, and all hypothesized correlations were statistically significant. These results generally indicate that the two types of passion for using artificial intelligence applications (harmonious – obsessive) are associated with changes in internet addiction, whether an increase or decrease, either directly or indirectly through their relationship with self-efficacy as a partial mediating variable. This study contributes to deepening the psychological understanding of how artificial intelligence applications influence the emergence of internet addictive behaviours. A harmonious and balanced passion for artificial intelligence applications reduces digital addiction when there is strong self-efficacy among university students.

title: Data Protection Readiness for AI Proctoring  in Albanian Higher Education
container-title: Journal of Educational and Social Research
7a96f615c159f5d443122845d9ebc6bda2b0611c.abstract:
<jats:p>AI-based proctoring has become a contested instrument for safeguarding examination integrity in higher education, yet it processes extensive personal data, including video, audio and potentially biometric data. No publicly documented deployment of AI-based proctoring in Albanian universities was identified, although digitalisation and European Union accession make future adoption plausible. This article therefore asks whether the Albanian data protection framework is ready for that prospect. It applies doctrinal analysis to the Albanian-language text of Law No. 124/2024 “On Personal Data Protection”, the Constitution and the higher education legislation, benchmarks them against the General Data Protection Regulation and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, and draws on decisions from Italy, the Netherlands and the United States as evidence of foreseeable legal risks. Hypothetical deployments are assessed in terms of legal risk, with attention to legal basis, the validity of student consent, special-category data, automated decision-making, impact assessment and proportionality. The analysis finds that Law 124/2024 would make the most intrusive designs, such as automated facial matching, home scans and solely automated sanctions, difficult to justify. It also finds that the legal basis for monitoring in public universities remains uncertain, that no dedicated AI legislation is in force, and that supervisory practice is untested. The article concludes with conditions under which less intrusive designs could potentially comply.

title: The Digital Transformation of Television Broadcasting Supported by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
35b7dc9c798c6869d6eeb6921fd0c44c284f95bc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation brought about by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in television broadcasting within a conceptual and critical framework. It discusses how processes such as content production, automation, scheduling, audience measurement and personalisation have been reorganised through data-driven systems. Furthermore, by assessing the impacts of algorithmicisation on editorial independence, public accountability, transparency, privacy and accountability, the study argues that the future of television broadcasting is shaped not only by technical innovation but also by institutional and ethical choices.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Television Platforms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
054cd1bab132b082e3e6a31810c1cc1a1ff38db7.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how artificial intelligence–driven algorithms on digital television platforms transform the processes of cultural production, distribution, and consumption within the media ecosystem. Focusing on Netflix as a case study, it analyzes how algorithmic recommendation systems structure content visibility, shape user preferences, and reorganize audience behavior through data-driven mechanisms. Drawing on sociological theories of power and cultural production, the study conceptualizes algorithms not merely as technical tools but as socio-technical actors that establish new regimes of visibility and control. In this context, the notion of the “algorithmic field” is proposed to explain how platform-based systems redefine power relations, mediate cultural hierarchies, and reproduce structural inequalities. The findings suggest that digital platforms operate as influential intermediaries that both organize and govern cultural circulation in contemporary media environments.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Local Broadcasting, and the Logic of Innovation From the Periphery
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
993d09fe2a97e708c317641849a351071457e373.abstract: <jats:p>Drawing on a qualitative case study of Radio Kepulauan Seribu, this chapter examines how these tensions unfold within Indonesia's small-island broadcasting context. Rather than framing AI as a disruptive force that automates editorial work, the chapter advances the concept of guided augmentation, in which AI supports preparatory cognitive tasks while ethical judgment, contextual interpretation, and public responsibility remain human-centered. Through interviews and non-participant observation, the study demonstrates how AI adoption emerges from structural constraints, limited resources, and public service mandates rather than technological ambition. The findings challenge dominant, Global North–centric narratives of AI-driven media transformation by presenting small islands as sites of adaptive innovation and relational accountability. By reframing hybrid broadcasting as a stable, context-sensitive media configuration, the chapter contributes to broader debates on AI, ethics, and the future of broadcasting in community-oriented media ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: The Transformation of News Discourse in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
8e94f02ed0fdcf254c98a1451e802610a07e5039.abstract: <jats:p>In the digital media ecosystem, AI-based text generation systems, particularly large language models, have become increasingly influential in news production processes. These systems are viewed not only as technical tools but also as new mechanisms of discourse production that reshape how news content is created. This development has made the comparative examination of human-produced and AI-generated news texts increasingly important. In this context, the study comparatively analyzes news texts selected from international news organizations such as Al Jazeera and Reuters alongside texts generated by ChatGPT. The research focuses on military interventions and violent incidents in Palestine. Using document analysis as a qualitative research method, the study evaluates the texts through Teun A. van Dijk's Critical Discourse Analysis approach and identifies major differences between human-produced and AI-generated news texts in terms of discourse structure, framing strategies, linguistic choices, and meaning production practices.</jats:p>

title: Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
36d6b77407653d455c80e2f500634a6232d7a5a9.abstract: <jats:p>The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Methods to Optimize Energy System Stability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
638e43b89445c1c4efd078d51246af0e90e11d12.abstract: <jats:p>This article presents a systematic analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods applied to the optimization of energy system stability. Deep learning architectures for forecasting electricity demand and renewable energy generation, reinforcement learning algorithms for microgrid control, the concept of digital twins, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are examined. The application of hybrid models reduces forecasting errors by 20–35% over ultra-short-term forecasting horizons ranging from several minutes to several hours. The transition to probabilistic forecasting reduces balancing costs by 8–15%, while the use of digital twins decreases operating costs by 15–25%. Current challenges limiting the implementation of intelligent technologies in the energy sector are identified, and priority areas for further research are outlined. The results are systematized in comparative tables suitable for practical use when selecting appropriate methodological tools.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health: Research Trends, Hotspots, and Emerging Themes (2004–2024)
container-title: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
92123be89a5907171175748ac1eab0d0dc52bb23.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Aims: Mental health disorders constitute a major global health burden, while mental health services remain inadequately resourced, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, have opened new possibilities for the early detection, diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment of mental health conditions. Despite rapid growth, research in this field is highly interdisciplinary and fragmented, limiting understanding of its overall development. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database. Peer-reviewed journal articles published between January 1, 2004, and December 31, 2024, were retrieved through title-based searches combining AI- and mental health-related terms. Bibliometric indicators, including publication output, authors, institutions, countries, journals, funding agencies, and highly cited articles, were analyzed. Science-mapping techniques and network visualization using VOS viewer were employed to explore intellectual, social, and conceptual research structures. Results: A total of 14,904 publications were included. Research growth was modest until 2015 but accelerated markedly after 2019 (R² = 0.9685). The field was dominated by medicine, neuroscience, and computer science. The United States, China, and the United Kingdom emerged as the leading contributors in both productivity and international collaboration. Key research hotspots included AI-driven neuroimaging, natural language processing for mental health assessment, social media–based surveillance, and digital mental health interventions. Conclusion: AI research in mental health has expanded rapidly, progressing from neurobiological modeling to scalable digital applications. Future advancement will require ethical governance, representative datasets, interdisciplinary collaboration, and robust clinical validation to ensure safe, effective, and equitable implementation.</jats:p>

title: An Ecocentric Assessment Framework for Artificial Intelligence and Computational Design in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
9e7e6f7f02173ae504c123506aca35adbabc2089.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) supports environmental performance prediction and the evaluation of alternatives in architectural design. However, improvements in energy or carbon indicators alone do not demonstrate that non-human life holds independent value in design decisions. This chapter examines AI and related computational design approaches in architecture from an ecocentric perspective through a focused narrative review and conceptual synthesis supported by a structured database search. The 375 raw records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science were reduced to 256 unique records; following title and abstract screening, a final purposive selection of 19 studies was established. Together with one supplementary publication, the 20 documents were examined under the themes of performance and decision-making, life cycle boundaries, the representation of non-human life, habitat geometry and materials, time and maintenance, and visual generation and ecological validation. The synthesis informs a preliminary ecocentric assessment framework comprising three dimensions: stakeholder scope, integration of environmental and ecological impacts into decision-making, and ecological responsibility. By distinguishing computational success from ecological outcomes, the framework provides an analytical basis for examining who benefits from design decisions, how environmental and ecological requirements influence those decisions, and how responsibility for their outcomes is addressed.</jats:p>

title: From Vernacular Ecological Intelligence to Planetary Design: Life Cycle Thinking as a Framework for Ecological Transformation in Architecture
container-title: Research into Ecological Transformation in Architectural Sciences: From Anthropocentric Design to Ecology-Focused Design
2fe3cfa7ebe20f96ad17653a7bea70674b592d24.abstract: <jats:p>The ecological transformation of architecture requires reconsidering how architectural knowledge is produced, environmental consequences are evaluated, and responsibility is addressed across spatial, temporal, and ecological scales. This chapter brings vernacular ecological knowledge into dialogue with Life Cycle Thinking and Planetary Design. Vernacular architecture is approached as a dynamic socio-ecological knowledge system shaped by culture, climate, materiality, and collective practices. Maintenance, repair, adaptability, and intergenerational learning are examined as forms of situated ecological intelligence rather than historical models to be replicated. Life Cycle Thinking provides a framework for integrating place-based knowledge into contemporary architectural decisions, extending environmental assessment beyond carbon to circularity, biodiversity, regeneration, cultural continuity, and resilience. The relationship with Planetary Design is understood as a scalar and epistemic connection through which local knowledge informs decisions affecting broader ecological and material systems. Rather than prescribing a universal method, Planetary Design is presented as a boundary-aware, sufficiency-led, regenerative, justice-oriented, and adaptive approach. The chapter argues that ecological transformation depends on combining quantitative assessment with local knowledge, social needs, interconnected system boundaries, and long-term stewardship.</jats:p>

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Reconstruction of Subjectivity in Literary Creation
container-title: Frontiers in International Humanities & Social Sciences
9bfbc70885f0b03f6339b725301ad8597529d0e7.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence can participate in literary composition by proposing plots, producing passages and revising prose. Its participation raises questions about the position from which a work is imagined, judged and presented to readers. This paper examines the reconstruction of literary subjectivity through theoretical argument and analysis of research on assisted writing. It distinguishes subjectivity from observable interaction, the institutional attribution of authorship and evaluations of textual quality. Literary theories of authorship and dialogue are brought into conversation with accounts of writing processes and technological mediation, with attention to their different explanatory purposes. A comparative framework considers intention, lived experience, narrative form and responsibility across conception, drafting and revision. The analysis identifies tensions involving delegated intention, narrative anchoring, simulated experience, stylistic specificity and public attribution. It proposes that agency can be sustained through active reconsideration of creative aims, consequential aesthetic judgement, attention to experiential and cultural particularity, and accountable relations with readers. These are analytical proposals, not a validated measure of subjectivity. Existing studies concern specific interfaces and writing tasks and cannot establish a universal effect on literary identity. The paper reports no new experiment or interviews; its focus is short fiction and novel writing.</jats:p>

title: Visualizing use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
container-title: Learning Futures and Emerging Technologies
4bca47f413a747fbb465cfa7fe3a205717cd5d47.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Higher education students are engaged with academic learning and research using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications. A major shift in pedagogical approach surfaces many challenges to academic integrity that urging to redefining assessment model and ethical literacy. This study aims to investigate impact of the GenAI apps among the students using survey of technical and non-technical disciplines. Survey is mainly focused on: use of GenAI apps, variations in observed effectiveness and student’s usage pattern, level of adoption and acceptance of GenAI apps. Reviews of existing literature on the implications of GenAI and emerging need for systemic changes are discussed with reference to result.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey was developed to assess the integration of GenAI apps in the higher education. It was conducted with undergraduate and postgraduate students so as to find the adoption and acceptance rate of GenAI apps among the students; it has been partitioned into two categories: non-technical disciplines and technical disciplines. Students from the social science and pure sciences are in the non-technical disciplines, while students from computer science and engineering students are in the technical discipline. The questionnaire included a mix of multiple-choice questions, scale items and open-ended responses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research is classified for students into technical and non-technical disciplines, revealing notable differences in adoption patterns. First, students from non-technical disciplines are not entirely using GenAI applications. Second, effectiveness of the usage can be analyzed by the purpose of usage of GenAI apps which is shown by graphs. However, technical students show higher inclination for AI usages. Third, regarding adoption or acceptance, many rural students initially adopt it through classmates or roommates. In contrast, students in urban areas, especially in technical disciplines, spend higher hours; here, they accept the technology and update themselves with new technology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey did not assess the accuracy or effectiveness of GenAI outputs. This is a limitation for drawing conclusions about the performance quality of these apps across disciplines.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Students come from different parts of India, so it is also possible that the places where they previously studied lacked facilities such as internet connectivity and stable power supply. This influences the usage. Students from many disciplines participated in the survey, so their perspective to look at the GenAI apps is a unique feature. GenAI apps are accepted among technical students, and non-technical students are gradually adopting. Over-reliance may hinder the individual learning and creativity; it can be an aid to the learning but not as a supplement of human intelligence. Universities face challenges in formulating policies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: DAVLAT XIZMATLARIDA SUN’IY INTELLEKTNI HUQUQIY TARTIBGA SOLISH: YEVROPA ITTIFOQI, AQSH VA XITOY MODELLARINING QIYOSIY TAHLILI VA O‘ZBEKISTON UCHUN XULOSALAR

title: Artificial intelligence-driven governance threshold and sellers’ performance in cross-border e-commerce platforms
container-title: South African Journal of Economic and Management Sciences
d7afb4489e313411b72ec593a41d8660fca53a6b.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven governance systems increasingly regulate seller decisions in cross-border e-commerce platforms. Mainstream research has treated AI-driven control intensity as a monotonically positive lever for platform coordination and seller outcomes.
Aim: This study examines whether AI-driven governance intensity exhibits a non-linear performance boundary and identifies the mechanism under which governance expansion becomes counterproductive.
Setting: The study was conducted among cross-border sellers on Amazon Global Selling, Alibaba International, and Shopee across China, Southeast Asia, and Eastern Europe.
Method: Survey data from 207 cross-border sellers were analysed by using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with 5000-resample bootstrapping. Nonlinearity was confirmed by using a dual-condition criterion and a one-sided monotonicity test.
Results: An inverted-U relationship emerged between AI governance intensity and seller performance (b_linear = 0.28, p = 0.021; b_quadratic = −0.19, p = 0.038), with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16 (bias-corrected and accelerated [BCa] 95% confidence interval: [3.9, 4.5]). Excessive governance suppresses independent strategic learning (b = −0.34, p < 0.001), partially mediating the performance penalty (indirect = −0.16; direct = 0.14, p = 0.046). Market volatility amplifies the post-threshold effect (b = 0.19, p = 0.014), with 23% of sampled sellers in the substitution regime.
Conclusion: Governance intensity must be calibrated relative to a structural threshold beyond which automation displaces the strategic-learning capability on which competitive performance depends.
Contribution: This study contributes a regime-contingent threshold model showing that AI-driven governance intensity and seller performance follow an inverted-U relationship, with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16. Strategic-learning suppression is empirically confirmed as the erosion mechanism (partial mediation, indirect effect = −0.16), and market volatility amplifies the post-threshold penalty, grounded in dynamic capabilities theory and offering platform designers a calibration boundary rather than a general prescription.</jats:p>

title: Reconstructing Core Competencies of Front-Office Employees in South Korean Professional Sports Organizations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study
container-title: Behavioral Sciences
e587e52f253c04e2e45f5c221904e7f9112853ee.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly reshapes organizational decision-making, fan engagement, and business operations, the competencies expected of front-office employees are also evolving. This study aimed to reconstruct the core competencies required of front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations in the AI era. To this end, a three-round Delphi study was conducted with 20 experts from academia, South Korean professional sports organizations, and research institutes. The Delphi process involved generating competency items, evaluating their relevance, and establishing expert consensus regarding the final competency framework. The findings identified 28 competency items grouped into the following five competency domains: Data & AI Utilization Competency, Human–AI Collaboration Competency, Marketing & Fan Engagement Competency, Communication & Execution Competency, and Ethics & Values Competency. These findings suggest that competencies in AI-enabled professional sports organizations extend beyond technical proficiency and warrant an integrated combination of technological, collaborative, organizational, relational, and ethical capabilities. This study refines the application of competency theory to AI-supported work by providing a context-specific framework for front-office employees in South Korean professional sports organizations. The proposed framework offers a foundation for understanding how South Korean professional sports organizations may reconstruct workforce competencies in response to the evolving demands of the AI era.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digitalization in Energy Markets: A Comprehensive Review of Optimization, Risk Management, Blockchain Integration, and the Electric Vehicle Landscape
container-title: Journal of Applied Sciences and Modelling
1455c02d6e2cf24cb2fe854491344b38f1e668ac.abstract: <jats:p>This paper analyzes the considerable impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization on energy markets and trading systems, as well as the expanding electric vehicle (EV) industry and its challenges. As the complexity of energy systems increases due to the incorporation of renewable energy, distributed generation (DG), and evolving regulations, traditional market models struggle to adapt. This evaluation examines how AI and digital technologies can enhance energy generation, distribution, and consumption across various applications, including improved forecasting, grid management, market organization, risk assessment, and automated trading. The research integrates findings related to AI-driven market improvement, risk evaluation, and relationships with blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and smart grids. The analysis also explores the potential effects of cryptocurrency mining on the energy industry, in both beneficial and detrimental ways. It examines global innovations in this field and specifically addresses the impacts of Monte Carlo simulation (MCS). Charts and factual investigations are examined, indicating potential avenues for future investigation. It emphasizes the opportunities and challenges that AI and digitalization present for the energy industry, highlighting the need to address information security, regulatory compliance, and ethical issues to advance a sustainable and resilient energy future.</jats:p>

title: Fully automated artificial intelligence-driven targeted literature review on clinical outcomes in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
container-title: Indian Journal of Medical Sciences
28dd4822fd1b581d47fdbef22bfbfc3e4270a713.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Evidence generation is a multistep process that remains labor-intensive and time-consuming. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled platforms support literature reviews, their complete automation is scarce. We utilized an online AI suite, SymproAI, to perform a fully automated targeted literature review (TLR) on treatment outcomes in patients with aquaporin-4 (AQP4)-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) and compared its performance with the manual process. This TLR summarizes the efficacy and safety of Food and Drug Administration-approved biologics or conventional immunosuppressants in patients with AQP4-positive NMOSD using SymproAI. Performance was validated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, overall accuracy, and overall speed of performance. SymproAI searches demonstrated 98.2% agreement with the manual retrieval (1,721 vs. 1,691 citations). For title/abstract and full-text screening, SymproAI achieved 94.4% and 80.5% accuracy, respectively. SymproAI generated TLR-identified 44 publications identical to those provided by the manual review. Overall, the TLR timeframe was estimated at ~120 min using SymproAI, compared with 96 work hours required for the manual process. The generative feature of SymproAI demonstrated good agreement with human findings and data interpretation. Both processes agreed on eculizumab with the strongest relapse-prevention efficacy (94.2% risk reduction), followed by satralizumab (74–79%) and inebilizumab (73%). Across conventional therapies, rituximab demonstrated superior relapse prevention compared with these oral immunosuppressants (mycophenolate mofetil and azathioprine), reducing relative relapse risk by ~60% (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    = 0.046), highlighting its greater efficacy. SymproAI enables rapid, accurate, and reproducible automation of TLRs without compromising study selection or clinical conclusions, supporting accelerated and methodologically rigorous evidence synthesis in time-sensitive clinical settings.
                  </jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Learning Behavior and Critical Thinking in Higher Education-A PLS-SEM Mediation Approach
container-title: Algorithmica International Journal of Computational Sciences
3983b77841bc76a1976c440d1ed04932f17c98f8.abstract:
<jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming higher education through personalised learning, intelligent tutoring, adaptive systems, and generative tools. However, concerns remain that excessive reliance on artificial intelligence may encourage cognitive offloading and weaken independent reasoning. This study examines the relationships among artificial intelligence use, learning behaviour, and critical thinking among students at Africa University in Zimbabwe, with learning behaviour tested as a mediator. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used, and data from 299 undergraduate and postgraduate students were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling. The measurement model demonstrated strong reliability and validity, while the structural model supported all four hypotheses. Artificial intelligence use positively predicted learning behaviour and critical thinking, and learning behaviour strongly predicted critical thinking. Learning behaviour also partially mediated the relationship between artificial intelligence use and critical thinking. The findings indicate that the educational value of artificial intelligence depends less on the mere use of technology than on whether it promotes active, reflective, and self-regulated learning. The study contributes empirical evidence from a Sub-Saharan African university and provides implications for the responsible integration of artificial intelligence in higher education.

Keywords—Artificial intelligence: Critical thinking: Higher education: Learning behaviour: Partial least squares structural equation modelling: Self-regulated learning</jats:p>

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN IMAGE-BASED DETECTION of FALL ARMYWORM: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
container-title: Algorithmica International Journal of Computational Sciences
8946c2c53f670de4d73522a8848b78dd6afff936.abstract:
<jats:p>Gaining full control over Fall Armyworm (FAW) infestation entails global food security. Several studies experimented with image-based Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques to manage FAW infestation and presented attractive findings. A systematic review of 22 studies was conducted in this work for the period from 2018 to 2025 that focused on detection of FAW using AI image-based methodologies. Based on the results reported in these studies, AI models exhibited exceptional performance in both FAW detection using its images and damage from it; however, datasets used were from controlled conditions. Some studies used images captured by smartphones and drone exhibiting reduced performance, bringing realism to this research. The main factors that have widened this ‘lab-to-field’ gap include datasets that are not reflective of the fields and geographical realities. Therefore, concentrating on data acquisition and model robustness instead of focusing on developing isolated algorithms gives momentum to lab work toward the field. The need to improve generalization of AI model requires further research to enhance robustness of these models by reducing sensitivity to environmental variability. Also, the adoption of these models by smallholder farmers requires further research on handheld, low-cost and edge-deployable tools. 
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Computer Vision; Deep Learning; Fall Armyworm; Pest Management</jats:p>

d5e98629272e9e41653142655b40ee55817bb172.abstract: <jats:p>У статті за результатами доповіді на XI Польсько-українському науковому форумі проаналізовано стан і перспективи регулювання використання штучного інтелекту (ШІ) в закладах професійної освіти України в умовах війни та європейської інтеграції. Показано, що генеративний ШІ увійшов в освітню практику раніше, ніж сформувалися правила його застосування, що зумовлює явище «тіньової цифровізації» – масового використання технології поза межами інституційних норм, прозорості та підзвітності. Здійснено аналіз Закону України «Про академічну доброчесність», який уперше на законодавчому рівні запровадив обов’язок повідомляти про використання об’єктів, згенерованих ШІ, та новий вид порушення – недоброчесне використання результатів, згенерованих ШІ. Встановлено, що закон, вносячи зміни до законів про вищу, фахову передвищу та повну загальну середню освіту, не містить спеціальних норм щодо професійної освіти, а для типових результатів навчання в цій ланці (навчальних робіт практичного характеру) вирішальним стає не обов’язок розкриття, а визначені педагогом умови виконання завдання. На підставі зарубіжних емпіричних досліджень обґрунтовано, що ставка на технічний контроль, зокрема на детектори ШІ, є методологічно ненадійною, створює ризик упереджених рішень і запускає «цикл недовіри» між здобувачами освіти й педагогами. Розкрито специфіку ризиків професійної освіти: безпеку праці, захист даних неповнолітніх здобувачів, практичну підготовку на робочих місцях. Запропоновано трирівневу модель переходу «від контролю до довіри» (держава – заклад освіти – педагог і майстер виробничого навчання) з процедурою «дозвіл – прозорість – перевірка – рефлексія – відповідальність», узгоджену з нормами закону та підходами Регламенту ЄС про штучний інтелект. Окреслено напрями польсько-української співпраці у цій сфері.</jats:p>

title: An Auditable Downstream Safety-Intelligence Framework for Manufacturing Workplaces: Reliability-Aware PPE Evidence, Regulation-Grounded Retrieval, and Role-Specific Decision Support
container-title: Applied Sciences
80c82a9906c570847d2f3c827f8ecb2fd91ebd0f.abstract: <jats:p>Vision-based industrial safety monitoring increasingly integrates heterogeneous accidents, personal protective equipment (PPE), and semantic evidence, yet preserving their reliability, uncertainty, and provenance throughout downstream decision support remains challenging. This study proposes an auditable downstream safety-intelligence framework that transforms frozen multimodal perception outputs into structured event evidence. Worker-centered temporal PPE observations are processed into Candidate and Confirmed operational evidence while accident-related uncertainty is preserved. In parallel, regulation-grounded retrieval maps the same evidence to candidate regulatory context from a frozen Korean industrial-safety corpus, and manager- and worker-oriented outputs are generated under distinct information boundaries and independently verified. On a fixed internal benchmark of 150 videos and 3000 frames, the Full-clean configuration achieved 98.23% frame-level accuracy (Macro-F1, 97.47%) and 98.67% video-level accuracy, although the video-level difference from the intermediate configuration was not statistically significant. PPE-violation detection based on the Raw temporal state achieved an F1-score of 99.31% on the ground-truth normal-scene stratum. Controlled Legal-RAG regression reproduced all 117 invariant cases and behaved as predefined across the 32 query-invariant evidence-change cases and the single query-changed case. All 234 notification–report links, 44 PPE semantic checks, and 82 verifier findings satisfied predefined validation criteria. These findings constitute an internal feasibility validation of provenance-preserving, human-review-oriented safety intelligence rather than independent external validation or evidence of field performance.</jats:p>

title: Reimagining Public Service Marketing in the UAE Through Artificial Intelligence: Dynamic Capabilities and Public Value Perspective
container-title: Administrative Sciences
c379c2c681cb269ef1f9de37ea7771b1a3b36ec0.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping public service marketing by enabling governments to deliver more personalized, responsive, and citizen-centered services. This study examines how AI-enabled public service marketing contributes to public value creation in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), drawing on public value theory and dynamic capabilities theory. A systematic literature review was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. From 460 records published between 2019 and 2025, 21 sources were selected comprising 18 peer-reviewed journal articles and three contextual sources through PRISMA-based screening, quality appraisal, and thematic analysis. Four interrelated themes emerged: AI-enabled public service marketing and public value creation; dynamic capabilities supporting AI integration; citizen experience, trust, and engagement; and citizen awareness, understanding, and participation. The findings indicate that predictive analytics, digital assistants and integrated smart government platforms may improve service personalization, accessibility, responsiveness, and citizen engagement. However, sustained value creation depends on organizational capabilities for strategic sensing, organizational learning, and institutional transformation, supported by ethical governance, transparency and responsible data practices. The study proposes an AI-powered public value creation framework linking AI technologies, organizational capabilities, citizen engagement and ethical governance. It contributes to digital governance and public administration scholarship by offering a theoretically grounded agenda for examining AI-enabled public service marketing in the UAE.</jats:p>

title: The Interplay Between Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Ac-counting, Digital Leadership, and Sustainable Competitive Performance
container-title: Administrative Sciences
d30f03819c7519381b41ff0102bfa9179d1a7de7.abstract: <jats:p>This paper explores the impact of Artificial Intelligence in Accounting (AIIA) on Sustainable Competitive Performance (SCP). It also examines how digital leadership (DL) moderates the AIIA-SCP relationship. Data were gathered from accountants, finance managers, CFOs, and internal auditors working at firms listed on the Egyptian Stock Exchange (ESE), with a sample size of 417. The analysis was conducted using Smart-PLS software. Results show that all elements of AIIA positively and significantly influence SCP. Moreover, DL enhances the connection between AIIA and SCP, strengthening their relationship. The model explains 76.2% of SCP’s variance. These findings serve as a useful benchmark for corporate policy and provide key insights for improving competitive advantage and performance. This research also has important managerial implications, highlighting AIIA and DL’s potential to boost SCP. As one of the first studies to examine DL’s moderating role in the AIIA-SCP link, it offers valuable insights for emerging markets.</jats:p>

title: صعوبات استخدام التكنولوجيا المساندة وتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في العملية التعليمية بحث نظري تحليلي في ضوء الأدبيات التربوية

530f778fe28301b802aeb0396f3ddad527649383.abstract:
<jats:p>يهدف البحث إلى تحليل صعوبات استخدام التكنولوجيا المساندة وتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في العملية التعليمية، وبيان العلاقة بين إتاحة الأدوات وجودة توظيفها تربويًا. وتتمثل المشكلة في أن توفير الأجهزة والمنصات لا يضمن مشاركة المتعلمين أو تحسن تعلمهم، ولا سيما لدى ذوي الإعاقة وصعوبات التعلم. اعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي من خلال مراجعة سردية موجهة لعينة قصدية من مجموعة قصدية من المصادر العربية والأجنبية، تشمل دراسات محكمة وأطرًا تربوية وتقارير مؤسسية ومعيارًا للإتاحة الرقمية، منشورة بين عامي 1988 و2026، مع الاستعانة بالمصادر التأسيسية لتفسير التقبل التقني والعبء المعرفي ومعرفة المعلم.
نُظمت المادة في محاور تقنية ومالية ومهنية ونفسية ولغوية وأخلاقية وتقويمية. ويخلص التحليل إلى أن الصعوبة لا تنشأ من خصائص الأداة وحدها، وإنما من ضعف التوافق بين احتياجات المتعلم والمهمة التعليمية وبيئة التطبيق والدعم المؤسسي. وقد يتيح الذكاء الاصطناعي تبسيط المحتوى وتعدد طرق التعبير، لكنه يضيف متطلبات للتحقق من الدقة والتحيز وحماية البيانات. ويقدم البحث تصورًا إجرائيًا يبدأ بتحديد الحاجة، ثم تجربة محدودة، فتدريب ودعم، ثم تقويم يربط القرار باستقلالية المتعلم وجودة الإنجاز.
يوصي البحث بإشراك المتعلمين في الاختيار، واختبار إتاحة المنصات والمحتوى العربي، وتأهيل المعلمين على التصميم التربوي والتحقق من المخرجات، وتحديد الاستخدام المسموح في التقويم. وهذه استنتاجات نظرية ومقترحات قابلة للاختبار، وليست نتائج دراسة ميدانية أو تقديرات إحصائية لمدى انتشار الصعوبات.</jats:p>

title: Navigating the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Frontier: Strategic pathways for Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption and entrepreneurial resilience in South African Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs)
container-title: E-Journal of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences
703e3c7efb4287b289410eafe07238cb633ffa45.abstract: <jats:p>The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) presents both opportunities and challenges for Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) in developing economies, particularly in South Africa, where the digital divide and resource constraints remain significant. This study examines how adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance entrepreneurial resilience and foster sustainable competitive advantage in SMMEs. Using a desktop research design, 38 academic and industry sources were systematically synthesised to identify drivers, barriers, and strategic pathways for digital transformation. The findings reveal that while AI technologies have substantial potential to improve operational efficiency, decision-making, and market responsiveness, SMMEs are hindered by financial limitations, inadequate technological infrastructure, skills shortages, and regulatory challenges. The study highlights the pivotal role of entrepreneurial leadership and dynamic capabilities in enabling firms to adapt to technological disruptions and sustain performance in volatile environments. Moreover, integrating supportive innovation ecosystems, including entrepreneurial universities and collaborative networks, is critical for knowledge transfer, capacity building, and access to innovation resources. A strategic framework is proposed that emphasises digital transformation, capability development, and ecosystem collaboration, providing actionable pathways for SMMEs to navigate the 4IR frontier. The research contributes to theory by contextualising the Resource-Based View (RBV), Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Diffusion of Innovation Theory within resource-constrained, rural environments, thereby addressing the limitations of predominantly Western-centric models. In practice, it offers policymakers, business owners, and practitioners guidance on fostering innovation-driven growth, narrowing the digital divide, and building resilience among SMMEs.</jats:p>

title: FROM ADOPTION TO TRANSFORMATION: ORGANIZATIONAL OUTCOMES OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION WITHIN TEXTILE SMES IN PAKISTAN
container-title: JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES DEVELOPMENT
883cbf3a8a204be8764bada393708dba5834b1c5.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose: The purpose of this study is to examine the organizational outcomes achieved by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Pakistan's textile industry after adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. This study uses the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities (DC) theories to understand how AI adoption will impact process efficiency, customer and market responsiveness, innovation, costs, and strategic growth. Design/Methodology/Approach: This study employed a qualitative multi-case design. Eleven SMEs from the textile industry in Punjab, Pakistan, were interviewed. The SMEs were then categorized by AI maturity level (Nascent, Intermediate, and Advanced). Thematic Analysis was conducted in NVivo 12 using the six steps outlined by Braun and Clarke (2006). Findings: Overall, 5 outcome categories were identified: Process Efficiency, Customer & Market Responsiveness, Innovation & Improvement, Cost Reduction & Improvements, and Strategic Growth. The range of outcomes seen differed across the AI maturity levels. Those with a higher maturity level experienced larger organizational change. Originality/Value: This study provides detailed qualitative insights into the outcomes of AI adoption in Pakistan's textile SMEs. Using RBV and Dynamic Capabilities theories, this study demonstrates how organizational AI maturity influences outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Emotional Intelligence and its Relationship to Self-Esteem among High School Students
container-title: International Journal of Educational Sciences and Arts
b620dc5c8866eb5f119bff7c665a7d4c844bfc52.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to determine the level of emotional intelligence and its relationship to self-esteem among secondary school students, and to identify the nature of the correlation between the average responses of the sample members and their scores on emotional intelligence and self-esteem. The researcher used the descriptive correlational approach. The study sample consisted of 150 secondary school students. The results showed that the prevailing level of emotional intelligence among secondary school students was high, with a mean score of 0.05 (standard deviation 0.05). Self-esteem among secondary school students in Taif Governorate was moderate, with a mean score of 0.05 (standard deviation 0.05). A correlation was found between the level of emotional intelligence and self-esteem among secondary school students in Taif Governorate. In light of these results, the researcher recommends that program designers at the Ministry of Education design long-term programs to promote and develop emotional intelligence practices, given the significant impact of this approach. To create a positive self-esteem within the school.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Emotional Intelligence and Perceived Coach Support in Sport Motivation Among Adolescent Athletes
container-title: Baltic Journal of Sport and Health Sciences
a48fd4e555bff021ad8c9195eee9124b7dc0f1be.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Sport motivation plays a crucial role in adolescents’ long-term participation in sport and psychological wellbeing. Emotional intelligence (EI) and perceived coach support are considered important psychological resources. However, their contribution to autonomous and controlled sport motivation among adolescent athletes remains insufficiently explored. Therefore, this study aimed to examine how EI and perceived coach support predict different types of sport motivation among adolescent athletes.
Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 276 adolescent athletes. Participants completed the Schutte Emotional Intelligence Scale, the Sport Motivation Scale II (SMS-II), and a questionnaire assessing perceived coach support.
Results: EI and coach support were positively associated with each other and with both autonomous and controlled motivation. Hierarchical regression analysis showed that both EI and perceived coach support significantly predicted autonomous and controlled motivation, EI demonstrating the stronger predictive effect. Gender also significantly and negatively predicted both forms of motivation.
Conclusions: EI and perceived coach support are important predictors of both autonomous and controlled sport motivation among adolescent athletes. Therefore, interventions aimed at strengthening sport motivation should address both athletes’ emotional competencies and the supportive role of coaches.
Keywords: Emotional competence, autonomous motivation, controlled motivation, coach–athlete relationship, youth athletes</jats:p>

<jats:p>Introducción: La inteligencia artificial generativa puede apoyar la comprensión lectora en inglés mediante explicaciones de vocabulario, resúmenes y preguntas guiadas. La evidencia sobre Microsoft 365 Copilot en la educación superior latinoamericana sigue siendo limitada. Este estudio examinó la comprensión lectora y las percepciones y experiencias de estudiantes de Física de la ESPOCH, Ecuador. Metodología: Se aplicó un enfoque mixto secuencial explicativo con un componente preexperimental de un solo grupo, con pretest y postest, en 23 estudiantes de primer nivel durante ocho sesiones semanales. Se utilizaron una prueba de lectura de 30 ítems, un cuestionario Likert de 20 ítems y entrevistas semiestructuradas. Resultados: La media aumentó de 14,57 (DE = 2,35) a 20,74 (DE = 3,00), con una ganancia de 6,17 puntos, t(22) = 18,03, p < 0,001 y dz de Cohen = 3,76. La percepción global fue favorable (M = 81,78/100; DE = 7,31) y superó el valor de referencia de 60 (Wilcoxon W = 276; p < 0,001). Las entrevistas destacaron el apoyo al vocabulario, la interpretación, la confianza y la participación, junto con dificultades al formular instrucciones, problemas de conexión y preocupaciones sobre dependencia de la IA. Conclusiones: Copilot se percibió como recurso complementario útil. La mejora observada coincidió con la intervención, pero la ausencia de grupo de control impide establecer causalidad.
 </jats:p>

title: Advances in Artificial Intelligence for the Ultrasound Diagnosis of Thyroid Nodules
container-title: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences
01c1889222964d368089730eb84373b3a4334a2b.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing detection of thyroid nodules and thyroid cancer has made timely malignancy detection and the avoidance of unnecessary biopsy, surgery, and overtreatment important clinical priorities. Ultrasound is a convenient, real-time, inexpensive, easy-to-obtain and repeated non-invasive imaging method for screening and risk assessment of thyroid nodules. The diagnostic results of human operators and equipment settings can affect the sensitivity of image interpretation. Recently, with the development of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and deep learning have been applied to thyroid disease diagnosis. Segmentation of images, feature extraction, differentiation of benign and malignant nodules, risk stratification, biopsy decision support, cytological examination, contrast-enhanced ultrasound video analysis, and prediction of lymph node metastasis are all included. Research has shown that, at present, AI support can improve the precision and uniformity of diagnosis independently of operator experience. It will also be convenient for new doctors and health workers in primary care to use. Review of the technical foundations, current applications, advantages and disadvantages, and future directions of artificial intelligence in ultrasound diagnosis of benign and malignant thyroid tumors. To provide information on the clinical application and use of these technologies in personalised diagnosis and treatment.</jats:p>

title: Kecerdasan Emosional dan Kepemimpinan Pelayan Kepala Madrasah Berbasis Keseimbangan Zikir dan Pikir: Studi Kasus di MAN 1 Nganjuk
Emotional Intelligence and Servant Leadership of the Head of Madrasah Based on the Balance of Dhikr and Pikir: A Case Study at MAN 1 Nganjuk
container-title: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
32bb8d45fda5d4c45467005aeb813fc9b3dcb8c5.abstract: <jats:p>Aim: This study examines how a madrasah principal enacts emotional intelligence, identifies its supporting and inhibiting factors, and explores the integration of dhikr and pikir within the ulul albab paradigm at MAN 1 Nganjuk, Indonesia. Method: A qualitative single-case study was conducted using three semi-structured interviews with the principal, participant observation by a researcher working as a teacher, and institutional documents. Data were analysed through condensation, display, and conclusion drawing. Results: Emotional intelligence was manifested through tabayun-based self-regulation, personal engagement and informal dialogue, and participatory, bottom-up communication. The principal understood leadership as service (khadimul ummah), delegated responsibilities according to organisational roles, and retained accountability. Enabling conditions included leadership experience, willingness to learn, clear delegation structures, and external partnerships; obstacles included resistance to change, limited cohesion, cultural differences, and unbudgeted needs. Decision-making combined verification and rational analysis with prayer, followed by spiritual consultation when reasoning reached an impasse. This integration was most evident in the principal's decision-making, while its application in classroom teaching remained insufficiently explored. Evidence came primarily from one principal, limiting transferability across educational settings. Implications: These findings suggest that madrasah leadership development should combine emotional regulation, participatory approaches, and spiritual reflection. They also highlight the importance of understanding Islamic educational leadership within its organisational and cultural context. Originality/Added Value: The study proposes a context-specific, provisional conceptual model connecting emotional intelligence, servant leadership, and the ulul albab paradigm. It identifies tabayun-based self-regulation as a distinctive, contextually documented expression of emotional intelligence in madrasah leadership, without claiming that the proposed model has been causally tested.</jats:p>

title: The Influence of Green Leadership, Emotional Intelligence, and 21st-Century Competence on Teacher Performance at the Sultan Agung Education Foundation in Pematangsiantar
container-title: The International Journal of Advanced Technology and Social Sciences
515ac406664c349d4ab9018a1890e50f8b9cf359.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the effects of green leadership, emotional intelligence, and twenty-first-century competence on teacher performance at the Sultan Agung Education Foundation in Pematangsiantar. A quantitative research approach was employed with 89 permanent teachers as respondents using census sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and documentation, while questionnaire items were measured using a five-point Likert scale. The research instruments were evaluated for validity and reliability before hypothesis testing. Data analysis involved normality testing, multiple linear regression, correlation analysis, coefficient of determination, t-test, and F-test. The findings show that green leadership, emotional intelligence, and twenty-first-century competence each have a positive and significant effect on teacher performance. Twenty-first-century competence demonstrated the strongest relative contribution among the three variables. Simultaneously, the three independent variables significantly influenced teacher performance, with a correlation coefficient of 0.798 and a coefficient of determination of 0.637. Thus, the model explains 63.7% of the variation in teacher performance, while the remaining 36.3% is attributable to other factors outside the model. The study highlights the importance of integrating responsible leadership, emotional capabilities, and contemporary professional competencies in efforts to strengthen teacher performance</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Spanish Secondary Education: Reported Uses and Pedagogical Practices
container-title: Education Sciences
4658af451af2b10f7367d193d2e6b33f4f139e52.abstract: <jats:p>Evidence on everyday uses of artificial intelligence (AI) in secondary education remains limited. This cross-sectional study examined teacher and student AI functions reported by 504 preservice teachers during school placements in Spain in 2025–2026. Each questionnaire summarized an entire placement and could cover multiple class groups. Within the categories assessed, instructional planning was the most frequently reported teacher function, while student functions centered on information management and content or task creation. Association analyses were restricted to 243 Year 4 compulsory secondary education reports (Educación Secundaria Obligatoria, ESO), where both AI items included an explicit “none of the above” option. Teacher and student AI functions were strongly associated within placement-stage reports, without establishing use in the same class or session. Teacher AI reporting was associated with digital content creation and publication resources, although the categories could overlap. No individual active methodology remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. The number of teacher AI functions showed a modest positive association with the number of methodologies reported in more than 25% of sessions. These findings describe contemporaneous associations between reported practices. They establish neither temporal order nor causality and do not demonstrate pedagogical transformation or improvements in student autonomy or learning.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Front Office Staff Emotional Intelligence on Guest Retention: Mediating Role of Guest Satisfaction in Five-star Hotels in Aqaba-  The Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
container-title: Arts and Social Sciences Series
1d504c9a7ebf348cdf69ec603ff8b50f62cb1970.abstract: <jats:p>This research aims to explore the significant influence that the emotional intelligence (EI) of front office workers has on the retention of guests at five-star hotels in Aqaba City, which is located in Jordan. Within this context, it specifically investigates the function that visitors' satisfaction plays as a mediator in this interaction, drawing on current research published in between the years 2020 and 2025. The study proposes that front office staff members who are emotionally intelligent are more suited to comprehend and manage the guests' emotions, which ultimately results in increased levels of satisfaction among guests, while it is expected that this increased level of satisfaction will, in turn, lead to increased levels of visitor retention in five-star hotels in Aqaba. The study employs a quantitative research methodology with a sample comprising both guests and front office staff. The findings are expected to highlight the vital importance of training front office staff in emotional intelligence skills, as well as underscore the significance of guests' satisfaction as a key factor in building a long-term customer loyalty within the competitive hospitality environment in Aqaba. The findings of this study will also provide valuable insights , that hotel  managers, decision-makers and future  researchers in the field can leverage to make scientifically grounded decisions.       </jats:p>

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Predict Financial and Administrative Risks: An Applied Study at the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (2015–2024)
container-title: International Journal of Financial, Administrative, and Economic Sciences
c9e7c3bcd6a34bdebf9b4c397f93c8b3f7064091.abstract: <jats:p>This research aims to determine the impact of using artificial intelligence (AI) techniques on predicting financial and administrative risks, through an applied study of the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, covering the period from 2015 to 2024. The study is motivated by the growing need within banking institutions to develop analytical tools capable of handling increasing data complexity and enhancing the accuracy of risk management decisions—particularly in light of the economic and financial shifts observed in the Iraqi market in recent years. The research employs an applied methodology based on the analysis of the bank’s historical data and the development of predictive models using AI techniques—such as Random Forests, XGBoost, and neural networks—to compare their risk-prediction capabilities against traditional risk management methods. The study examines various financial and administrative variables, including credit default indicators, liquidity levels, capital adequacy, compliance and governance metrics, and employee turnover, and assesses how these factors influence the bank’s risk exposure. The findings indicate that the use of AI can significantly improve the early detection of risks and reduce uncertainty in decision-making, while also enhancing resource allocation efficiency and the quality of internal governance. Furthermore, the research offers practical recommendations for integrating intelligent models into the risk management framework, ensuring the sustainability of their performance through periodic reviews and robust model governance.</jats:p>
