title: On the probability of extraterrestrial intelligence
container-title: Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences
85008bbad374cf8cbb98c94bfa3917b454c03718.abstract: <jats:p>On the face of it, the question of whether there exists extraterrestrial intelligent life within the Milky Way galaxy may seem as presently unanswerable as profound in its bearing upon our understanding of humanity’s place in the greater cosmos. To the contrary, however, the significant body of astronomical and paleontological knowledge amassed over centuries of inquiry can be shown well sufficient to support confident conclusions in such regard. In point of fact, all that is required is (1) a fair estimate of the relative age of our species in comparison to the galaxy, (2) a general understanding of the timing and phases through which life has progressed on Earth, and (3) a recognition that present rates of technological advancement will very shortly (relative to evolutionary timescales) propel humankind outward into the rest of the galaxy—the consequent inference being that the substantially advance advent of any extraterrestrial second species of similar intellect would have precluded our own through preemptive colonization of our planet. Hence, two such species may only coexist within the galaxy if evolved essentially in close, and probabilistically quantifiable, synchrony. The same model can further be applied to gauge galactic incidence rates of life in different stages of evolutionary development.</jats:p>

title: Designing a source‐grounded Socratic anatomy coach using artificial intelligence to support anatomical reasoning during clinical clerkships
container-title: Anatomical Sciences Education
8ea2d7548f26c7ff865386336ce779662a1f5e0f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Anatomical knowledge must remain retrievable and clinically usable during clerkships, yet previously learned anatomy is often least accessible when students need it most. Generative AI is increasingly available at the point of need, but unstructured use risks displacing the cognitive work required for durable learning. The educational problem is therefore not whether AI can answer anatomy questions, but how a chatbot can be designed so that it supports learning without replacing anatomical reasoning. In this discursive article, we present the design of a source‐grounded Anatomy‐AI Coach for medical students during clinical clerkships at Radboudumc. The current proof‐of‐principle covers musculoskeletal and neuroanatomical questions and is intended for preparatory, just‐in‐time, and reflective use around patient encounters. The design is organized around a five‐phase interaction protocol: goal clarification, concise answer with source citation and micro‐action, multimodal bridge, Socratic coaching with a mirror step, and reflective closure. The protocol draws on self‐regulated learning, the ICAP framework, and emerging work on cognitive offloading and AI as a cognitive mirror. We describe guardrails, scope restriction, source grounding, uncertainty communication, clinical boundaries, and privacy as didactic design features rather than purely technical constraints. This article is part of a larger design‐based research project; future phases will evaluate factual accuracy, pedagogical uptake, and effects on anatomical reasoning during clerkships. The present contribution offers a design blueprint rather than outcome data, specifying how the interactional architecture of an anatomy chatbot can be aligned with workplace learning.</jats:p>

title: Ideal L2 Self and L2 Willingness to Communicate: A Moderated Mediation Model of Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Artificial Intelligence-Mediated Informal Digital Learning of English
container-title: Journal of Learning and Teaching in Digital Age
25f1b6f98cac98ad11532bcbf12a050ee3748c24.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Communication in a second language (L2) is a primary goal for language learners, and willingness to communicate (WTC) is the final step before engaging in actual communication. Therefore, WTC has garnered scholarly interest. While previous research has demonstrated associations between motivational factors and L2 WTC, the mediating and moderating roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-relevant mechanisms remain underexplored. Therefore, this study examines the interplay among ideal L2 self, L2 WTC, AI-mediated informal digital learning of English (AI-IDLE), and AI literacy (AIL) through a moderated mediation model. To this end, data were collected from 402 undergraduate English majors in Türkiye via an online survey comprising four scales and were analyzed through mediation and moderation analyses. The findings revealed that IL2S positively predicted L2 WTC, while AI-IDLE partially mediated this relationship. Moreover, AIL was found to moderate the effect of IL2S on AI-IDLE. Drawing on these results, crucial pedagogical implications are suggested for improving EFL learners’ L2 communication skills.</jats:p>

title: How does Artificial Intelligence Impact Social Commerce in the Era of Digital Transformation? A Systematic Review and Research Agenda for a Sustainable Future
container-title: Journal of Administrative and Economic Sciences
e23afa88d2cae21c05adbb0bd0bb032e17e542a0.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform social commerce (S-commerce), changing how businesses interact with customers, personalising customer experiences, and optimising their operations. This study identifies recent AI developments and their impact on S-commerce through a systematic literature review, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 as a guideline. In the review, 51 articles are extracted from the Web of Science database and used for thematic analysis, revealing that AI developments, combined with machine learning and natural language processing capabilities, have refined personalisation in S-commerce. At the same time, although digital assistants powered by AI are helping consumers make decisions, important ethical and privacy-related issues have arisen. Ultimately, the success of AI integration into S-commerce platforms depends on consumer engagement and satisfaction. Based on the review, the study presents a conceptual model that synthesises five themes capturing AI’s role in S-commerce: personalisation, consumer engagement, recommendation systems, ethical and privacy considerations, and contributions to sustainable S-commerce. Potential gaps in the literature provide the basis for a structured future research agenda on AI-enabled social commerce.</jats:p>

title: A psychological health support system for vocational college students that integrates artificial intelligence and multimodal emotional analysis
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
29e5af36c3753318ebee33856814ce6568b05e37.abstract: <jats:p>This study introduces a technical framework for AI-driven mental health intervention tailored to the unique requirements of vocational college students. The system uses a multimodal emotion recognition engine to integrate facial images, voice audio, and free text data, which are collected in real-time from campus and smart device platforms. After rigorous standardization and secure preprocessing, data from each modality is then subjected to adaptive feature fusion and temporal modeling thru an LSTM-based predictor. Thru homomorphic encryption and continuous access monitoring, user privacy during all analysis processes is effectively protected, ensuring secure transmission and algorithm inference. Thru comprehensive data annotation and iterative model optimization based on academic environment feedback, it is implemented using Python and TensorFlow. To ensure the reliability of the comparison, the system was experimentally validated with 1,200 students from three colleges. Students were randomly and stratifiedly grouped. The results indicate that the anxiety scores of the intervention group were significantly lower than those of the control group, the accuracy of emotion detection was significantly improved, and the system response time was significantly shortened. The overall satisfaction index shows the users' high recognition and trust in the platform's technology and ethical safeguards. The system demonstrates how to enhance the reliability, timeliness, and accuracy of mental health education in professional environments by integrating advanced artificial intelligence, cross-modal feature engineering, and privacy technologies.  These findings lay a solid technical and practical foundation for addressing the complex mental health needs of students, thereby establishing a basis for implementing education in a broader and more realistic context.</jats:p>

title: Library book recommendation methods based on explainable artificial intelligence
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
d88cf0e848acd4f73e4c3d3068012d7b1139a947.abstract: <jats:p>An explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework is developed for library book recommendation, utilizing the fusion of structured borrowing data, semi-structured user behavior logs, and unstructured bibliographic information. A heterogeneous graph is constructed to represent users, books, and attribute entities, with multi-relational edges reflecting diverse real-world library interactions. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) based on relation-specific attention mechanisms are used in the core model. GNN propagates and aggregates information signals within the graph topology and supports direct and higher-order dependencies. The SHAP feature attribution module quantifies the impact of each user or content feature on individual recommendations to address interpretability issues. This enables the system to provide transparent and easily understandable output reasoning. Experiments conducted on large-scale library datasets show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art collaborative and neural baselines in terms of recall, precision, and F1 score. Qualitative and quantitative user studies confirm that the model's explainable outputs notably increase user satisfaction and trust, especially for novel titles and for users with sparse borrowing histories. The integration of multi-source data and transparent reasoning leads to both higher recommendation relevance and enhanced engagement, confirming the significant utility of explainable, graph-based AI for intelligent library services.</jats:p>

title: Construction method of an architectural artificial intelligence question-answering system oriented to engineering standards
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
5e5beaf2f2426e07fe3c900fe5ef6edf588a83d8.abstract: <jats:p>The construction engineering specification text contains a large number of professional terms and complex clause structures. The traditional keyword-based retrieval method is difficult to achieve semantic understanding and precise acquisition of specification knowledge. Focusing on the application of engineering standard interpretation and intelligent question answering, a method for constructing an intelligent question answering system for construction engineering specification texts is proposed. The research uses engineering standard documents as the data source, cleanses the specification clauses, parses the structure, and segments the semantics to build an engineering standard corpus containing approximately 18,000 specification provisions. Based on the pre-trained language model, the vector representation of specification texts is constructed, and the BiLSTM-CRF model is used to achieve entity recognition and professional term extraction in the engineering field, and the relationship extraction method is used to construct the engineering specification knowledge graph. In the question generation stage, a semantic retrieval enhancement generation mechanism is introduced to achieve semantic vector retrieval and the fusion of knowledge graph information for the specification question answering model. Experimental results show that on the constructed engineering standard question answering data set, the F1 value of entity recognition reaches 0.91, the semantic retrieval accuracy rate reaches 0.88, and the BLEU value of question generation reaches 0.37, which can effectively support the semantic query and intelligent question answering of construction engineering specification knowledge.</jats:p>

title: Computational complexity analysis of artificial intelligence-driven green supply chain collaborative optimization model
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
54a419e485b023a861a746d3a2fffa5c14b6c627.abstract: <jats:p>To address the computational complexity issue in the collaborative optimization of green supply chains under multiagent and multiconstraint conditions, this paper analyzes the impact of decision space expansion, constraint dimension superposition, and collaborative level enhancement on complexity evolution from the perspective of computer modeling. It also quantitatively compares the time and space costs of different artificial intelligence solution strategies. The results show that centralized collaborative learning takes 162.8ms for a single round of decision-making and consumes over 500MB of memory; after introducing problem decomposition, hierarchical collaboration, and local learning mechanisms, the single-round calculation time can be controlled within 30–70ms, and the memory usage is reduced to approximately 200MB. The relevant results indicate that the structured modeling based on artificial intelligence can effectively suppress the complexity growth in large-scale green supply chain collaborative optimization.</jats:p>

title: Optimization of green synthesis process for pharmaceutical intermediate under the enabling role of artificial intelligence
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
643847b71496b05a0ef2834c6b26f9021dc01de6.abstract: <jats:p>To address the issues of strong coupling of process variables, complex nonlinear relationships, and low efficiency of manual parameter adjustment in the synthesis of drug intermediates, an artificial intelligence-driven green synthesis process optimization method is proposed. Firstly, the multi-variable data such as temperature, time, catalyst ratio, and solvent dosage are preprocessed and feature represented; then, a multi-objective prediction model is constructed to establish the mapping relationship between process parameters and yield, energy consumption, and by-product indicators, and the parameter optimization algorithm is combined to achieve the search for the optimal process. Experimental results show that the R2 on the test set reaches 0.93, the RMSE is reduced by 12.6%, and the comprehensive target value is increased by 9.8%. Compared with the comparison methods, the proposed method demonstrates better prediction accuracy, convergence speed, and optimization stability.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence algorithms in identifying formulation patterns for traditional Chinese herbal feed additives
container-title: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
2f9269d9da4df4e00f010a837dc7a9d41b0fcf66.abstract: <jats:p>A deep learning framework integrating convolutional neural networks and graph neural networks was developed to systematically mine formulation patterns in traditional Chinese herbal feed additives (TCHFAs). The methodology processes a standardized dataset of over 12,000 additive records by extracting high-dimensional compositional features and mapping nonlinear ingredient interactions through graph-based architectures. An advanced multi-head attention mechanism is applied to interpret key component attribution and quantify synergistic relationships between herbal ingredients. Quantitative analysis demonstrates that the proposed system achieves 94.2% classification accuracy and a substantial performance margin over conventional random forest and support vector machine models. Sixteen central herbal components and nine significant synergistic pairs are empirically identified as primary drivers of feed efficacy, enabling transparent mechanistic understanding and data-driven optimization of additive design. The workflow further incorporates robust data preprocessing, outlier detection, and automated hyperparameter tuning to ensure model generalizability across diverse animal trial settings. Collectively, these results establish an operational paradigm for interpretable artificial intelligence in computational veterinary science, delivering a reproducible and scalable solution to accelerate evidence-based herbal feed additive development.</jats:p>

title: GOVERNANÇA GLOBAL DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: O PAPEL DA ONU E OS LIMITES DA REGULAÇÃO INTERNACIONAL
container-title: South American Sciences
ed38054765be62760fea84f79a9d9f11e16e407e.abstract: <jats:p>O estudo aborda os desafios que o desenvolvimento acelerado da inteligência artificial impõe ao Direito Internacional, diante da natureza transnacional dos fluxos de dados, da atuação global das empresas desenvolvedoras da tecnologia e dos riscos que ela representa para os direitos humanos e os processos democráticos. Trata-se de pesquisa teórica, de abordagem qualitativa, que objetiva analisar o papel da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) na construção de uma governança global da inteligência artificial e avaliar as potencialidades e os limites dos instrumentos de soft law e hard law na regulação internacional da matéria. A metodologia combina o método dedutivo com revisão bibliográfica de obras de Direito Internacional e de Direito Constitucional e com análise documental de instrumentos internacionais, como o relatório Governing AI for Humanity, a Recomendação da UNESCO sobre a Ética da Inteligência Artificial, a resolução da Assembleia Geral da ONU sobre o tema e a encíclica Magnifica Humanitas, complementada por casos ilustrativos de desinformação produzida com inteligência artificial. Os resultados indicam que a regulação nacional é insuficiente para enfrentar riscos que ultrapassam fronteiras e que a ONU tem atuado sobretudo por meio de instrumentos não vinculantes, opção explicada pelas divergências geopolíticas entre as potências tecnológicas e pela velocidade da inovação. Conclui-se que a ONU possui legitimidade para liderar a construção de parâmetros internacionais de governança da inteligência artificial e que a soft law constitui ponto de partida viável, mas que a efetiva proteção dos direitos humanos provavelmente exigirá sua complementação por mecanismos jurídicos dotados de força vinculante.</jats:p>

title: A Configurational Approach to Investigating the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Self‐Regulated Learning From Needs Satisfaction, Learning Environments and Perceived Affordances
container-title: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning
4797e107590ea3351ab21b6456696ccbfe0a6972.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools into self‐regulated learning (SRL) is complex and multifaceted. Configurational approaches are based on the concept that combinations (or configurations) of causally relevant factors should be connected to the desired outcome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Self‐determination theory (SDT), the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) and perceived affordances focus on basic needs, technology adoptions and technological designs, respectively. Taking a configurational approach, this study investigates how the combinations of SDT, UTAUT and perceived affordances affect SRL with AI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We employed fuzzy‐set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to uncover the complex interplay of factors that facilitate effective SRL. Data from 248 students reveal that a combination of autonomy satisfaction, relatedness satisfaction and performance expectancy is the most influential factor affecting the use of AI in SRL.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results and Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results suggest that both innate psychological needs and external learning environments should be considered together for understanding the adoption of AI in SRL. They also further highlight the critical role of perceived affordances as mediators and moderators, enhancing the relationships between innate psychological needs and external learning environments. This integrative approach provides valuable insights into the design and implementation of AI‐supported SRL environments. We recommend designing the environments to foster autonomy and relatedness while also ensuring ease of use for learners.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Videos on the Information Reception Behavior of Social Media Users
container-title: VNU Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
f524907c6b6de6d16a0a8410fe93af08345b4dc8.abstract:
<jats:p>The widespread proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated videos on social media presents an urgent need to evaluate their impact on information reception behavior. This article employs quantitative analysis techniques (Cronbach’s Alpha, exploratory factor analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression) to measure the factors influencing users' levels of acceptance and interaction. The results indicate that "positive perception of the authenticity and attractiveness of AI videos" is the most robust influential factor. Consequently, the article proposes scientific implications aimed at enhancing digital media education capacity and increasing the transparency of AI content, thereby optimizing the effectiveness of users' information reception.

title: Artificial Intelligence through the Lens of Martin Heidegger’s Philosophy of Technology
container-title: VNU Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
113ee5785a530bfdbf6fa6a25abe6e58dfa29346.abstract:
<jats:p>This article approaches artificial intelligence (AI) through the philosophical perspective of Martin Heidegger, arguing that AI should not be regarded merely as a technical tool but as a paradigmatic expression of the essence of modern technology: Gestell (enframing). For Heidegger, Gestell is a mode of revealing in which the world and human beings are transformed into Bestand (standing-reserve), that is, entities or resources ready for optimization and exploitation. AI, with its immense capacities for data processing and computation, replicates the entire logic of Gestell: it reduces life, language, and even the human being to manipulable units of data. Heidegger warns that the dominance of Gestell leads to nihilism, wherein the logic of calculation obscures the meaning and being of things. In response, he does not call for the rejection of technology. Instead, he proposes an attitude of Gelassenheit (releasement) and meditative thinking, aiming to cultivate a “free relationship” with technology – an understanding of the danger of enframing and the possibility that attentiveness to this danger may open a path toward a saving power. This article argues that AI is not merely a technical challenge but also poses profound ontological questions concerning human existence and freedom in the digital age.

title: The Degree of Utilization of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Teaching from the Perspective of Arabic Language Teachers in Arar City n The Light of Certain Variables
container-title: University of Bisha Journal for Educational Sciences
b45823d1a8b50e009f07a3514598a94bfe55d78a.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to reveal the degree of Arabic language teachers’ use of artificial intelligence applications and the obstacles to their use in teaching in the city of Arar from their perspective, as well as to reveal the existence of statistically significant differences at a significance level (α ≤ 0.05) in the degree of employment of AI apps according to (Gender, education, the stage of teaching, training programs in the field of AI, years of experience) variables and identifying the challenges they faced while using AI Apps in teaching process. To achieve the study objective, the researcher adopted the survey descriptive approach and used the questionnaire as a study tool. The study applied to a sample of (148) Arabic language male and female teachers of Primary, Middle, and Secondary stages in Arar city for the second semester of the scholastic year 1447H-1448H who were selected according to the simple random method. The study findings revealed that the level of applying AI Apps in the educational process as perceived by Arabic language teachers in Arar city was low, the main obstacles to implementation were insufficient technical support, weak digital capabilities and technical infrastructure in schools, and the need for privacy and data protection. The results also showed statistically significant differences at the α ≤0.05 level in the degree of their use of these applications attributed to the gender variable in favor of females, bachelor’s degree holders, secondary and primary stage teachers, those who completed (1-3) courses, and those with more than (11-15) years of experience in the experience variable ;while there are no differences regarding the obstacles to their use in teaching Arabic attributed to these variables. Based on above results, the study recommended to integrate AI apps into Arabic Language curriculum, and raising awareness of the benefits of AI apps and familiarize them with the developments in the field of AI Apps, and providing training opportunities for teachers in this area. The study suggested conducting further studies and research on the use of AI apps in the teaching of Arabic Language, and measuring its impact on students’ achievement.</jats:p>

title: From Generative Artificial Intelligence Competence to Entrepreneurial Intention: The Sequential Mediation of Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy and Opportunity Recognition
container-title: Administrative Sciences
dba738d3e58b7c82b1d01919a1c5dd454c69b728.abstract: <jats:p>Based on Social Cognitive Theory, this study examines the relationship between generative artificial intelligence competence and entrepreneurial intention, with entrepreneurial self-efficacy and opportunity recognition as mediators. Despite growing interest in generative AI and entrepreneurship, limited evidence exists regarding how generative AI competence is associated with entrepreneurial intention through these cognitive mechanisms, particularly through their sequential interplay. Using a cross-sectional quantitative design, data were collected from 1135 business students at a private university in Lima, Peru, and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results indicate positive relationships among generative artificial intelligence competence, entrepreneurial self-efficacy, opportunity recognition, and entrepreneurial intention. Furthermore, the proposed indirect effects were statistically significant, with opportunity recognition representing the strongest indirect pathway. A statistically significant but comparatively small sequential indirect association through entrepreneurial self-efficacy and opportunity recognition was also observed. Overall, the results broaden the application of Social Cognitive Theory by positioning generative AI competence as a technology-specific capability associated with entrepreneurial cognition and intention. From a practical perspective, the findings suggest that university entrepreneurship education could integrate generative AI training with activities focused on identifying and evaluating business opportunities.</jats:p>

title: Trust- and Energy-Aware Federated Learning for Robust and Sustainable IoT Edge Intelligence: Full-System Evaluation on PAMAP2 and Cross-Domain Robustness Assessment on CICIoT2023
container-title: Applied Sciences
93f1d4d07ba22853a1aee112cb033dfefbea7a8e.abstract: <jats:p>Federated learning (FL) supports collaborative edge intelligence without centralizing raw data, but non-IID data, Byzantine attacks, and limited client energy complicate IoT deployment. We study two complementary server-side mechanisms: TEA-FL, which couples consistency-based trust with residual energy in client selection and aggregation, and ARL-FL, which separates risk/lifetime-aware scheduling from pressure-adaptive robust aggregation. A matched two-domain protocol distinguishes full-system PAMAP2 evidence from aggregation-focused CICIoT2023 evidence and combines fold/seed-level inference with ablations, targeted sensitivities, and complete-round overhead measurements. Under the primary simulated resource model, TEA-FL achieved the highest overall PAMAP2 Macro-F1 and lowest normalized energy, but reduced participation fairness and did not complete every nominal-horizon run. ARL-FL preserved the largest active-client population and completed all PAMAP2 runs, but failed under the strongest sign-flip attack. Focused controls showed that trust drives TEA-FL’s sign-flip robustness, energy-aware selection drives ARL-FL’s sustainability benefit, and simpler fixed clipping-plus-trimming can be competitive under strong attack. The results support context-dependent robustness–sustainability trade-offs rather than universal superiority.</jats:p>

title: Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Among Pre-Service Primary Teachers in Mongolia: A Psychometric Evaluation of the Mongolian SATAI Scale
container-title: Education Sciences
65ccdbba255f3c200f66d7fa49374a3e9639ffaa.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) among pre-service primary school teachers in Mongolia and evaluated the psychometric properties of a Mongolian adaptation of the Students’ Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence (SATAI) scale. A cross-sectional survey yielded an analytic sample of 672 students at a public teacher education university, randomly divided by academic-year strata into exploratory (n = 334) and confirmatory (n = 338) subsamples. Factor-retention criteria disagreed, and the exploratory solution did not match the component grouping of the source adaptation. A model reproducing that structure fitted poorly and yielded an inadmissible solution. Of seven measurement models estimated from polychoric correlations by diagonally weighted least squares, a bifactor model fitted best (CFI = 0.975; TLI = 0.970), although RMSEA remained 0.086; a four-factor model fitted comparably, but its factor correlations (0.86–0.93) failed the Fornell–Larcker criterion for every pair. Omega hierarchical (0.949) and explained common variance (0.876) indicated a dominant source of common variance, while subscale-specific reliability was limited; internal consistency of the total score was high (α = 0.972). Attitudes were moderately positive (M = 3.59, SD = 0.85), with enjoyment and educational relevance endorsed more strongly than everyday application and self-rated competence. Metric and scalar invariance across academic years was supported by change-in-fit criteria, and fourth-year students scored higher than all earlier cohorts. The findings favor cautious use of the total score rather than subscale scores, and they provide a descriptive basis for designing and then evaluating structured, ethically informed AI preparation in teacher education rather than evidence that such provision is effective.</jats:p>

title: Synergizing IoT and Edge Artificial Intelligence: Architectures, Enabling Technologies, Challenges, and Future Directions
container-title: International Journal of Sciences and Innovation Engineering
d2c302320c4ff8b6e23cd8cb7bfd90641cc42198.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing intelligence of connected objects creates a design dilemma: devices must interpret sensor information quickly, yet continuous transmission to distant servers can waste bandwidth, energy, and time. This review examines how Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures and edge artificial intelligence (Edge AI) can be designed as a coordinated computing system rather than as separate technologies. It develops a four-tier architectural perspective, traces the technologies that make local inference practical, and discusses deployment choices across manufacturing, health monitoring, mobility, and environmental sensing. Particular attention is given to the interaction between model accuracy, response deadlines, device power, data governance, and operational maintenance. A comparative synthesis identifies unresolved issues in heterogeneous hardware, trustworthy model updates, distribution shift, and reproducible benchmarking. The paper proposes an application-driven decision framework and outlines research opportunities in adaptive inference, collaborative learning, and sustainable edge operations.</jats:p>

title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TALENT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF ORGANIZATIONAL JUSTICE AND THE MODERATING ROLE OF EMPLOYEE INNOVATIVE WORK BEHAVIOR IN PAKISTAN’S CONSTRUCTION SECTOR
container-title: JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES DEVELOPMENT
950ce8ae66eedd405958936b79e70b96d1b2f2b0.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing its coverage of human resources and staff-led recommendations. But the staff interpretations of automated recommendations are still important in project-based construction settings. The qualitative study examines how AI-supported recruitment, project implementation, performance assessment and learning in talent management are experienced in the Pakistan construction industry. Covering all HR management, engineering, supervision, skilled trade and digital operations, the study uses organizational equity to interpret staff responses and considers innovative performance as a requirement for interaction with AI-supported decisions on the basis of 18 codes of participant accounts. The thematic analysis identifies five interconnected issues: screening efficiency versus contextual competence; data visibility and procedural fairness; challenges to algorithmic ratings; unequal access to learning; and employee innovation as a source of improvement or resistance. The findings reveal that AI-supported decisions would be more acceptable if data mirrored practical skills, the assessment rules were transparent and the human assessment made available. Conversely, opaque evaluations, unequal digital access, and limited potential for challenging decisions can undermine perceived fairness. The study develops an evidence-informed qualitative framework and implications for governance without claiming statistically tested mediation, moderation or population-level generalizability.</jats:p>

title: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into tertiary health education: A scoping review
container-title: Online Learning
a31d38f6ba47e8c5a0a841abb0acff784491d28c.abstract: <jats:p>This scoping review aims to provide an overview of the integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in tertiary health education, including its practical applications in tertiary health education programs and how these applications are perceived by stakeholders. A literature search was conducted in five databases, including Ovid Medline, Ovid Emcare, Scopus, CINAHL, and ERIC. Articles integrating GenAI in tertiary health disciplines were included. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews checklist was followed in the reporting of results. Overall, 20 studies were included and three categories were identified: 1) application of GenAI in tertiary health education, 2) perceptions of GenAI use in health education, and 3) ethical and responsible use of GenAI in health education. Currently, GenAI is being integrated as a complementary tool to automate academic tasks and improve the critical thinking skills of tertiary health students through optimizing class designs. Although GenAI applications were well-received by students due to high accessibility, concerns over misinformation, over-reliance, and data confidentiality were consistently flagged. The review identified a lack of formal AI literacy training, highlighting the need for structured AI literacy training modules and clear ethical guidelines to support tertiary health students in using GenAI. GenAI applications are being rapidly integrated into tertiary health education, primarily for automated grading/feedback and improvement of learning outcomes. Future research is recommended to investigate the long-term impacts of GenAI and how to implement AI literacy training in current tertiary health education programs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Business Efficiency of Selected Banks in Benin City, Nigeria
container-title: JALINGO JOURNAL OF SOCIAL AND MANAGEMENT SCIENCES
bfe7da82db39053c1d46021250e7d2e36c22b438.abstract: <jats:p>The problem of inefficiency in the banking industry, particularly in service delivery, fraud prevention, routine process management, and security operations, has created the need for innovative technologies capable of improving business efficiency. This study examined the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the business efficiency of selected banks in Benin City, Nigeria. Specifically, the study investigated the effects of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Fraud Detection Technologies, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), and Computer Vision on business efficiency. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted. The study population comprised 662 employees of selected banks that had implemented AI technologies, from which a sample of 324 respondents was determined using the Taro Yamane (1967) formula. Structured questionnaires were used for data collection, while 280 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis with SPSS. The findings revealed that all four AI dimensions had a positive and statistically significant effect on business efficiency. Robotic Process Automation exhibited the strongest positive effect, followed by Natural Language Processing, Fraud Detection Technologies, and Computer Vision. Collectively, the AI dimensions explained 23.8% of the variation in business efficiency (R² = 0.238), and the overall regression model was statistically significant (p < 0.001). The study concludes that AI technologies significantly enhance business efficiency by improving service delivery, strengthening fraud prevention, automating routine processes, and enhancing security. The study recommended that commercial banks strengthen AI integration, invest in digital infrastructure, and provide continuous employee training to maximize the benefits of AI-driven banking operations.</jats:p>

title: Applications of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Bioinformatics and Their Experimental Validation
container-title: Research Journal of Life Sciences, Bioinformatics, Pharmaceutical and Chemical Sciences
e98d4a4e4187b8f96f2d2b3304fa430c6f2f0632.abstract: <jats:p>A sequence model can identify a base substitution predicted to alter a splice junction, and a cancer model can assign a tumour to a pathway-defined group. Researchers often interpret these outputs as explanations, although each calls for a different experimental test. This narrative review examines how explainable artificial intelligence is used in regulatory genomics, RNA processing, cancer genomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, protein science, molecular property prediction and microbial genomics. It compares the biological entity being explained, the reference used to calculate an effect and the evidence available beyond the original model. Base substitutions and matched molecular pairs permit explicit contrasts. Pathway scores, tissue neighbourhoods and internal protein features require additional tests to separate the proposed mechanism from correlated measurements. Recent evaluations of foundation models also show why comparisons with simple predictors and genuinely held-out biological units matter before interpretation. Across applications, the clearest route to experimental follow-up is to specify an expected molecular event, its direction and a result that would challenge the prediction. This approach separates faithful descriptions of model behaviour from claims supported by an independent assay and clarifies what an explanation contributes to the selection of the next experiment.</jats:p>

title: Employing Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Al Arabiya Newsrooms: A Field Study within the Framework of Technological Determinism Theory
container-title: International Journal of Educational Sciences and Arts
2d5142cd1039ac5d3016465edceca11a5cb5894a.abstract:
<jats:p>This study aims to understand how Al Arabiya channel utilizes artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in its newsrooms, through a field study framed within the theory of technological determinism. The research also aims to explore the extent to which journalists at the channel rely on these technologies in their work and identify the key areas they depend on in their journalistic work.
The study problem is framed around the main question: To what extent does Al Arabiya channel employ AI techniques in its newsrooms? 
Accordingly, this study belongs to descriptive studies using the survey method and relying on the electronic questionnaire tool. It was distributed to a purposive research sample consisting of 30 journalists, aiming to interrogate them through a variety of closed-ended multiple-choice questions and open-ended questions to determine the diversity of their opinions regarding the extent of AI technology utilization in Al Arabiya's newsroom.
The study yielded several key findings: 
•	The results showed that the majority of the sample had experience in using AI techniques, with a rate of 73.3%. However, approximately 46.7%, almost half of the sample, rely to a low degree on these technologies in their journalistic work.
•	All sample members benefited from education and self-training in the field of AI by 100%, with most relying on free websites supported by AI technologies in their journalistic work.
•	The results indicated a moderate relationship between AI technologies and the professional development of journalists. 80% of the sample pointed to the need for more training and development for journalists to enable them to effectively handle AI technologies.
•	The main challenges faced by sample members when using AI techniques in their journalistic work include the lack of necessary materials, lack of experience, and shortage of AI-related training courses and workshops.
•	The results showed no statistically significant relationship between the degree of reliance of sample members on AI techniques in their journalistic work and years of experience.</jats:p>

title: Exploring Teachers’ Practices in Advocating Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
db7fb069552b3b50e0d865774d2b9d385d49e6ec.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aim: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education creates opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning. As AI tools become accessible, teachers are essential in guiding students toward responsible, ethical, and effective use. Yet, teacher practices supporting responsible AI use remain underexplored, particularly in the Philippine context. This case study examined how teachers advocate responsible AI use in their classrooms.
Materials and Methods: A qualitative case study design was used. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with fifteen school teachers at Tabina National High School, Tabina District, Division of Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. Purposive criterion sampling selected participants who: (a) taught in basic education, (b) integrated AI tools or AI-related discussions into teaching, (c) demonstrated advocacy for responsible technology use, and (d) had at least three years of teaching experience. Interviews were conducted in Cebuano, transcribed verbatim, translated into English when necessary, and thematically analyzed following Merriam and Tisdell’s (2016) case study procedures. Data were collected from January to June 2026.
Results: Four sequential themes emerged: (1) challenges involving student overreliance, absent institutional policies, limited teacher training, and academic integrity; (2) coping mechanisms involving emotional responses, professional collaboration, and information-seeking; (3) adaptive strategies involving curriculum integration, AI-resistant assessments, responsible-use modeling, and critical classroom discussions; and (4) outcomes involving greater student awareness, stronger critical thinking, persistent misuse, and emerging teacher advocacy communities.
Conclusion: Despite limited institutional support and training, teachers employ practices to promote responsible AI use. Comprehensive AI literacy frameworks, sustained professional development, and institutional policies are recommended.</jats:p>

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DETECTING PUBLIC PROCUREMENT FRAUD THROUGH ESG RISK INDICATORS: A QUALITATIVE SECONDARY STUDY OF SDG 16
container-title: JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES DEVELOPMENT
209d53022469e30c6987be5451c9b8d0fca0ed74.abstract: <jats:p>Public procurement absorbs 12.7% of GDP across OECD countries (OECD, 2025), and bribery to win public contracts featured in 57% of concluded foreign-bribery cases in the OECD’s 2014 analysis. This study asks whether AI-enabled screening that incorporates environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators can deliver accountable procurement-integrity gains, and under what conditions. It uses a qualitative, theory-informed secondary comparative design: three core cases (Brazil, Ukraine, Italy), two supplier-side illustrations (Odebrecht, Grenfell Tower) and two algorithmic-accountability comparators (the Netherlands, Australia), assessed against a five-level evidence hierarchy running from operational scale to verified outcomes. Governance and procedural indicators are operational; no reviewed case demonstrates validated environmental or social integration. Reported benefits mostly measure exposure, activity or self-reported savings; low selectivity, signal decay and weak follow-through limit effect; and automated enforcement without due process has caused severe harm elsewhere. The paper contributes the ESG-Integrity Analytics Framework (EIAF), five testable propositions and a replicable evidence-grading protocol, and concludes that AI’s contribution to SDG 16.5, 16.6 and 16.10 is conditional on validation, institutional follow-through and accountability.</jats:p>

title: The Relationship between the Integration of Artificial Intelligence Technologies into Communication Strategies within Public Relations Departments and the Building of Government Institutional Reputation During Crises
container-title: International Journal of Educational Sciences and Arts
8ac2be4ed488d8584f5038d4f396a022d10333d3.abstract: <jats:p>Public relations departments play a pivotal role in building institutional reputation and reinforcing the positive image of official organizations through effective communication with the media, identifying the current and future needs of stakeholders, strengthening internal organizational communication, and leveraging modern communication technologies to ensure rapid outreach, greater efficiency, and enhanced communication effectiveness. The significance of these responsibilities becomes even more pronounced during crises and emergency situations, which impose additional demands on public relations departments to address challenges and manage circumstances that may adversely affect the organization's reputation, thereby requiring sustained efforts to protect, preserve, and enhance that reputation under exceptional conditions. This, in turn, necessitates the adoption of appropriate communication strategies capable of supporting institutional reputation during crises while ensuring their effectiveness in reducing public anxiety, particularly amid political and social tensions and rapidly changing environments. Furthermore, the design and implementation of these communication strategies should take into account the prevailing cultural and social contexts to maximize the effectiveness of communication processes and achieve their intended objectives. In this context, public relations departments within government institutions increasingly adopt comprehensive, integrated, and diversified communication strategies during crises, whereby the efforts of public relations practitioners are coordinated within a unified strategic framework. Such strategies should be characterized by clarity, accuracy, consistency, and flexibility, while being derived from broader strategic plans shared across government entities to promote institutional coordination and encourage constructive engagement with all segments of society. Moreover, in light of digital transformation and the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence applications, it has become imperative for public relations departments to integrate these advanced technologies into their communication practices to meet the demands of the contemporary communication environment, expand organizational reach and influence, and strengthen institutional reputation, particularly during periods of crisis and uncertainty.</jats:p>

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Governance in Procurement: Skills Transformation, Decision-Making Accountability and Ethical Issues
container-title: Technium Social Sciences Journal
7bcf4f39233137705dab8a75100d491e9144842a.abstract: <jats:p>This article analyzes the impact of generative artificial intelligence on the procurement function, starting from two converging directions: the operational and strategic transformation of procurement through GenAI, and the ethical issues generated by its use in processes involving suppliers, commercial data, contracts, and decisions with economic or legal effects. The paper proposes an integrated analytical framework in which GenAI is examined simultaneously as an efficiency-enhancing technology, a cognitive augmentation tool, and a source of organizational risk. The study adopts an empirical qualitative design based on an open-ended questionnaire completed by 40 professionals from procurement, IT, legal, compliance, and retail/supply chain, analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis. The findings show that GenAI is valued mainly for preparatory, document-intensive tasks, while respondents reject its use for autonomous decisions with legal or economic effects; confidentiality, hallucinations, and diffuse accountability emerge as the dominant concerns. Building on these findings, the paper proposes a risk-tiered governance matrix that links GenAI use cases to control mechanisms and professional competences. The results indicate that the responsible adoption of GenAI depends less on the isolated technical performance of tools and more on the existence of an institutional architecture combining data quality, human oversight, auditability, protection of confidential information, and continuous professional training. The main conclusion is that the future of GenAI-assisted procurement should not be built on replacing the human decision-maker, but on controlled human–AI collaboration, in which generative systems support analysis while decision-making responsibility remains clearly allocated to the organization and its professionals.</jats:p>

title:
Research Trends of Artificial Intelligence‐Facilitated Computational Thinking in K‐12
                    <scp>STEM</scp>
                    : A Systematic Review Through the Lens of Activity Theory
container-title: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning
50a7c557e85930f55486025b6c3e3d6739b9afa8.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), research in the cross‐disciplinary field of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education has increasingly focused on how to leverage AI to foster computational thinking (CT) among K‐12 students, given that CT, recognized as a core 21st‐century competency, plays a pivotal role in cultivating students’ literacy and equipping them with the ability to tackle complex problems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Grounded in activity theory, this study seeks to identify the key factors shaping K‐12 students’ CT development in AI‐enhanced STEM education. It systematically analyzes: (a) the subjects involved and the types and roles of AI tools employed, (b) the purposes, periods, and CT dimensions within the object, (c) the methods, strategies, and evaluation performance applied within rules, (d) the learning domains within communities and the interactions within the division of labor, and (e) the developmental trends in outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study employed the PRISMA framework to systematically review 57 SSCI journal publications published between 2017 and 2025. In addition, Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was utilized to examine the current state of CT evaluation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results and Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings indicate that: (1) the primary subjects of the studies were elementary school students; expert systems and robotics were the most prevalent types of AI, which were frequently employed as learning tools; (2) the primary objective was to evaluate the effectiveness of AI in CT–K12–STEM, with periods typically ranging from 2 to 6 months, focusing on conceptual knowledge and practical skills; (3) the rules focused on exploratory learning and gamification strategies, employing quantitative research methods; (4) communities spanned cross‐disciplinary domains, with division of labor tending towards mixed interaction types; and (5) outcomes focused on the learning cognitive perspective, encompassing aspects such as learning performance and problem solving. Based on the research results, practical recommendations are provided for educational researchers and policymakers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Data Governance and International Trade Law: A Review of Legal Challenges, Facilitation Technologies and Governance Pathways
container-title: European Journal of Theoretical and Applied Sciences
9e43289dfb320626b770857d66c17b99eb6d2082.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) now does much of the routine work of international trade administration. It classifies goods, scores consignments for risk, reads trade documents, forecasts demand and checks regulatory compliance, and it has been proposed for resolving trade disputes. These systems rely on data moving across borders, and many of their decisions are hard to explain. This review asks how AI is changing trade practice, what legal problems it raises for international trade law and the data protection rules connected to it, and how governments and international bodies are responding. The core corpus is seven studies from 2024 and 2025. Each was coded for focus, method, jurisdiction and evidence, rated for quality, and read alongside the legal, economic and policy work it draws on. The studies agree that AI improves customs risk management, document processing and supply-chain planning, but the reported gains come mostly from unnamed case studies and simulations that cannot be checked. The main legal problem is that data is governed by three incompatible models: the European Union's rights-based approach, the sectoral approach of the United States and China's sovereignty-based approach. AI also raises connected problems of data protection, jurisdiction, liability, intellectual property, non- discrimination and cybersecurity. Whether AI-based border measures comply with WTO rules has received almost no attention. Regulation is moving toward making national rules work together, through the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, soft law, technical standards and plurilateral digital economy agreements, with the WTO playing a secondary part. The review sets out seven research priorities, led by a WTO-law analysis of AI-based border measures and independent testing of the AI systems customs authorities already use.</jats:p>

title: Capacity Limits in Cognitive Processing Reflect the Curse of Generalization
65a5e431acc5d0a8d2c5143f2e9ef4740d73e2de.abstract: The striking constraints of some human cognitive processes stand in stark contrastto the near limitless capability of others. While we can acquire and flexibly use vast amountsof information, the amount we can process at any one time is often stiflingly limited: forexample the number of items we can hold in working memory or the number of tasks that canbe performed at once. Here, we integrate ideas from information theory, cognitive science,and neuroscience to offer a unified account of why processing is often so limited. We arguethat this reflects a fundamental tradeoff between generalization—how effectively existingrepresentations can be used in novel settings—and how many distinct representations canbe processed in parallel. Representations that best promote strong forms of generalization— a characteristically human cognitive strength — come at the expense of surprisinglystrict limits in the number of items that can be processed at once, an equally characteristichuman weakness. We refer to this as the “curse of generalization.” We formulate this first ininformation-theoretic terms, and then in process models, including a neural network modelof classic tasks used to demonstrate strict limits in human processing capacity. This tensionoffers a potential explanation for a range of phenomena — from performance on the tasks onwhich we focus, to representational learning and skill acquisition more broadly — as wellas the performance of modern machine learning architectures that exhibit generalizationcapabilities comparable to humans.

title: Large-Eddy Simulations Modeling of High-Lift High-Work Low-Pressure Turbine Blades: Validation and Application
container-title: Journal of Turbomachinery
c2a5abd9a2ff1806b534f5d813fc3ec103397ac0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Over the years, computational fluids dynamics (CFD) has matured to such a state so as to be indispensable in turbine design. In the past two decades alone, significant advances in turbine design have been made through the use of CFD—in particular, through the use of Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) simulations. Currently, turbine design is RANS-driven; however, significant gains in performance and efficiency are becoming more difficult to achieve using RANS. For this reason, the turbomachinery CFD community is moving toward Large-Eddy Simulations (LES). In the design of low-pressure turbine (LPT) blades, LES is particularly beneficial owing to its ability to capture accurately both transition and separation. In this paper, LES is used to characterize a new family of high-lift high-work LPT blades—designated the LXFHW-LS family—designed at the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL). LES simulations are conducted in accordance with the methodology outlined in Part I of this paper. The purpose of this paper is twofold: (1) to use LES to predict the performance of the LXFHW-LS family and compare it to measurements in a low-speed linear cascade and, in doing so, (2) to illustrate how LES may be used in LPT design as it evolves from RANS-driven to LES-driven. For each blade in the family, the loading distribution and loss coefficient are computed for 16 separate Reynolds numbers. Computational results are validated using detailed experimental measurements from a low-speed linear cascade wind tunnel. Experimental measurements include blade loading distributions, total pressure loss, and particle image velocimetry (PIV) measurements. In comparing computational and experimental results, particular emphasis is placed on the evolution of the suction surface (SS) separation bubble (if one exists). A variety of techniques are used to visualize the extent of the separation bubble, including machine learning.</jats:p>

title: Experiment-based calibration in psychology: foundational and data-generating model
896e44a978cf20bc63251037fbc18b086cf21d92.abstract: Experiment-based calibration is a novel method for measurement validation, which – unlike classical validity metrics – does not require stable between-person variance. In this approach, the latent variable to be measuredis manipulated by an experiment, and its predicted scores – termed standard scores – are compared against the measured scores. Previous work has shown that under plausible boundary conditions, the correlationbetween standard and measured scores – termed retrodictive validity – is informative about measurement accuracy, i.e. combined trueness and precision. Here, I expand these findings in several directions. First, Iformalise the approach in a probability-theoretic framework with the concept of a standardised calibration space. Second, I relate this framework to classical validity theory and show that the boundary conditionsin fact apply to any form of criterion validity, including classical convergent validity. Thus, I state precise and empirically quantifiable boundary conditions under which criterion validity metrics are informative onvalidity. Third, I relate these boundary conditions to confounding variables, i.e. correlated latent variables. I show that in the limit, calibration will converge on the latent variable that is most closely related to thestandard. Finally, I provide a framework for modelling the data-generating process with Markov kernels, and identify sufficient conditions under which the data generation model results in a calibration space. In sum,this article provides a formal probability-theoretic framework for experiment-based calibration and facilitates modelling and empirical assessment of the data generating processes.

title: Large inversions in Lake Malawi cichlids are associated with habitat, lineage, and sex determination
container-title: eLife
b641d8a47331fdefe6b0f48a514a41a05aa8f4a4.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic
                    <jats:italic>Diplotaxodon</jats:italic>
                    group into
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    ancestors at the time the
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of
                    <jats:italic>benthic</jats:italic>
                    species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.
                  </jats:p>

title: Large Language Models for Cyber Security: A Systematic Literature Review
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
b0bc58efd35742a0df2f019162f0c83912291f16.abstract:
<jats:p>The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened up new opportunities for leveraging AI in a variety of application domains, including cybersecurity. As the volume and sophistication of cyber threats continue to grow, there is an increasing need for intelligent systems that can automatically detect vulnerabilities, analyze malware, and respond to attacks. In this survey, we conduct a comprehensive review of the literature on the application of LLMs in cybersecurity (LLM4Security). By comprehensively collecting over 40K relevant papers and systematically analyzing 185 papers from top security and software engineering venues, we aim to provide a holistic view of how LLMs are being used to solve diverse problems across the cybersecurity domain.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Through our analysis, we identify several key findings. First, we observe that LLMs are being applied to an expanding range of cybersecurity tasks, including vulnerability detection, malware analysis, and network intrusion detection. Second, we analyze application trends of different LLM architectures (such as encoder-only, encoder–decoder, and decoder-only) across security domains. Third, we identify increasingly sophisticated techniques for adapting LLMs to cybersecurity, such as advanced fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and external augmentation strategies. A significant emerging trend is the use of LLM-based autonomous agents, which represent a paradigm shift from single-task execution to orchestrating complex, multi-step security workflows. Furthermore, we find that the datasets used for training and evaluating LLMs are often limited, highlighting the need for more comprehensive datasets and the use of LLMs for data augmentation. Finally, we discuss the main challenges and opportunities for future research, including the need for more interpretable models, addressing the inherent security risks of LLMs, and their potential for proactive defense.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Overall, our survey provides a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in LLM4Security and identifies several promising directions for future research. We believe that the insights and findings presented in this survey will contribute to the growing body of knowledge on the application of LLMs in cybersecurity and provide valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners working in this field.</jats:p>

title: CryoDECO: disentangling compositional and conformational heterogeneity in cryo-EM with foundation-model priors
1cbc6edf26ff53ee4978d8584f04c0294216609c.abstract: <jats:p>Cryo-electron microscopy has transformed macromolecular structure determination, but heterogeneous biological samples contain multiple complexes and conformational states that remain difficult to resolve. This difficulty reflects a circular dependency among particle separation, pose estimation and structure reconstruction. We developed CryoDECO, a prior-guided framework that enters this coupled inference problem from structural representations learned from large-scale cryo-EM data rather than from random initialization, and that reduces manual tuning. CryoDECO separates simulated mixtures of up to 100 structures, resolves experimental and native-derived mixtures into populations suitable for high-resolution refinement, and captures continuous motion together with local density differences within a shared trajectory.</jats:p>

title: Judges of Empire
The first uniform rail passenger fare model in Europe: Hungary's late 19th-century reform and its foreign judgement
container-title: Hungarian Studies
9f113d3a0ce5f82ca3c2c5368e0e16d06a94f6e4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The advent of the railways had a profound impact on the fates and economies of nations, transforming nearly every aspect of society and culture throughout the 19th century. Despite a somewhat late start, Hungary developed a large and sophisticated rail system. This system was revolutionized in 1889 with the introduction of the zone tariff system by Gábor Baross, which greatly simplified ticket pricing and made rail travel affordable for the average Hungarian. Though few believed it would be sustainable, the Baross system had a substantial international impact. Experts from across Europe traveled to Hungary to study the reform. This paper examines the impact of the unified zone tariff system—the first of its kind in Europe—and explores its reception abroad and the extent to which it served as a model for other nations, drawing on both Hungarian and international historical literature on railway and tariff policy, as well as primary sources.</jats:p>

title: MLLM-Driven Autonomous Driving: Closed-Loop Decision-Making with Language-State Alignment and Human Instruction Integration
container-title: ACM Journal on Autonomous Transportation Systems
d800c7e114eb4db4826982c6e016151dc7d88ec1.abstract: <jats:p>The core challenge of autonomous driving is achieving real-time decision-making and safety control in complex, dynamic environments, especially in long-tail scenarios where conventional systems often fail due to limited adaptability, poor human-vehicle interaction, and low interpretability. This article introduces MLLM-CLAD, a closed-loop decision-making framework powered by a multimodal large language model, which addresses semantic gaps and feedback limitations through a co-optimization strategy that integrates behavior-state alignment and language instruction fusion. MLLM-CLAD integrates three core modules: (1) The Mapping-Enhanced Language-State Alignment Module employs a deterministic mapping pipeline from language instructions to control signals, which enables highly accurate mapping from LLM semantic outputs to executable control signals. (2) The Hierarchical Dynamic Instruction Integration Module robustly categorizes and dynamically prioritizes human language instructions into different semantic types. (3) The Multimodal Fusion Module leverages a lightweight spatiotemporal Q-Former to jointly encode images and LiDAR point clouds, aligned with language in latent space for improved temporal reasoning and cross-modal consistency. Evaluated in the CARLA Town05 Long, MLLM-CLAD achieves a 78.3% Driving Score and reduces collision rates by 35% in safety-critical scenarios. On the LangAuto benchmarks, MLLM-CLAD attains a 78.5% long-tail scenario pass rate. Furthermore, the end-to-end latency is reduced to 128 milliseconds. This work establishes a scalable path toward safe, low-latency, and interpretable autonomous driving in simulation, with a clear roadmap for real-world extension.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
