title: Fast TDDB Hotspot Detection of Large-Scale BEOL Circuits Using Physics-Informed Central Emphasized CNN
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
43ca2ee0c70088e2af9b1e91e0c2fd8f1b809f8c.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) has emerged as a critical reliability concern in Back-End-of-Line (BEOL) interconnects. In Electric Path Generation (EPG) based TDDB analysis, the evolution of metal ion concentration is governed by a Partial Differential Equation (PDE). Traditional numerical methods for solving this equation are time-consuming and demand considerable computational resources, making them impractical for large-scale circuits analysis. To address this challenge, we propose a physics-informed learning framework for fast prediction of ion concentration distributions in large BEOL layouts. The framework represents BEOL patterns as two-dimensional images, partitions large layouts into overlapping sub-graphs for encoding, and predicts transient concentration fields for each sub-graph. Based on the reconstructed full-layout concentration map, the method supports efficient TDDB hotspot analysis. The proposed Physics-Informed Central Emphasized Convolutional Neural Network (PICE-CNN) is applicable to diverse interconnect patterns and operating conditions, including different line widths, line spacings, and supply voltages. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves up to 357.1× speedup over conventional numerical solvers while maintaining high prediction accuracy, with the mean squared error below 1× 10
                    <jats:sup>-4</jats:sup>
                    in the emphasized central region.
                  </jats:p>

title: Defense Mechanisms of Kiwifruit Against Corynespora cassiicola and Predictive Model for Estimating Resistance Levels
container-title: Plant Disease
990052124fc9424405291af90975f7c25d83260a.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Brown spot disease, caused by
                    <jats:italic>Corynespora cassiicola</jats:italic>
                    , poses a major threat to kiwifruit production, leading to severe defoliation, nutrient loss, and significant economic damage. This study assessed 25 kiwifruit germplasm accessions and found 64% exhibited resistance, including three highly resistant (HR) cultivars; most commercial and wild germplasm accessions were moderately resistant (MR) or highly susceptible (HS). Three cultivars representing different resistance levels—HR ‘Longshan’ (LS), MR ‘Jinyan’ (JY), and HS ‘Hongyang’ (HY)—were selected for mechanistic analysis. Resistant types showed stronger structural defenses: 64.55% lower stomatal density, 60.05% more trichome branching, and 52.28% higher epicuticular wax content than susceptible ones. These traits delayed appressorium formation by 12 h and hindered penetration peg development. After infection, resistant plants activated rapid immune responses—reactive oxygen species burst, hypersensitive reaction, and extensive lignin deposition. In LS, four defense enzyme activities rose 12 to 48 h earlier than in HY and reached levels 1.12 to 1.57 times higher. Six defense-related genes were significantly upregulated within 48 h postinoculation (hpi). Stepwise regression of 22 variables identified five key predictors of resistance: stomatal density, lesion diameter at 120 hpi (cm), average phenylalanine ammonia-lyase gene expression (0, 4, and 8 hpi), average peroxidase enzyme activity (36, 48, and 72 hpi), and average hydrogen peroxide accumulation area (12, 24, and 36 hpi). A model based on these achieved 94.24% accuracy (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.95) in field validation, offering a reliable tool for evaluating kiwifruit resistance.
                  </jats:p>

title: How to Live Nonviolently in a Large Sentient World: Replies to Pepper, Hurn and Badman-King, and O’Brien
container-title: Journal of Practical Ethics
53f4f1199a5323c23cb403b733503ed24f61e5c3.abstract: <jats:p>The three commentaries on ‘Ethics for a large sentient world’ raise several problems for a Gandhian approach to animal ethics. In my responses, I defend my position that granting robust rights to individual insects is untenable, pushing us to look harder at alternative options. I explain how Gandhi’s commitment to nonviolence allows him to avoid the unwelcome implications his principles might otherwise have. I consider his nuanced position on the interplay between general principles and embedded responses to particular situations. I explain why he should not be read as an antinatalist. That said, his framework undeniably presents an austere ascetic ideal that calls on us to rethink the meaning of ‘progress’. The framework condemns many aspects of modern industrialized economies, not just their treatment of nonhuman animals.</jats:p>

title: Ethics for a Large Sentient World: Insects, Ahimsa, and Gandhi’s Progressive Ahimsaism
container-title: Journal of Practical Ethics
e2cbdcc45bdaf054a824ada2de251917b2a7ef67.abstract: <jats:p>Positions that link rights to sentience face an insect challenge: insects are plausibly sentient, yet recognizing individual insects as rights-bearers would problematize public health, veterinary, and agricultural benefits obtained by harming them. The most obvious responses seem inadequate. Indian animal ethics, which has always taken the idea of insect sentience seriously, is a promising place to look for further options. Of particular relevance is the idea of ahimsa (nonviolence, noninjury), but ahimsa in its ancient form has metaphysical commitments that secular animal ethics should not accept. More promising still is the progressive ahimsaism developed by Gandhi in the 1920s, on which duties of nonmaleficence can be overridden by duties of care, provided the duty of care is adopted, interpreted, and exercised in accordance with the guiding ideal of ahimsa. This article provides an exposition and analysis of the view and relates it to the insect challenge.</jats:p>

title: Trayectorias y desafíos en el Modelo de la Esquizofrenia como Trastorno de la Ipseidad
The Model of Schizophrenia as a Disorder of Ipseity: Trajectories and Challenges
container-title: Análisis Filosófico
63b27267abc92a3cd87e002b8a2fef5a7fdbcabb.abstract: <jats:p>El Modelo de la Esquizofrenia como Trastorno de la Ipseidad (IDM) caracteriza los síntomas de la condición como alteraciones radicales en la estructura subjetiva de la conciencia. Recientes críticas provenientes desde la filosofía de la mente y la tradición fenomenológica han motivado la formulación de una versión revisada del modelo (IDMr). Sin embargo, no todos los defensores del IDM comparten esta estrategia y algunos se preguntan incluso si realmente existe continuidad entre los dos modelos. Este artículo analiza los alcances y limitaciones del tránsito del IDM al IDMr. Luego de clarificar las principales ideas del IDM con un énfasis especial en la manera en que conceptualiza las nociones de sí-mismo (self) e ipseidad en su caracterización de la esquizofrenia, el artículo explora las críticas más relevantes al modelo original y evalúa las respuestas de sus defensores. Luego, se examina la versión revisada del modelo, evaluando los avances que representa, los problemas que deja abiertos y el grado de continuidad que mantiene con respecto a su formulación original.</jats:p>

title: Escuchar las voces de las familias: perspectivas de las políticas lingüísticas familiares chinas en Cataluña para la educación del chino como lengua de herencia
Hearing Family Voices: Insights from Chinese Family Language Policies in Catalonia for Chinese Heritage Language Education
倾听家庭的声音：加泰罗尼亚中国移民家庭语言政策对华语传承教育的启示

67017b2ac54b28816a1864ec04e8bf3d1b66f027.abstract: <jats:p> This study explores Chinese heritage language (CHL) education among immigrant families in Catalonia, Spain. Moving beyond a school-centered approach, it adopts a family language policy (FLP) perspective within a home-school ecological framework. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with seven families, it examines how FLP shapes children’s CHL learning and parents’ perceptions of CHL schools. The findings identify both driving and hindering forces: strong ideologies and effective management promote CHL learning, while conflicting ideologies and inconsistent practices constrain it. Parents’ strong reliance on CHL schools reveals a mismatch between their expectations and the institutional capacity of CHL schooling. These challenges suggest that sustaining HL learning requires not only structural coordination between home and school but also greater attention to relational and motivational dimensions of language learning. Overall, this study contributes empirical insights into CHL education in Spain and extends FLP research by foregrounding the home-school dimension.</jats:p>

title: Can Language Models Go beyond Coding? Assessing the Capability of Language Models to Build Real-World Systems
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
4fe8b2d11bd01b8df011f057ea1bcdb5dd479092.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Large language models (LLMs) have shown growing potential in software engineering, yet few benchmarks evaluate their ability to repair software during migration across instruction set architectures (ISAs). Cross-ISA migration, such as between
                    <jats:monospace>x86_64</jats:monospace>
                    and
                    <jats:monospace>aarch64</jats:monospace>
                    , requires handling complex dependencies, heterogeneous toolchains, and long build logs while ensuring executable verification. To address this challenge, we present
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Build-bench</jats:italic>
                    (Homepage:
                    <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://aiops-lab-nku.github.io/Build-bench/">https://aiops-lab-nku.github.io/Build-bench/</jats:ext-link>
                    , Code at
                    <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://github.com/zcyyc/Build-bench">https://github.com/zcyyc/Build-bench</jats:ext-link>
                    ), an end-to-end benchmark that systematically evaluates the capability of LLMs to repair build failures in cross-ISA settings.
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Build-bench</jats:italic>
                    collects 268 real-world failed packages and integrates auxiliary tools including
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Structure Extraction</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">File Content Extraction</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Content Modification</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Build Verification</jats:italic>
                    to support autonomous, tool-augmented reasoning. The repair process operates in an iterative loop where, upon failure, the model receives updated build logs and previous repair outcomes to refine subsequent attempts. Through a comparative evaluation across the studied models,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Build-bench</jats:italic>
                    reveals that current models achieve a maximum build success rate of 63.19% and tool usage patterns differ significantly across models. By coupling real build environments with verifiable outcomes,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Build-bench</jats:italic>
                    establishes the first architecture-aware benchmark for studying LLM-based software build and repair.
                  </jats:p>

title:
<scp>A-ProS</scp>
                    : Towards Reliable Autonomous Programming through Multi-Model Feedback
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
f96d235f4b76d4bdde48d61fa85d6c72601127d9.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong potential for automated code generation, yet their ability to iteratively refine solutions using execution feedback remains underexplored. Competitive programming offers an ideal testbed for this investigation, as it demands end-to-end algorithmic reasoning, precise implementation under strict computational constraints, and complete functional correctness with rigorous evaluation. In this article, we present
                    <jats:sc>A-ProS</jats:sc>
                    , an autonomous AI agent that solves competitive programming problems through a hybrid multi-model feedback framework separating solution generation from specialized debugging.
                    <jats:sc>A-ProS</jats:sc>
                    combines ChatGPT-based generators (GPT-4 and GPT-5) with three debugging critics: Codestral-2508, Llama-3.3-70B, and DeepSeek-R1, under a 2 × 3 factorial design. We evaluate six workflows on 367 problems from ICPC World Finals (2011–2024) and Codeforces (rated 1,200–1,800). The results show that GPT-5 workflows improve from 39 initial accepted solutions to 85–90 after three refinement rounds, while GPT-4 improves from 15 to 31–38. A controlled ablation on 47 problems shows that stateful refinement outperforms stateless approaches by 8.5–10.6 percentage points and reduces repeated failures by up to 3.5×. Compared to baseline agent loops,
                    <jats:sc>A-ProS</jats:sc>
                    achieves over 2× greater gains, highlighting the importance of persistent context and multi-model feedback for reliable autonomous program synthesis.
                  </jats:p>

title: LLM-Driven Collaborative Model for Untangling Commits via Explicit and Implicit Dependency Reasoning
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
3505591e9a70ebf5dbef34064636340fdc7f5136.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Atomic commits, which address a single development concern, are a best practice in software development. In practice, however, developers often produce tangled commits that mix unrelated changes, complicating code review and maintenance. Prior untangling approaches—rule-based, feature-based, or graph-based—have made progress but typically rely on shallow signals and struggle to distinguish explicit dependencies (e.g., control/dataflow) from implicit ones (e.g., semantic or conceptual relationships). In this article, we propose
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">ColaUntangle</jats:italic>
                    , a new collaborative consultation framework for commit untangling that models both explicit and implicit dependencies among code changes.
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">ColaUntangle</jats:italic>
                    integrates Large Language Model (LLM)-driven agents in a multi-agent architecture: one agent specializes in explicit dependencies, another in implicit ones, and a reviewer agent synthesizes their perspectives through iterative consultation. To capture structural and contextual information, we construct Explicit and Implicit Contexts, enabling agents to reason over code relationships with both symbolic and semantic depth. We evaluate
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">ColaUntangle</jats:italic>
                    on two widely used datasets (1,612 C# and 14k Java tangled commits). Experimental results show that
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">ColaUntangle</jats:italic>
                    outperforms the best-performing baseline, achieving an improvement of 44% on the C# dataset and 82% on the Java dataset. These findings highlight the potential of LLM-based collaborative frameworks for advancing automated commit untangling tasks.
                  </jats:p>

title: ProjectEvalPlus: An Agentic Software Engineering Benchmark with Automatic Language Extension and User Simulated Evaluation
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
fde738cf0816d1d1923cdf6adf36c67b0774149d.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Large Language Models (LLMs)</jats:bold>
                    have shown impressive capabilities in
                    <jats:bold>Software Engineering (SWE)</jats:bold>
                    , yet evaluating their performance on realistic project-level SWE remains challenging. Existing benchmarks focus on isolated snippets, lacking project-level context, language extensibilities, and end-user reality. Thus, we introduce
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">ProjectEvalPlus</jats:italic>
                    , a comprehensive user-interaction-simulation benchmark that extends automatic evaluation to multiple programming languages via
                    <jats:bold>Automatic Language Extensibility (ALE)</jats:bold>
                    , supports multi-agent scenario stages evaluation, and provides detailed feedback on logical and runtime errors. Through unified testing on Python, Java, and JavaScript, we demonstrate that ProjectEvalPlus effectively assesses LLM agents’ capabilities, reveals language-specific biases, and enables iterative cross-language adaptation. Our results highlight both the strengths and limitations of current LLM agents in practical software development, offering actionable insights for future multi-language, project-level software engineering evaluation.
                  </jats:p>

                  <jats:p>
                    Tidal disruption events (TDEs) are powerful probes of supermassive black hole (SMBH) properties and accretion physics. The existing light curve fitting tools assume that the disrupted stars are on parabolic orbits, which may introduce systematic biases in derived parameters. In this work, we extend the model of Zhong to construct a non-parabolic TDE model that incorporates orbital energy of the disrupted star as a free parameter (

title: Gastric variceal pressure gradient in patients with large spontaneous shunts: A novel approach to local hemodynamic assessment
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
d2f42494f68d6f38b7319806ca4cf538b24dd7cf.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) is a widely used metric to assess portal hypertension and predict the risk for variceal bleeding. However, in patients with cirrhosis and large spontaneous portosystemic shunts (SPSS), portal decompression may reduce intrahepatic pressure gradients and lead to an underestimation of local variceal hemodynamic stress.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To evaluate portal and variceal pressure characteristics in patients with cirrhosis and fundal varices and large SPSS.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This retrospective, single-center study included data from patients with cirrhosis and gastric varices and large SPSS. All patients underwent simultaneous measurement of HVPG, endoscopic ultrasound-guided portal pressure gradient (PPG), and direct gastric variceal pressure (GVP). The GVP gradient (GVPG) was defined as the difference between GVP and inferior vena cava pressure. Patients were stratified according to the presence of variceal bleeding within 4 weeks. Correlation, Bland-Altman, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Data from 25 patients were analyzed. The mean GVP was significantly higher than portal vein pressure (PVP) (27.04 ± 7.67 mmHg vs  19.84 ± 7.94 mmHg) and GVP was strongly correlated with PVP. The GVPG was substantially higher than both HVPG and PPG (P  < 0.001). Although correlation analyses revealed significant associations among HVPG, PPG, and GVPG, agreement analyses indicated substantial variability, suggesting that they were not interchangeable. Among these parameters, only GVPG differed significantly between patients with and without recent bleeding (18.40 ± 6.07 mmHg vs  13.20 ± 5.13 mmHg; P  = 0.030), whereas HVPG and PPG exhibited no significant differences. ROC curve analysis revealed that GVPG had moderate discriminatory ability for recent bleeding (area under the ROC curve = 0.760).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In patients with cirrhosis and SPSS, conventional HVPG and PPG may underestimate local variceal pressure whereas GVPG may facilitate assessment of bleeding risk, thus meriting prospective multicenter validation.</jats:p>

title: Human mitochondrial DNA variants influence telomere length: evidence from a transmitochondrial cybrid model
4725b8e99f05ac13b837679013707693bcb6df16.abstract: <jats:p>Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably among individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function-characterized by low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production-is critical for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. Since mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, it may influence TL at birth by regulating mitochondrial function in utero. To explore the relationship between mtDNA and TL in human, we used a transmitochondrial cybrid approach, introducing mitochondria from donor platelets with varying telomere lengths into mtDNA-depleted cells. This revealed an inverse correlation between donor blood TL and mitochondrial ROS levels measured in the resulting cybrids, suggesting that specific mtDNA variants may contribute to the maintenance of long telomeres in humans by enhancing mitochondrial fitness. During in vitro cybrid formation, a transient phase of oxidative stress precedes cellular adaptation. In this specific window, mtDNA variants associated with reduced complex I (CI) activity induced rapid telomere shortening—an effect rescued by antioxidant and NAD⁺ precursor supplementation. While these variants occur naturally in certain individuals with long telomeres, our data suggest that, at least under in vitro conditions of acute oxidative stress, CI is critical to support PARP1 activity by maintaining the NAD⁺/NADH balance, thereby preserving telomere integrity. Collectively, these findings solidify the link between mtDNA variants and human TL regulation, highlighting potential therapeutic opportunities for mitochondrial replacement strategies.</jats:p>

title: Confused Deputy Attack against Model Context Protocol
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
e4526401547524ae03c4d0a81e4446f780680185.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The model context protocol (MCP) has rapidly emerged as a standard framework for integrating large language models (LLMs) with external tools and resources. However, its metadata-driven and non-deterministic tool selection mechanism introduces a previously overlooked security threat. Leveraging this weakness, we uncover the
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">confused deputy attack</jats:italic>
                    , where an adversarial server with subtly manipulated metadata covertly overshadows a benign one, intercepting tool invocations without exhibiting overtly malicious behavior. To systematically study this threat, we develop
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Puppet</jats:italic>
                    , the first automated security evaluation framework that: (i) enriches benign tool descriptions through selective requirement engineering to maximize semantic expressiveness, (ii) restructures them into LLM-preferred formats using description schema transformation, and (iii) applies name prioritization to introduce complementary lexical bias. Furthermore, Puppet synthesizes valid user queries to enable systematic attack evaluation. We comprehensively evaluate Puppet across 14 models from 6 providers on 2 MCP hosts, demonstrating tool selection hijacking rates up to 90.89% and end-to-end malicious payload execution rates up to 86.46%, while remaining undetectable by representative security scanners (MCP-Scan and McpSafetyScanner), which are architecturally incapable of detecting metadata-level manipulation attacks. Counterintuitively, we find that reasoning-enabled models are significantly more vulnerable than their non-reasoning counterparts. Our findings expose a critical design-level attack surface in the MCP ecosystem and highlight the urgent need for principled security safeguards.
                  </jats:p>

title: Diffraction Analysis and Experimental Measurement of the External Diaphragm for the Large-angle White-light Coronagraph
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
6c4fe9abcc9c5ee6019d9fcbe4b4caddf9137c1a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In recent years, with the rapid increase in demand for space weather monitoring, coronagraphs have increasingly adopted lightweight and compact direct-imaging configurations, which places stricter requirements on the diffraction stray light suppression capability of the instrument external diaphragm. To meet the external diaphragm selection requirements of the Large-angle White-light Coronagraph, this study conducts a preliminary study on multi-shaped external diaphragms. The diffraction intensity distribution characteristics of different external diaphragms are analyzed to provide a basis for optimal selection. Simulation calculations of diffraction intensity are carried out for six types of external diaphragms: round, square, U-shaped, serrated round, serrated square, and serrated U-shaped. Combined with structural characteristics and processing feasibility, three types of external diaphragms, namely round, U-shaped, and serrated U-shaped, are selected for experimental verification. The experimental results show that the diffraction intensity suppression level of the serrated U-shaped external diaphragm can reach the order of 10
                    <jats:sup>−9</jats:sup>
                    , and its performance is significantly better than that of other external diaphragms, which can meet the requirements of the Large-angle White-light Coronagraph. The data and conclusions obtained in this study can provide key performance references and theoretical basis for the design and selection of external diaphragms in similar coronagraphs.
                  </jats:p>

title: Error analysis of a fully discrete structure-preserving finite element scheme for a diffuse-interface model of tumour growth
container-title: IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis
fe6b9e84bc72cca71001db7f4f92a365473b7b1e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We develop a linear fully discrete structure-preserving finite element method for a diffuse-interface model of tumour growth. The system couples a Cahn–Hilliard-type equation with a nonlinear reaction–diffusion equation for nutrient concentration and admits a dissipative energy law at the continuous level. For the discretization we employ a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) formulation together with a mixed finite element method for the Cahn–Hilliard part and standard conforming finite elements for the reaction–diffusion equation in space, combined with a first-order time-stepping scheme. The resulting method is unconditionally energy-stable, mass-preserving, and inherits a discrete energy dissipation law associated with the SAV-based approximate energy functional, while requiring the solution of only linear systems at each time step. Under suitable regularity assumptions on the exact solution we derive rigorous error estimates in the $L^{2}$, $H^{1}$ and $L^\infty $ norms, establishing first-order accuracy in time and optimal-order accuracy in space. A key step in this analysis is the proof of boundedness of the numerical solutions in $L^\infty $. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the robustness of the method in capturing characteristic phenomena such as aggregation and chemotactic tumour growth.</jats:p>

title: Multi-Attribute Scene Context and Pedestrian Behaviour Recognition using PEFT-Tuned Vision Transformer Model for Autonomous Driving System
container-title: ACM Journal on Autonomous Transportation Systems
c63182f170d7cc099d124316d6d1c951edcbc67c.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the real-time behavior of pedestrians and their surrounding context is essential for road safety. Unfortunately, current perception systems struggle to capture how multiple cues jointly influence behavior in diverse traffic scenarios. Most existing models in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and Autonomous driving system (ADS) predict only a single attribute, such as intent or trajectory, while overlooking the interaction between behavioral and environmental factors. We propose a unified multi-attribute framework based on a Vision Transformer, which is enhanced with lightweight, parameter-efficient adapters. This innovative modular design enables independent learning of eight complementary attributes, including pedestrian behavior (action, attention, crossing, occlusion) and scene context (weather, time of day, road presence, density). Our proposed framework updates fewer than 2% of the model parameters. We ran our proposed framework using the JAAD dataset, and the framework achieves over 90% accuracy on most attributes and exhibits consistent behavior–context relationships and demonstrates robustness under varied environmental conditions. To evaluate real-time suitability, we implemented an adaptive strategy that activates only the most relevant adapters based on scene conditions. This approach reduces computational cost by 28.5% and increases throughput by 40.8% without loss of accuracy. This research distinctly highlights the practical potential of modular, PEFT-enhanced transformers for scalable multi-attribute perception as foundational vision models continue to advance. The best-performing adapters and inference code are available on Github Repo.</jats:p>

title: Enhanced authentication and access control using Deep Kronecker networks and quantum key distribution techniques
container-title: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing
ff6840800d8c001167eff31293d8c94af455e10e.abstract: <jats:p>Authentication and Access Control (AAC) verifies the user and grants permission to an authorized person. Existing techniques struggled to manage multiple complex passwords. Therefore, the new framework, Deep Kronecker Network with Addax Optimization Algorithm (DKN_AOA), is devised to enhance AAC. The network model combines the entities, such as data owner, data user, Cloud Service Provider (CSP), and authorization center. First, the security parameters are defined in the initialization phase, and secure communication of all the entities is ensured by the registration phase. Consequently, the authentication phase verifies the data owner and provides access to the data. Later, the secret key is generated by DKN in the Quantum Key Agreement (QKA) phase, and DKN is optimized by the AOA. Next, the secret key is converted into a quantum key. Subsequently, the data protection phase protects the data from unauthorized access. Data users receive the data and decrypt it using the secret keys. Finally, the data owner updates the new key. A novel DKN_AOA acquires a computational cost of 7.385[Formula: see text]s and memory usage of 35.8[Formula: see text]MB for key size 8 and data size 500[Formula: see text]MB. Furthermore, the DKN_AOA obtained an Authentication Success Rate (ASR) of 98.15% and a detection rate of 98.78% for key size 256 and data size 500[Formula: see text]MB.</jats:p>

title: Exploited People, Exploited Animals: A Multi-Perspective Approach to Christy Lefteri’s Songbirds
container-title: Forum for Modern Language Studies
18ce3adcbb57abfee2e136911ae034107dfb75cd.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Through her works The Beekeeper of Aleppo and Songbirds, Christy Lefteri has brought attention to the exploitation of vulnerable groups worldwide, including refugees, immigrants and animals. This article examines the intersecting points of migratory birds and Asian female immigrants working in Cyprus as depicted in Songbirds. It argues that Lefteri intertwines the exploitation of these groups to challenge the cycle of exploitation both in Cyprus and globally, aiming to reshape our relationship with marginalized groups and wildlife. Her advocacy for songbirds and immigrant women workers (also known as domestic female workers) in Cyprus reflects the author’s environmental activism. Building upon primarily Marxist and postcolonial ecocriticism, while also incorporating insights from animal studies, this article demonstrates how human exploitation is intricately connected to animal exploitation.</jats:p>

title: The Influence of Tourist Motivation on Intention to Attend the Seventeenth "Right Here" World Tour Jakarta 2025 Concert
container-title: LACULTOUR: Journal of Language and Cultural Tourism
a48f44a710a347433ced9db7a5e5060de49eba27.abstract: <jats:p>Concert attendance is no longer perceived merely as a form of entertainment but also as a type of event-based tourism influenced by tourists' travel motivations. This study aims to examine the effect of tourist motivation on visiting intention toward the Seventeen "Right Here" World Tour Jakarta 2025 concert. A quantitative approach was employed, involving 100 respondents who had attended the concert, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, simple linear regression, the t-test, and the coefficient of determination using IBM SPSS Statistics. The findings reveal that tourist motivation has a positive and statistically significant effect on visiting intention. The higher the level of tourist motivation, the stronger the intention to attend the concert. Motivations driven by the desire for entertainment, social interaction, and emotional experiences were identified as the primary factors influencing visiting intention. These findings provide practical insights for concert organizers and tourism stakeholders in developing effective marketing strategies to enhance visitor interest and support the sustainable growth of event tourism.</jats:p>

title: Visualizing Vibrancy: A Multimodal Analysis of Photographic Representations in Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guidebook
container-title: LACULTOUR: Journal of Language and Cultural Tourism
077e789b8f124b75a85275f2b96d982759df011e.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the meaning-making process of 224 photographic representations in Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guidebook (English e-version) in relation to its tourism slogan Vibrant Ho Chi Minh. The research adopts a multimodal discourse analysis approach, integrating both qualitative and quantitative methods. The primary theoretical framework is adapted from Hunter’s (2008) typology of photographic representations, which was, in turn, developed from Kress and Van Leeuwen's (2006) Visual Grammar. The findings indicate that the vibrancy of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam is significantly emphasized by these photographic representations, with its rich cultural aspects (51.79%) and modern infrastructure (20.98%) being prominently depicted together with its outstanding tourism products (21.87%). In other words, this vibrancy is constructed from both internal vibrancy (intangible values) and external vibrancy (tangible infrastructure and amenities). Furthermore, in the context of Vietnam’s robust tourism development and the globalizing trends within the industry, the study proposes recommendations aimed at enhancing the persuasive efficacy of the photographic representations in tourism texts promoting destinations in Vietnam.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Effective communication between clinicians and patients plays an important role in the successful delivery of health care.                     <jats:p>Gemma-3-27B-it, an instruction fine-tuned open-source large language model (LLM) by Google, was used, and few-shot prompting was applied to enable the generation of patient-friendly simplifications of 64 deidentified geriatric outpatient reports written in German while preserving clinical meaning. title: Bridging the Gap: Student Perceptions of Instructor Engagement in Pandemic-Era Online Learning
container-title: The Journal  of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering
452b4dd3c76ef236fdfaa05cc15c934e6b286cde.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines student perceptions of instructor engagement in online learning environments during the initial onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular attention to differences between students with prior online learning experience and those transitioning from traditional face-to-face instruction. Grounded in Moore’s transactional distance theory, the research explores how sudden shifts in instructional modality influenced students’ perceptions of instructor engagement and identifies strategies that may reduce perceived distance in online learning contexts. Survey data were collected during the summer of 2020 from students enrolled at a regional comprehensive university in the mid-South following the emergency transition to remote instruction. A comparative analysis was conducted across course modalities, focusing on seven survey items related to academic engagement, changes in instructor interaction, and student preferences for engagement. Findings indicate that students with prior experience in online courses perceived less disruption in instructor engagement following the transition, while students who had been enrolled primarily in face-to-face courses reported more noticeable declines. These differences suggest that familiarity with online learning environments may buffer students against perceived losses in engagement during periods of instructional disruption. Overall, this study contributes to the growing body of research on online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic by emphasizing how instructional practices and student experience intersect to influence motivation, engagement, and perceived learning success in online environments.</jats:p>

title: Inclusive Cognitive Design for Global Workforce
container-title: Creative Advantage of Cultural Diversity in Global Business
3c9423f36ac85a9387994c325c3b8405da65dee9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper combines microlearning and inclusivity by suggesting a cognitive design framework that deals with unstable memory at the organizational level. Precarious memory is infrequently addressed in organizational research. This study integrates cognitive science, instructional frameworks, and diversity practices while examining the challenges encountered in VUCA workforce environments. Microlearning as the primary mechanism, facilitated by cultural intelligence and bias awareness, results in task agility and is regulated by psychological safety. The research demonstrates the substantial effectiveness of microlearning in mitigating fragile memory. The results indicate that unstable memory and memory distortion can be trained and alleviated using the proposed framework. This framework makes things more fair and equal and less biased in the workplace. Microlearning's modular approach connects learning with making good decisions, which helps create a workplace that is fair and ethical.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Harmony
container-title: Innovative Strategies for Well-Being and Motivation in Education
010b400f9132cfa7bf09958baa6e7f8172d8af52.abstract: <jats:p>Previous research has shown how motivation and anxiety affect students' academic success, which highlights the importance of implementing strategies in the classroom to promote motivation and manage anxiety in students. Despite these findings, there is a lack of research offering practical guidelines for applying this knowledge in the classrooms. Therefore, the need arises to identify and compile educational strategies and practices that teachers can implement in the classroom to foster motivation and control their students' anxiety. In this chapter, we conducted a literature review aimed at compiling, from an educational scientific evidence approach, various interventions and teaching strategies to promote learning achievement through motivation and anxiety management.</jats:p>

title: Building Bridges
container-title: Innovative Strategies for Well-Being and Motivation in Education
c3f3856b951537f41d996226c542d7ca26a0519b.abstract: <jats:p>In the most recent research on the subject, the student's perception of having the unconditional support of his or her teacher has been shown to be a key variable in the student's school adjustment by promoting his or her school involvement and improving his or her academic performance. However, this knowledge still needs to be refined and the role of each type of support offered by the teacher on the different components of school adjustment still needs to be determined. Two questionnaires, one to assess perceived social support and the other for school involvement, were applied to a sample of 323 secondary school students. The results, extracted by means of a structural regression model, confirm the influence of the perception of the types of teacher support on school adjustment. The data are discussed in terms of previous research and their relevance for the improvement of the teacher-student relationship</jats:p>

title: Engagement and Satisfaction
container-title: Innovative Strategies for Well-Being and Motivation in Education
9de441fffe07454380a91a0e86cf35fa6a66ed49.abstract: <jats:p>Teachers are the pillars of the education system and are responsible for training and educating future citizens. However, nowadays, their level of commitment and satisfaction has sometimes been called into question, as this can directly influence their students. This influence is not only on students' motivation and emotional and personal development but also on students' academic performance. Therefore, the aim of this paper is to explore teachers' perceptions of how their commitment to the teaching profession contributes to students' academic performance and students' views of the impact of their commitment and satisfaction with the teaching profession on their academic performance. To achieve this objective, a non-systematic theoretical review of scientific articles was carried out. This allowed an in-depth unrestricted review of articles published between 2019 and 2024 in databases such as Web of Science and Scopus to study success stories of the influence of Engagement and Satisfaction from the point of view of both teachers and students.</jats:p>

title: Digital Quality Assurance for Refugee Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
be7e6eff4a1727c47e4a282be62ea19a563a46f3.abstract: <jats:p>The digital turn in higher education has redefined how quality is conceptualised, delivered, and measured, yet refugee learners continue to be excluded from these transformative shifts. Among them, the Rohingya refugees in India remain structurally marginalised, with little access to accredited or quality-assured higher-education opportunities. This chapter investigates how digital quality assurance frameworks can close these educational divides by drawing comparative lessons from Germany's refugee integration model. Through a doctrinal and expert-opinion legal-policy approach, the study interprets the role of technology, regulation, and institutional accountability in building inclusive quality systems. It analyses Germany's Akkreditierungsrat standards, DAAD Integra initiatives, and data-driven monitoring as benchmarks for digital assurance, then contrasts them with India's digital ecosystem within the framework of the National Education Policy 2020. The research develops a Digital Quality Assurance for Refugee Education model that aligns with SDG 4 and SDG 16.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Adaptation and Leadership in AI-Augmented Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
a5612c037c0c5391ee895bba1a4fc5ae65f530b1.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI poses pressing governance challenges regarding the future of human-AI interaction and how it enhances or diminishes the cognitive capabilities, professional role, and leadership of academic professionals. Three cognitive adaptation patterns emerge from the analysis of the qualitative data (retrieved from the interviews) and the quantitative data (PLS-SEM survey): AI Augmentation, AI Dependency, and AI Co-construction. The positive relationship between adaptation outcomes and AI trust is supported by PLS-SEM, with the cognitive load change as a mediator and the organisational learning orientation as a moderator, the most significant institutional factor influencing adaptation outcomes. The chapter suggests embedding metacognition and AI literacy in workforce governance, institutional reflection in HR and L&D processes, and complementarity guardrails. For practical governance tools for adopting responsible AI in higher education, a validated diagnostic instrument and a Human-AI Capability Convergence Model are provided.</jats:p>

title: An Individualized Approach to Augmentative and Alternative Communication for Cortical Visual Impairment: One Family's Progression Toward an Accessible Language System
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
f0ff7edf9656cc552dd1d0ce7c53989cc10572bd.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Speech-language pathologists report a desire for guidance to develop and maintain augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) supports that are customized and visually accessible for individuals with cortical visual impairment (CVI; Boster et al., 2021). In 2023, Wilkinson et al. introduced the “CVI/AAC Framework” that offered initial evidence-based considerations and data collection prompts to address this clinical challenge. The current article was written to illustrate the process of the clinical application of the CVI/AAC Framework for a young child with cerebral palsy and concomitant CVI. By demonstrating the team efforts to build a developmentally appropriate aided AAC system that was responsive to the child's CVI and motor support needs, we hope to demonstrate the utility of the framework and promote clinical uptake for decision making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The team, which included clinicians, other professionals, and the child's mother, implemented an iterative approach to AAC assessment and implementation based on ongoing discussions surrounding the CVI/AAC Framework domains and the child's progress. The relative frequency of different topics of discussion and the subsequent types of decisions made were quantified to illustrate the clinical process. Furthermore, a detailed case analysis of the contents of the discussion were extracted from the transcripts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The team met collaboratively for 8 months, resulting in 13 meetings. A total of 97 topics were discussed and coded related to the CVI/AAC Framework or general AAC assessment. Of the topics related to the framework, Domain 1 (characteristics of the individual) accounted for the most discussions followed by Domain 3 (AAC system design choices). Meeting documentation and screen captures of the child's AAC system across time demonstrated changes in the child's linguistic and visual functioning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This clinical focus article illustrates a starting point for implementation of the CVI/AAC Framework as a complementary approach to typical AAC assessment procedures. This approach should prompt clinicians to make individualized AAC changes that support meaningful communication and participation and provide a basis for future systematic research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    </jats:p>

title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based Digital Interventions for Illicit Substance Use Disorders: Scoping Review of Intervention Design, Efficacy Indicators, and Methodological Gaps
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
9d1858cff34c91ccfc45c7d996e799804ca90d99.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Illicit substance use disorders (SUDs) are escalating globally; yet, social stigma and legal barriers restrict access to conventional treatment, and existing research remains skewed toward alcohol and nicotine. Digital interventions incorporating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) offer a discreet, scalable alternative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review maps how CBT-based digital interventions for illicit SUDs are designed and delivered across platforms, identifying their theoretical frameworks, functional components, outcome indicators, and reported methodological limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). Six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycINFO, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) were searched from inception to June 28, 2026, without language, date, or study design limits, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching (July 3, 2026). Eligible studies were empirical primary studies quantitatively evaluating digital interventions incorporating CBT for illicit or nonprescribed substance use; alcohol- or nicotine-only populations were excluded. Three reviewers independently screened and charted all studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus or adjudication. Data were synthesized narratively, with tables, figures, and an evidence gap map.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fifty-six studies published between 2008 and 2026, drawn from 47 distinct participant samples, met the eligibility criteria. Most were conducted in North America (40/56, 71.4%) and used randomized controlled designs (39/56, 69.6%). Polysubstance-using populations were most frequently targeted (32/56, 57.1%), followed by cannabis (13/56, 23.2%), opioids (6/56, 10.7%), and stimulants (5/56, 8.9%). Interventions were delivered mainly via web (24/56, 42.9%) or app (24/56, 42.9%) platforms, and most (49/56, 87.5%) were grounded in traditional CBT, most often combined with contingency management (18/56, 32.1%) or motivational interviewing (17/56, 30.4%). Core functional components included therapeutic intervention (55/56, 98.2%), self-tracking and notification (25/56, 44.6%), reward (24/56, 42.9%), and support and feedback (21/56, 37.5%). Primary outcomes focused on substance use and abstinence (41/56, 73.2%), retention/feasibility (16/56, 28.6%), and mental health status or coping skills (14/56, 25%). Author-reported limitations were predominantly participant-level (52/56, 92.9%), measurement-level (43/56, 76.8%), study-level (34/56, 60.7%), and intervention-level (25/56, 44.6%) domains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Unlike previous reviews confined to a single substance or delivery platform, this review is innovative in mapping CBT-based digital interventions across the full spectrum of illicit substances, including polysubstance use, and in linking their functional components to intended therapeutic mechanisms. It thereby contributes to the development of these technologies and, by synthesizing author-reported limitations, proposes methodological improvements for their future evaluation. At present, CBT-based digital interventions are best positioned as adjuncts that extend the reach and continuity of existing addiction care rather than as stand-alone substitutes for it; substance-specific customization, objective outcome measures, and modular trial designs are needed to establish them as scalable clinical tools.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Multi-model ensemble projections of African humid heat extremes and their implications for future health studies
container-title: Environmental Research: Health
71c28d244b3645341138d8ea6a4574cf40f14c6b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Global warming and extreme heat events have well-documented adverse effects on human health. As a first step to understand the possible future risk for heat-related illness and mortality, this study analyzes climate model projections to constrain model variability and spread related to humid heat extremes over Africa. Using CMIP6, CESM2-LE, CORDEX and CMIP5 models, we examine the impacts of model uncertainty, horizontal resolution, and internal variability on projections of heat indices, including wet bulb temperature, wet bulb globe temperature, Humidex, and the extended heat index, over the next century. Across resolutions and model types, humid heat projections under moderate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission scenarios (SSP245/RCP45) indicate that Sub-Saharan Africa will experience a higher count of extreme heat events over the next century compared to the rest of the continent. Within CESM2-LE, the trends in humid heat metrics are driven almost entirely by external forcings (i.e. increasing GHG emissions), except in parts of Central, Northeast, and Southeast Africa, where natural variability accounts for roughly 10%–18% of the total variance. Model resolution has a significant impact on the simulated number of extreme humid heat events; low-resolution models from CMIP5 project roughly 40–80 more extreme event days per year over Central Africa by the end of the century compared to their corresponding downscaled CORDEX models. This work serves as a key precursor to future studies projecting heat-health outcomes due to climate change over Africa.</jats:p>

title: AttenResUNet: An RFI Detection Model Based on the AttenRes Architecture
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
0a352f0ee784005a79843fe4da749fce11f5fdcc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate classification and detection of Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) is a core step in the preprocessing of radio astronomy observational data, which directly affects the quality of astronomical signal extraction and analysis. Traditional threshold-based detection methods rely on manual parameter tuning, making it difficult to set appropriate thresholds and handle increasingly complex and diverse types of RFI. Since 2017, UNet-based models have become a popular research approach for RFI mitigation. However, conventional UNet-like models suffer from drawbacks such as high computational cost, easy loss of detailed information during deep feature propagation, and insufficient detection accuracy for small-scale RFI. To cope with these situations, this paper proposes the AttenResUNet model, which integrates strip pooling enhancement, adaptive attention weight calculation, and a blocking mechanism to construct an efficient and accurate multi-class RFI detection framework. Experimental results on the RFI image data set show that the average F1-score of the proposed model after excluding the background category is improved by more than 20% compared with threshold-based methods. For weak narrowband RFI, the F1-score is increased by 5% relative to traditional UNet, ResUNet, and other models, while the training cost is reduced by over 60%. The model enables fine-grained classification and detection of five RFI categories under limited computing resources, providing a new technical route for efficient processing of radio astronomy data. Validation experiments demonstrate that data denoised by our model yields significantly improved signal-to-noise ratio in pulsar search images for NGC 6517 B, F and G, with sharper peaks and more distinct pulsar characteristics.</jats:p>
