2090be89b86a832de409d77a4c6b2d9136db223e.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, we have developed a physics-based analytical framework for a dielectric-modulated MgZnO/ZnO MOS-high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) biosensor that can detect biomolecules. Biomolecule dielectric modulation is linked with effective gate capacitance, two-dimensional electron gas (2-DEG) density, surface potential and drain current. The analytical baseline MgZnO/ZnO HEMT model shows excellent agreement with the experimental data, with coefficients of determination ([Formula: see text]) of 0.9961 and 0.9987 for the transfer and output characteristics, respectively. Beyond conventional current-based sensing, the framework evaluates higher-order transconductances, quantum capacitance, gate charge, intrinsic capacitances, cut-off frequency and thermal noise. Thermal-noise-limited signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is evaluated to connect electrical sensitivity with intrinsic detectability. The further extension is the analytical evaluation of Z parameters [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] to analyze the small-signal electrical response of the biosensor. The drain-on sensitivity of 37.3% is obtained using the proposed model.</jats:p>

title: AI for Wind Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
d6d8adf202aed253644ed73dead2e3bcff980f7b.abstract: <jats:p>The renewable energy is being transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) to create smarter, efficient, and adaptive wind systems. AI forecasts the wind using machine learning and neural networks and optimizes the performance of turbines and minimizes costs related to maintenance using predictive analytics. These inventions assist the operators in predicting the changes, setting the turbines, and reducing downtime. Urban deployment of AI facilitates the seamless synchronization of mass-scaled wind energy with smart grids as well as the systems of IoT. It balances loads dynamically, for instance, it trades energy in real time and improves stability in the grid. Heavy reliance on fossil fuels and extensive reliance on carbon emissions and fossil fuels can be reduced through the implementation of AI-driven systems that enhance energy efficiency, reliability, and sustainability through the integration of renewable sources, storage, and intelligent control.</jats:p>

title: AI for Wind Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
4f4dc990deb9ecb4d79f7eb21160b4d6a0c8d4aa.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the wind energy sector, marking a major step toward sustainable and intelligent societies. As global energy demands rise and carbon reduction becomes urgent, AI offers powerful tools to enhance the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of wind power systems. Through technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins, and predictive analytics, AI optimizes turbine design, predictive maintenance, load forecasting, and smart grid integration. By leveraging big data from sensors, meteorological sources, and operational parameters, AI enables accurate wind prediction, timely fault detection, and real-time performance optimization. Additionally, AI-driven systems play an emerging role in urban wind integration by improving micro-wind utilization, energy storage, and distributed generation within smart cities. The chapter also addresses economic feasibility, environmental sustainability, and ethical implications of AI-enabled wind energy applications.</jats:p>

title: Aspect–Sentiment Triplet Extraction in Low-Resource Odia Language Using a Tri-Channel GCN
container-title: ACM Transactions on Asian and Low-Resource Language Information Processing
59165272f90e12f65ea2a5d353109678a1feea6a.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    With the proliferation of digital platforms and smartphones, users increasingly express opinions in their native languages through online reviews. However, fine-grained sentiment analysis for such low-resource languages remains underexplored, as most Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) methods target resource-rich languages such as English. To address this gap, we present Odia-TriGCN, a hybrid framework for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction in the low-resource Odia language. It integrates tree-distance relations (dependency and constituent trees), syntactic dependencies, and biaffine semantic attention to capture rich structural and semantic cues. The model further leverages auxiliary features from an Odia news corpus and cross-lingual supervision using an Odia–English parallel corpus. We also incorporate a
                    <jats:bold>customized dependency parser</jats:bold>
                    trained on manually annotated data following the Universal Dependencies (UD) scheme, to obtain consistent head-dependent relations. Additionally, we extend the existing Odia ABSA dataset and introduce
                    <jats:bold>Odia-Triplet</jats:bold>
                    , a manually annotated dataset comprising aspect-opinion-sentiment triplets. Experiments across five domains show that Odia-TriGCN outperforms the strongest compared non-LLM baseline in each domain by 5.6 to 7.1 absolute F1 points. The framework is further evaluated in cross-lingual (Odia→Hindi, Odia→Bengali) and code-mixed (Odia–English, Odia–Hindi–English, Odia–Bengali–English) settings, providing further evidence of its applicability in multilingual contexts.
                  </jats:p>

title: Impact of inoculum effect on in vitro activity of intermittent and continuous piperacillin-tazobactam infusion against ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in a hollow-fiber infection model
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
f6976a53f13352681d179f4ad8625f6e55828a7a.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Use of piperacillin-tazobactam (TZP) in the treatment of severe extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Escherichia coli</jats:italic>
                      (ESBL-EC) infections is controversial. Two features may explain treatment failures: the inoculum effect and suboptimal pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment, particularly in critically ill patients. To study the combined impact of the inoculum effect and a PK/PD optimization on the
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">in vitro</jats:italic>
                      efficacy of TZP against ESBL-EC infections. Five-day hollow-fiber infection model simulating TZP pharmacokinetics in critically ill patients was performed: two TZP infusion regimens (4/0.5 g q6h over 30 min, and 16/2 g q24h continuous infusion), three ESBL-EC clinical strains:
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">1146</jats:italic>
                      (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">bla</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>CTX-M-15</jats:sub>
                      , MIC = 2 mg/L),
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">3383</jats:italic>
                      (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">bla</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>CTX-M-15</jats:sub>
                      +
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">bla</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>TEM-1</jats:sub>
                      , MIC = 4 mg/L), and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">2262</jats:italic>
                      (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">bla</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>CTX-M-15</jats:sub>
                      +
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">bla</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>OXA-1</jats:sub>
                      , MIC = 8 mg/L), and two initial inocula (5 and 7 log
                      <jats:sub>10</jats:sub>
                      CFU/mL). Intermittent infusion was associated with systematic bacterial regrowth within 24 h, consistent with failure to reach the 100%fT >4× MIC threshold. Continuous infusion resulted in undetectable bacterial count for the strains
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">3383</jats:italic>
                      (MIC = 4 mg/L, low inoculum) and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">1146</jats:italic>
                      (MIC = 2 mg/L, low and high inocula). For strain
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">3383</jats:italic>
                      , the inoculum effect was demonstrated by total bacterial killing in continuous infusion with low inoculum, whereas early regrowth (>10 log
                      <jats:sub>10</jats:sub>
                      CFU/mL) with resistance emergence (MIC > 256 mg/L) was observed with high inoculum. Strain
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">2262</jats:italic>
                      (MIC = 8 mg/L) exhibited systematic treatment failure regardless of infusion mode or inoculum size. Continuous infusion of TZP may be considered as a carbapenem-sparing agent in ESBL-EC infection with a TZP MIC ≤ 2 mg/L regardless of inoculum, or a TZP MIC of 4 mg/L at low inoculum. TZP should not be used for strains with an MIC of 8 mg/L or suspected OXA-1 co-production, irrespective of the infusion mode.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Infections caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Escherichia coli</jats:italic>
                      represent a growing therapeutic challenge, particularly in critically ill patients. Carbapenems remain the reference treatment, but their overuse drives resistance emergence. Piperacillin-tazobactam is a potential carbapenem-sparing agent, but its clinical efficacy remains debated, partly due to the inoculum effect (a reduction in antibiotic activity at high bacterial densities) and suboptimal dosing regimens. Using a hollow-fiber infection model simulating the pharmacokinetics of critically ill patients, this study demonstrates that continuous infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam can overcome the inoculum effect under specific conditions, defined by the MIC of the infecting strain and the estimated bacterial density. These findings support a stratified approach to piperacillin-tazobactam use in severe ESBL-producing
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">E. coli</jats:italic>
                      infections, based on MIC, inoculum size, and β-lactamase profile, and may help clinicians identify patients who could safely receive piperacillin-tazobactam instead of a carbapenem.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Modeling of Therapist-Client Dynamics in Psychotherapy Using Large Language Model–Based Assessments: Retrospective Observational Study of 1573 Psychotherapy Sessions
container-title: JMIR Mental Health
bbd1b8bf00ce59fa6e0453907abaf3329d1f8fbe.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Psychotherapy is a primary treatment for many mental health conditions, yet the dynamic interplay among therapist behaviors, client responses, and the therapeutic relationship remains difficult to disentangle at scale. Traditional process research relies on labor-intensive human coding, limiting the ability to model moment-to-moment therapeutic dynamics across large datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to develop and validate a computational framework for modeling therapist-client interaction processes and to examine how therapist behaviors and relational qualities relate to client self-disclosure and emotional expression in psychotherapy sessions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed automated assessment pipelines using large language models (LLMs) to measure therapist behaviors (empathy or exploration), relational quality (rapport), and client outcomes (self-disclosure, self-directed negative emotion, or outward-directed negative emotion). Model-generated scores were validated against human annotations. We then applied these measures to approximately 2000 hours of psychotherapy transcripts from the Alexander Street corpus. This yielded an estimation sample of 119,233 client utterances from 1573 sessions and 37 clients. Because utterances are nested within sessions and sessions within clients, we estimated a saturated multivariate structural equation model with SEs clustered at the session level. Results were confirmed in a multilevel regression model with random intercepts for session and client.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Following comparative validation of 6 candidate language models, automated measures showed good to excellent agreement with human annotations (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]=0.60-0.81) for rapport (ICC=0.81), self-disclosure (ICC=0.78), empathy components (ICC=0.60-0.75), and emotion measurements (ICC=0.66-0.80). Structural equation modeling analyses revealed that therapist empathy and exploration were each associated with increased client disclosure (empathy: β=.086, 95% CI 0.078-0.095; exploration: β=.086, 95% CI 0.078-0.094; both P<.001) and increased expression of self-directed negative emotions, comprising sadness, anxiety, fear, and depression (empathy: β=.118, 95% CI 0.110-0.127; exploration: β=.078, 95% CI 0.070-0.087; both P<.001). Both behaviors were also associated with reduced expressions of enjoyment (empathy: β=–.037; exploration: β=–.041; both P<.001). Surprisingly, rapport in the prior session showed no association with client self-disclosure or negative emotion expression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates that LLM-based measurement combined with structural modeling can capture core therapeutic processes at scale. Empathy and exploration showed small but consistent turn-level associations with client disclosure and emotional expression, whereas prior-session rapport did not show a robust association. These findings provide a computational foundation for precision modeling of psychotherapy processes and may offer actionable insights for scalable therapist training and AI-supported clinical education systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Reduced-order statistical model for optical vortex singularity displacement in atmospheric turbulence
container-title: Journal of the Optical Society of America A
9b5d20a35977c346d5bef26afeee92d7b8db6ae9.abstract: <jats:p>The propagation of optical vortex beams through atmospheric turbulence leads to stochastic displacement and structural evolution of phase singularities, with important implications for singular optics and free-space optical communication. We present a reduced-order, semi-empirical statistical model for the ensemble-averaged radial displacement of vortex singularities, which decomposes the normalized displacement into two physically distinct contributions: a first-order (tilt-like) term that follows the classical Kolmogorov exponent, and a topology-dependent splitting term that grows with topological charge. The model is validated quantitatively against high-resolution numerical simulation of phase-screen turbulence and angular-spectrum propagation, with residuals, goodness-of-fit measures, and hold-out errors reported over its stated range of validity. Phase contour maps and intensity profiles further illustrate the turbulence-induced distortion of the helical phase structure and the emergence of multiple unit-charge singularities for higher-order modes. The framework offers a practical basis for assessing vortex beam stability in free-space optical systems.</jats:p>

title: Mobile Technology Engagement Among Caregivers and Its Implications for Childhood Antibiotic Stewardship in Northern Vietnam: Mixed Methods Community-Based Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
c305776fc7a17d9be4a5588ca0d1f0bbb7e0a81d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In Vietnam, antibiotic use without involvement of health care professionals is common in the community, despite the legal requirement for a prescription. In low- and middle-income countries, mobile health (mHealth) is perceived as having the potential to improve community health care at low cost.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, we aimed to explore the relationship between mobile phone ownership and health-seeking behaviors among caregivers of children aged 5 years or younger to inform the design of an mHealth intervention to improve antibiotic use practices in the community.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A convergent mixed methods approach combined a cross-sectional household survey and in-depth interviews (IDIs). We surveyed 450 households with children aged 5 years or younger and interviewed caregivers about their health-seeking behaviors and how they engage with mobile technology to inform their health care decisions and antibiotic use. Qualitative data were collected through IDIs and focus group discussions (FGDs) with a purposive sample of household survey respondents. Data collection was conducted between June and September 2023 at 2 sites: 1 urban and 1 rural area in a northern province of Vietnam. Factors associated with using mobile phones to seek health care information were identified through multivariable logistic regression and thematic analysis. Quantitative and qualitative findings were then integrated to provide contextual insights.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>For the quantitative household survey, 450 of 460 approached households completed the survey. For the qualitative component, 38 of 60 approached caregivers participated in 4 FGDs and 6 IDIs. Almost all households had an internet connection (444/450, 98.7%, 95% CI 97.1%-99.4%). While 80.2% (308/384, 95% CI 75.9%-83.9%) of caregivers used mobile devices to access child health care information, only 27.1% (29/107, 95% CI 19.6%-36.2%) reported using the internet to obtain antibiotic-related information. Older caregivers (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.65, 95% CI 0.43-0.99) and caregivers living in the urban area (aOR 0.45, 95% CI 0.24-0.85) were less likely to seek health-related information online using mobile devices than younger or rural caregivers, respectively. In contrast, a higher level of caregiver education was significantly associated with more favorable engagement in online health information–seeking behavior (aOR 2.73, 95% CI 1.61-4.61). Caregivers demonstrated highly active and intentional online information-seeking behaviors, driven by a strong desire to enhance their knowledge and confidence in making childcare and treatment decisions. Qualitative findings highlighted a need for trustworthy, professionally supported digital health platforms tailored to child health and antibiotic use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study highlights caregivers’ health care information–seeking behaviors and engagement with digital technologies for antibiotic-related information, demonstrating the potential of mobile phones to support antibiotic-related decision-making and improve antibiotic use practices. These findings provide insights to inform the design of context-appropriate mHealth interventions to support caregivers in making decisions about antibiotic use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Stuttering Treatment Priorities and Clinical Challenges Across the Lifespan in Iran: A Mixed-Methods Study of Speech-Language Pathologists
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
4689889123860e45750d2786a63d56293b4303c2.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provided an initial exploration of Iranian speech-language pathologists' (SLPs') treatment priorities, reported intervention approaches, and perceived clinical challenges for stuttering across the lifespan.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Seventy-four Iranian SLPs completed a Farsi online survey ranking three treatment aspects aligned with the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health—overt stuttering behaviors, reactions to stuttering, and communication participation—across preschool, school-age/adolescent, and adult clients. They also rated intervention use frequency and described clinical challenges. Quantitative data were analyzed using nonparametric tests, qualitative responses were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, and exploratory mixed-methods integration linked clinician priority profiles to qualitative themes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across all three age groups, clinicians ranked overt behaviors highest, reactions intermediate, and communication participation lowest. This hierarchy did not shift meaningfully across age groups and was not associated with education or clinical experience. Qualitative themes highlighted pressure for fluency, relapse, acceptance, generalization difficulties, emotional burden, and clinician uncertainty. Exploratory participant-level integration showed that clinicians with stronger fluency-anchored profiles appeared less likely to describe challenges related to relapse, generalization, and pressure for fluency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this initial sample, clinicians' self-reported priorities remained strongly oriented toward overt speech behaviors despite contemporary multidimensional models of stuttering. Findings should be regarded as exploratory and as a basis for larger replication studies. Findings highlight the need for training and service models that more explicitly integrate participation, counseling-informed support, and stigma-responsive care across the lifespan.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Clinical Interpretation and Structured Reporting of Velopharyngeal Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Framework for Multidisciplinary Decision Making
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
1108a9c74c2bb18f13f24e47f4b208b3a289c4cc.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables direct visualization of the velopharyngeal (VP) mechanism, including the soft palate, pharyngeal walls, adenoid tissue, and levator veli palatini (LVP) musculature. As VP MRI becomes more integrated into multidisciplinary craniofacial care, speech-language pathologists (SLPs) are increasingly involved in image interpretation. However, structured guidance for translating MRI findings into clinically relevant multidisciplinary decision making remains limited. This study presents a clinically oriented framework for interpretation of VP MRI and introduces a structured reporting approach to support consistent documentation and interdisciplinary communication.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A literature-informed, consensus-based framework for interpreting VP MRI was developed. Scoping review first identified MRI-derived anatomic variables relevant to VP function. These variables were organized into interpretive domains through multidisciplinary discussion among SLPs, surgeons, and radiologists. The framework was operationalized into structured reporting templates for speech-language pathology and radiology documentation and prospectively piloted in clinical VP MRI cases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The resulting framework organizes interpretation across five domains: VP proportional relationships, LVP morphology and function, VP closure dynamics, additional structural contributors, and articulatory context. title: Pentosan polysulfate sodium limits pulmonary inflammation in a SARS-CoV-2 mouse model
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
93ffcacb668992c3684105823afacb0518071004.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection remains prevalent globally, causing severe pulmonary inflammation and mortality in up to 10% of patients. While the introduction of effective vaccines has substantially reduced the number of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) cases, there are currently few available therapeutics that have been developed. Pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) has been shown to possess potent anti-inflammatory activity in influenza infection and allergen-induced rhinitis models and was recently demonstrated to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 infection
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">in vitro</jats:italic>
                      . As such, we hypothesized that PPS may represent an attractive therapeutic that could be utilized for SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19. Using the K18-hACE2 mouse model of SARS-CoV-2 infection, we administered PPS (6 mg/kg) from either 1 (early) or 3 (late) days post-infection via intranasal instillation and then examined the efficacy in mitigating viral-induced inflammation and severe disease outcomes. We found that the early administration of PPS was accompanied by significant improvements in weight loss, clinical disease presentation, and neutrophilic airway inflammation. Early PPS administration also significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production at both the mRNA and protein levels while having no impact on viral titers or interferon and antiviral gene expression. Histologically, early treatment significantly prevented severe pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling. Comparatively, late administration of PPS worsened weight loss and clinical disease presentation following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Moreover, late administration was unable to prevent significant increases in pro-inflammatory cytokines and was further associated with significantly downregulated antiviral-associated genes. Histological examination also showed no protection in the late PPS administered groups. Taken together, these findings underscore the significance of time-dependent administration and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of PPS for treatment of SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammation.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to cause infections globally, with most cases resulting in mild to moderate disease outcomes. However, approximately 10% of patients experience virally induced hyperinflammation leading to poor outcomes. As such, new or repurposed therapeutics need to be rapidly implemented to address this urgent medical need. Here, we show that pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) is a leading Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved therapeutic that significantly mitigates SARS-CoV-2-induced pulmonary inflammation. Critically, timing of PPS during the infection establishment and progression is critical for PPS efficacy, highlighting time-dependent responses that must be considered for further human clinical implementation. The findings from this study demonstrate that PPS holds significant promise as a repurposed anti-inflammatory agent for SARS-CoV-2 infection.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Population pharmacokinetics of piperacillin based on multicenter data to support model-informed precision dosing in critically ill women
container-title: Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy
a03c20349df948ad9f7b4247caaf02cb9613015f.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Sex-specific differences in pharmacokinetics are increasingly recognized as clinically relevant, yet most population pharmacokinetic models for antibiotics have been developed in predominantly male populations with limited transferability to female patients. This study aimed to develop and externally evaluate a population pharmacokinetic model of piperacillin specifically for critically ill women to support model-informed precision dosing (MIPD). A total of 923 samples from 165 critically ill women (from four previously published studies) receiving piperacillin/tazobactam were analyzed. The data set was randomly split into a training set (80%) and an independent external evaluation set (20%). Non-linear mixed-effects modeling was employed based on the training data using NONMEM, and covariates were identified using stepwise covariate modeling with cross-validation. Prediction accuracy and bias were quantified using the median prediction error (MDPE) and the median absolute prediction error (MDAPE) in an MIPD scenario. Model predictions for future concentrations were generated both
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">a priori</jats:italic>
                      and through Bayesian forecasting based on one prior sample. A two-compartment model provided the best fit for the data. Clearance was significantly affected by renal function estimated by the Cockcroft–Gault equation, along with procalcitonin and serum albumin. The external evaluation demonstrated strong predictive performance with very low systematic bias. In the MIPD scenario,
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">a priori</jats:italic>
                      predictions exhibited good predictive performance (MDPE < |5.2|%, MDAPE < 33.4%), which substantially improved with Bayesian forecasting (MDPE < |3.2|%, MDAPE < 19.1%). A female-specific population pharmacokinetic model of piperacillin was developed and externally validated, demonstrating robust predictive performance and clear benefits for Bayesian forecasting.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Spinal Diagnostics: Advances, Challenges and Future Directions
container-title: Journal of Orthopaedic Science and Research
228358c8fac2951f4dbb192b9ac4092ec5c41d96.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in spinal diagnostics, particularly through machine learning and deep learning applied to medical imaging and clinical data. These technologies may improve the detection and classification of spinal disorders, automate image interpretation and support clinical decision-making. This narrative review summarizes current applications of AI in spinal diagnostics, focusing on methods for detecting spinal cord injuries, spinal tumors, degenerative spine diseases and vertebral fractures, as well as predicting treatment outcomes and postoperative complications. It also examines convolutional and recurrent neural networks, automated image segmentation and other machine learning approaches for analyzing spinal images and clinical information. Available evidence suggests that AI models can perform comparably to conventional methods and expert assessments and may exceed them in some settings. However, implementation remains limited by challenges related to dataset quality and diversity, model generalizability and interpretability, data privacy and regulatory and ethical considerations. This review highlights both the clinical potential of AI and the major barriers to its integration into routine spinal diagnostic practice. Further prospective validation, external testing across diverse patient populations and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to establish the clinical utility and ensure the safe implementation of AI-based spinal diagnostic tools.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Youth Development: Assessing Negative Impacts in Cameroon
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
d065024e3a7a3a4c848e7dd0b39abb55c8f7917f.abstract: <jats:p>This research evaluates the negative impacts of Artificial Intelligence dependency on the cognitive and academic development of students within the Cameroonian higher education landscape. Utilizing a multiple case study design to facilitate literal replication across diverse settings, this study analyzed data collected from students at the University of Yaoundé, the University of Bamenda, and Yaoundé International Business School. A total of 525 students were surveyed using a purposive sampling strategy to account for the unique dynamics of public university massification and private sector specialization in Cameroon. The findings indicate a high prevalence of AI utilization, with 85.3% of respondents reporting daily or weekly usage for academic tasks.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Corporate Default Risk: Empirical Evidence Based on Large Language Models
container-title: Innovation in Science and Technology
8c5bb44368e92495913bc4e94627d80aa83c1fce.abstract:
<jats:p>Against the backdrop of rapid advances in digital technologies and growing uncertainty in the business environment, artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new opportunities to strengthen risk identification, improve managerial decision-making, and mitigate default risk. Using firm-level data from Chinese A-share listed companies over the period 2009–2024, this study empirically examines the relationship between AI adoption and corporate default risk.
The results indicate that AI adoption is associated with a significant reduction in corporate default risk. This finding remains robust to alternative fixed-effects specifications, different levels of standard-error clustering, and the exclusion of observations from periods affected by major external shocks. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that the negative association is particularly pronounced among firms in non-high-tech industries and those located in eastern and central China.
By examining AI adoption from a corporate risk management perspective, this study extends the literature on the economic consequences of AI adoption and provides firm-level empirical evidence on the role of digital technologies in mitigating financial risk. The findings also offer policy implications for integrating AI into corporate management practices and strengthening firms’ risk governance capabilities.</jats:p>

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Disease and Pest Management in Cauliflower: A Review
container-title: International Journal of Plant & Soil Science
753db756e336f6b9aa7e540e3ea996e945a89902.abstract: <jats:p>Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is a nutritionally important cole vegetable and a high-value component of intensive vegetable production. Its yield and market quality are frequently reduced by bacterial, fungal and oomycete diseases and by insect pests that cause direct feeding injury or facilitate secondary infections. Conventional disease and pest surveillance is largely dependent on visual scouting, expert diagnosis and periodic field observations. These approaches remain indispensable, but they can be labour-intensive, subjective and difficult to scale over large production areas. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, image segmentation, object detection, remote sensing and predictive analytics, offers a complementary approach for rapid and repeatable crop-health assessment. This review examines the potential role of AI in cauliflower disease and pest management, covering image acquisition, disease classification, lesion localisation, severity estimation, insect identification, automated counting, forecasting, smartphone applications, UAV-based surveillance and AI-enabled integrated pest management. Cauliflower-specific research has demonstrated promising performance of deep-learning models. The Cauli-Det modified YOLOv8 system reported precision of 93.2%, recall of 82.6% and mean average precision of 91.1% for bacterial soft rot, downy mildew and black rot in its experimental dataset (Uddin et al., 2024). Another recent cauliflower study reported 99.85% classification accuracy using EfficientNet-B3 under its experimental conditions (Malik et al., 2025). Broader plant-disease research also demonstrates strong potential for CNNs and transfer learning (Mohanty et al., 2016; Ferentinos, 2018), while pest-detection research supports automated insect recognition and monitoring (Thenmozhi & Reddy, 2019; Chakrabarty et al., 2026). However, field variability, limited crop-specific datasets, class imbalance, symptom similarity, model explainability, computational requirements and inadequate independent validation remain major constraints. Future research should integrate AI predictions with weather, crop stage, pest abundance, disease severity and economic thresholds so that the technology supports practical, affordable and environmentally responsible IPM in cauliflower.</jats:p>

title: Smart Democracy: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Combat Election  Misinformation in Nigeria
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
f1d22cab6b57313eee0fba509858e3670f0893e5.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing use of digital communication technologies has transformed democratic participation in Nigeria, but it has also accelerated the spread of election misinformation through social media and other online platforms. False political information, manipulated digital content, and coordinated disinformation campaigns have continued to undermine electoral credibility, public trust, and informed voter decision-making. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for detecting misinformation, verifying online content, identifying coordinated inauthentic behavior, and supporting evidence-based electoral communication. Despite these opportunities, there is limited empirical evidence on how AI can be effectively integrated into Nigeria's electoral communication system to strengthen democratic governance. This study examines the role of AI in combating election misinformation and promoting smart democracy in Nigeria. Specifically, it investigates the prevalence and patterns of election misinformation, assesses stakeholders' awareness and adoption of AI technologies for misinformation detection, examines the opportunities and challenges associated with AI deployment, and proposes communication strategies for responsible AI use during elections. The study adopts a mixed-methods research design, combining quantitative surveys with qualitative interviews involving electoral officials, journalists, fact-checkers, communication experts, and registered voters. Quantitative data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data will be analyzed through thematic analysis. The findings are expected to provide practical recommendations for policymakers, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), media organizations, technology developers, and civil society organizations on leveraging AI to enhance electoral transparency, improve information integrity, strengthen public trust, and promote democratic participation in Nigeria. The study contributes to the growing literature on artificial intelligence, development communication, digital governance, and democratic innovation in Africa.</jats:p>

title: Advances on triply periodic hyperbolic surface structures: from biological inspiration to artificial self-assembly
container-title: Micro Nano Science
3fa1bd2819a8df84fcf5db7511c954d322fdb9ee.abstract: <jats:p>Triply periodic hyperbolic surfaces (TPHSs) are a class of complex structures that extend periodically throughout three-dimensional space and possess smooth surfaces with non-positive Gaussian curvature. They appear in a wide range of natural systems, from cellular membranes to butterfly wing scales and beetle exoskeletons. Owing to their unique geometries and extraordinary properties, TPHSs have attracted extensive attention and research interest. Detailed structural characterizations of naturally occurring TPHSs have been performed, and a variety of artificial analogs have been fabricated by top-down physical methods and bottom-up chemical approaches. These efforts have deepened our understanding of TPHSs and broadened their application scope. This review discusses the progress on TPHSs in biological systems and their artificial synthesis, and it surveys current applications of these structures in fields such as photonics, energy storage and conversion, catalysis, sensing, thermal management and mechanical metamaterials. It thereby provides a new framework linking biological structures to artificial structures. Finally, this review concludes by outlining current challenges and proposing directions for future research.</jats:p>

We highlight the roadmap for EMLs and CW lasers across different generations of optical switching technologies and discuss key manufacturing challenges, including (1) technical complexity, (2) substrate constraints, and (3) process equipment requirements.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Timely detection of chemical and radiological incidents is crucial for public health surveillance; however, no global event-based surveillance system currently exists. Open-source intelligence (OSINT) and large language models (LLMs) present new opportunities for early detection; however, their application in these domains remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated GPT-4o’s performance for named entity recognition (NER) of chemical and radiological incidents from OSINT sources, assessing its potential to support global threat detection and early warning systems. Radiological entities were retained in the extraction schema throughout, but proved too sparse in the retrieved corpus to permit any evaluation of radiological performance; the evaluation reported here is therefore effectively confined to the chemical domain. A lexicon of 45 lay-accessible search terms, derived from 6646 technical chemical and radiological terms, was used to query the Bing News Application Programming Interface (API) from August 2024 to January 2025. Retrieved articles were scraped, translated when necessary, summarised by GPT-4o, and the summaries were and processed by GPT-4o using structured zero-shot prompts to extract entities, including event occurrences, substances, case numbers, fatalities, locations, and temporal features. Two annotators manually labelled a ground-truth dataset of 200 articles to evaluate performance using precision, recall, and F

                    Scores. Performance was compared against four baselines evaluated on the same corpus: a rule-based lexicon extractor, an off-the-shelf pretrained NER pipeline, a domain-pretrained biomedical NER model, and a supervised TF-IDF classifier. Of 37,618 retrieved articles, 8077 were parsed by GPT-4o. Event identification (F

title: Mapping multidimensional artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates: An exploratory survey
container-title: Journal of Information Science
bd50d5aaa7dce3fb50374d1d4938e706264f0cda.abstract: <jats:p>This exploratory study examines artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates, a multilingual context undergoing rapid digital transformation. A cross-sectional online survey of 72 academic library professionals, recruited through purposive and snowball sampling, employed a newly developed 35-item instrument covering seven conceptually derived dimensions: job role evolution, ethical and bureaucratic concerns, patron resistance and social trust, governance and strategic alignment, infrastructure and digital divide, vendor and sustainability, and linguistic and cultural anxiety. Internal consistency ranged from acceptable to strong (α = 0.774–0.898). Overall, AI anxiety was moderate (M = 3.33 on a five-point scale), with ethical and bureaucratic concerns (M = 3.47), infrastructure and digital divide (M = 3.42), and vendor and sustainability concerns (M = 3.36) recording the highest means. However, the narrow range across construct means (0.23 points) warrants treating these differences as descriptive rather than substantive rankings. Concerns about storing patron data on foreign servers and shortages of skilled staff received the highest item-level ratings. Although women reported higher scores across all seven dimensions, no gender or other demographic differences remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The findings highlight the institutional, infrastructural, ethical and governance conditions associated with AI anxiety in academic libraries. The proposed dimensions offer a context-specific framework for further investigation, subject to validation in larger samples. Practical implications include developing localized and multilingual AI tools, expanding inclusive professional development, and strengthening participatory governance of AI procurement and policy.</jats:p>

title: Bioactive Coatings and Engineered Settlement Interfaces for Artificial Coral Reefs: A Systematic Review of Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
container-title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
ce0f9894fa78296651511ec0004a2adfb58eae70.abstract: <jats:p>The use of concrete in artificial reefs presents a “recruitment paradox”: its inherent hyperalkalinity and delayed natural neutralization severely impair coral larval settlement. Functional surface coatings can mitigate this cytotoxicity and actively provide biological settlement cues. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review evaluates 16 years of experimental evidence on cementitious surface modifications across Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect up to September 2026. From 6436 screened records, 127 studies were assessed for full-text eligibility, with a strictly filtered subset of 12 experimental studies included for quantitative data extraction. To systematically categorize these technologies, we propose a novel dual classification framework mapping engineered interfaces by restoration approach (Classes I–IV) and Interfacial Activity Mode (A0–A4). The review evaluates relationships between coating architecture, bio-interfacial stability, and biological performance, identifying current technological bottlenecks. Addressing the need for scalable solutions, we propose a research roadmap integrating circular bioeconomy models and green biomaterials. Methodological quality was assessed by requiring biological validation of coatings in realistic larval settlement models, excluding purely theoretical material simulations. This systematic review was not prospectively registered. Ultimately, this materials-oriented framework clarifies bio-interfacial interactions and identifies research priorities for developing durable, biologically compatible substrates for coral reef restoration.</jats:p>

title: Causal Geospatial Intelligence Framework for Identifying Environmental Drivers of Landslide Risk in Mountainous Regions
container-title: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Information Technology
49984f88f1fcb8aa17bf5b4a4f3b17e39097a693.abstract: <jats:p>Landslide susceptibility models can effectively predict areas prone to landslides but generally provide limited evidence on whether specific environmental exposures causally influence landslide occurrence. This research proposes an integrated causal-geospatial framework combining predictive modeling with causal effect estimation and spatial heterogeneity analysis for landslide occurrence in Desa Wih Pase, Bener Meriah, Indonesia. An analytical dataset comprising 18,450 30 m × 30 m grid cells from observations in 2025 was analyzed using Random Forest and Logistic Regression for occurrence probability modeling, followed by Causal Forest to derive average treatment effect estimates together with grid-level Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATE). The Random Forest model reached a discrimination performance of 0.91 in AUC-ROC, exceeding the 0.79 achieved by the Logistic Regression baseline, demonstrating stronger predictive discrimination under the imbalanced landslide dataset. Causal analysis estimated a positive effect of cumulative rainfall, with a 100 mm increase associated with a 0.142 increase in landslide occurrence probability (95% CI: 0.089–0.195). A 10° increase in slope produced an estimated effect of 0.218 (95% CI: 0.161–0.275). Spatial CATE analysis revealed substantial heterogeneity, with rainfall effects ranging from ?0.039 to 0.302 and slope effects from ?0.024 to 0.490 across valid 30 m grid cells. Sensitivity analyses showed that the positive causal effects remained stable across alternative confounder sets, rainfall accumulation windows, and spatial resolutions. The framework distinguishes predictive susceptibility from causal environmental effects and provides a basis for spatially targeted landslide risk reduction and environmental engineering interventions</jats:p>

title: Mini review of multimodal intelligence for air quality modeling
container-title: Frontiers in Environmental Science
b6f314637b1e78f2441eb235b73cecca9f3a08fe.abstract: <jats:p>Single data sources can miss important information needed for air quality modeling. Ground stations provide accurate local measurements. Satellites, IoT sensors, traffic records, meteorology, and land-use data describe different parts of the same environmental process. These sources improve coverage and representation if they are combined. However, this combination does not guarantee better forecasting performance. Extra inputs may add noise, duplicate information, or become poorly aligned in time. This mini review examines 35 empirical studies published from 2024 to 2026. The review compares multimodal fusion, where information is combined through early, intermediate, and late fusion. It also compares how adaptive mechanisms change the contribution of individual modalities. The review then examines how reliable these models remain when sensors fail, satellite data is missing, or the model is used in a new place. Across the reviewed studies, the usefulness of a modality depends on the task, the quality of the input, and the conditions under which it is used. Future work should evaluate multimodal systems under missing inputs, changing environmental conditions, and physical constraints instead of relying only on complete benchmark datasets.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Women Entrepreneurship in the IT Sector: Emerging Opportunities and Entrepreneurial Challenges
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
57468ea9c09dfbf28e329fedbc923e46969e52db.abstract: <jats:p>The Information Technology (IT) industry is undergoing significant changes as Artificial Intelligence (AI) launches new areas for innovation, business expansion and entrepreneurship. Women entrepreneurs are increasingly embracing AI technologies to set up startups, to enhance their business operations. To increase productivity and take part more in domestic and international markets. In the present study, the role of Artificial Intelligence in the future of women entrepreneurship in the IT sector was discussed, with a special focus on emerging opportunities and challenges for the entrepreneurs. It brings to the forefront the potential of leveraging AI-powered tools, automation, machine learning, data analytics, and digital platforms for business planning, decision-making, customer relationship management, and resource optimization, particularly for women entrepreneurs. The research also pinpoints the major challenges such as limited access to finance, gender inequality, technical knowledge, digital skills gap, cyber security threats, and lack of institutional support. Particular emphasis is placed on the Indian context and how government’s initiatives, digital transformation and entrepreneurship development programmes are providing new opportunities for women entrepreneurs. The research method used in the study is descriptive and analytical descriptive method using secondary data or secondary sources of information. It seeks to grasp the potential of AI in fostering inclusive entrepreneurship, enhancing the role of women in the IT sector, and supporting sustainable economic growth.</jats:p>

title: An Assessment of the Familiarity of Undergraduates with the  Application of Artificial Intelligence Programs in Project Writing  and Development in Polytechnics in Nigeria
container-title: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
ce073cbba2236ec8c523b5b4bd7dcee50b6b1033.abstract:
<jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) programs have progressively permeated the academic ecosystem, 
altering the manner in which students conceive, research, write, and defend project reports. This 
study assessed the familiarity of undergraduates with the application of artificial intelligence 
programs in project writing and development in polytechnics in Nigeria. The study was anchored 
on the Technology Acceptance Model (Davis, 1989) and the Diffusion of Innovation Theory 
(Rogers, 2003), both of which provided a theoretical lens for interpreting how perceived 
usefulness, perceived ease of use, and innovation attributes shape students' adoption of AI-driven 
tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, the Turnitin AI detector, and Google Gemini. A 
descriptive survey design was adopted, and a multi-stage random sampling technique was used to 
select six federal and state polytechnics spanning the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria, namely 
Federal Polytechnic Nasarawa, Yaba College of Technology, Kaduna Polytechnic, Akanu Ibiam 
Federal Polytechnic Unwana, Rivers State Polytechnic, and Federal Polytechnic Bauchi. A 
structured questionnaire was administered to 300 final-year and penultimate-year Higher 
National Diploma (HND) and National Diploma (ND) students, out of which 268 copies (89.3%) 
were validly completed and returned. Data were analysed using frequency counts, simple 
percentages, mean scores, and chi-square statistics at the 0.05 level of significance. Findings 
revealed that undergraduates in Nigerian polytechnics possess a moderately high level of 
familiarity with generic AI programs such as ChatGPT (86%) and Grammarly (71%), but 
comparatively low familiarity with more specialised tools such as Jasper/Copy.ai (11%) and 
Perplexity AI (22%). AI programs were most frequently applied at the proofreading, grammar
checking, and literature-search stages of project writing, while application at the data-analysis 
stage remained the least explored. Unstable electricity and internet connectivity, inadequate 
digital literacy training, the cost of premium subscriptions, and the fear of being accused of 
academic malpractice emerged as the most prominent challenges limiting deeper engagement with 
these tools. The chi-square analysis indicated a statistically significant relationship between 
students' level of familiarity and their institutional location (urban versus semi-urban campuses). 
The study concluded that although AI literacy is gradually taking root among polytechnic 
undergraduates, its application remains uneven, superficial in places, and insufficiently guided by 
institutional policy. It was recommended, among other things, that polytechnic management 
should integrate AI literacy modules into general studies curricula, provide subsidised access to premium AI tools, and develop clear ethical guidelines that distinguish permissible assistive use 
of AI from outright academic misconduct.</jats:p>

title: THE EVOLUTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN CARDIOLOGY: FROM PRECISE ARRHYTHMIA DETECTION TO PREDICTION OF CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS AND MORTALITY RISK - A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW (2018–2026)
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science
640fe4248e0944062bdc4cd395d8fb263e3e992d.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death globally, with cardiac arrhythmia being one of the main causes of adverse clinical events. In recent years, psychophysiological medicine has undergone a major transition; however, the first step in this process is the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for predicting cardiovascular risk and establishing a framework for prognostic modeling.
Aim: This systematic review aimed to evaluate how AI has been applied in Electrocardiography (ECG) in the period from 2018 to 2026. More specifically, we sought to determine the accuracy of AI in diagnosing arrhythmias and the emerging use of AI for the prediction of major cardiovascular events and death.
Methods: A systematic search of the MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase and Cochrane Library databases for original studies published from 2018 to 2026 was conducted. The focus was on deep learning-based algorithms that utilized 12-lead ECGs or signals derived from wearables. The risk of bias and quality of the studies was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool.
Results: There were 30 initial studies included in the overall analysis. Most models were convolutional neural network (CNN) based and demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy as demonstrated by sensitivity and specificity commonly reported >90–95%. AI's ability to detect paroxysmal atrial fibrillation while in a normal sinus rhythm and for superior triage of occlusive myocardial infarction (STEMI equivalent) versus standard clinical criteria are important findings. Additionally, the establishment of "AI-ECG age" as a digital biomarker may enable long-term prediction of cardiovascular mortality and heart failure risk. Though there are substantial differences in methodological quality and limited standardized external validation among diverse populations are prominent obstacles.
Conclusion: This makes AI a revolutionary tool within cardiology where it can deliver results of accuracy equal to or greater than specialists on selective tasks. The transition from diagnostic to prognostic systems creates tremendous promise for the development of personalized medicine. Yet, in order to achieve appropriate integration into clinical practice, more standardized reporting, as well as rigorous validation to ensure patient safety and diminish the "black box" characteristics of deep learning models, must be undertaken within real-world, multi-national cohort studies.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Canada's Productivity Challenge: Bridging the Gap Between  Promise and Economic Reality
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
c4addb4e1955a9162443e022cebd9559c404098a.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) offers considerable potential to improve productivity, yet its growing adoption has not necessarily translated into corresponding gains in aggregate labour productivity. This paper examines Canada's AI productivity challenge using evidence from Statistics Canada, Bank of Canada research, academic literature, and documented expert commentary. It considers the historical productivity paradox alongside business adoption patterns, projected productivity gains, sectoral differences, and emerging labour-market adjustments. Canadian evidence highlights a gap between the widespread personal use of AI by business leaders and its integration into core business operations. Conceptual illustrations demonstrate how implementation costs, organizational restructuring, complementary investment, and workforce skill development may influence the realization of AI's economic benefits. The analysis distinguishes planned adoption from actual implementation, projected gains from observed outcomes, and associations from causal effects. It argues that realizing AI's productivity potential requires effective organizational integration, workforce learning, and broader diffusion across businesses. The paper concludes with policy implications for Canada and emphasizes the importance of monitoring productivity and labour-market outcomes as AI adoption evolves.</jats:p>

title: Calving area selection and prepartum behavior of dairy cows managed outdoors with access to artificial and natural shelters during winter
container-title: Frontiers in Animal Science
a29754b3a401aab3313c2741487727f6664082a9.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Before calving, dairy cows may seek a secluded area to express maternal behavior. Pasture-based systems may facilitate this behavior by allowing cows to move away from the group, but little is known about calving location selection and prepartum exploratory behavior in outdoor paddocks during winter. We therefore evaluated calving area selection and prepartum exploratory behavior in dairy cows with access to sheltered and open areas.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Forty-eight prepartum dairy cows (17 nulliparous, 31 multiparous) were enrolled in an 8,450 m
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      paddock with access to three potential calving areas: natural shelter (NS; area with bushes and trees with straw bedding, 440 m
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      ), artificial shelter (AS; three structures with three walls and straw bed, 18 m2 each), and open paddock (OP; 7,956 m
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      ). Continuous video monitoring recorded calving locations (n = 36), while prepartum exploratory behavior was assessed using 10-min instantaneous scan sampling from video recordings during the 24 h before calving (n = 23).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of the total sample (n = 36), 38.9% of cows calved in NS, 16.7% in AS, and 44.4% in OP. Multinomial logistic regression showed that higher lactation number was associated with lower odds of calving in NS versus OP (OR = 0.587; 95% CI = 0.365 – 0.943; p = 0.028). Cumulative rainfall increased the odds of calving in the AS (OR = 1.195; 95% CI = 0.980 – 1.456; p = 0.078); and a higher calf-to-dam weight ratio tended to be related to greater odds of calving in NS (OR = 3.047; 95% CI = 0.000 – 9.288; p = 0.050). Descriptive analysis of exploratory behavior showed that cows calving in AS and NS spent approximately one-third of the 24 h prepartum period in their respective calving areas (6.33 ± 4.02 h/d and 7.82 ± 3.68 h/d, respectively), with visits appearing to concentrate during the hours closest to parturition.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results indicate that dairy cows allocated outdoor during winter select sheltered and open areas to calve, and that the selection of sheltered areas was associated with individual and winter weather conditions. As parturition approached, the use of sheltered areas increased, as was observed descriptively.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Development of an Improved Model of the Point Location Problem in Indoor Spaces with Fingerprint and Artificial Neural Network Approaches
container-title: GAZI UNIVERSITY JOURNAL OF SCIENCE
777d745f6a394991123580865593adff5a2f2a08.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study proposes an approach to indoor positioning that combines the RSSI-based fingerprinting method with a dual artificial neural network (ANN) architecture. Unlike conventional approaches that use only RSSI vectors, this approach also incorporates the location information (x, y) of the measurement points into the learning process. The proposed structure consists of two ANNs. Model 1 can predict y′ from x and RSSI inputs. Model 2 can predict x′ from y and RSSI inputs. The outputs of both models are combined. The closest matching point pair represents the estimated position. The proposed approach increases sensitivity to changes in position and improves robustness against multipath effects and environmental noise. Measurements obtained from a simulation environment were prepared and divided into training, validation, and test sets. Multi-layer feedforward artificial neural networks were then trained. The results of the regression and residual analyses showed that both models produced similar results and that the final prediction made using the intersection was reliable. The results show that the suggested bidirectional ANN–fingerprint framework is a scalable, flexible, and data-driven solution that does not require additional hardware. It provides reliable and generalizable position estimation in the simulated indoor scenario considered.</jats:p>

title: Integrating artificial intelligence [AI] into music education: student teachers' engagement, attitudes and perceptions at methodist college of education, Akyem Asene-Aboabo, Oda, Ghana
container-title: SCIENCE MUNDI
7cf7ac5d922729319f8dcaf2bf9f33411de052d1.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly reshaping academic work in teacher training institutions, yet empirical evidence regarding their application within domain-specific practical fields like music education remains sparse in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined student teachers' utilisation patterns and perceptions of AI tools in music course assignments at Methodist College of Education, Akyem Asene-Aboabo, Oda, in the Eastern Region of Ghana. Anchored in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Diffusion of Innovations theory, the study adopted a quantitative descriptive survey design. A sample of 25 student teachers across levels 200 to 400 was selected via simple random sampling from a total population of 49 music education students; 24 fully completed questionnaires were retrieved (96% response rate). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (means and standard deviations). The findings revealed high baseline AI awareness (Grand Mean = 4.24, SD = 0.63) and strong positive perceptions regarding AI's capacity to enhance academic productivity, task comprehension, and lesson planning (Composite Mean = 4.22, SD = 0.61). ChatGPT, Grammarly and Gemini emerged as the primary tools used for information retrieval, text refinement and idea generation. However, reliance on AI raised concerns regarding reduced creative independence, diminished musical originality and infrastructural challenges such as unreliable internet access. The study concludes that while AI serves as an effective academic scaffold, its unchecked use threatens authentic musical creation and pedagogical reasoning. It recommends the implementation of institutional AI literacy frameworks and clear guidelines for ethical integration in creative disciplines.</jats:p>

title: Librarians in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
b4aafa45c108c0608892953dd42508752115d4ab.abstract: <jats:p>In the age of artificial intelligence, libraries and librarians are undergoing profound transformations in their missions, competencies, and professional roles. This conceptual paper examines how key 21st-century socio-technological trends – particularly the rise of artificial intelligence and changing labour market demands – are reshaping the ways in which libraries support education, research, and community engagement. Drawing on international policy documents and scholarly literature, complemented by illustrative examples of library practice, the paper analyses three interrelated dimensions: librarians’ professional attitudes towards technological change, the development of digital and AI-related competencies, and their emerging role as educational mediators. The analysis highlights the importance of librarians’ competencies, professional attitudes, and continuous professional development alongside technological infrastructure in shaping the integration of artificial intelligence into library services. The paper argues that libraries are emerging as human-centred, adaptive learning environments in which technological innovation is aligned with ethical, social, and educational values. By positioning librarians as key actors in mediating technological change, the study contributes to the ongoing redefinition of librarianship in an AI-driven world.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Generative Science of Food Formulation
container-title: Annual Review of Food Science and Technology
e4b4f2b38672ed32bee7f6a7389c7b1778ff372d.abstract: <jats:p>Food formulation requires balancing taste, nutrition, sustainability, and cost. Traditionally, new foods have emerged through empirical experimentation, expert intuition, and iterative refinement. Now, artificial intelligence (AI) offers the opportunity to accelerate this process. Yet despite rapid advances across food science, most AI applications remain isolated prediction and optimization tasks rather than parts of a broader scientific approach. Here we integrate these emerging technologies into a unified framework—the generative science of food formulation—in which digital food representations enable AI to predict, discover, generate, organize, simulate, and optimize. We illustrate this approach through sustainability and nutrition, where generative AI transforms environmental and nutritional metrics from post hoc evaluation criteria into explicit design objectives. Finally, we identify the data, models, benchmarks, and automation that will establish computational food design as a rigorous scientific discipline. Together, these advances have the potential to transform food formulation from an empirical discipline into a generative science.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Educational Games for Personalized Learning
container-title: Nexus Science Review
e6baf797786645b266252216627b9861c6a650e9.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence can enable educational games to select activities, regulate progression, and deliver feedback in response to students’ difficulties. Successful assisted gameplay, however, does not establish independent mastery. This critical narrative and thematic review examines how adaptation should be interpreted and evaluated when independently demonstrated learning is the primary endpoint. Targeted web discovery documented in the original manuscript was supplemented through October 31, 2026. The selective corpus comprises 28 sources, including 11 game-specific empirical publications and three adjacent empirical studies; 22 sources (78.6%) date from 2021–2026. A contemporary systematic review provides broader field coverage, whereas the present contribution concerns independent mastery, over-assistance, uncertain learner-state inference, teacher supervision, and prospective evaluation. Selected primary studies show favorable, mixed, and null findings under different instructional conditions. Increased correctness need not indicate misconception repair, and strong fixed support can limit the incremental benefit of adaptation. Activities, pace, and feedback are therefore treated as distinct instructional decisions. An author-developed, unvalidated adaptation cycle and proposed metrics specify assistance exposure, severity of feedback errors, independent assessment, retention, transfer, implementation fidelity, and educational opportunity. No new empirical experiment or pooled effect estimate is reported. The proposed adoption criterion is retained and transferable learning after unnecessary assistance is withdrawn, alongside acceptable workload, accessibility, privacy, and student agency.</jats:p>

title: Selective attention or inattention? Enabling efficient perception in embodied intelligence agents
container-title: Frontiers of Computer Science
977d66ee308835bba303da319eacf6e914bcb2b1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As embodied intelligence increasingly operates in the physical world, perception efficiency, robustness, and adaptability become central bottlenecks separating artificial agents from biological organisms. Unlike conventional perception pipelines, biological perception is inherently selective and resource-aware: attention amplifies task-relevant information, while inattention suppresses distraction and redundancy. This survey investigates attention-driven adaptive perception as a promising mechanism for improving embodied systems. We consolidate interdisciplinary findings from neuroscience, cognitive science, robotics, and machine learning to clarify the distinct yet complementary roles of selective attention and inattention in optimizing perceptual processing. Building on these insights, we introduce the Unified Selective Attention and Inattention Model (U-SAIM) and extend it into a three-tier architectural framework that maps biological principles to embodied perception systems. Guided by this structure, we review existing implementations across robotics, multimodal fusion, lightweight perception, and attention modulation strategies, extracting design patterns and performance implications. Moreover, we discuss the challenges and opportunities for future development. Together, these perspectives chart a unified theoretical and practical roadmap toward attentional embodied perception—agents capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting with the adaptive intelligence, efficiency, and flexibility that define human perception.</jats:p>

title: Beyond the Predicted Profile: Clinical  Validity of Artificial Intelligence Based  Facial Outcomes in Orthodontics
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
58d222465a35addb8ccd11d91af11889021d6e84.abstract: <jats:p>Introduction and Background: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being explored to predict facial soft tissue outcomes following orthodontic treatment. AI systems may aid in treatment expectations and profile prediction in patients. However, it is important to determine that the predicted outcome is not simply visually accurate.  Review: This narrative review discusses the differences between geometric accuracy, visual accuracy and clinical utility when using AI systems to predict post-orthodontic facial outcomes. Previous research has focused on using artificial neural networks, convolutional neural networks, deep neural networks and conditional generative adversarial networks. More recently, models have used machine learning with incisors and facial measurements, generative networks for lateral profile prediction and prediction from facial frontal photographs. Across all studies there has been varying success depending on the imaging type, region of interest, patient population and the type of measurement used. Difficulties were seen with predicting lower lip and chin areas. Additionally, even when there has been good success with numbers there has not been improved treatment decisions or outcomes.  Conclusions: Using AI to predict facial outcomes is an emerging field which may be beneficial. However, the clinical validity of the outcomes should be investigated. Future research should ensure independent validation occurs, measurement of error within each anatomical region, patient and clinician evaluation, clear communication of uncertainty and evidence of clinical decision making. Until this evidence is present the outcomes should be used as support.</jats:p>

title: Green AI for Sustainable Agriculture: An Explainable-AI (XAI) Perspective on Energy-Efficient Crop Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
88212f3988da8ca8d548c2cfd044d37d838996f1.abstract: <jats:p>In modern agriculture precision forecast crop yields, diagnose plant disease and schedule irrigation systems rely on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Cost of training and deploying these models is weighed their accuracy. Two research threads have far developed largely in parallel. Green AI, which treats computational and energy efficiency as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside accuracy and Explainable AI(XAI) uses technology like Shapley additive explanations(SHAP), LIME and Grad-CAM to open the “black box” models so that farmers , and policymakers can act on their predictions.This paper synthesises recent literature (2017–2026) at the intersection of these threads as they apply to agriculture, covering crop-yield prediction, plant-disease detection, and soil- and irrigation-modelling studies that report either energy-efficiency measures or explainability analyses, or both. The synthesis identifies a specific and consistent gap: while explainability is now common in high-performing agricultural ML studies, almost none of them report the energy or carbon cost of training the underlying models, and the one purpose-built Green-AI agriculture framework identified in the review explicitly leaves explainability as future work rather than integrating it. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes a unified Green-XAI methodological framework for agricultural ML that couples resource-appropriate model families – tree-based ensembles such as Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, alongside a compact CNN architecture for imagery – with SHAP-based interpretability and continuous energy/carbon instrumentation across the training and inference lifecycle. The paper details the proposed dataset scope, the governing model equations, the SHAP computation, and an accuracy-versus-energy evaluation protocol, and positions the framework against a comparative synthesis of the performance figures reported by prior studies</jats:p>
