container-title: Research, Society and Development
5c397e025796174684255ec56844367f8a275f72.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: To analyze the available scientific evidence regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an adjunctive tool for clinical evaluation in the diagnosis and screening of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), thoroughly assessing its diagnostic reliability, technical limitations, and relevant ethical aspects. Methodology: This study is a literature review in which structured searches for articles published between 2011 and 2026 were conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and Google Scholar electronic databases, using controlled descriptors and Boolean operators related to AI and oral pathology. Results: The scientific literature consistently demonstrates that Deep Learning models, trained primarily on conventional intraoral clinical photographs, achieve high sensitivity and accuracy rates in the detection of OPMDs. However, significant challenges remain, such as high methodological heterogeneity among studies, reliance on well-standardized training data, and the need for more diverse population representation. Conclusion: Artificial Intelligence emerges as a highly promising adjunctive technology for screening and clinical decision support. Nevertheless, its application must remain strictly complementary, in no way replacing the clinical judgment of the dental professional or the histopathological gold standard obtained through tissue biopsy.</jats:p>

title: Access, Management and Procedural Intervention-Explorations of Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Judicial Backlog in Indian Judiciary
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
4969c7f707717ae287c5503416fcd5b009a77a12.abstract:
<jats:p>The aim of this study is to discuss the problem of case pendency in the judicial system of India that, as of late 2025, violates the right to speedy trial guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution due to the number of pending cases exceeding 53 million across the country [1]. As per the data provided by the National Judicial Data Grid, some 88 percent of this pendency falls on subordinate courts, namely district and taluka courts [2, 3]. The factors identified by the study causing delay include the permanent lack of judges to the extent of approximately 35 percent on average, procedural failure in the form of frequent adjournments and counsels' absences, and administrative burden, with the Government being the biggest litigant in almost 46 percent of court cases [4, 5].
The comparative analysis of international judicial artificial intelligence systems like COMPAS of the USA, VICTOR of Brazil, and PROMETEA of Argentina reveals that the key advantage of artificial intelligence is the role of an augmentative nonjudgmental tool used in high volume of appeals triage and document creation [6, 7]. In turn, the digital infrastructure of India, based on the National Judicial Data Grid and e-Courts Phase 3, together with already existing software for legal research and translation in the Supreme Court, creates a solid ground for using of artificial intelligence; however, this process will require rigorous legal governance. In particular, such governance should take care of the threat of algorithmic bias and human supervision, which has been emphasized recently in the guidelines of the Kerala High Court [8].</jats:p>

8b7acf81037cef1cff64ca8380cd8edb9755b7b9.abstract: <jats:p>Decision-making has become an increasingly complex activity in management, governance, and day-to-day operations. Today’s volume of information available is higher than the human ability to cope with it. This is where artificial intelligence comes into play. It is a practical solution which totally changed the perception of AI as a research idea transforming it into an effective tool used by such industries as finance, health care, retail, manufacturing and human resources. The article describes the role of AI in the decision-making process from two sides which include the stage-based approach illustrating the activity of AI during the decision-making process and sector-based approach of its implementation. It has been concluded that AI is most productive at the stages of collecting data, assessing the collected data and monitoring it and it is the least effective in the stages of defining the problem and making decisions on the basis of values. Different industries are more or less appropriate for the implementation of AI because of the availability of data, number of repetitions in the decision-making process and cost of mistakes.</jats:p>

title: Beyond the Predicted Profile: Clinical  Validity of Artificial Intelligence Based  Facial Outcomes in Orthodontics
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
58d222465a35addb8ccd11d91af11889021d6e84.abstract: <jats:p>Introduction and Background: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being explored to predict facial soft tissue outcomes following orthodontic treatment. AI systems may aid in treatment expectations and profile prediction in patients. However, it is important to determine that the predicted outcome is not simply visually accurate.  Review: This narrative review discusses the differences between geometric accuracy, visual accuracy and clinical utility when using AI systems to predict post-orthodontic facial outcomes. Previous research has focused on using artificial neural networks, convolutional neural networks, deep neural networks and conditional generative adversarial networks. More recently, models have used machine learning with incisors and facial measurements, generative networks for lateral profile prediction and prediction from facial frontal photographs. Across all studies there has been varying success depending on the imaging type, region of interest, patient population and the type of measurement used. Difficulties were seen with predicting lower lip and chin areas. Additionally, even when there has been good success with numbers there has not been improved treatment decisions or outcomes.  Conclusions: Using AI to predict facial outcomes is an emerging field which may be beneficial. However, the clinical validity of the outcomes should be investigated. Future research should ensure independent validation occurs, measurement of error within each anatomical region, patient and clinician evaluation, clear communication of uncertainty and evidence of clinical decision making. Until this evidence is present the outcomes should be used as support.</jats:p>

title: Green AI for Sustainable Agriculture: An Explainable-AI (XAI) Perspective on Energy-Efficient Crop Intelligence
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
88212f3988da8ca8d548c2cfd044d37d838996f1.abstract: <jats:p>In modern agriculture precision forecast crop yields, diagnose plant disease and schedule irrigation systems rely on machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). Cost of training and deploying these models is weighed their accuracy. Two research threads have far developed largely in parallel. Green AI, which treats computational and energy efficiency as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside accuracy and Explainable AI(XAI) uses technology like Shapley additive explanations(SHAP), LIME and Grad-CAM to open the “black box” models so that farmers , and policymakers can act on their predictions.This paper synthesises recent literature (2017–2026) at the intersection of these threads as they apply to agriculture, covering crop-yield prediction, plant-disease detection, and soil- and irrigation-modelling studies that report either energy-efficiency measures or explainability analyses, or both. The synthesis identifies a specific and consistent gap: while explainability is now common in high-performing agricultural ML studies, almost none of them report the energy or carbon cost of training the underlying models, and the one purpose-built Green-AI agriculture framework identified in the review explicitly leaves explainability as future work rather than integrating it. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes a unified Green-XAI methodological framework for agricultural ML that couples resource-appropriate model families – tree-based ensembles such as Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, alongside a compact CNN architecture for imagery – with SHAP-based interpretability and continuous energy/carbon instrumentation across the training and inference lifecycle. The paper details the proposed dataset scope, the governing model equations, the SHAP computation, and an accuracy-versus-energy evaluation protocol, and positions the framework against a comparative synthesis of the performance figures reported by prior studies</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Firm Resilience: Investment Efficiency and Post-Shock Recovery
container-title: Systems
3e2ca44e69767704296f16606dbe58c2c1321616.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) offers firms new ways to detect changes in their business environment. We examine how AI adoption relates to firm resilience, focusing on investment decisions and post-shock adjustment. Our sample comprises 44,855 firm-year observations of Chinese nonfinancial A-share listed firms, with resilience measured by annual changes in total factor productivity. We estimate models with firm and year fixed effects and conduct robustness checks using alternative measures and sample restrictions. We also estimate instrumental variable models using the interaction between a post-policy indicator and firms’ pre-policy AI adoption as the instrument. We find a positive and significant association between AI adoption and next-year firm resilience. The main robustness checks and instrumental variable estimates yield results in the same direction. To examine the investment allocation channel, we measure AI adoption, investment allocation, and resilience in successive years and use a firm-level bootstrap for inference. The results support a channel through reduced investment inefficiency. Evidence is significant for the overinvestment channel, but not for the underinvestment channel. Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a shock, we examine post-shock adjustment through cross-sectional regressions and dynamic panel analysis. Firms with higher pre-shock AI adoption experience larger subsequent rebounds and are more likely to return to their pre-shock level. The association with initial losses is not statistically significant. By distinguishing between types of investment deviation and examining post-shock recovery, this study provides evidence on how AI adoption relates to firms’ resource allocation and adaptation over time.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications and Self-Directed Learning  in Curriculum and Teaching Methods Artificial Intelligence and Self- Learning
container-title: Journal of Educational and Social Research
0aa193cd356081d5a18980164d664b7ccc7c21cb.abstract:
<jats:p>This study investigated undergraduate students’ use of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in self-directed learning and their self-directed learning skills and behaviors. It also examined differences in these variables according to gender, academic year, and cumulative grade point average (GPA), and explored the relationship between AI usage and self-directed learning skills. A descriptive quantitative design was employed, and data was collected from 70 students enrolled in a Curriculum and Teaching Methods course using a validated 20-item questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, a three-way ANOVA, Scheffé post-hoc tests, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient were used for data analysis. The results indicated high levels of AI application use (M = 4.07, SD = 0.52) and self-directed learning skills (M = 3.98, SD = 0.57). Pearson’s correlation revealed a strong positive association between AI application use and self-directed learning skills (r = 0.797, p < .001). No statistically significant gender differences were found in either variable. A statistically significant effect of academic year was observed for AI usage; however, post-hoc comparisons did not identify significant pairwise differences. For self-directed learning skills, significant differences were found for academic year and GPA, with post-hoc results indicating higher scores among students with an Excellent GPA compared to those with Very Good and Good GPAs. The findings suggest a strong association between AI application use and self-directed learning skills, while variations across demographic variables are limited and primarily related to academic achievement.

title: Reported enterprise deployment readiness of privacy-preserving artificial intelligence: a governance and information management perspective
container-title: Journal of Enterprise Information Management
ab0f6827215d6725602ab8cd73d74baf20c2e553.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) technologies increasingly support data-driven decision-making while safeguarding sensitive information. However, peer-reviewed evidence documenting governance integration and operational deployment remains limited. This study examines how the peer-reviewed academic literature documents the technical maturity, governance integration, and operational implementation of privacy-preserving AI systems relevant to enterprise information systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-compliant systematic literature review examined 22 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018 to May 2026. The review synthesized evidence on privacy–utility trade-offs, governance integration, fairness, operational readiness, and implementation maturity. We used Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and a proposed Translational Readiness Index (TRI) to classify readiness evidence reported in the included studies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Privacy-preserving AI systems demonstrated favorable privacy–utility trade-offs in the reviewed academic literature, with privacy budgets of e = 1–3 preserving approximately 85–96% of baseline predictive performance. Federated learning combined with differential privacy was the dominant implementation architecture. Most included studies demonstrated intermediate technical maturity (TRL 4–6), primarily through controlled evaluations and prototype development while none documented deployment within operational payer workflows. Studies also inconsistently documented governance integration, privacy accounting, interoperability, and fairness assessment. We characterize this imbalance in the published academic evidence as the proposed Enterprise AI Documentation Gap Hypothesis. The hypothesis concerns the distribution of evidence in peer-reviewed literature and should not be interpreted as evidence that healthcare organizations or insurers are unprepared for deployment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study is limited to reviewing scholarly papers published in the academic literature and did not systematically examine industry literature, company records, patent information, or practitioner views. Therefore, the results reflect the scholarly evidence base and do not reflect health organizations' or insurers' readiness for implementation. The absence of evidence in the literature on deployment does not imply that implementation does not occur outside scholarly journals. Future studies should cross-check scholarly evidence with industry and practitioner evidence on the same topic.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The TRI offers an exploratory, multidimensional framework for organizing documented evidence across technology, privacy, governance, fairness, and operations. This study proposes the Enterprise AI Documentation Gap Hypothesis to describe the gap between the relative maturity of technical evidence and the lack of published evidence on governance and operations. These are conceptual contributions that require further empirical testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Quantum Explainable AI-Integrating Interpretability With Quantum Intelligence Using Information-Theoretic Approaches
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Quantum Information Theory, Entropy, and Computational Complexity
bbaeee6313fd99915c6f3dd1437a192a6d1cedf2.abstract: <jats:p>We introduce an Information-Theoretic Quantum Explainable Artificial Intelligence (IT-QXAI) framework to incorporate explainability in quantum machine learning models. The integration of quantum computing and AI can bring significant computational benefits. But it brings new challenges for interpretability, especially in critical applications such as health, cybersecurity, and vehicular fog computing (VFC). It uses entropy, quantum mutual information and quantum relative entropy to measure uncertainty, and to capture the interactions between features of quantum models. An architecture and taxonomy of QXAI are proposed to enable reliable explanations. VFC settings demonstrate IT-QXAI's potential to support smart task offloading, resource management, and decision-making in dynamic environments. The selection of information-theoretic measures ensures explanations are consistent with quantum processes. Challenges such as quantum noise, scalability, and the lack of evaluation metrics are discussed, along with research opportunities for scalable, user-friendly explainability techniques.</jats:p>

title: Applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Marketing: A Research Review and Future Prospects
container-title: Financial Economics Research
148e1986296fc80c4c7c67c8067c839c2db4ad52.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is turning marketing content into an abundant resource with near-zero marginal cost, but related research is highly fragmented. This paper thematically integrates Chinese- and English-language literature published from 2019 to 2026. The findings show that gains from GenAI marketing are “stratified along the funnel”: evidence of improvements at the attention and interaction stages is sufficient, whereas the effect on final conversion is weak; consumers’ evaluations of content are decoupled from evaluations of the “artificial intelligence (AI) source” label, and disclosure of the AI source significantly suppresses transactions; only 13% of the literature examines moderating variables. Accordingly, this paper proposes a five-stage integrated framework of “technical characteristics → marketing applications → psychological mechanisms → consumer responses → moderating boundaries” and a future research agenda.</jats:p>

title: A Study on Aerospace and Defence Industry: Competitive Intelligence on Disruptive Technologies and Market Growth
container-title: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
671ae4b84b9d8b55e9bc222761bda9a579f7c0c6.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper examines competitive intelligence on disruptive technologies and market growth in the aerospace and defence industry, drawing on a two-month industry research internship at Global Market Insights Pvt Ltd from 1 June to 31 July 2026. The research covered aerospace and defence alongside related technology-intensive markets. Activities included market definition, segmentation, company profiling, analysis of growth drivers and constraints, regional comparison, and monitoring of investments, partnerships, acquisitions, and product developments. The study used exploratory and descriptive secondary research, drawing on company websites, annual reports, investor presentations, government publications, international organizations, industry associations, and technical literature. Its findings are qualitative rather than statistical, no respondent sample, survey, hypothesis test, market-share model, or sales-conversion dataset was documented.

The analysis identifies four connected themes: technological ecosystems are interdependent, innovation, intellectual property, partnerships, and specialist capabilities influence competitive positioning; public policy and procurement shape strategic markets and source validation is essential when market definitions and reporting periods differ. The paper’s contribution is an applied synthesis of how structured secondary research can organize fragmented public evidence without overstating its implications. It recommends traceable sources, consistent market definitions, confidence labels, and a maintained competitive-intelligence register. Interpretations remain limited by the available evidence and documented research.</jats:p>

Kerangka etika kecerdasan buatan global umumnya bersifat prosedural dan belum menjawab dasar ontologis mengapa manusia wajib bertanggung jawab atas teknologi yang diciptakannya. Penelitian ini bertujuan merekonstruksi konsep tanggung jawab manusia dalam ekosistem kecerdasan buatan melalui konsep khalifah digital berdasarkan perspektif Al-Islam dan Kemuhammadiyahan transformatif. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kepustakaan. Data dianalisis melalui epistemologi bayani, burhani, dan irfani, yaitu tafsir tematik terhadap ayat-ayat tentang khilafah, amanah, dan taskhir, analisis isi terhadap literatur etika dan regulasi kecerdasan buatan, serta refleksi atas dimensi spiritual tanggung jawab. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa konsep khalifah menempatkan manusia sebagai pemegang amanah yang tidak dapat mengalihkan tanggung jawab moral kepada mesin. Rekonstruksi tanggung jawab khalifah digital mencakup dimensi teologis, sosial, ekologis, dan profesional yang melekat pada seluruh siklus kecerdasan buatan, mulai dari perancangan, penggunaan, hingga pengawasan. Penelitian ini merumuskan model konseptual khalifah digital sebagai kerangka operasional. Perspektif Al-Islam dan Kemuhammadiyahan transformatif menawarkan kerangka etis yang tidak hanya normatif, tetapi juga mendorong tajdid dan amal saleh dalam pemanfaatan teknologi. Temuan ini berimplikasi pada penguatan pembelajaran Al-Islam dan Kemuhammadiyahan di perguruan tinggi Muhammadiyah serta perumusan etika pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan yang berkeadaban.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Learning Tool: Its Influence on Students Academic Performance and Learning Engagement
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
e5e5365fb2e6e33264fdd844d2952c94acd2e247.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined the use of ChatGPT as a learning tool, students’ academic performance, and learning engagement in English reading comprehension. Specifically, it sought to describe the respondents’ profiles, frequency and duration of ChatGPT use, purposes of using the tool, academic performance, and levels of behavioral, emotional, cognitive, and agentic engagement. It also aimed to determine the relationships between ChatGPT use and academic performance, ChatGPT use and learning engagement, and academic performance and learning engagement. A correlational research design was employed to examine the relationships among the study variables. The intended respondents were 200 students from the participating schools. A researcher-made questionnaire was proposed to gather information regarding students’ use of ChatGPT and learning engagement, while academic performance was to be determined using authorized school records for the specified grading period, subject to appropriate permission. Descriptive statistics and an appropriate correlation coefficient were identified as the statistical tools for analyzing the data. The study was also intended to provide a basis for developing a Proposed Instructional Guide for the Responsible Use of ChatGPT in English Reading Comprehension. The proposed guide emphasizes purposeful AI use, vocabulary development, identification of main ideas and supporting details, interpretation of texts, critical evaluation of AI-generated responses, academic integrity, and independent learning. The study recognizes that ChatGPT may provide supplementary explanations and reading support, but its responses require verification and should not replace students’ own comprehension and critical thinking. Since the research design is correlational, any identified relationships would not establish cause and effect. The findings may provide information that teachers and school administrators can consider when developing responsible approaches to AI-assisted English instruction. The final conclusions and recommendations should be based on the actual collected data and statistical results.</jats:p>

title: Inteligência Artificial Generativa e educação: uma leitura a partir de revisão bibliográfica sistemática e análise de conteúdo
container-title: Brazilian Journal of Animal and Environmental Research
0f01a4f93558890523398cd04e68a86029816440.abstract: <jats:p>A inteligência artificial (IA) generativa tem se difundido rapidamente na sociedade e, em especial, no campo educacional, suscitando oportunidades e incertezas quanto às práticas de ensino e aprendizagem. Este estudo tem como objetivo examinar os desafios da incorporação da IA generativa no processo educacional, sistematizando as principais questões éticas, didáticas e pedagógicas discutidas na literatura. Metodologicamente, realizou-se uma Revisão Sistemática de Literatura estruturada a partir do protocolo PRISMA, nas bases Google Scholar e SciELO, com foco em publicações em língua portuguesa, que resultou na seleção de 33 textos acadêmicos e científicos, examinados por meio da Análise de Conteúdo, em abordagens quantitativo-descritiva e temática. Os resultados permitiram organizar o debate em seis macrotemáticas (desenvolvimento humano, relação professor-aluno, aspectos didáticos e pedagógicos, plágio, produção de escrita e algoritmos e controle), evidenciando o potencial da IA para a personalização do ensino, ao lado de preocupações com a autonomia e a criatividade dos estudantes, a integridade acadêmica, os vieses algorítmicos e as desigualdades de acesso às tecnologias. Conclui-se que a integração da IA generativa à educação exige planejamento criterioso, formação docente contínua e diretrizes éticas claras, de modo a garantir equidade e integridade pedagógica no contexto escolar.</jats:p>

title: Responsible use of artificial intelligence: Authorship, transparency, privacy, and fact-checking
container-title: Business Information Review
cfca2b0818f55c4a8cc8d3058c2c2728195a4b69.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has made fluent text cheap, but it has not made responsibility cheap. This opinion paper conceptualises responsible AI use as a discipline of accountability structured around four questions: Who is responsible for the work? What role did the AI tool play? Whose information was provided? Is the output accurate? Drawing on publication ethics, international AI governance frameworks, Nigerian data protection law and research on language-model limitations, the paper argues that authorship entails answerability rather than mere text production; transparency should be an established research practice; privacy requires safeguards when information is submitted to AI systems; and fact-checking remains indispensable despite the fluency of generated content. It further contends that institutional responses should prioritise critical AI literacy and responsible practice rather than rely excessively on prohibition or unreliable detection tools. Given their expertise in information evaluation, provenance, confidentiality and information literacy, library and information science professionals are well positioned to advance responsible AI governance. The paper proposes integrating transparent disclosure, data protection, human accountability and systematic verification into institutional policies and information literacy programmes. It concludes that the integrity of AI-assisted scholarship depends on the responsible evaluation and communication of information, not merely the efficiency of its production.</jats:p>

title: Transforming the Islamic Religious Education Curriculum in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Integrating Digital Literacy, Religious Moderation, and the Pancasila Student Profile
container-title: Bulletin of Pedagogical Research
ec5ed0b7c661bb3bbe5c376fe5040a74d8084124.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities and challenges for Islamic Religious Education (IRE), particularly in adapting curriculum structures to technological advancement while maintaining religious and national values. This study aims to analyze the transformation of the IRE curriculum through the integration of digital literacy, religious moderation, and the Pancasila Student Profile in the AI era. Employing a qualitative approach through library research, this study examines scholarly journal articles, academic books, educational policy documents, research reports, and relevant publications addressing AI in education, Islamic education curriculum development, digital literacy, religious moderation, and national character formation. Sources were identified through searches of Google Scholar, Garuda, DOAJ, Scopus, and relevant national journal portals. Data were analyzed using content analysis and thematic analysis, supported by the stages of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Source triangulation was employed to strengthen the credibility of the analysis. The findings indicate that IRE curriculum transformation requires the integration of three interconnected curricular dimensions. First, digital literacy should develop students’ abilities to access, evaluate, verify, and utilize digital information critically, ethically, and responsibly. Second, religious moderation should strengthen tolerance, justice, balance, and respect for diversity in digital and social environments. Third, the Pancasila Student Profile should support the development of religious commitment, critical reasoning, creativity, independence, global diversity, and collaboration. This study contributes a context-sensitive conceptual framework that connects these dimensions with responsible AI integration in Indonesian Islamic education. The framework provides a foundation for curriculum development, teacher preparation, educational policy, and future empirical research</jats:p>

title: The right to be forgotten in the context of Artificial Intelligence use
container-title: Tyumen State University Herald Social Economic and Law Research
a3baee234db338939d38988e01925cf5dd49c621.abstract: <jats:p>В статье проводится комплексный теоретико-правовой анализ института права на забвение в условиях цифровизации и активного внедрения технологий искусственного интеллекта. Особое внимание уделяется системным ограничениям действующего регулирования, которое фактически реализует лишь механизм удаления ссылок, не обеспечивая полного устранения информации из цифровой среды. Раскрывается доктринальная критика российской модели как «права на ссылку», не обеспечивающего полноценной защиты личности в цифровом пространстве. В работе анализируются технические особенности функционирования моделей машинного обучения, при которых персональные данные интегрируются в параметрическую структуру нейросетей и не поддаются изолированному удалению без существенного вмешательства в архитектуру модели. Отмечаются риски обратной инженерии, повторной идентификации субъектов данных, распределенного хранения информации и сложности переобучения моделей. Делается вывод о необходимости достижения сбалансированной правовой модели, обеспечивающей эффективную защиту персональных данных при сохранении возможностей технологического развития искусственного интеллекта.</jats:p>

title: Fundamental issues in the methodology of developing Artificial Intelligence systems and models and their associated legal and ethical regulation
container-title: Tyumen State University Herald Social Economic and Law Research
b736d6ff669c9c6df9cdb7f0e1c648463d01a33e.abstract: <jats:p>Статья посвящена фундаментальным проблемам правового и этического регулирования систем и моделей искусственного интеллекта в высшем образовании. Обосновывается, что данные проблемы обусловлены не только недостаточностью нормативного регулирования, но и особенностями методики разработки современных систем ИИ — зависимостью от качества и репрезентативности обучающих данных, непрозрачностью глубоких нейронных сетей, вероятностным характером алгоритмических выводов и генеративной природой больших языковых моделей. В статье рассматриваются три взаимосвязанные проблемы: допустимые пределы делегирования юридически значимых решений системам ИИ, обеспечение прозрачности и подотчетности алгоритмов, а также распределение ответственности за вред, причиненный их применением. Особое внимание уделяется проявлению этих проблем в университетской среде. Проведен сравнительно-правовой анализ подходов Европейского союза, США, Китая и России. Сформулированы практические рекомендации для образовательных организаций.</jats:p>

title: The application of civil law norms with evaluative concepts and artificial intelligence: Possibilities and limits
container-title: Tyumen State University Herald Social Economic and Law Research
09fa19c5647629ca0b8be290cbe97f07c80f10d4.abstract: <jats:p>Вопрос цифровизации правосудия является одной из современных тем юридической науки. Целью статьи является анализ возможности алгоритмизации процесса судебного разбирательства, в котором применяются гражданско-правовые нормы, содержащие оценочные понятия. В статье рассматривается противоречие между гибкой природой оценочных понятий и жесткой алгоритмической логикой искусственного интеллекта (далее — ИИ). Автор исследует проблему судейского усмотрения в условиях применения технологий искусственного интеллекта: допустимо ли передавать математическому алгоритму функции по интерпретации оценочных понятий. Поднимается вопрос о способности ИИ распознать, что имел в виду законодатель, используя в гражданско-правовой норме такие понятия, как разумный срок, разумная цена, существенный вред, несправедливые условия договора или добросовестное поведение, применительно к конкретной ситуации. На основе анализа правовой природы оценочных понятий делается вывод о том, что, несмотря на высокую скорость обработки судебной практики, ИИ не способен учесть содержание неопределенной нормы применительно к каждому индивидуальному спору так, как это делает судья с профессиональным правосознанием.</jats:p>

title: Does Speed Matter? Business Intelligence, Dynamic Capabilities and Managerial Decision Quality
container-title: Journal of Applied Business, Taxation and Economics Research
354d93f06eb6aefd8b168a59989cd4d9a5d1e1b0.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to examine the effect of business intelligence (BI) and dynamic capabilities on managerial decision quality, with decision-making speed as a mediating variable, using contingency theory and the dynamic capability view as the theoretical basis. Data were obtained from 157 managers of medium and large manufacturing companies in Banten Province, Indonesia, selected by purposive sampling, and were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. The results show that BI (0.390) and dynamic capabilities (0.505) have a positive effect on decision-making speed, while BI (0.250), dynamic capabilities (0.417), and decision-making speed (0.228) have a positive effect on managerial decision quality. In the mediation test, the indirect effect of dynamic capabilities through decision-making speed (0.115) is significant, indicating partial mediation, while the indirect effect of BI (0.089) is not, so BI affects decision quality only through its direct path; the model explains 72.7% of the variance in decision-making speed and 70.6% in decision quality. For manufacturing companies, these results mean that BI contributes to decision quality mainly through the content of its information, and that BI investment has to be accompanied by the development of organizational capabilities.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence and sustainable consumption efficiency in Chinese agriculture: evidence from SDG 12
container-title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
d75fc483e6760344757a2bd698a503d524a38616.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Agricultural artificial intelligence innovation offers new opportunities to transform agricultural production and improve resource-use efficiency, yet less is known about how efficiently technological innovations are converted into sustainable production and consumption outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using panel data for 30 provincial-level regions in China from 2019 to 2024, this study develops a dynamic three-stage network DDF-DEA model comprising agricultural AI technological innovation, sustainable agricultural production, and sustainable agricultural consumption. The model estimates both overall and stage-specific efficiencies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that the mean overall efficiency was 0.7284 during the study period and increased with fluctuations, leaving substantial room for improvement. Regional efficiency was highest in eastern China, followed by western and central China, while provincial disparities remained evident. The mean efficiencies of the three stages were 0.4177, 0.9053, and 0.8880, respectively. Stage 1 was the main efficiency bottleneck in most provinces, whereas inefficiencies in Stages 2 and 3 were concentrated in a smaller number of provinces, indicating varying degrees of imbalance across the three stages. The mean Dagum Gini coefficient was 0.1097, and transvariation density accounted for an average of 46.56% of the overall disparity, suggesting that the overlap between regional efficiency distributions was an important source of inequality. The main findings remained broadly stable after indicator substitution, changes in moving-window width, the exclusion of municipalities, alternative stage weights, and the use of a slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis (SBM-DEA) model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that efficiency improvement strategies should be tailored to provincial stage-specific bottlenecks, with particular attention to strengthening agricultural AI innovation capacity and improving the conversion of technological innovations into sustainable production outcomes and of production outcomes into sustainable consumption outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Teaching UX Design to Engineers in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The Double Diamond as a Framework for Reskilling
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
883eb6d750049ed9ab384415097dc29d20dfa0bb.abstract: <jats:p>As generative artificial intelligence transforms software development and digital design practices, engineering education must address the interplay between technical expertise, an understanding of user needs, and critical judgment. This article examines the contribution of UX Design education to this evolution, using the Double Diamond model as a framework for structuring the design process. The research is based on a pedagogical experiment conducted at the École Supérieure Privée d’Ingénierie et de Technologies (ESPRIT) in Tunisia, as part of a 21-hour module for fourth-year students in web and mobile development during the 2025–2026 academic year. The methodological approach is based on the observation of teaching practices and the analysis of student work, including user interviews, personas, usage scenarios, and prototypes. The Double Diamond framework organizes the process into four phases: discover, define, develop, and deliver. It allows for an examination of how students explore usage scenarios, reframe problems, develop solutions, and subject their proposals to evaluation. The article also proposes a cross-cutting examination of the role of generative artificial intelligence in these phases, distinguishing between assisted production and the validation of design choices. It advances the hypothesis that teaching UX design can help broaden the skill set of future engineers, provided that technical mastery is integrated with human understanding, experimentation, and decision-making responsibility. This exploratory research proposes an analytical framework for studying this integration without presupposing the effects of the approach prior to the analysis of empirical data</jats:p>

title: The Role and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Mitigating Fraud Risk in Digital Wallet Use
container-title: Corelytics: Insights into Business and Accounting Systems
881df61391c5b099d7dfc3033067a533fd09432c.abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: This study examines the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in detecting fraud in digital financial transactions compared with manual methods from an internal control perspective, identifies its limitations, particularly false positives and machine learning blind spots, and explains the role of system calibration and human intervention. 
Research Methodology: The study used a literature review of scientific articles, professional reports, and regulations on AI based fraud detection in digital financial transactions, including digital wallets. The literature was screened for relevance to the research questions and synthesized thematically. 
Results: AI outperforms manual and rule based methods in speed, scale, and detection accuracy because it can analyze entire transaction populations in real time. However, AI has structural limitations in the form of false positives and blind spots toward new fraud patterns caused by concept drift, data bias, adversarial behavior, and limited labeled data. Regular calibration and human professional judgment remain necessary to verify alerts and make final decisions, in line with regulations that require human involvement in automated decisions. 
Conclusions: Collaboration between AI and humans, with AI as the initial screening tool and humans as the final decision makers, is the most effective model for fraud detection. 
Limitations: The study is a literature review and has not been tested empirically with real transaction data. 
Contributions: The study integrates evidence on AI effectiveness and limitations into a human in the loop framework and offers guidance for financial institutions, regulators, and researchers.</jats:p>

title: ACCOUNTGUARD AI as Continuous Accounting Intelligence for Early Revenue Fraud Detection in Cashless Companies
container-title: Corelytics: Insights into Business and Accounting Systems
a0a19980285483519dd32f192a8d5f1b70e6484e.abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: This study develops ACCOUNTGUARD AI (Accounting Continuous Intelligence for Revenue Fraud Detection), a continuous accounting intelligence model based on artificial intelligence designed to detect fraud early in the revenue cycle of digital companies operating in a cashless society. 
Research Methodology: The study uses a conceptual design approach based on a literature review of the revenue cycle, fraud theory, continuous accounting and continuous auditing, artificial intelligence for fraud detection, and the digital payment ecosystem. The review is used to map fraud red flags at each revenue cycle stage and to design a model architecture and a conceptual dashboard prototype. 
Results: The model consists of four layers, namely a Data Integration Layer, a Feature Engineering Layer, a Hybrid Fraud Detection Engine that combines rule based detection, unsupervised anomaly detection, supervised classification, and graph analytics into a risk score from 0 to 100, and a Human in the Loop Reporting and Escalation Layer. The model monitors every stage from sales order to refund and covers the entire transaction population in real time.
Conclusions: ACCOUNTGUARD AI has the potential to accelerate and improve the accuracy of early fraud detection while keeping auditors and management as the final decision makers.
Limitations: The model is conceptual and has not been tested with real or simulated transaction data, so its accuracy, cost efficiency, and false positive rate remain unmeasured.
Contributions: The study integrates artificial intelligence with revenue cycle controls and revenue recognition principles and offers guidance for companies, auditors, regulators, and system developers.</jats:p>

title: Mediating Role of Artificial Intelligence Usage between Secondary Mathematics Teachers’ Knowledge of Human-Centric AI Pedagogy and Lesson Planning Skills
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
b6a575169a03f974de38ea5d95c9bf5f581371c8.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage among mathematics teachers has become an increasingly important part of their professional practice, including the planning, implementation, and assessment of instruction. As AI becomes more widely used, it continues to pose the challenge of maintaining ethical standards in its use and safeguarding human-led instructional planning. This study examined the mediating role of AI Usage in the relationship between Human-Centric AI Pedagogy (HCAP) Knowledge and Lesson Planning Skills among the 107 Junior High School mathematics teachers in Congressional District II of Valenzuela City. A descriptive-correlational research design with a mediation approach was utilized. Data were collected using validated instruments measuring HCAP Knowledge, AI Usage based on the four ILAW core elements, and Lesson Planning Skills, and were analyzed using descriptive statistics and mediation analysis with bootstrapping. The findings showed moderate levels of HCAP Knowledge and AI Usage, while Lesson Planning Skills were at a high level. Human-AI Collaborative Knowledge obtained the relatively lowest result among the HCAP domains, while Ways Forward obtained the lowest results in both AI Usage and Lesson Planning Skills. AI Usage significantly mediated the association between HCAP Knowledge and Lesson Planning Skills, indicating partial mediation. The findings highlight the need to strengthen teachers’ capacity to use AI as a collaborative and reflective support for instructional decision-making, leading to the development of a Targeted Mentoring Plan for Mathematics Master Teachers.</jats:p>

title: School Leaders’ Emotional Intelligence, Teacher Work Engagement, and Challenges in Professional Growth
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
483cb0b2f50e69bf02c31283a8825158a9789770.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined teachers’ perceptions of school leaders’ emotional intelligence, teacher work engagement, and challenges in achieving professional growth and maintaining well-being in selected public elementary and secondary schools in the Division of Maguindanao del Norte. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design involved 362 purposively selected respondents. A structured questionnaire assessed four emotional-intelligence domains, three work-engagement dimensions, and ten professional-growth and well-being challenges. Frequencies, percentages, means, standard deviations, independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlations were used. Respondents strongly agreed with indicators of leaders’ self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, and relationship management and with indicators of their own vigor, dedication, and absorption. The overall challenge mean was 2.40 (SD = 0.73), interpreted as Disagree, although respondents endorsed needing more instructional feedback, limited professional-development time because of workload, and difficulties integrating technology. Selected gender, rank, and school-type comparisons differed significantly; age and teaching-experience comparisons did not. Overall perceived emotional intelligence was positively associated with overall work engagement (r = .551, p < .01). Relationships involving professional-growth challenges were nonsignificant. Findings informed the proposed THRIVE-BARMM Professional Development Program. The results support attention to emotionally responsive leadership and targeted professional support but do not establish causal effects or program effectiveness.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Mediated Enhancement of Science Teachers’ Core Competencies for Implementing the Five-Step Scientific Inquiry Approach in Indonesian Classrooms
container-title: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
7044766985d3bd213e01147df2e95136e9d56552.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined science teachers’ core competencies and implementation of the Five-Step Scientific Inquiry Approach in Indonesian classrooms and developed an instructional strategic model for AI-supported inquiry. A descriptive-correlational design involved 50 purposively selected science teachers and a modified survey questionnaire, supplemented by a focus group discussion with eight teachers. Means and standard deviations described competencies and inquiry implementation, and Pearson’s correlation examined their association. Teachers were rated Highly Competent overall (M = 3.82, SD = 0.13), while inquiry implementation was Highly Evident (M = 3.79, SD = 0.13). Ethical and responsible AI use received the highest competency mean (3.86), and inquiry-based teaching competence received the lowest (3.78). Questioning was the lowest-rated inquiry stage (M = 3.65, SD = 0.38). A statistically significant moderate inverse association emerged between AI-related competencies and reported inquiry implementation (r = −.373, p = .008). Focus group findings identified challenges in responsible AI integration, perceived instructional benefits, and needs for sustained professional support. Teachers emphasized verification, ethical use, appropriate resources, and preservation of scientific reasoning. The findings informed the nine-component SARSADIAZ Instructional Strategic Model. The results describe reported practices and associations; they do not establish causal enhancement, student achievement effects, or the model’s effectiveness, which requires further validation.</jats:p>

title: <b>ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THESIS WRITING AMONG ALLIED HEALTH SCIENCES STUDENTS: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS</b>
container-title: International Journal of Multidisciplinary and Medical Research
27e15b7d191a1d0aad8fb257833fc87115cfa81e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed various aspects of higher education and scientific research. AI-powered tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Elicit, Consensus, and Research Rabbit are increasingly being utilized by undergraduate students to facilitate literature searching, idea generation, academic writing, data analysis, and reference management. Among Allied Health Sciences students, thesis writing often represents a significant academic challenge due to limited research experience and scientific writing skills. AI has emerged as a valuable supportive tool capable of enhancing research efficiency and improving the quality of academic outputs. However, concerns regarding academic integrity, reliability of AI-generated content, data privacy, and overreliance on technology have generated considerable debate within the academic community. This short communication discusses the potential benefits, limitations, and ethical considerations associated with AI use in thesis writing among Allied Health Sciences students. It emphasizes that AI should serve as an assistive technology rather than a replacement for critical thinking, scientific reasoning, and original scholarly contributions. Appropriate institutional guidelines and AI literacy training are essential to ensure responsible and ethical utilization of these technologies in academic research.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence and corporate green transformation: evidence from China’s A-share listed firms
container-title: Accounting Research Journal
192b57385339275fd1cbfefb289475658e3fd69b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption contributes to corporate green transformation. It analyses the mediating roles of green technological innovation and human capital upgrading, the moderating roles of organisational resilience and environmental regulation and the heterogeneous effects across industrial and regional contexts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study uses panel data on Chinese A-share listed non-financial firms from 2008 to 2023. Fixed-effects regressions, instrumental-variable estimation, propensity score matching, mediation analysis, interaction models and subgroup analyses are used to examine the relationship between AI adoption and corporate green transformation, its transmission mechanisms, boundary conditions and contextual heterogeneity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI adoption is positively associated with corporate green transformation, and the result remains robust to alternative measures and endogeneity tests. Green technological innovation and human capital upgrading partially mediate this relationship, while organisational resilience and environmental regulation strengthen it. The positive relationship is statistically significant among firms in non-heavily polluting industries, firms in eastern and western China and firms in non-resource-based cities, but not in the corresponding comparison groups.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends recent evidence on the environmental effects of AI by explaining how AI adoption is converted into firm-level green transformation and why this process varies across firms and locations. It provides an integrated account of the technological, workforce, organisational, institutional and structural conditions that shape the environmental value of AI adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The impact of an artificial intelligence learning platform on the teaching efficacy, professional development and digital burnout of accounting educators
container-title: Advances in Social Behavior Research
a83eb4301cd85425b2a7c5c6ff60f76aa61ae06f.abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid development of educational artificial intelligence (AI) technology, the field of accounting education is undergoing significant transformations. This study examines the impact of educational AI applications on accounting teachers’ self-efficacy, professional development, and burnout. A questionnaire survey was conducted with 400 accounting teachers from 30 universities in China, who were randomly assigned to either an experimental group or a control group. Teachers in the experimental group received training and guidance on the application of AI teaching tools, while those in the control group did not receive any relevant interventions. Data were collected using a self-efficacy scale, a professional development questionnaire, and a burnout scale, and were analysed through independent samples t-tests. The results indicated that the integration of AI technology significantly enhanced the self-efficacy and professional development of accounting teachers, while effectively reducing burnout. This study suggests that AI-assisted teaching tools not only foster teachers' professional growth but also enhance their teaching autonomy and innovation, thereby alleviating the professional fatigue associated with traditional teaching pressures. These findings provide a theoretical foundation and practical guidance for promoting the professional development of accounting teachers and improving teaching quality, highlighting the significant role of educational AI in the reform of accounting education in colleges and universities.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Solfeggio Teaching and Learning: Current Status, Needs, And Lecturer-Guided Priorities
container-title: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies
ee8e034db935c8130d1d88853d30058f3c3985c5.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Solfeggio requires repeated practice in listening, pitch production, rhythmic accuracy, and sight-singing, yet students may receive limited feedback during independent study. Objective: This study investigated teaching and self-practice difficulties, artificial intelligence (AI) readiness, and preferred support functions at Hong Duc University, Vietnam. Methods: A descriptive mixed-methods design used 12 valid lecturer questionnaires, 72 retained student questionnaires from 80 screened, and six semi-structured lecturer interviews collected during 1-7 September 2026. Frequencies, percentages, item-level means on five-point scales, and thematic summaries were examined without inferential testing. Results: Lecturers prioritized AI-assisted pitch practice and recognition (4.75/5) and listening, recording, and error identification (4.67/5). Students gave the strongest priority to exercises matched to individual errors (4.63/5) and recording with basic error detection (4.61/5). Readiness to try AI tools was 4.08/5 among lecturers; students’ readiness to use AI with lecturer guidance was 4.50/5. Concerns about feedback accuracy were substantial in both groups. Conclusion: The findings support a limited, lecturer-supervised role for AI in self-practice and formative feedback. They do not establish the effectiveness of any particular AI system.</jats:p>

title: Strengthening and safeguarding artificial intelligence for a planet under pressure
container-title: Environmental Research Letters
a3668b40759d3e7779e827f1f54b3e45ddd2b306.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping sustainability science through advances in climate modeling, ecosystem monitoring, resource management, and evidence synthesis. Yet its use also raises concerns about reliability, equity, and environmental impacts. In this Prospective, we identify four priorities for responsible AI integration: ensuring AI-supported claims are causal, transparent, and auditable; treating model selection as an environmental decision; building sustainability-focused AI infrastructure; and engaging sustainability scientists and affected communities in AI design and governance. With these safeguards, AI can enhance sustainability science while promoting equitable and environmentally responsible decision-making.</jats:p>

title: Tecnologias de precisão e Inteligência Artificial para avaliação do bem estar de bezerros
container-title: Brazilian Journal of Animal and Environmental Research
386f984c064e26ea42c2e5973a96db5c04247b76.abstract: <jats:p>Devido à elevada vulnerabilidade dos bezerros leiteiros, o monitoramento contínuo tornou-se essencial para a detecção precoce de alterações sanitárias e comportamentais. Esta revisão narrativa crítica discute as contribuições e limitações de tecnologias de precisão e inteligência artificial para a avaliação do bem-estar de bezerros, com base em publicações sobre acelerômetros, alimentadores automáticos, termografia, processamento de imagens e sistemas de apoio à decisão. As evidências indicam que essas ferramentas permitem caracterizar padrões individuais de decúbito, atividade e alimentação e identificar mudanças associadas a enfermidades. Contudo, o desempenho na classificação de comportamentos não assegura previsão clínica confiável, tampouco comprova melhoria do bem-estar. A interpretação dos registros depende da idade, do alojamento, do manejo alimentar e da validação dos dispositivos em condições compatíveis com seu uso. À luz dos Cinco Domínios, os indicadores automatizados contribuem principalmente para examinar condições nutricionais, ambientais, sanitárias e comportamentais, enquanto inferências sobre o estado mental exigem avaliação integrada. A aplicação prática dessas tecnologias deve ser orientada por objetivos de manejo, protocolos de intervenção e acompanhamento dos resultados obtidos para os animais.</jats:p>

title: Gouty Arthritis: Pathophysiology, Current Therapeutic Strategies and the Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Pharmacology and Toxicology Research
38895493bff7daa951e7f36dba5f8d2f7f88dc81.abstract: <jats:p>Gouty arthritis is a chronic inflammatory metabolic disorder that is one of the most prevalent forms of inflammatory arthritis worldwide and its burden continues to increase due to various factors, including obesity, dietary changes, sedentary lifestyles and metabolic disorders. Persistent hyperuricemia promotes the deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals, which triggers acute gout flares and may progress to chronic tophaceous gout, accompanied by irreversible joint damage and disability. The pathogenesis involves activation of innate immune pathways and the NLRP3 inflammasome, resulting in the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. The condition can be diagnosed by assessing serum urate levels, clinical manifestations and, when appropriate, MSU crystal deposition, while management includes pharmacological treatment and lifestyle modification. Emerging targeted therapies and artificial intelligence are expected to improve long-term disease monitoring, enhance clinical outcomes and reduce the global burden of gout.</jats:p>

title: Effect of Application-Based Learning Using Generative Artificial Intelligence on Information Literacy of First-Year Medical Students in Yunnan Province
container-title: Interdisciplinary Academic and Research Journal
ae5fca122b81c702af4a0f5001bbeece73180306.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aims: This experimental research aimed to 1) compare students’ information literacy before and after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence, 2) compare students’ information literacy after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence with the determined criterion set at 70%, and 3) assess students’ satisfaction after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence.
Methodology: The research instruments were lesson plans, students’ information literacy test, and a satisfaction questionnaire. The appropriateness of the lesson plans overall was at a very high level (M=4.62, SD=0.49). The students’ information literacy test had an IOC between 0.67–1.00, item difficulty (p=0.43-0.60), item discrimination (r=0.25-0.50), and KR20 equal to 0.76. The students’ satisfaction questionnaire had an IOC between 0.67 and 1.00 and a reliability index of 0.85. The statistics used to analyze data were mean, standard deviation, t-test for dependent samples, and t-test for one sample.
Results: 1) students’ information literacy after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence was higher than before at statistically significant level of .01 (t29=18.53, p=.000), 2) students’ information literacy was higher than the determined criterion of 70% at a significance level of .01 (t29=6.00, p=.000) and 3) students’ satisfaction after learning through Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence overall was at a high level (M=4.14, SD= 0.85).
Conclusion: The knowledge gained from the research is that a six-step learning management system using Application-Based Learning using Generative Artificial Intelligence (ABL-GAI), which represents an innovative instructional framework that systematically integrates human-AI co-creation into information literacy education. The most significant steps for enhancing students’ information literacy are step 4: Practice the skills + GAI, and step 5: Apply & create + GAI. Furthermore, this method has been shown to boost students' interest in learning and enhance their proficiency in core information literacy competencies, including information definition & planning, seeking & access, analysis, synthesis & communication, and reflection & self-evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Exploration and Practice of a Teacher–Student–Machine Tripartite Collaborative Teaching Model for the Modern Control Theory Course Empowered by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Education Research
57417a6e7218ecf8007df212b1d744c19eac1bc9.abstract: <jats:p>Modern Control Theory is a core course for automation majors. Its knowledge system takes the state-space method as its main thread, characterized by complex mathematical derivations and abstract physical concepts; compounded by the practical constraint of large-class instruction with over one hundred students, the course has long suffered from three structural contradictions: the teaching process is invisible, learning states are unmeasurable, and instructional support is inaccessible. Relying on the “AI+” Classroom Teaching Reform project and guided by the philosophy of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), this study constructs a tripartite collaborative teaching model involving teachers, students, and AI agents. Practice shows that, while firmly maintaining the teacher's leading role in education, the model transforms artificial intelligence into an embeddable, measurable, and iterable teaching element, providing a referable practical sample for the digital-intelligent transformation of engineering courses.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Cognitive Development: A Thematic Analysis
container-title: International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research
7caf6d26feca630c35a11a6a53d780581522a8b8.abstract: <jats:p>There is still uncertainty surrounding whether generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) enhances or decreases human cognition, as the proof is scattered all around. This thematic analysis synthesises 46 core peer-reviewed articles (2011–2026), selected from 165 Scopus records after an assessment, to conclude how AI applications affect the development of human cognition in learning. The six-phase process proposed by Braun and Clarke (2006) yielded six themes: (1) AI-assisted performance does not equal productive learning; (2) cognitive offloading is mixed in quality and dependent and autonomous vary in approach; (3) critical and higher-order thinking depend on usage of AI rather than simply on AI existence; (4) metacognition, self-regulation, and calibration play the main role; (5) either strengths of creativity and cognitive agency depend on process of engagement; and (6) pedagogical design has implications for all listed above. The proof of a long-lasting, self-sufficient gain is scarce and varies, whereas the data largely comprise cross-sectional opinions of university undergraduates. The final evaluation shows that the cognitive influence of artificial intelligence is variable. It's dependent on the governing behaviour and the teaching method. The research gives rise to a human-centred agenda, which aims to maintain productive effort, use artificial intelligence indirectly, and assess the process besides the result.</jats:p>

title: Beyond the Cleft: Can Artificial Intelligence Redefine the Future of Cleft Care
container-title: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
7353008bd6caa7c626928cb42aafa8d9a1eec7eb.abstract: <jats:p>Cleft lip and palate (CLP) represent a major group of congenital craniofacial conditions that require coordinated, long-term care involving multiple healthcare specialties. The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in dentistry and orthodontics has opened new avenues for addressing the diagnostic and therapeutic complexities associated with cleft management. This narrative review examines the evolving applications of AI throughout the CLP treatment pathway, highlighting its potential contributions to clinical assessment, treatment planning, and outcome evaluation. The review considers seven key areas in which AI-based technologies may support cleft care. These include the identification of cleft anomalies from prenatal ultrasound and photographic images using deep learning algorithms; computer-assisted planning and digital fabrication of nasoalveolar molding appliances; automated localization of cephalometric landmarks in patients with atypical craniofacial structures; three-dimensional assessment and segmentation of alveolar bone grafts using conebeam computed tomography (CBCT); radiographic identification of dental abnormalities frequently associated with CLP; predictive modelling of orthognathic surgical requirements and postoperative facial soft-tissue changes; and computerized analysis of speech patterns associated with velopharyngeal dysfunction. Research in these areas suggests that AI may improve the efficiency and consistency of diagnostic procedures, facilitate quantitative analysis, and assist clinicians in complex treatment decisions. However, the translation of these technologies into routine clinical practice remains challenging. Important barriers include limited sample sizes, inadequate representation of patient populations, insufficient validation across independent clinical settings, the possibility of algorithmic bias, and ethical issues related to patient data protection and professional accountability. For orthodontists involved in cleft care, AI offers opportunities to enhance clinical decision-making and streamline selected aspects of treatment. Nevertheless, its outputs must be interpreted in conjunction with comprehensive clinical examination, patient-specific findings, and multidisciplinary expertise. Future research should prioritize larger and more diverse datasets, independent clinical validation, transparent reporting, and evaluation of real-world patient outcomes to establish the reliability and clinical value of AI-assisted approaches in CLP management.</jats:p>

title: Applications of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Bioinformatics and Their Experimental Validation
container-title: Research Journal of Life Sciences, Bioinformatics, Pharmaceutical and Chemical Sciences
e98d4a4e4187b8f96f2d2b3304fa430c6f2f0632.abstract: <jats:p>A sequence model can identify a base substitution predicted to alter a splice junction, and a cancer model can assign a tumour to a pathway-defined group. Researchers often interpret these outputs as explanations, although each calls for a different experimental test. This narrative review examines how explainable artificial intelligence is used in regulatory genomics, RNA processing, cancer genomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, protein science, molecular property prediction and microbial genomics. It compares the biological entity being explained, the reference used to calculate an effect and the evidence available beyond the original model. Base substitutions and matched molecular pairs permit explicit contrasts. Pathway scores, tissue neighbourhoods and internal protein features require additional tests to separate the proposed mechanism from correlated measurements. Recent evaluations of foundation models also show why comparisons with simple predictors and genuinely held-out biological units matter before interpretation. Across applications, the clearest route to experimental follow-up is to specify an expected molecular event, its direction and a result that would challenge the prediction. This approach separates faithful descriptions of model behaviour from claims supported by an independent assay and clarifies what an explanation contributes to the selection of the next experiment.</jats:p>

title: Reconstructing literary space using artificial intelligence-enhanced architectural representation methods: Georges Perec and the Plassaert Apartment
container-title: Journal of Design, Planning and Aesthetics Research
6c5ea07a35976bf6022202653c674cb688cba9b5.abstract: <jats:p>Positioned at the intersection of literature and architecture, this study explores how abstract spaces constructed in literary texts can be reconstructed using architectural representation tools and artificial intelligence technologies. The focus of the research is the Plassaert apartment in Georges Perec’s Life: A User’s Manual, which details the space through everyday objects and lists, and the users of this space across different periods. The object-human relationships, hoarding tendencies, and the psychological weight of the space described in the text have been transformed into architectural representations through artificial intelligence (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot). The study’s methodology is based on a spatial accumulation model constructed around the parameters of Actor, Space, and Time. The 5-Level Prompt Model has transformed these literary data into a visual language, producing the spatial counterpart of each actor in their own time. Within the scope of the findings, the layering created by the material concerns, psychological and social states of space users through objects has been concretised through spatial indicators. The narrative structure in Perec’s literature (chess and jigsaw puzzle metaphors) has been represented through conceptual collages. In the final stage, plan and section planes were superimposed simultaneously, developing a representational model where the temporal traces left by different actors in the same physical space can be read in a multi-layered manner. In conclusion, this research demonstrates that literature offers a multi-layered research field for architectural analysis and representation; it also reveals that AI-supported tools can play a supportive role in visualizing this layered structure.</jats:p>

title: Finlet AI: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Financial Intelligence Platform Using Model Context Protocol and Deterministic Risk Governance
container-title: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
27dad0acee8d55eb44e2d11a6bed4fb2d73d8d08.abstract: <jats:p>Standalone conversational language models struggle to satisfy audit and compliance standards in institutional equity research. When an equity analyst prompts an ungrounded model to evaluate a listed company, three operational defects appear almost immediately: the model quotes outdated share prices from its pre-training cutoff, invents page or footnote numbers when summarizing regulatory filings, and produces inconsistent numerical risk ratings when executed repeatedly on identical inputs. This paper presents Finlet AI, a twelve-layer multi-agent financial intelligence platform that decouples quantitative market arithmetic and primary-source retrieval from neural text synthesis. Once an analytical query is submitted through our asynchronous FastAPI gateway, a stateful LangGraph supervisor triggers concurrent parallel fan-out across three specialized domain workers covering historical price series, live financial news feeds, and statutory annual reports isolated behind standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool interfaces. Technical price action, 20-day volume momentum ratios, and 30-day annualized volatility (σ	) are computed directly from three-month 30d Open-High-Low-Close-Volume (OHLCV) series fetched via Yahoo Finance. Real-time news catalysts are gathered through Google News RSS syndication and sanitized of HTML markup, while balance-sheet debt and liquidity disclosures are extracted page by page from SEC Form 10-K and Indian annual reports indexed locally in ChromaDB using 384-dimensional all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings. Rather than delegating risk scoring to subjective prompt completion, our Risk & Governance module evaluates a bounded mathematical index weighting volatility (45% weight), news sentiment risk (35% weight), and filing flags (20% weight). Live validation on Reliance Industries (RELIANCE.NS) demonstrates real-time tracking at ₹1,184.50 (−2.03%), 23.1% annualized volatility, 1.0x volume momentum, and a deterministic risk score of 0.365 (LOW), while high-risk runs (≥ 0.65) pause at a persistent SQLite Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoint before compiling the final ReportLab PDF dossier..</jats:p>
