title: AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Foundations of AI Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
9f630b63700f2df7c972c28e264e05e6ceddde77.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence governance has emerged as a critical imperative in contemporary digital societies, demanding comprehensive frameworks that balance innovation with accountability, human rights, and democratic values. This chapter examines the foundational principles, institutional mechanisms, regulatory approaches, and ethical considerations that constitute effective AI governance systems. Through analysis of global governance frameworks including the EU AI Act, risk-based regulatory models, and international cooperation mechanisms, the chapter explores how legal norms are being transformed to address AI's unique challenges. Key governance dimensions examined include algorithmic accountability, transparency requirements, human rights safeguards, and the integration of democratic oversight into AI systems. The chapter provides empirical insights from recent governance initiatives across jurisdictions, analyzing both regulatory successes and persistent governance gaps.</jats:p>

title: AI Governance Foundations
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
2b28db33bf306c935f211bfca2b70402877fdf38.abstract: <jats:p>Government Artificial intelligence altering the governmental systems and substituting the traditional e-government models with the more algorithmic system of governance, where the decisions are increasingly mediated by the automated systems and processes based on the data. This has created challenging legal, ethical, and regulatory challenges of responsibility, accountability, transparency and fairness. The governance principles of AI involve the establishment of legal definitions, framework and standards to define responsibilities, scope and rights of AI usage in government and civil service. System regulation, risk reduction and protection of the right of the citizens demands definite legal definitions of AI, automated decision-making, and algorithmic accountability. Efficiencies can be opened up by making e-government, centered around digital service delivery, to become algorithmic governance, with incorporation of AI tools to analyze policies to distribute resources, predictive services, and make administrative judgments.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI and Foundation Models
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
c1f53c26084dcc82007fb1323a246abfe7791ac5.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence and foundation models represent a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, raising unprecedented governance challenges. This chapter examines the intersection of these technologies with democratic institutions, legal frameworks, and ethical norms. It analyzes emerging regulatory approaches including the EU AI Act and OECD principles, explores algorithmic bias and accountability mechanisms, and investigates tensions between innovation and rights protection. Through systematic review of recent scholarship and policy developments, the chapter identifies critical challenges in transparency, intellectual property, and algorithmic decision-making legitimacy.</jats:p>

title: The New Social Contract
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
22bdcab34bf4ce9285fa937f0a7ef9efba76e478.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the transformation of democratic accountability in the age of artificial intelligence through legal, institutional, and political analysis. It examines how algorithmic decision-making reconfigures authority and responsibility, emphasizing the need for a new social contract integrating AI within constitutional frameworks. Focusing on India, the chapter proposes participatory, rights-based, and accountable governance models to align technological innovation with democratic legitimacy and public trust.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Constitutional Law in Structuring AI Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4b4b0de7a68d19261bb75753772840e30a18eec7.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the foundational role of constitutional law in structuring artificial intelligence governance frameworks. As AI systems increasingly influence democratic processes, individual rights, and societal structures, constitutional principles provide essential constraints and guidance for regulatory design. The analysis explores how fundamental rights doctrines, separation of powers, democratic accountability mechanisms, and rule of law principles shape AI governance approaches across jurisdictions. Drawing on comparative constitutional frameworks, including the EU AI Act and emerging international instruments, the chapter demonstrates how constitutional law bridges normative values and technical regulation. Key challenges include algorithmic accountability, automated decision-making impacts on fundamental rights, and the tension between innovation and constitutional safeguards.</jats:p>

title: A Conceptual Shift in Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
ab477729de01bf724d4e82f352be4fc70e322edf.abstract: <jats:p>Today, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an integral part of governance. This chapter examines the paradigm shift that is necessary for the governance of AI, which includes four key components: legality, transparency, accountability, and respect for human rights. By referring to global instruments like the European Union AI Act and the UNESCO's Ethics of AI as well as the respective national laws, it is proposed that the governance of AI should not only be about the technical but rather the rethinking of public law in light of human rights. The chapter conducts a conceptual analysis of the gaps between the regulatory framework and the actual implementation of AI in practice, particularly in high-risk industries. An Integrated Governance Framework (IGF) is proposed, in which all four pillars are interrelated.</jats:p>

title: Principles of Good Governance in the Age of AI
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
f1bf41b5e570221d1d030fc576b518faa6ad2712.abstract: <jats:p>The concept of artificial intelligence is becoming a part of the governance, artificial administration, and even the decision-making process in legal administration, which prompts serious questions about the quality of democracy and institutional control. With the impacts of algorithmic systems becoming a regulatory enforcer and in policy outputs, the opportunities of risks linked to transparency, discrimination, and lack of accountability escalate. This chapter discusses the ways in which the rule of law and democratic practices should be supported by relying on the principles of legality, transparency, and accountability in governing AI. It examines issues like black box problem, diffusion of responsibility and algorithmic discretion and suggests a normative model entailing the combination of legal protection, oversight and transparency norms to guarantee responsible and trustworthy AI usage.</jats:p>

title: Adaptive Regulation, Sandboxes, and Experimentalist Approaches
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
7e11bfc9418f4605cdb5f5a63e9b3f499236e89e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence technologies presents unprecedented challenges to traditional regulatory frameworks and democratic governance structures. This chapter examines how adaptive regulation, regulatory sandboxes, and experimentalist governance approaches are reshaping the social contract between citizens, governments, and technology corporations in the AI era. Through comprehensive analysis of emerging regulatory models across multiple jurisdictions, this study demonstrates how experimentalist approaches enable responsive governance while maintaining democratic accountability. The chapter evaluates the effectiveness of regulatory sandboxes in balancing innovation with risk management, explores the theoretical foundations of adaptive regulation in complex technological environments, and proposes a reconceptualized framework for the social contract that accommodates algorithmic decision-making while preserving fundamental rights.</jats:p>

title: Legal Ontologies as Semantic Infrastructure for Normative Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
f174114117b770c5b4a90db645fc80ad53f70442.abstract: <jats:p>The future challenge in AI & Law is not merely computational performance or post-hoc interpretability, but the translation of legal meaning into forms that computational systems can process without downgrading the normative structure of the Law into statistical correlations. This chapter introduces the philosophical argument that legal ontologies should be treated as semantic infrastructure for normative governance, that is, a mediating layer between legal texts, institutional practice, and AI-based decision support. Legal ontologies as computational artefacts that encode legal knowledge in a machine-understandable way, make explicit the conceptual commitments that enable systems to qualify facts in legally relevant terms, align conclusions to rules, exceptions, and principles, and generate explanations that simulate legal justification. Synthesizing the literature on legal ontologies (i.e., scope, engineering methodology, applications), this chapter focuses on developing a theoretical description of legal ontologies as semantic infrastructure for accountable AI in legal domains.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Economic Development, and Human Rights
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4ee6296fcf5b904bf56fa2f91c3f8be35f78cd19.abstract: <jats:p>Over the last century, the world witnessed unprecedented technological advancements and economic growth. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been a major technological breakthrough, decisively transforming economic interactions in various sectors. With their unique characteristics of speed, accuracy, and efficiency, AI-enabled systems enhanced innovation, increased productivity, and advanced economic growth. However, current experience affirms that the benefits of AI-empowered economic development are not equitably shared. It results in rising poverty, economic inequality, and human insecurity worldwide. Developing countries experience them most severely due to the increased digital divide. The human rights of millions of people are directly or indirectly denied on account of the biased interplay between AI and economic development that primarily favors advanced countries. From this perspective, this chapter, using the qualitative methodology's narrative synthesis and critical analysis tools, examines the correlation between AI and economic development through the lens of human rights.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Accountability and Protection of Fair Procedure Rights in AI-Driven Public Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
a83d8cfd752d0d873913a4e386493a38c0794f36.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyzes the paradigm shift from human-based bureaucracy to data-based governance and the tensions between algorithmic logic and fair procedure rights. The authors argue that automated decision-making in public administration triggers algorithmic procedural erosion, where traditional legal protections fail to address “black box” opacity. By identifying research gaps in how administrative law handles algorithmic discretion, this chapter explores the realignment of state power from officials to code developers. The authors propose reconstructing legal norms through an “Accountability by Design” framework, integrating procedural rights such as notification, intelligible explanation, and human intervention directly into AI architecture. Furthermore, this chapter advocates for independent algorithmic audits as legal evidence in judicial reviews to bridge information asymmetry. Finally, the authors conclude that normative redesign is essential to ensure digitalization strengthens democratic sovereignty and the rule of law, rather than creating an unaccountable technocracy.</jats:p>

title: The “Legitimate Interest Trap” in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
2e9944fcddef72768c2ae829a9e0e2ec444ccbc0.abstract: <jats:p>As organizations accelerate the deployment of AI systems, many default to the “legitimate interest” lawful basis for processing personal data. This move appears attractive because it avoids consent friction and accommodates broad operational goals such as security, fraud prevention, or service optimization. In practice, however, AI amplifies the evidentiary and governance burden embedded in legitimate interest, namely controllers must show a specific legitimate purpose, prove necessity (no equally effective, less intrusive alternative), and demonstrate that the interest is not overridden by individuals' rights and freedoms. Drawing on the European Data Protection Board's Guidelines 1/2024 on Article 6(1)(f) and the EDPB's Opinion 28/2024 on AI models, this chapter argues that “legitimate interest” becomes a trap when treated as a rhetorical justification rather than a structured test that must be operationalized through technical and organizational safeguards. The chapter proposes an “LIA-by-design” approach, that aligns privacy assessments under the EU AI Act.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Governance and Due Process in India
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
588dcb96d6cae7a2831ce0b99703c07178f2e3ab.abstract: <jats:p>The expansion of digital governance in India has embedded algorithmic systems within welfare administration, particularly in identity verification, eligibility determination, and benefit delivery. While these systems are justified on grounds of efficiency and scalability, they raise significant concerns for due process and administrative fairness. This chapter examines how core procedural safeguards notice, hearing, and reasoned decisions are affected by automated decision-making frameworks. It argues that algorithmic governance introduces opacity, limits avenues for contestation, and weakens accountability. The integration of digital identity further conditions access to welfare on technological compliance, increasing risks of exclusion. The chapter concludes that algorithmic systems fundamentally reshape state citizen relations and require recalibrated legal safeguards.</jats:p>

title: Digital Sovereignty and Legal Pluralism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
0e1ac7826c5e0fc071b7288b1558bb3f5df99b2a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving concept of digital sovereignty through a comparative analysis of the European Union, the United States, and India within conditions of legal pluralism. It explores how democratic systems negotiate authority, rights, and regulation across overlapping legal, technological, and market domains. The European Union's rights-based constitutionalism, the United States' market-oriented digital order, and India's developmental-democratic model reveal diverse strategies for governing data, platforms, and infrastructure. Drawing on secondary data from 2020–2025, the chapter analyzes regulatory frameworks such as the GDPR, DPDP Act 2023, and the U.S. FTC's enforcement regime. It identifies convergences in recognizing data as a strategic resource and divergences in institutional design, enforcement capacity, and global influence.</jats:p>

title: The Adoption of International Artificial Intelligence Frameworks in Latin America
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
4701fb43814a97a05be3830c6acecafd8a990cf2.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines emerging AI regulation in Latin America through qualitative comparison of countries participating in the Council of Europe's Framework Convention on AI—Argentina, Mexico, Uruguay (Group 1)—versus influential non-participants—Brazil, Chile, Colombia (Group 2). It contrasts international soft law with the first global binding treaty, highlighting its universal openness and risk-based approach. Group 1 shows proactive adherence (Uruguay pioneering signatory, Mexico active observer) through ethical yet fragmented national strategies, while Group 2 prioritizes sovereignty via advanced risk-based legislative projects, indirectly aligned with Council of Europe standards through EU AI Act and UNESCO guidelines. The study concludes that the globalist-national dichotomy is converging toward risk-based governance and proposes the OAS as a strategic forum for an Inter-American AI Declaration to harmonize both groups, standardize supervisory mechanisms, and catalyze Council of Europe adherence, strategically positioning Latin America within global AI governance frameworks.</jats:p>

title: Digital Illiteracy and Accounting Compliance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
5efe409d16d9b3864a79a51144be26f5f26411d2.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how digital illiteracy affects accounting compliance during the transition to mandatory e-invoicing in Greece. A quantitative approach was employed using data from 220 enterprises located in the Prefecture of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace. A structured questionnaire measured digital skills, awareness of e-invoicing procedures, and perceptions of state support. The results reveal that educational level and gender significantly influence the effective implementation of e-invoicing tools, while age has no significant impact. Despite gradual improvements in digital competence, digital illiteracy remains a key barrier to full compliance, especially among SMEs. The findings highlight the need for targeted digital training programs, simplified e-invoicing platforms, and policy incentives aimed at strengthening SMEs' technological capacity. This research empirically links digital literacy to compliance behavior in an emerging economy context, offering actionable insights for policymakers, tax authorities, and accounting practitioners.</jats:p>

title: Educating Citizens in the Algorithmic State
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
c36db21603c573e6fb9e8bf58f69f40ba2fba2e3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines ethical AI awareness as a necessary form of civic competence in the algorithmic state. As AI systems increasingly shape public administration, healthcare, welfare, education, local governance, public safety, and democratic communication, citizens need more than basic digital skills. They require the capacity to understand how AI may affect rights, equality, transparency, accountability, inclusion. The chapter presents a curriculum for ethical AI awareness designed to educate AI-aware citizens and stakeholders on the ethical foundations of AI, bias and discrimination, sources of algorithmic harm, mitigation strategies, ethical frameworks, transparency, accountability, policy advocacy, and collaborative problem-solving. It argues that such education should be accessible, interdisciplinary, participatory, and inclusive, addressing not only citizens but also public officials, policymakers, educators, developers, civil society actors, and professionals.</jats:p>

title: Smart Resilience
container-title: Strategic Planning and Adaptation of Resilient Agri-Food Systems in a Changing World
1daef2626367c084bc117f883f6ea817c3e58afb.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be integrated with strategies for adapting to climate change in the planning of the agricultural and food sectors. The goal is to make food systems more resilient and ensure long-term food security in the country. As climate change, resource shortages, and social and economic inequalities exert increasing pressure on global food systems, the utilization of data and flexible planning methods presents new opportunities for change. This chapter demonstrates how AI tools, such as machine learning, predictive analysis, and geospatial data, can facilitate climate-smart farming by enabling better decision-making, mitigating risks, and enhancing productivity. Examples from India, the Netherlands, and Kenya show how AI has been successfully used to build climate resilience worldwide. The chapter also introduces a new framework, the Data-Driven Strategic Planning Matrix (DSPM), to help match new technologies with fairness and sustainability objectives.</jats:p>

title: AI- and IoT-Driven Sustainable Smart Farming Through Modernizing Traditional Rice Machinery
container-title: Strategic Planning and Adaptation of Resilient Agri-Food Systems in a Changing World
1d19d443915e719ae530b58cbd9a0addd601cbb2.abstract: <jats:p>The combination of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) into the established works in rice farming is a radical change in the direction of sustainable and climatically adapted agriculture. By retrofitting traditional machinery with modular sensors, microcontrollers and edge/cloud AI, real-time data on soil moisture, temperature, crop health and nutrients is available. Intelligent irrigation, intelligent fertilizer prescriptions, and intelligent pest control maximize inputs, minimize labor, fuel, and chemical expenditures, and improve productivity. The chapter relies on secondary data and theoretical analysis, which limits its scope for empirical study. Bangladesh, Indian and Chinese case studies show that real efficiency, cost savings and yield stabilization are achieved. Adoption requires digital literacy, inclusiveness of services, and favorable policies; future research activities must focus on multi-season testing, interoperable systems, and gender-sensitive and sustainable deployment.</jats:p>

title: Explainable AI and ESG-Driven Decision Intelligence for Strategic Leadership in the Creative Economy
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
d8b4eafefe49e40a437d889529cb8c99644dca1c.abstract: <jats:p>As ESG principles and cutting-edge digital innovations intersect in the creative economy, strategic leadership is changing in ways never before imaginable. This chapter discusses the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in supporting ESG-driven decision intelligence by allowing a leader to make transparent, accountable, and data-informed decisions. Based on the Resource Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the chapter advances a conceptual framework that combines explainability, ESG performance measures, and strategic leadership capabilities. The conversation focuses on the benefits of explainable AI for governance, stakeholders' trust, sustainability, and organizational resilience in the creative sector. The chapter also provides future research directions in the context of responsible human-centric AI leaders in the changing digital and sustainability landscapes.</jats:p>

title: Navigating India's ESG–Digital Nexus Through AI-Driven Ethical Transformation
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
22f3457abdf2fffb7ebe5401b54c2f7bc15f8c5c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how India's creative economy might navigate the ESG–Digital Nexus via an AI-driven ethical shift, not just tech for tech's sake. It draws on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Stakeholder Theory, and basically looks at how AI-Driven Digital Capability, Big Data and IoT Integration, Ethical Digital Transformation, Strategic Leadership Agility, ESG Performance, and Sustainable Creative Economy Development connect together. The study uses survey data from 412 professionals, and it then analyses the whole thing with PLS-SEM. The outcome of the study is that AI capabilities and digital integration really do improve ESG performance, but they do it through ethical digital transformation. Strategic leadership agility tends to reinforce these effects, while ESG performance in turn supports sustainable creative economy development. Overall, the chapter stresses that technological experimentation has to be matched with ethical governance and sustainability objectives if India wants long-term competitiveness and responsible digital expansion.</jats:p>

title: Human-Centered Leadership in the Age of AI and Automation
container-title: Evolving Societies and Contemporary Workplace Issues
80fd311f525faf8dbdb5cda66118e610c171be8c.abstract: <jats:p>In the age of AI and automation, organizations need leadership that combines technological advancement with humanity. Human-centered leadership emphasizes empathy, ethics, and inclusiveness to ensure that innovation enriches and does not undermine the human experience at the workplace. As digital systems further impose decision-making, leaders will need to navigate complex ethical dilemmas, facilitate workforce development, and drive trust, culture, flexibility, and psychological safety. This approach requires open communication, equal access to opportunities, and anticipatory action in response to algorithmic discrimination and digital exclusion. This paper, based on international case studies and cross-cutting expertise, considers how leaders across the public, private, and nonprofit sectors are evolving their practices in response to the challenges of digitally reshaping workplaces. This study ends with actionable frameworks, policy guidance, and research directions.</jats:p>

title: Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Preparing Educators for an AI-Enhanced Classroom
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
63c7efe0ab89ec1cedd35e50942f938dfcdd14f9.abstract: <jats:p>The growth in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the classroom is transforming STEM education and the need for teacher preparedness and AI literacy. This chapter explores the influence of teachers' knowledge, skills and attitudes in AI integration in STEM classrooms. It offers approaches to AI literacy, including knowledge of AI concepts, principles, data analysis and pedagogic strategies to use AI technologies for teaching and learning. It explores professional learning programs, communities of practice and continuing education to help teachers thrive in an AI classroom. The chapter also discusses issues of equity of technology use, alignment with current curriculum, change management and the need for equity in access to AI. The chapter discusses successful strategies which have led to better teaching, learning and performance of STEM students through AI literacy. It also offers a guide to how to assess teacher readiness and confidence in using AI, and to promote reflexive teaching and learning.</jats:p>

title: AI Tools for Students
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
89bedececedb8d701eafe8c286aa09d05c376fc6.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become the indispensable element of the modern educational process that offers groundbreaking instruments to make the process more efficient, creative, and productive in terms of learning, creation, and academic achievements. Thoughtfully tutoring systems and customized learning guides are just but few examples of AI applications that are changing how students learn, collaborate and develop the requisite critical skills. Adaptive learning, automated testing and content development have become more effective with the use of AI in education, and has provided learners with an opportunity to engage with the learning content more interactively and meaningfully. Also, AI-based applications can be used to enhance time management, research assistance, and language translation to make the educational process more universal and globalized. The chapter analyses various AI tools that have been student specific and explain their functionality, advantages and its prospects on the learning environments.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Generative AI in STEM Projects
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
8c513f2bce0f9c081423352bfab5b70aee560367.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools—most notably large language models such as ChatGPT—are rapidly reshaping the landscape of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. This chapter examines the dual role of GenAI in STEM project-based learning: as a pedagogical enabler and a source of risk. Drawing on a synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2021 and 2025, the chapter identifies key opportunities including personalized learning, adaptive feedback, scaffolded inquiry, and increased instructional efficiency. It also examines risks such as academic dishonesty, algorithmic bias, data privacy violations, and equity gaps. Ethical frameworks for responsible GenAI integration are proposed, emphasizing AI literacy, transparent policy design, and teacher development. The chapter concludes that sustainable GenAI adoption in STEM requires not just technological fluency, but a principled, equity-centered pedagogical commitment from stakeholders.</jats:p>

title: AI, Collaboration, and Problem-Based Learning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
278cf8d6c69341c913088654ad8a5106e100950e.abstract: <jats:p>The following technologies are changing STEM education, Artificial Intelligence (AI), teamwork, and problem based learning (PBL) transform STEM education by providing interactive learning environments that are student centered. PBL assists learners to solve real life issues using teamwork, critical thinking and interdisciplinary learning. Personalized guidance, real time feedback, data analysis, simulations, and adaptive learning paths enhance this process with the help of AI. It enhances problem solving, creativity and independent learning besides equipping students in future careers in an AI driven world. The most important issues are equal access to technological assets, teacher training, data privacy, and algorithmic bias. Responsible and inclusive use of AI is essential for effective STEM learning.</jats:p>

title: GenVR-DSA
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
11b9b6c10cf0a7ae1f895921564cedcefbf2ef75.abstract: <jats:p>An Interactive VR Platform with GenAI Support for Learning Data Structures is a new educational tool that uses virtual reality to improve the understanding of abstract computer science concepts. The need for such a tool arises from the challenge of understanding abstract concepts of Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) faced by students. This new educational tool combines virtual reality with AI and aims to make the process of understanding data structures more intuitive and interactive. The AI technology will enable the creation of educational content on the fly as students engage with the educational tool. This educational tool will also enable a 3D experience that will allow students to perform various actions on different data structures. The system will provide a multi-sensory experience to the students where they can view as well as perform various actions on the data structures in a 3D reality. The aim of the new educational tool will be to increase the students' understanding of data structures and enable them to implement data structure concepts on a real-world scenario.</jats:p>

title: Connecting AI and Mathematical Thinking
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
476a3c539bb8b90dfc78b8d065ddaa3a938666bc.abstract: <jats:p>A revolutionary paradigm for education is presented by the fusion of AI & mathematics, which promises enhanced teaching strategies, adaptive evaluations, and individualized learning. AI tools can improve student comprehension and engagement by producing various explanations for mathematical topics, customizing learning experiences, and providing instant feedback. AI can also be used by educators to automate administrative duties, which will free up time for student interaction and better instruction. Creation of AI-powered adaptive learning platforms, intelligent tutoring programs, & automated grading tools—all of which can customize math instruction to meet requirements/skills of specific students—is made possible by this confluence. The potential of convergence of AI & mathematics is examined in this chapter, along with the opportunities & problems that result from this integration & its effects on teaching, learning, & evaluation. The way we teach/study maths could be completely transformed by the new paradigm for education brought about by the confluence of AI & maths.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid Minds in the Classroom
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
31efd69d86655a2b3ef454d7a86cbe76c6a4861a.abstract: <jats:p>Affective artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming modern learning environments by enabling systems to perceive, interpret, and respond to student emotions. This chapter explores a hybrid AI framework that integrates symbolic logic with neural networks to enhance emotional understanding and adaptive instruction in the classroom. The symbolic reasoning component provides transparency, rule based interpretability, and structured decision-making, while neural networks contribute perceptual accuracy through multimodal emotion recognition. By combining these complementary strengths, the hybrid model supports more reliable, context aware affective responses that improve student engagement and personalize learning pathways. The chapter presents the conceptual foundations of such hybrid systems, examines their relevance for real-time classroom interaction, and discusses implementation considerations, such as data processing, model integration, and ethical challenges.</jats:p>

title: Big Data Analytics in STEM Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
67098742d715ca31cccbe46cc7ccb35fff23432c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of Big Data Analytics in strengthening student competence in STEM education through predictive analytics and data-driven decision-making. Based on bibliometric mapping of Scopus-indexed publications (2016–2025), it identifies rapid research growth alongside structural concentration and thematic fragmentation. To address this gap, the chapter proposes an integrative framework linking the educational data ecosystem, predictive modeling, early warning systems, and intervention strategies. The framework highlights how predictive analytics enables early identification of at-risk students and supports personalized, adaptive learning. It also emphasizes improvements in both cognitive and non-cognitive outcomes, including problem-solving, persistence, and self-regulated learning. Ethical considerations such as fairness, transparency, and accountability are underscored as essential components in analytics design. Overall, the chapter positions predictive analytics as a responsible decision-support system for advancing inclusive and evidence-based STEM education.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating Critical Thinking in AI-Enhanced STEM Learning Environments
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
b768bdec9eab601fa3c02c0c0a2202ae0ec8d86a.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter provides a quantitative model of assessing critical thinking in AI-enhanced STEM learning setting. The model being proposed converts the AI-generated data in interaction with the student into quantifiable cognitive aspects through feature representation, normalization, and aggregation by multiple criteria. A hybrid weighting framework based on Analytical Hierarchy Process, combined with entropy, will enhance reliability and objectivity. The framework involves optimization, validation, and implementation of algorithms to provide scalability and accuracy. As illustrated through experimental examination, it has proved to be useful in evaluating critical thinking among learners. The research adds a mathematically based, evidence-supported perspective that facilitates real-time assessment, individual learning, and evidence-based decision making in current AI-infused STEM education systems.</jats:p>

title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of AI-Based STEM Learning Program
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
36d963a1d1ee635d82468a869ece86919b1df3b4.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the effectiveness of AI-based STEM learning programs in enhancing students' sustainability competencies, emphasizing the integration of ethics, innovation, and pedagogy into modern education. While numerous studies have examined the role of AI in enhancing engagement and personalization, few have holistically connected it to sustainability literacy and ethical responsibility. This research fills this gap by presenting a comparative-analytical approach to evaluate how AI technologies foster environmental awareness, critical thinking, and complex problem-solving skills essential for sustainability. Based on diverse case studies and empirical insights, the chapter proposes a conceptual framework that aligns AI integration with ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, and inclusivity. The findings highlight both the potential and challenges of AI adoption, including issues of teacher readiness, algorithmic bias, and data privacy.</jats:p>

title: A Comparative Case Study of Evolving Identities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
fca392da578d3680924b771d20282bcf500fd24b.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores how GenAI reshapes BSEd-Mathematics students' mathematical identity and ownership reasoning. Operating at the intersection of self-belief and AI-mediated cognition, this qualitative comparative case study analyzes student narratives based on contrasting GenAI usage styles. The findings reveal that while students view GenAI as a capable yet imperfect “second teacher,” its psychological impact depends on individual metacognitive control. Vulnerable users risk cognitive offloading, volatile confidence, and inadequacy. Conversely, resilient students preserve their math self-concept through textbook mastery and exam accountability. Professional agency is demonstrated through human-first sequencing and strict validation protocols. Ultimately, modern mathematics practitioner is defined not by rote calculation, but by higher-order capacities of structural auditing and pedagogical agency.</jats:p>

title: Learning Mathematics and its Relationship to Future Skills
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
50ef57a4f158de3deb869de87d54c97b66782e15.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the growing role of mathematics education in developing future-oriented skills within the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, including problem solving, critical thinking, creativity, computational thinking, and digital literacy. To address the fragmentation of existing research across cognitive science, STEM education, digital pedagogy, and inclusive practices, this chapter employs a bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review of studies published between 2020 and 2024. A total of 2,667 documents were screened from the Scopus database, of which 35 peer-reviewed articles met the PRISMA criteria for in-depth analysis, supported by VOSviewer mapping techniques. The findings highlight a significant increase in global research interest.</jats:p>

title: Building Ethical AI Competencies in STEM Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
b3fac40fb1116a024584ccb8584bba37de39d35f.abstract: <jats:p>The importance of AI ethics in STEM education is to train future technologists on how to create socially useful and responsible AI systems. It focuses on the incorporation of governance systems, transparency, and responsible innovation into the school curricula. Governance guarantees responsible behavior and ethical control, whereas transparency guarantees trust in the form of explainable and impartial AI systems. Responsible innovation informs the creation of technologies that balance between development and welfare of the society. The inclusion of these principles on every level of STEM education would enable students to think critically to solve the new ethical issues that will arise and make AI progress in accordance with human values and long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Ethical AI in Practice
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
ab5b1bd3683523d5f1774a4ed4666ed3be3f4bbd.abstract: <jats:p>The swift incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education has generated revolutionary prospects for customized learning, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, and automated evaluation. But with these benefits come important ethical issues that have to do with governance, openness, responsibility, prejudice, privacy, and responsible innovation. This chapter looks at how Ethical AI is changing in STEM education by looking at real-world case studies that show both good and bad uses of AI-powered educational technology. The chapter starts by putting AI in the context of modern STEM education systems. It talks about how data-driven decision-making, adaptive learning platforms, and AI-powered analytics are changing the way teachers and students learn. These technologies may lead to better learning and more efficient use of resources, but they also make people worry about things like algorithmic bias, unclear decision-making processes, monitoring of student data, and unfair access to AI tools. The chapter examines how educational institutions, technology creators, and legislators are dealing with the ethical issues that come up when AI is used in schools by looking at a few case studies that focus on institutions, technology, and policy. There is a lot of focus on governance structures that make sure AI-enabled classrooms are accountable and follow the rules. The chapter also analyzes transparency mechanisms such as explainable AI models, open algorithms, and participatory oversight systems that allow educators and students to understand and question automated decisions. The report also emphasizes responsible innovation strategies that incorporate ethical design principles, stakeholder involvement, and fairness concerns along the entire AI development process. The chapter presents a structured framework for the implementation of ethical AI practices in STEM education by integrating insights from several case settings. The results show that ethical governance, clear algorithms, and socially responsible innovation are all necessary to develop trust in AI systems and make sure that everyone has equal access to education. In the end, this chapter adds to ongoing academic debates about AI ethics in education and gives useful advice to politicians, teachers, and tech developers who want to use AI responsibly in STEM learning environments.</jats:p>

title: From Mathematics Anxiety to Critical Thinking
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Cases on Fostering Critical Thinking and Competence in AI-Based STEM Programs
ad3e9ae99bd6b95da9a9e22a916d15f8f8c6e668.abstract: <jats:p>Mathematics anxiety can constrain cognitive engagement and critical thinking in calculus, while Artificial Intelligence (AI) creates opportunities for personalised learning, problem solving, and STEM innovation. This chapter synthesises evidence on mathematics anxiety, critical thinking, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), contextual learning, and AI-supported STEM education through a Systematic Literature Review following PRISMA 2020. Searches across Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, Dimensions, and additional sources identified 2,700 records, with 191 studies meeting the inclusion criteria. The synthesis shows that quantitative studies (58.6%), higher education (72.3%), mathematics education (42.9%), and Asian contexts (46.6%) dominate the literature. Mathematics anxiety emerges as a barrier to cognitive engagement, whereas contextual learning, SDG-oriented tasks, and AI-supported learning can strengthen relevance, problem solving, personalisation, and critical thinking. The chapter positions REALMATH-SDGs as a contextual framework linking affective support, and critical thinking.</jats:p>

title: Unlocking Profits in Generative AI: The Impact of AI Adaptive Learning on Freemium Strategy
container-title: Information Systems Research
1e71b78eb99b705782120789109bb4b568ed47eb.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI firms increasingly rely on freemium strategies, offering a basic service at no charge while charging for a more capable version. Unlike conventional digital products, generative AI systems can improve through user interactions, making free users a potential source of valuable learning data. Using an analytical model, this study shows that freemium is not always the most profitable strategy. Free access can expand the user base and accelerate AI adaptive learning, but it can also cannibalize paid demand and create substantial service costs. More effective adaptive learning does not necessarily make freemium more attractive; under some conditions, the firm earns more by offering only a paid version at a lower price. When freemium is used, a moderate capability gap between free and premium versions can be more profitable than making the free tier either too limited or too close to the premium product. Managers should evaluate learning benefits alongside service costs, market coverage, and premium cannibalization. Policymakers should also avoid assuming that free access automatically improves consumer welfare, because capability gains may allow firms to raise premium prices.</jats:p>

title: Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Attention, Obligation, and the Rootedness of Human Identity in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
e4417ce1339c12cc05dc70011ea7ae674c983fe8.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how the AI renaissance is reconfiguring fundamental anthropological conditions of human existence and how Simone Weil's ethics of attention, obligation, and rootedness can provide a normative framework for understanding these transformations. Methodologically, the analysis combines conceptual reconstruction, philosophical-hermeneutic updating, and critically reflected conceptual engineering to translate Weil's categories into contemporary AI contexts. The analysis identifies three interconnected transformations: AI-mediated environments can reshape the conditions for sustained attention; distributed human-machine agency can create responsibility and obligation gaps; and digital infrastructures can weaken the conditions for social, economic, and political rootedness. The chapter develops a Weilian governance framework that deepens human-centered AI by identifying the anthropological conditions that underlie rights, human oversight, accountability, and participation.</jats:p>

title: Human Rights in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
b6cc6cdaede90b65d88551af1e19e431b12e7088.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is an innovation that is fast changing society, economy, and government structures. Although it is extremely advantageous, it also triggers the issue of human rights, fairness, and accountability. This chapter focuses on the discussion of the manner in which human rights will be protected in the ascendancy of AI. It raises the red flag over perilous algorithms, the absence of transparency and surveillance technologies proliferation. Legal frameworks and considerations that can be used to steer innovation towards dignity, equality, and justice are also addressed. Healthcare, employment, policing case studies gives an example of how AI affects the basic freedom. The chapter proposes a right based regulation of AI, stating that innovation should be moderated and should not harm people and society. It concludes with the policy suggestions that can make AI advocacy to social justice and maintain human freedoms.</jats:p>

title: From High-Level Ethics to Actionable Measures
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f6df0e82bb922344b07c7ca3d990ca38bb2a53f5.abstract: <jats:p>The active evolution of technology has led to new changes, and one of the trends that has become topical and actively discussed within the academic community and society in general is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Nevertheless, it has turned out that the data on which AI systems are built is not always neutral. This has resulted in cases where AI systems replicate and reinforce existing societal biases. At this point, no specific case law exists to cover the issues related to AI, so ethical frameworks have been developed. Such frameworks typically define top-level principles aimed at guaranteeing the credibility and justice of AI-based systems. However, principles such as explainability and accountability are frequently criticised because they are too abstract, as they do not provide any tangible measures that would guarantee their proper adoption. To develop recommendations on actions that can be taken to address these two principles, a qualitative literature review focusing on these themes has been conducted.</jats:p>

title: Reconfiguring Identity, Ownership, and Legal Framework in the Digital World
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f0a6336edb0b64a20e417a3a4a4f176bb513d8c1.abstract: <jats:p>Humankind's lived reality of an experience heavily mediated by Generative AI and the digital realm calls for a critical reconfiguration of existing social modes of being as well as legal contracts and regulations. The chapter attempts to address significant challenges presented by AI and AI-generated content specifically within literary creation in terms of copyright and ownership as well as legal systems pertaining to digital personhood and identity. A reworking of the traditional understanding of authorship and creativity also traces the inadequacy of existing global legal frameworks, largely anthropocentric in nature, grappling with the dilemma of attributing ownership and accountability for AI-generated creative content and prosecution of AI entities. The chapter also explores digital personhood with specific focus on the idea of digital necromancy and sophisticated AI crime as a threat to the world at large. The aim is to raise questions that could foster dialogue and initiate some form of policy change in the aforementioned realms.</jats:p>

title: Binary Biases
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
10d2652f77e6a8ecef648ea24ba8c77df85691ea.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of AI in content moderation raises major challenges in detecting hate speech and introduces new biases. This chapter explores the limits of binary classification models in addressing the complex nature of online hate. Standard machine learning methods often miss cultural context, evolving language, and the fine line between free speech and harmful speech, leading to unfair outcomes for marginalized groups. Through a mixed-method study using SVMs, deep learning, and transformer models on multilingual datasets, we reveal flaws in current systems. Findings show frequent mislabeling of cultural expressions, racial and gender gaps, and declining accuracy as language shifts. Qualitative evidence highlights social harms, including silencing advocacy and reinforcing discrimination. We stress the need for culturally aware, transparent detection and propose hybrid human–AI moderation to protect users while supporting democratic rights.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Labor, Employment Contracts, and Professional Identity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
34add7a445929817b91d0a85a92c50bba7824908.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping labor, employment contracts, and professional identity. It argues that AI is not merely automating tasks but transforming the nature of work through automation, new job categories, and human-AI collaboration. It analyzes the rise of platform labor and algorithmic management, the legal-ethical challenges of bias, transparency, and accountability, and the tension between flexibility and precarity. It explores identity shifts requiring reskilling, lifelong learning, and psychological adaptation. Policy, regulation, and collective bargaining frameworks are evaluated alongside case studies across sectors and regions. The chapter outlines scenarios for the future of work and calls for renewed social contracts that safeguard equity, inclusion, and meaningful human agency.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Electronic Health Record
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
160b86d6f7ca4a0340314e88b523dcae1039a032.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital in healthcare, especially in training medical officers for disease analysis and patient care. In diagnostics, AI algorithms enhance image interpretation accuracy and enable disease prediction like cancer and retinopathy. These modules analyze imaging data like MRIs, CT scans, and X-rays to identify nerve and cell injuries. In therapeutics, AI aids drug discovery by finding molecular interactions and optimizing trials, reducing time and costs. AI-based robotic systems enhance surgical precision and limit invasiveness. AI benefits healthcare management through predictive analytics for resource allocation and supply chain optimization. AI-powered chatbots provide 24/7 patient support and handle remote consultations. AI and IoT-enabled hospital-at-home modules allow home treatment, reducing facility strain. However, AI in healthcare raises ethical concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, and healthcare disparities. While AI develops, its limitations and transformative potential remain crucial for effective, equitable healthcare models.</jats:p>

title: Exploring ChatGPT-Assisted Qualitative Data: Comparing Human and AI-Assisted Coding Using Braun and Clarke’s Thematic Analysis
container-title: American Journal of Qualitative Research
d1da3462e4a00cf9a9e2a1ed853867d5195ec143.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en"><i>The use of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, has significantly expanded across academia and research in recent years. Of growing interest is AI’s potential role in qualitative research, especially in expediting tasks such as literature review and synthesis, data management and coding, and manuscript preparation, all while striving to maintain the rigor expected of qualitative inquiry. This paper explores the degree of alignment between AI-generated thematic analysis and a traditional, manual approach to analyzing focus group data and potential uses of AI in qualitative research. Using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis framework, a publicly available focus group dataset was analyzed in three stages: (1) Data Familiarization, (2) Human-Led Thematic Analysis, and (3) AI-Generated Analysis using ChatGPT. The human coders followed all six phases of the framework prior to engaging with the AI, to prevent influence from AI-generated output. The comparison revealed partial overlap between the human and AI-generated categories, particularly at the level of broader categories and themes. However, ChatGPT’s analysis tended to reflect a more superficial reading of the data, lacking the interpretive depth and nuance demonstrated by the human coders. While AI tools like ChatGPT show potential for supporting certain aspects of qualitative analysis, this study highlights key limitations in their ability to fully replicate the complexity and contextual understanding that human-led analysis provides. Further exploration is needed to define appropriate and ethical roles for AI in qualitative research workflows.</i></jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: A TOE–RBV–TBL Integrated Model of AI-Enabled Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
40d1fa5cdd6cd6c42b1d66704eea0c7b9caed768.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping food logistics by enhancing operational efficiency, reducing waste, and promoting sustainable supply chain practices. This study develops and validates an integrated Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE), Resource-Based View (RBV), and Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework to examine the determinants and outcomes of AI-enabled sustainable food logistics. Primary data were collected from 312 professionals in India's food supply chain and analysed using CB-SEM. The findings reveal that technological readiness, organisational capability, and environmental pressure significantly drive AI adoption, while AI capability positively influences environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The study offers a comprehensive theoretical framework and practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to build resilient, intelligent, and sustainable food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Cold Chain Optimization for Reducing Food Loss in Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
f7b19d3fb02e51972e9a5e5f799a5064e20516bb.abstract: <jats:p>With the combination of IoT-based monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making, AI-powered optimization of cold-chains increases the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of perishable chains. Sensors can provide real-time data, therefore, monitoring the temperature, humidity, and logistics status continuously and predict risks of spoilage and optimizing routing, storage, and inventory control with AI models. In case studies in dairy, seafood and fresh produce, there has been a substantial decrease in the spoilage and increased efficiency in work. Traceability and compliance are additionally improved with the help of the blockchain integration. In general, cold-chain systems with AI will help minimize food waste, advance food quality, and sustain logistics in complicated supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Quality Monitoring and Food Safety Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
2f988859afeb8045e1f8933ad6d0b777eed57974.abstract: <jats:p>AI has transformation in the area of food quality inspection and safety management due to the capabilities that have been introduced in rapid, precise, non-destructive and predictive assessment of food quality through the production process, processing, storage, transport, retailing and consumption. These techniques are applicable in fast monitoring and quick intervention in areas of dairy products, meat products, seafood, fruits and vegetables, cereals, beverages and ready to eat meals. This chapter discusses the principles, technologies, applications, benefits, challenges, and future prospects of AI-based food quality monitoring and safety management, with particular emphasis on intelligent sensors, real-time contamination detection, automated inspection, shelf-life prediction, process optimization, traceability, and predictive risk management across diverse food sectors.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Predictive Analytics for Sustainable Demand Forecasting in Agri-Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
ae908a7d83acc41af9c9be1d1de1a65faa9f8570.abstract: <jats:p>Predictive analytics, which is an AI technology, is changing the logistics of agri-foods by enhancing sustainability and demand forecasting. The conventional predictive approaches do not normally reflect their dynamic aspects, including weather fluctuations, market behavior and consumer behaviors, resulting into inefficiencies and food wastage. This chapter describes an AI-based framework that combines multi-source data, machine learning models, and decision support systems to come up with correct and real-time demand forecasts. The strategy facilitates optimal inventory control, effective distribution strategy, and minimized environmental concerns. There are enormous evidences of case studies showing enhancement of accuracy in forecasts, reduction of wastes, and efficiency in the operations. The results address the possible opportunities of AI assisting the resilient, adaptive, and sustainable food supply chains in the fast-changing global food system.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Innovations in Agri-Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
700ec2c44d31bcf14cea8b84c21efb4ae0bd8c73.abstract: <jats:p>Algorithms and other AI tools are increasingly being used to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and resilience of the Integrated Agri-food Supply Chain (IASC) across several areas of the agri-food sector. Innovations enabled by using AI technologies in agri-food systems referred to in this chapter are the ones that will achieve the best production, processing, distribution and consumption. The predictive analytics, machine learning, and intelligence-supporting tools are all about ensuring that requirements are always checked and predictable, resources are deployed,, and risk minimisation is done in real time. AI and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain platforms, and automated logistics are explored, and the potential for creating transparent, traceable supply chains that adapt to fluctuating demand and supply is investigated. Case studies have been presented that show successful applications and improvements in productivity, waste minimisation,, and operational costs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Driven Real-Time Route Optimization for Dynamic Food Logistics and Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
a3d254406bb275561bb5d6e8d0065c094ec34437.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter describes how to use real-time data analytics and machine learning to automatically simulate and execute alternative food logistics routes to predict supply chain bottlenecks (such as supplier failures or natural disasters) before they occur. Based on academic publications from 2024 to 2026, the chapter uses a systematic review and thematic content analysis. The findings show that AI and data analytics are transforming food logistics and supply chains into sustainable, efficient, and creative transportation. Traditional logistics systems suffer from poor order consolidation, low truck capacity utilization, static route planning, and significant environmental impacts. Efficiency losses increase operational expenses, delay supply, and increase carbon emissions, threatening sustainability. Cloud-based data platforms and reinforcement learning optimize logistics and route planning. Logistics sustainability demands data-driven decision-making and clever automation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
1ca0d752e991777e60571046cca42e7e93889d3a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of agri-food supply chains through artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing sustainable food logistics, resilience, and human resource management (HRM). It highlights how AI-driven technologies such as machine learning, IoT, and predictive analytics enable real-time decision-making, demand forecasting, and supply chain optimization, thereby reducing food waste and improving efficiency. The study integrates sustainability dimensions—environmental, economic, and social—with resilience strategies to address disruptions and uncertainties. Furthermore, it explores the critical role of HRM in facilitating workforce transformation, human–AI collaboration, and organizational change. An integrated AI–Sustainability–HRM framework is proposed to enhance adaptability and long-term performance. The chapter contributes to theory and practice by presenting a holistic, data-driven approach to building intelligent, resilient, and sustainable food logistics systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Food Waste Reduction in India's Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
fc88c02780841f38b3f41c69dae42b101d38d76a.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we focus on the role that AI-driven predictive analytics can play to assist with forecast accuracy, cold-chain orchestration, quality monitoring and speed of response upstream and downstream through the farm-to-market flows to abete food loss and waste in India´s perishable supply chains. It relies on a systematic secondary empirical synthesis of India-centric studies, policy papers, and analytics research on global experience pertaining to high perishability classes of vegetables, dairy, fish, and other fresh fruits. The chapter proves that besides infrastructural hurdles, food waste challenges of India is also a challenge of timing, visibility and coordination. Evidence from India reveals how much of the loss occurs is seasonally driven, how losses are correlated with harvest volume, storage, transport reliability, and the quality sorting and practices. This chapter presents a predictive analytics framework for agri-logistics, suggests how Indian firms and policymakers can implement the approach, and claims that digital traceability.</jats:p>

title: Predictive Business Intelligence Architectures for Cold-Chain Logistics Mitigating Food Waste Through AI-Driven IoT Sensor Integration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
791f2efff6e75d93d6ead2cbd5779a343d5628c2.abstract: <jats:p>Food loss and waste in cold-chain logistics result not only from refrigeration failures, but also from fragmented data, delayed responses, and weak coordination across supply-chain actors. This chapter presents an IGI-style conceptual and implementation framework for predictive business intelligence (BI) in cold-chain logistics. It argues that waste reduction is more effective when Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, event-driven data integration, and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics are designed as a layered architectural capability rather than as stand-alone monitoring tools. Drawing on literature in cold-chain management, food quality, wireless sensing, BI, predictive analytics, AI-enabled supply chains, and digital twins, the chapter shows how variables such as temperature, humidity, location, door events, shock, dwell time, and product condition can be transformed into risk scores, dynamic shelf-life estimates, prioritized exceptions, and closed-loop decisions. It also proposes architecture and seven implementation workstreams for deployment.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Cold Chain Management Using AI and IoT
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
60daab0ba3149ca77331fc247ab25917cceed633.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is fundamentally reshaping cold chain logistics, enabling unprecedented levels of precision, transparency, and sustainability. This chapter examines how intelligent sensing, predictive analytics, blockchain-based traceability, and digital twin simulation collectively address the chronic inefficiencies of temperature-sensitive supply chains. Drawing on recent empirical and review studies, the chapter presents an integrated framework that links real-time data acquisition to AI-driven decision-making and blockchain-anchored accountability. Key themes include spoilage prevention, carbon footprint reduction, regulatory compliance, and consumer trust. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on challenges and emerging directions for scalable, equitable, and ethically grounded cold chain transformation.</jats:p>

title: Digital Skills and Professional Judgment in AI-Driven Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
fa94d39fbd808cc46e56a32eb78b60762c9d5124.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping financial decision-making by altering how information is analyzed, interpreted, and translated into professional judgment. This chapter examines the role of digital skills in determining whether AI strengthens or undermines the quality and accountability of financial decisions. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature, the chapter conceptualizes digital skills as cognitive–governance capabilities that extend beyond technical proficiency to include critical interpretation, calibrated reliance on AI, explainability, professional skepticism, and ethical judgment. Particular attention is given to automation bias, accountability risks, and the organizational conditions that shape human–AI interaction. The chapter concludes that responsible AI-enabled financial decision-making depends not on algorithmic capability alone, but on the alignment of digital competence, professional judgment, and effective governance.</jats:p>

title: From Financial Accountant to Digital Finance Architect
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
301bb7a811700c54a3c8f72796dd343a397ed320.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyzes the digital transformation of the finance function as a structural reconfiguration of processes, decision-making logic, and governance. It demonstrates how automation, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and RegTech are shifting traditional job profiles from process execution to the architectural design of digital financial systems. On this basis, the Digital Finance Competency Architecture (DFCA) is developed, integrating technological, data-analytical, governance-related, and strategic-cognitive competencies. The analysis illustrates that effective performance in digital finance environments requires systemic competence, i.e., the ability to translate data, models, and regulatory requirements into coherent decision-making architectures. Finally, implications for education, organization, and governance are discussed, and the Digital Finance Architect is established as a new professional role model.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Financial Decision Support for Handicraft Artisans
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
1d34157c42ec302960b797359d16b132c9fe0d28.abstract: <jats:p>Handicraft artists play an important role in conserving cultural and social history while also contributing to the growth of their respective economies. It contributes four to five percent to the world economy and creates a huge number of job opportunities in the neighbourhood. Handicraft workers contribute to societal innovation in the shape of innovative work methods, techniques, and so on. This area sheds light on the hidden talents and abilities of craft workers. However, their salary and economic situation do not allow for this. They are frequently confronted with issues and obstacles such as limited market access, intense rivalry from major companies, a lack of technology, and a communication gap. The article focuses on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to solve difficulties for the handicraft industry. Primary data were acquired from 120 handicraft workers for the study using a structured questionnaire, including demographic information, production costs, profit from their company, and numerous problems they encounter.</jats:p>

title: AI and Predictive Analytics in Performance Monitoring
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
6734ced4b1406c8f7437d78ac9138a400a2eaba5.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics have revolutionized supply chain performance monitoring by enabling real-time visibility, proactive risk management, and data-driven decision-making.
