title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
95a62b89e12f29ec2d10ee4b3bff78918b9670c6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical communication skills are a core yet complex competency in medical education and practice. However, early-stage medical students often struggle to apply communication frameworks in practice due to limited opportunities for structured simulation training. Generative AI (GenAI)–supported training has the potential to offer a scalable and innovative approach for clinical communication skills training.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined the longitudinal development of medical students’ clinical communication skills over 1 academic year and investigated whether AI-powered simulation contributed to differential improvement relative to conventional training. In addition, the study explored motivational, behavioral, and affective mechanisms associated with communication skills development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A nonblinded randomized controlled design was used at a medical school in the United Kingdom, with students assigned either to the control group (n=28, 56%) or to the AI group (n=22, 44%), who practiced with SimPatient, a patient-simulator chatbot accessed through a web browser. Communication skills performance was assessed using standardized objective structured clinical examinations (OSCE) scores relative to the pass marks to enable comparison across time points. Paired t tests and difference-in-differences (DID) analyses were conducted between groups and over time to examine changes in communication skills. Latent change score modeling was used to identify predictors of communication skills change. Sentiment analysis was conducted on 6120 comments from AI-student conversations. Finally, a system quality survey was used to assess participants’ feedback on the AI-powered simulator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Latent change score modeling showed that gains in intrinsic motivation and behavioral learning were significant predictors of students’ communication skills change. The AI group showed a greater descriptive increase in communication skills than the control group, yet the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Within the AI group, consultations whose lexical tone trended more strongly toward resolution (consultation tone) were descriptively associated with communication skills improvement; given the small subsample (n=17), this finding is reported as exploratory. The AI group’s confidence level in AI use was negatively associated with communication skills improvement, while the group nevertheless reported a generally high level of satisfaction with the system.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, medical students’ clinical communication skills increased over the academic year, with this development most strongly associated with their motivation and behavioral engagement; the AI-supported group did not differ significantly from conventional training. The simulator responded appropriately and provided a usable environment for practicing foundational communication behaviors but was limited in capturing the affective complexity, vulnerability, and narrative unpredictability of real clinical encounters. In conclusion, this study suggests that GenAI holds promise for supporting foundational clinical communication training and providing positive practice environments, thereby fostering motivation and behavioral engagement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Health Tool Implementation in Clinical Practice Settings: Umbrella Review
container-title: JMIR AI
ed6b7c7bd88c542620745d58d7720ce6fb1ecaf8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI has the potential to improve clinical decision-making, efficiency, and patient outcomes, yet adoption in routine clinical practice has been slower than anticipated. While prior studies have identified factors that influence AI implementation, a comprehensive synthesis grounded in implementation science frameworks is lacking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to qualitatively and comprehensively describe barriers and facilitators to AI implementation in clinical care settings using an implementation science determinants framework, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), and to identify AI-specific determinants not fully captured by CFIR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted an umbrella review of reviews examining determinants of AI implementation in clinical practice. In accordance with the PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews) reporting guidance, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for English-language reviews published between January 2013 and July 2025. Reviews were included if they addressed barriers to and facilitators of implementing AI-enabled digital health tools in clinical care settings. Determinants were deductively mapped to the updated CFIR and inductively analyzed to identify emergent AI-specific constructs. Review quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklist, and overlap among primary studies was evaluated using the GROOVE (Graphical Representation of Overlap for Overviews) tool.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-two reviews published between 2021 and 2025 were included, encompassing studies conducted from 1990 to 2025. Reviews varied in design, including systematic, scoping, rapid, narrative, and literature reviews. Overall review quality was mixed, with 9 (41%) reviews rated at 100% quality and 4 (18%) at 50% or lower. Primary study overlap was slight, with a corrected covered area of 0.4%. Determinants of AI implementation were identified across all CFIR domains. Prominent barriers at the innovation level included limited evidence of clinical impact, poor interpretability, complexity, lack of adaptability, and insufficiently representative data. Facilitators included perceived relative advantage, co-design with clinicians, and evidence of local clinical benefit. At the implementer level, low AI literacy, limited confidence, time constraints, and concerns about professional displacement were common barriers, while training and technical support facilitated adoption. Inner setting barriers included inadequate infrastructure, limited resources, poor workflow compatibility, and weak governance structures. Outer setting barriers included unclear policies, laws, and liability frameworks, whereas partnerships and cross-sector collaboration were frequent facilitators. Inductively identified AI-specific determinants included transparency, trust, accountability, model bias, data governance, model maintenance, robustness, generalizability, existential threat, and concern about loss of the human element in care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI implementation in clinical settings is shaped by complex, multilevel, and AI-specific determinants that extend beyond traditional digital health considerations. Implementation science frameworks can be adapted to incorporate these constructs. Tailored, theory-informed strategies addressing technical, organizational, psychological, and regulatory factors are essential to support safe, equitable, and sustainable integration of AI into clinical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Beyond binary AI text detection: Partial authorship, source-text similarity, and an integrated threshold model of detectability
container-title: International Review of Applied Sciences and Engineering
acc924b3d1c0e2463fe1a308d503fda2a23b1d77.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study investigates AI text detection under conditions that more closely reflect real-world writing practices than conventional binary human-versus-AI benchmarks. Rather than treating authorship as a dichotomy, detectability is examined as a function of partial AI authorship, source-text similarity, and generator heterogeneity. Ten pre-LLM, human-written English scientific abstracts were used as reference texts, from which four authorship states (H100, AI50, AI75, and AI100) were constructed through controlled rewriting and paragraph-level mixing. AI-generated content was produced using four large language models: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and LLaMA. Detection outputs from Turnitin and GPTZero were evaluated using non-parametric statistics, correlation analysis, and logistic threshold modeling. The results demonstrate that fully human and fully AI-rewritten texts are statistically distinguishable: median AI scores increased from 0 in H100 to 53 in AI100 for Turnitin (
                    <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>
                    = 49.5,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001) and from 0 to 11 for GPTZero (
                    <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>
                    = 61.0,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001), although AI-generated texts did not constitute a homogeneous class. Detectability also varied significantly across the four nominal authorship states for both Turnitin (H = 30.39,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001) and GPTZero (H = 21.77,
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    < 0.001), and systematically with source-text similarity and the generating model. Turnitin showed greater sensitivity than GPTZero to changes in nominal AI proportion and transformation intensity, particularly under mixed-authorship conditions. Significant generator-dependent differences were also observed, with Gemini outputs generally receiving higher AI-detection scores than ChatGPT or LLaMA outputs. The main methodological contribution is the Integrated Detectability Threshold Model (IDTM), which represents detection probability as a joint function of nominal AI proportion and transformation intensity. Within the present sample, the model identified a similarity transition range of approximately 63–66%, below which Turnitin-based detection became more likely than non-detection. These findings support a shift from binary AI classification toward a threshold- and risk-sensitive interpretation of AI text detectability.
                  </jats:p>

title: Emotional Intelligence and Mental Well-Being in AI-Driven Hospitality
container-title: Experience Economy Insights on Human-Centric Hospitality 5.0
53a8b9399dccecdf1d6c3cc1543b58d05b5ccf4c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and digital service systems within the hospitality sector has ushered in an era known as Hospitality 5.0. While these advancements enhance efficiency, personalization, and guest satisfaction, they also increase emotional labor, psychological strain, and occupational stress among employees. This chapter analyzes, using major theories and frameworks, how emotional intelligence and mental well-being mediate sustainable workforce outcomes in AI-intensive hospitality. An original conceptual model, the Emotionally Sustainable Hospitality Workforce Model (ESHWM), is introduced, highlighting sustainable HRM as critical for maintaining emotional and psychological health amid digital disruption. The chapter summarizes empirical evidence linking AI adoption to increased workplace stress and shows how high emotional intelligence protects and boosts frontline hospitality worker performance. Practical implications are offered for managers, HR practitioners, and policymakers, aligning with UN SDGs 3, 8, and 9.</jats:p>

title: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists
container-title: JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies
c5049fe9025dc797144b0755cc5c8f46a237bd87.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
fe8ffd10b2aac6d85d74d4e0e162424399ee26ab.abstract:
<jats:p>As technology continues to evolve rapidly, the future of small business holds immense promise and potential. Though uncertainty and risk are key issues for both large companies and small businesses, in recent times applying new technology may allow for a better characterisation of uncertainty and reduce risk in small business decision-making.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The curated chapters cover topics including: business models, social innovation, green innovation, firm resilience, industry 5.0 and many more. The diverse chapter authors from around the world provide in-depth information on innovative behaviour and future trends in eco-innovation, frugal innovation, and AI innovation by entrepreneurs and small business and gather academic recommendations from research on innovation adaptations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The series Emerald Studies in Sustainable Innovation Management aims at exploring the advancements of innovation management in turbulent times with a special attention to the transition towards a sustainable economy. The practice of innovation management is evolving rapidly as a consequence of positive phenomena such as digitalization and the green transition and negative ones such as crises and global emergencies.</jats:p>

title: Exploring the Impact of Sustainable-Oriented Innovation Practices on Competitiveness of Listed Indigenous Small Businesses in West Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
58c0bfabdb27354497e128f229483d2ad85bd894.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In the current landscape, where businesses are propelled by fast changes, their survival relies on their capacity to engage in sustainable development via innovation. Sustainable-oriented innovation practices have sparked significant academic and research interest because it is a vital pillar. Therefore, the objective of this study is to examine the impact of sustainable-oriented innovation practices on the competitiveness of listed indigenous small businesses in Nigeria. The descriptive survey design was used, and the study population comprised staff of listed small businesses in Nigeria. A closed-ended questionnaire was designed and administered, and 421 were retrieved, representing a ninety-five percent (95%) response rate. The hypothesis was tested which showed the relationship between variables and define the effect of sustainable-oriented innovation practices on competitiveness. The findings show that sustainable-oriented innovation practices of listed indigenous small businesses impact their competitiveness. Specifically, the results showed that sustainable-oriented innovation practices contribute significantly to the competitiveness of listed indigenous small businesses in Nigeria (β = 0.465, t-statistics = 2.698 &gt; 1.96, p-value = 0.000 &lt; 0.05). The path coefficient of 0.465 implies a moderate and positive correlation between sustainable-oriented innovation practices and competitiveness. This study recommends that listed indigenous small businesses should foster an organizational culture that values creativity, experimentation and lifelong learning. In this scenario, sustainable-oriented innovation practices become a strategic priority for competitiveness and businesses seeking to achieve a competitive advantage.</jats:p>

title: Embracing Circularity: How Indian Small Businesses Are Redefining Sustainability
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
388e1a6a49f44beb29afa76ae81569d60c6bed87.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>On account of resource insufficiency and polluted environmental situations, companies in India have adopted the principles of circular economy to gain sustainable development. In the present study, an attempt has been made to investigate the practice of circular economy principles by small companies in India by emphasizing more on the pros and cons of the concept. For the purpose of this chapter, case studies of the companies that have adopted circular economy practices were considered. The outcome of this study provides guidelines about the integration of the principles of circular economy model into their business operations. This research also gives suggestions about the support required from change agents in order to make this framework a sustainable economic model.</jats:p>

title: Climate and Digital Transitions Among Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in Africa: The Role of Development Finance Institutions
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
8b27d253570775e220ff4e8a070d64f9459a0838.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this chapter, the authors examine the role of Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) in enhancing climate and digital transitions among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The authors iterate the crucial role of these transitions in achieving resilience, competitiveness and sustainability among MSMEs’ amid evolving global challenges. Additionally, the authors explain the importance of DFIs in providing critical financial and technical assistance, enabling MSMEs to adopt climate-smart technologies and embrace digital transformation. The authors also highlight case studies illustrating successful DFI interventions. This chapter concludes by emphasising the need for DFIs to prioritise outreach to marginalised communities, balancing developmental goals with financial sustainability and capacity building to scale their impact.</jats:p>

title: Understanding the Adoption of Renewable Energy Among Small Businesses in Africa: Evidence From Nigeria
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
b689d46e93f9663cc17810b561c17cc8034a38eb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The adoption of renewable energy technologies has gained growing attention in Africa due to increasing electricity shortages and rising energy costs. This chapter investigates the drivers and barriers to solar energy adoption among small businesses in Nigeria as a lens to understand the broader African context. The study used cross-sectional data collected from 150 small enterprises located across major cities. The authors found that only 22% of small businesses have adopted solar energy, with income identified as the primary driver of adoption (Z = 2.12, p = 0.034). As the firms had an estimated business value of ₦750,000 ($625) and an average workforce of four employees, the average monthly revenue was found to be ₦277,000 ($231), while the average monthly expenditures of ₦17,420 ($15) and ₦20,608 ($17) were incurred on electricity and fuel, respectively. Financial constraints emerged as the major barrier, highlighted by 82% of respondents. To address this challenge, the respondents (77%) recommended government-subsidized solar energy initiatives to accelerate solar energy transition among small-scale enterprises in Africa. These findings underscore the potential of financial incentives to enhance solar energy adoption. This chapter provides critical insights for policymakers aiming to promote renewable energy adoption in developing economies.</jats:p>

title: Disruptive Technology and Market Performance: The Role of Market Capability and Resource Orchestration Capability in Small Business
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
19aafbbeb67a23759acb6e57352235f544a24704.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter explores the role of disruptive technologies in enhancing the market performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This chapter also investigates the mediating effect of the market capability and resource orchestration capability (ROC) on the disruptive technology-market performance. Through a positivist lens, this chapter employs the deductive approach in data collection and analysis. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was employed to analyse data from 327 SMEs owner/managers. Results reveal that disruptive technologies significantly and positively influence market performance in emerging markets while both market capability and ROC mediate the relationship. SMEs in emerging markets need to improve their marketing and resource orchestration capabilities, as these are essential mediators in the interaction of disruptive technology and market performance.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Disruptive Innovation and Business Performance in Small Businesses in Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
3c4517a910cdfaf09c7b5b7cd9e6af10f41d05cb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examined the impact of disruptive innovation on the business performance of small businesses in Africa, with a focus on Southwest Nigeria. This chapter adopted a descriptive quantitative survey research design. Primary data were collected through a structured, closed-ended questionnaire distributed online. The population of the study, which also serves as the sample size, includes 282 owners and managers of small businesses in the southwest Nigeria. The purposive sampling technique was adopted, and the data were analyzed using a multiple regression analysis. The findings of this chapter show that there is a significant positive relationship between disruptive innovation and business performance (r = 0.52, p-value &lt;0.05, Sig 0.000). Also, there is a significant impact of market competitiveness on business performance (β = is 0.518, p-value &lt;0.05, Sig 0.000). This study concludes that small businesses need to prioritize investing in market competitiveness and technology adoption to maintain a competitive advantage in the global market. This chapter also recommends that small businesses should prioritize the adoption of technologies and market competitiveness to enhance operational efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Disruptive Technologies and Small Business Innovation Efficiency in West Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
4070bc2b188e534881e72bcf35de3b1a3949cc06.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examined the impact of disruptive technologies on small business innovation efficiency in West Africa. Guided by three objectives, this chapter identified the drivers and enablers of technology adoption, assessed the impact of disruptive technologies on innovation efficiency and analyzed the barriers to adoption. A qualitative approach included a literature review and case study examination. The collected data were from several sources, including government reports, industry research and peer-reviewed publications. The results showed that government policy, market competitiveness and digital infrastructure were significant accelerators for technology adoption. Case studies from Nigeria and Ghana showed how favourable settings helped mobile platforms, artificial intelligence and blockchain usage, enhancing operational efficiency, cost savings and service delivery. Adoption was hampered, especially in conventional industries, by high implementation costs, lack of technical knowledge and data security issues, among other obstacles. Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations Theory clarified adoption trends by stressing the need for external facilitators to overcome impediments. Although disruptive technologies might significantly increase innovation efficiency, this chapter found that more widespread adoption relied on strategic government assistance and competitive marketplaces and enhanced digital infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Implications of Green Technology Innovation in Sustainable Organizational Environment
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
84a25cde6e843092039826c464fcb47a0566a551.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The integration of green technology innovations in organizational practices is a critical driver of sustainability in today’s business landscape. As environmental concerns intensify, organizations are increasingly recognizing the need to adopt green technologies to reduce their environmental footprint while ensuring long-term economic viability. This study is aimed to analyze the implications of the green technology innovation on the sustainable organizational environment. It is assumed that a sustainable organizational environment can be affected by the promotion and development of green technology innovation. The methods used are meta-analytical, reflective, and descriptive based on the review of the conceptual, theoretical, and empirical literature. It examines how adopting energy-efficient systems, renewable energy solutions, waste reduction technologies, and eco-friendly production processes can enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and improve corporate reputation. Furthermore, this chapter discusses the role of green technologies in driving innovation and fostering a culture of sustainability within organizations. The analysis concludes that there are direct implications between the green technology innovation and the sustainability of the organizational environment. The implications of green technology adoption extend beyond environmental impact, influencing organizational behavior, stakeholder engagement, and long-term strategic planning. By embracing green technologies, organizations can align their business goals with global sustainability objectives, positioning themselves as leaders in the transition toward a more sustainable and resilient economy.</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence and Technological Innovations for SDG 9
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
4291b1d07c6c301ea5093a1541103751eefcaea7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The accelerating advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and technological innovations presents transformative opportunities for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 9 (SDG 9), which emphasizes building resilient infrastructure, promoting inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fostering innovation. Despite growing global attention, the integration of AI and emerging technologies into industrial development strategies, especially in developing economies, remains limited and uneven. As AI and emerging technologies transform industries and economies, their potential to advance SDG 9 is still largely untapped. This chapter explores the transformative impact of AI and technological innovations on the three pillars of SDG 9 through a series of case studies. The findings indicate that AI-driven solutions such as predictive maintenance for infrastructure, smart manufacturing systems and data-driven innovation ecosystems greatly improve efficiency, minimize resource waste and broaden access to industrial opportunities. However, several challenges remain, including the digital divide, ethical dilemmas associated with AI deployment and inadequate policy frameworks to ensure equitable benefits. The research emphasizes the necessity of collaboration among governments, industries, and civil society to scale AI applications while addressing inequalities in technological access and promoting sustainable practices. By recommending actionable strategies for integrating AI into national industrialization agendas and innovation policies, this study aims to bridge the gap between technological potential and the implementation of SDG 9. Ultimately, it advocates for a balanced approach that harnesses AI’s capabilities to create resilient systems, empower marginalized communities, and drive sustainable industrial growth, ensuring that technological advancements align with the inclusive and environmentally conscious principles of the 2030 Agenda.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Innovation EdTech Startups: A Bibliographic Review of Industry 5.0’s Implications for Sustainable Growth
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
65db5ccadd16a00e3aac401ac37197f7b011310f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter presents a systematic bibliographic review, investigating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in fostering innovation within Educational Technology (EdTech) startups, contextualized within the human-centric and sustainable framework of Industry 5.0. Analyzing 42 scholarly works published between 2014 and 2024, this chapter explores the alignment of AI-driven entrepreneurial ventures in education with the core tenets of sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity. The findings reveal a complex landscape where technological innovation, while promising personalized learning and operational scalability, often exacerbates ethical dilemmas, regulatory gaps, and the digital divide. This chapter identifies a critical tension between rapid, profit-driven technological adoption and the deliberate, value-led innovation advocated by Industry 5.0. It concludes that for AI-powered EdTech startups to truly contribute to sustainable growth, a fundamental shift is required, from a paradigm of disruptive techno-solutionism to one of responsible innovation. This necessitates collaborative governance, ethically conscious design, and entrepreneurial models that prioritize equitable access, thereby ensuring that AI acts as a catalyst for building smarter, fairer, and more resilient education systems.</jats:p>

title: Unpacking Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME) Fragility: A Multidimensional Index-Based Approach
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
bd6e9590beccd5dbfc8d81d0de8d40ff954badd4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Despite the critical role of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in driving employment and regional development, limited empirical research has systematically quantified their vulnerability, particularly within the Indian context. Most prior studies emphasize sectoral challenges or financial constraints but lack an integrated framework that captures the multidimensional risks MSMEs face in rapidly urbanizing regions like Chennai. Addressing this gap, the present chapter develops a comprehensive MSME Vulnerability Index (MVI) to measure the fragility of MSMEs in Chennai District, India. Using a primary survey of 150 MSMEs across manufacturing, service and retail sectors through a stratified random sampling technique, the study employs Multiple Linear Regression to assess the relationship between firm-level factors and vulnerability. Supplementary data from the World Bank Enterprise Survey provide comparative benchmarks for robustness. Findings reveal that over 56% of MSMEs fall within high or very high vulnerability categories. Key determinants of reduced susceptibility include access to finance, digital adoption, firm size and employee training. Exploratory Factor Analysis further identifies two major dimensions of vulnerability: financial fragility and operational flexibility. The study underscores the urgency for data-driven, cohesive policy interventions focused on financial inclusion, digital transformation and capacity building. Overall, the research offers a replicable model for assessing MSME resilience and emphasizes the necessity for evidence-based policymaking to strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of small enterprises in volatile economic environments.</jats:p>

title: Strategic and Regulatory Perspectives on Small Business Innovation and Innovation Systems
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
4d2563aac00235d3e17e71ba98514600070bb645.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter aims to analyze the implications of the strategic and regulatory perspectives on innovation and systemic innovation. It departs from the assumption that the regulatory and strategic dimensions have direct effects on innovation and the innovation systems. The method used is the meta analytical, reflective, and descriptive based on the conceptual, theoretical and empirical review of the literature. This chapter concludes that there is a direct influence of the regulatory and strategic dimensions on the innovation and innovation systems.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Talent Management and Acquisition for Small-Scale Handicraft Business in an Emerging Economy
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
94bfd2c739a06e30731f8df298b2a74d22dc2558.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The purpose of this study is to identify and investigate human resources (HR) challenges for SME-based handicraft businesses in the context of an emerging economy, which is one of the most critical and expanding industries for both the domestic economy and the global market. The study was conducted by following a qualitative approach to gather data through in-depth interviews and industry observations with 15 handicraft business owners from the Dhaka division in Bangladesh. It enabled the identification of transient and permanent operational patterns, as well as HR challenges, policies, and procedures in the industry. Results showed that typical HR procedures have essential flaws. Trusted recruitment approaches, primarily social media, promoted trust but limited diversity and innovation. Recruitment, especially for rural craftsmen, was a major logistical obstacle that hampered efficiency, as their items needed to be pure and genuine to preserve cultural authenticity. This chapter also found that informal incentives were used in the sector although low earnings and high personnel turnover caused motivation and retention to fluctuate. Inconsistent skill development due to poorly planned training programs affected product quality. Because most cultures undervalue handicrafts as a career, recruiting and retaining young people has become more difficult. Protecting proprietary designs hampered sector scalability. The report proposed a complete sustainable HR framework to solve these issues. Strategic ideas were valued, formal incentive systems were implemented, training programs were improved, and intellectual property protections were increased.</jats:p>

title: Strategic Flexibility, Competitive Advantage and Non-Financial Performance of Manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria: A Mixed-Methods Study
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
fdc040b5e65c152cf8dfbb8b23e78e2d546a7887.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In today’s dynamic and unpredictable business environment, strategic flexibility has become a critical capability for sustaining competitiveness and organizational performance, especially among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in developing economies. Despite extensive research on strategic flexibility and firm performance, limited empirical evidence exists on how strategic flexibility contributes to competitive advantage and non-financial performance within the manufacturing SME sector in Nigeria, where firms face volatile market conditions, infrastructural challenges and resource constraints. This study examined the role of business strategies on the performance of small and medium-sized manufacturing firms. The objectives were to examine the effects of cost leadership, differentiation and focus strategies on the market share, sales volume and customer relationships of SMEs. Results of the chapter showed that all the selected business capabilities (cost leadership, differentiation and focus strategies) are positively associated with SME performance. This chapter offers pragmatic improvements to SMEs, which are expected to be the next strategic driving force. This research contributes to improvement by serving as a reference for studies and financial institutions, seeking to utilize or learn more about business strategies for SME performance. It is recommended that SMEs review their business strategies regularly to ensure proper use and adapt to the continuous changes in the business environment, thereby improving performance. The current study may serve as a general guideline for future investigations into these similar topics.</jats:p>

title: Social Innovation and Social Value Creation as Drivers of Social Enterprises’ Survival in Developing Economies
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
cb12c6fbc405d4c990348f83384b4d2e10948d75.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The last 20 years have seen a significant increase in interest in social business organizations. This chapter examines how social enterprises that employ the strategy of social innovation and social value creation can accelerate their survival. Recognizing their enterprise survival is important for maintaining their long-term growth. The chapter employs a survey research strategy through the administration of a structured questionnaire on 400 members of staff of social enterprises in Lagos State, Nigeria, a developing economy in Africa. The findings indicate that social innovation has a positive and significant effect on social enterprise survival in Nigeria (β = 0.469, t = 6.702, p &lt; 0.00). The coefficient of determination, with a R2 value of 0.482, suggests that 48% of the variation in social enterprise survival is accounted for by social innovation. Furthermore, the findings indicate that social value creation has a positive and significant effect on social enterprise survival in Nigeria (β = 0.594, t = 6.524, p &lt; 0.00). The coefficient of determination, with a R2 value of 0.595, suggests that approximately 60% of the variation in social enterprise survival is accounted for by social value creation. This implies that an improvement in social innovation and social value creation tends to enhance the survival of social enterprises. Therefore, it can be concluded that social innovation and social value creation are important drivers of social enterprise survival.</jats:p>

title: Multi-R Strategy Adoption and Environmental Sustainability Practices Among Manufacturing Small Businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
18d3410ee433a99a52662b7205f15d2751959e4a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>For small manufacturing businesses across Africa, and particularly in Nigeria, the continent’s leading economy in logistics capacity environmental sustainability continues to pose a significant challenge, primarily due to the high levels of waste production. This chapter explores how the adoption of the Multi-R strategy is linked to environmental sustainability practices among small businesses in Nigeria. A descriptive survey design was used to profile 950 employees from small manufacturing businesses, examining their resource consumption patterns and waste generation habits. A sample size of 281 businesses was calculated using the Taro Yamane formula, with participants selected through simple random sampling. Responses were gathered from business owners, production managers, and machine operators using a structured questionnaire. The results revealed that all three strategies—reduce (β = 0.547, p &lt; 0.000), reuse (β = 0.468, p &lt; 0.001), and repair (β = 0.395, p = 0.001)—had statistically significant and positive impacts on environmental sustainability practices in these small businesses. Each strategy made a substantial contribution to improving environmental responsibility. This chapter concludes that integrating the Multi-R strategies significantly enhances environmental sustainability practices in small businesses in Nigeria and recommends that these businesses strengthen their application of these strategies to further promote environmental responsibility.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Energy Diplomacy in Advancing Renewable Energy Adoption: A Pathway to Global Energy Transition
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
fb03e3f902ad5bb0886fc74b42e02d4c4fa630c0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The transition to renewable energy is a critical global priority, necessitating international cooperation and strategic diplomacy to overcome geopolitical, economic and technological barriers. Energy diplomacy has emerged as a key mechanism for fostering collaboration between nations, facilitating technology transfer and mobilizing financial resources for sustainable energy initiatives. This chapter examines the role of energy diplomacy in advancing renewable energy adoption, highlighting its significance in mitigating climate change, enhancing energy security and promoting global economic stability. It explores the key drivers of energy diplomacy, including climate agreements, technological innovation and economic incentives, while also addressing the challenges such as geopolitical tensions, policy misalignment and financial constraints. By reflecting on successful international partnerships, including the International Solar Alliance, EU–China renewable energy collaborations and the African Renewable Energy Initiative, this chapter provides insights into effective diplomatic strategies. The recommendations propose strengthening global frameworks, fostering technology sharing mechanisms and enhancing international trust to accelerate the global energy transition. This chapter underscores the necessity of a unified diplomatic approach to unlock the full potential of renewable energy and achieve long-term sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Strengthening Smart Cities Across Africa With Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
8e02c0a6e6a18bb2a312aa95986a867b545eef6d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As the globe enters the machine learning era and the progress in smart systems, the ramifications for urban growth, especially in African cities, are significant. Utilizing artificial intelligence’s (AI’s) potential, African cities experience better infrastructure, more efficient resource distribution, and heightened resilience against urban issues like traffic congestion, insufficient services, internal security, conflicts, and environmental deterioration. Despite the benefits of sustainable cities in Africa, they encountered potential obstacles such as outdated infrastructure and limited resources. As such, this chapter’s objectives are as follows: (i) to scrutinize the task of AI in smart cities across Africa, (ii) to examine the success rate of African smart cities over the years, and (iii) to proffer pragmatic solutions to the identified challenges confronting smart cities in Africa. This chapter adopts a qualitative method of investigation to unravel what a smart city in Africa entails, its achievements, and possible challenges. This chapter argues that AI applications and innovations can be enablers and problem solvers for smart cities across Africa.</jats:p>

title: Defining Prompt Literacy in Higher Education and Faculty Development for Prompt Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
02732e64d99fbff87251316f3d9cd6bc3ce2f987.abstract: <jats:p>The current high rate of adoption of generative artificial intelligence in higher education has led to a sense of urgency in the need to come up with immediate faculty-level literacy development. The idea of prompt literacy described in this chapter is a conceptual extension of AI literacy, focusing on the skill of developing effective prompts to achieve meaningful results in teaching, learning and assessment. It explores the current gaps in faculty preparedness and points to the absence of systematic institutional strategies to promote this new competency. The chapter also suggests faculty developmental strategies that are based on experiential learning, ethical awareness and continuous skill improvement. It also gives a detailed institutional framework to inform the systematic incorporation of prompt literacy into the faculty development programs. The chapter, with its focus on pedagogical and organizational aspects, will also help create a sustainable, responsible and context-sensitive implementation of AI in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Typologies and Competencies of Prompt Literacy in Generative Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
013ea58d255cd2cb20230cf35206aa2e5da0de6b.abstract: <jats:p>This scoping review summarizes findings on an emergent area, “prompt literacy,” in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). It specifically maps key types identified in prompt literacy, including the competencies associated with each. Using a systematic approach to analyze recent literature on the types of prompts (e.g., instruction, exploration, iteration, and evaluation) used throughout GenAI's development provides insight into how they have shaped users' experiences and interactions with new AI-based systems. Additionally, this report provides a list of basic competencies to support effective development of prompt literacy skills, including linguistic accuracy/precision, context awareness, ethical reasoning, and iterative problem-solving—all of which help individuals become successful with their digital and information literacy skills but offer new challenges when people work with AI systems. In conclusion, this review revealed that prompt literacy is a technical/cognitive skill set that encompasses (but isn't limited to) flexibility and critical thinking at all levels.</jats:p>

title: Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
bf7bc1447e7ed3caf087f04fb77606d4e98c71c2.abstract: <jats:p>While research on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and prompt literacy has expanded rapidly, an integrated framework explaining prompt-mediated learning remains underdeveloped. We introduce the Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding (PBCS) model, which conceptualizes prompts as regulatory mechanisms that coordinate cognitive, epistemic, and metacognitive processes during human–AI interaction. Building on cognitive scaffolding, distributed cognition, epistemic cognition, and prompt literacy, PBCS explains learning as a recursive coordination process in which human reasoning and AI-generated outputs are continuously refined. The model is operationalized through three interacting scaffolding dimensions and a functional prompt typology. Its explanatory scope is demonstrated across seminar-based learning, academic writing, collaborative learning, and research-oriented inquiry. We provide a theoretical foundation for understanding recursive human–AI knowledge construction.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Engineering as Distributed Cognition and Epistemic Infrastructure in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
d3ce7c75e5f8d37877d734c90b6dc48c96bd1c5b.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter theorizes prompt literacy as epistemic infrastructure in higher education, conceptualizing prompting as distributed cognition across learners, generative systems, artifacts, and disciplinary genres. It models prompting as a regulated workflow of specification, constraint-synthesis, iterative diagnosis, triangulated verification, uncertainty labelling, and accountable disclosure, reframing authorship as auditable process rather than polished output. Integrating mediated action, activity-system contradictions, pragmatics, genre theory, and epistemic cognition, the chapter translates construct logic into scalable pedagogies, evidence-centred assessment architectures, and integrity-by-design governance. It foregrounds equity as a capability condition, embedding culturally responsive prompting, multilingual burden reduction, accessibility-by-design, and privacy-security postures within institutional quality assurance. The result is a tool-agnostic blueprint for future-ready universities that stabilizes validity, trust, and learning under platform volatility.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Competence in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
d32288e5236e0a2532c8a3039cde17ecc97a0f14.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of artificial intelligence in higher education has changed how knowledge is accessed, created, and assessed. A key idea in this shift is prompt competence. It refers to the ability to design, refine, and interpret inputs for AI systems. This chapter explains the basic ideas behind prompt competence. It links the concept with digital literacy and critical thinking. It also discusses simple ways to include prompt-based learning in different courses. Teaching methods, assessment approaches, and real-life uses are explained. The chapter also looks at policy issues such as ethical use, academic honesty, data privacy, and institutional rules. It connects theory with practice and policy. It offers clear guidance for educators and institutions to use AI in a responsible way and support future-ready learners.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Literacy as a Pedagogical Resource
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
feb94f033fe2b7abcd2d34ab83cd576746ea93a7.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education is reshaping teaching, learning, and assessment practices. Within this evolving landscape, prompt literacy, the ability to design, refine, and critically evaluate prompts for AI systems, has emerged as a crucial yet underexplored competency. This chapter conceptualizes prompt literacy as a pedagogical resource within the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework. It argues that while AI introduces new cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical demands, prompt literacy functions as a key resource that helps mitigate these challenges and enhances engagement, teaching effectiveness, and learning outcomes. Drawing on insights from digital literacy, AI literacy, and educational theory, the chapter develops a multidimensional understanding of prompt literacy. It also highlights implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and institutional policy, positioning prompt literacy as a strategic capability for fostering responsible and sustainable AI-enabled education.</jats:p>

title: Designing Prompt Literacy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
90eec376cccee410354ee6fd243510dd98fd84c6.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores prompt literacy in three interrelated aspects: theoretical, pedagogical, and institutional policy frameworks. Through a qualitative research design based on thematic analysis and systematic literature review, the study gathers the scholarly contributions from 2020 to 2026. The results show that prompt literacy improves critical thinking, learner agency, and academic achievement, while raising concerns about academic integrity, epistemic trust, and ethical use of AI. The chapter suggests an innovative interactive framework for incorporating prompt literacy in higher education curricula and emphasizes that it is time to be courageous in policy formation. It concludes by outlining future research directions and institutional strategies to ensure equitable and responsible integration of AI technologies in education.</jats:p>

title: Pedagogies of Prompting
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
8f0e6973756f9577bd3eeb5de26592a0529bcd79.abstract: <jats:p>The growing integration of generative AI in higher education has positioned prompt literacy as an essential pedagogical competency across disciplines. No longer confined to technical domains, prompting now shapes inquiry, learning, assessment, and knowledge production. This chapter argues for a shift from informal AI use to structured teaching grounded in constructivist, cognitive, and digital literacy frameworks. It explores how prompt literacy can be effectively taught across humanities, social sciences, sciences, and professional fields, emphasizing its role in problem framing, critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and reflective practice. A cross-disciplinary framework is proposed, integrating scaffolding, disciplinary alignment, and ethical engagement. Viewing prompting as dialogic interaction, the chapter highlights its potential to enhance creativity, inquiry, and responsible AI use while addressing risks of superficial learning and inequity.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI in Fashion Design Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
63247d82c461a4523c3e4a79b2e2ae1f0fd715d7.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter covers the transformative role of artificial intelligence in fashion design education, with particular attention to the creation of a framework for prompt literacy utilizing generative AI technologies, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Midjourney, and Newarc AI. This chapter also examines how second-year students in Amity University Kolkata's fashion design and fashion communication department generate virtual rapid clothing prototypes of their designs and develop print motifs using AI-powered tools, especially generative AI, which ultimately enhances the significance of these tools for the changing fashion landscape. Participants have created artwork in a variety of mediums, including Mahbubani art, terracotta, ceramics, and print motifs inspired by seashells, insect using mandalas art, Persian carpets, and other subjects like “Joy in Simplicity” and “The Harmony of Nature and Feminine Grace”. The AI-Augmented Fashion Design Education Framework (AI-AFDEF) was emphasized in this book chapter's discussion of traditional versus tech-driven approaches.</jats:p>

title: Prompt Literacy in Flipped Pedagogy
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
b2f959206d0e0830e780ed1979a8107c445901f6.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter critically examines scholarly literature on prompt literacy and its relationship with flipped pedagogy in Economics education. It aims to establish conceptual clarity, identify dominant research trends, and highlight gaps in the emerging scholarship. A PRISMA-informed scoping review methodology was adopted to map the evidence, clarify key concepts, and identify research gaps. The findings conceptualize prompt literacy as a multidimensional competence encompassing pedagogical, cognitive, ethical, and disciplinary dimensions. In response, the chapter proposes a Flipped Pedagogical–AI-Mediated Learning Framework that positions prompt literacy as a mediating competence connecting AI-supported flipped pedagogy with students' cognitive, behavioural, ethical, and disciplinary learning outcomes. The framework provides a conceptual foundation for responsible and pedagogically purposeful AI integration in flipped Economics education.</jats:p>

title: Prompting for Academic Writing and Research
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
381b8ae3adf774d45c5ddbe6dc73d8a600b6339a.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming academic writing and research, creating an urgent need for prompt literacy as a core competency in higher education. This chapter develops an integrated framework that positions prompt literacy as a cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical capability supporting responsible human–AI collaboration. Drawing on contemporary scholarship, this chapter synthesises existing literature to examine prompt design, evaluation, research applications, instructional strategies, and ethical governance. It further proposes a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) verification framework to strengthen transparency, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-assisted scholarship. This chapter contributes a structured conceptual model that informs curriculum design, research training, assessment practices, and institutional policy, enabling higher education institutions to foster responsible, critical, and future-ready AI-enabled scholarship.</jats:p>

title: Prompting for Academic Writing and Research
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
a33a6033f3bf398f73b26ab21bb6cfa211ed34c1.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter examines the role of prompt literacy as a structured academic competence in AI-supported writing and research within higher education. It develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework linking prompt quality to academic writing and research performance through the mediating role of cognitive engagement and the moderating influence of institutional academic integrity orientation. Drawing on cognitive, academic literacy, metacognitive, and socio-technical perspectives, the chapter demonstrates that effective prompting is not merely technical but central to scholarly practice. Findings indicate that high-quality prompts enhance analytical depth, coherence, and methodological clarity, particularly when users actively engage with AI outputs. Furthermore, institutional integrity environments strengthen responsible AI use and amplify performance outcomes. The chapter contributes theoretical, pedagogical, and policy insights by positioning prompt literacy as essential for sustaining academic rigor in AI-mediated scholarship.</jats:p>

title: From Prompts to Publications
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
0591dcbe31cc30e58b9111db20f64b03b4dde500.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid emergence of generative AI systems such as GPT-4, Gemini, and Claude has significantly transformed academic writing and research practices, raising critical questions about authorship, originality and intellectual labor. This chapter introduces the concept of prompt literacy as a foundational academic competency for effectively engaging with large language models. It proposes a four-mode typology of prompting strategies exploratory, analytical, generative and evaluative, mapped across different stages of the research lifecycle. Based on interdisciplinary scholarship, the chapter outlines practical techniques such as context-setting, iterative prompting and constraint specification to enhance AI-assisted research. It also critically examines ethical concerns including bias, academic integrity and over-reliance on AI. The chapter concludes by suggesting guidelines for responsible and pedagogically sound integration of generative AI in higher education, emphasizing the need to preserve human intellectual agency while leveraging AI as a supportive scholarly tool.</jats:p>

title: Assessing Prompt Literacy Without Rewarding AI Dependence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Prompt Literacy in Higher Education
87efe6b64abb52ecb3ebc29c6cb22b3f5ea3063e.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI has made a visible educational skill, yet many assessments still reward polished final outputs more than genuine understanding. This creates a perverse incentive: students who outsource the most thinking often appear the most competent. This chapter argues that prompt literacy must be assessed in ways that do not reward AI dependence. It reframes prompt literacy as evaluative and disciplinary judgement, demonstrated when students frame tasks, set constraints, iterate purposefully, verify outputs, document tool use, and decide when to limit or refuse AI support. The proposed approach rests on three ideas: rubrics that value judgement over polish, authentic tasks that make process and transfer visible, and academic integrity by design. Supported by seven tables and five figures, the chapter offers practical tools and concludes that the real challenge is designing assessment that promotes accountable thinking, calibrated trust, and durable learning rather than automated text production.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Plasma Surface Engineering for Advanced Aerospace and Material Applications
container-title: Theory, Applications, and Impacts of Advanced Plasma Engineering
d7a80a5a47a2eca8b31cfcd94a294b35c2480ee3.abstract: <jats:p>Plasma engineering has become a sophisticated technology for processing surfaces and enhancing functional properties of materials for a wide range of industrial processes. The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the integration of plasma-based surface engineering and optimization of material properties is explored in this chapter. This emphasizes low temperature and atmospheric plasma processes for coating deposition, surface activation and fabrication of nanostructures. The importance of AI and machine learning for predicting plasma behavior, optimizing process parameters and coating quality is emphasized. Applications such as aerospace, biomedical devices, semiconductor processing and sustainability (CO2 conversion and plasma-assisted catalysis) are discussed. Additionally, experimental diagnostics, numerical simulations, and scalability, process control and industrial integration issues are explored. Finally, future directions towards intelligent and sustainable plasma systems are summarized.</jats:p>

title: A Multilingual AI-Driven Conversational System for Cervical Cancer Awareness and Risk Assessment: Development and Evaluation Study
container-title: JMIR Cancer
4ef21e1247b3939cc59a2e2efcc517e8fb9da2e2.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women globally, with an estimated 660,000 new cases and 350,000 deaths in 2022. It imposes a disproportionate burden on underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries, where language barriers, cultural stigma, and limited access to health care hinder awareness and uptake of preventive measures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to design, develop, and evaluate a multilingual AI-driven dialogue system for cervical cancer awareness, personalized risk assessment, and health care facility navigation, targeting underserved populations through a culturally adaptive and privacy-preserving digital health platform.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A design science research framework guided the development of a 3-tier, cross-platform system comprising (1) a transparent, rule-based risk-stratification engine whose 30-item questionnaire mirrors the feature schema of the University of California, Irvine (UCI) Cervical Cancer Risk Factors dataset and whose weights encode established clinical risk factors drawn from World Health Organization, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and American Cancer Society guidance; (2) a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot powered by GPT-4o mini; and (3) a geospatial health care facility recommendation module. The system was implemented in TypeScript (NestJS) and Flutter (Google LLC) and deployed across Android, iOS, and web platforms with multilingual support for English, Spanish, Yoruba, and Swahili, of which English, Spanish, and Yoruba were included in the multilingual evaluation reported here. The risk engine was evaluated through clinical face-validity review of its factor weights; chatbot quality was assessed using retrieval precision, hallucination rate, large language model (LLM)–as-a-judge quality scoring, adversarial safety testing, and native-speaker rating of multilingual output.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The rule-based engine produced deterministic, fully traceable risk levels (low, moderate, and high) with per-factor explanations for every completed assessment. The RAG chatbot achieved retrieval precision@3 of 0.88 and a 71.4% reduction in hallucination rate compared with a non-RAG baseline. Automated LLM-as-judge evaluation rated factual correctness at 4.3/5, and independent clinician review of 50 responses identified factual errors in 8% (4/50) of RAG-grounded outputs compared with 28% (14/50) for a non-RAG baseline (Cohen κ=0.84). The geospatial module achieved a specialty relevance precision of 0.87. Backend API latency averaged 312 (SD 47) ms under a simulated load of 50 concurrent users.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates the technical feasibility of integrating transparent, guideline-informed risk stratification, RAG-grounded conversational AI, and geospatial health care navigation within a unified multilingual digital health platform. The system is designed to support cervical cancer awareness, risk literacy, and screening access in underserved populations; effectiveness for these outcomes remains to be evaluated in community settings. Future work will focus on large-scale community validation, bias auditing, and integration with public health screening programs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-Newton: A concept-driven physical law discovery system without prior physical knowledge
container-title: Physical Review Research
ea8da7c32b2a591d9ac52aeb9a7ee781fb421226.abstract: <jats:p>While current artificial intelligence (AI)-driven methods excel at deriving empirical models from individual experiments, a significant challenge remains in uncovering the common fundamental physics that underlie these models—a task at which human physicists are adept. To bridge this gap, we introduce AI-Newton, a framework for concept-driven scientific discovery. Our system autonomously derives general physical laws directly from raw, multiexperiment data, operating without supervision or prior physical knowledge. Its core innovations are twofold: (1) proposing interpretable physical concepts to construct laws and (2) progressively generalizing these laws to broader domains. Applied to a large, noisy dataset of mechanics experiments, AI-Newton successfully rediscovers foundational and universal laws, such as Newton's second law, the conservation of energy, and the universal gravitation. This work represents a proof-of-concept step toward autonomous, humanlike scientific discovery.</jats:p>

title: AI for Solar Energy Systems
