80e78eebcad6ce7cd583e1cff46a520d7991049e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid expansion of solar energy has accelerated the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve forecasting accuracy, photovoltaic performance, intelligent control, fault diagnosis, energy storage management, and smart grid operation. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, Digital Twins, Physics-Informed Machine Learning, Edge AI, Federated Learning, and Generative AI have transformed solar energy systems into more adaptive and data-driven infrastructures. Despite these advances, challenges related to data quality, model generalization, computational efficiency, cybersecurity, and explainability continue to limit large-scale deployment. An integrated perspective is presented by connecting AI applications across photovoltaic systems, solar thermal technologies, energy storage, and intelligent energy networks within a unified renewable energy ecosystem. Emerging research trends and future directions highlight the evolution toward AI-native energy systems that support efficient, resilient, and sustainable intelligent societies.</jats:p>

title: Standalone PV System for EV Charging Optimization Based on Loss of Power Supply Probability
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
0f779933daa21b2f965772ae79d941e341e497a6.abstract: <jats:p>The electric vehicle (EV) is the future transportation mode. It necessitates great power from the grid to be charged. The energy demand can affect its stability. The main chapter presents a charging system based on a standalone photovoltaic system. The PV production is intermittent. Thus, the integration of a storage system is recommended. The presented configuration consists of a PV array, a lithium-ion battery for the EV with a unidirectional inverter and another battery as a storage system with a bidirectional inverter. Effective charging system, an energy management system was developed. The designed approach aims to feed the EV through the PV array. BSS are used to store excess of energy during peak hours and to ensure a continuous charging in case of deficit power. The optimization is done using the loss of power supply probability. The battery State of Charge (SOC) is predicted using the Extended Kalman Filter. The Root mean Squared Error does not exceed 1%. The simulation results show that the proposed system ensures an effective charging process with an LPSP equal to zero.</jats:p>

title: AI for Wind Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
d6d8adf202aed253644ed73dead2e3bcff980f7b.abstract: <jats:p>The renewable energy is being transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) to create smarter, efficient, and adaptive wind systems. AI forecasts the wind using machine learning and neural networks and optimizes the performance of turbines and minimizes costs related to maintenance using predictive analytics. These inventions assist the operators in predicting the changes, setting the turbines, and reducing downtime. Urban deployment of AI facilitates the seamless synchronization of mass-scaled wind energy with smart grids as well as the systems of IoT. It balances loads dynamically, for instance, it trades energy in real time and improves stability in the grid. Heavy reliance on fossil fuels and extensive reliance on carbon emissions and fossil fuels can be reduced through the implementation of AI-driven systems that enhance energy efficiency, reliability, and sustainability through the integration of renewable sources, storage, and intelligent control.</jats:p>

title: AI for Wind Energy Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
4f4dc990deb9ecb4d79f7eb21160b4d6a0c8d4aa.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the wind energy sector, marking a major step toward sustainable and intelligent societies. As global energy demands rise and carbon reduction becomes urgent, AI offers powerful tools to enhance the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of wind power systems. Through technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins, and predictive analytics, AI optimizes turbine design, predictive maintenance, load forecasting, and smart grid integration. By leveraging big data from sensors, meteorological sources, and operational parameters, AI enables accurate wind prediction, timely fault detection, and real-time performance optimization. Additionally, AI-driven systems play an emerging role in urban wind integration by improving micro-wind utilization, energy storage, and distributed generation within smart cities. The chapter also addresses economic feasibility, environmental sustainability, and ethical implications of AI-enabled wind energy applications.</jats:p>

title: Geothermal Energy and AI Integration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
0a94185efa705e533048f8ecb2e7e97f676948cd.abstract: <jats:p>The future of sustainable power generation is being transformed by the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to geothermal energy systems that improves the precision of their exploration, efficiency of their operations, and sustainability of their reservoirs. The chapter analyzes the main principles of geothermal energy, considers the latest methods of AI in the energy system, and seeks to emphasize how AI-based models can contribute to real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and surface characterization. The chapter illustrates the real usefulness of AI-supported geothermal processes using case studies and worldwide initiatives and covering the current issues regarding data quality, integration of the system, and ethical concerns. New tendencies like digital twins, intelligent geothermal facilities, and powerful predictive analytics are discussed to demonstrate possible research opportunities in the future. On the whole, the integration of geothermal technologies with AI has a high potential to speed up the innovation of renewable energy and add to the global energy.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enhanced Geothermal Technologies for Next-Generation Power Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
427d1a26ce798d2133705e4eaa4fe9ba71a1502d.abstract: <jats:p>AI-powered geothermal systems are changing renewable energy by making it easier to find new sources of energy, lowering the cost of drilling, improving reservoir management, and making power plants work better. AI techniques look at data from geology, seismology, and operations to find anomalies, predict reservoir properties, and improve energy extraction. Intelligent drilling systems let you control parameters in real time and do predictive maintenance, which lowers costs and risks. AI-based reservoir simulations help with dynamic control of injection and extraction processes, which makes sure that they last for a long time. On the surface, smart monitoring and forecasting tools make plants more efficient and help them connect to the grid better, which supports stable hybrid renewable networks. AI also makes environmental monitoring better by finding seismic and emission risks early on. AI-enhanced geothermal technologies make things much more reliable, efficient, and sustainable, even though there are problems like not having enough data and models that are hard to understand.</jats:p>

title: AI Optimization of Energy Storage Systems for Enhancing Efficiency, Capacity, and Resilience
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
cea59c00d46249ed8267dc08bd0d2e35d2aa48a6.abstract: <jats:p>The global shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy has increased the need for energy storage systems to ensure reliability, flexibility, and resilience in modern power grids. Although solar and wind reduce emissions, their intermittency challenges grid stability and supply–demand balance. Energy Storage Systems (ESS), such as batteries, supercapacitors, hydrogen, and mechanical storage, play a key role in addressing these issues. However, ESS face limitations like efficiency loss, capacity degradation, uncertainty, and high costs. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution by improving prediction accuracy, optimizing real-time operation, managing degradation, and enabling smart decision-making. This chapter introduces the global energy transition, importance of ESS, major challenges, and the role of AI in enhancing ESS performance and lifecycle. It presents the mission, motivation, and scope of the work, forming the basis for detailed discussions on technologies, AI-driven control, predictive maintenance, and future smart storage systems.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Data Analytics for Smart Grid
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
36115464283b4a94eb1013a154df03e7f1a1e053.abstract: <jats:p>As the earth's energy requires to grow, it is important to make sustainable power sources like sun, wind, and hydropower work as efficiently as possible. As power lines get more complicated and energy sources change, old ways of managing energy are not always up to the task. So, there is a greater need for new energy systems and methods to deal with issues like energy loss and waste. Big data and AI are transforming renewable energy and grid system worldwide. These technologies optimise renewable energy generation as demand for novel energy systems develops. AI-powered Smart Grid Technology improves real-time monitoring and matches energy flows to demand. Additionally, AI-driven energy optimization improves solar and wind resource allocation and operating efficiency. Predictive analytics improves renewable energy management by predicting output and consumption. This article shows how AI and big data are becoming crucial in renewable energy and grid management system. It addresses how improved forecasting and energy efficiency create a more robust and sustainable energy future.</jats:p>

title: Smart Grid Optimization at the Building Scale
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
cf23bf1f0405a3031b63f652b560a34ed04f777f.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter addresses the intelligent management of energy resources at the microgrid level, with a strong focus on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for smart grid optimization. The main objective is to enhance economic efficiency, energy performance, and environmental sustainability through advanced AI-based energy management strategies. The study considers a grid-connected building integrating local renewable energy generation and energy storage systems. The microgrid configuration is presented along with the objectives of the proposed energy management approach and the performance indicators used to assess operational costs, environmental impacts, and renewable energy utilization. Particular attention is given to the interaction between the building and the main grid to optimize power exchanges while ensuring grid stability. A case study modeled and simulated using WindPRO software demonstrates the effectiveness of AI-driven solutions and highlights their potential to enable clean, resilient, and economically viable energy systems at the microgrid scale.</jats:p>

title: How Effectively Can AI Enhance Predictive Accuracy and Smart Grid Performance in Renewable Energy Systems?
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
f20481898dd366f5395dcbbf2be914d08a780e36.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a transformative role in enhancing predictive accuracy and operational performance in renewable energy systems. As the global shift toward sustainable energy intensifies, AI enables improved efficiency, reduced costs, and greater reliability across energy infrastructures. This study investigates AI's potential to optimize energy production forecasting, consumption patterns, and smart grid operations. Using a methodological approach that combines a comprehensive review of AI applications and real-world case studies, the research evaluates techniques such as predictive analytics, deep learning, and real-time grid optimization. Findings reveal that AI significantly enhances forecasting accuracy, system adaptability, and real-time energy management. By integrating AI, renewable energy systems become more resilient and efficient, supporting long-term sustainability goals. The study offers strategic insights into how AI technologies can be effectively leveraged to advance renewable energy development and intelligent grid performance.</jats:p>

title: The Synergy Between Smart Grids and Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI Technologies for Renewable Energy Systems and Intelligent Grid Optimization
0cb2dc1ceaa5b8676d1cb89d0dc6729d797fa8dd.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with smart grid systems to enhance renewable energy utilization and intelligent mobility. It highlights the transition from centralized power systems to decentralized, data-driven energy networks supported by IoT, big data, and advanced communication technologies. AI techniques such as machine learning and predictive analytics enable accurate demand forecasting, efficient energy management, and grid stability. The research also examines challenges in renewable integration, including intermittency and storage limitations, and presents AI-based solutions. Furthermore, it emphasizes the role of electric vehicles and vehicle-to-grid systems in achieving sustainable mobility, ultimately contributing to resilient, efficient, and environmentally friendly energy ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Design of AI-Based Perception Systems for Real-Time ADAS
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
d91ce310e605baffdae89107a02d0159ddd145de.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based embedded perception for real-time Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) for trustworthy electric ride-hailing services. It reviews recent perception approaches for road-scene understanding, including lightweight convolutional models, You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors, compact vision transformers, low-light perception, radar-aware methods, and multimodal fusion. Particular attention is given to safety-critical road elements such as pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists, obstacles, traffic signs, and traffic lights, because they directly influence driver awareness, decision-making, and perceived safety. The chapter proposes a methodological framework covering dataset selection, ADAS task definition, data preparation, model selection, AI optimization methods, embedded deployment, and evaluation. By linking perception reliability with perceived safety, user trust, and behavioral intention, the chapter positions embedded ADAS perception as a key contributor to the adoption of electric ride-hailing services.</jats:p>

13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

title: Building a Digital Chemistry Lab

<jats:p>Laboratory automation, new sensors and artificial intelligence are set to revolutionise the way we do science. But how can you get started incorporating these technologies into your lab?</jats:p>

title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
53110e8e5f76115bc805ea592d8fbaf8fceaa7dd.abstract: <jats:p>El propósito del libro es analizar, desde distintas perspectivas académicas, los cambios que las tecnologias digitales están generando en los modelos formativos de las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia. Cada capítulo profundiza en un aspecto clave: desde la validación del conocimiento asistido por inteligencia artificial, hasta la ética y la gobernanza tecnológica, pasando por los modelos pedagógicos institucionales y las estrategias de enseñanza en entorno híbridos. En la era digital, la educación militar enfrente uno de los procesos de transformación más profundos de su historia. Las Fuerzas Militares, tradicionalimente asociadas con la disciplina, la estrategia y la práctica operacional, se encuentran ante el desafío de integrar tecnologías emergente -como la inteligencia artificial, la analítica de datos, la simulación avanzada y los entornos virtuales de aprendizaje- en sus procesos de formación, instrucción y liderazgo. Esta convergencia entre lo tecnológico y lo humano redefine las formas de enseñar, aprender y evaluar, impulsando una nueva doctrina pedagógica que combina el rigor militar con la innovación educativa.</jats:p>

title: Estrategias para validar el conocimiento adquirido en procesos de aprendizaje asistidos por IA
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
64e7a88b3ff913a62dcdc0ba5b926c7c911b4695.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo analiza estrategias para validar el conocimiento en procesos formativos asistidos por inteligencia artificial (IA) en las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia. Mediante un  enfoque  cualitativo  de  análisis  documental,  se  revisan  metodologías  como  la  evaluación automatizada y la analítica del aprendizaje, comparando los modelos pedagógicos de las escuelas de oficiales ESMIC, ENAP y EMAVI. Aunque todas comparten fundamentos constructivistas y por competencias, cada una adapta herramientas de IA según su dominio estratégico: terrestre, marítimo o aéreo. Los hallazgos evidencian que la validación del conocimiento no puede depender exclusivamente de sistemas automatizados, de manera que se requiere una integración entre tecnología y pedagogía que permita evaluar no solo la competencia operativa, sino también el pensamiento crítico y el discernimiento ético. Se propone avanzar hacia modelos mixtos que articulen la analítica de datos con el juicio cualitativo del instructor para fortalecer la formación integral del futuro oficial en escenarios complejos y dinámicos.</jats:p>

title: Ética y gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos de las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
af434ca184d59d5ddf93af8a7cfe27022962cd0f.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo presenta un análisis sobre los marcos éticos y de gobernanza para el uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación, con especial énfasis en su incorporación en las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia. El objetivo es proponer lineamientos estratégicos que orienten un uso ético, responsable y contextualizado de la IA en los procesos educativos militares. Metodológicamente, se realizó una revisión documental de políticas institucionales nacionales e internacionales, contrastadas con recomendaciones de organismos como la UNESCO y la OCDE, así como diálogos académicos con expertos en la materia. Entre los resultados se identifican buenas prácticas y principios comunes, como la transparencia, la equidad y la alfabetización digital. Las conclusiones destacan la necesidad urgente de establecer políticas adaptadas al entorno militar, promover la formación crítica en IA en todos los niveles y garantizar que esta tecnología habilitadora complemente, mas no reemplace, el juicio humano en la formación de competencias como el pensamiento crítico, la toma de decisiones, el debate argumentativo, la solución de problemas, el discernimiento ético, entre otras competencias propias de la profesión militar.</jats:p>

title: Aportes de la inteligencia artificial a la enseñanza de la memoria histórica en el sector defensa
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
3e5814c496eff2daf13c4983ddcc53e4f747fd76.abstract: <jats:p>En el escenario de post-conflicto que vive Colombia, la memoria histórica ha cobrado un papel central en la implementación del Sistema Integral de Verdad, Justicia, Reparación y No Repetición, el cual tiene la titánica labor de visibilizar, dignificar y reconocer a las víctimas del conflicto armado colombiano. Por tal motivo, su enseñanza resulta indispensable para que las generaciones centenials del sector defensa comprendan las causas, el desarrollo y las consecuencias del conflicto. El objetivo de este capítulo es analizar cómo la inteligencia artificial puede contribuir al aprendizaje de la memoria histórica, a través de un análisis documental y bibliométrico, sustentado en el modelo de aprendizaje constructivista, que permita identificar tendencias, enfoques y experiencias relevantes. Entre los principales hallazgos, se identificó un creciente interés investigativo en la articulación entre memoria histórica, tecnologías de aprendizaje e inteligencia artificial, que brindan oportunidades para el diseño de estrategias educativas más eficaces dirigidas a las nuevas generaciones.</jats:p>

title: Transformaciones en la cultura militar: nuevas masculinidades ante el ascenso del liderazgo femenino
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
c8f3deadcd0e6449ded4b991a0742746c14a286e.abstract: <jats:p>La investigación analiza las tensiones y transformaciones que enfrenta la cultura militar colombiana ante el ascenso de mujeres a cargos de mando, desde un enfoque centrado en las nuevas masculinidades. Se parte del supuesto de que la autoridad castrense ha estado históricamente asociada a un modelo de masculinidad hegemónica, lo cual genera resistencias  simbólicas  y  actitudinales  frente  al  liderazgo  femenino.  El  estudio  adopta  un  enfoque cualitativo de tipo exploratorio-descriptivo, y utiliza como instrumento una encuesta estructurada con preguntas cerradas, aplicada a personal militar en servicio activo. Los resultados permiten identificar prácticas de deslegitimación, vigilancia informal y boicot pasivo hacia mujeres líderes, así como la emergencia de discursos masculinos más flexibles. Se concluye que la transformación del mando exige no solo ajustes normativos, sino una resignificación profunda de los imaginarios de género que configuran la autoridad militar.</jats:p>

title: La influencia de las redes sociales en la percepción del rol militar de los cadetes de la Escuela Militar de Cadetes “General José María Córdova”
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
a9bcf52b3766a8444821f3611229f82875561fe3.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo analiza cómo las redes sociales influyen en la construcción de la identidad profesional y la percepción institucional de los cadetes y alféreces de la Escuela Militar de Cadetes “General José María Córdova”. Se parte de la idea de que plataformas como TikTok, Instagram, X y YouTube no solo difunden información, sino que generan un espacio de socialización simbólica que puede reforzar o cuestionar los valores castrenses promovidos por la Doctrina Damasco. A través de encuestas, se identificaron cuatro tipologías de contenidos consumidos: institucional, de entretenimiento, histórico-militar y crítico/paródico, cada una con efectos diferenciados en la motivación y el sentido de pertenencia. Los hallazgos muestran que, aunque muchos cadetes resignifican los discursos digitales para fortalecer su identidad, cerca del 30 % experimenta disonancia cognitiva al confrontar las narrativas oficiales con las críticas. Ante este escenario, se plantea la necesidad de integrar la resiliencia mediática crítica en el currículo militar, promoviendo competencias comunicativas que permitan a los futuros oficiales desenvolverse con solvencia en un entorno digital descentralizado y en constante transformación.</jats:p>

title: Modelo de gestión institucional para el fortalecimiento de la investigación científica en contextos militares
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
b2b8b51b7182321f6f266dfaf4ed28d3a65e9c35.abstract: <jats:p>Este  capítulo  aborda  la  importancia  de  implementar  un  modelo  de  gestión  para  proyectos de investigación, desarrollo e innovación (I+D+i) en instituciones militares como la  Armada  Nacional,  considerando  los  desafíos  actuales  del  sector  defensa.  Se  reconoce  que la I+D+i son pilares esenciales para la seguridad y la soberanía nacional, y que las estructuras de gestión tradicionales no siempre permiten una articulación eficiente con los avances tecnológicos ni con las demandas operativas contemporáneas. A partir de un enfoque  cualitativo  y  documental,  se  analizan  experiencias  que  han  integrado  exitosamente  modelos  de  gestión  spin-off, spin-in  y  mixtos,  destacando  la  colaboración  entre  el  Estado,  la academia y la industria. El estudio permite identificar factores clave, limitaciones normativas  y  condiciones  para  una  transferencia  de  tecnología  efectiva  y  sostenible,  a  partir  de  lo  cual  plantea  un  modelo,  según  las  características  y  necesidades  de  la  institución,  que  promueva la innovación, optimice recursos y fortalezca la autonomía tecnológica mediante estrategias de integración institucional.</jats:p>

title: Entrenamiento físico militar basado en evidencia y datos: disciplina, cohesión y tecnología para la defensa nacional
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
b928587e6b62627213f2af7234bb179ccdd26506.abstract: <jats:p>El  presente  artículo  analiza  el  concepto  de  entrenamiento  físico  militar  basado  en evidencia y datos (EFMED) como una evolución respecto al modelo tradicional de preparación  física  en  las  Fuerzas  Armadas  de  Colombia.  La  investigación  empleó  un  diseño  de método mixto, en el cual se efectúo revisión bibliográfica sistemática en bases de datos académicas y se aplicó una encuesta exploratoria al personal militar, con el fin de examinar los impactos cognitivos, disciplinarios y tecnológicos de esta modalidad de entrenamiento. La encuesta, aplicada a un grupo de hombres y mujeres, entre oficiales y suboficiales de las Fuerzas Armadas de Colombia, reveló que el 50,3 % de los encuestados considera prioritaria  la  migración  hacia  un  modelo  basado  en  evidencias  y  datos.  Además,  se  destacan  como elementos clave la incorporación de tecnologías portátiles (68 %), la personalización de rutinas (45,1 %) y el fortalecimiento de la disciplina y la cohesión (30,1 %). Finalmente, el 73,3 % del personal emplea para su entrenamiento tecnologías con dispositivos wearables (pulsómetros  GPS).  Se  propone  un  marco  de  política  pública  para  Colombia  que  articule  ciencia del ejercicio, analítica de datos y doctrina militar, orientado a fortalecer la seguridad y defensa nacional en contextos multidominio.</jats:p>

title: El humor como recurso de resiliencia en el servicio militar en la Fuerza Aeroespacial Colombiana
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
22e1f54a86bea5f0c549929c8cdce8cfe152a0b1.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo analiza la influencia del humor en la resiliencia emocional y la cohesión grupal de soldados pertenecientes a los contingentes 2024 y 2025 de la Fuerza Aeroespacial Colombiana. Mediante un enfoque cualitativo hermenéutico y el uso del cuestionario Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ), complementado con entrevistas semiestructuradas, se identificaron las manifestaciones del humor, su relación con el afrontamiento del estrés y su papel en la construcción de vínculos grupales. Los resultados evidencian que el humor, en especial el afiliativo y el autoafirmante, contribuye significativamente a disminuir tensiones, fortalecer la confianza mutua y generar sentido de pertenencia, incluso en contextos de alta exigencia física y emocional. Asimismo, se establecen límites tácitos y códigos internos que regulan su uso, evitando la exclusión o incomodidad. Se concluye que el humor, implementado de manera estratégica, puede consolidarse como una herramienta institucional para mejorar el bienestar y la eficacia en entornos militares.</jats:p>

title: Beauty in the Digital Age
Beautiful Particulars
c6fe3d0377956ff06d423eb5e3d727284e365eac.abstract:
<jats:p>A fresh and eye-opening new explanation of AI—and how its focus on specifics is changing our ideas about ourselves and our world.From a Harvard researcher, philosopher, entrepreneur, former comedy writer, and bestselling author.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Amid the clamor about AI, Beautiful Particulars poses a unique question: Not how does our use of AI change what we do, but how is the idea of AI already subtly yet fundamentally reshaping how we think about ourselves and our world?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>In clear, engaging, and even humorous prose, David Weinberger offers a new perspective on how machine learning works and how it may already be changing our basic and deepest ideas. Through lively examples, he shows that AI’s success—with all its risks and dangers—is taking us past our millennia of reliance on laws and principles by revealing what morality, free will, creativity, causality knowledge, and even reality itself look like now that we’re able to let the particulars speak their tiny truths.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>The author poses questions not usually asked: What does a coin look like to AI? When AI gives you evidence that the earth is round, why are its own reasons for saying that so different? Why does an AI image generator create a “selfie” of ancient Aztec warriors with broad smiles that it “believes” are historically unlikely? If AI becomes conscious but bodiless, could it still make good moral decisions? Why is the world so much better at being causal than AI could ever “understand”? How does AI show us that genuine creativity is not about a “spark” but about moments that feel right? And how can you take the temperature of a joke?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>Beautiful Particulars offers a new—and hopeful—perspective on how machine learning works, and how that’s already changing how we understand what it means to be human in the age of AI.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Digital Green Accounting into Business Education: A Review and Future Directions for Sustainable E-Business Learning
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
0da0bb4b3e5fdf8ed07e61d8d65afb073ea961e4.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital green accounting into e-business and business education represents a critical step toward aligning technological innovation with sustainability imperatives. This study conducts a narrative literature review of research published between 2005 and 2025, examining how digital tools such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, IoT, and big data are reshaping accounting practices to enhance transparency, accountability, and environmental stewardship. Findings reveal that while e-businesses increasingly adopt green accounting to align with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), challenges such as curriculum rigidity, limited faculty expertise, and technological constraints hinder widespread adoption in business education. Nonetheless, innovative pedagogical practices including experiential learning, simulations, and industry partnerships which offers promising pathways for embedding sustainability literacy and digital skills into curricula. A conceptual framework is proposed to guide the integration of digital green accounting into academic programs, highlighting inputs, processes, outputs, and long-term impacts. The study concludes that collaboration among academia, industry, and policymakers is essential for preparing future business leaders to balance profitability with sustainability and drive systemic transformation.</jats:p>

title: Kapabilitas Jejaring Digital, Pemanfaatan E-CRM, dan Ekuitas Pelanggan pada Perusahaan Jasa Rintisan di Makassar
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
9be1e7e30d2b357f6622e75d1052b44d0b9a349b.abstract: <jats:p>Tingginya angka kegagalan perusahaan jasa rintisan pada tahun-tahun pertama operasional menuntut pergeseran strategi dari pendekatan transaksional menjadi relasional digital. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh kapabilitas jejaring digital dan pemanfaatan E-CRM terhadap ekuitas pelanggan pada perusahaan jasa rintisan di Kota Makassar. Pendekatan penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan teknik purposive sampling melibatkan 140 pemilik atau manajer startup jasa sebagai responden. Data primer yang dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner daring dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil analisis model struktural menunjukkan bahwa kapabilitas jejaring digital dan pemanfaatan E-CRM berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap ekuitas pelanggan, baik secara langsung maupun tidak langsung melalui jalur mediasi. Pemanfaatan E-CRM terbukti bertindak sebagai mediator yang menjembatani potensi jejaring eksternal menjadi ekuitas pelanggan yang berkelanjutan. Kesimpulan penelitian menegaskan bahwa orkestrasi modal sosial luar dan efisiensi sistem internal yang fleksibel menjadi jangkar pelindung kelangsungan hidup bisnis baru. Secara teoretis, penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi bagi perluasan Dynamic Capabilities Theory, serta memberikan panduan praktis berupa cetak biru strategi bagi tata kelola bisnis rintisan di wilayah ekonomi berkembang</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Early Detection of Epidemic Threats in a Resource-Constrained Health System: Implementation Research from Lebanon
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
94bf395e649f9c13344c021277ab854ad6c98be5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Global South countries face heightened infectious disease risks compounded by fragmented surveillance systems and resource constraints. Lebanon’s health system crisis and recurrent outbreaks highlight the urgent need for new approaches to epidemic and pandemic preparedness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To describe the design, implementation process, and early implementation findings of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled early warning system (AI-EWS) that automates detection of epidemiologically relevant events using laboratory data in Lebanon, with emphasis on feasibility, workflow integration, stakeholder engagement, and implementation learnings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We applied an implementation research approach to co-design and validate an AI-EWS prototype integrated within a university hospital laboratory. The system incorporates a hybrid statistical and machine learning analytic pipeline and a real-time dashboard for detecting epidemic events across multiple pathogens using routine laboratory information systems (LIS) data. The system was developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) to support future national adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The project produced a structured framework for pathogen selection, rule development, dataset creation, and platform co-design with clinical and epidemiological experts, medical informatics professionals, MoPH experts, and technical specialists. Early implementation observations indicate operational feasibility within existing infrastructure, strong stakeholder engagement, and trust-building around AI-enabled surveillance through participatory design and responsible-AI governance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-enabled laboratory surveillance is a viable and scalable approach to strengthening epidemic preparedness in low-resource health systems when grounded in implementation science and responsible AI, and when explicitly aligned with local workflows and national policy priorities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Bayesian Forecasting as the Analytical Core of an AI-Assisted Early Warning System for Dengue Outbreaks during the 2023 Epidemic: Implementation and Emergency Management in a Dominican Pediatric Hospital
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
056417fa3dbad64347775b6e5020ffb82cf01df1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dengue remains a major cause of pediatric morbidity in the Dominican Republic, with increasingly intense epidemic cycles. Advances in statistical modeling, probabilistic forecasting, and AI-assisted digital health systems offer new opportunities to enhance early warning capabilities and strengthen hospital preparedness. This study evaluated a Bayesian negative binomial regression forecasting model as the analytical core of an AI-assisted early warning system (EWS) for predicting weekly dengue cases nationwide, using strict out-of-sample validation during the 2023 epidemic and applying its outputs operationally in a high-demand pediatric hospital. National surveillance data (PLISA/PAHO), hospital records from the Dr. Hugo Mendoza Pediatric Hospital (HPHM), and climatic and satellite indicators (NOAA, MODIS) for 2014–2024 were integrated. The model incorporated climatically plausible lags, harmonic seasonality, two vegetation indices (NDVI_lag4 and EVI_lag4), a long-term spline trend, and weakly informative priors, achieving excellent convergence (Rhat = 1.00). Climatic and environmental predictors exhibited small and uncertain effects, whereas the temporal spline accounted for most long-term epidemic variability. In the 2023 national validation, the model captured the broad epidemic trajectory and improved RMSE and MAE compared with the historical seasonal baseline (RMSE = 783.3; MAE = 423.4; MAPE = 80.2%), although proportional accuracy remained limited during abrupt epidemic acceleration. The national model also captured ascending-phase signals that were temporally aligned with the HPHM hospital outbreak, including its sharp rise during epidemiological weeks 36–40. These outputs were used alongside routine surveillance and hospital indicators to support operational situational awareness, capacity planning, patient-flow reorganization, strengthened triage, and emergency preparedness during the epidemic. The model demonstrated temporal signal detection and operational relevance, positioning Bayesian probabilistic forecasting, embedded within an AI-assisted digital health workflow, as a useful analytical component for epidemic monitoring and hospital preparedness, subject to limitations in peak magnitude calibration and proportional accuracy.</jats:p>

title: Digital Augmentation of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 for Obesity Management: Retrospective Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
0c23ca513d5b5a47aa7bd9ddcc81c35d4082df21.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide and tirzepatide, are highly effective for weight management; however, long-term outcomes depend on sustained behavioral engagement. Digital health tools may enhance these behavioral components, but evidence regarding their real-world benefit alongside pharmacotherapy remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to evaluate whether augmenting a direct-to-consumer GLP-1 RA program with a behavioral support smartphone app improves weight-loss outcomes compared with medication alone, and to identify which app features are associated with weight loss over time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted using data from 6113 adults (older than 18 years) in Australia who self-enrolled into the Mosh direct-to-consumer weight-loss program between July 1, 2024, and August 13, 2025, with their weight data recorded at baseline and at least 1 other timepoint. Participants received semaglutide or tirzepatide, with optional access to a smartphone app and clinician support. Logistic regression models examined achievement of ≥5%, ≥10%, and ≥15% weight-loss thresholds at 60, 120, and 180 days. Linear mixed-effects models interacting with app feature use, with linear and quadratic time terms, assessed the association of different features with percentage weight loss trajectories over time. Both models adjusted for medication type, gender, ethnicity, age, and baseline BMI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Participants using the program plus medication had higher odds of achieving clinically significant weight loss than those using medication only. Adjusted odds ratio point estimates for day 60, 120, and 180 (±10) days indicated they were 1.38 (95% CI 1.09-1.75) times to 2.22 (95% CI 1.40-3.45) times more likely to achieve ≥5% weight loss across timepoints, 1.67 (95% CI 1.33-2.10) times to 1.97 (95% CI 1.35-2.90) times more likely to achieve ≥10% weight loss by day 120 and 180, and 1.99 (95% CI 1.26-3.29) times more likely to achieve ≥15% weight loss by 180 days. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated that progress logging was associated with more rapid weight loss over time (β=.26 percentage-point additional weight lost per 30 days, SE 0.06;
                      <jats:italic>t</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sub>4336</jats:sub>
                      =4.46; 95% CI 0.14-0.38;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001). No other app features were consistently associated with changes in weight-loss trajectories.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Augmenting GLP-1 RA treatment with a behavioral smartphone app was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving clinically significant weight loss, although differences in overall weight-loss trajectories were modest. Progress logging emerged as the primary behavioral predictor of improved outcomes. While not causal effects, these findings are consistent with the positive value of integrating digital tools with pharmacotherapy for weight loss.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Digital Transformation of Television Broadcasting Supported by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
35b7dc9c798c6869d6eeb6921fd0c44c284f95bc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation brought about by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in television broadcasting within a conceptual and critical framework. It discusses how processes such as content production, automation, scheduling, audience measurement and personalisation have been reorganised through data-driven systems. Furthermore, by assessing the impacts of algorithmicisation on editorial independence, public accountability, transparency, privacy and accountability, the study argues that the future of television broadcasting is shaped not only by technical innovation but also by institutional and ethical choices.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Television Platforms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
054cd1bab132b082e3e6a31810c1cc1a1ff38db7.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how artificial intelligence–driven algorithms on digital television platforms transform the processes of cultural production, distribution, and consumption within the media ecosystem. Focusing on Netflix as a case study, it analyzes how algorithmic recommendation systems structure content visibility, shape user preferences, and reorganize audience behavior through data-driven mechanisms. Drawing on sociological theories of power and cultural production, the study conceptualizes algorithms not merely as technical tools but as socio-technical actors that establish new regimes of visibility and control. In this context, the notion of the “algorithmic field” is proposed to explain how platform-based systems redefine power relations, mediate cultural hierarchies, and reproduce structural inequalities. The findings suggest that digital platforms operate as influential intermediaries that both organize and govern cultural circulation in contemporary media environments.</jats:p>

title: Aesthetics of Robotic Digital Pets
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
7e635f747fbbe5476f902f978891bbe7c498f00f.abstract: <jats:p>Robots designed to replace pets are being developed to meet the emotional, social and cognitive needs of different age groups, from children to seniors. This chapter analyzes the factors that influence people's perception of robotic pets as companionable and socially present, focusing on shape aesthetics and motion quality, sound quality and textural effects and behavioral patterns. By examining the history of how humans have created and used artificial beings, it also becomes possible to understand how aesthetics has been viewed in the past and how it continues to shape expectations for the future. User expectations regarding the design of artificial pets, as well as the personalization of these products, are shown to influence acceptance and engagement. Understanding the role of aesthetics in the development of artificial pets therefore supports the creation of ethical and meaningful companions within contemporary and global society.</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
Harnessing Digital Platforms and Artificial Intelligence for Quality Assurance and Monitoring
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
6492aae0c96a95ea65d135b36278e404e91578e1.abstract: <jats:p>Digital transformation: a paradigmatic shift toward data-driven and AI-supported academic excellence in higher education quality assurance. In this chapter, we offer a holistic framework for leveraging the power of digital platforms and AI technologies to enhance quality assurance and monitoring in HEIs. Combining systematic literature review, theoretical framework development, and empirical analysis through correlation analysis,  regression modeling, and structural equation modeling (SEM), we define the essential building blocks for implementing appropriate digital QA systems. This framework integrates various data points, predictive analytics, machine learning algorithms, and real-time monitoring capabilities to deliver a comprehensive solution for managing academic quality. Concrete data points include strong, positive correlations between digital platform use and quality, and regression analysis shows that AI-enhanced monitoring systems account for a 23.7% improvement in these indicators. Results of SEM confirmed the proposed framework, with good fit indices.</jats:p>

title: Digital Transformation in Quality Assurance Policy Frameworks
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
3f9040a021853702b8ad8707e72223d87d4b3e9f.abstract: <jats:p>Digital Transformation has reconfigure the quality assurance (QA) landscape in higher education by authorizing data-driven analysis, real time monitoring and transparency in institutional processes. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, learning analytics, blockchain credentialing and integrated management information systems have augmented the dependability of QA mechanisms. This chapter examines the key factors driving digital transformation in QA including policy frameworks, institutional capacity, technological readiness, governance and stakeholder engagement. It further explains how it influences QA outcomes and institutional excellence. Draft on global research and policy literature the chapter showcase the inference for higher education institutions and offers future research directions to consolidate digital QA ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Quality Assurance in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
fb5843c135ec13caf51a5f619643fd47db8d0fec.abstract: <jats:p>In today's dynamic landscape of higher education, institutions must prove to society the societal benefits of their teaching, learning, and research. Many organizations are embracing AI-enabled quality assurance (QA) to foster a mindset of constant growth and outstanding performance inside their institutions. This approach aims to enhance education, cater to the requirements of students and communities, and ultimately help them stay competitive. The complex quality assurance system is open to multiple interpretations and potential improvements due to the interconnected nature of technology in higher education. Excellence requires continuous institutional growth. It is common for stakeholders to see quality assurance as too bureaucratic. To prioritize institutional change and ongoing improvement, modern QA frameworks should use organic and dynamic operating methods.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Platforms for Learning-Centred Quality Assurance in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
2e6b9dfed2d61a7b891e8850e05ec19839ab8002.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter theorises AI-enabled digital platforms as socio-technical quality infrastructures that orchestrate learning, accountability, and equity in higher education. It fuses constructs from quality theory, learning sciences, organisational studies, and critical datafication to recast quality as holistic capability formation rather than performance compliance. The chapter outlines competing quality lenses, sketches platform typologies and algorithmic logics, and shows how governance architectures and stakeholder attitudes co-produce datafied regimes of merit and risk. It then advances design principles for learning-centred, justice-responsive AI ecosystems that foreground equity-sensitive analytics, participatory governance, and reflexive professional judgment. The chapter contends that AI must be treated as pedagogical and civic infrastructure, with human actors retaining epistemic primacy in steering quality work toward rigorous, inclusive higher education.</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Institutional Excellence in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
6a79dc2040cd825afcfc0670158591de7a4397d7.abstract: <jats:p>Colleges and universities across the globe are being pressurized to become accountable, deliver learning outcomes and to remain competitive in the fast changing digital economy. Digital transformation has also turned out to be an impulse of developing quality assurance (QA) systems and institutional excellence, allowing the development of more transparent, data-driven, and stakeholder-focused processes. This chapter discusses how digital platforms, which include Learning Management Systems (LMS), accreditation portal, analytics dashboard, digital credentialing technologies, and AI-based assessment systems, transform quality standards on institutional, national, and global levels. Using examples of the developed world (United States, United Kingdom, Australia) and the Indian reformed higher educational system, the chapter examines policy efforts such as NAAC digital reforms, National Academic Depository (NAD), Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF).</jats:p>

title: Quality by Design
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
99a02b8d40ae031ce9afe816538422b86464b6b0.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on how AI and digitalisation are affecting assurance and improvement activities within Higher Education and how the concept of Quality by Design (QbD) can help integrate AI technologies, automated governance, and advanced analytics into institutions' processes and workflows. It contends that the digital university must undergo both a technological and cultural transformation, moving away from a compliance-driven model of quality evaluation and moving toward a model focused on intelligent, seamless assurance. The AI-Enabled Quality Ecosystem Model is designed and offered as a means of accomplishing this aim as it integrates the appropriate data infrastructure, AI-augmented human supervision, and mechanisms for continuous improvement. The chapter draws on ethical, digital, participatory governance frameworks and on the role of AI as a complement to human judgment to advance the argument that AI enhances institutional quality and integrates the key institutional elements of leadership, inclusiveness, and collaborative, adaptive learning.</jats:p>

title: Digital Assurance Ecosystems
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
ea5f0137283fa7bf65376788b0b0b8d6da893fc2.abstract: <jats:p>The high pace of digitalization of higher education has changed the quality assurance to a standard data-based institutional process instead of a long-term and compliance-based process. The chapter focuses on the digital assurance systems based on artificial intelligence, analytics, and integrated platforms as the means to facilitate the continuous quality improvement within the higher education sector. It discusses the role of AI-driven dashboards, learning analytics, predicting models, and feedback loops in the process of coming up with good decisions in the areas of teaching, learning, governance, and accreditation. Quality by Design is highlighted in which quality is actively incorporated by tracking on time, detection of risks at early stages, and remedies. It discusses the stakeholder involvement, institutional benefits, ethical issues, and case studies of AI-based quality monitoring and student success management in the near past, and hence digital platforms would be the solution providers of quality assurance systems in the future.</jats:p>

title: Semantic Governance for Quality Assurance in Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
ff18d9cb409b73c05d5b621fa5f0ffcb62ed16f2.abstract: <jats:p>Quality assurance (QA) and monitoring in higher education increasingly operate through digital infrastructures that aggregate indicators, evaluations, reports, and analyses. While these systems increase the volume and speed of evidence, they also intensify a less visible problem, semantic inconsistency, i.e., the mismatch of meanings between measures, frameworks, and interpretations. Semantic inconsistencies are not simply a matter of data management, but concern the failure to convey correct and consistent meaning, resulting in incomparable indicators, questionable conclusions, and weak legitimacy of QA decisions. This theoretical chapter develops (i) a conceptualization of semantic inconsistency adapted to quality and monitoring in higher education, (ii) a classification of the main types of inconsistency relevant to QA in higher education and (iii) an argument for why semantic inconsistency is critical in the modern era, which is characterized by demands for interoperability and accelerated institutional change.</jats:p>

title: Implicative Statistical Analysis for the Development, Reliability, and Validity Assessment of the DMAIC Inventory
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
c45c79a198b3b501105c4e59024316dc6aa28c3f.abstract: <jats:p>In the present study, an attempt is made to develop and evaluate the reliability and validity of a new research instrument, named the DMAIC Inventory (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control Inventory).This Inventory aims to identify students' needs regarding their academic programs, record the current status of courses, teaching methods, and infrastructure, and determine the causes of deficiencies in the educational process. Furthermore, it seeks to focus on improving quality, both in terms of teaching content, curriculum design, and educational performance, and on enhancing this quality through feedback, curriculum evaluation, student participation in decision-making, and continuous training of teaching staff. For the evaluation of the reliability and validity of the DMAIC Inventory, a pilot sample of 120 university students participated. The assessment was conducted using Implicative Statistical Analysis. The results indicated that the DMAIC Inventory is a reliable and valid instrument for assessing quality in higher education.</jats:p>

title: A Psychometric Evaluation of the DMADV Inventory Using the Correspondence Factor Analysis (L'Analyse Factorielle des Correspondances) Methodology
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
be833f250e2c462b61da35c9665ea20f459beefe.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of the current study is a psychometric evaluation of the DMADV Inventory created by the author using the L'Analyse Factorielle des Correspondances Methodology. The DMADV Inventory is a structured questionnaire consist of 35 items, each rated on a 5-point Likert scale. The instrument is organized around five conceptual constructs that reflect the stages of the DMADV process: DEFINE; MEASURE; ANALYZE; DESIGN; and VERIFY, which checks whether the proposed solutions are effective and meet quality standards. The evaluation procedure was initially tested using a pilot sample of 50 students. Reliability was assessed through widely used indicators, including Cronbach's alpha (α). In addition, validity was investigated with L'Analyse Factorielle des Correspondances, a statistical technique that helps verify whether the items align appropriately with the underlying conceptual dimensions. Findings supported that the DMADV Inventory functions as a reliable and valid measurement tool for evaluating and monitoring quality in higher education settings.</jats:p>

title: Building a Culture of Quality in Online and Blended Higher Education Provision
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
f831ab388c81be176afeaafdad849c83443533fb.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter discusses how a sustainable culture of quality can be built in online and blended higher education in East, West and Southern Africa. It responds to rapid digital transitions accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, which exposed gaps in quality assurance (QA), infrastructure and faculty preparedness. Using a multi-theoretical lens combining Total Quality Management, Quality Maturity Models and Constructivist Learning Theory, the study applies the PRISMA approach in twelve countries. Findings reveal disparities in policy, technology and institutional capacity. The chapter proposes a context-sensitive QA framework emphasizing continuous improvement, stakeholder engagement and alignment with national bodies such as Zambia Qualifications Authority.</jats:p>

title: Digital Quality Assurance for Refugee Higher Education
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
be7e6eff4a1727c47e4a282be62ea19a563a46f3.abstract: <jats:p>The digital turn in higher education has redefined how quality is conceptualised, delivered, and measured, yet refugee learners continue to be excluded from these transformative shifts. Among them, the Rohingya refugees in India remain structurally marginalised, with little access to accredited or quality-assured higher-education opportunities. This chapter investigates how digital quality assurance frameworks can close these educational divides by drawing comparative lessons from Germany's refugee integration model. Through a doctrinal and expert-opinion legal-policy approach, the study interprets the role of technology, regulation, and institutional accountability in building inclusive quality systems. It analyses Germany's Akkreditierungsrat standards, DAAD Integra initiatives, and data-driven monitoring as benchmarks for digital assurance, then contrasts them with India's digital ecosystem within the framework of the National Education Policy 2020. The research develops a Digital Quality Assurance for Refugee Education model that aligns with SDG 4 and SDG 16.</jats:p>

title: Healthcare Service Quality in a Global Context
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
a5466a138b5898a0169d71dcfe5e464708f11ea3.abstract: <jats:p>Delivering quality service is crucial for achieving patient satisfaction in healthcare. In the digital era and growing competition, high-quality service is essential for healthcare providers to attract both in-service and out-service users. This paper evaluates the service performance of private hospitals in Dimapur, Nagaland, using the SERVQUAL tool and a sample of 400 respondents. The findings reveal significant gaps in reliability and assurance among private healthcare providers in the district. The results indicate that private hospitals in Dimapur have not met patient expectations, highlighting the need for improved service standards and performance to address these shortcomings.</jats:p>

title: Next-Generation AI Architectures for ECG Arrhythmia Detection
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
c06f20ff59b2a1a32fbb1574e77b84f20954089e.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized cardiac healthcare by enabling rapid, accurate, and automated arrhythmia detection using electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This chapter explores advanced AI-driven arrhythmia classification techniques that integrate deep learning (DL), preprocessing, and explainable model interpretation. Emphasis is placed on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent networks, and hybrid architectures capable of learning morphological and temporal ECG features. The proposed framework covers data acquisition, filtering, segmentation, feature extraction, model training, and validation. Ethical challenges, interpretability, and clinical deployment frameworks are discussed. By bridging computational intelligence with clinical expertise, AI systems have demonstrated near-cardiologist-level diagnostic accuracy, making them vital in next-generation cardiac care.</jats:p>

title: From Knowledge Transmission to Democratic Transformation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
14a3b3c15207f76fff58adce5bfb961062efee1c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapidly evolving context of digitalisation, democratic fragility, and educational inequality has highlighted the need to change conventional teacher education practices that focus on transmission of knowledge and skills. Although teacher identity is a key concept in contemporary educational reform discussions that focus on inclusion, digital innovation and democratic citizenship, the concept is still fractured in policy, curriculum and governance. This research faces this challenge and critically explores the changing landscape of teacher education in terms of reconstructing the teacher identity as a multidimensional and transformative professional construct to support democratic transformation. In this study, the doctrinal and analytical research methodology is used, which systematically reviews and synthesizes the current educational theories, international policy instruments, governance models, and scholarly debates on inclusive education, digital pedagogy, democratic citizenship and professional development.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence for the Development of Sustainable, Intelligent, and Efficient Physical–Digital Learning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
26c5b42ef86ad41f27f523603793d198bf2cb6ce.abstract: <jats:p>The application of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving towards a new era of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable smart campus ecosystems in higher education institutions. This research aims to examine the potential of IoT-powered physical–digital learning environments and AI systems in the fields of personalized learning, intelligent campus management, predictive analytics, and sustainable resource optimization. The study also explores the opportunities and challenges associated with the application of AIoT technologies for enhancing operational efficiency, learner participation, and environmental sustainability, as well as those of cybersecurity, data privacy, interoperability, and ethical governance. The results emphasize the need to implement human-centered, secure, and sustainable technological frameworks to empower future-ready universities and foster inclusive, efficient, and resilient educational ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Outreach to Improve Statin Refills in Patients With Low Statin Adherence
container-title: JAMA
de23854ddb695fdfe0447eb59653fe35a863d47b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Importance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Statin nonadherence is a leading, addressable driver of preventable cardiovascular events. Although health systems routinely use outreach to promote preventive care, most strategies are static and lack evidence from randomized clinical trials.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To determine whether an adaptive, sequential digital outreach strategy improves short-term statin refill vs usual communication among adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) or high ASCVD risk and recent nonadherence within a rapidly implemented, health system–embedded randomized clinical trial.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pragmatic, health system–embedded, prospective randomized open blinded end point (PROBE) clinical trial using a 2-stage sequential, multiple assignment, randomized trial (SMART) design. The trial was conducted via Kaiser Permanente Northern California, an integrated health care delivery system serving more than 4.6 million members. Eligible participants were adults 18 years or older with established ASCVD or high ASCVD risk, recent statin nonadherence, and eligibility for all study communication modalities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Interventions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Participants were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive secure portal messaging, SMS/text messaging, nonsecure email, or usual communication. Initial nonresponders within 14 days underwent prespecified second-stage randomization to repeat the same outreach, switch communication modality, or receive usual communication.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Rates of 14-day statin refill following each randomization, with 28-day follow-up.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 20 604 participants (mean [SD] age, 54.8 [9.0] years; 40.9% female; 27.8% Asian, 10.9% Black, 33.6% Hispanic; 15.3% with established ASCVD), initial digital outreach increased 14-day statin refill vs usual communication (14.4% vs 12.0%; adjusted risk difference, 2.3 percentage points [95% CI, 1.3-3.4]; adjusted risk ratio, 1.20 [95% CI, 1.10-1.30]). Among initial nonresponders, second-stage outreach further increased refill (13.0% vs 10.4%; adjusted risk difference, 2.5 percentage points [95% CI, 1.3-3.7]; adjusted risk ratio, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.11-1.39]). Switching communication modalities did not improve refill vs repeating the same modality (13.2% vs 12.5%; adjusted risk ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.94-1.17]). Cumulative statin refill through 28 days was higher in those receiving any digital outreach vs usual communication (24.9% vs 21.2%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.13-1.30]). Results were consistent across prespecified subgroups.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among adults with a statin indication and recent statin nonadherence, adaptive outreach improved short-term refill vs usual communication. A second outreach produced additional gains among initial nonresponders, although switching communication modalities provided no additional benefit. These findings support adaptive, sequential health system outreach strategies to improve cardiovascular prevention when integrated into population health programs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial Registration</jats:title>
