title: Technology, Digital Life, and Happiness
container-title: The Neuroscience of Happiness
6cfac7f3569751479eaa16befe7281b6b4613f80.abstract: <jats:p>The booming use of digital technologies is changing human thoughts, emotions, and social behaviours, thus creating important questions about the role of the digital existence on the well-being. The chapter is interdisciplinary and incorporates research findings in neuroscience, psychology, behavioural science and digital sociology to examine how the digital environment and dopaminergic reward circuitry, stress response mediated by amygdala, prefrontal control of attentional and neuroplastic habit formation interact. Even though it predetermines many possible dangers, like clogging the imagination, being a good comparer, and having a fractured attention, the text also illustrates how carefully constructed technologies can strengthen personal connectivity, innovation, education, self-building, and emotional control. The authors introduce an integrated model that summarizes neurobiological, psychological, behavioural, sociocultural, and technological aspects of online well-being, therefore, providing recommendations to individuals who need to find the balance.</jats:p>

title: How Digital Life Shapes the Neuroscience of Happiness
container-title: The Neuroscience of Happiness
46c95d48febb96d6e135f4b9d09cac8a0a32344c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores how digital technologies reshape the neural systems underlying happiness, motivation, and emotional regulation. It shows that dopamine-driven rewards from notifications and algorithmic feeds can create cycles of anticipation and compulsive use, while rapid stimuli and social comparison disrupt mood stability and attention. At the same time, digital tools such as mindfulness apps, supportive communities, and therapeutic platforms can strengthen prefrontal control, reduce stress, and enhance emotional resilience. The chapter argues that digital happiness is a neuro-cultural construct shaped by both neural plasticity and technological design. It proposes neuroscience-informed strategies—mindfulness, structured digital breaks, and intentional technology use—to restore balance, and presents a neuroethical framework emphasizing autonomy, transparency, and humane design to support well-being in a digitally mediated world.</jats:p>

title: Integration of Digital Technologies in Classroom Assessment Practices: Exploring Teachers’ Attitudes, Challenges, and Future Perspectives at Al-Madinah International School (A Field Study)
container-title: Arid International Journal of Educational and physcological sciences
0bb44354e3da33b5839adc96098976154dd8f08d.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to explore the attitudes of teachers at Al-Madina International School in Saudi Arabia towards integrating digital technologies into formative classroom assessment. It also sought to identify the types of technologies used, the enablers and barriers teachers encounter, and their future visions for development. The research adopted a mixed-methods approach, utilizing both a questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. The sample included 33 female teachers from various subjects and educational levels. Results revealed generally positive attitudes towards digital integration, although levels of use varied based on subject and experience. The most notable enablers were the availability of technical infrastructure and prior training, while the main barriers were lack of time and insufficient technical support. The study concluded with recommendations such as offering ongoing professional development, encouraging innovation in assessment practices, and refining school policies to better support the effective integration of digital tools in classroom assessment.</jats:p>

title: Association Between Early Postpartum Maternal Fatigue and Infant Emotional Development: Protocol for a Prospective Cohort Study
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
11bbe5e18751b43f8cc736e18a27301d404b9959.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postpartum fatigue (PPF) is clinically defined as persistent physical and mental exhaustion emerging after childbirth that cannot be fully relieved by rest. It is distinct from postpartum depression and has a prevalence of 76.13% among Chinese women within the first postpartum week. Existing evidence suggests that maternal PPF may alter salivary oxytocin concentrations, disturb maternal caregiving behaviors, and subsequently interfere with multiple dimensions of infant emotional development, including emotional expression, emotional regulation, and emotional recognition. Objective psychophysiological measurements, such as eye-tracking and galvanic skin response, have been validated for assessing infant emotional responses. Nevertheless, most existing studies focus merely on maternal mental well-being. Local longitudinal evidence clarifying this sequential mechanistic chain remains limited, and targeted early screening and intervention strategies for PPF-affected mother-infant dyads are insufficient.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This prospective cohort protocol aims to examine the independent association between maternal PPF and the emotional development of 3-month-old infants and to explore the sequential mediating roles of salivary oxytocin and mother-infant caregiving quality. The primary hypothesis is that higher PPF severity will correlate with poorer infant emotional development outcomes. The secondary hypothesis is that oxytocin levels and maternal caregiving sequentially mediate this association.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We will recruit 412 mother-infant dyads with maternal PPF within 1 week postpartum. PPF severity will be measured by the Postpartum Fatigue Scale. Infant emotional development, covering expression, regulation, and recognition, will be evaluated via questionnaires and physiological assessments, including eye-tracking and galvanic skin response, at an infant age of 3 months. General analytical frameworks will be applied for hypothesis testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was funded and initiated in September 2025. Participant recruitment commenced in October 2025. A total of 180 mothers-infants dyads underwent eligibility screening; 146 of these dyads completed enrollment, yielding a participation rate of 81.1%. Twelve dyads withdrew before the 3-month follow-up window, and 4 dyads were lost to follow-up at the 3-month assessment. To date, 112 dyads have completed the full 3-month postpartum assessment, and the remaining participants are still under follow-up. No major protocol deviations have occurred. Data analysis of samples from participants who have completed the 3-month assessments is ongoing. According to the prespecified timeline, full sample collection is projected to be completed by December 2027, and formal data analysis will begin shortly thereafter. The study is progressing steadily in accordance with preset schedules. Full dataset analysis and submission of the final manuscript are anticipated in early 2028.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cohort will generate longitudinal evidence describing links between maternal PPF and early infant emotional development in Chinese postpartum populations. The findings may help identify high-risk mother-infant subgroups and provide real-world evidence to develop targeted early screening and dyadic support strategies for postpartum mothers and their infants.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-Enabled Digital Health Tool Implementation in Clinical Practice Settings: Umbrella Review
container-title: JMIR AI
ed6b7c7bd88c542620745d58d7720ce6fb1ecaf8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI has the potential to improve clinical decision-making, efficiency, and patient outcomes, yet adoption in routine clinical practice has been slower than anticipated. While prior studies have identified factors that influence AI implementation, a comprehensive synthesis grounded in implementation science frameworks is lacking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to qualitatively and comprehensively describe barriers and facilitators to AI implementation in clinical care settings using an implementation science determinants framework, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), and to identify AI-specific determinants not fully captured by CFIR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted an umbrella review of reviews examining determinants of AI implementation in clinical practice. In accordance with the PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews) reporting guidance, we systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for English-language reviews published between January 2013 and July 2025. Reviews were included if they addressed barriers to and facilitators of implementing AI-enabled digital health tools in clinical care settings. Determinants were deductively mapped to the updated CFIR and inductively analyzed to identify emergent AI-specific constructs. Review quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklist, and overlap among primary studies was evaluated using the GROOVE (Graphical Representation of Overlap for Overviews) tool.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-two reviews published between 2021 and 2025 were included, encompassing studies conducted from 1990 to 2025. Reviews varied in design, including systematic, scoping, rapid, narrative, and literature reviews. Overall review quality was mixed, with 9 (41%) reviews rated at 100% quality and 4 (18%) at 50% or lower. Primary study overlap was slight, with a corrected covered area of 0.4%. Determinants of AI implementation were identified across all CFIR domains. Prominent barriers at the innovation level included limited evidence of clinical impact, poor interpretability, complexity, lack of adaptability, and insufficiently representative data. Facilitators included perceived relative advantage, co-design with clinicians, and evidence of local clinical benefit. At the implementer level, low AI literacy, limited confidence, time constraints, and concerns about professional displacement were common barriers, while training and technical support facilitated adoption. Inner setting barriers included inadequate infrastructure, limited resources, poor workflow compatibility, and weak governance structures. Outer setting barriers included unclear policies, laws, and liability frameworks, whereas partnerships and cross-sector collaboration were frequent facilitators. Inductively identified AI-specific determinants included transparency, trust, accountability, model bias, data governance, model maintenance, robustness, generalizability, existential threat, and concern about loss of the human element in care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI implementation in clinical settings is shaped by complex, multilevel, and AI-specific determinants that extend beyond traditional digital health considerations. Implementation science frameworks can be adapted to incorporate these constructs. Tailored, theory-informed strategies addressing technical, organizational, psychological, and regulatory factors are essential to support safe, equitable, and sustainable integration of AI into clinical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Hidden Burnout
container-title: The Lack of Asian Leadership in Higher Education
da72c4070d373bca9db47752958337d49386efbd.abstract: <jats:p>Although one of the fastest growing groups of faculties in American higher education, Asian faculty have been least studied in relation to burnout, emotional labour and participation with leadership in higher education. This chapter explores how Asian faculty may experience hidden burnout which gets missed by the culture of academia's Asian productivity expectations and by our culture's expectation of emotional containment, as well as by the long-standing impact of the model minority myth. These dynamics can often contribute to a lack of disclosures and actual institutional action. The chapter deconstructs and stages the interplay of emotional exhaustion that occurs among Asian faculty, drawing on theories in higher education, critical race theory, and organizational psychology, as well as Asian American studies, to understand it in multiple layers. The discussion focuses on the role faculty members hold as having to be “excessively productive” while at the same time being “neutral,” “emotion free” and “compliant” player/institutional representatives.</jats:p>

title: Retracting Attention
container-title: Seeing and Subjectivity
3a0cc0cdb516ebbc09d01859d15f1425d1efc074.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Further insight is at hand in a text Bhattacharyya does not discuss, but might have, Manu’s Code Law. Here we find a description of the lived experience of the wandering ascetic (yati), depicted as consisting in a state of ambient perceptual awareness; the experience of the ascetic is one of full attentional retraction. When Kalidas Bhattacharyya writes that ‘negative attention [is] a sort of concentrated withdrawal from, rather than positive fixation of, the content whose truth is sought to be discovered’, it is negative attention as attentional retraction that he has in mind, rather than either as absential attention or apophatic attention. The ascetic’s ambient awareness consists of a field of purely marginal consciousness, and it is here alone, Gurwitsch insists, that the sense of self (the dative of presentation) is to be found.</jats:p>

title: Optimized Emergency Sign Language Recognition with Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network for Accurate Gesture Classification
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
3737bdb37c2afdac92e2c8a956436c9b57e10253.abstract: <jats:p>Sign Language Recognition (SLR) plays a significant role in improving communication accessibility for hearing-impaired individuals, particularly in emergency scenarios where fast and reliable gesture interpretation is required. However, emergency Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition remains challenging due to rapid hand movements, visually similar gestures, and complex spatial–temporal relationships among hand components. This study proposes an SLR-HIE-LKAGCN framework that integrates topology-aware spatial representation, spatial–temporal feature learning, graph-based gesture modeling, and optimization-based parameter adaptation for emergency ISL recognition. Initially, input gesture frames are processed using a Simplicial Convolutional Filter (SCF) to preserve higher-order spatial relationships among hand regions and enhance gesture representation. The refined gesture sequences are then provided to a Spatial–Temporal Knowledge-Embedded Transformer (STKET) to capture temporal dependencies and contextual movement patterns. The extracted features are further analyzed employing a Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network (LKAGCN), which models relationships among hand landmarks and learns discriminative gesture representations. In addition, the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA) is employed to optimize critical network parameters and improve model convergence. The proposed framework is evaluated on emergency ISL gesture categories, including accident, call, doctor, help, hot, lose, pain, and thief. Experimental outcomes establish that the proposed technique achieves superior recognition performance with 98.82% accuracy, 98.57% precision, and 98.53% F1-score, outperforming existing approaches. The obtained results indicate that SLR-HIE-LKAGCN provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for real-time emergency ISL recognition.</jats:p>

title: ATT-SV2-ES Net: Hybrid Deep Learning Features and Lightweight Attention-Based Model for Early Glaucoma Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
bc275378bb5009d7f256155d09bb39b3c0bf9888.abstract: <jats:p>Glaucoma is one of the main causes of permanent blindness. Timely intervention is ensured by its early and precise identification. This paper proposes a new hybrid approach, integrating handcrafted features with Deep Learning (DL), for reliable glaucoma identification and prediction on the G1020 dataset. Initially, pre-processing is conducted, which includes data augmentation to increase the diversity of images, Gaussian filtering to reduce image noise, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to enhance local retinal contrast and then grayscale conversion to simplify retinal image representation. After pre-processing, the enhanced images were given to Depthwise Dilated Spatial Attention Mechanism (DDSAM)-based Glau-SegNet for optic disk (OD) and optic cup (OC) segmentation. From the segmented images, handcrafted features, such as Local Binary Patterns (LBPs) and fractal analysis, which describe complementary texture and structural information, are extracted. In parallel, the segmented images are processed by the Attention ShuffleNet V2 with Echo State Network (Att-SV2-ES Net) to obtain high-level deep feature representations. Then these deep features and handcrafted features are concatenated and fed to a fully connected layer with sigmoid activation to classify into the class for the prediction of glaucoma. This combined approach achieves a balance between high accuracy and scalability, addressing the growing need for accessible and reliable glaucoma screening solutions. The experimental results demonstrate the proposed system’s superior performance in detecting and predicting glaucoma. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the proposed model, which integrates DL features, outperforms all other models in terms of key performance metrics, including achieving 99.32% specificity, 99.43% sensitivity, and 99.37% accuracy.</jats:p>

title: Engagement Patterns and Clinical Outcomes Among Adolescents and Young Adults Enrolled in the Somethings Digital Peer Support Platform: Retrospective Observational Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
953c4720688eb14be414f54a77f8999fcbb1a1a0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adolescent mental health needs remain largely unmet, particularly among youth in geographically underserved communities. Digital peer support is a promising approach to expanding access to mental health support, yet real-world evidence on engagement patterns and clinical outcomes remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The purpose of this study was to characterize engagement patterns and real-world outcomes among adolescents and young adults enrolled in a commercially available, text-based peer support platform.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective observational study analyzed secondary data from 5673 adolescents and young adults enrolled in a commercially available digital peer support platform from January 29, 2023, through June 3, 2026. Engagement was operationalized as communication days per month. Standardized clinical outcome measures (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9], Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 [GAD-7], and World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index [WHO-5]) were administered as part of routine measurement-based care. Ordinary least squares regression was used to examine predictors of engagement, and complete-case pre-post change scores were evaluated across 4 assessment windows among participants with paired assessments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The sample was predominantly female (4600/5673, 81.1%) with a mean age of 16.4 (SD 2.1) years and moderate-to-severe symptom burden at baseline (PHQ-9: mean 12.6, SD 6.1; GAD-7: mean 10.7, SD 5.0; WHO-5: mean 44.8, SD 21.0). Of enrolled adolescents and young adults, 98.1% (5565/5673) had at least one recorded engagement with the platform, with a mean of 4.56 (SD 6.12) communication days per month. Female sex was a significant positive predictor of engagement intensity (β=.64, SE 0.22;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.004). Hispanic and Latino adolescents and young adults engaged significantly more frequently than White or non-Hispanic adolescents and young adults (β=.61, SE 0.26;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.02). Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) shortage score was significantly and positively associated with engagement intensity (β=.08, SE 0.02;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001). Baseline symptom severity was not associated with engagement intensity (β=.094, SE 0.23;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.68). Among participants with complete baseline and follow-up data (1437/5673, 25.3%), an exploratory complete-case analysis found within-measure paired scores improved significantly from baseline to follow-up across the PHQ-9, GAD-7, and WHO-5. At last assessment, 31.9% (237/742), 36.6% (222/606), and 37.8% (168/442) of adolescents and young adults met clinically meaningful improvement thresholds on the PHQ-9, GAD-7, and WHO-5, respectively.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Text-based peer support shows preliminary promise as a scalable approach to expanding mental health access for underserved adolescents, though clinical improvement estimates are based on the subpopulation exposed to the digital peer support platform and may not generalize to the full enrolled population. Prospective, controlled studies with more complete outcome ascertainment are needed to establish causal efficacy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
488230a323f4a1db95fece744265b1e2765b04ec.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer have substantially improved survival, resulting in a growing population of survivors of childhood cancer who may experience long-term treatment-related sequelae. Cognitive late effects are an important long-term consequence of childhood cancer and can affect cognitive functioning, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Digital health interventions offer accessible and flexible approaches to managing cognitive difficulties among children with cancer. However, the existing evidence has not yet been comprehensively synthesized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to map and synthesize the existing evidence on digital health interventions for cognitive management among children with cancer; characterize intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components; and identify evidence gaps and priorities for future research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O’Malley framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist. Six academic databases, including PubMed, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, were systematically searched for relevant studies published between January 2010 and August 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the population-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Screening was performed independently at the title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved through discussion and, when necessary, consultation with a third reviewer. Descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis were used to synthesize the findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 5371 records were identified through the literature search. Following screening, 19 publications representing 14 independent study samples and involving 566 children with cancer were included. Four digital health modalities were identified: computer-based interventions, internet-based interventions, mobile apps, and neurofeedback training. Computer-based interventions were the predominant modality. Across these modalities, working memory and attention were the most frequently targeted cognitive domains, while feasibility, acceptability, and adherence were the most commonly assessed implementation-related outcomes. However, relatively few interventions incorporated coach support, telephone-based communication, or educational components, and none evaluated economic outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health interventions that combine cognitive training with supportive care, education, monitoring, and communication. Multicenter randomized controlled trials should subsequently evaluate these interventions using clinically meaningful outcomes, with comprehensive assessments of safety, adherence, implementation, and health economic outcomes to establish their effectiveness, feasibility, and sustainability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Effectiveness of a Multicomponent Digital Therapeutic Program on Inhaled Medication Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: JMIR mHealth and uHealth
2bc33ab0b8ca8bbbac0cbbb8d8a5f79d36217054.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Poor medication adherence is a critical impediment to effective chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management and remains challenging to track in routine care. Digital therapeutic interventions may improve chronic disease management through remote monitoring and patient education. However, most existing digital interventions focus on individual components of disease management, and evidence from longer-term pragmatic randomized controlled trials evaluating integrated digital therapeutics in routine clinical practice remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent digital therapeutic program combining electronic inhaler monitoring (EIM) with behavioral support in improving medication adherence and symptom-related outcomes among patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers, and to assess patient engagement and implementation in routine clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this prospective, open-label, unblinded, randomized controlled trial, patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers were enrolled and randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either the intervention group or the control group. All participants received an EIM device to objectively record inhaler use throughout the 24-week study period. Patients in the intervention group also received personalized medication reminders from the EIM, adherence feedback, educational content, and clinician-supported follow-up through an integrated digital management platform based on EIM-derived data, whereas the control group received usual care. The primary outcome was medication adherence over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included exacerbations, COPD symptoms, quality of life, and lung function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 158 participants were randomized, including 106 in the intervention group and 52 in the control group. The median monitoring coverage was 161.5 (IQR 86.3‐168.0) days during the follow-up period. The self-reported adherence measured using the Test of Adherence to Inhalers showed no significant between-group differences at any follow-up time point. However, the electronically monitored adherence was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (59.5% vs 33.1%,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.009). Adherence declined over time in both groups, decreasing from 85.3% during weeks 0 to 4 to 43.0% during weeks 12 to 24 in the intervention group and from 76.8% to 11.9% in the control group over the same intervals, resulting in a progressively larger between-group difference over follow-up. No significant differences were observed in exacerbations, health-related quality of life, symptom burden, lung function, or mental health outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, a significantly greater proportion of participants in the intervention group achieved the minimal clinically important difference in the COPD Assessment Test score than in the control group (odds ratio 2.21, 95% CI 1.11‐4.41;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.02).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The multicomponent digital therapeutic program significantly improved objective medication adherence in patients with COPD over 24 weeks. While most clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, the higher proportion of participants achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in the COPD Assessment Test score warrants further investigation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Climate and Digital Transitions Among Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in Africa: The Role of Development Finance Institutions
container-title: Frugal Innovations, Eco-Innovations, and AI Innovations in Modern Small Businesses
8b27d253570775e220ff4e8a070d64f9459a0838.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this chapter, the authors examine the role of Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) in enhancing climate and digital transitions among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The authors iterate the crucial role of these transitions in achieving resilience, competitiveness and sustainability among MSMEs’ amid evolving global challenges. Additionally, the authors explain the importance of DFIs in providing critical financial and technical assistance, enabling MSMEs to adopt climate-smart technologies and embrace digital transformation. The authors also highlight case studies illustrating successful DFI interventions. This chapter concludes by emphasising the need for DFIs to prioritise outreach to marginalised communities, balancing developmental goals with financial sustainability and capacity building to scale their impact.</jats:p>

title: Engagement-Supportive Mechanisms in Stress-Focused Digital Mental Health Interventions With Adaptive, Conversational, and Context-Aware Systems: Narrative Review
container-title: JMIR Human Factors
7301e19c45feefeb630a365b5b8099fa710a891f.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Stress is a widespread public health concern associated with cardiovascular disease, depression, anxiety, and reduced quality of life. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs), delivered through smartphones, web platforms, and wearables, offer scalable support for stress management but often struggle to sustain user engagement. Evidence describing how adaptive, conversational, and context-aware mechanisms function together within stress-focused DMHIs remains fragmented.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This review aims to synthesize evidence on engagement-supportive mechanisms in stress-focused DMHIs, with attention to personalization; biometric feedback; just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs); gamification; AI, including large language models (LLMs); and methodological approaches to studying engagement. It also examines methodological, motivational, and experiential dimensions of engagement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This narrative review was informed by a structured search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2018 and April 2025, followed by an evidence update through August 2026. Eligible studies described stress-focused DMHIs or related affective support interventions reporting at least 1 engagement-supportive mechanism. Randomized controlled trials, qualitative investigations, simulation or modeling studies, and implementation studies were included. Data were extracted using a structured form capturing study characteristics, engagement mechanisms, outcomes, and alignment with the review domains. Descriptive mapping summarized study types and mechanism frequencies, while a narrative synthesis integrated behavioral, experiential, methodological, and theory-informed findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. Randomized or microrandomized controlled trials were the most common design (n=17), followed by qualitative investigations (n=6), design or implementation studies (n=3), mixed methods studies (n=3), simulation or modeling studies (n=2), and a quasi-experimental study (n=1). Dynamic adaptation was identified in 14 studies, conversational support in 10, static tailoring in 9, social or co-design mechanisms in 9, context-aware prompting in 7, gamified reinforcement in 5, biometric-responsive adaptation in 4, and narrative immersion in 2. These mechanisms frequently overlapped within layered adaptive architectures rather than functioning as isolated engagement features. AI-enabled systems included conversational agents, LLM-supported systems, recommender systems, reinforcement learning, and computational modeling approaches. Outcomes included behavioral indicators such as adherence, retention, and prompt receptivity, alongside experiential indicators such as perceived relevance, trust, emotional support, and immersion. Evidence strength varied substantially; many AI-enabled systems contributed feasibility, acceptability, or optimization-oriented evidence rather than definitive comparative effectiveness evidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Stress-focused DMHIs are increasingly adopting adaptive, conversational, and context-aware engagement-supportive mechanisms, but the evidence base remains heterogeneous and methodologically uneven. Dynamic adaptation, conversational support, and static tailoring were most frequently represented, whereas biometric-responsive adaptation, narrative immersion, and deeply integrated gamified systems were less common. AI-enabled systems may support contextual responsiveness and personalized interaction but require transparent adaptive logic, privacy safeguards, and human-centered evaluation. Future work should prioritize longitudinal, mixed methods research capable of distinguishing behavioral engagement, experiential engagement, feasibility, acceptability, and sustained stress-related outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital Twin Technologies for Plasma Reactor Modeling and Optimization
container-title: Theory, Applications, and Impacts of Advanced Plasma Engineering
3126707e07403a777025e8a7263a74fb5f1629d5.abstract: <jats:p>Technology based on the creation of a digital twin has been developed as an innovative solution to cope with increasing complexities of modern plasma engineering systems. Traditional approaches to modeling plasma reactors are focused on performing static simulations, empirical optimization, and inadequate experiments to obtain insights into their behavior. However, due to nonlinear dynamics of plasma reactors, these methods do not provide comprehensive understanding of their complex behavior. The use of edge computing, cloud computing, robotics, and autonomous control systems has enabled the application of digital twins in the areas of semiconductor processing, plasma medicine, advanced material synthesis, environmental remediation, aerospace propulsion systems, fusion energy, and plasma-assisted manufacturing. The current chapter offers an in-depth look at the principles, architectures, methods, applications, optimization techniques, limitations, and future possibilities associated with digital twins of plasma reactors.</jats:p>

title: Maternal Health Outcomes of Digital Health Interventions in Low- and Middle-Income Countries in Southeast Asia: Scoping Review
container-title: Asian/Pacific Island Nursing Journal
f49e7cd3356464d89b8b2c9eac76e9e3454f488d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Digital health interventions (DHIs) have gained increasing attention as strategies to improve maternal health in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Previous reviews of DHIs have included studies from Southeast Asia (SEA) but have not examined maternal health outcomes in SEA LMICs as a distinct regional evidence base.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review aimed to map maternal health outcomes of DHIs in SEA LMICs using an adapted proximal-intermediate-distal (PID) framework, describe DHI characteristics, and summarize contextual factors related to target groups and intervention settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The review followed the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) and the Joanna Briggs Institute guidance. PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus were searched for English-language interventional studies evaluating DHIs that were published from January 2005 through May 2025. Google Scholar, reference lists, and the Index Medicus for the South-East Asia Region were searched as supplementary sources. Maternal health outcomes were mapped using an adapted PID framework, and all results were summarized descriptively.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-five studies from 7 SEA LMICs were included. Mobile apps and SMS were the most commonly used technologies, reported in 22 (88%) studies. Fourteen (56%) studies reported maternal health outcomes across more than one PID domain. Intermediate outcomes were reported most frequently (n=23, 92%), followed by proximal knowledge outcomes (n=10, 40%) and distal biomedical and clinical outcomes (n=8, 32%). Findings related to proximal knowledge outcomes were predominantly significant, whereas intermediate and distal outcomes showed mixed results. All but one study (n=24, 96%) recruited participants through existing health care services, and most interventions were implemented in primary care settings (n=17, 68%).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Maternal health outcomes were represented across all 3 PID domains, with intermediate outcomes reported most frequently and distal biomedical and clinical outcomes least frequently. Future studies should give more attention to distal biomedical and clinical outcomes, as well as underrepresented SEA LMICs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title:
Three-dimensional particle velocimetry in digital in-line holography
				via a channel-attention autofocusing network
container-title: Applied Optics
f645074bdb03734330a8cf37f576379abaf3187a.abstract:
<jats:p>Three-dimensional particle velocimetry using digital in-line holography
					is limited by axial localization errors. This paper proposes a method
					based on a channel-attention autofocusing network (CAF-NET), which
					predicts particle axial distances end-to-end via a channel attention
					mechanism and reconstructs three-dimensional velocity fields combined
					with a two-frame matching algorithm. On a public dataset, CAF-NET
					reduces the average axial localization error by 40.4% compared to
					FocusNET and improves PSNR and SSIM by 16.7% and 6.7%, respectively.
					In simulated velocimetry, the average absolute velocity error is
					reduced by 40.9% relative to FocusNET. Experiments yield a maximum
					relative error of 6.7% for the measured average velocities. The method
					effectively mitigates the impact of axial localization errors on
					velocimetry, offering a high-precision solution for holographic
					three-dimensional flow field measurement.</jats:p>

title: Surface contouring of reflective and diffuse samples using dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry
container-title: Applied Optics
f7e95171c668b2140ffa8cdb75473a935df5f18f.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, a grating-based dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry system is presented for generating synthetic wavelengths and extending the measurable height range. A geometric-phase (GP) grating and mirror configuration generates laterally sheared wavefronts at multiple shear orientations, while a polarization camera enables simultaneous phase-shifted intensity acquisition. Measurements are performed at two illumination angles, and the reconstructed complex wavefields are combined to obtain a synthetic phase distribution whose sensitivity is determined by the angular separation between the two measurements. The system was experimentally evaluated using standard step-height artifacts and surface features on both reflective and diffuse samples. Step-height measurements demonstrated the dependence of measurement performance on the selected synthetic wavelength. An analytical uncertainty analysis identified the illumination angle as a significant contributor to the overall measurement uncertainty, emphasizing the importance of system calibration using a standard artifact. Temporal repeatability was also evaluated through repeated measurements. The results demonstrate the capability of grating-based dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry for quantitative three-dimensional surface reconstruction while maintaining a compact common-path configuration.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
Electrifying Tourism
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
ade9a7b0c000e4daa35c59a0be1889d6014f749f.abstract: <jats:p>Electric transport represents an important approach towards achieving sustainability within the tourism sector and providing tourists with better transport means and more enjoyable journeys. In this regard, the present chapter focuses on how electric cars, buses, bicycles, scooters, and ferries may be used in tourism. Through the study of recent literature as well as country-specific examples from Norway, Iceland, China, Greece, France, Canada, and Italy, this chapter analyzes the various environmental, economic, and experience-based advantages of electric mobility within the tourism sector. Moreover, issues related to the uptake of electric transport by the tourism industry, including problems of charging infrastructure, policies, investments, and consumer behavior, are discussed. Theoretical perspectives such as the Theory of Planned Behavior and Technology Acceptance Model are analyzed as well to determine travelers' behavior regarding electric transport.</jats:p>

title: Role of Electric Transportation in Enhancing Tourist Experience
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
e7c644ea139820441fefbea966dcf9e0a5547129.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of electric transportation and tourism is transforming sustainable mobility and visitor experiences. This chapter examines how electric buses, e-bikes, e-scooters, electric ferries, and autonomous shuttles enhance tourism through sustainability, smart technology integration, and universal accessibility. Drawing on recent peer-reviewed literature, policy documents, and international case studies, it demonstrates that integrated electric mobility ecosystems supported by renewable energy, digital infrastructure, and inclusive design improve visitor satisfaction, environmental quality, and destination competitiveness. The chapter also discusses challenges such as range anxiety, charging infrastructure, and accessibility barriers, and concludes with policy recommendations and future research directions aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the UNWTO 2030 Tourism Agenda.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Mobility and Electric Ride Hailing in Tourism Management
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
43a119d8d43a3474c23e969ab8d6529e489a5c2f.abstract: <jats:p>Transportation is the largest contributor to tourism-related carbon emissions, creating challenges for sustainable tourism development. This chapter examines the role of electric ride-hailing systems within the broader framework of sustainable mobility and low-carbon tourism. It discusses the concept of sustainable mobility, the environmental impacts of tourism transportation, and the emergence of electric ride-hailing as an innovative mobility solution. Drawing on international case studies, the chapter highlights key opportunities, challenges, and policy considerations associated with adoption. The findings suggest that electric ride-hailing can support emission reduction, improve accessibility, and enhance transportation efficiency when supported by appropriate infrastructure, governance, and stakeholder collaboration, thereby contributing to more sustainable tourism systems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Transformation in Smart Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
bdb23f442d428cea7c60fce9bd787c0e0f234367.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization has intensified congestion, pollution, and inefficiencies in transportation systems, necessitating sustainable and intelligent mobility solutions. Smart mobility has emerged as a transformative approach driven by digital transformation and advanced technologies. This chapter examines the role of the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Big Data Analytics, and Cloud Computing in enhancing operational efficiency, real-time decision-making, and service integration. It conceptualizes smart mobility through Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS), enabling seamless coordination among stakeholders. Drawing on global and Indian examples, the chapter highlights the impact of digital platforms and electric mobility. It also addresses challenges such as infrastructure limitations, regulatory complexity, data privacy, and the digital divide. Finally, it proposes a framework for sustainable, efficient, and user-centric smart mobility systems.</jats:p>

title: Green Transportation Strategies for Hotels and Tourism Destinations
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
97dd0471f02229140159ce6d04a733a4560a867c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on green transportation strategies as a key component of sustainable tourism, which is essential in the path towards achieving net-zero, climate-resilient tourism. This chapter adopts a critical narrative review method that integrates a multidisciplinary review of the literature on smart urban mobility, environmental psychology, and tourism management. The results show that smart transportation solutions, like predictive navigation and electric mobility, have a significant impact on reducing traffic jams and carbon emissions. Stakeholders receive actionable frameworks based on the Avoid-Shift-Improve concept to easily integrate green transport, sharing and dynamic pricing into the hotel business and regional planning. Finally, this chapter provides an overview of tourist psychology and hospitality management to build resilient tourism systems from the bottom up (micro) to the top (macro) of the destination.</jats:p>

title: Design of AI-Based Perception Systems for Real-Time ADAS
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
d91ce310e605baffdae89107a02d0159ddd145de.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based embedded perception for real-time Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) for trustworthy electric ride-hailing services. It reviews recent perception approaches for road-scene understanding, including lightweight convolutional models, You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors, compact vision transformers, low-light perception, radar-aware methods, and multimodal fusion. Particular attention is given to safety-critical road elements such as pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists, obstacles, traffic signs, and traffic lights, because they directly influence driver awareness, decision-making, and perceived safety. The chapter proposes a methodological framework covering dataset selection, ADAS task definition, data preparation, model selection, AI optimization methods, embedded deployment, and evaluation. By linking perception reliability with perceived safety, user trust, and behavioral intention, the chapter positions embedded ADAS perception as a key contributor to the adoption of electric ride-hailing services.</jats:p>

title: Electric Ride-Hailing and Sustainable Mobility in Tourism
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
638e76b7eccb79512c031f2f30de6c75244c33e7.abstract: <jats:p>This book chapter examines electric ride-hailing as a strategic solution for sustainable mobility in tourism destinations. It explores how electric vehicle fleets, digital ride-hailing platforms, charging infrastructure, business models, and destination governance can jointly support low-carbon, smart, and visitor-friendly tourism mobility. The chapter highlights that tourism destinations face growing challenges such as congestion, pollution, weak last-mile connectivity, seasonal demand, and pressure on destination sustainability. It argues that electric ride-hailing can improve airport transfers, hotel connectivity, attraction access, safety, payment convenience, tourist experience, and destination competitiveness. The chapter also discusses fleet-owned, aggregator, hotel partnership, MaaS, subscription, and public–private business models for scalable tourism mobility.</jats:p>

title: Socio-Economic Impacts of Electric Ride-Hailing Services
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
2de488357061569d8c6156451c654e89d1671d73.abstract: <jats:p>Electric ride-sharing is a paradigm-shifting mode of urban transportation that combines the benefits of digital platforms (i.e., scalability, efficiency) with clean transportation technologies (i.e., electric). As we have seen, ride-sharing can produce large amounts of greenhouse gases, estimated to be about 69% greater than the trips they replace, but the electric vehicle represents a key solution to reducing emissions associated with urban transportation. In this Chapter, we will explore the various socio-economic implications of electric ride-sharing, and particularly how these new modes of transportation are reshaping economic systems, social relationships, and environments. From an economic perspective, electric ride-sharing has generated growth in markets, increased efficiencies in costs, and created jobs, yet at the same time challenged traditional taxi and transport sectors. From a social standpoint, electric ride-sharing has enhanced access to affordable and inclusive mobility options; influenced consumer behaviors relative to travel; and shaped tourist trends.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Campus Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
97361003db90435a242e827f01d09cd7561bb035.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of electric bicycle-sharing systems in promoting sustainable campus mobility within higher education environments. The purpose of this chapter is to analyze the challenges, opportunities, and strategic implications of implementing electric bicycle-sharing systems through perspectives of user acceptance, behavioral intention, smart mobility, and sustainability-oriented governance. The discussion highlights urban mobility issues, infrastructural and institutional barriers, environmental and ethical concerns, and the integration of digital technologies in smart campus ecosystems. Furthermore, this chapter explores solutions related to user engagement, inclusive mobility innovation, infrastructure development, and policy frameworks supporting sustainable transportation. Future research directions concerning digital transformation, smart mobility ecosystems, and data-driven transportation management are also discussed to support long-term sustainable mobility transitions in higher education institutions.</jats:p>

title: Sacred Pilgrims Meet Smart Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
2c08c58b31077e9ced33672f5cc506c606de8c6e.abstract: <jats:p>Religious tourism is one of the major forms of tourism, where almost 330 million pilgrimages are made every year. As Electric Ride-Hailing Services (ERHS) gain popularity, the mobility trends of pilgrimage areas are changing, providing sustainable and effective ways of mobility. This chapter explores the theoretical linkages of the religious tourism and e-ride sharing adoption in Ayodhya-Mathura-Varanasi pilgrimage circuit using secondary sources of data. The study emphasizes the positive and negative effects of ERHS, such as lower emissions, better transportation options, equity aspects, carrying capacity, but also issues of cultural appropriation. Past studies suggest that there are significant demographic differences in technology adoption, with younger and more educated people having greater acceptance than older and less educated.</jats:p>

title: Impact of Electric Ride-Hailing on Heritage Tourism Experience
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
f979b437ccc4180f6b285f099a083a3aa2570c48.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the impact of electric ride-hailing on tourist experience, perceived authenticity, and tourist satisfaction in heritage tourism destinations. Using a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of 54 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, this chapter explores the relationship between sustainable mobility and visitor experiences. The findings show that electric ride-hailing improves accessibility, convenience, flexibility, and environmental sustainability while influencing how tourists engage with heritage environments. Mobility is identified as an experiential component of tourism rather than merely a transport service. The review further highlights that authenticity and satisfaction are shaped by both service quality and meaningful cultural engagement. This chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking mobility, tourist experience, perceived authenticity, and satisfaction, and provides implications for sustainable destination management and heritage preservation.</jats:p>

title: Understanding the Electric-Taxi Travel Experience Through Identity, Autonomy, and Anxiety
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
b41e83d8bb453710cd9b87555c0ca5a4f01b3ba2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how sustainable travel identity, perceived autonomy, and electric vehicle usage anxiety shape travellers' hedonic experience of electric taxis. Drawing on experiential consumption, self-determination, environmental self-identity, and perceived-risk perspectives, it develops an experiential mobility framework for platform-mediated travel. Survey data were collected online from prospective electric-taxi users in Delhi, India. After screening 250 responses, 227 cases were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings identify perceived autonomy as the principal predictor of hedonic travel experience. Sustainable travel identity did not significantly influence autonomy or enjoyment, and its indirect effect through autonomy was unsupported. EV usage anxiety was positively associated with autonomy but did not directly affect hedonic experience, indicating that anxiety may encourage information seeking and preparedness rather than restrict perceived control.</jats:p>

title: From Common Asset Demand to Intermediary Choice: A Focused Reanalysis of Attention Complementarity across U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs
container-title: The Journal of FinTech
1ecd734f11db66af0507144de857e9a9ea778797.abstract: <jats:p>The launch of U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds created an unusual allocation problem: 10 intermediaries offered nearly the same underlying exposure, yet their flows diverged sharply. This paper is a focused reanalysis of the fund-flow and Reddit panel introduced by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]. It does not present the dataset, text measures, BrandScore or the baseline sentiment-by-visibility association as new. Instead, it asks what the established association reveals about the division between category demand and intermediary choice. The contribution consists of three interpretive emphases applied to estimates already reported by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]: within-date differences across funds as evidence about allocation, asymmetry across the conditional flow distribution and variation across market states. The pairwise flow-sensitivity formulation makes the allocation interpretation explicit. In the previously reported two-way fixed-effects model, common daily shocks are absorbed and the sentiment-by-visibility coefficient is identified from differences in issuer visibility among funds facing the same Bitcoin news. The coefficient is positive, the direct visibility effect changes sign between large-redemption and large-creation states and the interaction appears less consistently during stressed markets. The Driscoll–Kraay and issuer-bootstrap checks apply to the baseline coefficient (2.930), not the two-way fixed-effects coefficient (3.802), for which those checks were not conducted. The evidence is thus an associative allocation regularity, not a causal social-media effect: differences in issuer visibility are consistent with different flows across financial wrappers conditional on common category sentiment.</jats:p>

title: MULTIMODAL SPATIOTEMPORAL BIOMECHANICAL MODELING FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL INJURY RISK SCREENING OF BODY MOVEMENTS BASED ON CROSS-MODAL ATTENTION NETWORK
container-title: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology
f75d4115ac94c6b86ec43f361db77e566c5bf6af.abstract: <jats:p>Ethnic dance involves large-amplitude and repetitive movements that may impose substantial and uneven mechanical demands on the musculoskeletal system, potentially increasing the risk of joint and soft-tissue injuries. Conventional injury assessment relies largely on manual observation and clinical evaluation, which limits the ability to continuously and quantitatively characterize movement-related risk. To address this limitation, this study proposed a Cross-Modal Attention-based Injury Risk Perception Network (CMA-IRPN) for noncontact movement analysis, movement-pattern risk screening, and injury risk assessment in ethnic dance. The framework jointly modeled Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) video sequences and human skeletal keypoints. A dual-branch encoder combining a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) and a graph convolutional network (GCN) was used to extract spatiotemporal visual and skeletal features, while spatiotemporal cross-modal attention modules were introduced to model interactions between movement appearance and joint-topological information. The model was evaluated for movement recognition using the publicly available MPII Human Pose and SportsPose datasets and for movement-pattern risk grading using a self-constructed ethnic dance dataset. CMA-IRPN achieved accuracies of 96.03% and 94.86% on the MPII and SportsPose datasets, respectively, with statistically significant improvements over the comparison models ([Formula: see text]). On the ethnic dance dataset, the model achieved a Macro-F1 score of 92.25% for movement-pattern risk grading and a sensitivity of 93.75% for the high-risk category. These results suggest that CMA-IRPN can identify risk-related movement patterns from noncontact multimodal data and provide quantitative support for movement screening and injury risk assessment in ethnic dance training. The predicted risk levels represent visual–kinematic movement patterns rather than direct measurements of joint torque, tissue stress, or other mechanical loads and therefore should not be interpreted as operational real-time injury early warnings or as substitutes for clinical biomechanical assessment or medical diagnosis.</jats:p>

title: #GirlDad: Exploring the representations of Black fatherhood in digital spaces
container-title: Communication, Culture & Critique
fd53ba85d1fdcc5643e0fdfcc57cf87fdd6c2489.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article explores representations and identity politics surrounding Black fatherhood on Twitter (now known as “X”) through the #GirlDad hashtag. First, we interrogate Black heteronormative practices of masculinity to situate the historical and contemporary framing of Black fatherhood in media representations. Next, we examine how Black men utilize Twitter, situating #GirlDad within collective mourning during media disasters. Using thematic analysis, we analyzed a purposeful sample of #GirlDad tweets from Black fathers to reveal patterns in their articulations of fathering daughters. This paper argues that #GirlDad operates as a political form of digital escorting and resistance, whereby Black fathers publicly display involvement and resist absentee narratives. These counternarratives challenge stereotypical representations of Black fatherhood by imagining new definitions and promoting communal relationship building among Black fathers.</jats:p>

title: Derechos digitales y educación en Suramérica: privacidad, protección de datos y acceso educativo
Digital rights and education in South America: privacy, data protection and access to education
container-title: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales
51db361c59c8bb83382256f745c25ba84087494b.abstract: <jats:p>La educación mediada por plataformas digitales amplió las posibilidades de acceso, pero también expuso a estudiantes y docentes a la recolección de datos personales y a brechas de conectividad. El artículo analizó la relación entre el derecho a la educación y los derechos digitales, en particular la privacidad y la protección de datos, en Suramérica. Se realizó una revisión documental de normas constitucionales y legales de Ecuador, Brasil y la Unión Europea, instrumentos internacionales y literatura arbitrada, con análisis en tres ejes. Se identificó que el acceso a la educación depende hoy de infraestructura y de competencias digitales, que la protección de datos de menores exige reglas específicas y que ambos derechos se refuerzan o se debilitan según el diseño de las plataformas. Se concluye que las políticas educativas digitales deben incorporar la protección de datos desde su diseño. No se recogieron datos primarios.</jats:p>

title: AI and the Digital Divide in Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
6f35cbc8c37837db42e9888922aa3f76c437d688.abstract: <jats:p>The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) into the educational field promises a revolution of greater individualization, automation, and access however, unequal access poses a risk of amplifying already extant socio-economic and gender, as well as geographic, digital inequality, favouring some and disadvantaging others. In the chapter, the researcher conducts a meta-analysis of policy frameworks in various nations and regions globally to explore how structural obstacles, including poor infrastructure, teacher ill-equipment, and forms of governance vacuums, could limit the equitable use of AI, further fuelling algorithmic bias, exclusion and ethical hazard. It offers a threefold equity-based argument connecting computer infrastructure, educator maturity improving, and answerable information mechanisms, intended to carry out decentralized, responsible, and sustainable AI practices.</jats:p>

title: Ethical AI and Financial Inclusion
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
b0a013beb14c35675ffb52135d960aea3b6a70e3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of ethical artificial intelligence in advancing inclusive financial education for persons with disabilities within contemporary digital financial systems. It aims to analyse how AI-driven technologies can enhance access to financial knowledge, improve decision making, and support participation in formal financial services. The chapter also explores the risks associated with algorithmic bias, data inequality, and limited representation, which may reproduce existing patterns of exclusion. It further discusses the importance of inclusive design, accessibility, and ethical governance in the development and deployment of AI systems. The chapter argues that financial literacy, when supported by responsible and context-sensitive AI, can contribute to economic empowerment and social inclusion. It concludes by outlining institutional and policy strategies required to ensure equitable and sustainable financial participation.</jats:p>

title: Visual-Auditory Assistive Systems for People With Visual Impairment
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
0f243d3bed6fd13cf514ca1c736e49a820b62b59.abstract: <jats:p>Visual impairment makes the same state of visual information that is available to others inaccessible for people with vision impairment, creating a major difficulty to their independence. In this paper, an integrated deep Learning system is evaluated to assist persons with vision impairment in automatically understanding scenes. The system generates descriptive image captions and sends them to the speakers. VGG-16 is used as a feature extractor, but LSTM networks and attention mechanisms are often used in the encoder-decoder pipeline. Combined models translate visual information effectively into auditory feedback. However, some difficulties still remain. The system must work in real time, maintain high accuracy in various practical scenes, and meet users' daily needs for testing. To advance from research into practical assistive technology, future work should focus on adding modern architectures, such as Visual Transformers; exploring multimodal learning; bringing accessibility even closer with edge devices; and setting up rigorous, human-centered benchmarks for evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Empathetic Digital Leadership
container-title: Governance for Sustainability, Resilience, and Innovation
6e36dbcf27fd9077eea7376620ff324efa90bc72.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how compassionate leadership might enhance resilience in public administration and strengthen digital governance. This chapter aims to investigate how emotional intelligence enhances the legitimacy of governance, builds institutional trust, and supports leadership effectiveness in digitally evolving public sectors. The conversation focuses on important issues in governance transition, such as organizational resistance, legitimacy threats, and gaps in leadership competencies. Additionally, the chapter offers public sector organizations implementation tools and a framework for empathic leadership. To promote theoretical advancement and innovative governance, future research avenues are suggested. This chapter advances knowledge of human-centered leadership strategies that facilitate sustainable public management and adaptive governance in quickly changing digital contexts.</jats:p>

title: Design and Development of An Iot-Based Digital Scale for Measuring Cement Weight Using A Load Cell Sensor at Pt Semen Tonasa, Balikpapan Branch
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Networking and Internet of Things
38c49952e7a774648a167b0d3ce377206cc224a4.abstract: <jats:p>Manual cement weighing in the industrial environment of PT Semen Tonasa, Balikpapan Branch, is considered inefficient and prone to human error. This study aims to develop a prototype Internet of Things-based digital conveyor weighing system capable of automatically measuring, sorting, and monitoring the weight of cement packages. The system is controlled by an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with a load cell sensor and an HX711 amplifier module to read the dynamic weight of packages moving on the conveyor. The conveyor belt is driven by a DC motor with a BTS7960-series driver, while a servo motor serves as the sorting arm actuator. The system is programmed to recognize a target cement weight of 500 grams with a tolerance of 10 grams. Remote monitoring is performed through a local web server dashboard with a client–server architecture that displays indicators and weighing history charts without excessively burdening the microcontroller memory. Test results show that the system successfully identifies peak loads dynamically, allows on-target packages to proceed, and automatically removes nonconforming packages. The device demonstrates very high accuracy, with an average reading error of only 0.63%. The system exhibits substantially better precision and operational consistency than conventional weighing methods</jats:p>

title: Digital Forensic Analysis of a Case of Pornographic Content Dissemination on WhatsApp Using the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Method
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Networking and Internet of Things
24ae9ffc0d6f3eb270924486470e872df2264723.abstract: <jats:p>The dissemination of pornographic content through instant messaging applications such as WhatsApp is becoming increasingly widespread. A major obstacle to establishing legal proof in these cases is that perpetrators frequently use the "Delete for Everyone" feature to eliminate digital evidence. This study aims to apply the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) method to obtain digital artifacts from messages deleted on the perpetrator's device. A simulated scenario was conducted between the victim's device (Xiaomi Redmi 10C) and the perpetrator's device (a rooted Xiaomi Redmi S2). The investigation used MOBILedit Forensic Express for physical acquisition and Belkasoft Evidence Center for data analysis. The results show that the NIST framework successfully overcame anti-forensic obstacles. The recovered digital evidence included metadata from 3 deleted text messages with logical deletion status, 3 image files containing pornographic content (.tmp/.jpeg), and 2 video files (.mp4). Cross-validation between fragments from the perpetrator's msgstore.db database and the victim's screenshots demonstrates that this method can produce legally valid and compelling electronic evidence for court proceedings.</jats:p>
