title: Jones matrix extraction using single-shot common-path digital holographic measurement
container-title: Optics Letters
f560691a84d1a2e5aafbd10da30a414a17dc76e3.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, we propose a compact, polarization-sensitive, single-shot, common-path digital holographic microscopy (PSC-DHM) system for extracting the Jones matrix of anisotropic specimens. The proposed approach employs Fourier multiplexing to simultaneously record multiple polarization-dependent interference terms within a single hologram, thereby capturing complete polarization information in a single camera exposure. The multiplexed hologram is processed to reconstruct the optical fields, and subsequently the Jones matrix elements are evaluated. Experimental results obtained from birefringent samples validate the capability of the proposed system to accurately retrieve phase and polarization properties. The proposed technique offers a simple, stable, and efficient solution for quantitative polarization imaging and Jones matrix characterization in digital holography.</jats:p>

title: Cybersecurity Awareness and Digital Literacy for Students and Educators Strengthening Data Privacy with AI-Powered Cybersecurity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
30cafb06bf9daabec321a6848bf1479377de9a8e.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to investigate the significance of cybersecurity awareness, digital literacy, and artificial intelligence in fostering data privacy protection for students and teachers in North India. The study was an exploratory descriptive study with a cross-sectional quantitative design, based on primary data gathered from a structured questionnaire with 620 respondents. The methods used were descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression. The correlation was positive for all of the variables, and the highest was between the AI-driven cybersecurity and data privacy protection (r = .741, p < .001). The results of the regression showed that artificial intelligence cybersecurity, digital literacy and cyber security awareness had significant predicting power for data privacy protection, accounting for 66.3% of its variance. The results highlight the need for a holistic approach to integrating AI into education, fostering digital literacy, and raising cybersecurity awareness to ensure safer and privacy-conscious learning spaces.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Financial Phishing and the Digital Literacy Deficit Protecting Student and Young Learner Data
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
65ab6f5f760fd3d653bfc26c66ada7b9512e9487.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence has structurally transformed financial phishing, collapsing the cost of personalised attacks; India recorded 135,173 financial phishing attacks in H1 2024, a 175% rise over 2023. This chapter examines the convergence of AI-enabled phishing, student data vulnerability, and digital literacy deficits in India's skill-based educational institutions (ITIs, polytechnics, skill universities), a population absent from existing cybersecurity literature despite holding data regulated under the DPDP Act, 2023. Drawing on Routine Activity Theory, Protection Motivation Theory, the Digital Literacy Continuum, and Institutional Theory, it develops the Protection Gap construct and a Four-Layer Institutional Defence Model. A primary survey (N = 96, seven states) finds 66.7% encountered suspected phishing, mostly via WhatsApp; only 25.0% identified a genuine message; 59.4% were unaware of the DPDP Act; and 43.8% reported no explicit consent for Aadhaar/bank data. The chapter closes with recommendations for MeitY, AICTE, NSDC, and the Data Protection Board of India.</jats:p>

title: AI-Generated Deepfakes and Trust in Digital Communication in Namibia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
9ae33c567c1e3c1be30b3c19886f0820b1ea2ad9.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the development of deepfake technology, enabling the creation of highly realistic fabricated audio, video, and visual content that closely resembles authentic media. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining an online survey of 47 Namibian internet users and a total of 12 key informants were interviewed. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were subjected to thematic analysis. The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on deepfake technologies by providing empirical evidence from Namibia and offering practical recommendations for enhancing digital literacy, strengthening regulatory frameworks, and improving institutional preparedness.</jats:p>

title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network
container-title: Applied Optics
8265acd6d2b87f6713dd6ef322c348c2ccd4b056.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Phase aberration compensation based on iteratively reweighted Zernike polynomial fitting for digital holographic microscopy
container-title: Applied Optics
717cdbec8bc18ada1558dfd35fa00220c37d18df.abstract: <jats:p>Phase aberration compensation is essential for quantitative imaging in digital holographic microscopy (DHM), as undesired background distortions severely degrade phase measurement reliability. Conventional Zernike polynomial fitting (ZPF) either relies on manually or automatically selected background regions, which restricts its applicability to samples with sparse or ambiguous background, or performs a global least-squares (LS) fit over all pixels, in which sample structures and outliers bias the estimated aberration. This work proposes a global iteratively reweighted ZPF (GIR-ZPF) method to overcome these issues. The proposed method performs global fitting using all valid pixels across the full field and introduces a Tukey-based iterative reweighting strategy to suppress structural and outlier interference, thereby eliminating the requirement for background selection. Simulation results show that, compared with the naive global ZPF (G-ZPF), GIR-ZPF reduces the RMSE and MAE of phase reconstruction by ∼13.3%, increases the PSNR from 24.8 to 26.0 dB, and improves the Zernike-coefficient estimation accuracy by nearly two orders of magnitude, while reaching an accuracy comparable to mask-based ZPF methods without requiring any mask prior. Experiments on microspheres and live A549 cells demonstrate that GIR-ZPF achieves flat phase backgrounds, clear sample contours, and well-preserved microstructural features. GIR-ZPF provides an effective and robust solution for phase aberration compensation of samples with sparse or ambiguous backgrounds in DHM.</jats:p>

title: PMDA-Net: a polarization-conditioned multi-scale dynamic attention network for polarimetric hyperspectral camouflage target classification
container-title: Applied Optics
e3741308864e6d0ff381ac36b7b4229b1f39913f.abstract: <jats:p>To effectively fuse heterogeneous polarimetric hyperspectral data and improve the classification performance of camouflage targets in complex backgrounds, this paper proposes a polarization-conditioned multi-scale dynamic attention network (PMDA-Net). PMDA-Net adopts a dual-stream framework for modality-specific feature extraction, where spectral and polarimetric information are separately modeled. A multi-scale dynamic AoLP attention module is designed to transform geometric information encoded in the angle of linear polarization into dynamic weights. A polarization-conditioned spatial-channel attention module is designed to adaptively calibrate spectral features using polarimetric information, facilitating cross-modal interaction and complementary feature fusion. Experimental results on three self-collected datasets and one public dataset show that PMDA-Net outperforms mainstream hyperspectral deep learning models, traditional polarization-feature-based methods, and recent multimodal fusion methods on all four datasets. Compared with the model using only hyperspectral information, PMDA-Net improves the average accuracy by 5.87, 5.38, 25.71, and 5.01 percentage points on the four datasets, respectively. These results indicate that polarization information can effectively complement spectral representations and help suppress aliasing responses caused by spectral similarity in complex scenes. This work provides a promising approach for polarimetric hyperspectral image classification and camouflage target recognition.</jats:p>

title: Single-image phase retrieval method  based on fusion coding of fringe and digital speckle patterns
container-title: Applied Optics
4774675cd2bdb18b0fed7d09bc5a5d3878b9d1ec.abstract: <jats:p>To address the challenge of balancing speed and accuracy in structured light-based 3D reconstruction, this paper proposes a single-image phase retrieval method based on the fused coding of fringe patterns and digital speckle. By employing the GD-DCUNet model—integrated with multi-branch dilated convolution for feature extraction, a residual fusion mechanism, and an information integration and distribution strategy—the method achieves the effective separation of fringe pattern and digital speckle information from the fused coded image. With the assistance of a newly constructed CSAS-UNet, the separated fringe pattern image is used to predict the numerator and denominator terms of the wrapped phase. Concurrently, the separated digital speckle image is utilized to predict the fringe order via correlation calculation with a reference speckle image. Under a multi-constraint strategy involving epipolar lines, wrapped phases, and connected domains, this correlation calculation significantly narrows the search range of candidate points matching the sampling points, thereby providing robust and rapid fringe order prediction. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-precision phase retrieval using only a single image. It maintains exceptional stability and reconstruction quality even on complex surfaces and low-texture regions, indicating promising potential for engineering applications.</jats:p>

title: Digital product imports and firm productivity: do winner-takes-all dynamics arise?
container-title: Oxford Economic Papers
6ca6427dac04dbd8fe9751b5ad6ce7f8c8f44860.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article examines how imports of digital products affect the productivity of Chinese manufacturing firms. Digital products, including advanced machinery, electronic equipment, and software-related technologies, may enable firms to upgrade production processes and adopt new technologies. Using three instruments and two exogenous shocks, we find that digital imports significantly enhance firm productivity, with effects substantially larger than those of traditional product imports. Digital intermediate goods raise productivity primarily through innovation and technological spillovers, while the evidence suggests that competitive pressures are an important channel for digital capital goods. Both channels help capable follower firms catch up with frontier firms and expand their market shares. Overall, the findings suggest that digital imports promote selective productivity catch-up rather than the winner-takes-all outcomes often emphasized in the literature on high-income countries.</jats:p>

title: Playology
516b87233a939c6cf8ec30574d0b1518aad42230.abstract:
<jats:p>Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village offers a sharp, timely exploration of how digital technologies and global media reshape the ways we think, communicate, and understand ourselves. As multinational corporations like Google increasingly mediate our access to information, identity, and civic life, this book examines the profound consequences of living in what it calls the “Googleburg Galaxy.”</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Blending cultural critique with accessible theory, the book traces how our practices of reading, writing, and meaning making have been transformed by digital systems that both empower and constrain. It argues that play—reimagined as a form of critical media literacy—is essential for navigating these complexities. Through play, individuals can question dominant narratives, expose hidden power structures, and reclaim agency over their digital lives.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>By unpacking the ideologies embedded in contemporary media and the subtle ways they shape citizenship, knowledge, and authenticity, Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village invites readers to engage more consciously with the technologies that define modern existence. It is a call to resist passive consumption, embrace creative inquiry, and cultivate the critical literacies necessary for a more open, pluralistic, and humane digital future.</jats:p>

title: Dichotomies Reconsidered: Towards More Reliable Conceptual Tools of Social Science in the Digital Age
container-title: Insecurity and the Eclipse of Enlightenment
2ec5c7e914db6d84ac0cf49e7e38b1269c6e7500.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter examines binary oppositions in social sciences. There are four types of such concepts in the tradition of social thought identified, which might be labelled as 4D of social sciences: dualism, dialectic, distinction and dichotomy. Dualisms rest on assumptions of polarized nature of a substance and are ontological in their matter; dialectic is primarily a methodological tool of comprehending opposites in their dynamical relation; distinctions are logical instruments that enable observing an aspect of reality different than the other, while a dichotomy presumes that an entity consists of two confronted categories. A special attention is given to dichotomies as most frequently present form of 4D’s in the legacy of social sciences. On the one hand, their epistemological merits as a heuristic tool in depicting emerging modern societies opposite to traditional societies are acclaimed; on the other hand, they are unfolded as contentious forms of concepts, often providing over simplistic image of a far more complex social reality. Therefore, in the final section, possible refinements of dichotomies in direction of their capability to grasp intermediaries and fine details between the two opposites are discussed. This discussion is set in the framework of recent attempts of digitization of a social theory, though combination of digital and analogue mode of theorizing is suggested in the final instance.</jats:p>

title: Validating the Shift to Digital Diary Journal as a Pedagogical Tool for Student Social-Emotional Growth
container-title: Negotiating Faith, Fact, and the Future of Higher Education
f8b4c386e77eb6131965b54aa7fbfcaf7ba06d83.abstract: <jats:p>Diaries using books and pens have been a vehicle for years for fostering students' emotional development. Their role remains dominant and unwavering despite the ever-changing dynamics of the times. This study aims to validate a digital diary journal platform developed to foster social and emotional learning in elementary school students. Through the 4D model of development research method, data were processed. Six expert validations, including lecturers from computer science, visual communication design programs, psychology and also elementary school teachers, validated the digital diary platform's design to ensure it meets the needs of elementary school students. The results indicate that the digital diary platform is attractive and capable of contributing to students' SEL with a UI/UX feasibility level score of 3.8 and a content feasibility level score of 4.53. However, further refinement of the platform is needed in terms of user experience, interface, and digital diary content.</jats:p>

title: Use of Digital Transformation to Create an Inclusive Learning Environment in Tourism by Mediation of Artificial Intelligence in Africa
container-title: Inclusion and Diversity in Business and Tourism Education
17dc2e9d71a5c2404fd74c20991d5e29adb15fed.abstract: <jats:p>Inspecting the connection among digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), as well as the synthesis of inclusive environment of learning in the awareness among tourists sector is the article's primary goal. It tackles the issue of how this technological synthesis can augment educational accessibility and participation for a range of scholar demographics. The investigation employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews to gather data from educators and scholars. Key outcomes demonstrate that digital transformation considerably promotes inclusivity in learning experiences, while AI plays a critical mediating function in personalizing education and catering to expert scholar requirements. In order to incubate more equitable environment of learning s, educational institutions should strategically incorporate digital tools along with artificial intelligence (AI) into their curricula, as per to the outcomes. Future initiatives assimilate comparative investigations across various educational contexts.</jats:p>

title: Global Health at the Crossroads in 21st Century
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
bf5b791a1fdca3dc6b1be16bffda51af575a3d3d.abstract: <jats:p>Global health in the 21st century is at a crossroads as digital innovation rapidly transforms health systems while exposing deep institutional challenges. This paper explores growing role of digital technologies such as AI, big data, telemedicine, improving disease surveillance, service delivery, and health system efficiency. At the same time, it critically examines the institutional constraints that shape the adoption and governance of these innovations, including regulatory fragmentation, limited infrastructure, and unequal digital capacity. Ethical concerns related to data privacy, algorithmic bias, and exclusion of marginalized populations are highlighted as central governance challenges. The chapter argues that without robust institutional frameworks, digital health innovations risk reinforcing existing inequalities rather than reducing them. It concludes by emphasizing the need for coordinated global governance, inclusive policy design, & strengthened public institutions to ensure that digital innovation advances equity, accountability, and resilience in global health systems.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Health Policy for Reducing Global Health Inequalities
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
a214df633cac73fcb7c72dbe04bdbf9a60400dd6.abstract: <jats:p>There are still high levels of inequality in healthcare access, quality of services and health outcomes between regions and populations in global health systems. Digital health technologies and Artificial Intelligence have already become the potential solution to close such disparities through better disease surveillance, increasing telemedicine service access, and assist in making health policy decisions based on the data. This chapter explores how AI-powered healthcare applications and digital health platforms can help to enhance healthcare access and health surveillance of populations as well as identify critical issues related to governance, ethical issues, data privacy, and the digital divide. The chapter, based on the conceptual analysis and the recent case studies, outlines the policy strategies that should be in place to ensure the responsible, inclusive, and equitable implementation of AI technologies in the healthcare systems across the world.</jats:p>

title: Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence in Global Health Policy
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
9d2e274995dd8f32b7735b3232f10a964121b207.abstract: <jats:p>Digital health and artificial intelligence are becoming influential in shaping global health policy due to the opportunities they will offer in improving access, efficiency and health outcomes globally. At the same time, such technologies spark critical issues regarding inequality, ethics, and governance-especially in developing countries in low-income and middle-income countries. This chapter focuses on how digital health and AI are changing the global health systems and just how both these can have a positive effect or a threat towards those who might not have access to usable technology or AI. It examines policy issues concerning governance, regulation, and human rights and the role of international collaboration when working towards equitable and responsible adoption of health technologies using artificial intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Infodemic and Information Warfare
container-title: Innovation, Governance, and Resilience in Global Health Systems
9091786ca356292581ffc9b46446f803cf327b1b.abstract: <jats:p>The paper examines the impact of infodemics and information warfare on public health and democratic processes in the digital age. Disinformation in modern conditions is no longer just an information problem; it has become a strategic tool that influences public behavior, reduces trust in institutions, and increases health risks. Special attention is paid to the COVID-19 pandemic as an example of information warfare that has deepened polarization and facilitated the spread of manipulative narratives. The paper analyzes national and international legal mechanisms, including issues of the regulation of digital platforms. The study concludes that information security is an integral component of public health protection in modern society.</jats:p>

title: Digital Intelligence and AI-Based System Optimization in Waste-to-Energy Infrastructure for Net-Zero Cities
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With AI and Machine Learning
ff36013178296736d6e2747d2c7e1830b32bd841.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital intelligence and artificial intelligence in waste-to-energy (WtE) infrastructure optimization to achieve net-zero cities is presented in this chapter. The rapid urbanization and the growing amount of waste demand efficient and sustainable solutions. Municipal waste is turned into energy in WtE systems, and traditional operations lack flexibility and efficiency. The chapter uses systematic literature review as a method on the topic indexed in more than 200 articles and summarizing main conclusions of the quality research. It discusses monitoring with IoT, digital twins, and real-time optimization based on AI and predictive maintenance and energy recovery that is better. Case studies show the changes in the operational efficiency, emission control, and stability of systems. A conceptual AI-enabled framework is presented to find a solution to combine WtE systems with smart grids and urban energy networks. The results conclude on how smart WtE infrastructure contributes to the use of the circular economy and sustainable, low-carbon urban development.</jats:p>

title: Digital Constitutionalism and the Protection of Customary Law People’s Rights in Indonesia
container-title: Verdict: Journal of Law Science
1550186a7789202fdb696659dd9f4104a7a42a91.abstract: <jats:p>Digital revolution has altered the manner in which public authority is administered and how citizens engage with public services, partake in democratic activities, and assert their constitutional rights. This research examines the effects of digital transformation on the constitutional rights of customary law communities and delineates Indigenous Data Sovereignty within the Indonesian legal system. Contemporary studies on digital constitutionalism mostly emphasise individual rights, state power, and the governance of digital platforms, but Indigenous Data Sovereignty discourse specifically underscores collective management of Indigenous data. However, the relationship between these two fields remains insufficiently developed in Indonesia, particularly with communal data, indigenous wisdom, and cultural identity. This research employs a normative legal approach utilising statutory and conceptual frameworks. Primary and secondary legal texts were collected through library research and analysed qualitatively. The findings suggest that digital transformation improves cultural preservation, information availability, civic participation, and public service provision. Concurrently, it fosters unequal digital accessibility, administrative exclusion, diminishment of community control over collective data, and the unauthorised utilisation of indigenous knowledge without authorisation or fair benefit-sharing. Indonesia’s personal data protection framework primarily emphasises identifiable individuals and is deficient in explicit restrictions concerning communal data or collective detriment. This research contends that Indigenous Data Sovereignty should be founded on recognising communal data and customary law communities as collective rights-holders, employing consent based on traditional practices, guaranteeing community governance over data access and use, instituting benefit-sharing, performing collective impact assessments, ensuring institutional oversight, and delivering effective remedies.</jats:p>

title: MOSQMIXERNET: A CUSTOM DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURE FOR EARLY-STAGE MOSQUITO CLASSIFICATION AND GENUS-LEVEL IDENTIFICATION
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
3f9de5f6c7ac23f07c42f175676e294f0e8b124c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, zika, and chikungunya impose a disproportionate heavy public health burden on Africa. While artificial intelligence (AI) tools have been applied in species identification on the adult mosquitoes, the early aquatic stages have been largely ignored. Yet, these early stages are critical since vector control strategies often target larvae and pupae to break the transmission cycle before mosquitoes mature into biting adults. Moreover, the identification of these specimens is prone to human error by experts due to the striking similarity in morphological features between larval and pupal stages across species. This limitation delays surveillance and increases the risk of misclassification, potentially compromising vector control efforts. In response, an Africa-based curated dataset is introduced, encompassing the larval and pupal stages of Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex species, along with non-mosquito specimens of similar morphology. This dataset helps address the underrepresentation of African samples in global repositories and provides a rare contribution to pupal-stage classification, a category largely overlooked in most classification tasks. MosqMixerNet is introduced as a lightweight deep learning model designed for image-based classification of mosquito early stages. The proposed MosqMixerNet balances compactness and accuracy with only 169 666 trainable parameters and was benchmarked against MobileNetV2, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile. For genus-level identification, it achieved 99.37% accuracy, surpassing NASNetMobile (97.30%), MobileNetV2 (97.26%), and DenseNet121 (80.39%). The work advances computer vision for public health and tropical disease control, and provides a foundation for integration into digital vector monitoring platforms in endemic settings.</jats:p>

title: Postpartum fatigue: a concept analysis
container-title: British Journal of Midwifery
08789c1deaa2d04dc70104279d9bbcec9e17fc32.abstract: <jats:p>Postpartum fatigue is a multidimensional condition commonly experienced by women during the early postpartum period. It has been associated with substantial physical, psychological and social impacts on women. This concept analysis aimed to clarify the concept of postpartum fatigue, distinguish it from related phenomena and develop a more precise definition to support operationalisation in research and clinical practice. Three defining core attributes were found: persistent subjective discomfort manifested as prolonged fatigue and energy depletion that is not alleviated by short-term rest; reduced physical activity capacity resulting in functional dependence for basic activities of daily living; and decreased mental capacity, particularly impaired attention, concentration and cognitive processing. The condition's antecedents span biological, psychological, social and environmental domains, including intrapartum blood loss, perineal pain, hormonal changes, sleep disruption, role transition, low social support and sociodemographic disadvantages. Its consequences include delayed physical recovery, impaired mobilisation and wound healing, disruption of the mother–infant bond and an increased risk of postpartum depression.</jats:p>

title: Tau hadronic decay channel reconstruction with a Lorentz-covariant graph attention network
container-title: Physica Scripta
48dd6af93c13d027dd2a5b2312100fb17c5e3a52.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The reconstruction of hadronic decay modes of the
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    lepton is a key task in high-energy physics experiments, directly impacting precision measurements and new physics searches. Conventional reconstruction approaches rely on handcrafted features and rule-based algorithms, which face challenges in handling complex decay topologies and detector effects. In this work, we propose LCGA-Net, a physics-informed deep learning framework for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay channel classification and four-momentum reconstruction. The method represents decay products as particle graphs and employs a multi-head attention mechanism to capture inter-particle correlations. To ensure physical consistency, Lorentz-invariant constraints are explicitly incorporated into the model architecture. A dedicated single-
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    dataset is constructed from the simulation data of the Circular Electron Positron Collider, covering six major hadronic decay modes. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.2% on the validation set, matching or slightly exceeding baseline models. More importantly, full physics constraints substantially improve the physical plausibility of reconstructed four-momenta—particularly the energy–momentum relation—without degrading classification performance. These results demonstrate that integrating physics priors with attention-based deep learning on particle clouds provides an effective approach for
                    <jats:italic>τ</jats:italic>
                    decay reconstruction, with potential applications in future high-energy physics analyses.
                  </jats:p>

title: Pembuktian Digital dan Pertanggungjawaban Pidana Pelaku Penjualan Akun Streaming Premium Ilegal: Perspektif Hak Cipta serta Batasnya terhadap <i>Terms of Service</i> dan UU ITE
container-title: Verdict: Journal of Law Science
bf1a4c4bf1b308dc3fd22ddd77000c616dfcf57a.abstract: <jats:p>The rise of subscription-based streaming services has been accompanied by the unofficial sale of premium accounts through social media and digital marketplaces in Indonesia. Although such practices are commonly labelled illegal, the label does not automatically establish criminal liability. This study addresses two issues: first, how difficulties in digital evidence and offender anonymity constrain criminal enforcement, and the standing of electronic evidence in linking offenders, accounts, transactions, and copyright-related objects; second, how criminal liability of sellers of illegal premium streaming accounts is constructed under the Copyright Law, and where its limits lie in relation to Terms of Service violations and offences under the Electronic Information and Transactions Law. Using normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, the study analyses primary legal materials and secondary literature through descriptive-analytical qualitative analysis. The findings show that digital infringement leaves no physical trace, so proof depends on authentic, intact, and relevant electronic evidence supported by digital forensics. Criminal liability under the Copyright Law arises only when the act is committed without right or permission, relates to economic rights over protected works, including computer programs, is carried out for commercial use, involves fault and capacity to be held accountable, and is proven by valid electronic evidence. Violations of Terms of Service remain contractual, while the Electronic Information and Transactions Law applies only when its prohibited elements are met. The study contributes a framework linking digital proof with criminal liability in digital copyright enforcement.</jats:p>

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
container-title: Journal of Product & Brand Management
f4411bb0ddc28ff8c7ca11de384db891845accaf.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adoption potential, timeline and implementation measures for bio-digital integration in South African construction: a modified Delphi study
container-title: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
09260d9d2b1e62bf4440faed69464f113c4b9415.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Limited empirical evidence exists on the adoption potential, expected implementation timeline and measures required to support bio-digital integration in developing-country construction contexts. This study aims to examine expert perspectives on these dimensions within the South African construction industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An exploratory modified Delphi approach was adopted with 12 built environment experts. Adoption potential and expected timelines were assessed using categorical scales and descriptive statistics. Fifteen implementation measures were evaluated using a ten-point Likert scale and reassessed in a second round following controlled feedback. Consensus was assessed using median, interquartile deviation and percentage agreement, with mean and standard deviation additionally reported for Round 2.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The expert panel indicated moderate adoption potential and predominantly anticipated adoption within 6–10 years and beyond. Regulatory frameworks, circular economy principles and workforce training were among the most highly rated implementation measures. However, consistently high ratings across all measures indicate limited differentiation between their relative importance. A structured adoption pathway is proposed to support implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings reflect the perspectives of a small, predominantly academically affiliated expert panel and should not be interpreted as representative of the South African construction industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings provide context-specific guidance for policymakers, industry stakeholders and researchers on policy development, capacity building and innovation investment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides context-specific empirical evidence on expert assessments of bio-digital integration in South Africa by jointly examining adoption potential, anticipated timelines and highly rated implementation measures within a single framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Digital Evolution of Migration Management in the Russian Federation: Stages, Tools, and Legal Risks
container-title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AND PROCEDURE
d4468aef69f6d0153d066280ec14e7aa52225f7d.abstract:
<jats:p>The article examines the stages of the digitalization process of migration management in the Russian Federation.
The article analyzes innovations based on the State Migration Registration Information System created in 2007, including
the Register of Controlled Persons and the Digital Profile of a Foreign Citizen. Experiments based on the use of digital
technologies to improve the rules and conditions of entry into the Russian Federation, to introduce additional mechanisms
for accounting for migrant workers, as well as the automatic termination of a patent are considered. The shortcomings
of legal regulation have been identified, measures have been proposed to eliminate them, as well as to improve the
management of migration processes using modern digital technologies.</jats:p>

title: Administrative Liability for Violations in the Sphere of Digital Currency Circulation: Issues of Defining Offense Elements and Prospects for Legislative Development
container-title: ADMINISTRATIVE LAW AND PROCEDURE
09d9b7697e26bf7eb33286344f2bb9a8cf46316c.abstract:
<jats:p>The article examines the theoretical and practical issues of establishing the institution of administrative liability
for violations in the sphere of digital currency circulation in the Russian Federation. Based on the analysis of federal laws
of 2020–2026, legislative initiatives including Draft Federal Law No. 1194944-8, as well as doctrinal approaches to defining
the legal nature of digital currency, the author identifies systemic shortcomings in the legislative construction of new
administrative offence compositions. It is substantiated that the fragmentary nature of legislative activity, the absence
of a unified conceptual framework and a procedural mechanism for bringing to liability create risks of regulatory
inconsistency and reduce the effectiveness of legal regulation. An author’s classification of offences in the field under
study is proposed according to the subject composition, the nature of the act, and the degree of public danger, and specific
proposals are formulated for the systematisation of the compositions within a new chapter of the Code of Administrative
Offences of the Russian Federation.</jats:p>

title: Self-attention-aided multi-layer CNN-LSTM for non-uniform 4-level differential amplitude modulation and detection with atmospheric turbulence for OWANs
container-title: Optics Express
fedd060d0254eff3eb9ce0c2cc0964613783fd42.abstract: <jats:p>This paper proposes an environment-aware four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation and detection scheme assisted by self-attentive multi-layer CNN-LSTM (SA-CNN-LSTM) for optical wireless access networks (OWANs) under atmospheric turbulence, to mitigate severe distortions induced by atmospheric turbulence in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems. Relying on four-level non-uniform differential amplitude modulation (NUADM-4) and a self-attention-aided detection algorithm at the receiving terminal, the proposed scheme can effectively suppress both multiplicative turbulence fading and additive Gaussian noise simultaneously. Numerical results reveal that the proposed scheme achieves remarkable bit error rate (BER) improvements compared with conventional detection frameworks for NUADM-4, and it substantially outperforms the classical uniform four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) across diverse turbulence strength regimes. Moreover, the tailored architecture integrating self-attention with multi-layer CNN-LSTM maintains high transmission efficiency, reduces the dimension of the fully-connected layer at the receiver to a certain extent, and accelerates the computation speed compared with the CNN-based algorithm. In comparison with conventional detection-aided algorithms such as vanilla CNN, LSTM, and MLP, the presented scheme delivers a universal BER performance gain. Furthermore, the machine-learning-aided design philosophy for different modulation systems offers a practical design paradigm and implementable solution for the engineering deployment of high-speed OWC systems serving OWANs operating in volatile atmospheric turbulence environments.</jats:p>

title: The Antecedents of Trust and Its Effects on Credibility Within Digital Infrastructure
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
a60dd27e017c4b64f6840b661e9f7bbbd2753353.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the antecedents of digital trust and their influence on brand credibility within digital infrastructure, encompassing websites, e-commerce platforms, the Internet of Things (IoT), and chatbots. The chapter concludes by identifying gaps in the literature around competence and benevolence in emerging and AI-driven digital technologies, and proposes a future research agenda focused on cross-cultural and empirical investigation of these antecedents, intended to support students, researchers, policymakers, and brand managers engaging with questions of trust in digital environments.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain-Enabled Supply Chain Transparency
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
86065cac2611a56130774f5b230d0727cdc835e3.abstract: <jats:p>The blockchain has emerged as a new technology that is revolutionizing the transparency of the supply chain, allowing for the decentralization, security, and protection of data in Industry 4.0 environments. Often the traditional supply chains lack real-time visibility and have traceability problems, fraud, and counterfeiting. Smart contracts, decentralized identity management, and cryptographic security mechanisms are just a few of the ways that blockchain increases trust, automation, and accountability. The chapter offers insights into evolving innovations like blockchain-based digital twins, NFT product authentication, and AI-powered predictive analytics for intelligent supply chain management. In addition, the chapter outlines future trends like quantum-resistant cryptography, cross-chain interoperability, and autonomous supply chains powered by Web3 to enhance transparency, efficiency, and security in the global supply chain.</jats:p>

title: Bridging the Digital Divide
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
9ee41e2d5686c557723f6c732c26a61e168620d6.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid rise of digital technologies has been a game-changer in global communication, commerce and governance, but it has also created the spread of digital inequality and complex cybersecurity challenges. The chapter provides an overview of the relationships of digital inequality and cybersecurity risks with evolving global governance system. Digital inequality manifests as uneven access to digital infrastructure, digital literacy and online economies and is disproportionately prevalent among disadvantaged populations and nations. Meanwhile, the expansion of digital network exposes people, organizations,nations to cybersecurity threats, including cyber-crime, systemic insecurity, data breaches, which can undermine trust and socioeconomic systems. The chapter explores the role of international governance arrangements, and partnerships in minimizing the risks and promoting equitable access to technology. The case studies indicate the success stories and failures of multilateral treaties, cybersecurity policies and public-private partnerships in solving access and security problems.</jats:p>

title: Data Sovereignty and Algorithmic Governance in Developing Economies
container-title: Enabling Human Transformation Through Socio-Technical Systems in Industry 4.0
6fdbeb58e96e829a460768ed1eba7412a41afc2e.abstract: <jats:p>Data is among the most contested resources of the twenty-first century. Citizens in developing and middle-income economies generate it constantly through mobile transactions, health services, and social platforms. Yet, the infrastructure that processes it and the governance frameworks that regulate it have largely been designed elsewhere. This chapter examines data sovereignty and algorithmic governance as twin pillars of an equitable digital transformation agenda, using South Africa as its primary lens. It argues that three connected interventions are essential: sovereign infrastructure architecture, algorithmic transparency and accountability, and genuine community participation in governance design. Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and institutional economics, the chapter demonstrates that data sovereignty cannot be achieved through any single instrument but requires deliberate alignment between technical architecture, governance institutions, and participatory process to produce inclusive Fourth Industrial Revolution outcomes in structurally unequal economies.</jats:p>

title: Digital and AI tools in informal care: understanding caregivers’ experiences in rural Nigeria
container-title: Working with Older People
9193766175c91a5d0c22308aaadf2db77e3cb6ef.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although informal caregiving for older adults is well-researched, a significant gap exists in understanding how informal caregivers navigate their caregiving roles with the help of digital technologies, especially in rural Nigeria, where internet connectivity is poor and access to digital devices is limited. This study aims to explore how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support care for older adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study adopted a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 10 informal caregivers, using semi-structured interviews. The data were further analysed thematically using NVivo 14.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results identified that caregivers use digital technology for communication and care coordination, learning and self-empowerment, responding to emergency situations, improving efficiency, reducing stress and maintaining contact between older adults and their diaspora family members. The study also found poor access and limited internet infrastructure as barriers to the use of digital technology to improve caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Only caregivers in rural areas were interviewed. This excluded the experiences of caregivers in urban areas, who may face urban economic stressors that shape their overall caregiving experience and their use of digital technology for caregiving.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings highlight the potential of digital technology to support informal caregiving in rural Nigeria. Improving access to affordable digital devices, reliable internet connectivity and digital literacy can enhance care coordination, caregiver support, emergency response and communication with older adults and their families.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study is important because it provides new insight into how informal caregivers in rural Nigeria use digital technology to support older adults despite limited connectivity and access to digital devices. It highlights both the potential of digital tools to strengthen caregiving and the infrastructural barriers that must be addressed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Constitutional Right to Healthcare in the Context of the Digital Transformation of Healthcare: Legal and Ethical Issues of Personal Data Protection
container-title: CONSTITUTIONAL AND MUNICIPAL LAW
89cd5c472802f9641674d0dcc7c62d35be1df2d6.abstract:
<jats:p>As part of the work, a comprehensive analysis of the legal and ethical issues related to the protection of personal
data in the healthcare sector in the context of digital transformation was carried out; conclusions were drawn regarding
the content and relationship between the concepts of «medical confidentiality» and «personal data». Judicial practice
on the transfer and dissemination of medical data was analysed; proposals were formulated to expand the content of the constitutional right to health protection and medical care in the context of digital transformation, as well
as to improve legislation taking into account bioethics and digital constitutionalism.</jats:p>

title: Digital literacy competencies among library professionals: a systematic literature review
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
dbcbc3e8a445c7ba8f3b2a1c5fbdf1881528cedb.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to assess the digital literacy proficiency, identify gaps in digital literacy and challenges encountered by library professionals in acquisition and application of digital literacy skills.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature review was carried out by using PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The databases used in this study includes Scopus, Web of Science, Emerald, Taylor and Francis. Articles published from 2020 to 2024 were included in this study. Initially, a total of 561 articles were identified from the selected databases, and after applying the criteria of inclusion and exclusion, 18 articles were selected for detailed analysis. The included studies were conducted across various countries, which indicates a broad geographical coverage of this study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings of this study indicated that most of the library professionals were well-versed in basic digital literacy skills, while a gap was observed in advanced level of digital literacy skills. The major challenges faced by them were lack of funds or budget allocation, followed by lack of digital infrastructure and lack of support from the authorities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review examines digital literacy competencies among library professionals to identify key competency areas, gaps and challenges faced by them. Existing literature lacks a comprehensive review focusing on current level of digital literacy competencies among library professionals. Therefore, this research work contributes to better understanding of digital literacy competencies among library professionals. The findings will also help inform future strategies, training programmes and initiatives aimed at strengthening digital literacy within the library profession.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
container-title: International Journal of MS Care
550d518bc31ff2cc3221d079ed64302d8a7e10a5.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration–approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL’s efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS.

Methods: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs.

Results: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, –4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%).

Conclusions: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.</jats:p>

title: Agricultural Water Management for Rice Production: A Comprehensive Analysis
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE
c92167c10c493f951b9b5f61be37cf4bfb12167e.abstract:
<jats:p>The identified problem revolves around establishing the water requirements for rice seeding,
growth, and maturity in hot climatic conditions. This study reviews the net water requirement
for rice growth or production under various climatic conditions in the Cross River Basin. It
was observed that the water requirement from seeding to harvest varies from location to
location, maintaining a FAO range, as postulated by Brouwer et al., 1986, ultimately falling
between 450mm to 700mm for hot weather.The methodology used for investigating the Net
Irrigation Water Requirements for rice growth to maturity involves the application of
New_Clim Location and CropWater software. These tools were utilized to compute Reference
Evapotranspiration (ETo) and Crop Water Requirements (CWR) for the net irrigation water
requirements of rice, respectively. The data were obtained from meteorological stations within
the Cross River Basin. In rainfed conditions, no water stress is practically observed throughout
the entire crop cycle, affirming that no irrigation system is needed in such a specific climate.
This study uses data generated through New_LocClim as input into CropWat, which, among
other factors, determines the net water requirement for rice growth and production.
Consequently, the results obtained from the use of the CropWat model in determining rice
water requirements for Obudu, Nkari, Ikom, and Ijegu-Yala were 633.7 mm, 397.9 mm, 303.0
mm, and 548.4 mm, respectively. The water requirement of only two locations, Obudu and
Ijegu-Yala, fell within the FAO-suggested range of 450 mm to 700 mm (Brouwer et al., 1986)
for hot climates, while Nkari and Ikom LGAs did not comply with Brower et al., 1986
postulation due to their location in a relatively less hot climate.</jats:p>

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain Technology in Management: Opportunities, Risks and Governance Challenges
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
37cc95f3465e4e0fb32f40a5e9c5644d70c42fdc.abstract: <jats:p>The idea of using blockchain seems to be gaining support as a way to facilitate transactions between organizations which don't have a shared database or administration. The importance of its management, however, is subject to debate. This article provides a critical assessment of the opportunities, risks and governance issues of organizations taking up blockchain technology. Research is synthesized into a focused narrative organized by three themes—Organizational Value, Implementation Constraints and Institutional Governance Responsibilities—that are grounded in the foundational research, further developed by management and information-systems scholarship, and then extended by institutional guidance. Several potential benefits are suggested in the literature: record reconciliation, traceability of the supply chain, auditing and rule-based transaction processing. This is only achievable by partner willingness to share, the validity of the source information and the appropriateness of blockchain over traditional databases. Potential gains might be offset by technical risks, privacy issues, organizational challenges, and uncertainties regarding regulations. In arguing this, the article does not suggest that you can forgo identifiable decision responsibilities, human responsibility or good dispute resolution when you decentralize record validation. Strategic fit, network design, accountability, information stewardship and performance review are the elements of an integrated governance framework. The paper provides an action-oriented consideration of blockchain adoption, considering benefits not as inherent properties of blockchain but rather possibilities that are likely to occur when blockchain is adopted.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
