title: Attention, Obligation, and the Rootedness of Human Identity in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
e4417ce1339c12cc05dc70011ea7ae674c983fe8.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how the AI renaissance is reconfiguring fundamental anthropological conditions of human existence and how Simone Weil's ethics of attention, obligation, and rootedness can provide a normative framework for understanding these transformations. Methodologically, the analysis combines conceptual reconstruction, philosophical-hermeneutic updating, and critically reflected conceptual engineering to translate Weil's categories into contemporary AI contexts. The analysis identifies three interconnected transformations: AI-mediated environments can reshape the conditions for sustained attention; distributed human-machine agency can create responsibility and obligation gaps; and digital infrastructures can weaken the conditions for social, economic, and political rootedness. The chapter develops a Weilian governance framework that deepens human-centered AI by identifying the anthropological conditions that underlie rights, human oversight, accountability, and participation.</jats:p>

title: Human Rights in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
b6cc6cdaede90b65d88551af1e19e431b12e7088.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is an innovation that is fast changing society, economy, and government structures. Although it is extremely advantageous, it also triggers the issue of human rights, fairness, and accountability. This chapter focuses on the discussion of the manner in which human rights will be protected in the ascendancy of AI. It raises the red flag over perilous algorithms, the absence of transparency and surveillance technologies proliferation. Legal frameworks and considerations that can be used to steer innovation towards dignity, equality, and justice are also addressed. Healthcare, employment, policing case studies gives an example of how AI affects the basic freedom. The chapter proposes a right based regulation of AI, stating that innovation should be moderated and should not harm people and society. It concludes with the policy suggestions that can make AI advocacy to social justice and maintain human freedoms.</jats:p>

title: From High-Level Ethics to Actionable Measures
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f6df0e82bb922344b07c7ca3d990ca38bb2a53f5.abstract: <jats:p>The active evolution of technology has led to new changes, and one of the trends that has become topical and actively discussed within the academic community and society in general is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Nevertheless, it has turned out that the data on which AI systems are built is not always neutral. This has resulted in cases where AI systems replicate and reinforce existing societal biases. At this point, no specific case law exists to cover the issues related to AI, so ethical frameworks have been developed. Such frameworks typically define top-level principles aimed at guaranteeing the credibility and justice of AI-based systems. However, principles such as explainability and accountability are frequently criticised because they are too abstract, as they do not provide any tangible measures that would guarantee their proper adoption. To develop recommendations on actions that can be taken to address these two principles, a qualitative literature review focusing on these themes has been conducted.</jats:p>

title: Reconfiguring Identity, Ownership, and Legal Framework in the Digital World
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f0a6336edb0b64a20e417a3a4a4f176bb513d8c1.abstract: <jats:p>Humankind's lived reality of an experience heavily mediated by Generative AI and the digital realm calls for a critical reconfiguration of existing social modes of being as well as legal contracts and regulations. The chapter attempts to address significant challenges presented by AI and AI-generated content specifically within literary creation in terms of copyright and ownership as well as legal systems pertaining to digital personhood and identity. A reworking of the traditional understanding of authorship and creativity also traces the inadequacy of existing global legal frameworks, largely anthropocentric in nature, grappling with the dilemma of attributing ownership and accountability for AI-generated creative content and prosecution of AI entities. The chapter also explores digital personhood with specific focus on the idea of digital necromancy and sophisticated AI crime as a threat to the world at large. The aim is to raise questions that could foster dialogue and initiate some form of policy change in the aforementioned realms.</jats:p>

title: Binary Biases
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
10d2652f77e6a8ecef648ea24ba8c77df85691ea.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of AI in content moderation raises major challenges in detecting hate speech and introduces new biases. This chapter explores the limits of binary classification models in addressing the complex nature of online hate. Standard machine learning methods often miss cultural context, evolving language, and the fine line between free speech and harmful speech, leading to unfair outcomes for marginalized groups. Through a mixed-method study using SVMs, deep learning, and transformer models on multilingual datasets, we reveal flaws in current systems. Findings show frequent mislabeling of cultural expressions, racial and gender gaps, and declining accuracy as language shifts. Qualitative evidence highlights social harms, including silencing advocacy and reinforcing discrimination. We stress the need for culturally aware, transparent detection and propose hybrid human–AI moderation to protect users while supporting democratic rights.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Labor, Employment Contracts, and Professional Identity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
34add7a445929817b91d0a85a92c50bba7824908.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping labor, employment contracts, and professional identity. It argues that AI is not merely automating tasks but transforming the nature of work through automation, new job categories, and human-AI collaboration. It analyzes the rise of platform labor and algorithmic management, the legal-ethical challenges of bias, transparency, and accountability, and the tension between flexibility and precarity. It explores identity shifts requiring reskilling, lifelong learning, and psychological adaptation. Policy, regulation, and collective bargaining frameworks are evaluated alongside case studies across sectors and regions. The chapter outlines scenarios for the future of work and calls for renewed social contracts that safeguard equity, inclusion, and meaningful human agency.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Electronic Health Record
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
160b86d6f7ca4a0340314e88b523dcae1039a032.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital in healthcare, especially in training medical officers for disease analysis and patient care. In diagnostics, AI algorithms enhance image interpretation accuracy and enable disease prediction like cancer and retinopathy. These modules analyze imaging data like MRIs, CT scans, and X-rays to identify nerve and cell injuries. In therapeutics, AI aids drug discovery by finding molecular interactions and optimizing trials, reducing time and costs. AI-based robotic systems enhance surgical precision and limit invasiveness. AI benefits healthcare management through predictive analytics for resource allocation and supply chain optimization. AI-powered chatbots provide 24/7 patient support and handle remote consultations. AI and IoT-enabled hospital-at-home modules allow home treatment, reducing facility strain. However, AI in healthcare raises ethical concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, and healthcare disparities. While AI develops, its limitations and transformative potential remain crucial for effective, equitable healthcare models.</jats:p>

title: Exploring ChatGPT-Assisted Qualitative Data: Comparing Human and AI-Assisted Coding Using Braun and Clarke’s Thematic Analysis
container-title: American Journal of Qualitative Research
d1da3462e4a00cf9a9e2a1ed853867d5195ec143.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en"><i>The use of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, has significantly expanded across academia and research in recent years. Of growing interest is AI’s potential role in qualitative research, especially in expediting tasks such as literature review and synthesis, data management and coding, and manuscript preparation, all while striving to maintain the rigor expected of qualitative inquiry. This paper explores the degree of alignment between AI-generated thematic analysis and a traditional, manual approach to analyzing focus group data and potential uses of AI in qualitative research. Using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis framework, a publicly available focus group dataset was analyzed in three stages: (1) Data Familiarization, (2) Human-Led Thematic Analysis, and (3) AI-Generated Analysis using ChatGPT. The human coders followed all six phases of the framework prior to engaging with the AI, to prevent influence from AI-generated output. The comparison revealed partial overlap between the human and AI-generated categories, particularly at the level of broader categories and themes. However, ChatGPT’s analysis tended to reflect a more superficial reading of the data, lacking the interpretive depth and nuance demonstrated by the human coders. While AI tools like ChatGPT show potential for supporting certain aspects of qualitative analysis, this study highlights key limitations in their ability to fully replicate the complexity and contextual understanding that human-led analysis provides. Further exploration is needed to define appropriate and ethical roles for AI in qualitative research workflows.</i></jats:p>

title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, gut microbiome composition, impulsivity, and attention covary in a human cohort
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
4b2ea61ea8ae67962d02b43bdd0ca11c398c565c.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are pervasive environmental pollutants linked to adverse neurobehavioral outcomes, yet the biological pathways coupling exposure to behavior are poorly defined. The gut microbiome is both sensitive to PAH exposure and a modulator of central nervous system function, suggesting it may mediate how PAH exposure influences neurobehavior. We tested whether PAH exposure, gut microbiome composition, and neurobehavioral function covary in a statewide sample of 34 adults stratified into high-impulsivity/poor-attention (HH) and low-impulsivity/fast-attention (LL) groups. Participants wore silicone wristbands for 30 days to passively sample PAH exposure and provided a single fecal sample for 16S rRNA profiling at the end of the wear period. Higher PAH exposure was associated with HH group membership in a sex-dependent manner, with the largest elevations among HH males. At the community level, PAH exposure profiles correlated with microbiome dissimilarity, and HH membership was associated with increased alpha-diversity and altered community composition relative to LL members. At the taxon level, 22 genera were significantly associated with 14 PAH compounds (FDR < 0.1). No individual genera were significantly associated with neurobehavioral group after multiple testing correction. Nevertheless, cross-referencing PAH-responsive genera (FDR < 0.1) against those with nominal neurobehavioral associations (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                      < 0.05) identified two candidate genera
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">—Hydrogenoanaerobacterium</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Methanobrevibacter</jats:italic>
                      —whose abundance covaries with both PAH exposure and neurobehavioral phenotype. Both have been independently linked to cognitive or neurological outcomes in prior work. These findings support a three-way relationship among environmental chemical exposure, gut microbiome composition, and neurobehavioral function, establishing an empirical foundation for testing microbiome-mediated links between PAH exposure and neurobehavioral outcomes.
                    </jats:p>
                    <jats:sec>
                      <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                      <jats:p>Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) exposure is widespread and is associated with impulsivity and attention problems, but how exposure translates into neurobehavioral risk is unclear. The gut microbiome is a plausible intermediary: gut microbes biotransform environmental chemicals and produce metabolites that influence brain function. In a statewide adult cohort, higher PAH exposure associated with with greater impulsivity and poorer attention in a sex-dependent manner, and both PAH exposure and neurobehavioral phenotype were associated with distinct gut microbiome features at the community and taxon levels. We identify candidate genera at the intersection of PAH exposure and neurobehavioral group whose biology independently implicates them in cognitive and neurological function. Because their associations with neurobehavioral phenotype are nominal, we present these genera as hypothesis-generating candidates for future study. By showing that all three domains covary within a single cohort, this work moves beyond pairwise associations toward testable microbiome-targeted and exposure-reduction strategies for PAH-related neurobehavioral risk.</jats:p>

title: A TOE–RBV–TBL Integrated Model of AI-Enabled Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
40d1fa5cdd6cd6c42b1d66704eea0c7b9caed768.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping food logistics by enhancing operational efficiency, reducing waste, and promoting sustainable supply chain practices. This study develops and validates an integrated Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE), Resource-Based View (RBV), and Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework to examine the determinants and outcomes of AI-enabled sustainable food logistics. Primary data were collected from 312 professionals in India's food supply chain and analysed using CB-SEM. The findings reveal that technological readiness, organisational capability, and environmental pressure significantly drive AI adoption, while AI capability positively influences environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The study offers a comprehensive theoretical framework and practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to build resilient, intelligent, and sustainable food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Cold Chain Optimization for Reducing Food Loss in Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
f7b19d3fb02e51972e9a5e5f799a5064e20516bb.abstract: <jats:p>With the combination of IoT-based monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making, AI-powered optimization of cold-chains increases the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of perishable chains. Sensors can provide real-time data, therefore, monitoring the temperature, humidity, and logistics status continuously and predict risks of spoilage and optimizing routing, storage, and inventory control with AI models. In case studies in dairy, seafood and fresh produce, there has been a substantial decrease in the spoilage and increased efficiency in work. Traceability and compliance are additionally improved with the help of the blockchain integration. In general, cold-chain systems with AI will help minimize food waste, advance food quality, and sustain logistics in complicated supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Quality Monitoring and Food Safety Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
2f988859afeb8045e1f8933ad6d0b777eed57974.abstract: <jats:p>AI has transformation in the area of food quality inspection and safety management due to the capabilities that have been introduced in rapid, precise, non-destructive and predictive assessment of food quality through the production process, processing, storage, transport, retailing and consumption. These techniques are applicable in fast monitoring and quick intervention in areas of dairy products, meat products, seafood, fruits and vegetables, cereals, beverages and ready to eat meals. This chapter discusses the principles, technologies, applications, benefits, challenges, and future prospects of AI-based food quality monitoring and safety management, with particular emphasis on intelligent sensors, real-time contamination detection, automated inspection, shelf-life prediction, process optimization, traceability, and predictive risk management across diverse food sectors.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Predictive Analytics for Sustainable Demand Forecasting in Agri-Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
ae908a7d83acc41af9c9be1d1de1a65faa9f8570.abstract: <jats:p>Predictive analytics, which is an AI technology, is changing the logistics of agri-foods by enhancing sustainability and demand forecasting. The conventional predictive approaches do not normally reflect their dynamic aspects, including weather fluctuations, market behavior and consumer behaviors, resulting into inefficiencies and food wastage. This chapter describes an AI-based framework that combines multi-source data, machine learning models, and decision support systems to come up with correct and real-time demand forecasts. The strategy facilitates optimal inventory control, effective distribution strategy, and minimized environmental concerns. There are enormous evidences of case studies showing enhancement of accuracy in forecasts, reduction of wastes, and efficiency in the operations. The results address the possible opportunities of AI assisting the resilient, adaptive, and sustainable food supply chains in the fast-changing global food system.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Innovations in Agri-Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
700ec2c44d31bcf14cea8b84c21efb4ae0bd8c73.abstract: <jats:p>Algorithms and other AI tools are increasingly being used to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and resilience of the Integrated Agri-food Supply Chain (IASC) across several areas of the agri-food sector. Innovations enabled by using AI technologies in agri-food systems referred to in this chapter are the ones that will achieve the best production, processing, distribution and consumption. The predictive analytics, machine learning, and intelligence-supporting tools are all about ensuring that requirements are always checked and predictable, resources are deployed,, and risk minimisation is done in real time. AI and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain platforms, and automated logistics are explored, and the potential for creating transparent, traceable supply chains that adapt to fluctuating demand and supply is investigated. Case studies have been presented that show successful applications and improvements in productivity, waste minimisation,, and operational costs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Driven Real-Time Route Optimization for Dynamic Food Logistics and Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
a3d254406bb275561bb5d6e8d0065c094ec34437.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter describes how to use real-time data analytics and machine learning to automatically simulate and execute alternative food logistics routes to predict supply chain bottlenecks (such as supplier failures or natural disasters) before they occur. Based on academic publications from 2024 to 2026, the chapter uses a systematic review and thematic content analysis. The findings show that AI and data analytics are transforming food logistics and supply chains into sustainable, efficient, and creative transportation. Traditional logistics systems suffer from poor order consolidation, low truck capacity utilization, static route planning, and significant environmental impacts. Efficiency losses increase operational expenses, delay supply, and increase carbon emissions, threatening sustainability. Cloud-based data platforms and reinforcement learning optimize logistics and route planning. Logistics sustainability demands data-driven decision-making and clever automation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
1ca0d752e991777e60571046cca42e7e93889d3a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of agri-food supply chains through artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing sustainable food logistics, resilience, and human resource management (HRM). It highlights how AI-driven technologies such as machine learning, IoT, and predictive analytics enable real-time decision-making, demand forecasting, and supply chain optimization, thereby reducing food waste and improving efficiency. The study integrates sustainability dimensions—environmental, economic, and social—with resilience strategies to address disruptions and uncertainties. Furthermore, it explores the critical role of HRM in facilitating workforce transformation, human–AI collaboration, and organizational change. An integrated AI–Sustainability–HRM framework is proposed to enhance adaptability and long-term performance. The chapter contributes to theory and practice by presenting a holistic, data-driven approach to building intelligent, resilient, and sustainable food logistics systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Food Waste Reduction in India's Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
fc88c02780841f38b3f41c69dae42b101d38d76a.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we focus on the role that AI-driven predictive analytics can play to assist with forecast accuracy, cold-chain orchestration, quality monitoring and speed of response upstream and downstream through the farm-to-market flows to abete food loss and waste in India´s perishable supply chains. It relies on a systematic secondary empirical synthesis of India-centric studies, policy papers, and analytics research on global experience pertaining to high perishability classes of vegetables, dairy, fish, and other fresh fruits. The chapter proves that besides infrastructural hurdles, food waste challenges of India is also a challenge of timing, visibility and coordination. Evidence from India reveals how much of the loss occurs is seasonally driven, how losses are correlated with harvest volume, storage, transport reliability, and the quality sorting and practices. This chapter presents a predictive analytics framework for agri-logistics, suggests how Indian firms and policymakers can implement the approach, and claims that digital traceability.</jats:p>

title: Predictive Business Intelligence Architectures for Cold-Chain Logistics Mitigating Food Waste Through AI-Driven IoT Sensor Integration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
791f2efff6e75d93d6ead2cbd5779a343d5628c2.abstract: <jats:p>Food loss and waste in cold-chain logistics result not only from refrigeration failures, but also from fragmented data, delayed responses, and weak coordination across supply-chain actors. This chapter presents an IGI-style conceptual and implementation framework for predictive business intelligence (BI) in cold-chain logistics. It argues that waste reduction is more effective when Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, event-driven data integration, and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics are designed as a layered architectural capability rather than as stand-alone monitoring tools. Drawing on literature in cold-chain management, food quality, wireless sensing, BI, predictive analytics, AI-enabled supply chains, and digital twins, the chapter shows how variables such as temperature, humidity, location, door events, shock, dwell time, and product condition can be transformed into risk scores, dynamic shelf-life estimates, prioritized exceptions, and closed-loop decisions. It also proposes architecture and seven implementation workstreams for deployment.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Cold Chain Management Using AI and IoT
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
60daab0ba3149ca77331fc247ab25917cceed633.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is fundamentally reshaping cold chain logistics, enabling unprecedented levels of precision, transparency, and sustainability. This chapter examines how intelligent sensing, predictive analytics, blockchain-based traceability, and digital twin simulation collectively address the chronic inefficiencies of temperature-sensitive supply chains. Drawing on recent empirical and review studies, the chapter presents an integrated framework that links real-time data acquisition to AI-driven decision-making and blockchain-anchored accountability. Key themes include spoilage prevention, carbon footprint reduction, regulatory compliance, and consumer trust. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on challenges and emerging directions for scalable, equitable, and ethically grounded cold chain transformation.</jats:p>

title: Management of a fishery in a heterogeneous environment
container-title: Comptes Rendus. Biologies
52a6c206dca29c0801cd34fb34c88fe5c247420b.abstract: <jats:p>We consider the Schaefer model with a single species of fish caught in an environment consisting of patches connected by fast movements. We show that the maximum sustainable yield (MSY) of the fishery is always less than the sum of the yields of the isolated sites, unlike the total biomass of the total population at equilibrium, which can exceed the sum of the local carrying capacities. We then present a predator–prey model with predator fishing. We show that the overall MSY of the system of sites connected by fish movements can now be greater than the sum of the MSYs of the unconnected sites. To achieve a significant increase in overall MSY, it is useful to connect two heterogeneous sites, one rather favorable to the growth of the prey and not very favorable to the predator growth, with a site presenting opposite characteristics. We show that global MSY can be achieved in various ways, including the establishment of a marine protected area (MPA). We then study a Nutrient–Phytoplankton–Zooplankton–Fish (NPZF) model. We show that there exists a unique globally stable positive equilibrium point under certain conditions for which we calculate the MSY. We further consider a two-site version of the NPZF model. Our work highlights the importance of considering lower trophic levels, spatial heterogeneity between sites, asymmetry in the spatial distribution of fish, and marine protected areas, which have the effect of significantly increasing the overall MSY compared to the sum of the MSYs of the isolated sites.</jats:p>

title: Adolescents’ Perspectives on Uptake, Engagement, and Implementation to Inform the Development of a Preventive Transdiagnostic Digital Mental Health Intervention: Qualitative Interview Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
035d301ed77fce4e74ca0175c7cadf9839d24f1a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adolescence is a critical period for mental health prevention; yet, many young people face barriers to help-seeking, including stigma, limited mental health literacy, and restricted access to services. Preventive digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer a scalable, low-threshold approach to early support, but uptake and sustained engagement remain limited. Existing research has predominantly relied on quantitative methods and has only partly captured adolescents’ perspectives. Qualitative research is therefore needed to inform the design and implementation of preventive DMHIs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to explore adolescents’ perspectives on factors influencing the anticipated uptake, expected engagement, and implementation of preventive transdiagnostic DMHIs across person, intervention, and system levels.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This qualitative study was conducted in Switzerland using a single-interview design in the predesign phase of the development of a transdiagnostic preventive DMHI. Adolescents aged 12‐21 years were recruited through voluntary response sampling via social media and the project website. Semistructured interviews explored experiences with online help-seeking, factors influencing DMHI anticipated uptake and expected engagement, and recommendations for implementation. Interviews were conducted in person or via video call between January and June 2022, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using a hybrid deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis. Intercoder agreement was assessed using Cohen κ (κ=0.72).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 48 adolescents (mean age 16.52, SD 2.67 years; 32/48, 72.9% female) participated. In total, 8 main topics and multiple subtopics were identified across person, intervention, system, and cross levels. Person-level factors highlighted the importance of mental health literacy, preuptake communication, and relevance of social networks. Intervention-level factors emphasized usability, personalization, and privacy, while system-level findings reflected expectations for adaptive, integrated, and low-threshold mental health services. Trust and support emerged as cross-level factors for engagement. In addition, participants described several discrepancies between desired intervention characteristics and practical implementation, particularly regarding personalization, anonymity, peer exchange, and human support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adolescents’ perspectives highlight that successful implementation of preventive DMHIs requires attention beyond intervention design to preuptake communication strategies, mental health literacy promotion, and integration within adaptive care systems. The tension between adolescents’ desire for immediate human-delivered support and the self-guided nature of preventive DMHIs underscores the need for clear clinical boundaries and explicit escalation pathways.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Management of Bullous Pemphigoid and Norwegian Scabies with Dupilumab Plus Ivermectin
container-title: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
340dc16ab1a69e23e758b600bf41fe503779ce62.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT.</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bullous pemphigoid is a severe autoimmune blistering disease, and Norwegian scabies is a rare comorbidity. However, conventional treatment methods, such as systemic corticosteroids, carry a high risk in the treatment of elderly patients. Herein, this rare comorbidity is described in an elderly patient. After an initial induction treatment with a low-to-moderate dose of corticosteroid, this patient achieved complete remission with a combination therapy of dupilumab (a monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-4/13 signaling pathway) and ivermectin. Therefore, the successful treatment of this rare case provides a promising strategy for reducing reliance on corticosteroids in high-risk populations.</jats:p>

title: The Management of Swallowing Disorders in Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 1: A Scoping Review
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
ee60069e9a5c3d0dbb8e2b2202f4fdea5aea5418.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Spinal muscular atrophy Type 1 (SMA1) is a rare autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder with progressive muscle weakness and atrophy. Dysphagia is common among children with SMA1, and its complications are frequently documented. This scoping review aimed to describe the management of swallowing disorders in this population.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, four electronic databases were searched (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library) for studies on children with SMA1. We investigated the management of swallowing disorders in children with SMA1, including methods and protocols used to assess swallowing and feeding, and treatment option. The quality of included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists; two independent researchers conducted study selection and data extraction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-eight studies with a total of 1,784 SMA1 patients were included. Swallowing was evaluated using instrumental methods (flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing and videofluoroscopic swallowing study) and clinical assessments, with one validated protocol identified for pediatric SMA (Oral and Swallowing Abilities Tool). Delayed initiation of swallowing, oral impairment, pharyngeal residues, and aspiration were frequently reported. Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy was used in cases of severe dysphagia, malnutrition, and failure to thrive. Few studies reported information on compensatory strategies and rehabilitative treatments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Further research is needed to standardize swallowing assessment approaches and to evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitative and compensatory interventions in children with SMA1.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Tenecteplase Before Thrombectomy at 4.5 to 24 Hours for Basilar Artery Occlusion
container-title: JAMA
ef60472e8a004149c416d5f14b5651c60704d5a8.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Importance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Whether intravenous tenecteplase before endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) improves outcomes in patients with basilar artery occlusion presenting 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset remains uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT vs EVT alone in patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This multicenter, open-label, blinded end point, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 40 stroke centers in China. Between March 16, 2023, and February 4, 2025, a total of 330 patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥10) presenting within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset to EVT-capable centers were enrolled. Final follow-up was completed on May 4, 2025.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Interventions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients were randomized 1:1 via a centralized web server using a minimization method to receive either intravenous tenecteplase (bolus injection, 0.25 mg/kg; maximum, 25 mg) followed by EVT (n = 166) or EVT alone (n = 164).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The primary outcome was functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 332 patients randomized, 2 withdrew consent. Of the remaining 330 patients (mean [SD] age, 66 [11] years; 241 males [73%]; 89 females [27%]), 329 completed 90-day follow-up. Of whom, 50 of 165 (30%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 50 of 164 (30%) in the EVT alone group achieved functional independence (adjusted rate ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.67 to 1.25]; risk difference, −0.18% [95% CI, −10.13% to 9.76%]). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 8 patients (5%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 6 (4%) in the EVT alone group. Mortality at 90 days was similar between the groups (66 [40%] vs 70 [43%], respectively).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted directly to EVT-capable centers who presented 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset, the addition of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT did not result in improved functional outcomes compared with EVT alone.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital Transformation of Accounting and Financial Management Through Emerging Technologies
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
072ee30c1139742aaee5825be31b3e984571eca4.abstract: <jats:p>Digital transformation has created an opportunity for accountants and financial managers to create new efficiencies, add transparency to their work, and develop better strategies for decision-making. This chapter looks at how artificial intelligence, automation, big data analytics, and cloud-based financial management are changing how accountants use technology, as well as how those technologies are changing the practices and processes that accountants follow when doing their jobs. It also describes how the digital transformation of Finance will cause a dramatic shift in the way financial services are delivered to customers from being reactive to value-driven. By integrating intelligent systems into forecasting, performance management, risk assessment, and real-time reporting functions, the ability to make informed decisions is enhanced. The chapter identifies the organizational, regulatory, and ethical challenges that digital finance poses, including data privacy, cybersecurity, and governance risks.</jats:p>

title: Digital Skills and Professional Judgment in AI-Driven Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
fa94d39fbd808cc46e56a32eb78b60762c9d5124.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping financial decision-making by altering how information is analyzed, interpreted, and translated into professional judgment. This chapter examines the role of digital skills in determining whether AI strengthens or undermines the quality and accountability of financial decisions. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature, the chapter conceptualizes digital skills as cognitive–governance capabilities that extend beyond technical proficiency to include critical interpretation, calibrated reliance on AI, explainability, professional skepticism, and ethical judgment. Particular attention is given to automation bias, accountability risks, and the organizational conditions that shape human–AI interaction. The chapter concludes that responsible AI-enabled financial decision-making depends not on algorithmic capability alone, but on the alignment of digital competence, professional judgment, and effective governance.</jats:p>

title: From Financial Accountant to Digital Finance Architect
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
301bb7a811700c54a3c8f72796dd343a397ed320.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter analyzes the digital transformation of the finance function as a structural reconfiguration of processes, decision-making logic, and governance. It demonstrates how automation, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and RegTech are shifting traditional job profiles from process execution to the architectural design of digital financial systems. On this basis, the Digital Finance Competency Architecture (DFCA) is developed, integrating technological, data-analytical, governance-related, and strategic-cognitive competencies. The analysis illustrates that effective performance in digital finance environments requires systemic competence, i.e., the ability to translate data, models, and regulatory requirements into coherent decision-making architectures. Finally, implications for education, organization, and governance are discussed, and the Digital Finance Architect is established as a new professional role model.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Financial Decision Support for Handicraft Artisans
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
1d34157c42ec302960b797359d16b132c9fe0d28.abstract: <jats:p>Handicraft artists play an important role in conserving cultural and social history while also contributing to the growth of their respective economies. It contributes four to five percent to the world economy and creates a huge number of job opportunities in the neighbourhood. Handicraft workers contribute to societal innovation in the shape of innovative work methods, techniques, and so on. This area sheds light on the hidden talents and abilities of craft workers. However, their salary and economic situation do not allow for this. They are frequently confronted with issues and obstacles such as limited market access, intense rivalry from major companies, a lack of technology, and a communication gap. The article focuses on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to solve difficulties for the handicraft industry. Primary data were acquired from 120 handicraft workers for the study using a structured questionnaire, including demographic information, production costs, profit from their company, and numerous problems they encounter.</jats:p>

title: AI and Predictive Analytics in Performance Monitoring
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
6734ced4b1406c8f7437d78ac9138a400a2eaba5.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics have revolutionized supply chain performance monitoring by enabling real-time visibility, proactive risk management, and data-driven decision-making. This chapter examines the integration of AI technologies—including machine learning, deep learning, and advanced analytics—into supply chain performance measurement systems. It explores how predictive models enhance forecasting accuracy, optimize resource allocation, and improve sustainability outcomes while maintaining compliance standards. Through systematic analysis of current research and practical applications, the chapter demonstrates how organizations transition from reactive compliance monitoring to proactive competitive advantage through intelligent performance systems.</jats:p>

title: Strategic Supply Chain Auditing and Performance Management
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
2f8e16ebf20d137d16d174e3cac43c93df52a09d.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined the relationship between supply chain auditing systems and performance management. A systematic desk review was conducted using peer-reviewed literature from Scopus, the Web of Science, the IBSS, and Google Scholar. The search strategy combined keywords related to supply chain auditing, performance measurement, governance, risk management, and ESG auditing. Only English-language peer-reviewed journal articles were included, whereas nonacademic and methodologically weak sources were excluded. The findings indicate a bidirectional relationship in which performance management systems identify risk areas that inform audit prioritization, whereas auditing enhances the reliability of performance data. Emerging technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things enable greater real-time integration between auditing and performance systems.</jats:p>

title: Digitally Integrated Disease Management System in Rwanda: Community Healthcare Worker Perspectives
container-title: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
ba0b9fd0a0d5ae27c4978d51884c98d8476fc33d.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT.</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As digital health tools are increasingly deployed to support community-based primary healthcare, understanding frontline user experiences is critical for effective implementation and scale-up. Here, community health workers’ (CHWs) perspectives on the digitally integrated disease management system (d-IDS) in Rwanda are discussed. The d-IDS intervention was intended to improve the cost-effectiveness of community-based screening, patient management, and disease surveillance through a mobile digital platform. Before implementation, user acceptance testing and cascade training prepared CHWs, their supervisors, and health facility staff. During implementation, continuous supervision and qualitative assessments of the system were conducted. Qualitative data were collected through focus group discussions and semi-structured key informant interviews. The CHWs widely appreciated the system’s ease of use, comprehensiveness, availability in Kinyarwanda (local language), offline functionality, improved data management, and ability to expedite effective patient management cascades compared with paper-based registers. Home-based screening reduced patient time and costs of care and enhanced equity and access to care, bringing Rwanda closer to achieving Universal Healthcare Coverage. However, challenges included increased workload, inadequate or lack of incentives, internet connectivity constraints, system rigidity in updating household records, and initially low digital literacy among some CHWs. Ongoing digitalization initiatives will inform national scale-up and policy choices.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
95a62b89e12f29ec2d10ee4b3bff78918b9670c6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical communication skills are a core yet complex competency in medical education and practice. However, early-stage medical students often struggle to apply communication frameworks in practice due to limited opportunities for structured simulation training. Generative AI (GenAI)–supported training has the potential to offer a scalable and innovative approach for clinical communication skills training.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined the longitudinal development of medical students’ clinical communication skills over 1 academic year and investigated whether AI-powered simulation contributed to differential improvement relative to conventional training. In addition, the study explored motivational, behavioral, and affective mechanisms associated with communication skills development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A nonblinded randomized controlled design was used at a medical school in the United Kingdom, with students assigned either to the control group (n=28, 56%) or to the AI group (n=22, 44%), who practiced with SimPatient, a patient-simulator chatbot accessed through a web browser. Communication skills performance was assessed using standardized objective structured clinical examinations (OSCE) scores relative to the pass marks to enable comparison across time points. Paired t tests and difference-in-differences (DID) analyses were conducted between groups and over time to examine changes in communication skills. Latent change score modeling was used to identify predictors of communication skills change. Sentiment analysis was conducted on 6120 comments from AI-student conversations. Finally, a system quality survey was used to assess participants’ feedback on the AI-powered simulator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Latent change score modeling showed that gains in intrinsic motivation and behavioral learning were significant predictors of students’ communication skills change. The AI group showed a greater descriptive increase in communication skills than the control group, yet the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Within the AI group, consultations whose lexical tone trended more strongly toward resolution (consultation tone) were descriptively associated with communication skills improvement; given the small subsample (n=17), this finding is reported as exploratory. The AI group’s confidence level in AI use was negatively associated with communication skills improvement, while the group nevertheless reported a generally high level of satisfaction with the system.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, medical students’ clinical communication skills increased over the academic year, with this development most strongly associated with their motivation and behavioral engagement; the AI-supported group did not differ significantly from conventional training. The simulator responded appropriately and provided a usable environment for practicing foundational communication behaviors but was limited in capturing the affective complexity, vulnerability, and narrative unpredictability of real clinical encounters. In conclusion, this study suggests that GenAI holds promise for supporting foundational clinical communication training and providing positive practice environments, thereby fostering motivation and behavioral engagement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Attention Trap? How Visual Motion Shapes Children’s Screen Time and Engagement on Video Platforms
container-title: Information Systems Research
3836bd62e72740b25fd59c7e03808cdae1f4dd40.abstract:
<jats:p>Children spend considerable time watching online video, yet we know relatively little about which features of video content shape their engagement. This research examines one measurable feature: visual motion. Analyzing more than 32,000 videos from popular children’s channels on YouTube, we find that videos with greater visual motion receive more views, even after accounting for other visual, audio, and content characteristics. A randomized YouTube advertising experiment using professionally produced educational videos confirms this relationship; adding motion to the background increased view rates by about 2% at essentially no additional cost.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>An eye-tracking study with children aged 6–10 helps explain why. Visual motion does not prevent children from looking away. Instead, it reduces the duration of longer attentional lapses by bringing their gaze back to the screen more quickly. The additional attention is directed primarily toward the moving background rather than the instructor. The findings show how a measurable design feature can shape children’s attention and provide creators and platforms with a way to assess and design children’s video content more systematically.</jats:p>

title: Communication Difficulties and Management: The Lived Experience of Individuals With Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Spectrum Disorders
container-title: American Journal of Speech-Language Pathology
1d522ff35f2664ebda12366ebfdad1028663284f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is the neuropathology that underlies a collection of progressive clinical syndromes typically classified by the initial/primary symptom. For example, individuals with loss of word meaning as a first manifestation are often diagnosed with the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia. Growing evidence suggests that language and communication can be impacted in all clinical syndromes across the FTLD spectrum, but the functional relevance of these symptoms has yet to be explored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) Insights Survey is the largest community survey of individuals affected by FTLD. It was administered online and included questions related to demographics, symptoms, life participation, quality of life, and experiences with and hopes for treatment. Self-reported diagnoses of respondents included the nonfluent/agrammatic, semantic, and unspecified variants of primary progressive aphasia, semantic dementia, corticobasal syndrome, progressive supranuclear palsy, and behavioral variant FTD. Here, we grouped respondents according to whether they had a language-predominant (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 43), motor-predominant (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 43), or behavior-predominant (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">n</jats:italic>
                      = 90) variant of FTLD and used descriptive statistics to explore how they perceive their own communication difficulties and gauge their motivation for management.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Over 65% of respondents in each group identified changes to communication as a symptom; subsequent analyses focused on the responses of this cohort. Across groups, word finding and speaking were two of the most frequently endorsed difficulties. Over 50% of each group identified improved communication as a treatment priority, reflecting the impact that these symptoms have on their day-to-day life. Speech-language therapy is an important approach to manage these changes and minimize their impact. Whereas 76% of the language and motor groups had attended speech-language therapy, this was true for only 16% of the behavior group.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Individuals across the FTLD spectrum experience changes to communication that impact their social engagement and quality of life. Management needs to be tailored to the needs of each individual, but recommendations are provided based on the insights and group-level preferences reported here. Future research is needed to identify current referral practices and how to increase engagement in skilled communication interventions, especially for individuals with the behavioral variant of FTD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Supplemental Material:</jats:title>

title: Gcn5 and mTORC1 mediated regulation of autophagy controls Drosophila blood cell homeostasis
container-title: eLife
700db83f75519837e25d45ca5d0f3b8c17d2c4a4.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    .
                  </jats:p>

title: Beyond Belief Updating: A Framework for Self-Belief Formation
3796862ab71587287fb46c3bdf9532408a32202a.abstract: From early childhood, we form self-beliefs about where we belong, what we are good at, or who loves us. Despite extensive psychological research on self-beliefs, the fundamental question of how they initially form has received surprisingly little attention. Existing work on self-belief updating overlooks two critical limitations. First, it treats self-related learning as arising from isolated events, ignoring that self-beliefs typically emerge from sequences of meaningfully connected experiences. Second, because updating paradigms operate in familiar domains, participants already hold precise prior beliefs intertwined with established motives and emotional states making it impossible to study belief formation from a genuinely uninformed starting point. We propose that studying novel experiential domains addresses both problems: individuals enter such domains with neutral, imprecise self-beliefs, enabling formation of “artificial” self-beliefs through repeated feedback in a controlled setting. As a concrete implementation, we introduce the Learning Of Own Performance (LOOP) task, in which participants form beliefs about their abilities in a novel performance domain. Extensions of this approach could illuminate broader aspects of self-belief formation, including personality and identity. This Perspective bridges psychology, computational neuroscience, and sociology around a foundational question: how do we come to think about ourselves the way we do?

title: Decentralized Finance and Digital Assets: A New Perspective on Financial Management and Risk
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
13b14090a5c64d7c3224b43ae85f72408e707dbf.abstract: <jats:p>Financial services are being transformed, how they are designed, accessed, and managed, by the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital assets. These innovations via blockchain networks, smart contracts, and tokenization offer alternatives to existing models for payments, lending, investment, and asset exchange. But the economic, institutional and operating risks of financial intermediation are not eroded when transactions are automated. In this conceptual study, the impact of DeFi and digital assets on financial management is explored, including capital allocation, treasury operations, risk management, and the governance of digital assets. It assesses what could be gained from this technology, alongside its potential technological vulnerabilities, market instability, regulatory uncertainty and inability to provide meaningful financial inclusion. An analysis approach is built to present a managerial perspective, which considers digital financial arrangements from an economic function, dependency and accountability standpoint. It points out that sustainable adoption requires coordination of technology with financial management, strong rights, organizational efficiency and appropriate governance. DeFi is therefore a reorganization of financial management and not the automatic replacement of existing financial institutions.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain Technology in Management: Opportunities, Risks and Governance Challenges
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
37cc95f3465e4e0fb32f40a5e9c5644d70c42fdc.abstract: <jats:p>The idea of using blockchain seems to be gaining support as a way to facilitate transactions between organizations which don't have a shared database or administration. The importance of its management, however, is subject to debate. This article provides a critical assessment of the opportunities, risks and governance issues of organizations taking up blockchain technology. Research is synthesized into a focused narrative organized by three themes—Organizational Value, Implementation Constraints and Institutional Governance Responsibilities—that are grounded in the foundational research, further developed by management and information-systems scholarship, and then extended by institutional guidance. Several potential benefits are suggested in the literature: record reconciliation, traceability of the supply chain, auditing and rule-based transaction processing. This is only achievable by partner willingness to share, the validity of the source information and the appropriateness of blockchain over traditional databases. Potential gains might be offset by technical risks, privacy issues, organizational challenges, and uncertainties regarding regulations. In arguing this, the article does not suggest that you can forgo identifiable decision responsibilities, human responsibility or good dispute resolution when you decentralize record validation. Strategic fit, network design, accountability, information stewardship and performance review are the elements of an integrated governance framework. The paper provides an action-oriented consideration of blockchain adoption, considering benefits not as inherent properties of blockchain but rather possibilities that are likely to occur when blockchain is adopted.</jats:p>

title: Managing Investment Decisions and Risk in Decentralized Financial Markets: Evidence from Blockchain-Based Platforms
container-title: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
5970dbe0d163fa1f2d86a6ee377a5277f5d7e7c5.abstract: <jats:p>Decentralized finance (DeFi) has provided alternative investment, lending, trading, asset management and other methods via blockchain on both public and private platforms. Unlike traditional financial institutions, DeFi protocols rely on smart contracts for transactions, collateral, and financial returns and do not depend on the entire reliance of the centralized intermediaries. The innovations provide access, transparency and operational efficiency but also financial, technological, liquidity, and governance risks to the investor. This study adopts a structured literature review approach of academic studies, institutional reports and documented platforms mechanisms and investigates the investment decision making and risk management in decentralized financial markets. The cases of platform Uniswap, Aave, Compound, and MakerDAO are not meant to represent an empirical sample, but instead serve as examples to illustrate the platforms. Thematic synthesis take account of the concepts of portfolio theory and information asymmetry, highlighting the centrality of factors like expected return, collateral management, security of smart contracts, the reliability of oracles, concentration of governance, and regulatory uncertainty. It concludes that transparency of record and liquidation automation can enhance transaction discipline, but will not be enough to prevent losses in stressed markets all on its own. The study suggests an integrated decision-making approach that incorporates elements of financial, technological due diligence, governance appraisal, Exposure limits and ongoing monitoring. The results offer a basis for future transaction level tests of the effectiveness of risk adjusted investment strategies.</jats:p>

title: A Survey of Learning-based Method Name Prediction
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
48b81eddcf90694d4fefcd0a971c62e474bcae45.abstract: <jats:p>The choice of method names significantly influences code comprehension and maintenance, posing a considerable challenge, especially for novice developers. Automating the prediction of appropriate method names based on the method code body has emerged as a promising approach to address this challenge. In recent years, numerous Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL)-based Method Name Prediction (MNP) techniques have been proposed. However, a systematic review of these techniques is currently lacking, hindering future researchers from understanding the research status, development trends, challenges, and opportunities in this field. To fill this gap, in this article, we conduct a systematic literature review on learning-based MNP studies. Specifically, we first perform a thorough review of the literature concerning publication venue, publication year, and contribution types. This analysis enables us to discern trends in studies related to MNP. Second, we depict the general workflow of learning-based MNP techniques, which involves three consecutive subprocesses: context extraction, context preprocessing, and context-based prediction. Subsequently, we investigate contemporary techniques/solutions applied in the three subprocesses. Third, we scrutinize the widely used experimental databases, evaluation metrics, and replication packages utilized in MNP studies. Moreover, we summarize existing empirical studies on MNP to facilitate a quick understanding of their focus and findings for subsequent researchers. Finally, based on a systematic review and summary of existing work, we outline several open challenges and opportunities in MNP that remain to be addressed in future work.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The time course of neural activity predictive of self-initiated movement
6bb29c0fa61a9bb6f281a6f43aa6ce014a54e928.abstract: <jats:p>Decades of research have shown that early ramping activity is a very reliable antecedent of self-initiated movement. However, the dominant paradigm has been to only analyze data epochs culminating in movement, which discounts how often slow ramping might occur when no movement follows. To address this, we introduced a matched control condition that did not culminate in movement. We recorded electroencephalography data and compared these two conditions using a variety of powerful machine-learning classifiers. Although early ramping activity was present, it was not useful in predicting movement. Instead, classification accuracy rose abruptly about 100 ms before movement. By contrast, the traditional approach reproduced the spurious impression of early predictability. Our results substantially constrain the interpretation that early EEG antecedents, including the RP, reflect a commitment to act, instead indicating that EEG-detectable evidence consistent with such a commitment emerges closer to movement onset, in line with the timing of conscious intention and the capacity for late movement inhibition. More broadly, our results show that a reliable antecedent is not necessarily a good predictor, underscoring the need for proper control conditions in time series analyses.</jats:p>

title: Feasibility Analysis of Education in Indonesian Provinces: A Machine Learning Clustering Approach for Regional Classification
container-title: Engineering and Technology Journal
1b5bd0dfe6cab0a4e4dc5dc25d573208b2fdac15.abstract: <jats:p>Education system feasibility varies significantly across Indonesian provinces due to geographic, socioeconomic, and infrastructural disparities. This study applies unsupervised machine learning clustering algorithms (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, Gaussian Mixture Models, and Self-Organizing Maps) to classify Indonesian provinces into homogeneous groups based on education feasibility indicators. Using 39 provinces and special territories, we evaluated clustering quality through internal validation metrics (Silhouette coefficient and Davies-Bouldin index) and inter-algorithm agreement measures (Adjusted Rand Index and Normalized Mutual Information). Results demonstrate that Hierarchical Clustering achieves the best Davies-Bouldin index (0.782), while K-Means and GMM produce identical partitions (ARI = 1.0, NMI = 1.0). Self-Organizing Maps identified nine distinct regional education feasibility profiles, with provincial distributions revealing significant heterogeneity in education conditions. These findings provide a quantitative framework for targeted policy interventions and resource allocation to improve education feasibility across Indonesia’s diverse regions.</jats:p>

title: Entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills, and self-esteem in students participating in sports programmes in Colombia
container-title: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
7487e0e532b00ca3a9d308c88e1fc9fc09e90f2f.abstract:
<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

The authorship information, affiliations, author contributions (CRediT), and related statements have been updated accordingly. The scientific content and conclusions of the article remain unchanged.</jats:p>
