title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Multi-omic integration using interpretable machine learning reveals genetic mechanisms of trait variation and phenotypic plasticity in switchgrass
d5ecaf8e9c0ab25f0f77449121b30e109d87be40.abstract: <jats:p>Uncovering the genetic architecture of quantitative traits is challenging because polygenic control yields small individual gene effects and because gene–gene and genotype-by-environment interactions add further complexity. To understand the genetic basis of polygenic traits and their plasticity across environments, we integrated genome-wide SNPs and RNA-seq transcript data with interpretable statistical and machine learning models in a switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) diversity panel grown at contrasting field sites in Michigan and Texas. Notably, in addition to single environments, our trait prediction models were able to predict phenotypic differences, across environments i.e., plasticity. By interpreting trait prediction models with explainable machine learning methods, we identified genes that are the most predictive of flowering time and annual biomass production across environments, based on their associated gene expression levels and nearby SNPs. This approach recovered canonical flowering regulators and revealed novel, environment-specific candidate flowering genes. Further, transcriptome models consistently recovered more switchgrass genes homologous to experimentally validated genes in Arabidopsis and rice than SNP-based models. Feature interaction scores from the models also allow the identification of trait- and environment-dependent gene–gene interactions, where flowering time showed stronger and more abundant interactions than biomass. While some of the interactions identified are consistent with the link between flowering time and yield, most are novel predictors that need to be further evaluated. These findings provide insight into the genetic basis of trait variation and plasticity across environments and help prioritize candidate genes for functional validation and cultivar improvement.</jats:p>

title: Endoscopic ultrasound-based deep learning for predicting chemotherapy response in unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
1f6a560325fb967b8d7fb19fd1972b99328cdc40.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and chemotherapy remains the main treatment option for patients with unresectable disease. Reliable prediction of chemotherapy response is therefore critical for individualized treatment planning. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) provides high-resolution, tumor-specific imaging that may be well suited for deep learning-based prediction of chemotherapy response.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To develop and validate an EUS-based deep learning model for predicting first-line chemotherapy response in patients with unresectable PDAC, and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) stratification.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this retrospective, single-center study, 190 patients with histologically confirmed PDAC diagnosed between February 2016 and March 2025 were included. All patients were deemed ineligible for upfront surgical resection based on formal multidisciplinary team evaluation, including those with locally advanced or metastatic disease and those considered medically or personally unsuitable for surgery. Patients diagnosed in 2023 or earlier were assigned to the training and internal validation cohort (n  = 152) using five-fold cross-validation, whereas patients diagnosed from January 2024 onward at a separate campus of the same institution constituted a temporally independent test cohort with site separation (n  = 38). Tumor regions of interest were manually annotated on pre-treatment EUS images. Four convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (VGG19, VGG19-BN, ResNet50, and ResNeXt50) were trained to predict progressive disease, as defined by RECIST version 1.1 after first-line chemotherapy. Model performance was evaluated at the patient level using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and accuracy, and model-derived risk stratification was assessed for OS.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In the independent test cohort, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the best discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.848; sensitivity, 65.38%; specificity, 84.19%), followed by ResNet50 (AUC = 0.844), whereas VGG19-BN (AUC = 0.775) and VGG19 (AUC = 0.614) showed lower performance. Model-predicted probabilities enabled effective risk stratification, with high-risk patients exhibiting significantly shorter OS compared with low-risk patients (log-rank P  < 0.01; hazard ratio = 1.77). In contrast, baseline carbohydrate antigen 19-9-based stratification did not significantly discriminate survival, and CNN-based models demonstrated higher discriminatory performance compared with the conventional serum biomarker.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CNN models based on region-of-interest-level EUS imaging can predict chemotherapy response and provide clinically meaningful prognostic stratification in PDAC. Among the evaluated architectures, ResNeXt50 demonstrated the most consistent and robust performance across independent testing and sensitivity analyses. This noninvasive imaging-based approach shows potential for integration into clinical workflows to support personalized treatment planning.</jats:p>

title: Towards Realistic Project-Level Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration and Semantic Architecture Modeling
container-title: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
2e98affb75fe6b1c9fa0a80bf39cb6bb48af6b14.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in automated code generation. In real-world software engineering, the growing demand for rapid iteration and continuous delivery underscores the importance of project-level code generation, where LLMs are expected to generate complete software projects directly from complex user requirements. This task, however, presents greater challenges due to larger input scales, multi-modal information, and the need for holistic architectural reasoning. Although existing studies have made initial explorations, they still face key limitations, including unrealistic datasets and unreliable evaluation metrics that fail to reflect real-world complexity, the semantic gap between human-written requirements and machine-interpretable structures, and difficulties in managing hierarchical dependencies and maintaining quality throughout the generation process. To address these limitations, we first introduce
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , a project-level code generation dataset built from 18 real-world repositories with 12.7 files and 2,388.6 lines of code per task on average, supplemented with documentation and executable test cases for automatic evaluation. We further propose
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    , a multi-agent framework that decomposes projects into architecture design, skeleton generation, and code filling stages with iterative refinement and memory-based context management. Within this framework, we introduce the Semantic Software Architecture Tree, a structured and semantically rich representation that effectively bridges user requirements and source code implementation. Experiments show that
                    <jats:sc>ProjectGen</jats:sc>
                    achieves state-of-the-art performance, passing 52/124 test cases on the small-scale project-level code generation dataset DevBench, a 57% improvement over the baseline approaches, and 310 test cases on
                    <jats:sc>CodeProjectEval</jats:sc>
                    , representing an improvement of roughly tenfold compared to the baselines.
                  </jats:p>

title: Wine, Politics, and Markets
a1477911e3f6fe9d8e457d1b117363ace5c1f507.abstract:
<jats:p>Wine has been at the heart of human civilization for thousands of years, and for centuries governments around the world have regulated wine production, consumption, and trade for reasons ranging from consumer protection and quality assurance to tax revenue and the protection of vineyard owners’ rents. The European Union (EU) alone has introduced more than two thousand wine regulations. Some of today’s regulations date back hundreds of years; others are more recent; and there is considerable variation over time.

The rich history of wine regulation offers fascinating insights into the political economy of public policy and the ways in which such policies persist and evolve. This book examines specific historical developments involving wines that are well known today, such as Champagne, Port, Chianti, and Burgundy. Drawing on original historical sources and multilingual archival research, it provides the first comprehensive analysis of global wine regulations from an integrated political, economic, and historical perspective.

It will appeal to a wide range of readers, including academics and students across disciplines, and anyone interested in wine and wine markets around the world.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning-assisted Polarimetric Calibration and Optimization of a Coronagraph with an LCVR-based Modulator
container-title: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
78aec6cfe6bb506ccb6d999d9be11e72466e5dea.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Coronal polarimetry is essential for electron density inversion and magnetic field diagnostics. Liquid crystal variable retarders (LCVRs) are promising for active polarimetric modulation in coronagraphs. However, their practical performance depends on voltage, wavelength, temperature, and instrument integration. As a result, conventional component calibration is insufficient for determining the optimal modulation scheme. A machine learning-assisted calibration and optimization method is proposed for a coronagraph with an LCVR-based modulator. The active modulation system, consisting of two LCVRs, a quarter-wave plate and a polarizer, is applied to a spaceborne coronagraph prototype to retrieve the full-field modulation matrix pixel-by-pixel. The eight LCVR driving voltages are treated as optimization variables, and a Gaussian Process Regression surrogate model with an Expected Improvement principle is used to identify the optimal modulation voltage. Both local and complete-instrument calibration experiments demonstrate that the method maintains high linear-polarization modulation efficiency while reducing the deviation between the measured and theoretical modulation matrices and improving demodulation stability. In particular, the rms amplitude of two dominant non-target crosstalk terms is reduced by 75.9%. This method provides a convenient approach for full-field calibration and performance evaluation of polarization modulators, and shows strong potential for autonomous on-orbit calibration of future solar observation instruments.</jats:p>

title: A physics-informed active learning framework for the inverse design of vacuum coatings
container-title: Friction
ae34ed81c5672e26d3d9a557c43e534317209d67.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The multiobjective optimization of physical vapor deposition (PVD), as a predominant modality of vacuum coating, is indispensable for surface engineering, yet its optimization is bottlenecked by the conflict between experimental efficiency and data scale. Traditional trial-and-error and purely data-driven machine learning (ML) suffer from low efficiency and severe overfitting under typical “small-sample” constraints, often recommending nonphysical or unsafe parameters. To address these challenges, this study proposes a closed-loop physics-informed active learning (PIAL) framework integrating three core modules: physics-enhanced feature engineering, a physics-regularized heteroscedastic neural network (PR-HNN), and a risk-aware dual-point batch acquisition strategy. By embedding fundamental sputtering kinetics into the PR-HNN via continuous partial derivative constraints, the model is softly regularized toward physically plausible monotonic and saturating trends within the investigated CoCrFeNiTi magnetron sputtering process window while effectively quantifying nonstationary experimental noise. Experimental results demonstrate that physics-based regularization reduces the generalization error of the PR-HNN by 41% compared to purely data-driven baselines, effectively eliminating nonphysical fluctuations in sparse data regions. Guided by the risk-aware acquisition function, the framework progressively expanded the initial Pareto front through three closed-loop iterations. The PIAL-optimized coatings achieved a peak hardness of approximately 13.4 GPa and a minimum wear depth of 0.25 μm while maintaining robust corrosion resistance. This methodology establishes a highly efficient, physically interpretable, and safe paradigm for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven surface engineering and high-performance coating development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Epitranscriptomic regulation of the COX-2/PGE2 axis by hnRNPA2B1 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
7c2ee6386786dadf3d4dd72c2b09eef27c92ad5e.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is frequently overexpressed in ESCC, yet the mechanisms leading to its dysregulation remain poorly understood. Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2/B1 (hnRNPA2B1), an oncogenic N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, has been implicated in various cancers, but its role in regulating COX-2 expression and promoting ESCC progression has not been defined.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To investigate how hnRNPA2B1 promotes ESCC progression through COX-2 regulation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Expression of hnRNPA2B1 and COX-2 was analyzed in ESCC tissues and cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Stable hnRNPA2B1 knockdown and overexpression models were established to assess cellular proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth. Bulk RNA-seq, m6A RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR and RNA immunoprecipitation-qPCR, and actinomycin D assays were used to delineate post-transcriptional regulation of COX-2. Functional and therapeutic relevance of the hnRNPA2B1-COX-2/prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) axis was evaluated using PGE2 supplementation and celecoxib treatment in vitro  and in vivo .</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>HnRNPA2B1 was significantly upregulated in ESCC and early intraepithelial neoplasia, correlating with advanced stage and poor survival. Functionally, hnRNPA2B1 promoted proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth, whereas its silencing had opposite effects. Transcriptomic and mechanistic analyses identified COX-2 as a downstream effector. HnRNPA2B1 bound to m6A-modified COX-2 transcripts, stabilized its mRNA, and enhanced COX-2/PGE2 axis. Exogenous PGE2 supplementation rescued the inhibitory effects of hnRNPA2B1 knockdown, while celecoxib treatment suppressed hnRNPA2B1-driven malignant phenotypes both in vitro  and in vivo .</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>HnRNPA2B1 drives ESCC initiation and progression by epitranscriptomically activating the COX-2/PGE2 axis. Targeting COX-2 or hnRNPA2B1-mediated m6A stabilization may offer a therapeutic strategy for ESCC.</jats:p>

title: DECODE: Detecting Structural Obfuscation in HLS based DSP Designs using Machine Learning Framework
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
095f7ff7d24d9759b348b94a06c3ce25cdef85dd.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Structural obfuscation has been a widely used hardware security technique that is used to transform the internal structure of a high-level synthesis (HLS) digital signal processing (DSP) intellectual property (IP) design such that it becomes unobvious and obscure. The intent is to thwart deobfuscation/reverse-engineering (RE) attempts. These transformations in structurally obfuscated DSP designs are elusive and non-intuitive, making them arduous to identify and detect from an attacker's perspective. In this article, we for the first time, present a novel strategy for detecting structural obfuscation in HLS based DSP designs using machine learning (ML) frameworks. This article presents a novel technique called
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">‘DECODE’</jats:italic>
                    :
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      <jats:underline>DE</jats:underline>
                      tecting Stru
                      <jats:underline>C</jats:underline>
                      tural
                      <jats:underline>O</jats:underline>
                      bfuscation in HLS based
                      <jats:underline>D</jats:underline>
                      SP Designs using Machine L
                      <jats:underline>E</jats:underline>
                      arning Framework
                    </jats:italic>
                    . The presented approach introduces a set of unique/distinct features that can successfully classify between structurally obfuscated HLS DSP designs and its non-obfuscated versions. The article also presents a novel ML database consisting of several instances of structurally obfuscated and un-obfuscated DSP HLS designs that can be fed into our ML framework (logistic regression and random forest classifier). Results of the proposed approach revealed successful detection of structurally obfuscated DSP designs with high accuracy.
                  </jats:p>

title: AI-Generated Exposure Hierarchies for Body Dysmorphic Disorder: Proof-of-Concept Study
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
475970c23de59b336f5f102fda0e80aa46b47e4e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) is a chronic, impairing condition for which cognitive behavioral therapy, including exposure and response prevention (ERP), is the first-line treatment, but few clinicians are trained in BDD-specific ERP. Constructing personalized exposure hierarchies is time-intensive and requires clinical expertise, particularly for patients with absent insight who may hold appearance beliefs with delusional conviction. Generative AI (GenAI)–powered chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have shown utility for clinical content, but their capacity to produce safe, appropriate ERP hierarchies for BDD has not been examined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study evaluated the feasibility of using ChatGPT (GPT-5) to generate ERP hierarchies for BDD, assessed the influence of clinical and demographic characteristics on output quality, benchmarked AI-generated hierarchies against those created by doctoral-level BDD specialists, and tested whether blinded experts could distinguish AI-generated from expert-generated hierarchies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GPT-5 generated 10-item graded exposure hierarchies for 72 simulated vignettes that varied by body area, insight level (good, limited, or absent), symptom specificity, age, and gender. Expert clinicians independently generated hierarchies for a subset of 18 vignettes. Two researchers rated all GPT-5 hierarchies for task completion and information integration. Three BDD expert clinicians, blinded to the hierarchy source (expert vs GPT-5), rated all 90 hierarchies for relevance, specificity, variability, safety, and overall quality. After unblinding, raters attempted to identify the AI-generated hierarchy in the 18 matched pairs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      GPT-5 generated complete hierarchies for 69 of 72 (95.8%) vignettes. Blinded experts rated GPT-5 hierarchies highly across all dimensions (mean scores ranging from 4.39, SD 0.26 to 4.90, SD 0.16 out of 5), with no significant differences from expert-generated hierarchies except for variability, where experts scored modestly higher (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.02;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.24). After unblinding, raters correctly identified AI-generated hierarchies only 31.5% (17/54) of the time, significantly below chance (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.009); this below-chance result was mostly due to one rater, and no rater performed above chance. Insight level was the most consistent predictor of quality: absent-insight hierarchies received significantly lower safety (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.73) and overall quality ratings (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.01;
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.43). This pattern was not unique to GPT-5; safety ratings for expert-generated hierarchies also declined significantly by insight level (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.03). Miscalibration of exposure difficulty, particularly for low- and absent-insight cases, was the most common rater concern (30/43, 69.8% comments), disproportionately directed at GPT-5 hierarchies.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GPT-5 generated ERP hierarchies for BDD that blinded experts rated as comparable to clinician-created hierarchies and could not reliably distinguish them from clinician-created hierarchies. However, hierarchies for patients with absent insight received lower safety and quality ratings from both AI and expert sources, and qualitative comments suggested AI-generated hierarchies were less well calibrated to delusional-level presentations. GenAI thus shows promise as a clinician-facing aid for ERP hierarchy generation, but these findings underscore the need for clinician oversight, especially for patients with delusional conviction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Leveraging Electronic Patient-Reported Symptoms to Optimize Family Caregivers’ Symptom Support for Patients With Cancer: Qualitative Formative Evaluation of the FamilyAWARE Intervention Concept
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
77a46eb0bb30e09a8143711ec91383c2587a92c6.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Each year, family caregivers help the 2 million patients newly diagnosed with cancer manage their symptoms; however, few interventions have been developed and proven efficacious to enhance their symptom-support role. The recent expansion of electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs), including remote symptom monitoring, presents an opportunity to explore novel approaches to supporting caregiver symptom management by leveraging patient ePRO data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The objective of this study was to elicit feedback on a theory-based intervention concept, called FamilyAWARE, consisting of one-on-one coaching on providing effective symptom support to patients and access to a web-based dashboard reporting summaries of their care recipient’s most recent ePRO symptom reports and tailored recommendations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This was a qualitative formative evaluation study (National Institutes of Health stage IA) where family caregivers (n=20), patients with stage I to IV cancer (n=20), and oncology clinicians (n=25) were recruited from a comprehensive cancer center in the US South and participated in semistructured, one-on-one interviews (January 2025-July 2025). Participants were shown an outline of the FamilyAWARE intervention concept and asked open-ended questions about the proposed content, format, and delivery of the intervention. Professionally transcribed interviews were analyzed using a thematic analysis approach.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Analysis yielded 4 primary themes. The first theme was first impressions and relevance. Participants’ initial impressions of FamilyAWARE were generally positive, with caregivers viewing it as highly relevant and potentially beneficial. Patients and clinicians expressed more cautious optimism, shaped by considerations of relevance and minimizing burden. The second theme was key factors for acceptability and engagement. Caregivers showed strong interest in the intervention’s potential to increase confidence in symptom support; however, engagement was seen as contingent on the perceived value, minimal burden, and flexible delivery of the intervention, particularly given time and technology constraints. The third theme was coaching content and delivery. The proposed format was widely viewed as feasible. Participants emphasized content that helps caregivers balance supporting patients with promoting patient independence while also guiding them in deciding when to seek additional help and providing proactive symptom management strategies. Opinions on delivery by phone, in person, or videoconference varied. The fourth theme was dashboard design and information access. Participants emphasized the importance of a simple, mobile-friendly dashboard designed for low digital literacy, with plain language and visual cues. Caregiver access to patient symptom data was broadly supported if patient permission was obtained.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings highlight strong interest and insights into designing a caregiver-focused intervention that integrates one-on-one coaching with ePRO patient symptom reports and tailored recommendations. Participant insights from this study will directly inform refinement of the intervention’s content, format, and delivery, with the goal of advancing it to pilot testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial Registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>N/A</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Integrating Digital Green Accounting into Business Education: A Review and Future Directions for Sustainable E-Business Learning
container-title: Business and Accounting Education Journal
0da0bb4b3e5fdf8ed07e61d8d65afb073ea961e4.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of digital green accounting into e-business and business education represents a critical step toward aligning technological innovation with sustainability imperatives. This study conducts a narrative literature review of research published between 2005 and 2025, examining how digital tools such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, IoT, and big data are reshaping accounting practices to enhance transparency, accountability, and environmental stewardship. Findings reveal that while e-businesses increasingly adopt green accounting to align with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), challenges such as curriculum rigidity, limited faculty expertise, and technological constraints hinder widespread adoption in business education. Nonetheless, innovative pedagogical practices including experiential learning, simulations, and industry partnerships which offers promising pathways for embedding sustainability literacy and digital skills into curricula. A conceptual framework is proposed to guide the integration of digital green accounting into academic programs, highlighting inputs, processes, outputs, and long-term impacts. The study concludes that collaboration among academia, industry, and policymakers is essential for preparing future business leaders to balance profitability with sustainability and drive systemic transformation.</jats:p>

title: Power Switch Network Optimization Using Machine Learning for Inrush Current and Wakeup Latency Prediction
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
1d4a10e18fcc47d5840c7c7d713e8e016023088a.abstract: <jats:p>Today’s large-scale designs leverage power gating to achieve low power consumption, which necessitates the design of an efficient power switch network that accounts for both inrush current and wakeup latency. Optimizing this power switch network involves striking a balance between minimizing inrush current and reducing wakeup latency. However, analyzing inrush and wakeup latency for a given network is computationally expensive, particularly for complex systems, making optimization frameworks that rely on analysis engines prohibitively slow. To address this challenge, we frame the analysis of inrush and wakeup latency as a regression problem and train machine-learning (ML) models to predict these metrics. The ML model achieves mean errors of less than 10% for inrush current prediction and for wakeup latency prediction, while providing a speedup of over 50× compared to SPICE. By leveraging an ML model, we efficiently explore the design space and identify optimized power switch network patterns that minimize both wakeup latency and inrush current.</jats:p>

title: SAI: Virtualizing Shared Memory of GPU for AI workload acceleration
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
c8fa29b0323351e1659db262fc936958ed20d580.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    AI workloads increasingly demand high parallelism and efficient on-chip memory utilization on modern GPUs. However, the limited capacity of shared memory often constrains thread-level parallelism, while portions of the L2 cache remain underutilized. In this work, we propose
                    <jats:bold>SAI</jats:bold>
                    , a mechanism that virtualizes shared memory into the L2 cache to improve GPU performance for AI applications. SAI dynamically activates virtualization based on runtime resource usage, enabling additional CTAs with minimal architectural modifications. We further introduce an L2 cache management strategy that integrates associativity-based virtual page allocation and a replacement information table, reducing page-swapping overhead while preserving L2 cache performance. Experimental results demonstrate that SAI achieves an 18.6% performance improvement over the baseline design and outperforms SMILE-opt, our reproduced state-of-the-art baseline, by 8.8%. Moreover, SAI captures 60.2% of the performance gain delivered by the idealized Double SMEM design while reducing energy consumption to 87.7% of the baseline. These results highlight the effectiveness of SAI in enhancing thread-level parallelism and optimizing on-chip memory for AI workloads.
                  </jats:p>

title: Co-Designed Text Messaging Intervention for Parents of Children With Early Childhood Caries: Randomized Controlled Trial
container-title: JMIR mHealth and uHealth
a6850389fd0c78a00994c29313541824776e2e31.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Early childhood caries (ECC) is a prevalent yet preventable disease that significantly impacts young children’s health and quality of life. The World Health Organization’s
                      <jats:italic>Global Strategy and Action Plan on Oral Health 2023–2030</jats:italic>
                      highlights the potential of mobile health programs to enhance engagement and support sustained oral health behavior change.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of the SmilesUp 12-week SMS text messaging–based education and support program to improve parents’ management of their children’s oral health behaviors compared to standard clinical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a multisite, assessor-blinded, parallel-design randomized controlled trial among parents of children aged 0 to 6 years who had an ECC diagnosis and attended 1 of 6 public dental clinics in metropolitan, regional, and rural New South Wales, Australia. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving the fully automated 12-week SmilesUp program (3 SMS text messages weekly) or a control group. Both groups continued to receive usual standard dental clinical treatment. The primary behavioral outcome was parent-reported twice-daily toothbrushing with fluoride toothpaste. Secondary outcomes included adherence to oral health–promoting bedtime routines and child consumption of sugar-sweetened foods and beverages. Oral health self-efficacy was measured using 6 behavioral theory–mapped items across oral hygiene, diet, and bedtime routines.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 154 participants were enrolled and randomized (n=78, 50.6% in the control group; n=76, 49.4% in the intervention group) across 6 sites, with 80.5% (124/154) completing the follow-up assessment. High program adherence was observed, with 96.1% (73/76) of intervention participants completing the program. At 12 weeks, a greater proportion of SmilesUp participants reported brushing their children’s teeth twice daily (45/61, 73.8% vs 42/63, 66.7%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.45, 95% CI 0.95-6.74;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.07), though this difference was not statistically significant. Significant improvements were observed in adherence to bedtime routines (54/61, 88.5% vs 45/63, 71.4%; aOR 3.25, 95% CI 1.15-10.18;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.03) as well as oral health knowledge on toothbrushing (46/50, 92.0% vs 41/52, 78.8%; aOR 5.47, 95% CI 1.48-25.19;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.02). No statistically significant differences were found in sugar-sweetened food (10/61, 16.4% vs 4/63, 6.3%; aOR 3.72, 95% CI 1.02-17.14;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.06) or beverage (25/61, 41.0% vs. 27/63, 42.9%; aOR 1.08, 95% CI 0.49-2.30;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.85) consumption.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that co-designed SMS text messaging–based programs show promise and may represent a feasible strategy for oral health behavior change. However, larger-scale and longer-term studies are needed to confirm sustained effectiveness using clinical outcomes. Future research should also explore ways mobile health can be scaled and cost-effectively embedded into comprehensive, interdisciplinary primary models of care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-Enabled Early Detection of Epidemic Threats in a Resource-Constrained Health System: Implementation Research from Lebanon
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
94bf395e649f9c13344c021277ab854ad6c98be5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Global South countries face heightened infectious disease risks compounded by fragmented surveillance systems and resource constraints. Lebanon’s health system crisis and recurrent outbreaks highlight the urgent need for new approaches to epidemic and pandemic preparedness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To describe the design, implementation process, and early implementation findings of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled early warning system (AI-EWS) that automates detection of epidemiologically relevant events using laboratory data in Lebanon, with emphasis on feasibility, workflow integration, stakeholder engagement, and implementation learnings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We applied an implementation research approach to co-design and validate an AI-EWS prototype integrated within a university hospital laboratory. The system incorporates a hybrid statistical and machine learning analytic pipeline and a real-time dashboard for detecting epidemic events across multiple pathogens using routine laboratory information systems (LIS) data. The system was developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) to support future national adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The project produced a structured framework for pathogen selection, rule development, dataset creation, and platform co-design with clinical and epidemiological experts, medical informatics professionals, MoPH experts, and technical specialists. Early implementation observations indicate operational feasibility within existing infrastructure, strong stakeholder engagement, and trust-building around AI-enabled surveillance through participatory design and responsible-AI governance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-enabled laboratory surveillance is a viable and scalable approach to strengthening epidemic preparedness in low-resource health systems when grounded in implementation science and responsible AI, and when explicitly aligned with local workflows and national policy priorities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Bayesian Forecasting as the Analytical Core of an AI-Assisted Early Warning System for Dengue Outbreaks during the 2023 Epidemic: Implementation and Emergency Management in a Dominican Pediatric Hospital
container-title: Oxford Open Digital Health
056417fa3dbad64347775b6e5020ffb82cf01df1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dengue remains a major cause of pediatric morbidity in the Dominican Republic, with increasingly intense epidemic cycles. Advances in statistical modeling, probabilistic forecasting, and AI-assisted digital health systems offer new opportunities to enhance early warning capabilities and strengthen hospital preparedness. This study evaluated a Bayesian negative binomial regression forecasting model as the analytical core of an AI-assisted early warning system (EWS) for predicting weekly dengue cases nationwide, using strict out-of-sample validation during the 2023 epidemic and applying its outputs operationally in a high-demand pediatric hospital. National surveillance data (PLISA/PAHO), hospital records from the Dr. Hugo Mendoza Pediatric Hospital (HPHM), and climatic and satellite indicators (NOAA, MODIS) for 2014–2024 were integrated. The model incorporated climatically plausible lags, harmonic seasonality, two vegetation indices (NDVI_lag4 and EVI_lag4), a long-term spline trend, and weakly informative priors, achieving excellent convergence (Rhat = 1.00). Climatic and environmental predictors exhibited small and uncertain effects, whereas the temporal spline accounted for most long-term epidemic variability. In the 2023 national validation, the model captured the broad epidemic trajectory and improved RMSE and MAE compared with the historical seasonal baseline (RMSE = 783.3; MAE = 423.4; MAPE = 80.2%), although proportional accuracy remained limited during abrupt epidemic acceleration. The national model also captured ascending-phase signals that were temporally aligned with the HPHM hospital outbreak, including its sharp rise during epidemiological weeks 36–40. These outputs were used alongside routine surveillance and hospital indicators to support operational situational awareness, capacity planning, patient-flow reorganization, strengthened triage, and emergency preparedness during the epidemic. The model demonstrated temporal signal detection and operational relevance, positioning Bayesian probabilistic forecasting, embedded within an AI-assisted digital health workflow, as a useful analytical component for epidemic monitoring and hospital preparedness, subject to limitations in peak magnitude calibration and proportional accuracy.</jats:p>

title:
Template-guided stacking regulation and morphology evolution of multilayer 2H- and 3R-WS
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    during layer-by-layer epitaxy
container-title: Nano Research
749faa6389b626de3c292112b87f9d5e747bee79.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Two-dimensional layered materials have attracted extensive interest owing to their highly tunable electronic and optoelectronic properties associated with layer number and interlayer stacking. Tungsten disulfide (WS2), a representative transition metal dichalcogenide, mainly adopts 2H and 3R stacking configurations in multilayer form, which exhibit distinct crystal symmetries and nonlinear optical responses. However, how template-guided stacking evolution influences the layer and morphology evolution of multilayer WS2 during layer-by-layer epitaxy remains insufficiently understood. Herein, we demonstrate a WS2-template-guided van der Waals epitaxial strategy to regulate the stacking propagation pathways and morphology evolution of multilayer WS2. Under the combined effects of template-guided epitaxial regulation and deposition-temperature-dependent stacking evolution, distinct stacking propagation pathways preferentially lead to AB-stacked 2H-WS2 and ABC-stacked 3R-WS2. Notably, multilayer 2H-WS2 exhibits asynchronous layer-dependent morphology evolution from triangular to hexagonal tower-like structures, whereas 3R-WS2 maintains a self-similar pyramidal growth pathway with highly ordered stacking propagation. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and second harmonic generation (SHG) mapping further establish the intrinsic correlation among stacking evolution, layer evolution, morphology evolution, and symmetry response in multilayer WS2, including odd-even SHG oscillation in 2H-WS2 and progressively enhanced SHG response in multilayer 3R-WS2. These findings provide new insights into template-guided stacking regulation during multilayer van der Waals epitaxy, offering a potential strategy for the controllable structural engineering of layered transition metal dichalcogenide materials.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Toward Human-Centered Pedagogy in the Age of Generative AI Among Higher Education Educators: Qualitative Phenomenological Study
container-title: JMIR Medical Education
46248c918f688c3c5f2cc8bb261f150c45f4e9cf.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative AI (GenAI) expands possibilities for content generation, feedback, personalization, and instructional support in higher education. Its growing use also challenges established assumptions about teaching, assessment, professional expertise, academic integrity, and educational responsibility. Although research has examined technology adoption and AI competencies, less is known about how educators experience and interpret the pedagogical transformation associated with GenAI in everyday teaching.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study explored how higher education educators experience GenAI-mediated pedagogical transformation, focusing on pedagogical practices, professional roles and expertise, educator agency, human-AI relationships, and associated opportunities and tensions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A qualitative phenomenological inquiry involved 23 educators from 3 Palestinian universities. Purposive maximum-variation sampling sought variation in academic rank, discipline, teaching experience, and experience with AI tools. Individual semistructured, in-depth interviews were conducted from March to April 2026, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and returned to participants for review. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by phenomenology. Initial coding was inductive and grounded in participants’ accounts; human-centered AI and sociomateriality subsequently informed interpretation as sensitizing concepts. Themes were developed through iterative comparison of transcripts, analytic memos, and alternative interpretations. Informational sufficiency was observed after approximately 20 interviews, with 3 additional interviews used to examine the developing thematic structure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The analysis generated 8 interconnected themes. Educators described a shift from content transmission toward mediation, inquiry, reflective learning, creative exploration, and process-oriented assessment. Professional expertise increasingly centered on facilitation, pedagogical design, contextual interpretation, ethical guidance, and evaluation of AI-generated content. Human-AI collaboration involved bounded and integrated configurations, with humans retaining responsibility for judgment and educational consequences. Educator agency appeared through decisions about AI participation, independent student reasoning, and the boundaries of human expertise. Credibility, bias, authorship, authenticity, and academic integrity became embedded as pedagogical concerns. Participants valued opportunities for creativity, personalization, flexibility, and instructional support while expressing concerns about dependence, reduced intellectual effort, and weakened human connection.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GenAI-mediated pedagogical transformation depends on educators’ alignment of AI use with learning purposes, the allocation of responsibilities, and the preservation of ethical accountability and meaningful relationships. The resulting human-centered pedagogy framework positions pedagogical intentionality, contextual judgment, negotiated agency, and relational presence as central to responsible integration. Universities should complement technical training and institutional policies with support for pedagogical design, critical evaluation, process-oriented assessment, and ethical reasoning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Deep learning tearing mode evolution prediction for instability control
container-title: Nuclear Fusion
2b70a4bf80d9630abceb20e0df96992b7b79667e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    To address the general need for control oriented prediction of deleterious
                    <jats:italic>m</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 2/1 tearing mode (TM) evolution in tokamak plasmas, this work develops a data-driven framework and is validated on J-TEXT experimental database. Based on multi-diagnostic histories and future control reference trajectories, including resonant magnetic perturbation (RMP) and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) references, the framework forecasts the rotating 2/1 TM evolution trajectory over the energy confinement time scale by jointly forecasting the occurrence probability, rotation frequency, and mode amplitude, while locked phases are treated as the termination of the rotating state in the present framework. A sequence based learning model is adopted to capture correlations among diagnostic signals and control references, enabling direct multistep generation of full evolution trajectories for multiple prediction targets in a single forward pass. To help the model form latent representations of the rotating 2/1 TM state, a curriculum learning strategy is employed to guide the model from simpler present window, 2/1 mode identification tasks, to long horizon evolution prediction, which is informative for predicting control relevant transitions. To further evaluate the prediction performance critical for TM suppression involving the appearance and termination of rotating TM states, this research constructed targeted subsets. Finally, the model achieves an AUC of 98.4% on the full test dataset. On targeted subsets, it attains an onset prediction accuracy of 82.87%, and achieves an 11.4% relative improvement in similarity of predicted amplitude evolution trends. Finally, to examine the physical consistency of the model’s response to changes in control references, counterfactual analyses are performed under modified control conditions. The results indicate that the framework is capable of reproducing the corresponding evolution of key parameters of the rotating 2/1 TM state, supporting its potential as a data driven surrogate for future control-oriented studies.
                  </jats:p>

title: Machine Learning methods for Small Wet-Lab Data Challenges in Enzyme Engineering
affbcb424b77004583a7f76fb097a4f706d93a61.abstract:
<jats:p>Enzyme engineering is fundamentally constrained by the scarcity of high-quality sequence-function data. The reliance of traditional machine learning models on massive labeled data further exacerbates this dilemma. This review systematically surveys machine learning methods under small-sample wet-lab data conditions, covering three technical routes: zero-shot prediction of mutation effects, few-shot transfer learning (parameter-efficient fine-tuning, meta-learning, and in-context learning), and active learning-guided directed evolution. On this basis, we summarize the applications of these methods in fitness, enzyme kinetic parameters, thermostability, selectivity and substrate specificity, and other tasks, categorized by enzyme properties, and evaluate their effectiveness from the perspectives of data efficiency, optimization magnitude, and experimental validation scale. We further discuss the challenges of collaboration, tool accessibility, and computational cost in practical workflows, and finally outline future directions. This review provides a methodological reference for enzyme engineering researchers working under limited experimental data and offers a clear and comprehensive theoretical framework for methodology developers to build more powerful solutions.
 </jats:p>

title: Bridging the Gap: Student Perceptions of Instructor Engagement in Pandemic-Era Online Learning
container-title: The Journal  of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering
452b4dd3c76ef236fdfaa05cc15c934e6b286cde.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines student perceptions of instructor engagement in online learning environments during the initial onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular attention to differences between students with prior online learning experience and those transitioning from traditional face-to-face instruction. Grounded in Moore’s transactional distance theory, the research explores how sudden shifts in instructional modality influenced students’ perceptions of instructor engagement and identifies strategies that may reduce perceived distance in online learning contexts. Survey data were collected during the summer of 2020 from students enrolled at a regional comprehensive university in the mid-South following the emergency transition to remote instruction. A comparative analysis was conducted across course modalities, focusing on seven survey items related to academic engagement, changes in instructor interaction, and student preferences for engagement. Findings indicate that students with prior experience in online courses perceived less disruption in instructor engagement following the transition, while students who had been enrolled primarily in face-to-face courses reported more noticeable declines. These differences suggest that familiarity with online learning environments may buffer students against perceived losses in engagement during periods of instructional disruption. Overall, this study contributes to the growing body of research on online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic by emphasizing how instructional practices and student experience intersect to influence motivation, engagement, and perceived learning success in online environments.</jats:p>

title: Machine-learning-assisted tracking of magnetic objects using quantum diamond magnetometry
container-title: Physical Review Applied
52aed64f9c56977441f670308dcbeab4c213e986.abstract: <jats:p>Remote magnetic sensing can be used to monitor the position of objects in real time, enabling ground transport monitoring, underground infrastructure mapping, and hazardous detection. However, magnetic signals are typically weak and complex, requiring sophisticated physical models to analyze them and a detailed knowledge of the system under study, factors that are frequently unavailable. In this work, we provide a solution to these limitations by demonstrating a machine-learning (ML) method that can be trained exclusively on experimental data, without the need of any physical model, to predict the position of a magnetic target in real time. The target can be any object with a magnetic signal above the floor noise, and in this case, we use a quantum diamond magnetometer to track variations of a few hundred nanoteslas produced by an elevator moving along a single axis. The one-dimensional movement is a simple yet challenging scenario, resembling realistic environments such as high buildings, tunnels, or train circuits, and is the first step toward building broader applications. Our ML algorithm can be trained in approximately 40 min, achieving over 80% accuracy in predicting the target’s position at a rate of 10 Hz, for a positional error tolerance of 30 cm, which is well within the the 4-m spacing between parking levels. Our results open up the possibility to apply this ML method more generally for real-time monitoring of magnetic objects, which will broaden the scope of magnetic detection applications.</jats:p>

0cea04df1f33891ac6e61332b69e78c30652b6e1.abstract: <jats:p>News gathering, production, verification, and distribution have been reshaped—sometimes profoundly, sometimes quietly—by the growing presence of artificial intelligence and machine learning in broadcast operations. This chapter surveys the main areas where these technologies operate: automated news production, deepfake detection, audience analytics, recommender systems, and voice synthesis. It also examines ethical questions emerging in each domain. Drawing on recent scholarship across journalism studies, computer science, media ethics, and communication research, the chapter explores tensions between operational efficiency and journalistic integrity, between personalization and information diversity, and between AI-assisted verification and its vulnerability to synthetic content. A key theme is that productivity gains, though real, are not self-sustaining. Responsible deployment requires editorial oversight, effective governance, and transparent disclosure to audiences. The chapter concludes by outlining a research agenda for an information environment increasingly shaped by AI.</jats:p>

title: The Digital Transformation of Television Broadcasting Supported by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
35b7dc9c798c6869d6eeb6921fd0c44c284f95bc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation brought about by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in television broadcasting within a conceptual and critical framework. It discusses how processes such as content production, automation, scheduling, audience measurement and personalisation have been reorganised through data-driven systems. Furthermore, by assessing the impacts of algorithmicisation on editorial independence, public accountability, transparency, privacy and accountability, the study argues that the future of television broadcasting is shaped not only by technical innovation but also by institutional and ethical choices.</jats:p>

title: The Future of Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
bff6f50e054390e2c139c80e7fb45824d6ff514a.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are transforming the television and broadcast media industry by reshaping production workflows, distribution models, and audience engagement strategies. Intelligent systems are increasingly applied in automated content creation, smart studio operations, personalized recommendation services, and predictive audience analytics. These innovations enhance efficiency, reduce operational costs, and enable broadcasters to deliver more adaptive and customized viewing experiences across digital platforms. However, the growing integration of AI also raises important challenges related to ethical accountability, algorithmic bias, transparency, and workforce transformation. Human creativity, editorial judgment, and trust remain essential elements in ensuring responsible media practices. The future of television will depend on balancing technological innovation with human-centered values to build sustainable and socially meaningful broadcast ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Television Platforms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
054cd1bab132b082e3e6a31810c1cc1a1ff38db7.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how artificial intelligence–driven algorithms on digital television platforms transform the processes of cultural production, distribution, and consumption within the media ecosystem. Focusing on Netflix as a case study, it analyzes how algorithmic recommendation systems structure content visibility, shape user preferences, and reorganize audience behavior through data-driven mechanisms. Drawing on sociological theories of power and cultural production, the study conceptualizes algorithms not merely as technical tools but as socio-technical actors that establish new regimes of visibility and control. In this context, the notion of the “algorithmic field” is proposed to explain how platform-based systems redefine power relations, mediate cultural hierarchies, and reproduce structural inequalities. The findings suggest that digital platforms operate as influential intermediaries that both organize and govern cultural circulation in contemporary media environments.</jats:p>

title: From Broadcast to Platform Power
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
0039e4646b5f12e04840a5816064712c21fdb48a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of Turkish television from a broadcast-centered system into a platform-based, datafied media ecology shaped by Netflix, BluTV, Exxen, and related streaming services. It argues that streaming in Turkey cannot be understood as a simple technological shift, because platforms entered a media system already defined by dizi exports, RTÜK regulation, broadcast scarcity, censorship pressures, and audience dissatisfaction with long-form television. Through case studies of The Protector, Ethos, BluTV, and Exxen, the chapter analyzes how platform commissioning, personalization, metadata, recommendation systems, and AI-assisted workflows reshape cultural visibility, editorial authority, and creative labor. The chapter also considers how state regulation and media capture complicate platform governance in Turkey. It concludes that Turkish television's future depends on balancing algorithmic efficiency, cultural specificity, regulatory pressure, and editorial responsibility.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Local Broadcasting, and the Logic of Innovation From the Periphery
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
993d09fe2a97e708c317641849a351071457e373.abstract: <jats:p>Drawing on a qualitative case study of Radio Kepulauan Seribu, this chapter examines how these tensions unfold within Indonesia's small-island broadcasting context. Rather than framing AI as a disruptive force that automates editorial work, the chapter advances the concept of guided augmentation, in which AI supports preparatory cognitive tasks while ethical judgment, contextual interpretation, and public responsibility remain human-centered. Through interviews and non-participant observation, the study demonstrates how AI adoption emerges from structural constraints, limited resources, and public service mandates rather than technological ambition. The findings challenge dominant, Global North–centric narratives of AI-driven media transformation by presenting small islands as sites of adaptive innovation and relational accountability. By reframing hybrid broadcasting as a stable, context-sensitive media configuration, the chapter contributes to broader debates on AI, ethics, and the future of broadcasting in community-oriented media ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
857bae5718eff00351eeae246d5c2a40314cac99.abstract: <jats:p>With the process of digitalization, television broadcasting has evolved into a data-driven, algorithmic structure through digital platform services. In this context, the use of artificial intelligence is regarded as a tool that increases efficiency in television broadcasting. However, gaining competitive advantage through algorithmic infrastructures and the commodification of viewer data create forms of algorithmic management. This study examines the transformation created by artificial intelligence in the field of television broadcasting through platformization shaped by data ownership, the reshaping of labor processes through automation, and algorithmic governmentality as the outcome of these processes. The fact that artificial intelligence produces transformations in relation to capital accumulation, labor regimes, data ownership, and ideological control makes it necessary to evaluate television broadcasting from a political-economic perspective.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Curatorial Shift
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
1559be582d93ad91c2a432d936327ea610496ff5.abstract: <jats:p>Television program scheduling has long been an exercise in editorial authority: decisions regarding which programs to air, when, and in what order have shaped viewer behavior, structured the revenue logic of commercial broadcasting, and reproduced the broader ideological and economic conditions of the broadcasting system. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into broadcasting operations is restructuring this framework. Algorithmic tools are increasingly shaping audience forecasting, ad placement, content performance evaluation, and recommendation systems. Drawing on Raymond Williams' flow theory, gatekeeping theory, and platform capitalism, this chapter examines this transformation through the concept of algorithmic curatorial shift, the redistribution of editorial authority from human planning experts to algorithmic systems.</jats:p>
