title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based Digital Interventions for Illicit Substance Use Disorders: Scoping Review of Intervention Design, Efficacy Indicators, and Methodological Gaps
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
9d1858cff34c91ccfc45c7d996e799804ca90d99.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Illicit substance use disorders (SUDs) are escalating globally; yet, social stigma and legal barriers restrict access to conventional treatment, and existing research remains skewed toward alcohol and nicotine. Digital interventions incorporating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) offer a discreet, scalable alternative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review maps how CBT-based digital interventions for illicit SUDs are designed and delivered across platforms, identifying their theoretical frameworks, functional components, outcome indicators, and reported methodological limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). Six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycINFO, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) were searched from inception to June 28, 2026, without language, date, or study design limits, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching (July 3, 2026). Eligible studies were empirical primary studies quantitatively evaluating digital interventions incorporating CBT for illicit or nonprescribed substance use; alcohol- or nicotine-only populations were excluded. Three reviewers independently screened and charted all studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus or adjudication. Data were synthesized narratively, with tables, figures, and an evidence gap map.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fifty-six studies published between 2008 and 2026, drawn from 47 distinct participant samples, met the eligibility criteria. Most were conducted in North America (40/56, 71.4%) and used randomized controlled designs (39/56, 69.6%). Polysubstance-using populations were most frequently targeted (32/56, 57.1%), followed by cannabis (13/56, 23.2%), opioids (6/56, 10.7%), and stimulants (5/56, 8.9%). Interventions were delivered mainly via web (24/56, 42.9%) or app (24/56, 42.9%) platforms, and most (49/56, 87.5%) were grounded in traditional CBT, most often combined with contingency management (18/56, 32.1%) or motivational interviewing (17/56, 30.4%). Core functional components included therapeutic intervention (55/56, 98.2%), self-tracking and notification (25/56, 44.6%), reward (24/56, 42.9%), and support and feedback (21/56, 37.5%). Primary outcomes focused on substance use and abstinence (41/56, 73.2%), retention/feasibility (16/56, 28.6%), and mental health status or coping skills (14/56, 25%). Author-reported limitations were predominantly participant-level (52/56, 92.9%), measurement-level (43/56, 76.8%), study-level (34/56, 60.7%), and intervention-level (25/56, 44.6%) domains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Unlike previous reviews confined to a single substance or delivery platform, this review is innovative in mapping CBT-based digital interventions across the full spectrum of illicit substances, including polysubstance use, and in linking their functional components to intended therapeutic mechanisms. It thereby contributes to the development of these technologies and, by synthesizing author-reported limitations, proposes methodological improvements for their future evaluation. At present, CBT-based digital interventions are best positioned as adjuncts that extend the reach and continuity of existing addiction care rather than as stand-alone substitutes for it; substance-specific customization, objective outcome measures, and modular trial designs are needed to establish them as scalable clinical tools.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Cybersecurity in Digital Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a2d591ae29b63d49c8f5b0f24754dec3ea764c2d.abstract: <jats:p>With ever-increasing exposures of interconnected networks to threats and complex vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity of digital supply chains acquires importance. The principle of zero-trust architecture is, never trust always verify. An implication of this is that stringent authentication must be validated, real-time acknowledgment and monitoring must be ensured at all points, and the least-privilege access must be granted to all the users and devices. An undeniable fact is that blockchain guarantees security in transactions through its decentralized and tamper-proof record. Thus, building a truly trust less infrastructure in logistics and supply chain, blockchain and smart contract-based applications can be employed to automate business processes, remove intermediaries, and prevent fraud. For a quantum computer, post-quantum cryptography becomes an answer to preserve secrets in view of any threat of decryption; it thereby replaces classical ways of encryption with one that resists quantum attack.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Supply Chain Security
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a9fac601cba8221d0a0ca6b6ee0491173add368e.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are the backbone of global trade, yet they face unprecedented risks in the digital era. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into supply chain security has emerged as a transformative strategy to manage complex risks, enhance cyber defenses, and build resilient networks. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of how AI is reshaping supply chain risk management, from predicting disruptions to automating responses. It discusses how AI-driven tools bolster cybersecurity in increasingly digital supply chains, identifying threats and safeguarding critical links. The chapter also examines the ethical challenges—such as data privacy, bias, and accountability—arising from AI integration, along with governance measures to ensure responsible use. Policy and international cooperation aspects are explored, recognizing that global supply chains require harmonized regulations and collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Architecting Antifragile Supply Chains With AI, Digital Twins, and Zero Trust Architecture
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
633ea892d6852074e94cf9336e159d7797152a41.abstract: <jats:p>In an era defined by perpetual disruption, traditional supply chain models have proven dangerously fragile. This chapter introduces the “Sentient Shield,” a novel framework for architecting antifragile supply chains that benefit from disruptions rather than merely withstanding them. The framework integrates three critical technologies: AI driven predictive analytics for precognition, Digital Twins for hyper realistic visualization and simulation, and Zero Trust Architectures as a foundational security posture. Through detailed case studies of the COVID 19 vaccine distribution, semiconductor trade wars, and the SolarWinds cyberattack, this chapter demonstrates how the Sentient Shield creates supply chains that learn from disruption. The chapter concludes with practical implementation principles and discusses governance challenges, providing a comprehensive blueprint for C suite leaders, government strategists, and researchers seeking to build self-improving supply networks in an increasingly volatile global environment.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twin Architecture in Supply Chain Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
d99b6055016f0e8c84e8e502fe276ebb105bc5e1.abstract: <jats:p>The major gap that still exists is the operationalization of the application of the concept of digital twist in the supply chain management although more research has been done on the area. This is more so in the emerging countries where its adoption is impeded by infrastructural and fragmented logistic ecosystems and limited capital. This chapter addresses that gap by introducing digital twin architectures within supply chain processes through a structured conceptual framework to support adaptive governance, anticipate risks, and intelligence in decision-making. Three basic mechanisms are discussed in the chapter such as (1) bi-directional data synchronization in real-time among supply chain nodes; (2) predictive simulation modeling of demand volatility and disruption; and (3) cross-tier visibility as an architecture requirement of coordination. These processes rest on a critical review of the literature, industry experience and systems-thinking concepts.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Digital Twins and Blockchain Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
800c4603905b0b481af418f93c27b335627b538c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops an architecture for combining cognitive digital twins with blockchain ecosystems to deliver predictive business intelligence in the industrial metaverse. It argues that digital-twin initiatives create value only when operational telemetry, semantic context, decision models, and human governance are connected through trusted data-sharing and executable coordination mechanisms. Drawing on research in digital twins, industrial metaverse design, blockchain-enabled provenance, smart contracts, human-centric manufacturing, and explainable AI, the chapter proposes a layered reference architecture, performance metrics, implementation logic, and governance controls. It also examines persistent challenges, including semantic fragmentation, model drift, latency, privacy, interoperability, energy cost, and the oracle problem. The chapter concludes with design recommendations and a research agenda for resilient, trustworthy, and economically useful industrial intelligence systems across networked industrial-metaverse platforms and ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twins and Blockchain-Enabled Trust for Resilient Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
6cae48cda77d8a51b8ca2bc4b94e05b4a9e8c301.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we explore the process of achieving supply chain resilience in Industrial Metaverse environments by embedding digital twin technology and blockchain-based distributed trust mechanisms. No single technology is sufficient to address the triple crises of disruption, opacity, and accountability in contemporary supply chains. The chapter makes its case through trans-disciplinary scholarship spanning supply chain management, digital transformation, blockchain governance, and Industry 4.0. They introduce a 5-layer conceptual framework to illustrate how these physical operations, data connectivity, simulation, distributed verification, and governance layers are interdependent among each other via the Digital Twin–Blockchain Trust Framework, which allows us to visualize how such Human-centric smart systems can lead towards Visibility, Traceability, and Adaptive Resilience eventually. Investigates sustainability implications, ethical risks, and cyber vulnerabilities, as well as concrete pathways for managerial adoption.</jats:p>

title: Immersive Stock Control for Virtual Depots via Process Digital Twins and Topological Data Analysis
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
181d6ce5803b6924cc02dfd46f21bf24456d4579.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents the development of an advanced inventory management model for virtual warehouses. By combining process digital twins with Topological Data Analysis, this model strives to support supervisors in pinpointing bottleneck formations that standard performance indicators are unable to reveal. The methodology describes how IoT-like intralogistics events are interpreted as augmented point clouds. The methodology also describes how persistent homology is computed through Vietoris-Rips and Alpha-complex filtrations, and how topological indicators are transformed into an immersive decision layer through the framework's comprehensive approach to bottleneck and Wasserstein distances. The computational case interprets fragmentation, routing loops, and volumetric cavities as congestion, vulnerability, and latent capacity indicators. The results show how the persistent topology of the model offers a candidate articulate layer for the process digital twins. The model still needs additional empirical calibration, for operational interventions in a physical warehouse.</jats:p>

title: Metaverse-Enabled Leadership for Industrial Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
655782e4fe7f1ef790e19e8011646a5a0b9572a9.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of digital technologies, including digital twins, blockchain, and the Industrial Metaverse, is transforming global supply chains from linear systems into interconnected, data-driven ecosystems. This study examines how immersive metaverse environments reshape leadership practices within supply chains, emphasizing adaptive, collaborative, and inclusive behaviors. Through avatar-mediated interactions, gamification, and virtual prototyping, leaders engage in realistic simulations, enhancing decision-making, coordination, and stakeholder engagement across distributed operations. While immersive technologies offer experiential learning and operational resilience, challenges such as cognitive overload, limited nonverbal cues, and unequal access highlight the need for context-sensitive strategies. A conceptual framework is proposed linking technological affordances, leadership behaviors, and supply chain outcomes, providing a foundation for research and practical guidance on metaverse-enabled leadership in complex industrial networks.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Recognition
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
8d55c03606f397dfebd690ec5704784da2344f3c.abstract: <jats:p>Current e-learning systems are still not well-suited to learn in real-time as individuals' emotional and cognitive state. The chapter presents AIALE (Affective Intelligence Adaptive Learning Engine), a multimodal system capable of embedding facial coding, bio signals, keystroke dynamics and eye-tracking in a single pipeline and with sub-500ms inference latency. The AIALE's three-tier architecture consists of a deep learning-based effect inference, a reinforcement learning-based curriculum control and a pedagogic intervention broker. AIALE was tested with 214 university students from four disciplines and led to statistically significant increases in knowledge gain (31% above that of a knowledge-adaptive baseline) as well as to an increase in engagement duration and a balance of cognitive load, compared to a knowledge-adaptive baseline and a non-adaptive control. An ablation analysis shows that the most significant affective dimensions for adaptive interventions' quality are confusion and cognitive load detection. The chapter also introduces five research gaps and explores emerging research avenues such as generative AI tutoring agents and explainable affective adaptation.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning-Driven Emotion Recognition for Personalized and Adaptive E-Learning Systems
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
ce676f08ce46956bb22f53f59a27b6cbe5ec864b.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores how deep learning–based emotion recognition enhances student engagement and cognitive growth in e-learning environments. By leveraging CNN and LSTM architectures, the proposed framework detects learners' emotions from facial and behavioral cues in real time, enabling adaptive instructional responses. Through camera-based, non-invasive monitoring, emotions such as confusion, curiosity, or satisfaction are quantified to personalize learning experiences and improve retention. The chapter also discusses dataset selection, model design, and integration into Learning Management Systems (LMS). Case insights demonstrate how emotion-aware systems foster empathy, motivation, and inclusivity in digital education. Ethical considerations privacy, fairness, and explainability are addressed to ensure responsible AI deployment. The study establishes emotion recognition as a cornerstone for intelligent, adaptive, and human-centered e-learning ecosystems that align technology with emotional intelligence and pedagogical effectiveness.</jats:p>

title: Passive Learning to Active Engagement
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
eacaa5f4ae36bc7dc2909810ec0a52e6a7081ebd.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of digital technologies has transformed the educational landscape, challenging traditional passive learning models and emphasizing the need for active engagement in deep learning. Passive learning, characterized by one-way information delivery and limited learner interaction, often results in superficial comprehension and low retention. In contrast, active engagement leverages interactive digital tools, collaborative strategies, and learner-centered approaches to foster critical thinking, problem-solving, and meaningful knowledge construction. This chapter explores the theoretical underpinnings of passive and active learning, examines the pedagogical shift facilitated by digital technologies, and highlights effective strategies for promoting deep learning in contemporary educational environments. Case studies from diverse educational contexts illustrate how digital pedagogy can bridge the gap between passive reception and active participation, ultimately enhancing learner motivation, engagement, and long-term retention.</jats:p>

title: Digital Catalytic Leadership for Governing Agentic AI
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
a7a2f25db22c009ea70fb3c60ff8c7c5966288e7.abstract: <jats:p>The evolution of agentic AI is transforming higher education administration beyond simple automation. This chapter examines the governance challenges of AI integration in universities and proposes Digital Catalytic Leadership (DCL) as an adaptive governance framework. The study finds that while agentic AI can improve administrative effectiveness, it also creates challenges related to accountability, data security, and human–AI relations. This chapter argues that DCL is important for building adaptive, ethical, and human-centered higher education governance in the AI era.</jats:p>

title: Custody, keys and concessions: digital assets in Hong Kong family office and trust structures—property, private keys, fiduciary duty and the price of the licensed intermediary, with English, offshore and Singapore perspectives
container-title: Trusts & Trustees
61fc6e2da3e0a708c06ee1d8178961aceb151cb6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In three years, Hong Kong has built a regulatory and fiscal architecture for digital assets reaching every layer of the private wealth structure. This article argues that the private key, not the token, is the operative subject matter of the digital-asset trust: constitution, certainty of subject matter, custody, delegation, exoneration and succession must all be restated in terms of who can sign. Hong Kong’s concessions, fiscal and regulatory alike, are the price the state pays to move key control into supervised hands; the settlor who declines that bargain keeps a structure more fragile than its documentation suggests.</jats:p>

title: A city of “ambiguous loss”: digital methods and a multiscalar examination of Jewish Budapest in the aftermath of the Holocaust
container-title: Holocaust And Genocide Studies
cebbff4d4a63fa42432f4291ab92c22389f06978.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article focuses on an understudied phenomenon in the immediate postwar period: the existence of a liminal group of Jewish men whose fate remained unknown. To identify this group in one city with a large postwar Jewish population, the article intentionally draws on mixed methods, including a traditional close reading of oral history interviews and a spatial analysis of a large-scale survey of Jewish survivors living in Budapest that was quickly undertaken by a coalition of Jewish organizations in summer 1945 and published and distributed in 1946 under the title Counted Remnant: Register of the Jewish Survivors in Budapest. This article addresses the narrow question of how what contemporary therapists dub “ambiguous loss” was experienced in one post-Holocaust city, as well as two broader issues. First, it signals that the postwar context was more complex than the binary of returning Jewish survivors (the names listed in Counted Remnant) and non-returning Jewish victims who had been murdered (the names not listed in Counted Remnant). Rather, by adopting a method dubbed distant reading “against the grain,” this study identifies the existence of a third, large group of Hungarian Jewish men who neither were dead nor had returned home in the postwar years. Second, by intentionally adopting a range of methods that include both distant and close reading, this article explores the value in adopting mixed-method approaches, including from the digital humanities—alongside multiscalar geographical analysis—within “integrated” histories and geographies of the Holocaust.</jats:p>

title: Fostering Classroom Wellbeing Through Reflective Teaching
container-title: Enhancing Classroom Well-Being Through Relational Teaching
551026cff8324f78936ec3a631e7525fdeb5953d.abstract: <jats:p>Teaching is both a fulfilling and a demanding profession. Teachers are a key stakeholder within socio-educational spaces and their wellbeing has implications for schools, students and society at large. Currently, there are growing concerns regarding teachers' wellbeing and their retention in the profession. Reflective teaching can serve as a powerful tool for enhancing teacher wellbeing by encouraging them to critically analyze their teaching practices and classroom interactions. Thus, besides enhancing teaching effectiveness, reflective teaching can be viewed as a pathway to foster relational well-being in the classroom as it helps build healthier relationships between teachers and students. Through a narrative review approach, the present chapter synthesizes existing conceptualizations of reflection and models of reflection, and offers actionable insights on reflective teaching practices, that are grounded in empirical literature. Finally, the chapter highlights common barriers to reflective practice and presents strategies for addressing them.</jats:p>

title: Media, Information Literacy, and Digital Inclusion
container-title: Designing and Implementing Literacy Ecosystems
85d8685daef775e3add303b6478de7ce0dff10c3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter intersects media, information literacy (MIL), digital inclusion and community informatics in rural Zambia. The development of digital technologies, media platforms and information systems has transmogrified how people access information, communicate, participate in civic life and contribute to socioeconomic development. Notwithstanding these advancements, noteworthy digital inequalities persist between urban and rural communities, predominantly in developing countries. There, access to information and communication technologies (ICTs), digital skills and information resources remains uneven. Besides brining out disablers, the chapter argues that MIL is a critical enabler of meaningful participation in contemporary information societies and a prerequisite for reducing digital exclusion. The chapter proposes an integrated framework linking media access, information literacy, community empowerment and sustainable rural development. It concludes with policy and practice recommendations for strengthening digital inclusion and community transformation in rural Zambia.</jats:p>

title: Reframing Health Literacy in Aging
container-title: Health Literacy and Social Innovation for Healthy Aging
1286e0cc2398e0dd86e434eb02858f763b46a838.abstract: <jats:p>Population aging has widened the gap between life expectancy and healthy life expectancy, increasing pressure on health systems and reinforcing the need for preventive, literacy-based interventions. Although Health Literacy (HL) is recognized as essential for autonomy within the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing, its emotional dimension remains underexplored in aging research. This chapter argues that emotional literacy functions as a regulatory mediator between cognitive HL and effective self-management in later life. Building on integrated HL models and lifespan motivational theory, we propose the Adaptive Emotional Health Literacy Model (AEHLM), which explains how affective processes shape information processing, decision-making, and adherence. The chapter also introduces EMOT-AGE, a structured intervention framework, and examines social prescribing, age-friendly environments, and ethically governed AI as mechanisms for advancing emotionally intelligent health systems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Health Literacy and Technology Adoption in Older Adults
container-title: Health Literacy and Social Innovation for Healthy Aging
696ce5355159b7b2dd640efe61a749c981fb222e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines digital health literacy as a key determinant of older adults' engagement with digital health technologies and associated health-related outcomes. Drawing on a systematic synthesis of recent empirical evidence and a theoretically informed framework, the chapter situates digital health literacy at the intersection of health literacy, ageing, technology adoption, and social determinants of health. The analysis highlights how digital health literacy is associated with the use of digital health technologies, health information-seeking behaviours, self-management, and perceived wellbeing among older adults, while also reflecting underlying social inequalities. By confronting theoretical models with empirical findings, the chapter underscores the multidimensional, dynamic, and socially embedded nature of digital health literacy in later life. The discussion emphasises implications for research, policy, and practice, particularly in relation to equity, inclusive digital health design, and the promotion of healthy ageing in increasingly digitalised health systems.</jats:p>

title: Exploring Digital Health Utilisation in Ageing Populations
container-title: Health Literacy and Social Innovation for Healthy Aging
3605c53a33c41781b1506c9b7d5efed67a5f8b3a.abstract: <jats:p>Population ageing represents one of the most significant demographic transformations of the twenty-first century, profoundly reshaping health systems, social structures, labor markets, and patterns of care delivery worldwide. As life expectancy increases across diverse socio-economic, cultural, and geographical contexts, societies are confronted with the challenge of ensuring that longer lives are lived not only in good physical health but also with dignity, autonomy, equity, and social participation. In parallel with these demographic shifts, healthcare systems are undergoing rapid digital transformation. Digital technologies such as telemedicine, electronic health records, mobile health applications, wearable and assistive devices, artificial intelligence–supported decision tools, and remote monitoring systems are increasingly positioned as essential mechanisms for improving access, efficiency, continuity, and personalisation of care.</jats:p>

title: The Effect of Bipolar Disorder Illness Course on Physiological Digital Signals: Observational Study
container-title: JMIR Mental Health
01f0bfe7880c7f8dce5bb83ca1c195cfb3aee348.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Although bipolar disorder (BD) lacks objective biomarkers of illness progression, wearable devices enable continuous, real-world collection of physiological digital biosignals, offering a promising approach to address this gap. Measures such as electrodermal activity (EDA) and heart rate variability (HRV) fluctuate with mood state and symptom severity. Previous studies have reported reduced EDA during depressive episodes and increased HRV following symptom resolution after acute mood episodes. Furthermore, greater illness burden in BD has been associated with lower HRV, suggesting that digital biosignals may capture not only state-related changes but also aspects of illness course.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigated whether naturalistic EDA and heart rate (HR) profiles differ according to illness course variables in BD—including diagnosis, predominant polarity, years since onset, and lifetime number of episodes—in euthymic patients, to evaluate their potential as illness course biomarkers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      This cross-sectional post hoc analysis used data from 80 euthymic patients on the BD spectrum from the INTREPIBD-TIMEBASE cohort. Participants were recruited at Hospital Clínic de Barcelona (Spain) between 2021 and 2024 and wore an Empatica E4 wristband for 48 hours in naturalistic settings. Inclusion criteria comprised a current or past
                      <jats:italic>DSM-5</jats:italic>
                      (
                      <jats:italic>Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders</jats:italic>
                      , Fifth Edition) diagnosis of BD confirmed by structured interview and sustained euthymia. We examined the effects of 4 illness course variables (diagnosis, predominant polarity, years since onset, and number of lifetime episodes) on 3 biosignals (mean EDA, EDA peaks per minute, and HR) using generalized additive models. Interactions between illness course variables and circadian patterns were also assessed. All models were adjusted for age, sex, and current antipsychotic use and included a participant-specific random effect.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Of the 80 participants, 49 (61.3%) were female; participants’ mean age was 46.9 (SD 14.1) years. After adjustment for covariates and multiple comparisons, no significant associations were observed between illness course variables and EDA or HR. In sensitivity analyses excluding patients with schizoaffective disorder (n=75), years since illness onset and predominant polarity were associated with EDA peaks per minute after multiple comparison correction. Specifically, patients with more than 22 years since illness onset had fewer EDA peaks compared with other groups (β=−1.06, 95% CI −1.71 to −0.41;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.001). No significant interactions were found between illness course variables and circadian patterns of EDA or HR.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To our knowledge, this is the first study to examine the association between illness course variables and EDA and HR recorded in naturalistic settings in BD. In contrast to prior findings linking illness burden with HRV, our results suggest that years since illness onset may show modest associations with phasic EDA activity. These findings indicate that digital biosignals may be more sensitive to state-related changes than to illness course characteristics, limiting their use as longitudinal biomarkers of disease progression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Adaptive Regulation, Sandboxes, and Experimentalist Approaches
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
7e11bfc9418f4605cdb5f5a63e9b3f499236e89e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence technologies presents unprecedented challenges to traditional regulatory frameworks and democratic governance structures. This chapter examines how adaptive regulation, regulatory sandboxes, and experimentalist governance approaches are reshaping the social contract between citizens, governments, and technology corporations in the AI era. Through comprehensive analysis of emerging regulatory models across multiple jurisdictions, this study demonstrates how experimentalist approaches enable responsive governance while maintaining democratic accountability. The chapter evaluates the effectiveness of regulatory sandboxes in balancing innovation with risk management, explores the theoretical foundations of adaptive regulation in complex technological environments, and proposes a reconceptualized framework for the social contract that accommodates algorithmic decision-making while preserving fundamental rights.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Governance and Due Process in India
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
588dcb96d6cae7a2831ce0b99703c07178f2e3ab.abstract: <jats:p>The expansion of digital governance in India has embedded algorithmic systems within welfare administration, particularly in identity verification, eligibility determination, and benefit delivery. While these systems are justified on grounds of efficiency and scalability, they raise significant concerns for due process and administrative fairness. This chapter examines how core procedural safeguards notice, hearing, and reasoned decisions are affected by automated decision-making frameworks. It argues that algorithmic governance introduces opacity, limits avenues for contestation, and weakens accountability. The integration of digital identity further conditions access to welfare on technological compliance, increasing risks of exclusion. The chapter concludes that algorithmic systems fundamentally reshape state citizen relations and require recalibrated legal safeguards.</jats:p>

title: Digital Sovereignty and Legal Pluralism
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
0e1ac7826c5e0fc071b7288b1558bb3f5df99b2a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolving concept of digital sovereignty through a comparative analysis of the European Union, the United States, and India within conditions of legal pluralism. It explores how democratic systems negotiate authority, rights, and regulation across overlapping legal, technological, and market domains. The European Union's rights-based constitutionalism, the United States' market-oriented digital order, and India's developmental-democratic model reveal diverse strategies for governing data, platforms, and infrastructure. Drawing on secondary data from 2020–2025, the chapter analyzes regulatory frameworks such as the GDPR, DPDP Act 2023, and the U.S. FTC's enforcement regime. It identifies convergences in recognizing data as a strategic resource and divergences in institutional design, enforcement capacity, and global influence.</jats:p>

title: Digital Illiteracy and Accounting Compliance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI, Democracy, and the Transformation of Legal Norms
5efe409d16d9b3864a79a51144be26f5f26411d2.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how digital illiteracy affects accounting compliance during the transition to mandatory e-invoicing in Greece. A quantitative approach was employed using data from 220 enterprises located in the Prefecture of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace. A structured questionnaire measured digital skills, awareness of e-invoicing procedures, and perceptions of state support. The results reveal that educational level and gender significantly influence the effective implementation of e-invoicing tools, while age has no significant impact. Despite gradual improvements in digital competence, digital illiteracy remains a key barrier to full compliance, especially among SMEs. The findings highlight the need for targeted digital training programs, simplified e-invoicing platforms, and policy incentives aimed at strengthening SMEs' technological capacity. This research empirically links digital literacy to compliance behavior in an emerging economy context, offering actionable insights for policymakers, tax authorities, and accounting practitioners.</jats:p>

title: Identification of Regional Zones Based on the Adaptive Potential of Agricultural Crops to Climate Change in Belarus
container-title: Strategic Planning and Adaptation of Resilient Agri-Food Systems in a Changing World
6567f9fea79ac75d8718f3fc2ae11e3bc134a856.abstract: <jats:p>Adapting Belarus' agriculture to climate change requires assessing the adaptive potential of major crops across its regions. Since environmental shifts vary regionally and crops differ in adaptability, measuring this potential helps align crop selection with favorable areas, optimize sowing plans, and enhance resilience and economic efficiency. This study calculates adaptive potential for in each Belarusian region, identifies regional trends, and ranks regions by their adaptive capacity. Regions are classified into high, moderate, and low adaptive-potential zones, highlighting where yields are most climate-dependent. Incorporating this differentiated potential into regional and national cropping-structure planning ensures stable agricultural output under evolving climate conditions. The resulting recommendations guide rational crop-area allocation to secure food production and economic sustainability amid global warming.</jats:p>

title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
Integrating Digital Leadership and Sustainable Development in Higher Education
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
f9556c46c081fd9e96d6b9496bd9d3baa50a5603.abstract: <jats:p>Higher education institutions (HEIs) serve as fundamental pillars for societal advancement and economic growth, acting as the primary source of human capital for all other sectors. In the era of the “ESG-Digital Nexus,” this study investigates the critical intersection of digital leadership and sustainable development within the academic landscape. The primary objective of this research is to propose and validate a to collect data from a representative sample of faculty members and administrative staff in higher education. With a valid sample size of 326 participants, the data were analyzed using advanced statistical techniques, specifically employing SPSS for data processing and Amos (v.26) for structural equation modeling. The findings reveal a strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship between digital leadership and sustainable development. The results demonstrate that effective digital leadership acts as a critical catalyst, significantly influencing the institution's capacity to achieve sustainable development goals.</jats:p>

title: ESG and Digital Transformation
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
4cb1b6c028ee97f087b97bd7c427757b1b2a3264.abstract: <jats:p>Environmental Social Governance (ESG) merged with Digital Transformation has become one of the hottest research areas influenced by sustainability, technology, and business requirements. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ESG correlated with digital transformation through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis. Searches were conducted on the Scopus database using keywords associated with ESG, sustainability, AI, Industry 4.0, and digital keywords. Initially, 919 publications were found; after screening and eligibility assessment, 43 studies indexed in Scopus were included for final analysis. For bibliometric analysis, a three-stage thematic protocol consisting of assembling, arranging, and assessing was followed. Bibliometric analysis was performed by using Microsoft Excel, Bibliometrix (R Studio), and VOSviewer to demonstrate publication patterns, research areas, keywords with cluster analysis, research themes over time, and country-wise contribution to research.</jats:p>

title: Human Resource Transformation in the Digital Era
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
d4ef2013f1e8922fc1e7b3571f8651af88e991ac.abstract: <jats:p>The digital transformation has profoundly transformed organizations, their HR practices, and the nature of work in today's business environment. This study explores the interplay between the following aspects of digital human resource transformation: diversity, equity, and inclusion in digital workplaces; remote work performance and productivity; digital leadership and virtual management competency; employee digital well-being and engagement; and digital upskilling and career development. The research underscores the impact of technology integration on employee experiences, organizational sustainability, and strategic workforce management. It also highlights the ethical use of digital tools, leadership practices inclusive of everyone, lifelong learning, and the well-being of employees as key drivers of sustainable organization and competitive advantage in today's digitally driven world.</jats:p>

title: Mastering Network Traffic With Deep Learning and Predictive Intelligence
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
ea07c60ff4a108f8c2a76cd458aff86715d93608.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid expansion of digital communication and cloud-based services has resulted in highly complex and dynamic network environments, challenging the effectiveness of traditional traffic analysis and management techniques. In the context of the creative economy and the evolving ESG–digital nexus, this chapter explores how deep learning and predictive intelligence can support reengineered strategic leadership in designing resilient, efficient, and secure digital infrastructures. By leveraging advanced neural network architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, the proposed approach enables accurate traffic classification, anomaly detection, and proactive traffic forecasting. Predictive intelligence empowers technology leaders to move from reactive management to forward-looking decision-making by anticipating congestion, identifying potential cyber threats, and optimizing resource utilization in real time.</jats:p>

title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
f53eda3732d4f7978e656b0379b1de25b609ae9b.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, the authors explore the shift in the nature of strategic leadership in a VUCA (Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity, and Ambiguity) economy. The leadership style of command and control is no longer effective in highly dynamic and technologic business environments. A chapter delves into digital leadership strategies focused on agility, collaboration, data fluency and adaptive governance. It also explores the theme of ethical stewardship in the era of artificial intelligence and automation, addressing the principles of responsible innovation, transparency, accountability and “AI for Good”. Furthermore, the chapter examines the use of predictive analytics, scenario planning and strategic foresight to aid organisational resilience and long-term decisions. Taking the latest research and real-life organisational examples, the chapter offers a blueprint for leaders to create agile, ethical organisations for the future in the digital age.</jats:p>

title: The ESG–Digital Nexus and the Future of Strategic Leadership in Creative Industries
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
8d45fe6887f5e07b8a58898e894e46b8b98ede25.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the intersection of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles and digital transformation in shaping the future of strategic leadership within creative industries. As organizations face increasing sustainability expectations and rapid technological change, leaders must balance innovation, ethical responsibility, and long-term value creation. The chapter explores how digital technologies support ESG objectives, enhance organizational resilience, and drive sustainable growth. It highlights emerging leadership challenges, governance considerations, and strategic opportunities, offering insights into building adaptive, responsible, and future-ready creative enterprises.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting ESG Performance With Machine Learning Regression Models
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
805d0ecd3846bd85b1099b9082798b01f3c05e93.abstract: <jats:p>Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance has become a critical indicator of sustainable value creation in the digital economy. This chapter examines how machine learning regression models, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM, can support ESG forecasting and strategic leadership decision-making. Drawing on Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capability Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Digital Leadership Theory, the chapter develops a conceptual framework linking predictive analytics capabilities, leadership effectiveness, ESG performance, organizational resilience, and sustainable value creation. It also discusses implementation challenges, model validation considerations, and future research opportunities. The chapter contributes to the ESG–Digital Nexus literature by highlighting the strategic role of AI-driven forecasting in proactive sustainability management and long-term organizational performance.</jats:p>

title: Explainable AI and ESG-Driven Decision Intelligence for Strategic Leadership in the Creative Economy
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
d8b4eafefe49e40a437d889529cb8c99644dca1c.abstract: <jats:p>As ESG principles and cutting-edge digital innovations intersect in the creative economy, strategic leadership is changing in ways never before imaginable. This chapter discusses the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in supporting ESG-driven decision intelligence by allowing a leader to make transparent, accountable, and data-informed decisions. Based on the Resource Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the chapter advances a conceptual framework that combines explainability, ESG performance measures, and strategic leadership capabilities. The conversation focuses on the benefits of explainable AI for governance, stakeholders' trust, sustainability, and organizational resilience in the creative sector. The chapter also provides future research directions in the context of responsible human-centric AI leaders in the changing digital and sustainability landscapes.</jats:p>

title: Navigating India's ESG–Digital Nexus Through AI-Driven Ethical Transformation
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
22f3457abdf2fffb7ebe5401b54c2f7bc15f8c5c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how India's creative economy might navigate the ESG–Digital Nexus via an AI-driven ethical shift, not just tech for tech's sake. It draws on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Stakeholder Theory, and basically looks at how AI-Driven Digital Capability, Big Data and IoT Integration, Ethical Digital Transformation, Strategic Leadership Agility, ESG Performance, and Sustainable Creative Economy Development connect together. The study uses survey data from 412 professionals, and it then analyses the whole thing with PLS-SEM. The outcome of the study is that AI capabilities and digital integration really do improve ESG performance, but they do it through ethical digital transformation. Strategic leadership agility tends to reinforce these effects, while ESG performance in turn supports sustainable creative economy development. Overall, the chapter stresses that technological experimentation has to be matched with ethical governance and sustainability objectives if India wants long-term competitiveness and responsible digital expansion.</jats:p>

title: Blockchain-Enabled ESG Transparency and Strategic Leadership in Creative Industries
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
b553b53616cc5e3395977513c47c690e1d98db23.abstract: <jats:p>Digital transformation, sustainability, cultural value and accountability of stakeholders are influencing the creative economy more and more. Creative industries are those that generate value based on creativity, intellectual property, symbolic content and knowledge-based assets. However, they are also subject to issues concerning the environment, social justice, equitable remuneration, recognition of creators, transparency of the supply chain and accountability of how they are governed. This chapter explores the potential of blockchain to enhance ESG transparency and the re-engineered strategic leadership in creative industries. Blockchain is a digital trust infrastructure that can improve the traceability, immutability, smart contracts and verification of stakeholders. The chapter is based on theories of dynamic capabilities, stakeholder and institutional theories and proposes a Blockchain-Enabled ESG Strategic Leadership Framework for Creative Industries.</jats:p>

title: Digital Ecosystems and ESG-Driven Leadership
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
78409cc29ce19e6bf455fc5e7f4e4f16638a2dfe.abstract: <jats:p>Digital transformation and ESG expectations are reshaping leadership in the creative economy. This chapter examines digital business ecosystems as governance structures that connect organisations, platforms, technologies and stakeholders to support responsible innovation and sustainable value creation. It argues that digital ecosystems are not merely operational tools, but integrated systems that strengthen ESG transparency, accountability, coordination and stakeholder trust. Using a multi-theoretical approach, the chapter develops a conceptual framework linking digital ecosystem maturity, ESG leadership capability and creative economy outcomes such as performance, innovation, social impact and human-centred value creation. It highlights the role of ethical AI, blockchain, data governance and inclusive ecosystem design in enabling verifiable ESG commitments. The chapter offers insights for executives, policymakers and researchers seeking to align digital strategy with sustainability.</jats:p>

title: Dynamic Capabilities Perspective on Sustainable Transformation in Knowledge-Based Industries
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
0450fcee15b075d9562afe76ae931e910af380b0.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the strategic convergence of digital transformation and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) priorities within the emerging “twin transition” paradigm. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study develops an integrated conceptual framework linking strategic leadership, digital capabilities, ESG integration capability, organizational transformation, and ESG performance outcomes. Through an analytical review of contemporary literature, the chapter explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, IoT, and big data analytics enhance sustainability governance, transparency, and organizational resilience. The findings highlight that effective ESG–digital alignment depends not only on technological adoption but also on leadership orientation, governance quality, and institutional support. The chapter contributes theoretically by extending dynamic capability perspectives into the ESG–digital domain and offers practical insights for sustainable organizational transformation.</jats:p>

title: ESG-Oriented Sustainable Campus Leadership in Higher Education
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
54b32d43cbad7920138b9b4f41defb57664effab.abstract: <jats:p>Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks are reshaping higher education by transforming sustainability from fragmented environmental initiatives into integrated system of institutional governance and strategic leadership. This chapter examines how sustainability-oriented leadership, participatory governance, systems thinking, and whole-institution approaches support the integration of ESG principles across university operations, academic strategy, and stakeholder engagement. It analyzes the growing role of digital technologies, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and smart campus systems in advancing data-driven sustainability management while simultaneously raising concerns regarding ethical governance, cybersecurity, and institutional accountability. Through theoretical discussions and case-based illustrations, the chapter argues that effective ESG integration depends on adaptive leadership, collaborative governance, and organizational resilience, positioning universities as transformative actors in advancing long-term sustainability and global development.</jats:p>

title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for Sustainable Innovation and Creative Value Creation in the ESG-Driven Digital Economy
container-title: Reengineering Strategic Leadership for the Creative Economy in the ESG-Digital Nexus
a7c02b867addefdc423bd0d9e7801a1bcd3190de.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how organizations strengthen long-term performance by integrating responsible governance with digital transformation and adaptive leadership. It develops an integrated conceptual framework connecting environmental, social, and governance principles with digital capability, human-centred innovation, and organizational resilience. A conceptual review methodology synthesises literature from strategic management, sustainability, digital governance, and innovation research. The discussion examines theoretical relationships, implementation challenges, and institutional factors influencing sustainable transformation. The proposed framework explains how governance quality, leadership capability, and digital technologies support responsible innovation and long-term value creation. The chapter concludes with practical implications for organizational leaders, policymakers, educators, and researchers while identifying future research directions.</jats:p>

title: Emotional Intelligence and Communication in Digital Leadership
container-title: Evolving Societies and Contemporary Workplace Issues
57b1d0c5263295d13b2b72a62998b736c8525ece.abstract: <jats:p>This study provides a valuable contribution to understanding the relationships between emotional intelligence (EI), communication, affective organisational commitment (AOC), strategic fit, and organisational performance (OP) within higher education institutions (HEIs) in Dubai in the post-COVID-19 era. The findings offer methodological support for the proposed conceptual framework and highlight EI, communication, affective commitment, and strategic alignment as strategic assets that enhance organisational resilience and effectiveness amid emerging challenges. As HEIs strive to recover from the pandemic's impact, the study's insights and recommendations can support universities in developing effective strategies to adapt and thrive in the new reality. Ensuring sustainability requires a focus on developing the EI of leaders and instructors, implementing meaningful communication with stakeholders, fostering affective commitment among employees, and aligning institutional strategies and resources with stakeholder needs to support education, research, and social development.</jats:p>

title: Mental Health and Resilience in Evolving Work Environments
container-title: Evolving Societies and Contemporary Workplace Issues
334e62f7c59d41a5397d7d851df80c3cecb16721.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of work environments—driven by digital transformation, remote work paradigms, economic volatility, and socio-cultural change—has foregrounded mental health and resilience as pivotal concerns in workplace research. This chapter adopts a research-oriented lens to critically explore the dynamic interplay between shifting organizational structures and the psychological well-being of employees. Anchored in empirical studies and contemporary research frameworks, the chapter investigates how resilience acts as a moderating factor in mitigating stress, enhancing adaptability, and sustaining performance amidst workplace disruption. The chapter begins by synthesizing key literature across organizational psychology, human resource development, and behavioral science to map the antecedents and consequences of mental health challenges in the modern workplace. Research evidence is presented on issues such as digital exhaustion, role overload, job insecurity, and social isolation—particularly within hybrid and decentralized work settings.</jats:p>

title: Gain and loss of acquired doxycycline resistance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum : an adaptive laboratory evolution study
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
a50f16413165cc2c0728daeb775157bb69729fbb.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Probiotics interact in a mutualistic way with humans. Exposure of probiotics to sublethal concentrations of commonly prescribed antibiotics can cause resistance to arise. Over 1,000 generations, we performed an adaptive laboratory evolution experiment to determine if the fitness of the probiotic
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Lactiplantibacillus plantarum</jats:italic>
                      is altered by exposure to doxycycline (DOX) at one-tenth of the minimal inhibitory concentration. Compared to the original culture,
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">L. plantarum</jats:italic>
                      exposed to sublethal DOX acquired modest resistance (~4-fold) over time. When the selection pressure was removed, resistance was lost rapidly in ~50 generations. This suggests that resistance, once acquired, is not fixed. The mechanism by which resistance is acquired and subsequently lost was investigated by whole genome sequencing (WGS). Analysis of the single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) identified in the WGS of the generation 1,000 DOX-treated cultures reveals 16 distinct variants across 15 genes. Two of these variants are in the
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                      gene, which encodes ribosomal protein S10, a component of the 30S ribosomal subunit, and result in non-synonymous mutations (H56Y and S94N). This gene has been previously reported to harbor mutations associated with tetracycline-class resistance, including DOX and tigecycline. WGS of archived cells from generations 350 and 750 reveals that one of these
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                      variants (H56Y) arises early in the experiment. Additional
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                      variants at position 57 (K57M and K57I) could be identified within intermediate generations. Most
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                      SNVs identified from the WGS could be verified by colony PCR and Sanger sequencing. Importantly, no
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                      variants are observed in the original culture sequences or in same-generation controls.
                    </jats:p>
                    <jats:sec>
                      <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                      <jats:p>
                        Probiotics are beneficial bacteria often found in fermented foods and beverages. When consumed, they can colonize the gut and provide several advantages. Antibiotics, even at levels too low to kill bacteria, can exert pressure that leads to antibiotic resistance. Though well studied in harmful bacteria, the effects this may have on probiotics are less well understood. Using experimental evolution, we grew a popular probiotic,
                        <jats:italic toggle="yes">Lactiplantibacillus plantarum</jats:italic>
                        , in the presence of a low concentration of doxycycline, one of the most highly prescribed antibiotics in the US. Over the course of 5 months, roughly a thousand generations, the probiotic became ~4-fold more resistant; once we removed the antibiotic and continued the experiment, this resistance disappeared rapidly. DNA sequencing identified variants in the
                        <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                        gene, which encodes a protein important for translation. As doxycycline interferes with this process, the
                        <jats:italic toggle="yes">rpsJ</jats:italic>
                        variants may underlie the emergence of the modest resistance we observe.
                      </jats:p>
