title: Polarimetric image restoration with adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization-based color correction
container-title: Applied Optics
c078e5f1f51a99201f07a5bf4da8407d0a8b63a0.abstract: <jats:p>Optical electronic devices often exhibit certain limitations when attempting to capture underwater images, such as poor contrast, color casts, and blurry details. To improve the image quality of underwater scenes, polarization-based methods are introduced to enhance the underwater image. Nevertheless, the enhancement performance of most current methods is limited by their manual backscatter region selection processes and their disregard for color and brightness restoration. In this paper, we propose an underwater polarimetric image restoration method based on adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization (AoP)-driven color correction. Specifically, we construct an adaptive standard deviation of Gaussian filter-based on the entropy of the input image to capture the complete backscatter light. Afterward, we correct the color casts based on a reference channel and two gain coefficients, fully considering the color attenuation introduced by the difference in the AoP, and simultaneously utilize the AoP map and the gray-world assumption to spatially modulate the correction process. Finally, we comprehensively consider the brightness information of HSV and normalized backscatter light estimation to design an adaptive gamma revision function, thus naturally adjusting the enhancement results. The enhancement results on the underwater polarimetric image dataset show that our method achieves a good enhancement ability with high contrast, reasonable appearance, and natural brightness. Moreover, the extensive histogram distribution and image segmentation experiments demonstrate that our enhancement results have almost the same histogram distribution for the r, g, and b channels and can yield more accurate segmentation effects.</jats:p>

title:
Three-dimensional particle velocimetry in digital in-line holography
				via a channel-attention autofocusing network
container-title: Applied Optics
f645074bdb03734330a8cf37f576379abaf3187a.abstract:
<jats:p>Three-dimensional particle velocimetry using digital in-line holography
					is limited by axial localization errors. This paper proposes a method
					based on a channel-attention autofocusing network (CAF-NET), which
					predicts particle axial distances end-to-end via a channel attention
					mechanism and reconstructs three-dimensional velocity fields combined
					with a two-frame matching algorithm. On a public dataset, CAF-NET
					reduces the average axial localization error by 40.4% compared to
					FocusNET and improves PSNR and SSIM by 16.7% and 6.7%, respectively.
					In simulated velocimetry, the average absolute velocity error is
					reduced by 40.9% relative to FocusNET. Experiments yield a maximum
					relative error of 6.7% for the measured average velocities. The method
					effectively mitigates the impact of axial localization errors on
					velocimetry, offering a high-precision solution for holographic
					three-dimensional flow field measurement.</jats:p>

title: Surface contouring of reflective and diffuse samples using dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry
container-title: Applied Optics
f7e95171c668b2140ffa8cdb75473a935df5f18f.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, a grating-based dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry system is presented for generating synthetic wavelengths and extending the measurable height range. A geometric-phase (GP) grating and mirror configuration generates laterally sheared wavefronts at multiple shear orientations, while a polarization camera enables simultaneous phase-shifted intensity acquisition. Measurements are performed at two illumination angles, and the reconstructed complex wavefields are combined to obtain a synthetic phase distribution whose sensitivity is determined by the angular separation between the two measurements. The system was experimentally evaluated using standard step-height artifacts and surface features on both reflective and diffuse samples. Step-height measurements demonstrated the dependence of measurement performance on the selected synthetic wavelength. An analytical uncertainty analysis identified the illumination angle as a significant contributor to the overall measurement uncertainty, emphasizing the importance of system calibration using a standard artifact. Temporal repeatability was also evaluated through repeated measurements. The results demonstrate the capability of grating-based dual-angle digital holographic shear interferometry for quantitative three-dimensional surface reconstruction while maintaining a compact common-path configuration.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
Electrifying Tourism
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
ade9a7b0c000e4daa35c59a0be1889d6014f749f.abstract: <jats:p>Electric transport represents an important approach towards achieving sustainability within the tourism sector and providing tourists with better transport means and more enjoyable journeys. In this regard, the present chapter focuses on how electric cars, buses, bicycles, scooters, and ferries may be used in tourism. Through the study of recent literature as well as country-specific examples from Norway, Iceland, China, Greece, France, Canada, and Italy, this chapter analyzes the various environmental, economic, and experience-based advantages of electric mobility within the tourism sector. Moreover, issues related to the uptake of electric transport by the tourism industry, including problems of charging infrastructure, policies, investments, and consumer behavior, are discussed. Theoretical perspectives such as the Theory of Planned Behavior and Technology Acceptance Model are analyzed as well to determine travelers' behavior regarding electric transport.</jats:p>

title: Role of Electric Transportation in Enhancing Tourist Experience
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
e7c644ea139820441fefbea966dcf9e0a5547129.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of electric transportation and tourism is transforming sustainable mobility and visitor experiences. This chapter examines how electric buses, e-bikes, e-scooters, electric ferries, and autonomous shuttles enhance tourism through sustainability, smart technology integration, and universal accessibility. Drawing on recent peer-reviewed literature, policy documents, and international case studies, it demonstrates that integrated electric mobility ecosystems supported by renewable energy, digital infrastructure, and inclusive design improve visitor satisfaction, environmental quality, and destination competitiveness. The chapter also discusses challenges such as range anxiety, charging infrastructure, and accessibility barriers, and concludes with policy recommendations and future research directions aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the UNWTO 2030 Tourism Agenda.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Mobility and Electric Ride Hailing in Tourism Management
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
43a119d8d43a3474c23e969ab8d6529e489a5c2f.abstract: <jats:p>Transportation is the largest contributor to tourism-related carbon emissions, creating challenges for sustainable tourism development. This chapter examines the role of electric ride-hailing systems within the broader framework of sustainable mobility and low-carbon tourism. It discusses the concept of sustainable mobility, the environmental impacts of tourism transportation, and the emergence of electric ride-hailing as an innovative mobility solution. Drawing on international case studies, the chapter highlights key opportunities, challenges, and policy considerations associated with adoption. The findings suggest that electric ride-hailing can support emission reduction, improve accessibility, and enhance transportation efficiency when supported by appropriate infrastructure, governance, and stakeholder collaboration, thereby contributing to more sustainable tourism systems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Transformation in Smart Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
bdb23f442d428cea7c60fce9bd787c0e0f234367.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urbanization has intensified congestion, pollution, and inefficiencies in transportation systems, necessitating sustainable and intelligent mobility solutions. Smart mobility has emerged as a transformative approach driven by digital transformation and advanced technologies. This chapter examines the role of the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Big Data Analytics, and Cloud Computing in enhancing operational efficiency, real-time decision-making, and service integration. It conceptualizes smart mobility through Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS), enabling seamless coordination among stakeholders. Drawing on global and Indian examples, the chapter highlights the impact of digital platforms and electric mobility. It also addresses challenges such as infrastructure limitations, regulatory complexity, data privacy, and the digital divide. Finally, it proposes a framework for sustainable, efficient, and user-centric smart mobility systems.</jats:p>

title: Green Transportation Strategies for Hotels and Tourism Destinations
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
97dd0471f02229140159ce6d04a733a4560a867c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on green transportation strategies as a key component of sustainable tourism, which is essential in the path towards achieving net-zero, climate-resilient tourism. This chapter adopts a critical narrative review method that integrates a multidisciplinary review of the literature on smart urban mobility, environmental psychology, and tourism management. The results show that smart transportation solutions, like predictive navigation and electric mobility, have a significant impact on reducing traffic jams and carbon emissions. Stakeholders receive actionable frameworks based on the Avoid-Shift-Improve concept to easily integrate green transport, sharing and dynamic pricing into the hotel business and regional planning. Finally, this chapter provides an overview of tourist psychology and hospitality management to build resilient tourism systems from the bottom up (micro) to the top (macro) of the destination.</jats:p>

title: Design of AI-Based Perception Systems for Real-Time ADAS
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
d91ce310e605baffdae89107a02d0159ddd145de.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based embedded perception for real-time Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) for trustworthy electric ride-hailing services. It reviews recent perception approaches for road-scene understanding, including lightweight convolutional models, You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detectors, compact vision transformers, low-light perception, radar-aware methods, and multimodal fusion. Particular attention is given to safety-critical road elements such as pedestrians, vehicles, cyclists, obstacles, traffic signs, and traffic lights, because they directly influence driver awareness, decision-making, and perceived safety. The chapter proposes a methodological framework covering dataset selection, ADAS task definition, data preparation, model selection, AI optimization methods, embedded deployment, and evaluation. By linking perception reliability with perceived safety, user trust, and behavioral intention, the chapter positions embedded ADAS perception as a key contributor to the adoption of electric ride-hailing services.</jats:p>

title: Electric Ride-Hailing and Sustainable Mobility in Tourism
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
638e76b7eccb79512c031f2f30de6c75244c33e7.abstract: <jats:p>This book chapter examines electric ride-hailing as a strategic solution for sustainable mobility in tourism destinations. It explores how electric vehicle fleets, digital ride-hailing platforms, charging infrastructure, business models, and destination governance can jointly support low-carbon, smart, and visitor-friendly tourism mobility. The chapter highlights that tourism destinations face growing challenges such as congestion, pollution, weak last-mile connectivity, seasonal demand, and pressure on destination sustainability. It argues that electric ride-hailing can improve airport transfers, hotel connectivity, attraction access, safety, payment convenience, tourist experience, and destination competitiveness. The chapter also discusses fleet-owned, aggregator, hotel partnership, MaaS, subscription, and public–private business models for scalable tourism mobility.</jats:p>

title: Socio-Economic Impacts of Electric Ride-Hailing Services
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
2de488357061569d8c6156451c654e89d1671d73.abstract: <jats:p>Electric ride-sharing is a paradigm-shifting mode of urban transportation that combines the benefits of digital platforms (i.e., scalability, efficiency) with clean transportation technologies (i.e., electric). As we have seen, ride-sharing can produce large amounts of greenhouse gases, estimated to be about 69% greater than the trips they replace, but the electric vehicle represents a key solution to reducing emissions associated with urban transportation. In this Chapter, we will explore the various socio-economic implications of electric ride-sharing, and particularly how these new modes of transportation are reshaping economic systems, social relationships, and environments. From an economic perspective, electric ride-sharing has generated growth in markets, increased efficiencies in costs, and created jobs, yet at the same time challenged traditional taxi and transport sectors. From a social standpoint, electric ride-sharing has enhanced access to affordable and inclusive mobility options; influenced consumer behaviors relative to travel; and shaped tourist trends.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Campus Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
97361003db90435a242e827f01d09cd7561bb035.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of electric bicycle-sharing systems in promoting sustainable campus mobility within higher education environments. The purpose of this chapter is to analyze the challenges, opportunities, and strategic implications of implementing electric bicycle-sharing systems through perspectives of user acceptance, behavioral intention, smart mobility, and sustainability-oriented governance. The discussion highlights urban mobility issues, infrastructural and institutional barriers, environmental and ethical concerns, and the integration of digital technologies in smart campus ecosystems. Furthermore, this chapter explores solutions related to user engagement, inclusive mobility innovation, infrastructure development, and policy frameworks supporting sustainable transportation. Future research directions concerning digital transformation, smart mobility ecosystems, and data-driven transportation management are also discussed to support long-term sustainable mobility transitions in higher education institutions.</jats:p>

title: Sacred Pilgrims Meet Smart Mobility
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
2c08c58b31077e9ced33672f5cc506c606de8c6e.abstract: <jats:p>Religious tourism is one of the major forms of tourism, where almost 330 million pilgrimages are made every year. As Electric Ride-Hailing Services (ERHS) gain popularity, the mobility trends of pilgrimage areas are changing, providing sustainable and effective ways of mobility. This chapter explores the theoretical linkages of the religious tourism and e-ride sharing adoption in Ayodhya-Mathura-Varanasi pilgrimage circuit using secondary sources of data. The study emphasizes the positive and negative effects of ERHS, such as lower emissions, better transportation options, equity aspects, carrying capacity, but also issues of cultural appropriation. Past studies suggest that there are significant demographic differences in technology adoption, with younger and more educated people having greater acceptance than older and less educated.</jats:p>

title: Impact of Electric Ride-Hailing on Heritage Tourism Experience
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
f979b437ccc4180f6b285f099a083a3aa2570c48.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the impact of electric ride-hailing on tourist experience, perceived authenticity, and tourist satisfaction in heritage tourism destinations. Using a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of 54 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025, this chapter explores the relationship between sustainable mobility and visitor experiences. The findings show that electric ride-hailing improves accessibility, convenience, flexibility, and environmental sustainability while influencing how tourists engage with heritage environments. Mobility is identified as an experiential component of tourism rather than merely a transport service. The review further highlights that authenticity and satisfaction are shaped by both service quality and meaningful cultural engagement. This chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking mobility, tourist experience, perceived authenticity, and satisfaction, and provides implications for sustainable destination management and heritage preservation.</jats:p>

title: Understanding the Electric-Taxi Travel Experience Through Identity, Autonomy, and Anxiety
container-title: Transforming Tourism Through Electric Mobility
b41e83d8bb453710cd9b87555c0ca5a4f01b3ba2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how sustainable travel identity, perceived autonomy, and electric vehicle usage anxiety shape travellers' hedonic experience of electric taxis. Drawing on experiential consumption, self-determination, environmental self-identity, and perceived-risk perspectives, it develops an experiential mobility framework for platform-mediated travel. Survey data were collected online from prospective electric-taxi users in Delhi, India. After screening 250 responses, 227 cases were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings identify perceived autonomy as the principal predictor of hedonic travel experience. Sustainable travel identity did not significantly influence autonomy or enjoyment, and its indirect effect through autonomy was unsupported. EV usage anxiety was positively associated with autonomy but did not directly affect hedonic experience, indicating that anxiety may encourage information seeking and preparedness rather than restrict perceived control.</jats:p>

title: From Common Asset Demand to Intermediary Choice: A Focused Reanalysis of Attention Complementarity across U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs
container-title: The Journal of FinTech
1ecd734f11db66af0507144de857e9a9ea778797.abstract: <jats:p>The launch of U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds created an unusual allocation problem: 10 intermediaries offered nearly the same underlying exposure, yet their flows diverged sharply. This paper is a focused reanalysis of the fund-flow and Reddit panel introduced by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]. It does not present the dataset, text measures, BrandScore or the baseline sentiment-by-visibility association as new. Instead, it asks what the established association reveals about the division between category demand and intermediary choice. The contribution consists of three interpretive emphases applied to estimates already reported by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]: within-date differences across funds as evidence about allocation, asymmetry across the conditional flow distribution and variation across market states. The pairwise flow-sensitivity formulation makes the allocation interpretation explicit. In the previously reported two-way fixed-effects model, common daily shocks are absorbed and the sentiment-by-visibility coefficient is identified from differences in issuer visibility among funds facing the same Bitcoin news. The coefficient is positive, the direct visibility effect changes sign between large-redemption and large-creation states and the interaction appears less consistently during stressed markets. The Driscoll–Kraay and issuer-bootstrap checks apply to the baseline coefficient (2.930), not the two-way fixed-effects coefficient (3.802), for which those checks were not conducted. The evidence is thus an associative allocation regularity, not a causal social-media effect: differences in issuer visibility are consistent with different flows across financial wrappers conditional on common category sentiment.</jats:p>

title: MULTIMODAL SPATIOTEMPORAL BIOMECHANICAL MODELING FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL INJURY RISK SCREENING OF BODY MOVEMENTS BASED ON CROSS-MODAL ATTENTION NETWORK
container-title: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology
f75d4115ac94c6b86ec43f361db77e566c5bf6af.abstract: <jats:p>Ethnic dance involves large-amplitude and repetitive movements that may impose substantial and uneven mechanical demands on the musculoskeletal system, potentially increasing the risk of joint and soft-tissue injuries. Conventional injury assessment relies largely on manual observation and clinical evaluation, which limits the ability to continuously and quantitatively characterize movement-related risk. To address this limitation, this study proposed a Cross-Modal Attention-based Injury Risk Perception Network (CMA-IRPN) for noncontact movement analysis, movement-pattern risk screening, and injury risk assessment in ethnic dance. The framework jointly modeled Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) video sequences and human skeletal keypoints. A dual-branch encoder combining a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) and a graph convolutional network (GCN) was used to extract spatiotemporal visual and skeletal features, while spatiotemporal cross-modal attention modules were introduced to model interactions between movement appearance and joint-topological information. The model was evaluated for movement recognition using the publicly available MPII Human Pose and SportsPose datasets and for movement-pattern risk grading using a self-constructed ethnic dance dataset. CMA-IRPN achieved accuracies of 96.03% and 94.86% on the MPII and SportsPose datasets, respectively, with statistically significant improvements over the comparison models ([Formula: see text]). On the ethnic dance dataset, the model achieved a Macro-F1 score of 92.25% for movement-pattern risk grading and a sensitivity of 93.75% for the high-risk category. These results suggest that CMA-IRPN can identify risk-related movement patterns from noncontact multimodal data and provide quantitative support for movement screening and injury risk assessment in ethnic dance training. The predicted risk levels represent visual–kinematic movement patterns rather than direct measurements of joint torque, tissue stress, or other mechanical loads and therefore should not be interpreted as operational real-time injury early warnings or as substitutes for clinical biomechanical assessment or medical diagnosis.</jats:p>

title: #GirlDad: Exploring the representations of Black fatherhood in digital spaces
container-title: Communication, Culture & Critique
fd53ba85d1fdcc5643e0fdfcc57cf87fdd6c2489.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article explores representations and identity politics surrounding Black fatherhood on Twitter (now known as “X”) through the #GirlDad hashtag. First, we interrogate Black heteronormative practices of masculinity to situate the historical and contemporary framing of Black fatherhood in media representations. Next, we examine how Black men utilize Twitter, situating #GirlDad within collective mourning during media disasters. Using thematic analysis, we analyzed a purposeful sample of #GirlDad tweets from Black fathers to reveal patterns in their articulations of fathering daughters. This paper argues that #GirlDad operates as a political form of digital escorting and resistance, whereby Black fathers publicly display involvement and resist absentee narratives. These counternarratives challenge stereotypical representations of Black fatherhood by imagining new definitions and promoting communal relationship building among Black fathers.</jats:p>

title: Derechos digitales y educación en Suramérica: privacidad, protección de datos y acceso educativo
Digital rights and education in South America: privacy, data protection and access to education
container-title: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales
51db361c59c8bb83382256f745c25ba84087494b.abstract: <jats:p>La educación mediada por plataformas digitales amplió las posibilidades de acceso, pero también expuso a estudiantes y docentes a la recolección de datos personales y a brechas de conectividad. El artículo analizó la relación entre el derecho a la educación y los derechos digitales, en particular la privacidad y la protección de datos, en Suramérica. Se realizó una revisión documental de normas constitucionales y legales de Ecuador, Brasil y la Unión Europea, instrumentos internacionales y literatura arbitrada, con análisis en tres ejes. Se identificó que el acceso a la educación depende hoy de infraestructura y de competencias digitales, que la protección de datos de menores exige reglas específicas y que ambos derechos se refuerzan o se debilitan según el diseño de las plataformas. Se concluye que las políticas educativas digitales deben incorporar la protección de datos desde su diseño. No se recogieron datos primarios.</jats:p>

title: AI and the Digital Divide in Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
6f35cbc8c37837db42e9888922aa3f76c437d688.abstract: <jats:p>The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) into the educational field promises a revolution of greater individualization, automation, and access however, unequal access poses a risk of amplifying already extant socio-economic and gender, as well as geographic, digital inequality, favouring some and disadvantaging others. In the chapter, the researcher conducts a meta-analysis of policy frameworks in various nations and regions globally to explore how structural obstacles, including poor infrastructure, teacher ill-equipment, and forms of governance vacuums, could limit the equitable use of AI, further fuelling algorithmic bias, exclusion and ethical hazard. It offers a threefold equity-based argument connecting computer infrastructure, educator maturity improving, and answerable information mechanisms, intended to carry out decentralized, responsible, and sustainable AI practices.</jats:p>

title: Ethical AI and Financial Inclusion
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
b0a013beb14c35675ffb52135d960aea3b6a70e3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of ethical artificial intelligence in advancing inclusive financial education for persons with disabilities within contemporary digital financial systems. It aims to analyse how AI-driven technologies can enhance access to financial knowledge, improve decision making, and support participation in formal financial services. The chapter also explores the risks associated with algorithmic bias, data inequality, and limited representation, which may reproduce existing patterns of exclusion. It further discusses the importance of inclusive design, accessibility, and ethical governance in the development and deployment of AI systems. The chapter argues that financial literacy, when supported by responsible and context-sensitive AI, can contribute to economic empowerment and social inclusion. It concludes by outlining institutional and policy strategies required to ensure equitable and sustainable financial participation.</jats:p>

title: Visual-Auditory Assistive Systems for People With Visual Impairment
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Advancing Disability Inclusion Through AI
0f243d3bed6fd13cf514ca1c736e49a820b62b59.abstract: <jats:p>Visual impairment makes the same state of visual information that is available to others inaccessible for people with vision impairment, creating a major difficulty to their independence. In this paper, an integrated deep Learning system is evaluated to assist persons with vision impairment in automatically understanding scenes. The system generates descriptive image captions and sends them to the speakers. VGG-16 is used as a feature extractor, but LSTM networks and attention mechanisms are often used in the encoder-decoder pipeline. Combined models translate visual information effectively into auditory feedback. However, some difficulties still remain. The system must work in real time, maintain high accuracy in various practical scenes, and meet users' daily needs for testing. To advance from research into practical assistive technology, future work should focus on adding modern architectures, such as Visual Transformers; exploring multimodal learning; bringing accessibility even closer with edge devices; and setting up rigorous, human-centered benchmarks for evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Empathetic Digital Leadership
container-title: Governance for Sustainability, Resilience, and Innovation
6e36dbcf27fd9077eea7376620ff324efa90bc72.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how compassionate leadership might enhance resilience in public administration and strengthen digital governance. This chapter aims to investigate how emotional intelligence enhances the legitimacy of governance, builds institutional trust, and supports leadership effectiveness in digitally evolving public sectors. The conversation focuses on important issues in governance transition, such as organizational resistance, legitimacy threats, and gaps in leadership competencies. Additionally, the chapter offers public sector organizations implementation tools and a framework for empathic leadership. To promote theoretical advancement and innovative governance, future research avenues are suggested. This chapter advances knowledge of human-centered leadership strategies that facilitate sustainable public management and adaptive governance in quickly changing digital contexts.</jats:p>

title: Design and Development of An Iot-Based Digital Scale for Measuring Cement Weight Using A Load Cell Sensor at Pt Semen Tonasa, Balikpapan Branch
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Networking and Internet of Things
38c49952e7a774648a167b0d3ce377206cc224a4.abstract: <jats:p>Manual cement weighing in the industrial environment of PT Semen Tonasa, Balikpapan Branch, is considered inefficient and prone to human error. This study aims to develop a prototype Internet of Things-based digital conveyor weighing system capable of automatically measuring, sorting, and monitoring the weight of cement packages. The system is controlled by an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with a load cell sensor and an HX711 amplifier module to read the dynamic weight of packages moving on the conveyor. The conveyor belt is driven by a DC motor with a BTS7960-series driver, while a servo motor serves as the sorting arm actuator. The system is programmed to recognize a target cement weight of 500 grams with a tolerance of 10 grams. Remote monitoring is performed through a local web server dashboard with a client–server architecture that displays indicators and weighing history charts without excessively burdening the microcontroller memory. Test results show that the system successfully identifies peak loads dynamically, allows on-target packages to proceed, and automatically removes nonconforming packages. The device demonstrates very high accuracy, with an average reading error of only 0.63%. The system exhibits substantially better precision and operational consistency than conventional weighing methods</jats:p>

title: Digital Forensic Analysis of a Case of Pornographic Content Dissemination on WhatsApp Using the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Method
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Networking and Internet of Things
24ae9ffc0d6f3eb270924486470e872df2264723.abstract: <jats:p>The dissemination of pornographic content through instant messaging applications such as WhatsApp is becoming increasingly widespread. A major obstacle to establishing legal proof in these cases is that perpetrators frequently use the "Delete for Everyone" feature to eliminate digital evidence. This study aims to apply the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) method to obtain digital artifacts from messages deleted on the perpetrator's device. A simulated scenario was conducted between the victim's device (Xiaomi Redmi 10C) and the perpetrator's device (a rooted Xiaomi Redmi S2). The investigation used MOBILedit Forensic Express for physical acquisition and Belkasoft Evidence Center for data analysis. The results show that the NIST framework successfully overcame anti-forensic obstacles. The recovered digital evidence included metadata from 3 deleted text messages with logical deletion status, 3 image files containing pornographic content (.tmp/.jpeg), and 2 video files (.mp4). Cross-validation between fragments from the perpetrator's msgstore.db database and the victim's screenshots demonstrates that this method can produce legally valid and compelling electronic evidence for court proceedings.</jats:p>

title: Strategic AI Integration in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Harnessing AI for Education Reforms
da3558bb98cb0ef90363674494624fdfcfde03c2.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of artificial intelligence in higher education is occurring at a rapid pace and institutions are still playing catch-up with piecemeal strategies. This chapter presents a governance model that integrates artificial intelligence into curricula, teaching practices, ethical considerations and student learning outcomes. The work is informed by recent research on adaptive learning systems, algorithmic accountability, and outcome-based education (OBE). The model places emphasis on four key elements: curriculum design, faculty training, student data management and institutional governance, outlining roles and decision-making processes. The argument is clear. The incorporation of AI is not a technical issue The framework presented here is grounded in current literature from 2020 to 2024 and incorporates evidence from global pilot programmes in the US, United Kingdom, Australia and India. The chapter concludes that sustainable AI integration depends not on the sophistication of the tools deployed but on the quality of the human decisions made around them.</jats:p>

title: Jones matrix extraction using single-shot common-path digital holographic measurement
container-title: Optics Letters
f560691a84d1a2e5aafbd10da30a414a17dc76e3.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, we propose a compact, polarization-sensitive, single-shot, common-path digital holographic microscopy (PSC-DHM) system for extracting the Jones matrix of anisotropic specimens. The proposed approach employs Fourier multiplexing to simultaneously record multiple polarization-dependent interference terms within a single hologram, thereby capturing complete polarization information in a single camera exposure. The multiplexed hologram is processed to reconstruct the optical fields, and subsequently the Jones matrix elements are evaluated. Experimental results obtained from birefringent samples validate the capability of the proposed system to accurately retrieve phase and polarization properties. The proposed technique offers a simple, stable, and efficient solution for quantitative polarization imaging and Jones matrix characterization in digital holography.</jats:p>

title: Cybersecurity Awareness and Digital Literacy for Students and Educators Strengthening Data Privacy with AI-Powered Cybersecurity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
30cafb06bf9daabec321a6848bf1479377de9a8e.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to investigate the significance of cybersecurity awareness, digital literacy, and artificial intelligence in fostering data privacy protection for students and teachers in North India. The study was an exploratory descriptive study with a cross-sectional quantitative design, based on primary data gathered from a structured questionnaire with 620 respondents. The methods used were descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression. The correlation was positive for all of the variables, and the highest was between the AI-driven cybersecurity and data privacy protection (r = .741, p < .001). The results of the regression showed that artificial intelligence cybersecurity, digital literacy and cyber security awareness had significant predicting power for data privacy protection, accounting for 66.3% of its variance. The results highlight the need for a holistic approach to integrating AI into education, fostering digital literacy, and raising cybersecurity awareness to ensure safer and privacy-conscious learning spaces.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Financial Phishing and the Digital Literacy Deficit Protecting Student and Young Learner Data
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
65ab6f5f760fd3d653bfc26c66ada7b9512e9487.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence has structurally transformed financial phishing, collapsing the cost of personalised attacks; India recorded 135,173 financial phishing attacks in H1 2024, a 175% rise over 2023. This chapter examines the convergence of AI-enabled phishing, student data vulnerability, and digital literacy deficits in India's skill-based educational institutions (ITIs, polytechnics, skill universities), a population absent from existing cybersecurity literature despite holding data regulated under the DPDP Act, 2023. Drawing on Routine Activity Theory, Protection Motivation Theory, the Digital Literacy Continuum, and Institutional Theory, it develops the Protection Gap construct and a Four-Layer Institutional Defence Model. A primary survey (N = 96, seven states) finds 66.7% encountered suspected phishing, mostly via WhatsApp; only 25.0% identified a genuine message; 59.4% were unaware of the DPDP Act; and 43.8% reported no explicit consent for Aadhaar/bank data. The chapter closes with recommendations for MeitY, AICTE, NSDC, and the Data Protection Board of India.</jats:p>

title: AI-Generated Deepfakes and Trust in Digital Communication in Namibia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Securing Data Privacy in Education With AI-Powered Cybersecurity
9ae33c567c1e3c1be30b3c19886f0820b1ea2ad9.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the development of deepfake technology, enabling the creation of highly realistic fabricated audio, video, and visual content that closely resembles authentic media. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining an online survey of 47 Namibian internet users and a total of 12 key informants were interviewed. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were subjected to thematic analysis. The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on deepfake technologies by providing empirical evidence from Namibia and offering practical recommendations for enhancing digital literacy, strengthening regulatory frameworks, and improving institutional preparedness.</jats:p>

title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network
container-title: Applied Optics
8265acd6d2b87f6713dd6ef322c348c2ccd4b056.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Phase aberration compensation based on iteratively reweighted Zernike polynomial fitting for digital holographic microscopy
container-title: Applied Optics
717cdbec8bc18ada1558dfd35fa00220c37d18df.abstract: <jats:p>Phase aberration compensation is essential for quantitative imaging in digital holographic microscopy (DHM), as undesired background distortions severely degrade phase measurement reliability. Conventional Zernike polynomial fitting (ZPF) either relies on manually or automatically selected background regions, which restricts its applicability to samples with sparse or ambiguous background, or performs a global least-squares (LS) fit over all pixels, in which sample structures and outliers bias the estimated aberration. This work proposes a global iteratively reweighted ZPF (GIR-ZPF) method to overcome these issues. The proposed method performs global fitting using all valid pixels across the full field and introduces a Tukey-based iterative reweighting strategy to suppress structural and outlier interference, thereby eliminating the requirement for background selection. Simulation results show that, compared with the naive global ZPF (G-ZPF), GIR-ZPF reduces the RMSE and MAE of phase reconstruction by ∼13.3%, increases the PSNR from 24.8 to 26.0 dB, and improves the Zernike-coefficient estimation accuracy by nearly two orders of magnitude, while reaching an accuracy comparable to mask-based ZPF methods without requiring any mask prior. Experiments on microspheres and live A549 cells demonstrate that GIR-ZPF achieves flat phase backgrounds, clear sample contours, and well-preserved microstructural features. GIR-ZPF provides an effective and robust solution for phase aberration compensation of samples with sparse or ambiguous backgrounds in DHM.</jats:p>

title: PMDA-Net: a polarization-conditioned multi-scale dynamic attention network for polarimetric hyperspectral camouflage target classification
container-title: Applied Optics
e3741308864e6d0ff381ac36b7b4229b1f39913f.abstract: <jats:p>To effectively fuse heterogeneous polarimetric hyperspectral data and improve the classification performance of camouflage targets in complex backgrounds, this paper proposes a polarization-conditioned multi-scale dynamic attention network (PMDA-Net). PMDA-Net adopts a dual-stream framework for modality-specific feature extraction, where spectral and polarimetric information are separately modeled. A multi-scale dynamic AoLP attention module is designed to transform geometric information encoded in the angle of linear polarization into dynamic weights. A polarization-conditioned spatial-channel attention module is designed to adaptively calibrate spectral features using polarimetric information, facilitating cross-modal interaction and complementary feature fusion. Experimental results on three self-collected datasets and one public dataset show that PMDA-Net outperforms mainstream hyperspectral deep learning models, traditional polarization-feature-based methods, and recent multimodal fusion methods on all four datasets. Compared with the model using only hyperspectral information, PMDA-Net improves the average accuracy by 5.87, 5.38, 25.71, and 5.01 percentage points on the four datasets, respectively. These results indicate that polarization information can effectively complement spectral representations and help suppress aliasing responses caused by spectral similarity in complex scenes. This work provides a promising approach for polarimetric hyperspectral image classification and camouflage target recognition.</jats:p>

title: An acoustic-vibration adaptive deformable quadratic fusion network for rolling bearing fault diagnosis under strong noise conditions
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
eb59fbea1d8edd3169f5cd804495f92c2153b880.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In practical applications, various factors such as strong background noise, complex transmission paths, variable and fluctuating operating conditions, and limited information representation capabilities of single sensors often lead to the early subtle fault impacts of rolling bearings being overwhelmed, insufficient feature extraction in diagnostic models, and inadequate noise resistance and robustness. To address the aforementioned issues, an acoustic-vibration adaptive deformation quadratic fusion network (ADQFN) for strong noise scenarios is proposed. Firstly, an adaptive deformable quadratic convolution module is proposed, which combines high-order nonlinear quadratic mapping with a dynamic geometric sampling mechanism. This enables the convolution kernel to adaptively adjust the sampling positions according to the local morphology of the signal, thereby enhancing the dynamic capture capability for non-stationary weak fault impacts. Secondly, a mechanism for consistency verification and evidence-guided feature reconstruction between sound and vibration is designed. By utilizing bidirectional couple softmax, a mutual verification and matching relationship between sound and vibration, as well as vibration and sound, is established. Only reliable semantic information that commonly points to the same fault source in both modalities is selected, thereby suppressing noise propagation in a single modality and enhancing the quality of cross-modality fusion. Experimental analysis indicates that ADQFN exhibits high diagnostic accuracy and stability across various load conditions and multiple signal-to-noise ratio scenarios, achieving an average diagnostic accuracy rate of 99.68%, surpassing mainstream methods such as CDCN, QCNN, and GCFAN. Ablation studies and interpretability analysis further validate the effectiveness of the proposed module in weak impact extraction, reliable acoustic-vibration fusion, and noise suppression.</jats:p>

title: A fast and reliable quality assurance framework for CBCT-based synthetic CTs for adaptive proton radiotherapy
container-title: Physics in Medicine & Biology
2dbe6f218102320781e90f53c4c461c6fbf6ad69.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Objective.</jats:italic>
                    Cone-beam CT based synthetic CTs (sCTs) enable online adaptive proton therapy (PT) by preserving daily patient anatomy without additional acquisition of diagnostic-quality CTs. However, clinical adoption is limited by the lack of fast, reliable quality-assurance (QA) methods. This study proposes and evaluates a practical QA workflow to assess sCT suitability for proton dose optimization.
                    <jats:italic>Approach.</jats:italic>
                    A two-step sCT-QA workflow was developed in which a candidate sCT intended for reoptimization reference sCT (sCTref) is compared with an independently generated secondary sCT (sCTtest). The workflow combines image-based metrics and dose-based metrics, with doses derived from recalculating a template proton plan on both sCTs. In this study, the framework was evaluated using a deformably propagated virtual CT (vCT) as sCTref and either a deep learning-based sCT (sCTDL) or an analytically corrected CBCT (CBCTcorr) as sCTtest. Same-day CTs were deformably registered to the CBCT and used as ground truth (CT
                    <jats:sub>GT</jats:sub>
                    ) for evaluation. Thresholds were optimized using 5-fold cross-validation on 182 head-and-neck (H&N) CT-CBCT pairs. Dose calculation suitability was defined as a gamma pass rate (2%, 1 mm) exceeding 95% between dose distributions computed on sCT and CT
                    <jats:sub>GT</jats:sub>
                    . The method was further tested on an external H&N dataset and on abdominal cases.
                    <jats:italic>Main results.</jats:italic>
                    Optimal classification performance was achieved using a combination of image mean absolute error (MAE) and dose MAE. On the H&N test set, the workflow achieved balanced accuracies of 91.2% and 89.7% for the vCT-CBCTcorr and vCT-sCTDL comparisons, respectively, while maintaining a low false positive rate. When applied without modifications to the external H&N and abdominal datasets, balanced accuracy was 94.7% (HN) and 85.0% (abdominal) for vCT-CBCTcorr, and 37.9% (HN) and 61.1% (abdominal) for vCT-sCTDL.
                    <jats:italic>Significance.</jats:italic>
                    This study introduces a clinically feasible sCT-QA workflow for CBCT-based adaptive PT and showed promising transferability across datasets.
                  </jats:p>

title: Single-image phase retrieval method  based on fusion coding of fringe and digital speckle patterns
container-title: Applied Optics
4774675cd2bdb18b0fed7d09bc5a5d3878b9d1ec.abstract: <jats:p>To address the challenge of balancing speed and accuracy in structured light-based 3D reconstruction, this paper proposes a single-image phase retrieval method based on the fused coding of fringe patterns and digital speckle. By employing the GD-DCUNet model—integrated with multi-branch dilated convolution for feature extraction, a residual fusion mechanism, and an information integration and distribution strategy—the method achieves the effective separation of fringe pattern and digital speckle information from the fused coded image. With the assistance of a newly constructed CSAS-UNet, the separated fringe pattern image is used to predict the numerator and denominator terms of the wrapped phase. Concurrently, the separated digital speckle image is utilized to predict the fringe order via correlation calculation with a reference speckle image. Under a multi-constraint strategy involving epipolar lines, wrapped phases, and connected domains, this correlation calculation significantly narrows the search range of candidate points matching the sampling points, thereby providing robust and rapid fringe order prediction. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-precision phase retrieval using only a single image. It maintains exceptional stability and reconstruction quality even on complex surfaces and low-texture regions, indicating promising potential for engineering applications.</jats:p>

title: Digital product imports and firm productivity: do winner-takes-all dynamics arise?
container-title: Oxford Economic Papers
6ca6427dac04dbd8fe9751b5ad6ce7f8c8f44860.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article examines how imports of digital products affect the productivity of Chinese manufacturing firms. Digital products, including advanced machinery, electronic equipment, and software-related technologies, may enable firms to upgrade production processes and adopt new technologies. Using three instruments and two exogenous shocks, we find that digital imports significantly enhance firm productivity, with effects substantially larger than those of traditional product imports. Digital intermediate goods raise productivity primarily through innovation and technological spillovers, while the evidence suggests that competitive pressures are an important channel for digital capital goods. Both channels help capable follower firms catch up with frontier firms and expand their market shares. Overall, the findings suggest that digital imports promote selective productivity catch-up rather than the winner-takes-all outcomes often emphasized in the literature on high-income countries.</jats:p>

title: Playology
516b87233a939c6cf8ec30574d0b1518aad42230.abstract:
<jats:p>Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village offers a sharp, timely exploration of how digital technologies and global media reshape the ways we think, communicate, and understand ourselves. As multinational corporations like Google increasingly mediate our access to information, identity, and civic life, this book examines the profound consequences of living in what it calls the “Googleburg Galaxy.”</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Blending cultural critique with accessible theory, the book traces how our practices of reading, writing, and meaning making have been transformed by digital systems that both empower and constrain. It argues that play—reimagined as a form of critical media literacy—is essential for navigating these complexities. Through play, individuals can question dominant narratives, expose hidden power structures, and reclaim agency over their digital lives.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>By unpacking the ideologies embedded in contemporary media and the subtle ways they shape citizenship, knowledge, and authenticity, Playology: A Media-Critical Exploration of Digital Technologies and Identity in the Global Village invites readers to engage more consciously with the technologies that define modern existence. It is a call to resist passive consumption, embrace creative inquiry, and cultivate the critical literacies necessary for a more open, pluralistic, and humane digital future.</jats:p>

title: Capacity Limits in Cognitive Processing Reflect the Curse of Generalization
65a5e431acc5d0a8d2c5143f2e9ef4740d73e2de.abstract: The striking constraints of some human cognitive processes stand in stark contrastto the near limitless capability of others. While we can acquire and flexibly use vast amountsof information, the amount we can process at any one time is often stiflingly limited: forexample the number of items we can hold in working memory or the number of tasks that canbe performed at once. Here, we integrate ideas from information theory, cognitive science,and neuroscience to offer a unified account of why processing is often so limited. We arguethat this reflects a fundamental tradeoff between generalization—how effectively existingrepresentations can be used in novel settings—and how many distinct representations canbe processed in parallel. Representations that best promote strong forms of generalization— a characteristically human cognitive strength — come at the expense of surprisinglystrict limits in the number of items that can be processed at once, an equally characteristichuman weakness. We refer to this as the “curse of generalization.” We formulate this first ininformation-theoretic terms, and then in process models, including a neural network modelof classic tasks used to demonstrate strict limits in human processing capacity. This tensionoffers a potential explanation for a range of phenomena — from performance on the tasks onwhich we focus, to representational learning and skill acquisition more broadly — as wellas the performance of modern machine learning architectures that exhibit generalizationcapabilities comparable to humans.

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Ambivalencias en torno a las técnicas de reproducción asistida
Ambivalences Regarding Assisted Reproductive Technologies
container-title: Análisis Filosófico
b86ff439826d1f77775ac23357cee21dae26a817.abstract: <jats:p>Este artículo analiza las técnicas de reproducción asistida (TRHA) desde una perspectiva feminista, abordando las tensiones entre autonomía, deseo y justicia. Se examinan las implicancias éticas de la medicalización, la mercantilización del cuerpo, y las normas de género y familia que estas tecnologías pueden reforzar o desafiar. A partir del concepto de autonomía relacional, se considera cómo las condiciones sociales, económicas y culturales influyen en las decisiones reproductivas. Se propone integrar la ética del cuidado y la justicia reproductiva como marcos analíticos que permitan una comprensión más inclusiva y crítica de las TRHA, con énfasis en la equidad, la dignidad y los derechos.</jats:p>

title: Ética y gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos de las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
af434ca184d59d5ddf93af8a7cfe27022962cd0f.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo presenta un análisis sobre los marcos éticos y de gobernanza para el uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación, con especial énfasis en su incorporación en las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia. El objetivo es proponer lineamientos estratégicos que orienten un uso ético, responsable y contextualizado de la IA en los procesos educativos militares. Metodológicamente, se realizó una revisión documental de políticas institucionales nacionales e internacionales, contrastadas con recomendaciones de organismos como la UNESCO y la OCDE, así como diálogos académicos con expertos en la materia. Entre los resultados se identifican buenas prácticas y principios comunes, como la transparencia, la equidad y la alfabetización digital. Las conclusiones destacan la necesidad urgente de establecer políticas adaptadas al entorno militar, promover la formación crítica en IA en todos los niveles y garantizar que esta tecnología habilitadora complemente, mas no reemplace, el juicio humano en la formación de competencias como el pensamiento crítico, la toma de decisiones, el debate argumentativo, la solución de problemas, el discernimiento ético, entre otras competencias propias de la profesión militar.</jats:p>

title: Aportes de la inteligencia artificial a la enseñanza de la memoria histórica en el sector defensa
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
3e5814c496eff2daf13c4983ddcc53e4f747fd76.abstract: <jats:p>En el escenario de post-conflicto que vive Colombia, la memoria histórica ha cobrado un papel central en la implementación del Sistema Integral de Verdad, Justicia, Reparación y No Repetición, el cual tiene la titánica labor de visibilizar, dignificar y reconocer a las víctimas del conflicto armado colombiano. Por tal motivo, su enseñanza resulta indispensable para que las generaciones centenials del sector defensa comprendan las causas, el desarrollo y las consecuencias del conflicto. El objetivo de este capítulo es analizar cómo la inteligencia artificial puede contribuir al aprendizaje de la memoria histórica, a través de un análisis documental y bibliométrico, sustentado en el modelo de aprendizaje constructivista, que permita identificar tendencias, enfoques y experiencias relevantes. Entre los principales hallazgos, se identificó un creciente interés investigativo en la articulación entre memoria histórica, tecnologías de aprendizaje e inteligencia artificial, que brindan oportunidades para el diseño de estrategias educativas más eficaces dirigidas a las nuevas generaciones.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence for kinematic (procedural motion) analysis in gastrointestinal endoscopy: A systematic review
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
b57da8d69347ef96ad6b53af36bb1108bb32c469.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal endoscopy has focused on computer-aided detection (CADe) for recognition errors; AI addressing endoscope motion, coverage, workflow, and skill – collectively kinematic analysis – has not been systematically synthesized.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To map kinematic AI evidence across eight predefined domains and assessed its quality relative to CADe and surgical AI.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE-OVID, Cochrane, and IEEE Xplore were searched following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist (CRD420261320279). Studies applying AI to kinematic data in gastrointestinal endoscopy were eligible. Risk of bias used Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2, and PROBAST + AI; certainty of evidence used GRADE.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Fifty-eight studies were included. Evidence generation was asymmetric: (1) Randomized controlled trial ratio approximately 5:1 (> 40 vs  8); (2) Patient ratio approximately 4:1 (> 27000 vs  approximately 6200); (3) Annual publication ratio approximately 12:1; and (4) ≥ 6 vs  0 regulatory approvals favoring diagnostic AI. Withdrawal speed monitoring and coverage/blind-spot mapping reached moderate GRADE certainty, but all 8 randomized controlled trials were from China and 6 of 8 used the ENDOANGEL platform. The remaining six domains have not reached moderate certainty: (1) Workflow recognition and skill assessment are approaching clinical readiness; and (2) Autonomous navigation, robotic control, simultaneous localization and mapping/three-dimensional reconstruction, and instrument tracking remain at the engineering stage. Comparison with surgical AI indicated that the gap reflects ecosystem-level factors – absence of open datasets, benchmarking challenges, and regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI – rather than technical immaturity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Kinematic AI addresses exposure errors that CADe cannot correct and has shown additive benefit alongside CADe. Two domains are ready for geographically diverse validation; six remain at the engineering stage. Priorities are open datasets, benchmarking infrastructure, and dedicated regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI.</jats:p>

title: Beautiful Particulars
c6fe3d0377956ff06d423eb5e3d727284e365eac.abstract:
<jats:p>A fresh and eye-opening new explanation of AI—and how its focus on specifics is changing our ideas about ourselves and our world.From a Harvard researcher, philosopher, entrepreneur, former comedy writer, and bestselling author.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Amid the clamor about AI, Beautiful Particulars poses a unique question: Not how does our use of AI change what we do, but how is the idea of AI already subtly yet fundamentally reshaping how we think about ourselves and our world?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>In clear, engaging, and even humorous prose, David Weinberger offers a new perspective on how machine learning works and how it may already be changing our basic and deepest ideas. Through lively examples, he shows that AI’s success—with all its risks and dangers—is taking us past our millennia of reliance on laws and principles by revealing what morality, free will, creativity, causality knowledge, and even reality itself look like now that we’re able to let the particulars speak their tiny truths.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>The author poses questions not usually asked: What does a coin look like to AI? When AI gives you evidence that the earth is round, why are its own reasons for saying that so different? Why does an AI image generator create a “selfie” of ancient Aztec warriors with broad smiles that it “believes” are historically unlikely? If AI becomes conscious but bodiless, could it still make good moral decisions? Why is the world so much better at being causal than AI could ever “understand”? How does AI show us that genuine creativity is not about a “spark” but about moments that feel right? And how can you take the temperature of a joke?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>Beautiful Particulars offers a new—and hopeful—perspective on how machine learning works, and how that’s already changing how we understand what it means to be human in the age of AI.</jats:p>

title: Masked denoising diffusion for accurate anomaly recognition and reconstruction
container-title: CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research
828c4288e3166ed63db2c3796155bc6efb0fa4e2.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In data-driven industrial anomaly detection, the scarcity of defect samples and the emergence of unknown defect types pose significant challenges to quality control. While unsupervised generative models offer a viable solution, existing diffusion-based methods (e.g., DDAD) face a critical limitation: they often fail to distinguish between normal and anomalous patterns during reconstruction. Consequently, these models may inadvertently reconstruct the defects themselves rather than restoring the healthy state, leading to missed detections and inaccurate anomaly localization. To address this dilemma, we propose masked DDAD (mDDAD), which integrates masked image modeling (MIM) to enforce the learning of global semantic context, thereby enhancing sensitivity to anomalies. We further introduce a dynamic noise adjustment mechanism (DNAM) that selectively reduces noise intensity in masked regions to preserve essential structural information. Additionally, we optimize the training process via dynamic weighted loss optimization (DWLO) to prioritize critical regions. Experiments on the MVTec-AD and VisA datasets demonstrate that mDDAD effectively mitigates the reconstruction failure of baseline methods, significantly outperforming existing approaches in both anomaly detection and reconstruction accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/zhg-SZPT/mDDAP.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
