title: Attention, Obligation, and the Rootedness of Human Identity in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
e4417ce1339c12cc05dc70011ea7ae674c983fe8.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how the AI renaissance is reconfiguring fundamental anthropological conditions of human existence and how Simone Weil's ethics of attention, obligation, and rootedness can provide a normative framework for understanding these transformations. Methodologically, the analysis combines conceptual reconstruction, philosophical-hermeneutic updating, and critically reflected conceptual engineering to translate Weil's categories into contemporary AI contexts. The analysis identifies three interconnected transformations: AI-mediated environments can reshape the conditions for sustained attention; distributed human-machine agency can create responsibility and obligation gaps; and digital infrastructures can weaken the conditions for social, economic, and political rootedness. The chapter develops a Weilian governance framework that deepens human-centered AI by identifying the anthropological conditions that underlie rights, human oversight, accountability, and participation.</jats:p>

title: Human Rights in the AI Renaissance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
b6cc6cdaede90b65d88551af1e19e431b12e7088.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is an innovation that is fast changing society, economy, and government structures. Although it is extremely advantageous, it also triggers the issue of human rights, fairness, and accountability. This chapter focuses on the discussion of the manner in which human rights will be protected in the ascendancy of AI. It raises the red flag over perilous algorithms, the absence of transparency and surveillance technologies proliferation. Legal frameworks and considerations that can be used to steer innovation towards dignity, equality, and justice are also addressed. Healthcare, employment, policing case studies gives an example of how AI affects the basic freedom. The chapter proposes a right based regulation of AI, stating that innovation should be moderated and should not harm people and society. It concludes with the policy suggestions that can make AI advocacy to social justice and maintain human freedoms.</jats:p>

title: From High-Level Ethics to Actionable Measures
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f6df0e82bb922344b07c7ca3d990ca38bb2a53f5.abstract: <jats:p>The active evolution of technology has led to new changes, and one of the trends that has become topical and actively discussed within the academic community and society in general is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Nevertheless, it has turned out that the data on which AI systems are built is not always neutral. This has resulted in cases where AI systems replicate and reinforce existing societal biases. At this point, no specific case law exists to cover the issues related to AI, so ethical frameworks have been developed. Such frameworks typically define top-level principles aimed at guaranteeing the credibility and justice of AI-based systems. However, principles such as explainability and accountability are frequently criticised because they are too abstract, as they do not provide any tangible measures that would guarantee their proper adoption. To develop recommendations on actions that can be taken to address these two principles, a qualitative literature review focusing on these themes has been conducted.</jats:p>

title: Reconfiguring Identity, Ownership, and Legal Framework in the Digital World
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
f0a6336edb0b64a20e417a3a4a4f176bb513d8c1.abstract: <jats:p>Humankind's lived reality of an experience heavily mediated by Generative AI and the digital realm calls for a critical reconfiguration of existing social modes of being as well as legal contracts and regulations. The chapter attempts to address significant challenges presented by AI and AI-generated content specifically within literary creation in terms of copyright and ownership as well as legal systems pertaining to digital personhood and identity. A reworking of the traditional understanding of authorship and creativity also traces the inadequacy of existing global legal frameworks, largely anthropocentric in nature, grappling with the dilemma of attributing ownership and accountability for AI-generated creative content and prosecution of AI entities. The chapter also explores digital personhood with specific focus on the idea of digital necromancy and sophisticated AI crime as a threat to the world at large. The aim is to raise questions that could foster dialogue and initiate some form of policy change in the aforementioned realms.</jats:p>

title: Binary Biases
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
10d2652f77e6a8ecef648ea24ba8c77df85691ea.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of AI in content moderation raises major challenges in detecting hate speech and introduces new biases. This chapter explores the limits of binary classification models in addressing the complex nature of online hate. Standard machine learning methods often miss cultural context, evolving language, and the fine line between free speech and harmful speech, leading to unfair outcomes for marginalized groups. Through a mixed-method study using SVMs, deep learning, and transformer models on multilingual datasets, we reveal flaws in current systems. Findings show frequent mislabeling of cultural expressions, racial and gender gaps, and declining accuracy as language shifts. Qualitative evidence highlights social harms, including silencing advocacy and reinforcing discrimination. We stress the need for culturally aware, transparent detection and propose hybrid human–AI moderation to protect users while supporting democratic rights.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Labor, Employment Contracts, and Professional Identity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
34add7a445929817b91d0a85a92c50bba7824908.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping labor, employment contracts, and professional identity. It argues that AI is not merely automating tasks but transforming the nature of work through automation, new job categories, and human-AI collaboration. It analyzes the rise of platform labor and algorithmic management, the legal-ethical challenges of bias, transparency, and accountability, and the tension between flexibility and precarity. It explores identity shifts requiring reskilling, lifelong learning, and psychological adaptation. Policy, regulation, and collective bargaining frameworks are evaluated alongside case studies across sectors and regions. The chapter outlines scenarios for the future of work and calls for renewed social contracts that safeguard equity, inclusion, and meaningful human agency.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Electronic Health Record
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Reconfiguring Human Identity and Social Contracts in the AI Renaissance
160b86d6f7ca4a0340314e88b523dcae1039a032.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital in healthcare, especially in training medical officers for disease analysis and patient care. In diagnostics, AI algorithms enhance image interpretation accuracy and enable disease prediction like cancer and retinopathy. These modules analyze imaging data like MRIs, CT scans, and X-rays to identify nerve and cell injuries. In therapeutics, AI aids drug discovery by finding molecular interactions and optimizing trials, reducing time and costs. AI-based robotic systems enhance surgical precision and limit invasiveness. AI benefits healthcare management through predictive analytics for resource allocation and supply chain optimization. AI-powered chatbots provide 24/7 patient support and handle remote consultations. AI and IoT-enabled hospital-at-home modules allow home treatment, reducing facility strain. However, AI in healthcare raises ethical concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, and healthcare disparities. While AI develops, its limitations and transformative potential remain crucial for effective, equitable healthcare models.</jats:p>

title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, gut microbiome composition, impulsivity, and attention covary in a human cohort
container-title: Microbiology Spectrum
4b2ea61ea8ae67962d02b43bdd0ca11c398c565c.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are pervasive environmental pollutants linked to adverse neurobehavioral outcomes, yet the biological pathways coupling exposure to behavior are poorly defined. The gut microbiome is both sensitive to PAH exposure and a modulator of central nervous system function, suggesting it may mediate how PAH exposure influences neurobehavior. We tested whether PAH exposure, gut microbiome composition, and neurobehavioral function covary in a statewide sample of 34 adults stratified into high-impulsivity/poor-attention (HH) and low-impulsivity/fast-attention (LL) groups. Participants wore silicone wristbands for 30 days to passively sample PAH exposure and provided a single fecal sample for 16S rRNA profiling at the end of the wear period. Higher PAH exposure was associated with HH group membership in a sex-dependent manner, with the largest elevations among HH males. At the community level, PAH exposure profiles correlated with microbiome dissimilarity, and HH membership was associated with increased alpha-diversity and altered community composition relative to LL members. At the taxon level, 22 genera were significantly associated with 14 PAH compounds (FDR < 0.1). No individual genera were significantly associated with neurobehavioral group after multiple testing correction. Nevertheless, cross-referencing PAH-responsive genera (FDR < 0.1) against those with nominal neurobehavioral associations (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                      < 0.05) identified two candidate genera
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">—Hydrogenoanaerobacterium</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Methanobrevibacter</jats:italic>
                      —whose abundance covaries with both PAH exposure and neurobehavioral phenotype. Both have been independently linked to cognitive or neurological outcomes in prior work. These findings support a three-way relationship among environmental chemical exposure, gut microbiome composition, and neurobehavioral function, establishing an empirical foundation for testing microbiome-mediated links between PAH exposure and neurobehavioral outcomes.
                    </jats:p>
                    <jats:sec>
                      <jats:title>IMPORTANCE</jats:title>
                      <jats:p>Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) exposure is widespread and is associated with impulsivity and attention problems, but how exposure translates into neurobehavioral risk is unclear. The gut microbiome is a plausible intermediary: gut microbes biotransform environmental chemicals and produce metabolites that influence brain function. In a statewide adult cohort, higher PAH exposure associated with with greater impulsivity and poorer attention in a sex-dependent manner, and both PAH exposure and neurobehavioral phenotype were associated with distinct gut microbiome features at the community and taxon levels. We identify candidate genera at the intersection of PAH exposure and neurobehavioral group whose biology independently implicates them in cognitive and neurological function. Because their associations with neurobehavioral phenotype are nominal, we present these genera as hypothesis-generating candidates for future study. By showing that all three domains covary within a single cohort, this work moves beyond pairwise associations toward testable microbiome-targeted and exposure-reduction strategies for PAH-related neurobehavioral risk.</jats:p>
                    </jats:sec>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A TOE–RBV–TBL Integrated Model of AI-Enabled Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
40d1fa5cdd6cd6c42b1d66704eea0c7b9caed768.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping food logistics by enhancing operational efficiency, reducing waste, and promoting sustainable supply chain practices. This study develops and validates an integrated Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE), Resource-Based View (RBV), and Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework to examine the determinants and outcomes of AI-enabled sustainable food logistics. Primary data were collected from 312 professionals in India's food supply chain and analysed using CB-SEM. The findings reveal that technological readiness, organisational capability, and environmental pressure significantly drive AI adoption, while AI capability positively influences environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The study offers a comprehensive theoretical framework and practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to build resilient, intelligent, and sustainable food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Cold Chain Optimization for Reducing Food Loss in Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
f7b19d3fb02e51972e9a5e5f799a5064e20516bb.abstract: <jats:p>With the combination of IoT-based monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making, AI-powered optimization of cold-chains increases the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of perishable chains. Sensors can provide real-time data, therefore, monitoring the temperature, humidity, and logistics status continuously and predict risks of spoilage and optimizing routing, storage, and inventory control with AI models. In case studies in dairy, seafood and fresh produce, there has been a substantial decrease in the spoilage and increased efficiency in work. Traceability and compliance are additionally improved with the help of the blockchain integration. In general, cold-chain systems with AI will help minimize food waste, advance food quality, and sustain logistics in complicated supply chains.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Quality Monitoring and Food Safety Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
2f988859afeb8045e1f8933ad6d0b777eed57974.abstract: <jats:p>AI has transformation in the area of food quality inspection and safety management due to the capabilities that have been introduced in rapid, precise, non-destructive and predictive assessment of food quality through the production process, processing, storage, transport, retailing and consumption. These techniques are applicable in fast monitoring and quick intervention in areas of dairy products, meat products, seafood, fruits and vegetables, cereals, beverages and ready to eat meals. This chapter discusses the principles, technologies, applications, benefits, challenges, and future prospects of AI-based food quality monitoring and safety management, with particular emphasis on intelligent sensors, real-time contamination detection, automated inspection, shelf-life prediction, process optimization, traceability, and predictive risk management across diverse food sectors.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Predictive Analytics for Sustainable Demand Forecasting in Agri-Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
ae908a7d83acc41af9c9be1d1de1a65faa9f8570.abstract: <jats:p>Predictive analytics, which is an AI technology, is changing the logistics of agri-foods by enhancing sustainability and demand forecasting. The conventional predictive approaches do not normally reflect their dynamic aspects, including weather fluctuations, market behavior and consumer behaviors, resulting into inefficiencies and food wastage. This chapter describes an AI-based framework that combines multi-source data, machine learning models, and decision support systems to come up with correct and real-time demand forecasts. The strategy facilitates optimal inventory control, effective distribution strategy, and minimized environmental concerns. There are enormous evidences of case studies showing enhancement of accuracy in forecasts, reduction of wastes, and efficiency in the operations. The results address the possible opportunities of AI assisting the resilient, adaptive, and sustainable food supply chains in the fast-changing global food system.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Innovations in Agri-Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
700ec2c44d31bcf14cea8b84c21efb4ae0bd8c73.abstract: <jats:p>Algorithms and other AI tools are increasingly being used to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and resilience of the Integrated Agri-food Supply Chain (IASC) across several areas of the agri-food sector. Innovations enabled by using AI technologies in agri-food systems referred to in this chapter are the ones that will achieve the best production, processing, distribution and consumption. The predictive analytics, machine learning, and intelligence-supporting tools are all about ensuring that requirements are always checked and predictable, resources are deployed,, and risk minimisation is done in real time. AI and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain platforms, and automated logistics are explored, and the potential for creating transparent, traceable supply chains that adapt to fluctuating demand and supply is investigated. Case studies have been presented that show successful applications and improvements in productivity, waste minimisation,, and operational costs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Driven Real-Time Route Optimization for Dynamic Food Logistics and Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
a3d254406bb275561bb5d6e8d0065c094ec34437.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter describes how to use real-time data analytics and machine learning to automatically simulate and execute alternative food logistics routes to predict supply chain bottlenecks (such as supplier failures or natural disasters) before they occur. Based on academic publications from 2024 to 2026, the chapter uses a systematic review and thematic content analysis. The findings show that AI and data analytics are transforming food logistics and supply chains into sustainable, efficient, and creative transportation. Traditional logistics systems suffer from poor order consolidation, low truck capacity utilization, static route planning, and significant environmental impacts. Efficiency losses increase operational expenses, delay supply, and increase carbon emissions, threatening sustainability. Cloud-based data platforms and reinforcement learning optimize logistics and route planning. Logistics sustainability demands data-driven decision-making and clever automation.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
1ca0d752e991777e60571046cca42e7e93889d3a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of agri-food supply chains through artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing sustainable food logistics, resilience, and human resource management (HRM). It highlights how AI-driven technologies such as machine learning, IoT, and predictive analytics enable real-time decision-making, demand forecasting, and supply chain optimization, thereby reducing food waste and improving efficiency. The study integrates sustainability dimensions—environmental, economic, and social—with resilience strategies to address disruptions and uncertainties. Furthermore, it explores the critical role of HRM in facilitating workforce transformation, human–AI collaboration, and organizational change. An integrated AI–Sustainability–HRM framework is proposed to enhance adaptability and long-term performance. The chapter contributes to theory and practice by presenting a holistic, data-driven approach to building intelligent, resilient, and sustainable food logistics systems.</jats:p>

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Food Waste Reduction in India's Perishable Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
fc88c02780841f38b3f41c69dae42b101d38d76a.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we focus on the role that AI-driven predictive analytics can play to assist with forecast accuracy, cold-chain orchestration, quality monitoring and speed of response upstream and downstream through the farm-to-market flows to abete food loss and waste in India´s perishable supply chains. It relies on a systematic secondary empirical synthesis of India-centric studies, policy papers, and analytics research on global experience pertaining to high perishability classes of vegetables, dairy, fish, and other fresh fruits. The chapter proves that besides infrastructural hurdles, food waste challenges of India is also a challenge of timing, visibility and coordination. Evidence from India reveals how much of the loss occurs is seasonally driven, how losses are correlated with harvest volume, storage, transport reliability, and the quality sorting and practices. This chapter presents a predictive analytics framework for agri-logistics, suggests how Indian firms and policymakers can implement the approach, and claims that digital traceability.</jats:p>

title: Predictive Business Intelligence Architectures for Cold-Chain Logistics Mitigating Food Waste Through AI-Driven IoT Sensor Integration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Driven Sustainable Food Logistics and Supply Chains
791f2efff6e75d93d6ead2cbd5779a343d5628c2.abstract: <jats:p>Food loss and waste in cold-chain logistics result not only from refrigeration failures, but also from fragmented data, delayed responses, and weak coordination across supply-chain actors. This chapter presents an IGI-style conceptual and implementation framework for predictive business intelligence (BI) in cold-chain logistics. It argues that waste reduction is more effective when Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, event-driven data integration, and artificial intelligence (AI) analytics are designed as a layered architectural capability rather than as stand-alone monitoring tools. Drawing on literature in cold-chain management, food quality, wireless sensing, BI, predictive analytics, AI-enabled supply chains, and digital twins, the chapter shows how variables such as temperature, humidity, location, door events, shock, dwell time, and product condition can be transformed into risk scores, dynamic shelf-life estimates, prioritized exceptions, and closed-loop decisions. It also proposes architecture and seven implementation workstreams for deployment.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Cold Chain Management Using AI and IoT
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

60daab0ba3149ca77331fc247ab25917cceed633.abstract: <jats:p>The convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is fundamentally reshaping cold chain logistics, enabling unprecedented levels of precision, transparency, and sustainability. This chapter examines how intelligent sensing, predictive analytics, blockchain-based traceability, and digital twin simulation collectively address the chronic inefficiencies of temperature-sensitive supply chains. Drawing on recent empirical and review studies, the chapter presents an integrated framework that links real-time data acquisition to AI-driven decision-making and blockchain-anchored accountability. Key themes include spoilage prevention, carbon footprint reduction, regulatory compliance, and consumer trust. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on challenges and emerging directions for scalable, equitable, and ethically grounded cold chain transformation.</jats:p>

title: From Data–Model Fit to Model–World Fit: A Framework for Integrating Domain Knowledge into Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Information Systems Research
90b62a3119c6508d0cc057bd92609f5992407b47.abstract:
<jats:p>Machine learning (ML)–based artificial intelligence (AI) systems often perform well in controlled settings but fail when deployed in the real world. These failures stem from a fundamental problem: ML/AI models optimize data–model fit by increasing statistical performance on training data, whereas real-world deployment demands a new paradigm in ML/AI: model–world fit that preserves domain semantics and contextual understanding. We propose a machine learning model–world fit framework that provides both a conceptual structure for understanding how domain knowledge shapes ML/AI systems and a research road map for investigating these relationships. The framework identifies how domain knowledge can be integrated into the ML/AI development process via external knowledge representations, such as data, value, process models, or domain ontologies. Incorporating external knowledge representations can help overcome three types of knowledge deficiencies in AI: know-what, know-how, and know-why. To illustrate the framework, we apply it to a child welfare placement case, a domain in which contextual understanding is critical and statistical accuracy is an insufficient evaluation criterion. Our insights lead to several directions for scholars working at the intersection of machine learning, design science, and knowledge representation.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>History: Ahmed Abbasi, Senior Editor; Min Zhao, Associate Editor.</jats:p>

title: Tenecteplase Before Thrombectomy at 4.5 to 24 Hours for Basilar Artery Occlusion
container-title: JAMA
ef60472e8a004149c416d5f14b5651c60704d5a8.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Importance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Whether intravenous tenecteplase before endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) improves outcomes in patients with basilar artery occlusion presenting 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset remains uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT vs EVT alone in patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This multicenter, open-label, blinded end point, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 40 stroke centers in China. Between March 16, 2023, and February 4, 2025, a total of 330 patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥10) presenting within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset to EVT-capable centers were enrolled. Final follow-up was completed on May 4, 2025.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Interventions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients were randomized 1:1 via a centralized web server using a minimization method to receive either intravenous tenecteplase (bolus injection, 0.25 mg/kg; maximum, 25 mg) followed by EVT (n = 166) or EVT alone (n = 164).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The primary outcome was functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 332 patients randomized, 2 withdrew consent. Of the remaining 330 patients (mean [SD] age, 66 [11] years; 241 males [73%]; 89 females [27%]), 329 completed 90-day follow-up. Of whom, 50 of 165 (30%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 50 of 164 (30%) in the EVT alone group achieved functional independence (adjusted rate ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.67 to 1.25]; risk difference, −0.18% [95% CI, −10.13% to 9.76%]). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 8 patients (5%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 6 (4%) in the EVT alone group. Mortality at 90 days was similar between the groups (66 [40%] vs 70 [43%], respectively).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted directly to EVT-capable centers who presented 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset, the addition of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT did not result in improved functional outcomes compared with EVT alone.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial Registration</jats:title>

                      <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05701956">NCT05701956</jats:ext-link>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Mixed Reality
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
e04323502a4b153b2e9de555a487f931fc1a6812.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter looks at the ways in which Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Mixed Reality are inextricably linked. To do that, this chapter first looks at what is meant by current “Artificial Intelligence” and argues that in some ways it is best thought of as being neither artificial nor intelligent. The chapter then discusses the various ways in which Mixed Reality is the “eyes and ears” of AI, including using data collected via MR to train AI, using AI to create or improve MR elements in real time, and using AI to process MR data for users to allow a more minimally virtual mixed reality. Ultimately, the chapter argues that AI and MR work in concert to alter our experience of the environment and people’s roles in it.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
9804e231d1b385dde790b1cf795ea7aaec80b1c1.abstract: <jats:p>Financial decision-making is being revolutionized by the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Whereas traditional statistical methods may be limited by the scope and complexity of contemporary financial datasets, AI technologies such as machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) permit companies to analyze not only structured but unstructured datasets efficiently. As such, there have been significant improvements in financial decision-making processes related to portfolio management, risk analysis, fraud detection, and algorithmic trading. However, the use of AI in the financial industry is also associated with issues such as lack of model transparency, algorithmic bias, and high reliance on past data, which create certain problems when it comes to transparency and reliability.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Decision-Making
container-title: Digital Competencies and Skills for Future Finance Professionals
478d0167085f2f271218a60ba78cf0ed82a89eb2.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping financial decision-making by enhancing analytical accuracy, speed, and strategic insight across corporate finance and financial services. The primary objective of the study is to evaluate how AI applications support strategic and operational financial decisions, while also assessing associated risks related to transparency, accountability, and decision control. A qualitative case study methodology is adopted, drawing on secondary data sources including corporate reports, financial disclosures, technology implementation documents, and industry publications. The findings indicate that AI significantly improves forecasting accuracy, real-time financial monitoring, and scenario analysis, leading to more informed and timely financial decisions. The study offers original value by providing practical, case-based evidence on how AI transforms financial decision-making processes beyond theoretical models. The implications are relevant for stakeholders seeking to leverage sustainable financial performance.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience of Goods Transportation
container-title: Auditing and Measuring Supply Chain Success and Sustainability
0f13c500235813cb1b24d53993c3fde254735b7c.abstract: <jats:p>In an era marked by heightened uncertainty and frequent disruptions, building resilient supply chains for goods has emerged as a strategic imperative for organizations. This study evaluates the role of Artificial Intelligence in enhancing supply chain resilience while transporting goods within a context of heightened disruption frequency by examining patterns of AI adoption, its practical applications, and the resulting organizational outcomes. Based on survey data from 160 industry professionals across various goods industries, we analyze the current state and perceived impact of AI integration. Findings indicate significant AI adoption, predominantly leveraging Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics. Significant statistical associations were found linking AI adoption to cost savings, specific resilience outcomes, and benefits. This research provides empirical validation of AI's positive influence on Supply Chain Resilience of goods transportation highlighting its capacity to improve organizational efficiency.</jats:p>

title: Attention Trap? How Visual Motion Shapes Children’s Screen Time and Engagement on Video Platforms
container-title: Information Systems Research
3836bd62e72740b25fd59c7e03808cdae1f4dd40.abstract:
<jats:p>Children spend considerable time watching online video, yet we know relatively little about which features of video content shape their engagement. This research examines one measurable feature: visual motion. Analyzing more than 32,000 videos from popular children’s channels on YouTube, we find that videos with greater visual motion receive more views, even after accounting for other visual, audio, and content characteristics. A randomized YouTube advertising experiment using professionally produced educational videos confirms this relationship; adding motion to the background increased view rates by about 2% at essentially no additional cost.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>An eye-tracking study with children aged 6–10 helps explain why. Visual motion does not prevent children from looking away. Instead, it reduces the duration of longer attentional lapses by bringing their gaze back to the screen more quickly. The additional attention is directed primarily toward the moving background rather than the instructor. The findings show how a measurable design feature can shape children’s attention and provide creators and platforms with a way to assess and design children’s video content more systematically.</jats:p>

title: Reconnoitring Yogic Peace of Mind and Transient Happiness With Their Perceived Psychological Correlates
container-title: The Neuroscience of Happiness
2a08909a0d86148aae4b34a85733003e4a4fe6d2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter discusses yogic peace of mind as a complex, self-reported psychological construct and looks into its linkages with perceived cognition, emotional regulation, meditative consciousness, and well-being. The empirical part of the research is a pilot cross-sectional study conducted only using data collected via questionnaires; it did not include measurements of brain activity, neurotransmitter levels, the autonomic nervous system, or any other biological parameters. Consequently, all neurological hypotheses are discussed as interpretations based on existing neuroscience literature and not on the findings of this particular research. Some preliminary findings of factor, regression, and structural modeling analyses will be used to evaluate the proposed theoretical links between the concepts. There is evidence of correlations between long-term yogic practice, reported peace of mind, and positive psychological outcomes; however, there is no proof of causation or physiological changes. Further large-scale longitudinal studies are required to verify the hypothesis.</jats:p>

title: The application of an artificial intelligence–enhanced virtual reality cognitive behavioral therapy tool is feasible and acceptable in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: A multicenter mixed methods pilot study
container-title: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
34e53c5af6594279fbcef7d176c277418b8c6c44.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently experience anxiety, pain, and reduced quality of life. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective for anxiety, but access may be limited. We evaluated the feasibility and explored the potential clinical impact of an artificial intelligence–powered virtual reality CBT-based application (XAIA [eXtended Reality Artificially Intelligent Ally]) in patients with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This was a multicenter, mixed-methods pilot study recruiting adults with IBD from the University of Chicago and Cedars-Sinai medical centers. Participants completed a single 30-minute session with the XAIA conversational avatar. Pain and anxiety were measured before and after the session using a visual analog pain scale and State–Trait Anxiety Inventory, respectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted after the session to assess acceptability. Quantitative analysis was completed using paired t tests, and interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-four participants (median age 34 years, 71% women, 59% with Crohn’s disease) participated in this study. Qualitative analysis revealed high acceptability, with participants reporting feelings of safety, validation, and improved coping. Participants valued the immersive environment, conversational avatar, and ability to discuss sensitive topics without judgment. As an exploratory outcome, participants reported a statistically significant improvement in pain (−0.46; P = .011) and anxiety (−10.65; P &lt; .001) immediately following a single session.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A single artificial intelligence–driven virtual reality CBT-based session in patients with IBD was feasible and well accepted and demonstrated preliminary evidence for acute reductions in pain and anxiety scores. Immersive digital behavioral health interventions may represent a scalable adjunct to traditional mental health support among adults with IBD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Cognitive Stimulation for Delirium Prevention in Older Surgical Intensive Care Unit Patients With Cognitive Impairment: Protocol for a 3-Arm Randomized Pilot Trial
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
6a0305024bfe7ca8c2a7ec25512ab1521c9d9887.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative delirium is common among older adults after major surgery, especially those with cognitive impairment, and is associated with prolonged hospitalization, functional decline, mortality, and subsequent cognitive deterioration. Nonpharmacologic delirium-prevention strategies are recommended but are difficult to deliver reliably in high-acuity environments because they require repeated staff-intensive interactions, consistent patient engagement, and integration into complex intensive care unit (ICU) workflows.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, usability, safety, acceptance, and adherence of ReCognitionVR 2.0, an immersive virtual reality (VR)–based cognitive stimulation intervention designed for older surgical ICU patients with mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This is a single-center, 3-arm, parallel-group randomized pilot trial. Ninety adults aged 65 years or older undergoing major surgery with expected postoperative ICU admission and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores of 15 to 24 will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to ReCognitionVR 2.0 cognitive stimulation, passive VR control exposure, or standard-of-care nurse-led reality orientation. VR sessions will be delivered once daily for up to 20 minutes on postoperative days 1 through 3 when participants are calm and alert. The primary outcomes are feasibility metrics, including recruitment, outcome completion, safety and tolerability, usability, acceptance, and adherence. Secondary outcomes estimate preliminary changes in attention and executive function using the Months Backward Test and NIH Toolbox Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention Test. Postoperative delirium incidence is an exploratory clinical outcome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was funded in September 2025. Participant recruitment and data collection are currently ongoing. Preliminary data quality assessments and exploratory reviews of the collected data are underway. Formal statistical analyses of the trial outcomes will be conducted after participant enrollment is completed and the study database has been finalized and locked. As of July 29, 2026, we had enrolled 18 participants. Early operational experience informed the refinement of exploratory VR performance metrics and the documentation of protocol deviations. Following an oxygen-connection near miss, we added a preintervention oxygen/readiness checklist as an operational safety safeguard. Enrollment of 90 participants is projected to be completed in 2027 if the current recruitment pace is sustained. Results are expected to be published in winter 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This protocol will generate data on feasibility, safety, usability, adherence, digital performance, cognitive assessment, and delirium measurement, all needed to optimize ReCognitionVR 2.0 and to design a future multicenter efficacy trial of VR-enabled delirium prevention in critical care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Irresponsible regional future-making: fast forward as if there were no crises?
container-title: Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society
0e1287016d1aad62bdab34f124d9d1d4357d5d3d.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Although the current era is one of multiple global crises that call for more sustainable solutions, the futures imagined in many regions do not seem to address these crises adequately but are marked by irresponsibility, that is, the shifting of negative effects in time, space or within the population. These futures can be irresponsible in regions whose imagined future is a continuation of the past, as well as in regions whose imagined futures involve radical transformations. The article uses the discursive-institutionalist concept of ideational power to discuss how irresponsible futures emerge in these regions and which role power relations play in these imagined futures.</jats:p>

title: Safeguarding Democracy in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Warfare
container-title: Reframing Democracy Through International Relations, Strategy, and Governance in a Fragmented World
a76d47ff83e1035fea0593c859a1f74dd1205877.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has transformed the contemporary information environment, creating new forms of digital influence capable of shaping political narratives and public perception. While artificial intelligence offers significant benefits for governance, innovation, and communication, it also introduces complex risks for democratic societies. One of the most pressing challenges is the emergence of AI-driven disinformation, where automated systems are used to generate and disseminate misleading or fabricated content at unprecedented scale. Such developments threaten electoral integrity, institutional trust, and the credibility of public information systems. This chapter examines the relationship between artificial intelligence–enabled information warfare and democratic governance from a global perspective. It explores how disinformation campaigns operate within digital ecosystems and evaluates policy responses aimed at protecting democratic processes.</jats:p>

title: Should quantum physics be approached with mathematical formalism in school? Effects of instructional approach on functional understanding under cognitive and affective controls
container-title: Physical Review Physics Education Research
6493f05b70eb976685bab6227f1a5b655fc3ff28.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Evidence from physics education research suggests that the introduction of mathematical formalism in quantum physics instruction can support the development of students’ conceptual understanding, particularly by promoting functional ways of reasoning about quantum phenomena. However, empirical findings on the effectiveness of such approaches at the secondary school level remain inconclusive, and little is known about the extent to which learning outcomes are shaped by instructional design as opposed to learners’ affective and cognitive characteristics. This study addresses this gap by investigating the relative influence of instructional approach on students’ understanding of single-photon states, while controlling for prior knowledge, cognitive load, situational interest, and physics self-concept. A quasiexperimental pre-post design was implemented with

                      <a:mi>N</a:mi>
                      <a:mo>=</a:mo>
                      <a:mn>172</a:mn>
                    </a:math>
                    upper secondary students, comparing a qualitative instructional condition with an approach supplemented by a reduced Dirac formalism. Learning outcomes were assessed using the framework of Functional Fidelity and Fidelity of Gestalt. A multivariate analysis of covariance, followed by univariate analyses of covariance, was conducted to examine the contributions of instructional and learner-related variables. The findings indicate that affective variables emerge as strong predictors of functional understanding and suggest that learning in quantum physics is driven less by instructional format than by learners’ affective and cognitive prerequisites. In particular, fostering interest appears to be a key mechanism for supporting the development of functional understanding. The results highlight the importance of integrating affective dimensions into instructional design and provide a basis for future research on the interaction between instructional approaches and learner characteristics in quantum physics education.

title: Retracting Attention
container-title: Seeing and Subjectivity
3a0cc0cdb516ebbc09d01859d15f1425d1efc074.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Further insight is at hand in a text Bhattacharyya does not discuss, but might have, Manu’s Code Law. Here we find a description of the lived experience of the wandering ascetic (yati), depicted as consisting in a state of ambient perceptual awareness; the experience of the ascetic is one of full attentional retraction. When Kalidas Bhattacharyya writes that ‘negative attention [is] a sort of concentrated withdrawal from, rather than positive fixation of, the content whose truth is sought to be discovered’, it is negative attention as attentional retraction that he has in mind, rather than either as absential attention or apophatic attention. The ascetic’s ambient awareness consists of a field of purely marginal consciousness, and it is here alone, Gurwitsch insists, that the sense of self (the dative of presentation) is to be found.</jats:p>

title: CL-GGD: Cross-layer Semantic Geometry Distillation for Lightweight Text Embedding Reconstruction
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
c056e1f76834c570bfad1b62f317100538dd3eb1.abstract: <jats:p>Lightweight sentence embedding models are critical for large-scale retrieval and semantic matching, yet aggressive compression often disrupts the semantic geometry learned by powerful teachers. Existing distillation methods primarily rely on point-wise feature matching or task-specific supervision, which fails to preserve fine-grained relational structure across samples. In this work, we propose Cross-layer Gram Geometry Distillation, a geometry-centric framework that transfers semantic structure by aligning pairwise similarity relations across teacher and student layers. By projecting multi-layer representations into a unified hyperspherical space and matching their Gram matrices under a cross-layer weighting mechanism, the student is optimized to reconstruct the teacher’s neighborhood geometry. An additional covariance regularizer is introduced to mitigate representation collapse and anisotropy. Extensive experiments on sentence embedding benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing distillation baselines under strict parameter and latency constraints. Theoretical analysis further establishes that minimizing Gram discrepancy yields explicit guarantees on nearest-neighbor preservation, providing a principled foundation for retrieval-oriented lightweight embedding reconstruction.</jats:p>

title: PGP-FD: A Lightweight Phase-Guided Generative Graph Process for Resource-Efficient Edge Fault Pattern Recognition in Fire-Protection Valve Sensing Systems
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
e8c77c8dfb0acb232d4d72b81bf0990419bebb53.abstract: <jats:p>Edge fire-protection sensing systems must recognize latent valve faults under limited computation, memory, and energy budgets, although fault samples are scarce and operational responses are strongly phase-dependent. This paper proposes PGP-FD, a lightweight phase-guided generative graph process for event-driven edge fault pattern recognition. Each valve operation or inspection is represented as a compact response window. A depthwise temporal encoder captures local dynamics, a monotonic phase gate models the ordered evolution of standby, actuation, transient, recovery, and settling phases, and a compact measurement graph learns hydraulic-mechanical coupling among pressure, valve motion, and event context. To reduce class imbalance, a fault-conditioned stochastic process generates rare events during training under range, phase-order, and valve-pressure consistency constraints. The training-only posterior and offline synthesis branches are removed during deployment, while confidence-uncertainty prefix inference avoids unnecessary continuous computation and retains full processing for difficult cases. Experiments on real fire-protection valve data show that PGP-FD improves recognition quality, response speed, and online model compactness over representative baselines. The results demonstrate a practical integration of lightweight pattern recognition and mechanism-consistent generative learning for resource-efficient industrial edge intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Optimized Emergency Sign Language Recognition with Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network for Accurate Gesture Classification
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
3737bdb37c2afdac92e2c8a956436c9b57e10253.abstract: <jats:p>Sign Language Recognition (SLR) plays a significant role in improving communication accessibility for hearing-impaired individuals, particularly in emergency scenarios where fast and reliable gesture interpretation is required. However, emergency Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition remains challenging due to rapid hand movements, visually similar gestures, and complex spatial–temporal relationships among hand components. This study proposes an SLR-HIE-LKAGCN framework that integrates topology-aware spatial representation, spatial–temporal feature learning, graph-based gesture modeling, and optimization-based parameter adaptation for emergency ISL recognition. Initially, input gesture frames are processed using a Simplicial Convolutional Filter (SCF) to preserve higher-order spatial relationships among hand regions and enhance gesture representation. The refined gesture sequences are then provided to a Spatial–Temporal Knowledge-Embedded Transformer (STKET) to capture temporal dependencies and contextual movement patterns. The extracted features are further analyzed employing a Large-Kernel Attention Graph Convolutional Network (LKAGCN), which models relationships among hand landmarks and learns discriminative gesture representations. In addition, the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA) is employed to optimize critical network parameters and improve model convergence. The proposed framework is evaluated on emergency ISL gesture categories, including accident, call, doctor, help, hot, lose, pain, and thief. Experimental outcomes establish that the proposed technique achieves superior recognition performance with 98.82% accuracy, 98.57% precision, and 98.53% F1-score, outperforming existing approaches. The obtained results indicate that SLR-HIE-LKAGCN provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for real-time emergency ISL recognition.</jats:p>

title: Time-Series Load Prediction and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient-Based Task Scheduling Optimization for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Networks
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
4426ee3d8d3e458e60b0b22081da6f21626d3046.abstract: <jats:p>Cloud-edge collaborative networks have become an important computing paradigm for latency-sensitive and resource-intensive applications, but dynamic workload variation makes efficient task scheduling difficult. Existing scheduling methods often rely on current system states and cannot proactively respond to future load fluctuations, leading to congestion, delayed execution, and unbalanced resource utilization. This paper proposes PL-DDPG, a prediction-enhanced load-aware deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm for cloud-edge task scheduling. The method first predicts multi-horizon edge load trajectories from historical workload sequences, then integrates predicted loads, current observations, task features, and prediction residuals into an augmented reinforcement learning state. A deterministic actor–critic scheduler generates continuous task assignment, CPU allocation, and bandwidth allocation decisions, while a feasibility projection layer and risk-aware reward improve constraint satisfaction and service reliability. Experiments on four public workload datasets show that PL-DDPG consistently improves delay, energy efficiency, SLA satisfaction, load balancing, and scheduling stability. These results demonstrate that prediction-enhanced continuous control provides an effective solution for proactive cloud-edge resource orchestration.</jats:p>

title: ATT-SV2-ES Net: Hybrid Deep Learning Features and Lightweight Attention-Based Model for Early Glaucoma Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
bc275378bb5009d7f256155d09bb39b3c0bf9888.abstract: <jats:p>Glaucoma is one of the main causes of permanent blindness. Timely intervention is ensured by its early and precise identification. This paper proposes a new hybrid approach, integrating handcrafted features with Deep Learning (DL), for reliable glaucoma identification and prediction on the G1020 dataset. Initially, pre-processing is conducted, which includes data augmentation to increase the diversity of images, Gaussian filtering to reduce image noise, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to enhance local retinal contrast and then grayscale conversion to simplify retinal image representation. After pre-processing, the enhanced images were given to Depthwise Dilated Spatial Attention Mechanism (DDSAM)-based Glau-SegNet for optic disk (OD) and optic cup (OC) segmentation. From the segmented images, handcrafted features, such as Local Binary Patterns (LBPs) and fractal analysis, which describe complementary texture and structural information, are extracted. In parallel, the segmented images are processed by the Attention ShuffleNet V2 with Echo State Network (Att-SV2-ES Net) to obtain high-level deep feature representations. Then these deep features and handcrafted features are concatenated and fed to a fully connected layer with sigmoid activation to classify into the class for the prediction of glaucoma. This combined approach achieves a balance between high accuracy and scalability, addressing the growing need for accessible and reliable glaucoma screening solutions. The experimental results demonstrate the proposed system’s superior performance in detecting and predicting glaucoma. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the proposed model, which integrates DL features, outperforms all other models in terms of key performance metrics, including achieving 99.32% specificity, 99.43% sensitivity, and 99.37% accuracy.</jats:p>

title: Toward Lightweight Fine-Tuning of YOLO via Guided Optimization for Cross-Domain Remote Sensing Object Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
5932f2f56a4def2ac4f225db5167f427ca7ef859.abstract: <jats:p>Deep learning has advanced remote sensing object detection, yet prevailing detectors are tailored to individual datasets, generalize poorly across domains, and rely on large labeled corpora and heavy computation ill-suited to on-device platforms. This paper presents RMoE-YOLO, a lightweight fine-tuning framework that adapts a pretrained YOLOv8n detector to new remote sensing domains under tight label and compute budgets. Its core component is an object-oriented mixture-of-experts (OMoE) module placed before the detection head, where lightweight expert subnetworks learn object-category-conditioned representations and an image-level gating network selects the most relevant experts for each input. A saliency-aware sparsity term and a phased hierarchical fine-tuning schedule guide the adaptation, balancing retention of pretrained knowledge against adaptation to the target domain. On NWPU-VHR-10, RSOD, and SIMD, together with cross-domain transfer, RMoE-YOLO improves low-label cross-domain detection while remaining efficient. Under a controlled multi-seed protocol on a 5% label single-class adaptation setting, its multi-expert configuration significantly outperforms the YOLOv8n baseline by 1.7[Formula: see text]mAP[Formula: see text] points ([Formula: see text]), while its single-expert configuration matches the baseline accuracy at only 19.5 active GFLOPs, below YOLOv8n, and a comparable frame rate. RMoE-YOLO offers a practical route to accurate, generalizable, and efficient detection in low-resource remote sensing.</jats:p>

title: An Enhanced RT-DETR with Selective Boundary Aggregation and Tri-Focal CIoU Loss for Real-Time Object Detection
container-title: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
8fe4d107db20a206822cedf0a8fc129f1135e150.abstract: <jats:p>Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) is the first detection transformer-based model to achieve real-time performance. However, the concatenation operation treats all scale features equally without adaptive weighting, leading to insufficient multi-scale feature fusion. In addition, Generalized Intersection over Union (GIoU) does not explicitly consider the center distance and aspect ratio between the predicted bounding boxes and the ground-truth boxes, leading to slow convergence. To address the above problems, this paper proposes Tri-Focal DEtection TRansformer (TriDETR) by replacing the GIoU loss function with the Tri-Focal Complete Intersection over Union (CIoU) loss to optimize overlap and assign weights, allowing the model to focus on difficult patterns. Additionally, TriDETR uses Selective Boundary Aggregation (SBA) to better fuse multi-scale features. Experiments were conducted on PASCAL VOC 2007, Foggy Cityscapes, and ACDC datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Specifically, in terms of [Formula: see text], TriDETR outperforms RT-DETR with the same backbone by 0.80-0.98 on PASCAL VOC, 0.20-1.23 on Foggy Cityscapes, and 0.30–0.95 on ACDC (snow, rain, and nighttime). Additionally, TriDETR outperforms the best-performing YOLO26 variant while maintaining approximately the same frames per second.</jats:p>

title: Design and Validation of a Novel Planar 2R1T Remote Center-of-Motion Mechanism Composing of Dual-Triangular and Straight-Line Linkages
container-title: Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics
caf43fb798aa694f48d6f5c32707dcb9a24ad400.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Benefiting from small incision and fast recovery, minimally invasive surgeries (MIS) exhibit great advantages in clinical operations. In such kind of surgeries, the remote center-of-motion (RCM) mechanisms play an important role owing to their special motion characteristics. This paper presents the design of a novel planar RCM mechanism of two rotational and one translational degrees-of-freedom (DOF). In the proposed design, the mobility of RCM mechanism is decomposed into one-DOF pure rotation and translation with a remote stationary point. The dual-triangular linkage and the Peaucellier–Lipkin straight-line linkage are introduced to achieve the remote rotation and translation, respectively. Inspired by the concept of virtual screw, a dual-helical differential-motion joint is particularly designed to generate the coaxial rotation and translation. A preliminary prototype is developed to validate the feasibility of the designed RCM mechanism. The experimental results show that the developed prototype is easy to control and of acceptable positioning accuracy, which manifests potential application in MIS.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

Entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills, and self-esteem in students participating in sports programmes in Colombia
container-title: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
7487e0e532b00ca3a9d308c88e1fc9fc09e90f2f.abstract:
<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

title: VHMP: A High-efficacy and Parallel Processing Approach for CGRCA Supporting Virtual Heterogeneous Multi-core and Intra-core Multitask Pipeline
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
6069641410fbf34886a36b583f52e136660d22c8.abstract: <jats:p>The performance enhancements of coarse-grain reconfigurable cryptographic arrays (CGRCAs) through technology upgrades and increasing chip size are approaching limits. Enhancing parallel processing capabilities can relieve the computational burden on CGRCA in high-density computing scenarios. Specifically, a novel parallel processing approach is introduced in this article, named virtual heterogeneous multi-core pipelining (VHMP). VHMP supports virtual heterogeneous multi-core and intra-core multitask pipelining. Informed by hardware virtualization principles and analysis of CGRCA architectures, VHMP constructs virtual computing cores (VCCs) on CGRCA using multi-launch pipelines and implements multitask interleave pipelines within each VCC, enabling parallel processing at pipeline, task, and instruction levels. Furthermore, a hierarchical control mechanism is embedded within VHMP, integrating virtual computing path level and task-level management. This control mechanism allows diverse cryptographic algorithms to run concurrently without being bound to specific types or modes. Finally, applying VHMP to a 32 × 4 CGRCA, 32 heterogeneous VCCs are instantiated, with each core handling up to 16 interleaved tasks. Compared to treating CGRCA as a homogeneous multi-core processor, the VHMP approach achieves an average acceleration of 4.33 × (up to 6.34 ×) with quadrupled instruction execution capability. Additionally, the control mechanism reduces context volume to 18.7% and boosts configuration speed by 3 ×. Compared with related architectures, VHMP improves CGRCA throughput by an average of 5.3 ×.</jats:p>

title: Graphene-Based Interconnect Exploration for FPGA Design and Optimization Towards the End of the Roadmap
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
e4661457e8c7a67399488d41681b0b4a0b41cb22.abstract: <jats:p>The emerging graphene interconnect technology is expected to be a promising alternative to traditional interconnect technologies due to its superior conductivity. Because of the dominant impact of global routing on the overall performance of a widely used application, the Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), this work investigates the potential advantage of using graphene-based interconnects to replace conventional copper (Cu) for global routing. Furthermore, a scalability analysis is performed, and the effects of technology node scaling from 7 nm to 1.5 nm are evaluated using lateral gate-all-around field-effect transistors (LGAAFETs) within the proposed system-technology co-design (STCO) framework. Key material-level parameters, including the mean free path (MFP), contact resistance, and the number of graphene layers, are systematically analyzed. Benchmark simulations demonstrate that a 32% improvement in the energy-delay product (EDP) is achieved with graphene-based interconnects compared to Cu counterparts at the 7 nm technology node, and an additional 46% reduction is observed at the 1.5 nm technology node. It is important to note that this work is an exploratory STCO study incorporating cross-layer design considerations, with a focus on long-term trends rather than short-term manufacturability.</jats:p>

title: LASM: Extensible Competitive Scheduling Framework for VLIW Assembly Optimization
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
d1804df4679dc580d7bd65e32240c18e9cb9fc7f.abstract: <jats:p>Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architectures deliver compelling performance-energy-cost advantages for automotive, AI, and high-performance computing. However, a persistent performance-productivity gap limits broader adoption: manual assembly optimization achieves superior performance but requires substantial expertise, while automated compilation underperforms. Existing assembly-level optimization tools commit to single scheduling strategies, unable to adapt to diverse program patterns. This article presents LASM, the first symbolic assembly framework enabling competitive multi-strategy orchestration for complete VLIW programs. Rather than committing to a single algorithm, multiple scheduling strategies simultaneously optimize identical code regions, with the framework automatically selecting the top solution through feasibility-driven ranking. LASM features standardized extension interfaces enabling plugin-style strategy integration and unified scheduling primitives eliminating algorithmic redundancy. We contribute two novel strategies: Longevity-Aware Expanded Modulo Scheduling (LAEMS) with dependency relaxation, proactive reordering, and parallel expansion search, and Front-Back Block Fusion (FBBF) for cross-boundary scheduling. Evaluation on 13 benchmarks across two production VLIW-SIMD processors demonstrates LASM achieves 103.6% and 101.6% of expert assembly performance while reducing manual code by 72.6%. A full YOLOv5 deployment validates production applicability at 95.9% of expert performance. Code is available at https://github.com/urays/lasm.</jats:p>

title: PolarGate: Breaking the Functionality Representation Bottleneck of And-Inverter Graph Neural Network
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
0aa9885c6dd1a82ee1b521ebf2ec7bff9bf19fb8.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the functionality of Boolean networks is crucial for processes such as functional equivalence checking, logic synthesis, and malicious logic identification. With the proliferation of deep learning in electronic design automation (EDA), graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used to embed and-inverter graphs (AIGs)—a standard form of Boolean networks—into vectorized representations. A key challenge in applying GNNs for Boolean representation is that although GNNs can effectively encapsulate the structural properties of AIGs, they struggle to efficiently capture Boolean logic functionality. In this work, we focus on breaking this bottleneck by enhancing the functional representation capability of GNNs, proposing PolarGate, an efficient solution that not only aligns message passing with AIG logical functionality but also effectively integrates global information. Leveraging the intrinsic ambipolar states (0 and 1) of AIG nodes, PolarGate maps gate behavior into an ambipolar state space, customizes differentiable logical operators, and designs a functionality-aware message passing strategy. To further capture global circuit information, PolarGate integrates a structure-aware preprocessing module and a global linear attention module, transcending the locality constraint of message passing. Experimental results on two functionality-related basic tasks (signal probability prediction and truth-table distance prediction) and a downstream task (logic equivalence prediction) show that PolarGate outperform state-of-the-art GNN-based methods.</jats:p>

title: ODCGate: Leveraging Observability Don’t Care Conditions for Enhanced Power Efficiency in Clock Gating
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
9cab47548290de0fcb0e5c4f5470bbe3c4f9a5e9.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Clock gating reduces dynamic power by integrating activation functions and integrated clock gating (ICG) cells into the clock path, selectively disabling the clock signal to register when unnecessary.
