title: Three-dimensional source localization of natural gas leakage using an experimentally-calibrated Gaussian plume model and enhanced particle swarm optimization
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
d03f299a7fb3fcb50ffc6e358abbcaf71cb3d553.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To address the challenges associated with the three-dimensional source localization of surface natural gas micro-leakages, this study proposes a novel three-dimensional localization method that integrates an experimentally-calibrated Gaussian plume model with an enhanced particle swarm optimization algorithm (EGPM-EPSO). The proposed method was evaluated systematically through controlled test-rig experiments, followed by preliminary field demonstration. A well-conditioned experimental platform was first designed to quantitatively characterize the spatial distribution of the leaked gas concentrations using tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy. A plume rise impact factor was introduced to describe the coupled effect of the leakage rate and wind speed, based on which an exponential saturation model for the plume rise height was developed. An EGPM was established by further deriving the lateral and vertical diffusion parameters using experimental data. Compared to traditional models, the EGPM substantially improved the concentration prediction accuracy, reducing the average relative error to 1.65%. The EGPM was then integrated with an EPSO algorithm incorporating several strategic improvements, achieving a mean localization error of 0.0084 m on the experimental platform. Additionally, field testing for natural gas leakage was conducted via a vehicle-mounted mobile monitoring system. The results indicate that the proposed three-dimensional localization method can accurately identify the leakage source with a total localization error of 3.1 m. The measurement-driven inversion framework establishes a robust foundation for the safety monitoring and emergency response of gas pipeline leakages.</jats:p>

title: Cross-database generalization of a single-feature threshold model for congestive heart failure detection from short-term heart rate variability
container-title: Physiological Measurement
5c9583b6bf29c4f3dc894e70421e869426aacc0c.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Objective.</jats:italic>
                    To evaluate the transferability of interpretable single-feature threshold models across the five evaluated databases for congestive heart failure (CHF) detection from short-term heart rate variability (HRV), and to compare their performance with optimized multi-feature classifiers.
                    <jats:italic>Approach.</jats:italic>
                    Twenty HRV features from 60 s inter-beat interval windows in five databases were evaluated using leave-one-database-pair-out nested cross-validation with six outer-test sets and their corresponding outer-development sets. Within each outer-development set, directions and thresholds were fitted on inner-train sets, and features were selected according to mean inner-validation
                    <jats:italic>F</jats:italic>
                    1 score. The selected model was refitted on the complete outer-development set. The most frequently selected feature was further evaluated across the six outer-test sets with separately fitted directions and thresholds. Eight multi-feature classifiers were optimized and evaluated using the same data splits. Performance was assessed using record-balanced window-level metrics and database-stratified recording-level bootstrap confidence intervals.
                    <jats:italic>Main results.</jats:italic>
                    The short-term detrended fluctuation analysis scaling exponent (f14) was selected most frequently. The f14 threshold model achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.881 ± 0.038),
                    <jats:italic>F</jats:italic>
                    1 score (0.718 ± 0.079), and sensitivity among the evaluated single-feature and multi-feature models. Among the eight multi-feature classifiers, Random Forest achieved the highest mean test AUC (0.858 ± 0.067).
                    <jats:italic>Significance</jats:italic>
                    . An interpretable single-feature threshold model showed strong CHF–normal sinus rhythm discrimination in the five evaluated databases. f14 was the strongest candidate in this evaluation, although its thresholds varied across outer-development sets and its clinical specificity requires further validation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Dysregulated splenic glucocorticoid sensitivity in aging and an a-synuclein transgenic mouse model of Parkinson’s disease
container-title: Neuroimmunomodulation
39f466965511191eee8538a6dca02227d313edb6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Introduction: Parkinson's disease (PD) and aging both disrupt hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis function and peripheral immune homeostasis. Whether aging or α-synuclein (α-syn) pathology alters glucocorticoid (GC) sensitivity of peripheral immune cells has not been investigated. Methods: Using an ex vivo GC sensitivity assay, we assessed the responsiveness of isolated and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated splenocytes to the anti-inflammatory effects of increasing doses of corticosterone (CORT) in a wild-type (WT) aging cohort and in a PD α-syn transgenic mouse model and respective age-matched controls. Results: Compared with splenocytes from 6-month-old WT mice, splenocytes from 20-month-old WT mice were less sensitive to 0.1 and 0.5 µM CORT. Isolated splenocytes from PD vs. control mice were less sensitive to 0.05, 0.1, and 0.5 µM CORT specifically at 16 months of age, but not at 6 or 20 months of age. As peripheral immune phenotyping revealed neither differences in HPA axis-related parameters nor in splenic GC receptor expression between PD and age-matched control mice, splenic GC resistance in PD mice at 16 months of age seems to be mediated by downstream GR signaling dysfunction. Conclusion: Together, our results support the hypothesis that α-syn pathology accelerates an aging-associated decline in the peripheral sensitivity to anti-inflammatory GCs and may thereby sustain systemic and neuroinflammatory processes in PD.</jats:p>

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram Predictive Model for Postoperative Complications After Laparoscopic Partial Nephrectomy by Combining RENAL Score, MAP Score and Preoperative Baseline Characteristics
container-title: Urologia Internationalis
1358faadfe81a51635934fc8c708a059e5a16ac2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Introduction: To investigate the predictive value of integrating tumor anatomical characteristics (RENAL score, MAP score), preoperative baseline conditions and perioperative indicators for postoperative complications of laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN), and to construct a predictive nomogram model. Methods: Clinical data of patients with renal tumors who underwent LPN at our hospital from 2020 to 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Demographic characteristics, tumor imaging parameters (RENAL and MAP scores), preoperative laboratory examinations and intraoperative indicators were collected. Postoperative Clavien-Dindo grade ≥Ⅱ complications were set as the endpoint. Independent risk factors were screened by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses to construct a nomogram. The discrimination, calibration and clinical benefit of the model were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: A total of 473 eligible patients were enrolled. Multivariate analysis showed that E score (exophytic rate), P score (perirenal fat thickness), ASA classification, hemoglobin level, and warm ischemia time were independent risk factors for postoperative complications (P&lt;0.05). The nomogram model based on the above factors exhibited excellent predictive performance in both the training cohort and internal validation cohort, with AUCs of 0.95 and 0.93, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the RENAL score alone (AUC=0.79), MAP score alone (AUC=0.68) and their simple combination. Calibration curves revealed high consistency between predicted and actual probabilities, and DCA confirmed significant net clinical benefit of the model. Conclusion: The integrated model constructed in this study allows comprehensive and accurate assessment of the risk of postoperative complications following LPN, with significantly superior predictive performance compared with traditional scoring systems. It helps clinicians identify high-risk patients preoperatively, optimize surgical strategies and perioperative management, and thus improve patient prognosis.</jats:p>

title: Comparing LLM automated grading with IELTS writing essays: evidence from rubric prompting and model stability
container-title: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education
01bd6a41d25d0400d50d6f9b4502b63fdb520d06.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study assesses the extent to which large language models (LLMs) reproduce the IELTS Writing Task 2 band scores assigned by professional IELTS examiners. It also evaluates whether incorporating the official IELTS band descriptors into the grading prompt improves scoring accuracy and agreement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Six LLM routes (GPT-4o, incept5/llama3.1-claude, Gemma 3, Aya, deepseek-local and deepseek-remote) graded a stratified 100-essay subset from a public IELTS benchmark containing dataset-provided band labels. Each essay was graded 10 times under No Rubrics (NR) and With Rubrics (WR). Scores were treated as single-label multi-class ordinal classifications over the 4.0–9.0 half-band scale and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, grading gaps, directional bias and run-to-run stability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Rubric guidance improved average performance and most model-level classification metrics, with cross-model mean gains of 8.8% in accuracy, 14.9% in precision, 23.2% in recall and 18.7% in F1-score. Within the parseable-response subset, GPT-4o achieved the highest reported accuracy and the strongest agreement with the dataset-provided labels; however, its results rest on a substantially smaller set of valid responses than the other routes, and agreement remained moderate at best. Inter-model agreement was negligible; most models inflated scores, and in this model pool, the local/Ollama routes showed larger gaps and instability. The results do not support unsupervised high-stakes marking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides an applied, risk-aware evaluation protocol for LLM-assisted writing assessment by jointly reporting correctness, agreement, directional bias and run-to-run stability rather than accuracy alone. It supports rubric-anchored, human-in-the-loop LLM use for formative feedback, triage and moderation, not examiner replacement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From records to claims: a model of documentary transformation and evidential accountability
container-title: Journal of Documentation
8da042d658550db46d973aa66f84f4cf6d3e28d3.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This article examines how records are represented as support for documentary claims. It asks what claim-centred appraisal adds to established approaches to records, provenance and argument when different claims rely on the same record complex but make different evidential and corrective demands.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on archival record theory, document theory, cognitive authority, social epistemology, argumentation, provenance and paradata, the article develops a conceptual model. A hypothetical comparison of three claims derived from one record complex illustrates its use and identifies possible empirical tests.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The claim–record configuration joins an assertion to its cited records, transformation history, warrant, backing, responsible roles and derivative versions. The model distinguishes three constitutive operations, two regulatory operations and six accountability relations in three domains. Six propositions concern reconstruction, claim–support fit, claim-type differences, attribution, mediation and correction after reuse.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The versioned claim provides a common unit for examining documentary support, inferential judgment and subsequent repair. The framework distinguishes inspectable claim–record relations from warrant adequacy, allowing claims drawn from the same records to receive different assessments and correction responses. Six propositions enable comparison with established integrated professional practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Optimization of oil production rates under geomechanical stress constraints: a coupled reservoir–geomechanics approach using cascaded artificial neural network surrogates

fa5909b8825dfee9f51e38efc3867c9cf22d0d6b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Geomechanical constraints can limit oil production from deep carbonate reservoirs, because depletion raises the effective stress and, with it, the risk of compaction and rock failure. Enforcing such a limit inside a production optimizer is costly, since every candidate rate schedule produces its own pore-pressure field and one coupled reservoir–geomechanical simulation takes about 3 h. This study develops a cascaded artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate to maximize oil production from the MB21 unit of the Mishrif Formation, Buzurgan Oil Field, while keeping the effective mean stress below 11,200 psi. A Pressure ANN predicts the pore-pressure field from the well rates and geomechanical inputs, and a Stress ANN converts the predicted field into effective mean stress. Unlike single-network stress surrogates, which need pore pressure as a known input, the cascade evaluates the stress constraint for the depletion that each proposed rate schedule would itself cause. The networks were trained on 2,446 high-fidelity CMG-GEM coupled simulations and coupled with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to allocate the rates of 18 producers. On independent test scenarios, the Pressure and Stress ANNs reached coefficients of determination of 0.95 and 0.94. PSO produced 42,799.02 bbl/day against 42,592.96 bbl/day for GA (+ 206.06 bbl/day, 0.48%) and reached a near-optimal solution within about 25 iterations; both algorithms identified Well 8 as the most geomechanically sensitive producer. Re-simulation of the PSO schedule with the original CMG-GEM model over the seven-year horizon delivered the allocated 42,799.02 bbl/day with a maximum effective mean stress of 11,198 psi, and no violations of the 11,200 psi constraint were observed over the 155,540 evaluated spatio-temporal points. With one candidate evaluated in about 0.13 s, a complete optimization run of about 3 × 10
                    <jats:sup>4</jats:sup>
                    evaluations took about 1 h. The cascaded surrogate therefore makes geomechanically constrained rate optimization tractable at field scale, provided the selected schedule is confirmed by a final high-fidelity simulation.
                  </jats:p>

title: The emotional intelligence of a teacher in the conditions of education internationalization: formation features in the process of foreign language training in higher educational institutions
container-title: TRANSDISCIPLINARITY OF MODERN EDUCATION: PHILOSOPHICAL-METHODOLOGICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL-DIDACTIC AND DIGITAL DIMENSIONS
04acbc5fbaa1aa22c5c09aa5cd68ac9e86b0159e.abstract: <jats:p>The section examines the development of future teachers’ emotional intelligence in the process of foreign language training. Its key components, which ensure effective management of one’s own emotions, understanding of students’ emotional states, and the formation of interpersonal skills, are considered. It is established that a high level of emotional intelligence contributes to the professional skills of a teacher, increases the effectiveness of the educational process, the development of communicative and interpersonal skills, stimulates self-reflection, the ability to self-regulation, and conscious pedagogical interaction. Particular attention is paid to the importance of emotional competence in the formation of a humanistically oriented educational environment and supporting the students’ individual development. Modern methods of developing emotional intelligence are analyzed, which contribute to the development of self-awareness, control of emotions and effective interaction with others. It is proven that its formation is a key factor in the preparation of a competent, personally mature and responsible teacher, able to effectively interact with students and colleagues. The analysis of studies on the emotional intelligence development emphasizes the importance of integrating emotional training into modern professional education and training of teachers for the challenges of the educational process in a globalized society.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted tree diameter-at-breast-height measurement
container-title: Measurement Science and Technology
e8f74459fb7b0b4ff902a5dc275359c7c36fcbba.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate diameter-at-breast-height (DBH) measurement is essential for forest inventory and ecological monitoring. This work evaluates two AI-assisted smartphone frameworks: a text-prompt Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) that segments trunks from red-green-blue (RGB) images, and a depth-guided MobileSAM model that uses depth cues to generate geometry-based prompts. The resulting masks are integrated into a geometric pipeline for DBH estimation. The proposed frameworks combine AI-based trunk segmentation with geometry-guided DBH measurement to improve the accuracy, interpretability, and practical efficiency of smartphone-based DBH estimation, with the depth-guided MobileSAM framework enabling near real-time use and the SAM3 for its robustness and accuracy despite of the high computational power requirement.&#xD;Both methods were tested on 202 planted and 285 natural trees. In planted forests, both achieved high accuracy with no failures (root mean square error, RMSE: 1.2 cm for SAM3, 1.1 cm for MobileSAM). In natural forests, SAM3 remained robust (1.7 cm RMSE), while MobileSAM failed in four cases and showed lower accuracy (2.4 cm RMSE excluding failures).&#xD;MobileSAM runs in ~0.89 s per image on a smartphone, enabling near real-time use. SAM3 is much slower on CPU (~160 s on 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1260P) but can be accelerated on GPUs (0.13 s on A100, 3.71 s on T4). Overall, MobileSAM is more practical for on-device deployment, while SAM3 offers greater robustness in complex environments but requires high-performance hardware.</jats:p>

title: Optimization of artificial neural network models using genetic algorithm for accurate estimation of water saturation

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Accurate estimation of water saturation (
                    <jats:italic>S</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>w</jats:sub>
                    ) is a critical task in reservoir engineering, as it directly influences reservoir characterization, hydrocarbon volume estimation, and decision‐making in field development. Traditional empirical and deterministic models often fail to provide the required accuracy due to the nonlinear and complex relationships between petrophysical parameters. To address this challenge, this study investigates the application of advanced artificial neural network (ANN) models optimized by genetic algorithm (GA) for
                    <jats:italic>S</jats:italic>

                    prediction. A total of 42 924 data samples were collected from well log records, containing 13 petrophysical input parameters: depth, total porosity (PHIT), hydrocarbon total neutron porosity (HTNP), true formation resistivity (RT), flushed zone resistivity (RXO), computed gamma ray (CGR), spectral gamma ray (SGR), hole caliper (HCAL), compressional slowness (DTCO), photoelectric factor (PEFZ), Bulk density (RHOZ), Gamma ray density (RHGA), and temperature. To enhance data quality, 14.5% of the samples identified as outliers using a Gaussian distribution‐based method (the 3‐sigma rule) were removed. Five ANN architectures—convolutional neural network (CNN), recurrent neural network (RNN), feedforward neural network (FNN), multi‐layer perceptron (MLP), and radial basis function network (RBFN)—were developed. GA was used to optimize the hyperparameters of each model. Model performance was evaluated using coefficient of determination (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    ) values for training, validation, and test datasets, while prediction errors were assessed using mean absolute error (
                    <jats:italic>MAE</jats:italic>

                    ), and root mean squared error (
                    <jats:italic>RMSE</jats:italic>
                    ). Among all models, CNN achieved the best results, with
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    values of 0.9843 (train), 0.9645 (validation), and 0.9637 (test), and
                    <jats:italic>RMSE</jats:italic>
                    of 0.0019 (train) and 0.0029 (test). These results confirm the effectiveness of CNN with GA optimization in capturing complex relationships within petrophysical data for accurate
                    <jats:italic>S</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>w</jats:sub>
                    prediction.

title: Titin‐Mimetic Phase Separation Enables a High‐Performance Dielectric Elastomer for Artificial Muscles

ed33559ec6033b89c0026dcc873c626d460652ce.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Dielectric elastomers (DEs) are promising candidates for soft robots to achieve efficient electromechanical conversion and lightweight integration. However, conventional homogeneous DE networks face multiple inherent contradictions among compliance, robustness, and dielectric performance due to the lack of differentiated structural design at the molecular scale. Inspired by the hierarchical responsiveness of titin, we present a phase‐separated fluorinated polyacrylate DE that achieves synergistic optimization of electrical and mechanical properties while exhibiting excellent self‐healing capability. The proposed elastomer achieves a maximum actuation strain of 235% and an ultrahigh specific energy density of 386 J kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    approximately 9.65 times that of natural muscle. As such, our work demonstrates a remarkably comprehensive performance among contemporary advancements. We further demonstrate a biomimetic swimming robot that achieves efficient aquatic locomotion, highlighting the potential of our DE as a suitable candidate for high‐performance artificial muscle.
                  </jats:p>

title: Pathways for Enhancing Faculty Members’ Practical Teaching Competence at Application-Oriented Universities through Artificial Intelligence
container-title: World Journal of Educational Research
a22ec319e1846e03b63961cd6d734ca1dbc387f8.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing higher education at a remarkable pace, and it has created new conditions for strengthening the practical teaching competence of young faculty members. Taking Hankou University as the case and drawing on the literature as well as publicly available institutional information, this study examines why AI-enabled practical teaching is valuable for young teachers and where the main barriers lie. Four stand out: misconceptions about professional roles, insufficient digital competence, inadequate institutional incentives, and superficial industry–education collaboration. The study then builds a multidimensional framework for AI-enabled professional development in practical teaching, organized around three interconnected pathways—cultivating digital literacy, transforming teaching paradigms through the integration of virtual and physical environments, and redesigning evaluation systems with data intelligence. How these pathways reinforce the faculty capacity needed for the dynamic adjustment of academic programs at local application-oriented universities amid industrial upgrading is also discussed. The aim is to provide a theoretical reference and practical insights for the high-quality, substantively driven development of comparable application-oriented undergraduate institutions.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in English for Specific Purposes Instruction: A Systematic Review of Trends, Outcomes, and Challenges (2022–2025)
container-title: Journal of Language Teaching and Research
b50db2080539b888b02a565d02bce37abcadc584.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence integration in English for Specific Purposes education since 2022 demands a thorough analysis of new developments, educational results, and implementation barriers. An evaluation of AI usage in ESP teaching and learning through 70 peer-reviewed empirical studies published during January 2022 to March 2025 forms this systematic review. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 70 studies were selected. Research shows that large language models, including ChatGPT, GPT-3, and GPT-4, appeared in 46% of the analyzed studies. Grammar correction programs, adaptive learning platforms, and automated assessment solutions were among the tools currently used by educators at a rate of 21%, 18%, and 15%, respectively. Business English (37%) was the most popular domain, followed by English for Medical Purposes (22%), English for Engineering (21%), and Technical English (Engineering and IT) (20%). The analyzed research papers revealed positive learner outcomes in 82% of the studies, particularly in core language skills. The research findings also revealed issues with teacher training, ethical concerns, and limitations in accessing AI technology, as mentioned by 18% of the analyzed studies. The review demonstrates how AI integration in ESP instruction has brought about transformative changes, but these changes vary in their implementation. It underscores the importance of context-aware deployment, robust educator support, and longitudinal evaluations to ensure sustained impact. The findings in this research guide upcoming investigations while providing direct, implementable knowledge for educators who wish to utilize AI for teaching specialized languages.</jats:p>

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Analyze Linguistic Features in Literary Texts and Its Application in the Teaching Process
container-title: Journal of Language Teaching and Research
452acca86c224fd958d87f32481d0bf564d80e1c.abstract: <jats:p>This article explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies for analyzing linguistic features in literary texts and their application in the teaching process. To achieve this objective, two novels–The Last Duty by A. Nurpeisov and Zharmak by M. Magauin–are selected as primary materials, and the methods and advantages of their analysis using AI tools are demonstrated. Traditional literary language analysis is typically based on manual interpretation and experience-driven judgment, which leads to several limitations such as low efficiency, high subjectivity, insufficient quantitative assessment, and limited scalability. Modern AI-based approaches–including natural language processing, language models, and knowledge graphs–help address these challenges. These technologies enable the accurate identification of linguistic features in literary texts, their quantitative evaluation, visualization, and comparative analysis. The article systematically examines the technical foundations and analytical criteria of AI in literary language analysis. Based on teaching experience, an AI-supported learning model is proposed, consisting of the stages: “before the lesson – during the lesson – after the lesson – assessment.” The findings indicate that AI significantly enhances both accuracy and interactivity in teaching language and literature. At the same time, it is essential to maintain a humanistic perspective, clearly define the boundaries of AI use, and minimize risks related to technological dependency and data ethics. Ultimately, a balance can be achieved between technological capabilities and the development of literary competence.</jats:p>

title: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) in Nigeria: Empirical Analysis of Personality traits, Emotional intelligence and Gender as Determinants.

db22bd6539e265ed987f56bbb1d5839a2ce7ffa4.abstract:
<jats:p>This study investigated the Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) in Nigeria: Empirical Analysis of
Personality traits, Emotional intelligence and Gender as Determinants. The current study
adopted a cross-sectional survey research design and a random sampling technique to select
eighty-five (85) consisting 43 (50.58%) female and 42 (49.41%) male married adolescents.
Their age ranges from 21-41 years, as well as an estimated 56.4% from polygamous family,
and 44.6% from monogamous family. On their educational qualification, 7(8.4%) of the
respondents had SSCE, 46 (55.4%) had ND/NCE, 25(29.4%) had BSC, while 7(8.2%) had
postgraduate qualification. Participants completed the intimate partner violence, emotional
intelligence, and personality traits scales as study’s means of data collection. Three hypotheses
are tested at 0.05 level of significance, and results following multiple regression analysis
showed that personality traits jointly (R2 = .483; F (5, 58) = 10.824; p< .000) predicted
intimate partner violence. On the independent basis, agreeableness (β = -.356, t = -2.864; p<
.006), neuroticism (β = .245, t = 2.393; p< .020), openness to experience (β = -.010, t = -
3.012; p<.008) and extraversion (β = -.524, t = -5.604; p< .001) independently predicted
intimate partner (IPV) violence. While, conscientiousness (β = -.162, t = 1.271; p > .209) did
not significantly predict IPV. In addition, emotional intelligence did not significantly predict (β
= -.289, t = -2.374; p > .021) IPV. Lastly, result revealed a significant gender difference [t (65)
= 1.260; p < .212] in intimate partner (IPV) among Married Adolescents in Lagos, Nigeria.
The study recommended that developing and expanding counseling programs for individuals

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Transformative Potential, Implementation Challenges, and Future Trajectories
container-title: Journal of Research in Engineering and Computer Sciences
4f57fb5aa53ffc9a9ad9de6e928127777efd4d6e.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into educational systems has accelerated dramatically, transitioning from experimental pilot programs to mainstream pedagogical practice by 2026. This paper examines the current landscape of AI in education through quantitative analysis of global adoption data, stakeholder perceptions, and performance outcomes. Drawing on surveys from over 3,800 students across 16 countries, institutional reports, and longitudinal studies, we find that 86% of higher education students now utilize AI tools. In contrast, 60% of teachers have integrated AI into their teaching practice. The global AI education market is projected to reach $112.03 billion by 2034, reflecting a compound annual growth rate of approximately 38%. However, significant challenges persist: 65% of educators’ express concern about plagiarism, 71% of K-12 teachers lack formal AI training, and only 7% of schools worldwide have established AI usage guidance. This paper synthesizes current evidence, identifies critical implementation barriers, and proposes a framework for responsible AI integration that preserves human-centric pedagogy while leveraging technological affordances.</jats:p>

title: A Graph-Based Ontology for Automotive Cyber Threat Intelligence Integration and TARA Evidence Retrieval
container-title: Information
ca898c24b51d097860ee964555b705b7a2738948.abstract: <jats:p>Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) in automotive cybersecurity requires connecting cyber threat intelligence (CTI) with the architecture and technical context of the system under evaluation. However, relevant evidence is dispersed across heterogeneous repositories whose records do not directly establish automotive applicability or correspondence with regulatory threat categories. This paper presents an OWL 2 DL ontology linking structured CTI with automotive system concepts, selected ISO/SAE 21434 TARA concepts, UN Regulation No. 155 threat categories, and STRIDE classifications. A Neo4j implementation combines deterministic ingestion of CAPEC, CWE, and CVE/NVD records and their explicit cross-references with large-language-model-assisted candidate annotations for automotive relevance and contextual classification. Evaluation comprises ontology consistency checking with HermiT, competency-question assessment, and comparison with a human-curated automotive reference. HermiT reported no inconsistency or unsatisfiable classes. Of the 59 CAPEC Meta patterns in the reference, the evaluated output selected 52 as automotive-relevant (88.1%); label overlap was highest for technology domain (50/59) and STRIDE (49/59) and lowest for UN R155 threat categories (27/59). A headlamp proof of concept demonstrates node-centric retrieval of candidate regulatory threats, attack patterns, weaknesses, and vulnerabilities. The framework provides a semantic foundation for traceable TARA evidence preparation; product-specific applicability assessment and complete attack-path and risk analysis remain outside the demonstrated scope.</jats:p>

title: University Students’ Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Enhancing Emotional Intelligence Skills: A Descriptive Survey at Yarmouk University
container-title: European Journal of Educational Research
e792c02fd3592770d9de359eee71145abea4e309.abstract: <jats:p>This study employed a descriptive survey to investigate Yarmouk University students’ perceptions of AI as a tool for enhancing five specific EI skills. A self-administered questionnaire comprising 25 items was completed by a convenience sample of 384 students across five domains: AI’s role in stimulating motivation, developing social skills, developing self-awareness, developing empathy, and developing self-regulation. Both validity and reliability were established. Findings indicate that students perceived AI as moderately useful across all domains (overall M = 2.83, SD = 0.63). Statistically significant differences at α = 0.05 were found in all five domains based on gender, favoring males, though effect sizes were small (partial η² = 0.01-0.03). No statistically significant differences were found by college type. Although a significant multivariate effect emerged for academic level, none of the individual EI domains showed a statistically significant univariate difference. The results suggest that AI has emerged as a supplementary tool for developing aspects of EI among students, though its perceived effectiveness remains moderate. Implications for integrating AI into higher education to support emotional development.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Digital Heritage Reconstruction and Smart Design System
container-title: Journal of Cases on Information Technology
c747f65970ccd164a91fa9fc30e7a1949cf07919.abstract: To solve poor semantic consistency and algorithm-manufacturing disconnection in intangible cultural heritage pattern digitalization, this paper proposes a semantic-preserving model with dual-loop mapping. Based on 212 high-definition scans of Sichuan brocade and Qinghai pile embroidery, a dual-loop platform with a four-layer semantic tag system was constructed. A style generative adversarial network version 3 and vector quantized variational auto encoder fusion network with multi-scale semantic loss suppresses style drift, and the dual-domain guided projection algorithm ensures adaptability on complex surfaces. Experiments show the four-layer tag reduces the final Fréchet inception distance to 13.2. Dual-domain guided projection achieves 2.7% stretching rate, less than 0.27 mm deformation error, 37 s modeling time, and 97.9% one-time 3D printing success rate. User satisfaction shows an improvement of 7.9 points compared with Scheme B (p < 0.01). This work fills the “generation-mapping-manufacturing” gap for intangible cultural heritage pattern digitalization.

title: Sistem Rekomendasi Kenaikan Golongan Guru SD Menggunakan Analytical Hierarchy Process dan Artificial Neural Network
container-title: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
37ff3ce8fafb5dd9a30688cf85c9be478b58e28e.abstract: <jats:p>Kenaikan golongan guru melibatkan banyak kriteria, seperti masa di golongan, angka kredit, karya ilmiah, pendidikan, dan penilaian kinerja. Penilaian yang masih dilakukan secara manual berpotensi subjektif, tidak konsisten, dan memakan waktu. Penelitian ini membangun sistem rekomendasi kelayakan kenaikan golongan guru SD berbasis web dengan studi kasus SD Negeri 98 Kendari. Metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) digunakan untuk membobotkan enam kriteria dan menyusun peringkat guru, sedangkan Artificial Neural Network (ANN) berarsitektur 6-12-1 dilatih dengan backpropagation untuk menghitung probabilitas kelayakan. Pengembangan sistem mengikuti Rational Unified Process (RUP). Hasil pengujian menunjukkan matriks AHP konsisten (CR = 0,0109) dengan angka kredit sebagai kriteria berbobot tertinggi (0,2433). ANN mencapai akurasi 98,20% pada data latih dan 97,40% pada data uji. Guru dinyatakan Layak jika seluruh syarat wajib terpenuhi dan probabilitas ANN minimal 50%. Data latih ANN dibangkitkan dari aturan syarat kenaikan pangkat, sehingga akurasi tersebut belum menggambarkan keputusan kenaikan golongan yang sebenarnya. Oleh karena itu, pengujian lanjutan dengan data aktual sangat diperlukan agar validitas sistem dapat dipastikan secara objektif dan akurat. Sistem berbasis web ini diharapkan mampu membantu pihak sekolah serta dinas pendidikan dalam mempercepat proses verifikasi berkas secara efisien. Implikasinya, transparansi pengambilan keputusan dapat ditingkatkan demi mendukung objektivitas kelayakan karier para tenaga pendidik.</jats:p>

title: Wearable Health Monitoring from Sensors to Clinical Intelligence: A Critical Review of Sensing Technologies, Signal Processing, IoT Architectures and Clinical Translation 2020 to 2026
container-title: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
74896a92a34a7382df36adbe10e728a960b358d1.abstract: <jats:p>Health-monitoring systems are now used outside the clinic. Technological advances have allowed us to capture more physiological measures and use them elsewhere. The possibilities have been broadened with advances in ECG, photoplethysmography (PPG), temperature, inertial measurement, embedded processing, and wireless communication. However, the clinical utility and applications of wearable devices remain limited due to a lack of reliability, energy, interoperability, demographics, cybersecurity, and integration into clinical practice. In this paper, studies were searched in the database of Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar in September 2026. After screening 123 records, 22 studies have been identified to fit into the scope of study of this paper. Data were collected in areas of sensing, analytics, system architecture, and clinical translation. According to the existing data, these studies have reported a range of sensor, with varying skin contact, perfusion, or environment. Although there has been no significant improvement in signal quality, there appears to be little support for a clinically applicable device. The primary contribution of this review is a holistic design perspective that includes multimodal monitoring, evaluation of signal quality, adaptive edge analytics, energy-aware communication, privacy and interoperability, and clinically useful decision support. Future studies will focus on independent and longitudinal testing among a variety of populations and realistic activity conditions and evaluate clinical utility technical performance.</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Promote Inclusivity in Hybrid Model: Information Systems Academics' Perceptions
container-title: Digital Technologies Research and Applications
3ceb84b1d35d43e06a04d0b54d899991eb0deb28.abstract: <jats:p>Globally, there is a noticeable shift in higher education institutions (HEIs). This shift in innovation is driven by artificial intelligence (AI). Initially, AI was not readily accepted in educational contexts because it requires significant changes, including reconsiderations of infrastructure and resources, as well as innovative reskilling. Although literature indicates a slight shift, many academics, researchers, and institutions recognize AI’s potential to enhance the provision of tuition. However, in universities of technology in the Global South, perceptions of AI for advancing tuition remain underexplored. Therefore, the aim of this study is to establish how AI is harnessed in tuition at Durban University of Technology (DUT). To address this gap, this study is underpinned by structuration theory, with three primary concepts, namely structure and human agency, deemed relevant for collecting academic opinions, experiences, and views about the main artifact under study. Accordingly, a qualitative approach aligned with the interpretivist paradigm was used to guide this research. An autoethnographic research design was employed because it permits the collection of participatory opinions and experiences about the artifact under study. The findings reveal that academics hold different views on AI harnessing hybrid pedagogy. Although contradictions were noted in their views, these were evaluated as stemming from a lack of policies and frameworks governing AI appropriation. The major contribution was based on three propositions. Limitations were also noted, as the study captured only participatory opinions. Therefore, the recommendation for future research is to address similar topics and opt for both quantitative and qualitative approaches to capture the views of academic representatives.</jats:p>

title: Compliance-by-Design in an AI-Enabled Platform for Early Crohn Disease Interception: A Viewpoint
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
51c3cf4682e1640bc274480c0925c7d09ca3e377.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>AI-enabled digital medicine platforms in Europe are developed within overlapping rules for personal data, medical devices, AI, clinical research, health data access, and health technology assessment. This viewpoint represents the authors’ experience and interpretation from the preimplementation phase of INTERCEPT, an Innovative Health Initiative consortium that plans to validate biomarkers and develop a blood-based risk score for early Crohn disease interception. It does not report original empirical research, a systematic regulatory review, a deployed platform, or a validated AI model. Our aim is to explain how compliance-by-design can be translated into an auditable governance architecture and to identify what still requires scientific evaluation. We advance 3 messages. First, governance must begin with intended purpose and boundary mapping: a digital platform may contain research, operational, and medical device software functions, and conformity of one module cannot be inferred for the platform as a whole. Second, overlapping obligations can be operationalized through 5 linked controls: modular responsibility and change control, federated data governance, traceable AI life cycle management, consent and participant rights orchestration, and a common cross-border governance core with local adaptations. Third, compliance is not a surrogate for model validity, clinical benefit, trust, scalability, or market access. Before clinical deployment, planned AI components require prespecified labels and cohorts, leakage prevention, missing data and imbalance strategies, calibration, subgroup assessment, external validation, human factors evaluation, and postdeployment algorithmovigilance. A hypothetical biomarker risk score update illustrates how the 5 controls interact. INTERCEPT is informative because it combines cross-border biomarker research, planned predictive analytics, and heterogeneous institutional settings while key design decisions remain modifiable. Its contribution is nevertheless conceptual: the proposed framework is a testable governance hypothesis, not evidence of implementation success. Prospective studies should compare it with alternative governance models and assess safety, workload, participant experience, evidence generation, and regulatory performance.</jats:p>

title: Disrupting gendered task division without achieving equity of parity: a centrality-affective paradox from a design experiment in undergraduate physics labs
container-title: European Journal of Physics
6889aca767aa7b0a489dcab0dbeecc485cda6785.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Prior research has shown that, without careful design, group dynamics in undergraduate physics labs are often inequitable with respect to gendered task division. In this study, we implemented a three-change design experiment: changing lab group size from two-student to up to four-student groups; assigning group members randomly every week instead of allowing students to self-select stable groups for the entire semester; and adding the component of predefined, rotating roles. Through observations, we found that in an algebra-based lab with a majority-women population of bioscience majors, a woman consistently played a central, leading role regardless of role title, and that women assumed the Experimentalist role much more often than they did in two-student mixed-gender groups. However, matched pre and post E-CLASS results show that men do not exhibit any significant change over the course of the semester, whereas women show a significant decline in their attitudes toward experimental physics. These paradoxical results demonstrate that designing equitable learning environments is a complex process, and show that disrupting one pattern of inequity, does not, on its own, produce equity.</jats:p>

title: Bias in Medical AI in Relation to Patient Empowerment and Digital Equity: Scoping Review
container-title: Online Journal of Public Health Informatics
f32f1aabe6ae0bf9d4d8547544d818e333a71e0b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI is increasingly embedded in health care and digital health applications, shaping clinical processes as well as how patients access information and participate in care. Research on bias in medical AI has largely focused on technical and performance-related disparities. Less attention has been paid to how such biases may affect patients’ access, understanding, trust, and opportunities for meaningful involvement in care.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review aimed to map how studies of bias in medical AI describe patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment and the digital divide and to identify gaps across technical, social, structural, and patient-centered perspectives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review followed JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE and EBSCOHost databases were searched in August 2025 and supplemented by Google Scholar searches. Peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 onward were included if they addressed bias in medical AI and described patient-related consequences relevant to patient empowerment or digital inequality. Data charting focused on AI application types, bias dimensions, patient empowerment domains, digital divide–related factors, intersectionality, and debiasing strategies. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The search identified 497 records, of which 22 studies met the inclusion criteria. Bias was represented as a multidimensional sociotechnical phenomenon, with social bias identified most frequently (21/22 studies), followed by algorithmic bias (16/22 studies), structural bias (14/22 studies), and design-related bias (12/22 studies). Patient empowerment was most frequently addressed through involvement in care (n=13), followed by health literacy (n=9) and trust and assurance (n=7), whereas broader psychosocial and everyday-life domains were addressed less frequently. Digital divide–related factors were identified in 19 of the 22 studies, with digital literacy and usability barriers reported most frequently. Seven studies considered 2 or more social or structural dimensions of disadvantage. Although many studies discussed approaches that could mitigate bias-related barriers, explicit empirical evaluation of debiasing strategies in relation to patient empowerment or digital equity was largely absent.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patient-related consequences of bias in medical AI extend beyond algorithmic performance and are reflected in access, understanding, trust, and involvement in care. Broader empowerment dimensions, multidimensional disadvantage, and empirically evaluated mitigation strategies remain comparatively underexplored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Detecting Emotional Signals of Relationship Well-Being Using AI: A Cross-Sectional Comparison of Transformer-Based and Lexicon-Based Models for Couples Therapy Research
container-title: JMIR AI
9a1dea4de03ecd7baadc72f963637ef4a595c7ee.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Natural language processing and AI models are increasingly used to extract emotional signals from textual data; however, systematic validation of different computational paradigms in emotionally complex relational contexts remains limited. Such approaches may contribute to digital health research, particularly in the fields of digital mental health and couples therapy, where understanding emotional expressions within romantic relationships is especially relevant.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to compare a lexicon-based approach (NRC Emotion Lexicon) and a transformer-based model (Pysentimiento) in detecting affective patterns within spontaneous romantic relationship narratives and to evaluate their criterion-related associations with a theory-driven measure of relational well-being.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional exploratory study, 112 Spanish adults completed the Couple Flourishing Measure (CFM) and provided an open-ended description of their romantic relationship. Narratives were analyzed using both computational approaches to generate emotion and sentiment indices. Pearson correlations were computed between model outputs and CFM scores. Steiger Z tests were conducted to compare dependent correlations across models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Both approaches showed significant associations with couple flourishing, although the transformer-based model yielded stronger correlations for several affective dimensions, particularly positive sentiment (
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =0.66, 95% CI 0.54-0.76) and negative sentiment (
                      <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                      =−0.74, 95% CI −0.82 to −0.65). The lexicon-based approach showed smaller associations, primarily for negative emotions. Steiger Z tests identified significant between-model differences for disgust (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.04), joy (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.01), sadness (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.004), surprise (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      =.03), and positive and negative sentiment (both
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      <.001), but not for anger or fear.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this sample, Pysentimiento showed stronger associations with couple flourishing than the NRC Emotion Lexicon across several affective dimensions, although differences were not consistent across all categories. These findings support the value of theory-driven external criteria for evaluating computational emotion detection in relational narratives and underscore the importance of context-sensitive interpretation when applying AI tools in psychologically sensitive domains. These findings also highlight the potential relevance of computational emotion analysis for digital health research, particularly in digital mental health and couples therapy research, although further validation in clinical settings is needed before clinical implementation.</jats:p>

title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
container-title: Physical Review A
f6e3b076d2c8fe4a522ed55998ca8b61da435589.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding channel model has twice as many parameters compared with the unitary model, scaling as
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <a:mrow>
                        <a:mi>N</a:mi>
                        <a:mo>×</a:mo>
                        <a:mi>D</a:mi>
                      </a:mrow>
                    </a:math>
                    , where
                    <b:math xmlns:b="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <b:mi>N</b:mi>
                    </b:math>
                    is the number of logical qubits (width) and
                    <c:math xmlns:c="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <c:mi>D</c:mi>
                    </c:math>
                    is the depth of the VMBQC model. This can often make optimization more difficult and may lead to poorly trainable models. In this paper, we present a restricted VMBQC model that extends the unitary setting to a channel-based one using only a single additional trainable parameter. We show, both numerically and algebraically, that this minimal extension is sufficient to generate probability distributions that cannot be represented by the corresponding unitary model.
                  </jats:p>

title: Beyond Ethical Principles: A Comparative Review of National and Institutional AI Policies in Higher Education
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
8536db1c538358f24ed4b0c46d8e64444efc0c9d.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has produced a proliferation of ethical guidelines, national strategies, and institutional policies. Yet convergence around principles such as transparency, fairness, and accountability has not produced consistent governance outcomes across contexts. This chapter offers a comparative review of national and institutional AI policies in higher education, examining how ethical commitments are translated into regulatory frameworks and operational practice. Drawing on policy texts and institutional guidance from multiple regions, the analysis traces how governance logics shift as they move from ethical aspiration to national strategy and, ultimately, to institutional implementation. This chapter argues that national AI strategies consistently frame higher education instrumentally as part of workforce development and technological competitiveness agendas, while institutional responses remain shaped by organizational capacity, fiscal constraint, and fragmented governance. A cross-national comparison reveals that differences in regulatory philosophy matter less than variations in institutional design and resource distribution. This chapter concludes by identifying methodological implications for comparative education research and outlining a future agenda focused on policy translation, capacity building, and the uneven global distribution of educational risk associated with AI.</jats:p>

title: National AI Strategies and Higher Education in the Global South: Policy, Practice, and Power
container-title: Annual Review of Comparative and International Education 2025, Part B
aea880b7dde6be71ddcff68393b451b2c7d9de49.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how national artificial intelligence (AI) strategies are translated into higher education (HE) policy and practice across the Global South (GS), with particular attention to issues of equity, governance, and power. Drawing on cases from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and South Africa, this chapter explores how universities are positioned within national AI agendas and respond through fragmented policies, pedagogical experiments, administrative adoption, and partnerships. The analysis also highlights how structural constraints shape institutional responses and how Global North–developed AI intensifies concerns about autonomy, bias, and inequalities within and between HE systems. Situating these dynamics within the broader political economy of AI, this chapter shows how market concentration, industry influence, and North–South power relations shape both the possibilities and limits of AI integration in GS universities. It argues that meaningful, context-responsive AI adoption requires closer alignment between national strategies and institutional governance, sustained public investment, and equity-focused pedagogical frameworks that move beyond market-driven models of innovation.</jats:p>

title: Diminishing returns to calibrated reliance on AI: effects on deliverable quality and rework effort, moderated by task verifiability
container-title: Information Technology & People
18ace5ca3b42d9fb0b8f41f64d72dabeee644487.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can function as both “performance accelerators” and “risk propagators” in organizations. This study investigates how AI-enabled work capability, particularly employees' decomposition and evaluation skills, is associated with deliverable quality and rework effort through the behavioral pathway of calibrated reliance on AI. Additionally, it examines task verifiability as a critical boundary condition that shapes the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Guided by appropriate reliance and automation trust theories, data from 380 workers were analyzed using SmartPLS 4 (partial least squares structural equation modeling) and hierarchical polynomial regression to test mediation, moderation, and quadratic effects. Procedural remedies and a latent method factor approach were employed to assess common method bias.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI-enabled work capability was positively associated with calibrated reliance on AI. Calibrated reliance on AI was associated with higher deliverable quality and lower rework effort. A double diminishing marginal pattern emerged: as reliance calibration increased, quality gains and rework reductions leveled off, indicating a “too-much-of-a-good-thing” pattern. Task verifiability strengthened the positive association between calibrated reliance and deliverable quality and also strengthened its negative association with rework effort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study shifts the focus from reliance intensity to reliance calibration in explaining AI-enabled work outcomes. It documents a double diminishing marginal pattern, showing that the benefits of calibrated reliance are meaningful but not unlimited. It also identifies task verifiability as a boundary condition that helps explain when calibrated reliance is more strongly associated with improved deliverable quality and reduced rework effort. These findings provide focused guidance for capability development, reliance calibration, and task-specific AI governance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Newspapers Blocking AI Crawlers Expose Their Voters to a Partisan Flood
ff70f45920800194d1d03e1d4f840cbc01c7805f.abstract: Major newspapers block AI crawlers, while parties and partisan sites leave their text open. This paper builds a game-theoretic model of the hold-out and asks what voters hear while it lasts. In the model, an AI that cannot grade its sources pools the text it can read; two persuaders choose how much nearly free text to publish; and an AI lab may license a newspaper's reporting for its lost revenue. Neither the newspapers nor the lab has a political aim. Three results follow. First, the persuaders flood the AI, and the lab licenses each newspaper once a fixed share of the voters closest to it asks the AI, whatever the AI says. Second, newspapers whose voters dislike the AI's answers more hold out longer, and their voters hear the flood longer. Third, licensing bends the persuaders' contest by a small tilt from where the costs alone put it: patient persuaders tilt the AI's answers against the voters' average ideology, and impatient ones toward it. Business decisions with no political aim thus set how long each group hears the flood and which way the AI's answers tilt.
