title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business: Concepts, Contexts and Sustainable Pathways
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
4cc459244c5d01d40c24a4fb5821cef731816520.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative facilitator for organizations in different industries, reshaping how organizations design processes, make decisions and aim for sustainable values. Though there have been intense examinations of AI and analysis tools and methodologies in past studies, there is a pressing need for a wide and competent understanding of the different dynamics of AI as a transformative tool in real-world contexts. To address this issue, this chapter develops a case study analysis of how AI is influencing education and businesses and develops definitions based on transformative analytics. In this chapter, real-life examples of how AI has or can transform big businesses, educational systems of a nation and college and university systems have been examined. In fact, examples of educational institutions illustrate how AI can impact teaching and governing as well as how it can be used at a systemic level for inclusion. In turn, examples of big businesses illustrate how AI can influence excellence in work processes and administration as well as innovation directed at environmental friendliness. This chapter does not only focus on AI adoption as an issue of technology adoption; it also emphasizes the transformative process as socio-technical in nature. This chapter conducts a cross-case analysis to identify common enablers, sector-specific obstacles and various patterns of transformations in both business and the education sector. These elements are further integrated to develop various sustainable AI-based pathways of transformation in relation to long-term institutional viability, ethical use of AI and social purpose.</jats:p>

title: Applications and Reflections on AI in the Field of Education
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
7206fa36ebcf87cfdfd10e5f5663f14218c34b82.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The cognitive artificial intelligence (AI) radically transforms the educational ecosystem through data-driven thinking and algorithmic optimization, which focuses on precision, personalization and collaboration of the educational process, leading to significant changes in metacognitive development, human-machine cognitive synergy and ethical considerations. This technology overcomes the barriers of traditional standardized teaching by dynamically adapting learning paths through cognitive diagnosis, intelligent content adaptation and personalized goal setting. Regarding the development of metacognitive abilities, AI visualized abstract thinking processes and identified self-directed learning capabilities as skills that can be taught and learnt through strategic training and dynamic modification, ultimately redefining them as talents. Nonetheless, the use of technology raises ethical issues, including educational equity, algorithmic bias, data privacy and diminished cognitive autonomy, as overreliance on AI and instant feedback may hinder students’ ability to think independently. This means that a future development should strike a balance between technological advancement and humanism, base technological orientation in human concern and find synergy between tool empowerment and human leadership to build up education to a more fair and equitable evolution.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Learning Analytics for Outcome-Based Education in Higher Education Institutions
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
7fce1b0d95bc2f3628c57161d85d7dc67cfec2c9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the recent emphasis on Outcome-Based Education (OBE), it has become even more essential that colleges and universities have excellent data-driven systems that are able to not only compile, evaluate and interpret learning evidence into measurable outcomes, but essentially do it accurately and comprehensively as well. The traditional way of implementing OBE tends to rely on imperfect assessment data, looking backward in time and lacking depth, which further handicaps it from being useful in executing continual enhancements and making rapid academic decisions as well. To address such a difficulty, there comes across a framework within this chapter that proposes needing data-driven systems that incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into learning analytics as part of OBE systems as well. This chapter illustrates how AI is beneficial in increasing accuracy, monitoring, prediction and intelligent interventions regarding various types of institutional settings and is based on actual data and proves that primary data at an institutional level can be employed to reveal students’ actual engagement, their performance on tests and their success rates in accomplishing their goals within various programmes and academic cycles as well. To ensure that AI is used responsibly in the best interest of the institution and its stakeholders, the paper also addresses issues related to ethics, issues related to data governance challenges and readiness of the institution. This chapter offers a very useful and viable strategy for universities that are on a path of successful implementation of Outcome Based Education using AI learning analytics.</jats:p>

title: The Future of Customer Experience: AI-Powered Personalization in Marketing 5.0
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
dd4d3eb2de50f031c9aa810623c4914231bd7f36.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this era of cut-throat marketing campaigns, where every brand is devising strategies to stand out and grab attention, traditional methods are often unable to establish the required customer connections. The future of effective customer experience (CX) lies in personalization, and artificial intelligence (AI) is truly a revolution in marketing personalization. Personalized marketing campaigns definitely increase the conversion rate by fostering deeper customer connections. Natural language processing (NLP) powered by AI is used to understand the customer sentiment. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can provide personalized customer support. Huge data sets can be analyzed, and through predictive analytics, personalized campaigns can be created. This paper explores the potential of AI to develop personalized marketing experiences based on individual consumer preferences, behaviour and demographics.</jats:p>

title: AI Adoption in MSMEs: Opportunities, Barriers and Strategic Readiness in Emerging Economies
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
16639e264d9fc26bf269c5bf026df0b84d63dfe4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for harnessing competitiveness, learning and results of performance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging economies. Despite requiring greater policy emphasis and greater access to technology, little research data have been collected on emerging perceptions of AI opportunities, adoption challenges and strategic preparedness of MSMEs. In an endeavour to generate such research data, this chapter will examine AI adoption by MSMEs using data. The use of AI not only serves as an aid to organizations but also an innovation for organizations to acquire knowledge on data that influence performance outcomes on results. In this chapter, a survey-structured approach to the analysis is used, and a pragmatic and empirical method of data handling is used to describe MSMEs in operating crucial sectors of emerging nations. The descriptive and interpretational statistics, such as comparison of mean tests, correlation and regression, are used to spot trends in the adoption of AI, intensity of value creation sentiments, degree of constraint and readiness. These trends and patterns are spotted with the help of bar chart comparison, trend charts, scatter charts and heat maps, among others. The findings highlight that there is great potential for AI to make working more efficient for MSMEs, to help them make good decisions and to help them react better to the market.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Talent Management: Transforming Recruitment, Performance and Employee Engagement
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
ae74557c2bb6838779534a55f3892de085a328d8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the way organizations recruit, assess, engage and retain employees by transforming the way they do these in the organization. Although existing literature has deeply explored various AI-based tools and applications in the field of human resource management, there is a strong need for a theoretical understanding of how AI alters the basic principles of talent management as a practice. Addressing the need, in this chapter, a theoretical and integrative approach has been applied, applying various established theories in the realms of organization, human resource and behaviours as a way of reinterpreting talent management in the AI era. Counter to conventional thinking that regards AI as a mere technological advancement, in this analysis, AI-based talent management has been identified as a social, technical and strategic phenomenon that alters the way organizations recruit members, manage their performance and encourage them to work. This analysis has applied classical concepts such as Person–Job Fit Theory, Signalling Theory, Human Capital Theory, Goal Setting Theory, Expectancy Theory, Agency Theory, Job Demands–Resources Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. This chapter develops these new viewpoints and constructs a conceptual framework for AI-enabled talent management. The framework describes how talent outcomes are impacted by AI capabilities via hiring, performance and engagement processes.</jats:p>

title: Ethical, Legal and Governance Challenges of AI Implementation in Education and Enterprises
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
8bc7df27ed7151347b97dd89022391ba28abff8a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid application of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools and organizations has impacted the process of decision-making, performance measurement and value addition. In post-secondary education, AI-powered learning analytics is increasingly being employed to support outcome-oriented education. In organizations, AI solutions are being employed to enhance organizational operation, employee management and organizational-level decision-making. Nevertheless, emerging parallel to these advances, ethical, legal and governance (ELG)-related challenges have appeared to have immense potential to become important considerations for systematic and evidence-based analysis, rather than simply normative discussion (Floridi et al., 2018; Mittelstadt et al., 2016). This chapter applies a data-driven model for analysis of ethical, legal and governance-related concerns emerging due to the employment of AI within schools and organizations. This research avoids literature-based discussion for its focus by applying hypothetical but realistic primary research data to test concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, regulatory compliance and maturity in a governed context. Based on business enterprises and colleges, the chapter applies structured synthetic data in the application of comparative, correlational and descriptive analytics to uncover quantifiable risk exposure and governance readiness scores (Kshetri, 2021; Raji et al., 2020). This chapter is an application of pattern identification in the quantification of ethical risk vulnerabilities, regulatory issues of compliance and governance inadequacies in sectors through the application of tables, analytics and text analysis (Jobin et al., 2019).</jats:p>

title: Exploring the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence as a "Learning Scaffold" in Junior High School Students' Self-Regulated Learning
container-title: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
8852c321c745692ee238e92824943d5f5fd29736.abstract: <jats:p>As digital technology becomes more deeply embedded in education, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly present in junior high school students' daily learning. This paper explores the "scaffolding" role of GenAI in students' self-regulated learning (SRL) and its possible influence on enhancing academic self-efficacy. Based on Zimmerman's cyclical phase model of SRL and learning scaffolding theory, the study systematically deduces the human-AI interaction process. The analysis suggests that GenAI acts as planning, monitoring, and reflective feedback scaffolds across the forethought, performance, and self-reflection phases, effectively addressing the lack of personalized support in traditional autonomous learning. Furthermore, GenAI assistance contributes to the internalization of academic self-efficacy by accumulating direct mastery experiences and alleviating trial-and-error anxiety. Acknowledging the potential risks of cognitive offloading and academic misconduct associated with GenAI dependency, the paper proposes coping strategies such as cultivating students' critical GenAI literacy and implementing dynamic scaffold fading. This research provides theoretical support and practical guidance for educators to optimize GenAI-assisted self-regulated learning environments.</jats:p>

title: Generative AI Misuse and Rule Compliance Among University Students in Bhutan: Implications for Assessment and Institutional AI Policy
container-title: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
2911814f66aa2cdd17af909fac6352dfb960069a.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aim: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) use is expanding in Bhutanese universities while institutional policies remain under development. Guided by an extended Theory of Planned Behavior, this study examined factors associated with unauthorized AI use and intention to comply with institutional AI policies.
Materials and Methods: An anonymous, cross-sectional survey was conducted in June 2026 among a convenience sample of 713 Bhutanese university students. Seven-point Likert-type responses were analyzed using factor analyses, reliability assessments, correlations with false discovery rate correction, multiple and moderated regression, and bootstrapped indirect association tests. Robustness checks included robust standard errors and demographic controls.
Results: The models explained 24.5% of variance in AI misuse and 19.6% in compliance intention. Approximately 29% of respondents endorsed at least one misuse item. Misuse was associated with misuse acceptability, AI familiarity, academic pressure, moral rationalization, rule clarity, subjective norms, and learning impact. Compliance intention was associated with subjective norms, rule clarity, behavioral control, productive AI use, institutional enforcement, and moral rationalization. Institutional enforcement showed a small independent association with compliance intention (β = .086). Compliance intention was inversely associated with misuse (B = −0.10, p = .004). All six indirect associations were small, with bootstrap confidence intervals excluding zero. Demographic adjustment preserved findings; academic level showed no significant moderation.
Conclusion: Findings support evaluating assignment-specific AI guidance, coordinated workloads, classroom discussion of misuse rationalizations, and communicated institutional policies. Cross-sectional data preclude causal inference, and convenience sampling limits generalizability. These associations provide a basis for evaluating approaches to responsible AI governance.</jats:p>

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in High School Science Education: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, Pedagogical Strategies, and Critical Thinking Development
container-title: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
7ae48f59180fb1d3c9a8abac185c2aa46794f0d3.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aim: Evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in secondary science education remains limited. This systematic review examined students’ conceptual understanding and engagement, teachers’ pedagogical strategies and challenges, and students’ critical thinking and scientific inquiry.
Materials and Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, ERIC, Scopus, and Lens.org were searched for peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026. Two authors independently screened 187 unique records (Cohen’s κ = .78), identifying 20 eligible studies. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Framework synthesis integrated findings, informed by Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK).
Results: Seven studies assessed AI capabilities rather than classroom implementation. Only two compared learning outcomes across conditions; none employed a randomized controlled design. Student perceptions and engagement were generally positive, whereas learning outcomes were mixed. A chatbot supporting self-regulated learning outperformed a rule-based chatbot, but ChatGPT-4o yielded smaller gains than peer collaboration. Teachers reported concerns regarding content accuracy, assessment reliability, and instructional readiness. Generative AI matched or exceeded student performance on structured examinations but demonstrated lower grading reliability than human assessors. Evidence concerning critical thinking was particularly limited. Richer reasoning was reported with dialogue-oriented tools or teacher guidance, whereas answer-seeking use of general-purpose tools was associated with weaker reasoning.
Conclusion: Pedagogical structuring was recurrently associated with productive AI use, although causal inference remains limited. A provisional model warrants empirical testing. Priorities include structured tasks, science-specific teacher development, human assessment oversight, explicit AI literacy instruction, school governance, and controlled comparisons of structured and unstructured use across secondary science classrooms.</jats:p>

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
f171216399a007e7c399c672df322f23f7504b96.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

The study's findings confirm a strong correlation and a significant positive impact of using AI technologies on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi Public Sector. title: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in Hotel Revenue Management
container-title: Accounting and Revenue Decisions in Hospitality
570dee157ad55b3ea50c1d1ffed173551cdad606.abstract: <jats:p>Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are central to hotel Revenue Management (RM) because they translate complex demand, pricing, and inventory-control decisions into measurable outcomes for managerial learning, accountability and benchmarking. For decades, the hotel sector relied heavily on a small canon of room-centric metrics. Yet contemporary hospitality markets challenge the sufficiency of traditional KPIs. Distribution costs and digital intermediaries make gross revenue measures less decision-relevant. Total Revenue Management broadens RM beyond rooms into food and beverage, function space, and ancillaries. In parallel, customer-centric measurement is rising but remains operationally constrained by data fragmentation and organizational silos. This chapter provides a comprehensive, educational and critical review of KPIs used in hotel RM. It traces the roots of major indicators and evaluates what each KPI reveals and conceals. The chapter proposes a modern KPI portfolio—rooms, net, total, and profit metrics complemented by process KPIs.</jats:p>

c8f56a2bf0969823e9ba93e29f22b69fab0eb346.abstract:
<jats:p>Artificial Intelligence is rapidly reshaping the landscapes of education and business, driving innovation and redefining operational norms. The latest volume of the Advanced Series in Management brings together interdisciplinary perspectives to explore how AI technologies—from predictive analytics and automation, to adaptive learning systems—are enabling smarter decision-making, personalised experiences, and enhanced efficiency. At the same time, it critically examines the ethical, infrastructural, and skill-based challenges that accompany this digital shift, offering a balanced view of both promise and complexity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Bridging theory and practice, AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business presents empirical research, real-world case studies, and policy insights that illuminate the evolving role of AI in organisational and educational contexts. It contributes to global conversations around digital transformation and sustainability, aligning with key UN Sustainable Development Goals such as Quality Education and Responsible Management. Ideal for scholars, students, and practitioners, this volume offers a comprehensive guide to navigating the AI-driven future, especially in a post-pandemic world where hybrid learning and intelligent business models are becoming the norm.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Marketing 5.0 in the South Asian Business Sector
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
a849ff49fc6a6ee78d41646e64936a056f63afbc.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This research explores the five core components of the revolutionary marketing phase of the ongoing era, Marketing 5.0, across diverse business sectors in South Asia. The study takes a qualitative, inductive approach to analyze primary and secondary data collected from exclusively picked marketing professionals’ opinions and insights, as well as published interviews on YouTube, blogs, academic papers, books focusing on relevant evidences in the context of South Asian business sectors. The research findings develop an integrated theoretical framework of the disciplines, applications and enablers of the concept ‘Technology for Humanity’ under artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketing phenomena. The study upholds the synergistic value of the collaboration of humans and technologies complementing human cognitive skills with advanced technological skills in the post-pandemic world. The appropriate applications of AI-driven marketing approaches are evaluated in respect to close the widening generation gap, societal and digital polarization gap. The research concludes the foundational disciplines of the appropriate applications of AI-powered technologies for marketers, intended to create unique, yet inclusive and sustainable value that bridges these gaps while upholding the core value of humanity across the region.</jats:p>

title: The Future of Customer Experience: AI-Powered Personalization in Marketing 5.0
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
dd4d3eb2de50f031c9aa810623c4914231bd7f36.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this era of cut-throat marketing campaigns, where every brand is devising strategies to stand out and grab attention, traditional methods are often unable to establish the required customer connections. The future of effective customer experience (CX) lies in personalization, and artificial intelligence (AI) is truly a revolution in marketing personalization. Personalized marketing campaigns definitely increase the conversion rate by fostering deeper customer connections. Natural language processing (NLP) powered by AI is used to understand the customer sentiment. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants can provide personalized customer support. Huge data sets can be analyzed, and through predictive analytics, personalized campaigns can be created. This paper explores the potential of AI to develop personalized marketing experiences based on individual consumer preferences, behaviour and demographics.</jats:p>

title: AI Adoption in MSMEs: Opportunities, Barriers and Strategic Readiness in Emerging Economies
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
16639e264d9fc26bf269c5bf026df0b84d63dfe4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool for harnessing competitiveness, learning and results of performance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in emerging economies. Despite requiring greater policy emphasis and greater access to technology, little research data have been collected on emerging perceptions of AI opportunities, adoption challenges and strategic preparedness of MSMEs. In an endeavour to generate such research data, this chapter will examine AI adoption by MSMEs using data. The use of AI not only serves as an aid to organizations but also an innovation for organizations to acquire knowledge on data that influence performance outcomes on results. In this chapter, a survey-structured approach to the analysis is used, and a pragmatic and empirical method of data handling is used to describe MSMEs in operating crucial sectors of emerging nations. The descriptive and interpretational statistics, such as comparison of mean tests, correlation and regression, are used to spot trends in the adoption of AI, intensity of value creation sentiments, degree of constraint and readiness. These trends and patterns are spotted with the help of bar chart comparison, trend charts, scatter charts and heat maps, among others. The findings highlight that there is great potential for AI to make working more efficient for MSMEs, to help them make good decisions and to help them react better to the market.</jats:p>

title: Smart Supply Chains and Operations: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Understanding Smart Logistics
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
f5312670a1c73ec3f336d6875d9228c62155b4ee.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Smart Supply Chains is one of the evolving concepts in management. From making to procuring to sourcing products, everything is artificial intelligence (AI)-driven. The applications of AI, like warehouse optimization, real-time stock tracking and product optimization, are popular applications of AI. With the use and adoption of fuzzy models like artificial neural network (ANN) frameworks, the dependency on humans has eventually reduced, making smart AI ensure the best decisions for operations. The paper includes a case study and a study of a theoretical model known as Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) (Model), which is very popularly used in supply chain management and tracking logistics. The process includes plan, source, make, deliver and return. This is a good framework applied with AI in automation logistics for smoother functioning. It includes the use of fuzzy algorithms, genetic models and ANN networks to efficiently update and track product specifications as well as the delivery process without much human interaction. The ANN model is popular and widely used in data science as well as behavioural science.</jats:p>

title: Industry 4.0 and the Future of Digital Strategy: Pathways to Digital Value Creation
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
ae407cbd9af8ff9265d5af1ab1f6c5380deb09c9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The acceptance and addition of such progressive digital technologies into operational processes and decision-making platforms have totally redefined how businesses conceptualize strategy in Industry 4.0. This chapter explores how digital value creation (DVC), as a process, has been facilitated through Industry 4.0 technology, with digital strategy orientation (DSO) as the intermediary. For instance, employing a quantitative research strategy that focuses on theoretical constructs, the chapter integrates theories from dynamic capability theory, the resource-based view (RBV) and IT business value theory to explain how businesses achieve strategic and performance outcomes from their digital investments. Data collection entailed conducting surveys among managers whose business entities adopted Industry 4.0 technology. The examples given for Industry 4.0 technology were Internet of Things technology, artificial intelligence technology, analytics technology, automation technology and cyber-physical system technology. This chapter empirically explores Industry 4.0 technology and DVC and how Industry 4.0 technology influences DSO through structural equation modelling techniques. The results show that Industry 4.0 technology affects DVC both directly and through DSO. Digital strategy is an integral part of any business through which technology capabilities are actually linked with overall business goals. Organizations primarily benefit from the outcomes of a digital strategy by making their operations more efficient, starting new creative activities and gaining a competitive advantage in Industry 4.0. The findings quite clearly bring out that firms focusing on digital strategy are better positioned to achieve long-term value from their Industry 4.0 investments.</jats:p>

title: Building Resilient Supply Chains: Collaborative Approaches to Cybersecurity for Critical Infrastructure
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
b57fcc57786ba25935b4333be4ce3e40bade0906.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cybersecurity resilience has become a major factor in determining the strength of the supply chain, especially in sectors which constitute the national critical infrastructure, such as energy, transport and healthcare industries. This chapter examines the importance of collaboration to cyber resiliency in interdependent supply chains. The analysis is carried out through a conceptual literature review in which synthesis of 122 scholarly and policy papers published from 2014 to 2025 is made based on the concept of a network that brings into consideration theories of supply chain resiliency, resource dependency, collective action, socio-technological system and network governance. Cybersecurity resilience can be achieved only when more than one player is involved in the network. Through collaboration, information exchange concerning the nature of the threats, addressing such threats and public and private partnership will make the environment less vulnerable to cyberattacks and therefore more flexible. On the other hand, fragmented environments where there is very little cooperation are likely to be victims of system failure. This chapter outlines a framework called the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework, which is made up of components such as threat environment, actors, collaboration mechanism, governance and cyber resilience outcomes. One of the most essential things about collaboration according to the Collaborative Cyber Resilience Framework is that coordination will make collaboration better and sustainable. This study contributes to the existing literature in this field through offering a theory-based cyber security approach that focuses on the network aspect.</jats:p>

title: Sustainable Business Models and Artificial Intelligence for Handicraft Entrepreneurship: A Cross-Cultural Case Study

                  <jats:p>Across the globe, handicrafts have been validating cultures, identities and traditions that have been present in the modern world. At the same time, the craftsmen who are a part of the process of manufacturing the product not only validate themselves on the capability of manufacturing the product but also sustain their culture, heritage and tradition. title: Measuring What Matters: A Systematic Review and Future Agenda for Social Impact Assessment
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
71e3de4341dbb64b682404cd5dddd056873c72b2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The use of Social Impact Assessment (SIA) is indispensable when considering the consequences of changes occurring in organizations, policies and initiatives to the society in which we live. Unfortunately, the present methods of SIA are fragmentary, instrumentally driven and lack a theoretical basis. To address these weaknesses, in this chapter, an extensive study of the current scientific literature on SIA methods is conducted based on the PRISMA approach and conceptual thematic analysis as well as the assessment of theoretical foundation of each tool. The most popular SIA methodologies, including Social Return on Investment (SROI), Theory of Change, environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) criteria and well-being measures, are examined. This chapter proposes Adaptive Social Impact Measurement (ASIM) as a methodological meta-framework aiming to reinterpret the notion of measurement through its adaptability, participation and educative dimensions. While the traditional measurement approach relies on indicators, ASIM values an interactive, dynamic process of assessment enabling it to tackle such challenges as standardization and context, accountability and learning, control and empowerment, and other problems. From the conclusions drawn from this chapter, it is possible to state that the current stage of development implies not one methodology of measuring social impact but several ones. Furthermore, some directions for future research are suggested by the author, such as the application of artificial intelligence and big data techniques, participation, hybrid valuation, ethics and decolonizing methods.</jats:p>

title: AI-Enabled Talent Management: Transforming Recruitment, Performance and Employee Engagement
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
ae74557c2bb6838779534a55f3892de085a328d8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the way organizations recruit, assess, engage and retain employees by transforming the way they do these in the organization. Although existing literature has deeply explored various AI-based tools and applications in the field of human resource management, there is a strong need for a theoretical understanding of how AI alters the basic principles of talent management as a practice. Addressing the need, in this chapter, a theoretical and integrative approach has been applied, applying various established theories in the realms of organization, human resource and behaviours as a way of reinterpreting talent management in the AI era. Counter to conventional thinking that regards AI as a mere technological advancement, in this analysis, AI-based talent management has been identified as a social, technical and strategic phenomenon that alters the way organizations recruit members, manage their performance and encourage them to work. This analysis has applied classical concepts such as Person–Job Fit Theory, Signalling Theory, Human Capital Theory, Goal Setting Theory, Expectancy Theory, Agency Theory, Job Demands–Resources Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. This chapter develops these new viewpoints and constructs a conceptual framework for AI-enabled talent management. The framework describes how talent outcomes are impacted by AI capabilities via hiring, performance and engagement processes.</jats:p>

title: Ethical, Legal and Governance Challenges of AI Implementation in Education and Enterprises
container-title: AI-Driven Transformation in Education and Business
8bc7df27ed7151347b97dd89022391ba28abff8a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid application of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools and organizations has impacted the process of decision-making, performance measurement and value addition. In post-secondary education, AI-powered learning analytics is increasingly being employed to support outcome-oriented education. In organizations, AI solutions are being employed to enhance organizational operation, employee management and organizational-level decision-making. Nevertheless, emerging parallel to these advances, ethical, legal and governance (ELG)-related challenges have appeared to have immense potential to become important considerations for systematic and evidence-based analysis, rather than simply normative discussion (Floridi et al., 2018; Mittelstadt et al., 2016). This chapter applies a data-driven model for analysis of ethical, legal and governance-related concerns emerging due to the employment of AI within schools and organizations. This research avoids literature-based discussion for its focus by applying hypothetical but realistic primary research data to test concerns regarding privacy, bias, transparency, regulatory compliance and maturity in a governed context. Based on business enterprises and colleges, the chapter applies structured synthetic data in the application of comparative, correlational and descriptive analytics to uncover quantifiable risk exposure and governance readiness scores (Kshetri, 2021; Raji et al., 2020). This chapter is an application of pattern identification in the quantification of ethical risk vulnerabilities, regulatory issues of compliance and governance inadequacies in sectors through the application of tables, analytics and text analysis (Jobin et al., 2019).</jats:p>

title: Modular non-Hermitian topology and its application to critical sensing
container-title: Quantum Science and Technology
75c06209d17d4410bc24ef09764b8cd965be31ab.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Non-Hermitian topological systems have attracted a lot of research activities in recent times, both theoretically and experimentally, due to their unique physical properties and association with open quantum systems. We show that modular structures, where specific couplings at regular intervals take distinct values, enrich the unique topological attributes of these systems such as the non-Hermitian skin effect and the breakdown of conventional bulk-boundary correspondence. These systems also possess the capability of displaying criticality-enhanced sensitivity for precision metrology. We establish how the modular structure, in suitable parameter regime, enhances their sensing performance near spectral topological phase transitions and show that the enhancement can be achieved in multi-parameter estimation scenarios as well.</jats:p>

title: AI时代编译原理分层实践教学改革
container-title: 教育发展论坛
e4762fdbdc679a1953605ceea5e22b06cbf63f7f.abstract: <jats:p>随着AI发展对软件开发与计算机教育的影响,地方工科高校的编译原理课程在课时压缩和学生基础差异明显。传统的从零手写完整编译器,学生容易感受到挫败,且实验成果仅停留于理论层面,学生学习兴趣不高。本文在原"课程实验+课程设计"的两阶段安排的基础上,探索面向工程应用和能力拓展的分层实践教学改革。改革中第一阶段开展AI协同的编译原理性实验,第二阶段保留编译系统集成的同时,增强编译理论的实际工程应用,相应地,实践考核改用编译系统集成保底,加应用拓展项目增值的组合方式。对比改革实施组与历史比较组的实验提交、代码相似度检测、答辩记录和归档作品,发现改革后完整编译流程完成率从70%多增长到99%,存在代码抄袭的作品比例从约20%降至约1%;课程设计作品类型也更加丰富。但是也存在着"程序能运行、代码难解释"、重度依赖AI整体构建和代码验证不足等问题。针对这些问题,本文提出编译各模块的接口约束、版本追溯、提示词记录与随机代码走查等手段,加强对学生学习过程的管理。由于本研究采用历史队列比较,相关结果主要用于呈现改革后的变化趋势,不能将其仅仅归因于AI工具使用的效果。</jats:p>

f3d2aee2f4a9713a544292c0671de9fe59cd0fa5.abstract: <jats:p>以AI为代表的数智时代,对民事诉讼法的教学提出新挑战。传统的民事诉讼法教学存在着教学模式固化、学生被动学习、学情不客观、评价方式单一等问题,亟须进行全面而深刻的改革。AI赋能民事诉讼法个性化学习有现实的可行性,它符合国家教育教学改革政策导向,符合社会发展与学生培养需求,同时有强大的数智技术支持。AI可以从学情画像、学习资源供给、学习过程引导、学习评价反馈四个角度赋能,对前面提到的问题进行破冰,提供有针对性的措施,推动民事诉讼法课程个性化学习路径不断优化。</jats:p>

666f1bc9af0e59eab5efea204fb481b069053c0b.abstract: <jats:p>随着生成式AI的快速迭代,以生成式AI为代表的智能技术深度融入高等教育,已成为推动专业数字化转型、提升人才培养质量的核心路径。数据计算及应用专业作为新工科背景下的应用理科专业,具有理论性强、实践要求高、技术迭代快等特征。本研究立足生成式AI赋能教育的时代需求,明确数据计算及应用专业人才培养目标与能力定位,从课程体系、教学模式、实践平台、评价机制四个维度构建AI赋能人才培养路径,推动专业教学向智能化、个性化、实战化转型,为地方高校同类专业改革提供借鉴。</jats:p>

title: Empowering the anesthesiologist: Navigating the future of AI-driven visualization and wearable technology in regional anesthesia
container-title: Perioperative Precision Medicine
a31df87ef0bca8da413e630a2b5161d0bb5254eb.abstract: <jats:p>In current regional anesthesia practice, “visualization” typically refers to the real-time imaging and display of subcutaneous anatomical structures with ultrasound imaging, and “wearable technology” refers to hands-free, optical head-mounted displays (e.g., smart glasses) that can project digital information directly into the clinician’s field of view. The paradigm shift in the history of regional anesthesia from anatomical landmark techniques to ultrasound guidance has revolutionized the art of regional anesthesia and transformed a blind procedural technique into a visually guided intervention.</jats:p>

title: The Autonomous Learner; Decoding Cognitive Logic of Generation Z in the Sri Lankan Advanced Level Classroom

66c36a7cdf6e51d9fdecfc4ac37f940042bdf340.abstract: <jats:p>The Advanced Level (AL) classroom in the modern era is no longer a site of passive reception but a dynamic ecosystem of negotiation and cognitive autonomy. This paper explores the behavioral and cognitive shifts within Generation Z (Gen Z) individuals born between 1997 and 2012, who currently occupy the 17-to-19-year-old cohort in Sri Lanka (Dimock, 2019). Despite geographical, cultural & subject streamwise specificities, Sri Lankan Advance level students are increasingly bridging cultural disparities through digitalization, adopting a globalized "digital-native" logic. This article analyzes the "Authenticity Filter," the "Fast Brain" paradox, and the transition from instruction-following to instruction-making, arguing that modern pedagogy must direct toward relationship-based facilitation.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Ultrasound Power: Acoustic Cavitation, Nucleation Kinetics and Polymorphic  Control in Palm Oil Crystallization-A Critical Review
container-title: Journal of Advanced Physics and Interdisciplinary Science
fe955e1daf445ff89acd8dd9b00f546d1e06dc36.abstract: <jats:p>Ultrasound-assisted crystallization offers a route to manipulate the microstructure and functional properties of palm-based fats, yet acoustic, thermal, and hydrodynamic mechanisms are frequently conflated. This critical qualitative literature review synthesizes journal evidence published in 2020–2026 concerning acoustic cavitation, nucleation kinetics, polymorphic transitions, analytical characterization, and engineering translation. Direct palm-oil studies are differentiated from related work on cocoa butter, milk fat, coconut oil, and general sonocrystallization. The literature indicates that treatment position, subcooling, agitation, lipid composition, and emulsion architecture strongly moderate the observed response. Faster crystallization and smaller crystals do not necessarily predict higher hardness, greater solid fat content, or more stable emulsions. Nominal ultrasound power also provides an incomplete description of the actual acoustic field. A multiscale attribution framework is proposed that links acoustic forcing and energy dissipation to local temperature and flow, nucleation and growth, evolving polymorphs, crystal-network architecture, and application-specific performance. The review recommends thermal-history-matched controls, characterization of delivered acoustic energy, time-resolved scattering and NMR measurements, and transparent system-level energy balances. It concludes that ultrasound should be evaluated as a conditional, state-dependent processing tool rather than a universally beneficial crystallization intensifier.</jats:p>

title: Identification of critical displacements and deformations at subsoil assets based on GNSS observation time series
container-title: Mining Industry Journal (Gornaya Promyshlennost)
e7bc07548c037c0b38b135ee1f8163ef1df27ca7.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines approaches to identifying critical displacements and deformations at mining assets using the GNSS observation time series. It is shown that assessing the stability of mining-engineering facilities should not be limited to analyzing absolute displacements of individual stations only, since displacements of the same magnitude may correspond to different stages of the deformation process. Existing approaches to interpretation of the displacement rates, allowable deformations, and hazard levels are reviewed based on an analysis of Russian and international publications, as well as regulatory and methodological documents. Particular attention is given to transition from assessing the kinematics of individual points to analyzing the spatial deformation field. The principal strain axes, dilatation, and maximum shear strain are proposed as informative parameters, which combined analysis makes it possible to identify zones of extension, compression, loosening, compaction, and shear strain concentration. It is shown that universal threshold criteria cannot be directly transferred to all the mining assets and should be refined with regard to the specific engineering-geological conditions, mining regime, characteristics of the monitoring network, and measurement accuracy. It is also noted that reliability of the time-series interpretation largely depends on the quality of data processing, which highlights the relevance of developing domestic high-precision GNSS data processing tools for geomechanical and geodynamic monitoring tasks.</jats:p>

title: Research into the motivational mechanism in activities of Russian mining companies in the critical metals segment as a factor in improving the quality of production efficiency
container-title: Mining Industry Journal (Gornaya Promyshlennost)
a4b16b574706106ba827a0d999b5ab8ca337d222.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a research into employee motivation in the mining industry of the Russian Federation. The mining industry is the foundation of economic stability for resource-rich countries and is critical to global supply chains. Despite having its own resource base, Russian industry has long remained dependent on imports of certain types of rare metals and rare-earth products. Given the sanctions, this dependence becomes a vulnerability; therefore, development of mining and processing of critical metals is a prerequisite for sustainability of technological processes. The industry’s development is impossible without skilled workforce. The analysis conducted allowed the authors to identify two main groups of challenges that contribute to the low efficiency of workforce provision: the first is related to recruitment and retention, while the second one concerns training and development. Both groups are interconnected in terms of candidates’ unrealistic expectations and subsequent professional deformation of their personalities. The authors propose using a comprehensive evaluation index to assess the impact of employee motivation on the production efficiency indicators. It is calculated as the weighted sum of 10 key components. The proposed index makes it possible to determine the level of motivation and make timely management decisions. The results of the study led the authors to conclude that overcoming the labor shortage is impossible without developing an employer value proposition that shifts the emphasis from physical endurance to the intellectual management of complex systems. This entails the widespread implementation of the behavioral safety audit methods, modular training in hybrid skills, and implementation of dual mentorship programs. The economic viability of such investments is evident as the losses caused by downtime of highperformance equipment due to staff incompetence significantly exceed the costs of educational technologies.</jats:p>

title: OSIRA, an AI Early Warning System Using Open Source Intelligence for Digital Fraud Prevention
container-title: Jurnal Teknika dan Informatika (JTI)
5dead0b7fe2ba842d9a05a05911a1db96b858d75.abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: This study designs and evaluates OSIRA (Open Source Intelligence Risk Analyzer), an early warning system based on artificial intelligence that integrates Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to identify digital fraud indications before they enter formal reporting mechanisms in a cashless society. 
Research Methodology: The study uses a design science approach consisting of problem analysis, system design, risk score formulation, and a limited scale proof of concept simulation. The simulation used 540 synthetic texts from 50 template groups, divided into 394 training and 146 testing texts through a group based split, and classified them with Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF IDF) features and logistic regression. 
Results: OSIRA integrates web crawling, text preprocessing, fraud classification, entity extraction, a risk engine, and an early warning module. At a threshold of 0.50, the model achieved 82.88% accuracy, 79.66% precision, 98.95% recall, an F1 score of 88.26%, and a ROC AUC of 0.8528, but its false positive rate reached 47.06%, mainly for normal texts discussing fraud related topics. 
Conclusions: OSIRA shows initial feasibility as an additional intelligence layer that can shift fraud mitigation from reactive response toward proactive fraud intelligence. 
Limitations: The evaluation used synthetic rather than real OSINT data, a baseline classifier with limited contextual understanding, and risk score weights and thresholds that have not been empirically calibrated. 
Contributions: The study offers a conceptual and technical framework for using pre reporting public signals in fraud risk management and provides guidance for banks, digital wallet providers, and regulators.</jats:p>

title: AI-driven urban futures from global trends to African perspectives
container-title: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
63c95f886296ed5fe014fb5ab0afb87306d891c0.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), and specifically Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for urban planning, a gap persists between these innovations and their applicability in African contexts shaped by informality, data scarcity, limited capacity and climate vulnerability. This study examines how GenAI is reshaping urban planning globally and assesses its relevance, adaptability and risks in African contexts, identifying pathways for inclusive, legitimate and context-sensitive deployment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature review used a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided framework extended through PRALSMA (Preferred Reporting of AI-integrated Literature Search and Meta-Analysis), a reporting extension for transparent AI-assisted reviews. Peer-reviewed articles (2020–2025) from Web of Science and OpenAlex, with selected grey literature, gave 82 sources analysed through manual review and AI-assisted tools, with all outputs verified and triangulated for robustness and traceability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GenAI is transforming urban planning through multimodal workflows enabling rapid scenario generation, visualisation and communication, but effectiveness depends on localisation, bias mitigation, institutional capacity and legitimacy. Without these, GenAI risks misleading or exclusionary “blueprint” solutions, underscoring the need for context-sensitive adaptation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study integrates creativity-in-design, relational agency and democratic design to frame GenAI as a socio-technical participant rather than an autonomous planner, offering an Africa-relevant agenda for responsible, human-centred implementation aligned with equity, sustainability and resilience.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Beyond TAM: a mediated-moderated analysis of perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust as catalysts for AI adoption
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
6da4b5961b80fb182f0f7449a891d8ffaa5aa46f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines customers’ adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Jordanian telecommunications sector by extending the technology acceptance model (TAM). Specifically, it aims to investigate the effects of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism on actual use of AI, while testing customer intention as a mediator and technology trust as a moderator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative approach was employed. Data were collected through self-administered questionnaires from customers of telecommunications companies in Jordan. Using stratified random sampling, 482 questionnaires were distributed, and 438 valid responses were analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling using SmartPLS 4 was applied to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, mediation effects and moderation effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism significantly and positively influence customers’ intention to adopt AI, whereas perceived usefulness has no significant effect. Customer intention significantly predicts actual AI use and mediates the relationships between perceived ease of use, perceived anthropomorphism and actual AI use. However, intention does not mediate the relationship between perceived usefulness and actual AI use. Technology trust significantly moderates the relationship between customer intention and actual AI use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Telecom providers should design AI-enabled services that are simple, intuitive, human-like and trustworthy. Managers should also communicate the tangible benefits of AI more clearly to strengthen customers’ usefulness perceptions and encourage sustained usage.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends TAM by integrating perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust into a mediated-moderated model of AI adoption in an underexplored Middle Eastern telecommunications context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
container-title: Industrial Management & Data Systems
5d21c3cc1f8c08275de358484446f42d7cf150b1.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-function alignment are addressed before deployment. The stratified agentic AI governance framework is proposed that translates hierarchical structure into a sequenced intervention architecture, providing practitioners with governance priorities organized by risk-propagation logic.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper contributes a systematically derived risk taxonomy and a causally weighted governance map for agentic AI risks in supply chains. Five propositions are derived from the causal structure and are advanced as a testable research agenda.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The AI augmentation gap: data richness, automation and business value
container-title: EuroMed Journal of Business
013fd2494fa83d2bf73f0ae86b92503f4db8d54d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how data richness, as an organisational resource, is associated with business value through two deployment processes, automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled augmentation, and whether they differ in their capacity to generate value.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data from 366 Greek firms across four sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped mediation analysis and coefficient-difference tests; business value is measured as perceived value from digital technology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data richness is positively associated with both deployment processes. Automation is positively associated with business value and channels part of the association between data richness and value, whereas AI-enabled augmentation, the less developed process, shows no significant direct association; the difference is statistically significant, revealing an AI augmentation gap. Data richness also retains a significant direct association with value, and additional analyses suggest that the capability associations with value run through enacted digital transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Firms should build a strategically governed data foundation, expand automation for near-term returns and develop augmentation as a longer-term capability built on skills, role redesign, validation and trust in AI-supported decisions; EuroMed policy instruments can be aligned with this sequencing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on the RBV, the study shows that deployment processes of the same digital resource differ significantly in their association with value, a heterogeneity interpreted as reflecting the maturity of the complementary capabilities each requires, and provides evidence from a resource-constrained Mediterranean economy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Architectural hedging capacity: preserving strategic optionality in AI provider relationships
container-title: Strategy & Leadership
267e7c1615be5deddc9a991e32b3b7c4c5ddc35b.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Firms increasingly depend on a small number of external providers for artificial intelligence (AI) models, yet that dependence is not only imposed by supplier concentration; it can also be reproduced by a firm’s own technology-integration decisions. This paper aims to examine how provider-specific integration progressively erodes a firm’s ability to switch providers, and what company leadership can do about it.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper is conceptual. Using resource dependence theory as its base, it draws on transaction cost economics, modularity and real options reasoning, organisational routines theory, and the attention-based view to develop a mechanism and an organisational capability, formalised in four core propositions, a typology matrix and a remedy audit.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper develops integration drift, a reinforcing process in which locally rational integration decisions cumulatively raise the cost of switching providers. It also introduces architectural hedging capacity (AHC), an organisational capability enacted through three recurring routines: governance-enforced modularity, rehearsed recalibration and sustained managerial attention. And lastly, the argument also identifies a boundary condition in resource dependence theory: where dependence is continuously reproduced through organisational integration, maintaining autonomy requires continuously reproduced exit capacity rather than a one-time remedy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper extends resource dependence theory to settings where dependence is reproduced inside the firm through its own architecture, not only imposed externally. A typology and a remedy audit checklist give boards and managers a diagnostic for assessing and managing AI-provider dependence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: When AI signalling backfires: a threshold model of perceived firm innovativeness
container-title: Journal of Services Marketing
756ffe6f906e26c28ec21cab27a632588e7de924.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to interrogate the implicit monotonicity assumption in service-dominant logic by examining whether AI signalling intensity uniformly enhances perceived firm innovativeness (PFI) or exhibits threshold-dependent fragility. The study empirically validates relational coherence as a perception-level mediating state, thereby confirming its role as the integrator of AI-enabled capability inference, and specifies structural and demographic boundary conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A two-study archival design tests the proposed threshold model. Study 1 exploits discrete AI capability announcements among 1,012 Asian service firms (2012–2024) using event-study difference-in-differences to identify dynamic shifts in customer text-based PFI. Study 2 estimates a dynamic panel system generalised method of moments model incorporating lagged PFI, non-linear AI intensity and relational coherence, addressing reverse causality and omitted capability shocks while computing turning points and moderated curvature.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AI signalling exhibits an inverted-U relationship with PFI: moderate intensity strengthens capability perception, whereas high intensity attenuates and reverses effects. Relational coherence mediates this relationship, with the indirect pathway weakening and becoming negative beyond a calculable threshold. The curvature steepens and the threshold occurs earlier in high-contact services and firms serving older customer segments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study advances service-dominant logic by introducing threshold-fragility into its resource-integration premise, repositioning technological operant resources as legitimacy-constrained rather than uniformly accretive. It conceptualises relational coherence as the perception-level integrator governing AI-enabled capability inference and embeds demographic and structural heterogeneity within a formally identified non-linear, dynamic analytical model structure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The impact of explorative generative AI usage on construction project professionals' innovative work behavior: a technology affordance actualization perspective
container-title: Engineering, Construction and Architectural Management
bcb995eeec16228179498f7bb885d9c193f525b7.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study attempts to investigate the influence of generative AI (GenAI) on construction project professionals' innovation, specifically by exploring how and under what contextual conditions the use of GenAI fosters innovative work behavior.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Grounded in the technology affordance actualization perspective, we identified explorative GenAI usage as the critical trigger of innovative work behavior, specifically by boosting knowledge acquisition, and organizational support as a buffer of the translating process. The theoretical model was empirically tested using the structural equation modeling approach with 239 valid responses from the Chinese construction industry.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings reveal that explorative GenAI usage acts as a critical actualization behavior that significantly enhances construction project professionals' knowledge acquisition, which subsequently empowers their innovative work behavior. Crucially, this study highlights that the positive effects of explorative GenAI usage are valid when organizational support is high, instead of low.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to construction project management literature by deepening the understanding of the impact of emerging GenAI on micro-level individual behavioral patterns and provides valuable implications for construction managers in today's GenAI era.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI-enabled lead temperature: a narrative review and five-dimension framework for machine-learning lead prioritization
container-title: Vilakshan - XIMB Journal of Management
2f1fd2678470fdddb4e42bffd7bb75c7d78bd931.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to reconceptualize cold, warm, hot and sales-ready leads as dynamic states of sales-readiness and develops a five-dimension framework based on customer-profile fit, engagement, buying intent, authority and timing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A narrative review integrates the original 47-source DOI-bearing peer-reviewed analytical corpus with a reviewer-directed verification and update of recent peer-reviewed evidence. The synthesis covers qualification/scoring, nurturing, marketing-sales handoff, CRM/pipeline governance, inside sales/follow-up and AI/predictive lead management, using explicit eligibility, coding and bias-mitigation procedures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lead temperature is a reversible, timestamped configuration rather than a fixed label or engagement score. The framework translates the five dimensions into four operational levels: cold, warm, hot and sales-ready. Machine-learning models can estimate or rank this state, but decision value depends on recency, calibration, explainability, data quality and managerial governance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework requires longitudinal, multi-firm validation across channels, industries and sales-cycle lengths.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>RevOps, marketing and sales teams can use the model for routing, nurturing, response-time SLAs, downgrading stale leads and governing predictive scores.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper links practitioner lead-temperature terminology to machine-learning lead prioritization through an interpretable feature architecture and eight testable propositions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Are you a positive or negative user of AI? Exploring the impacts of undergraduates' GenAI use
container-title: Journal of Research in Innovative Teaching & Learning
49ee98c7eeacb7dbccf5fcc9ceb17fefa88e08b7.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly becoming commonplace in many academic environments; however, studies examining not just whether students use these technologies but how their usage patterns shape learning outcomes and academic integrity remain understudied. This study begins to address this gap by exploring undergraduates' patterns of constructive or problematic use of AI and their relation to academic and ethical behaviors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This exploratory study used a cross-sectional design employing quantitative data collection methods. A correlation and multiple regression analysis were conducted with college students' (N = 110) self-reports of AI use, academic motivation and engagement, reliance on AI, and digital citizenship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Negative and positive AI use were correlated with AI Reliance. Negative AI use also predicted stronger AI reliance with weaker digital citizenship skills, unlike positive AI use. Notably, positive and negative AI use were strongly correlated, suggesting that use patterns are not uniform on an individual level and may vary by context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results suggest that students may shift between different AI patterns. Future researchers should aim to clarify the causal mechanisms and recruit a larger and more diverse sample to validate and expand upon our findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To our knowledge, this paper is a rare empirical study that explores the relationship between specific student academic outcomes and AI use in distinctive usage patterns: positive and negative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Design of systems thinking assessment through laboratory activities to foster sustainability awareness
container-title: Chemistry Teacher International
7d03ebbbaad5555a0607b6f6a45758ee23b48616.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Presented here are lab-based activities (LBA) that incorporate students’ systems thinking (ST) skills by having students analyse pure and artificial seawater to stimulate sustainability awareness. Those skills were demonstrated by students’ scores and explanations. The design-based research (DBR) method was applied by following three principles: First was the real educational context principle, involving sixty-two (62) 16-year-old students who live around the Southern Java coast. Second, we conducted iterative investigations by designing and testing the model, including experiments, collecting cognitive scores online, and explaining system-related ocean phenomena through in-person interviews. Third, DBR was grounded in learning theory to provide measurable students’ ST skills from the laboratory. Here, inadequate explanations about seawater pH and acidity levels hinder the ability to think in systems. The results show that participants find it difficult to recognise seawater at the particle level as a system component. While participants struggle to recognise interactions between components of ocean systems, the ST purposes that emerge from their willingness to engage with ocean protection indicate high achievement. The appearance of Systems Thinking skills in the LBA is demonstrated here.</jats:p>
