title: The challenge of AI dependence: exploring its impact on cognitive autonomy and elaboration in creative performance
container-title: Information Technology & People
5d10468ae5a26c2d8ac92ce1ad78fb5842569e0a.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As artificial intelligence advances and its application scenarios continue to expand, human–artificial intelligence interaction grows increasingly close. While artificial intelligence brings convenience, it also raises concerns that it may weaken users' cognitive autonomy. To investigate this issue. This study aims to explore the composition of AI dependence and its impact on cognitive autonomy and specific aspects of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study draws on cognitive evaluation theory and the elaboration likelihood model to construct a dual-pathway model with instrumental dependence and affective dependence as core variables. The model explains the formation mechanisms of the two types of artificial intelligence dependence and their differential effects on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily examines their potential role in the elaboration dimension of creative performance. A two-stage mixed-method design was employed to test the model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Study 1 found that perceived trust mainly had a positive effect on instrumental dependence. Different dimensions of interactivity differentially affected affective dependence and cognitive autonomy. Mediation analysis further confirmed the core mediating role of Dependence. Study 2, a small-sample exploratory experiment, re-tested selected hypotheses and found a possible negative effect of instrumental dependence on the elaboration dimension of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The main theoretical contribution of this study lies in revealing the dual-pathway formation mechanisms of artificial intelligence dependence and the reshaping effects of different types of dependence on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily explores the potential effects of dependence on elaboration performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The dual-pathway dependence model constructed in this study offers practical implications for understanding how long-term use of artificial intelligence affects cognitive autonomy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: AI Maturity
32d694777c78ec4dd68570fed164b2d11c3eceb0.abstract: <jats:p>This Element explores how generative AI transforms education, not only by requiring new forms of literacy but by demanding a framework of autonomy, responsibility, and epistemic virtues. Current AI literacy frameworks emphasize technical proficiency, yet remain incomplete without addressing the normative risks of AI immaturity. This Element argues that education must promote AI maturity: the ability to use AI without succumbing to cognitive offloading, algorithmic dependence, or epistemic heteronomy. It identifies key forms of AI immaturity and reconceptualizes prompting as a dialogical practice paralleling the Socratic method – the art of questioning, iterating, and critically engaging AI. Finally, it introduces a framework of epistemic virtues that enables students and citizens to resist disempowerment and cultivate epistemic autonomy. By bridging philosophy and pedagogy, the Element shows how generative AI can become a medium of epistemic autonomy, offering concrete guidance for curricula, assessment, and classroom practice.</jats:p>

title: Gate the claim, not the tool: verification for AI-accelerated research in nutrition
f12ea9f56f0544e10310af3dc62d8ee611663f6e.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic workflows can accelerate nutrition science across living systematic reviews, dietary assessment and cohort analyses, yet they have also fuelled a surge of formulaic papers mined from open datasets. Journals and funders have responded largely by restricting how AI may be used, especially in writing. Because AI use leaves no reliable trace in a single paper, such rules cannot be enforced; they drive use out of sight, penalize honest authors who disclose it, and fall out of date within months as models improve. A gate works only when what it checks is visible at submission. When three publishers stopped accepting unvalidated papers built on the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), their NHANES publications fell by 72% in the first nine months of 2026, showing that visible gates work, though a rule that blunt can also turn away sound epidemiology. Rather than policing the tool, nutrition science should use AI openly under human scientific judgement and hold every result to four verification gates scaled to its consequence: depositing data, code and agent logs so others can rerun the work; naming an accountable investigator who understands the study design and answers for each claim made; independently verifying findings that could change clinical practice or dietary policy; and disclosing what AI and humans did without penalty. As output grows, papers will likely become concise accounts for human readers resting on machine-auditable records, shifting prestige from the journal name to whether a claim matters when verified.

title: Gate the claim, not the tool: verification for AI-accelerated research in nutrition
088ae7cb875899ff787a91e094e621517c98151a.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic workflows can accelerate nutrition science across living systematic reviews, dietary assessment and cohort analyses, yet they have also fuelled a surge of formulaic papers mined from open datasets. Journals and funders have responded largely by restricting how AI may be used, especially in writing. Because AI use leaves no reliable trace in a single paper, such rules cannot be enforced; they drive use out of sight, penalize honest authors who disclose it, and fall out of date within months as models improve. A gate works only when what it checks is visible at submission. When three publishers stopped accepting unvalidated papers built on the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), their NHANES publications fell by 72% in the first nine months of 2026, showing that visible gates work, though a rule that blunt can also turn away sound epidemiology. Rather than policing the tool, nutrition science should use AI openly under human scientific judgement and hold every result to four verification gates scaled to its consequence: depositing data, code and agent logs so others can rerun the work; naming an accountable investigator who understands the study design and answers for each claim made; independently verifying findings that could change clinical practice or dietary policy; and disclosing what AI and humans did without penalty. As output grows, papers will likely become concise accounts for human readers resting on machine-auditable records, shifting prestige from the journal name to whether a claim matters when verified.

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
b9ccdb38f6597ed3e62466f34e81e1c68972ba14.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title:
Extracellular
Polymeric Substances Govern Horizontal
Gene Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Mechanisms, Pathway
Specificity, and Research Gaps
container-title: Environmental Science & Technology
3f9525b6615b07cbebd1a6547de6cc5d3829b3e4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in environmental systems is recognized as being shaped by local matrix conditions, yet the pathway-specific role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), the dominant matrix of biofilms, sludge flocs, and granules, remains poorly resolved. In this Review, we develop a mechanism- and pathway-resolved perspective for evaluating how EPS govern horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of ARGs. Current evidence indicates that conjugation is the most directly supported pathway, with EPS facilitating or restricting transfer through effects on donor–recipient contact, matrix organization, and transfer-related physiology. For transformation, EPS-associated extracellular ARGs constitute reservoirs, but EPS–DNA binding can both preserve genetic material and limit its immediate bioavailability. By contrast, EPS involvement in phage-mediated transduction and vesicle-mediated transfer remains mechanistically plausible but insufficiently validated. We identify five interconnected mechanisms: physical retention and spatial organization, DNA adsorption and bioavailability, regulation of intercellular contact, modulation of cell physiology and transfer competence, and community-scale mobilome coupling. By clarifying evidence boundaries across pathways, this Review moves EPS–HGT research from correlation-based interpretation toward mechanism-informed assessment of ARG mobility. We conclude by outlining research needs, including standardized EPS definition and extraction, component-resolved characterization, pathway-resolved causal assays, and validation in realistic environmental aggregates.</jats:p>

title: From Listeners to Investigators: A Critical, Evidence-Based Synthesis of Project-Based Learning (PjBL) in the Science Classroom
container-title: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
9007b9bba28dfd013f837093c912b67debe08c8e.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aim: In many education systems, science classrooms have traditionally followed a transmission model in which teachers explain content and students listen, copy notes, and memorise facts for tests. This model teaches knowledge but does not always teach students to think and work like real scientists. Existing reviews of project-based learning (PjBL) in science education tend to catalogue its reported benefits without systematically weighing the strength of the evidence behind them, or clarifying how PjBL differs from closely related approaches such as inquiry-based and problem-based learning. This article addresses that gap: rather than claiming PjBL is a universally superior alternative, it critically synthesises the literature to ask under what conditions shifting responsibility from teacher-led delivery toward student-led inquiry is justified, and where the evidence is thinner than the enthusiasm surrounding it might suggest.
Materials and Methods: This is a literature-based academic article employing document study and narrative synthesis. Sources were located through structured searches of the Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar databases using terms including project-based learning, science education, scaffolding, and student outcomes, and were included where they reported empirical or conceptual work on project-based science learning published mainly between 2008 and 2026. Each source was also read critically for the strength of its research design, so that claimed benefits could be weighed rather than simply reported.
Results: The literature converges on a plausible, though not unanimous, account: a science project is an extended, student-driven inquiry into a real problem producing a concrete product, in which teachers act as facilitators whose guidance shifts with students’ age and experience, while students plan, investigate, collaborate, and report as active researchers. What is less settled is the strength of evidence behind the many claimed benefits: reported gains in process skills, creativity, motivation, self-efficacy, collaboration, real-world skills, and sustainability awareness recur across studies, yet many rely on quasi-experimental designs, small or single-site samples, and short interventions, a tension this article treats as central rather than incidental to its conclusions.
Conclusion: Rather than declaring PjBL simply effective or ineffective, this article argues that the balance of evidence favours treating project work as a deliberate restructuring of responsibility between teacher and student, one whose value for classroom practice and teacher-education policy depends on careful design, realistic scaffolding, and honest engagement with the limits of current evidence.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid Metaheuristic–AI Modeling for Accurate Prediction of CO₂ Solubility in Amine–Ionic Liquid Hybrid Solvents
container-title: Journal of Machine Learning Advances
b3f8f108327b6c30c355b18c27f514d24927d2c0.abstract: <jats:p>Reducing CO₂ emissions from fossil-fuel-based processes requires accurate and reliable predictive tools for designing advanced solvent systems for post-combustion carbon capture. In this study, an extensive experimental database of CO₂ solubility in hybrid amine–ionic liquid (IL) solvents was compiled and modeled using four hybrid metaheuristic–machine-learning frameworks: Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting combined with the Multi-Verse Optimization Algorithm (HistGBoost-MVOA), Tabular Neural Network combined with the Moth-Flame Optimization Algorithm (TabNet-MFOA), Support Vector Regression combined with the Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (SVR-IWOA), and Extreme Learning Machine combined with the Jellyfish Optimization Algorithm (ELM-JFOA). The input variables included temperature, amine concentration, IL concentration, molecular weights of the amine and IL, and CO₂ partial pressure, while the CO₂ mole fraction in the liquid phase (xCO₂) was considered the target variable. To ensure robust model development, outlier detection was performed using the Isolation Forest algorithm, followed by Robust Scaling for data normalization. Model performance was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation and independent testing based on R², RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and PBIAS, together with Taylor diagrams, centered RMSE (cRMSE), SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap uncertainty quantification. All developed models demonstrated excellent predictive capability (testing R² > 0.96), with SVR-IWOA consistently achieving the highest prediction accuracy and the narrowest uncertainty intervals. SHAP analysis identified the molecular weight of the ionic liquid and temperature as the most influential variables governing CO₂ solubility. The proposed modeling framework provides a robust and interpretable data-driven approach for accurately predicting CO₂ solubility and supports the design and optimization of hybrid amine–ionic liquid solvents for carbon capture applications.</jats:p>

title: Can Generative AI Preserve Tail-Risk Networks? Evidence from Cryptocurrency Markets
a7b8b619dc1031d40b391ec9469ab85ae17f02f8.abstract: Generated financial scenarios inform risk estimation and portfolio decisions, but agreement with standard distributional diagnostics does not show that a generator preserves the structure a decision depends on. We evaluate generated scenarios in three layers: conventional distributional and risk diagnostics; preservation of a conditional lower-tail network, judged against the sampling uncertainty of the empirical network; and realised outcomes of an allocation rule that uses the network’s node rankings. Using hourly data for ten cryptocurrencies over 2020–2025, we compare a stationary bootstrap, a GARCH-t copula model and a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM). The layers yield different conclusions about these generators. The discrepancy between the aggregated GARCH-t network and the observed network exceeds the bootstrap reference band at all 16 evaluation refits, yet overall distributional discrepancy stays within its band in 96 of the 157 GARCH-t panels that fall outside both the conventional-diagnostic and network bands. DDPM meets the joint conventional-diagnostic criterion in no panel but meets the single-panel network criterion in 120 of 160. Network differences change allocation weights and volatility exposure. After ex ante risk matching, differences in daily expected shortfall relative to the historical-network rule range from −0.09 to −0.02 percentage points, and every paired 95% interval contains zero. Controlled simulations show when ranking errors are costly: if tail hubs differ mainly in asymmetric downside dependence, a correlation-matching copula reverses the hub ranking and raises population expected shortfall by 3.1% relative to the true-network benchmark. Conventional diagnostics, network preservation and allocation outcomes give distinct assessments of these generators. JEL classification: C45 · C58 · G11 · G32

title: Mapping data privacy at the intersection of AI and the digital economy: a bibliometric review, taxonomy, and research agenda
container-title: Electronic Commerce Research
4771700294a9adc8d5aa2955311b1e6641f61402.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence and related emerging technologies has intensified data privacy challenges across the digital economy. Although scholarship has grown substantially, it remains fragmented across technical, legal, ethical, and sector-specific domains, limiting a clear view of the field’s structure and development. This study presents a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping of 434 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026 in the Web of Science Core Collection. It identifies seven thematic clusters and finds that applied and privacy-preserving technical work dominates, while business strategy, trust, and public-sector governance remain underdeveloped. The study extends this mapping with a multi-dimensional privacy taxonomy and a TCCM (theory, context, characteristics, and methodology) synthesis, moving beyond the topic- and domain-specific scope of prior reviews to diagnose where the field is structurally weak. It argues that privacy remains under-theorized as an economic and behavioral phenomenon despite its centrality to digital commerce and sets out a research agenda of economically grounded questions derived from these gaps.</jats:p>

title: Integrating AI General Education with Digital Literacy Cultivation and Cognitive Construction in Industry-Specific Universities
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
ed572e57c1cc41bc9396ae2882f5f643647c0276.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence has evolved into a general-purpose technology that permeates nearly every corner of knowledge production and social governance. This transformation is pushing college students' digital literacy far beyond the traditional "digitization" benchmark toward what this paper terms "intelligent-digital" literacy. For industry-specific universities—institutions committed to serving specific industries and cultivating application-oriented talents—the significance of AI general education is perhaps even greater than for other types of universities, because their graduates directly enter the industrial chain. Taking the practice of Moutai Institute as a concrete case, this paper elaborates on the internal logic, practical challenges, and feasible pathways for integrating AI general education into students' digital literacy cultivation and cognitive construction. The core argument of this paper is that such education should be anchored in industrial scenarios rather than abstract theory, and that cultivating compound talents equipped with digital literacy, industrial awareness, and social responsibility requires simultaneously grasping three main threads: technological empowerment, value guidance, and cognitive construction. On this basis, this paper proposes a trinity integration framework and offers actionable strategies from four dimensions: curriculum system, teaching model, faculty development, and evaluation mechanism. This paper aims to provide theoretical reference and practical insights for general education reform in industry-specific universities.</jats:p>

title: Contemporary Trends in Sharia: Critical Debates in Historical Contexts, written by Hadi Enayat and Mohamed M. Keshavjee
container-title: European Journal of Comparative Law and Governance
971f5f59977089a00e152b451717b173e66ae1dd.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This review assesses Hadi Enayat and Mohamed M. Keshavjee’s
                    <jats:italic>Contemporary Trends in Sharia</jats:italic>
                    as a synthetic intervention on contemporary efforts to understand sharia in ways apposite for the 21st century. Situating the book against historical transformations since the nineteenth century—including the movement from jurists’ law to state law, the secularisation of Islamic law through constitutional courts, and the changing authority of the ulama, Muslim religious scholars—the review argues that the book’s chief contribution is methodological. It reframes sharia-related controversies as questions of institutional site, interpretive authority, and enforcement pathways rather than as disputes over a monolithic legal code. The review highlights the book’s relevance for European debates on legal pluralism, gender justice, alternative dispute resolution, and private international law, while arguing that its synthetic strength would be enhanced by fuller doctrinal, empirical, and European case-law engagement.
                  </jats:p>

title: Lightweight AI Fundus Image Model for Early Screening of Diabetic Retinopathy
container-title: Theoretical and Natural Science
38e8c941ab04c8055d965b13e632d05e98f1bf8e.abstract: <jats:p>Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is now the main cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults worldwide. With the rising prevalence of diabetes, the need for DR screening is becoming increasingly urgent. Traditional DR screening requires professional ophthalmologists; thus, there are problems of a shortage of expert resources, uneven distribution, and lengthy manual interpretation. Most of the current deep-learning models have too many parameters and are computationally expensive; therefore, they are not suitable for deployment on edge devices. To solve the problem of deployment bottlenecks, the development of lightweight artificial intelligence models for fundus images has become necessary. This paper systematically reviews the recent developments in lightweight artificial intelligence models for DR screening based on fundus photographs. Custom image pre-processing, a lightweight network design, advanced model compression techniques and interpretability mechanisms are employed to reduce both the number of parameters and computational cost substantially without losing the sensitivity to early retinopathy. The model's diagnostic reliability and computational resource consumption have been examined. Ablation studies and visual analyses show the respective contributions of each module to the model's performance and efficiency. Additionally, to improve the interpretability of the model and boost clinical trust, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is introduced. Future research will enhance the adaptability of cross-device and cross-domain applications, expand the scope of clinical verification, and integrate multimodal clinical data for reliable and fair ophthalmic AI deployment.</jats:p>

title: Applications of Markov Chains in Financial Risk Modeling: A Critical Literature Review
container-title: Theoretical and Natural Science
63120c2cca3604cfa025e9c0e30991ddfb293ce6.abstract: <jats:p>Markov chains represent financial risk as movement between credit or market states. This review examines how that representation supports credit migration analysis, default estimation, market risk forecasting, and portfolio decisions. It compares foundational models with subsequent research on rating heterogeneity, switching volatility, and economic conditions. The literature supports Markov models as interpretable tools for connecting current information to future loss distributions, but their usefulness depends on the state definition and stability of transition probabilities. A three-state numerical illustration shows how persistent adverse conditions can amplify cumulative default risk through repeated migration. The review distinguishes physical probabilities used for forecasting from risk-neutral probabilities used for pricing, and explains why a transition matrix alone cannot determine portfolio tail risk. It concludes that Markov models are most credible when combined with economic conditioning, explicit dependence assumptions, parameter uncertainty, and evaluation on observations unavailable during estimation.</jats:p>

title: Discursive Manipulation of National Security and Industrial Competitiveness in U.S. AI Regulation: Domestic Contestation and the Fragmentation of Global AI Governance
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
89095b329b35762814611822e8bb5c6fb5fbdc85.abstract: <jats:p>Against the backdrop of generative AI emerging as a core strategic asset for major powers, the rhetorical tropes of national security and industrial competitiveness are subject to strategic manipulation by divergent domestic actors. The deregulatory camp within the White House invokes industrial competitiveness to roll back security-focused executive orders; the security faction in Congress expands chip export controls in the name of national defense; state-level authorities counter federal overreach through consumer protection mandates; and Silicon Valley deploys a two-pronged lobbying strategy. Taking the 2023-2026 policy pendulum and BIS chip regulations as its analytical case, this paper demonstrates that domestic contestation spills over globally through transmission channels. This has produced a global AI governance landscape defined by fragmentation, hollowed-out soft law processes, and a three-bloc divide across the U.S., the EU, and China, while the shortening commitment half-life of U.S. policy positions has inflated the costs of multilateral cooperation. The study also identifies limited positive spillover effects. In response, the paper puts forward targeted strategies. The conclusion argues that U.S. internal regulatory divisions constitute a mechanism that externalizes domestic political costs as global governance uncertainty. Understanding this mechanism is a prerequisite for reshaping the multilateral AI order.</jats:p>

title: Substitution Boundaries of AI Agents in Team Collaboration: An Empirical Analysis Based on Front-Line Employees' Perceptions
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
059dfca0efb815d1c92ad658bc09d215d808d6b8.abstract: <jats:p>With AI agents increasingly involved in teamwork, whether AI can substitute human collaboration has become a heated topic in academia. Large-model-driven agents are now capable of participating in team brainstorming, task coordination, and collaborative problem-solving, and knowledge-intensive industries are beginning to form a large number of human-machine hybrid teams. Existing research mostly relies on theoretical reasoning and lacks empirical perceptual data from front-line practitioners. Drawing on a questionnaire survey of 158 employees with cross-industry teamwork experience, this paper explores practitioners' perceptions regarding the substitution of human collaborative behaviors by AI. The results show that AI can only partially substitute procedural and rule-oriented collaborative tasks, whereas social-emotional communication, conflict mediation and value judgment remain irreplaceable human strengths. Position, work experience and AI familiarity jointly shape individual perceptions of the substitution boundary. Most practitioners regard AI as an auxiliary tool rather than a leader of team collaboration. This study provides a practical reference for enterprises applying AI collaboration tools.</jats:p>

title: Take the Bull by the Horns—The Impact of Threat of AI & Avoidance Job Crafting on Job Burnout

b5fdf72363d1bb76895e498654fbc5c437394167.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence becomes more ‍‌common in everyday work, it can improve ‍‍organizational efficiency while also making employees worry ‌‍about being replaced‍‍ or seeing their skills lose value. Even‍‌ so, less attention ‌‍has been given to what happens within employees themselves, ‌especially the part ‌‍a growth mindset may‍‍ play in shaping reactions to the threat of AI. Using survey data from working adults (N = 228)‌‌, this study examine‍‌s whether a growth mindset weakens the l‍‍ink between the threat of AI and job burnout, and whether avoidance job crafting‍‍ explains that relationship.‍‌The relationship. The‌‍ two main points. When employees have a ‌‌stronger growth mind‍‌set, the negative association between the threat of AI and j‌‌ob burnout is notice‍‌ably weaker. Avoidance job crafting also‍‍ appears to mediate ‌‌this relationship. B‍‌y considering both a‌‍ psychological factor and a behavioral pathway, this study p‍‌laces growth mindset‌‍ within research on ‍‍the threat of AI and‌‌ shows more clearly ‍‌how work behavior connects t‍‍o job burnout. In practicaltos, the results suggest that organization may be able to red organizations out ‌‌by helping employees‍‌ develop a growth mindset.‍‍</jats:p>

title: Traditional Chinese Cultural Branding and Premium Positioning: A Critical Evaluation of CHAGEE's Marketing Strategy
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
a6609b7f1cc816ac807c94daf1c0f5134c232986.abstract: <jats:p>China's freshly brewed tea market is growing rapidly, making cultural branding a key differentiator. This study explores how CHAGEE leverages traditional Chinese culture to build a premium brand position. It addresses three questions: (1) How cultural branding shapes its segmentation, targeting, and positioning, (2) How positioning is executed through the marketing mix—product, price, place, and promotion, and (3) What challenges threaten brand authenticity, perceived customer value, and message consistency. Using a qualitative single-case study approach, the research analyzes CHAGEE's official materials, industry reports, and academic literature. Findings show that CHAGEE targets urban consumers who prioritize tea quality, convenience, and brand experience. Its premium positioning is built through origin-sourced leaf tea, culturally resonant product names, heritage-inspired packaging, minimalist-store aesthetics rooted in Chinese design principles, and digital storytelling that modernizes tea culture. These elements jointly deliver both functional value (e.g., freshness, taste) and symbolic value (e.g., identity, tradition)—anchored firmly in tea itself as the core product. However, "premium" positioning alone does not automatically translate into higher willingness-to-pay, repeat purchases, or loyalty. Rapid physical expansion, inconsistent service quality across stores, and overuse of promotions risk diluting brand authenticity and eroding perceived value. The study concludes that cultural branding sustains differentiation only when grounded in three pillars: reliable product quality, demonstrable customer value, and consistently delivered service experiences.</jats:p>

title: Does Bilingual Code-Switching Enhance Executive Function in Children? A Focused Review of When and under What Conditions Cognitive Benefits Emerge
container-title: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
bd62b75a4cfe050f48f813b62ed113b68438e32a.abstract: <jats:p>Research on the bilingual executive-function advantage has produced positive, null, and inverse findings. One likely reason is that bilingualism is often treated as a uniform category, even though children differ substantially in how they use their languages. This focused critical review examines whether code-switching, rather than bilingual status alone, is associated with cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control in children and identifies the conditions under which benefits are most plausible. Eleven peer-reviewed sources were selected from the project's literature corpus to provide theoretical foundations, broad child-level syntheses, methodological critiques, and direct evidence. The evidence does not support a universal code-switching advantage. Direct child studies report a conditional positive association, a null association, and an inverse association; another study shows that the relation between language control and cognitive control may also operate in the opposite direction. Across this literature, language ability, interactional context, switching type, task choice, and age emerge as candidate boundary conditions. The most defensible conclusion is therefore not that code-switching generally improves executive function, but that specific forms of regulated switching may be associated with specific executive processes in particular children. Longitudinal, ecologically valid, and better harmonized studies are required before causal or educational claims can be made.</jats:p>

title: Exploring the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence as a "Learning Scaffold" in Junior High School Students' Self-Regulated Learning
container-title: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
8852c321c745692ee238e92824943d5f5fd29736.abstract: <jats:p>As digital technology becomes more deeply embedded in education, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly present in junior high school students' daily learning. This paper explores the "scaffolding" role of GenAI in students' self-regulated learning (SRL) and its possible influence on enhancing academic self-efficacy. Based on Zimmerman's cyclical phase model of SRL and learning scaffolding theory, the study systematically deduces the human-AI interaction process. The analysis suggests that GenAI acts as planning, monitoring, and reflective feedback scaffolds across the forethought, performance, and self-reflection phases, effectively addressing the lack of personalized support in traditional autonomous learning. Furthermore, GenAI assistance contributes to the internalization of academic self-efficacy by accumulating direct mastery experiences and alleviating trial-and-error anxiety. Acknowledging the potential risks of cognitive offloading and academic misconduct associated with GenAI dependency, the paper proposes coping strategies such as cultivating students' critical GenAI literacy and implementing dynamic scaffold fading. This research provides theoretical support and practical guidance for educators to optimize GenAI-assisted self-regulated learning environments.</jats:p>

title: Selecting Cooling Architectures for High-Density AI Data Centres
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
13867b477e89fe2a96c46275f080027c2bda15cf.abstract: <jats:p>Rising power concentration in artificial intelligence servers has made cooling architecture a primary design constraint for high-density data centres. This paper compares recent peer-reviewed studies of air cooling, direct-to-chip cold plates, single- and two-phase immersion, and their environmental effects. The findings show that liquid cooling expands the thermal operating envelope of high-power hardware, although the size of the benefit depends on the measurement boundary. Direct-to-chip systems can retain a substantial air-side load, warmer coolant may increase server power, and immersion performance varies with flow distribution, fluid properties, and hardware design. Facility-level outcomes also depend on climate, electricity supply, water source, coolant production, and equipment lifetime. Cooling options should therefore be compared under a common workload and system boundary. Optimised air remains suitable for moderate-density or legacy facilities, direct-to-chip cooling provides a practical route for many high-density racks, and immersion is best suited to cases where exceptional heat density and purpose-built infrastructure justify changes to hardware and maintenance.</jats:p>

title: AI-Assisted Adaptive Interface Design for Lowering Entry Barriers in Real-Time Strategy Games
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
261cd914c24b8aed2dfbb25fe91dae18d6978867.abstract: <jats:p>Real-time strategy (RTS) games require players to make strategic decisions while executing numerous commands. This paper presents a qualitative synthesis of recent academic research on game accessibility, human–Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistance, interface design, and community content. Six design directions are examined against accessibility, strategic depth, long-term engagement, and practical value. A layered control model is proposed with beginner, traditional, and competitive profiles sharing the same strategic rules. Routine automation requires player approval and remains visible and reversible, while tutoring uses information available to the player. Cooperative practice, hybrid interactions, and community content are considered as supporting design contexts. A conceptual mission walkthrough examines how the model could separate repeated operations from consequential decisions. The analysis yields design requirements and testable hypotheses; no prototype or new participant experiment was conducted. Controlled player studies, including unassisted transfer tasks and return-session measures, are needed to determine whether the model lowers entry barriers while preserving strategic depth.</jats:p>

title: Efficacy of AI in the diagnosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma from clinical images: A systematic review and meta-analysis
container-title: Annals of the Academy of Medicine Singapore
55d0133adc92293d29021b700330577fd33c6c47.abstract:
<jats:p>Introduction: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a common malignancy that is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages, partly because of limitations in conventional diagnostic approaches. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models in detecting OSCC from clinical images.

Methods: PubMed, ScienceDirect, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from January 2000 to September 2024. Studies assessing the diagnostic accuracy of AI models for OSCC using clinical images were included. Studies that did not involve clinical images, were not specific to OSCC, or were not published in English were excluded. In accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, study selection was performed independently by 4 reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus. Subsequently, diagnostic accuracy data were extracted, risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies using AI, and thematic analysis was performed by 2 reviewers. Where appropriate, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted.

Results: Nine studies comprising 47,987 oral clinical images were included, with 6 studies in the meta-analysis. AI models demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.94 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87–0.97), specificity of 0.95 (95% CI 0.86–0.98), and an area under the curve of 0.975 (95% bootstrap CI 0.911–0.986). AI systems generally achieved higher diagnostic accuracy than general practitioners and performance comparable to specialists under controlled study conditions.

Conclusion: AI models show strong diagnostic performance for OSCC detection from clinical images. However, current evidence is largely derived from retrospective and heterogeneous datasets without external validation. Prospective and blinded studies are required to determine their role as decision-support tools in real-world settings.</jats:p>

title: National AI Strategies and the Green Transition: Cross-Country Evidence from Staggered Difference-in-Differences and Double Machine Learning
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
18d2a178b8fa138df5c3a849ab66f5cc1913d7f8.abstract: <jats:p>National artificial intelligence (AI) strategies have proliferated since 2017, yet whether they advance the green transition remains unknown. We exploit the staggered adoption of national AI strategies by 59 countries within an 85-country panel over 2000–2021, combining two-way fixed effects (TWFE), Callaway–Sant'Anna difference-in-differences, and double machine learning (DML). Strategy adoption raises the renewable energy share of consumption by 1.87 percentage points in fixed-effects estimates and by 1.47 points in dynamic event-study aggregation, and reduces the CO₂ intensity of GDP (−0.026 kg per 2017 PPP dollar), a result corroborated by a significant decline in CO₂ emissions per capita. In contrast, we find no robust effect on the share of environment-related patents: pre-trends are rejected and point estimates switch sign across estimators. Green-patenting effects are concentrated, albeit imprecisely, in high-income economies, and carbon-intensity reductions are larger where renewable endowments are high. DML estimates for green patenting are sensitive to the choice of learner. National AI strategies appear to green the energy mix before they green the innovation base.</jats:p>

title: From EEG Classification to Personalized Neurofeedback: An Explainable AI Framework for Alzheimer's Disease
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
15826c011ae5b849d03e8be5dd37e202ae56c6b2.abstract: <jats:p>This study developed an explainable machine learning (ML) framework for Alzheimer's disease classification using resting-state EEG-BCI recordings from the OpenNeuro ds004504 cohort, which consists of 36 patients with AD and 29 Healthy Control (HC). Four EEG biomarkers and a normative-deviation score are integrated with feature weighting and logistic classification, while SHAP, gradient saliency, and layer-wise relevance propagation provide complementary explanations of model predictions. The performance of the framework was evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation and a locked 15-subject holdout set (8 AD, 7 HC). The model achieved a mean cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.823 ± 0.095 and a holdout ROC-AUC of 0.929. The Explainable AI (XAI) feature attribution identified posterior alpha power, alpha peak frequency, and frontal theta/beta ratio as significant discriminators between AD and HC (p < 0.05), with posterior alpha power showing the strongest association with classification (p < 0.001). Posterior alpha power alone achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.900 ± 0.074. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using explainable AI to extract important spectral features that can distinguish AD from healthy controls and may inform the future development of adaptive neurofeedback protocols tailored to individual brain patterns. However, a larger and more diverse data set is needed for future studies of real-time, personalized neurofeedback applications.</jats:p>

title: Based on Personalized Content: Addressing Homogenization in AI-Supported Learning Through the Smart Mistake Solver
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
f56143676e29ab45adf9be52f314b12afa86fb31.abstract: <jats:p>The adoption of artificial intelligence allows for an advancement in personalized learning, since the development of diverse types of learning materials and content may not succeed in always developing highly personalized experience. This article will explore personalized learning in relation to the homogeneity of a course program design based on an example of the Smart Mistake Solver program, an artificial intelligence learning assistance tool, which detects and corrects students' mistakes while dealing with math problems. The process of error detection, student model created with the help of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) and development of personalized content are crucial aspects of the artificial intelligence support in learning. The conceptual analysis of Smart Mistake Solver demonstrates the limitations of artificial intelligence in enhancing personalized learning, which are conditioned by the necessity to use a list of predestined errors and measurable performance metrics. In conclusion, it was found that meaningful personalization should occur with respect to the specific needs of each learner within a learning experience along with distinction of learning materials; these cannot be fully met in all cases with the help of artificial intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Lower cerebrovascular reactivity in HIV-associated cognitive impairment: compared with normal aging and vascular cognitive impairment
container-title: NeuroImmune Pharmacology and Therapeutics
b7b6013c810a5656beb0317decbaf8ad10b9fd67.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Older people living with HIV (PWH) have a higher risk for HIV-associated cognitive impairment, which may be exacerbated by age-related cerebrovascular disorders. However, the pathophysiology underlying the cognitive impairment in PWH remains unclear. The goal of this study is to evaluate cerebrovascular dysfunction in PWH and investigate its relationship with cognition.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_002">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cross-sectional study included 83 eligible subjects (ages 50–81 years) who completed MRI scans. Cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) was assessed using blood-oxygenation-level-dependent functional MRI (BOLD-fMRI) during a 5 % carbon dioxide inhalation (hypercapnia challenge). A global cognitive measure of Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and a battery of neuropsychological tests were also performed to assess their cognitive status.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Quality-assured CVR scans were obtained from 63 subjects (22 PWH, 41 non-HIV controls), who were divided into 4 groups: 11 PWH without symptomatic cognitive impairment (PWH-sCI–), 11 PWH with symptomatic cognitive impairment (PWH-sCI+), 23 non-HIV controls with normal cognition (non-HIV-NC), and 18 non-HIV controls with cognitive impairment (non-HIV-CI). HIV status was associated with relatively lower regional gray matter CVR in the frontal lobe (p=0.001), parietal lobe (p=0.003), and basal ganglia (p=0.001), indicating cerebrovascular dysfunction in these brain regions in PWH compared to the non-HIV controls. Lower whole-brain and regional gray matter CVR were significantly associated with worse global cognition measured by MoCA in older PWH (p<0.037).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_004">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings provided direct evidence that cerebrovascular dysfunction is associated with cognitive impairment in aging PWH, suggesting CVR is a promising candidate imaging biomarker of cerebrovascular dysfunction associated with cognitive impairment in PWH.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial generativa y su relación con el rendimiento académico en carreras de negocios a nivel superior
The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence and Its Relationship to Academic Performance in Business Programs at the Higher Education Level
container-title: Revista Científica Ciencia y Método
c7a6b6c5246fb9a95e9dc8afe69d3370331ab19e.abstract: <jats:p>The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into higher education raises questions about its use and its relationship to academic performance, especially given the lack of contextualized evidence. The objective was to describe patterns of use and perceptions of the usefulness, benefits, and risks of GAI among students in the School of Business Administration at the Chimborazo Polytechnic University. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, and descriptive study was conducted, incorporating exploratory correlational analysis; 280 students selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling participated by completing an online survey. Eighty-seven point five percent had used IAG for studying, 80.9% reported using it always or frequently, and 84.7% perceived improvements in their academic performance. Frequency of use was moderately associated with perceived usefulness (ρ = 0.539; p < 0.001). However, concerns were identified regarding a decline in critical thinking (34.6%) and dependency (26.4%). These findings reflect favorable acceptance but do not demonstrate objective improvements or causal relationships. It is concluded that their institutional integration requires digital literacy, ethical guidelines, and assessments based on learning outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Conceptualizing cognitive load as motivational cost: a mixed methods perspective
container-title: Instructional Science
d9558edd00cfd5db59203400e7b1047bb082ca47.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Through the theoretical lens of cognitive load theory and expectancy-value-cost theory, this exploratory mixed methods study examines the associations between cognitive load and motivational and affective constructs. This study evaluates the experiences of Ph.D. students in the biological sciences, particularly those involving motivational constructs and costs, and how these costs can be conceptualized as unproductive cognitive load (i.e., extraneous cognitive load). In this study, semi-structured interviews (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 80) were drawn from a separate longitudinal study and coded using a grounded theory approach. Using the qualitative codes, frequencies of co-occurrence were evaluated using Spearman’s rho. Results indicate that common sources of unhelpful or unproductive cognitive load (e.g., via lack of support, guidance, and/or instruction from professors and advisors) are differentially associated with value, expectancy, and motivational costs (particularly overwhelm). Specifically, extraneous cognitive load is significantly correlated with low expectancy for success (i.e., low self-efficacy), subjective task value, and overwhelm. These findings are consistent with the emerging understanding of relationships between cognitive load type and motivation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity in Higher Education: A Comparative Study of Students and Academic Staff
905a2abf00a86d0c53f0e66140442bee60836f03.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, is transforming teaching and learning practices in higher education while also raising important concerns about academic integrity, transparency, ethics, and the responsible use of AI. This study examines and compares the perceptions and practices of students and academic staff regarding generative AI, with particular attention to AI use, academic integrity, institutional ambiguity, transparency, and citation practices. The study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected through a structured, paper-based questionnaire administered in person to 202 participants at Kadri Zeka University in Kosovo, including 168 students and 34 academic staff members. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and an independent-samples t -test. The findings revealed statistically significant differences between students and academic staff across most of the dimensions examined. Academic staff reported a higher overall frequency of AI use, greater perceived institutional ambiguity, more critical attitudes toward AI use in relation to academic integrity, and stronger support for transparency. In contrast, students reported greater use of AI for academic purposes and more tolerant attitudes toward its use. No statistically significant differences were found between the two groups regarding the perceived importance of academic integrity or citation practices. These findings highlight the need for clearer institutional policies and shared standards for the transparent and responsible use of generative AI in higher education.

title: Diagnostic and prognostic values of selected biomarkers as a vital indicator in critically ill patients
container-title: Journal of Critical Care Medicine
69c5e19ea31920e47cb17510b624e57fffea8a87.abstract:
<jats:p>Objectives: The accurate diagnosis and prognostic assessment of Critically ill patients with pneumonia remain challenging, necessitating the evaluation of multiple biomarkers to enhance clinical decision-making. This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic and prognostic value of interleukin-6 (IL-6), procalcitonin (PCT), C-reactive protein (CRP), selenium, lactate, soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), and peptidyl arginine deiminase 2 (PAD2), and to determine their associations with disease severity and mortality.
Methods: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted on 130 critically ill pneumonia patients and 45 non-critically ill outpatient controls. Biomarker levels were assessed using ELISA, PCR, and standard biochemical assays, and correlated with severity indices and clinical outcomes.
Results: Lactate, PCT, CRP, IL-6, and PAD2 levels were significantly elevated in patients versus controls (p < 0.001), with higher levels observed in non-survivors (p < 0.001) except for PAD2 levels  were not significantly associated with survival status (p = 0.346). Although suPAR and selenium differed between patients and controls, they did not distinguish survivors from non-survivors. suPAR correlated positively with PCT, while PAD2 showed significant associations with inflammatory markers and severity scores. No biomarker demonstrated superior prognostic accuracy.
Conclusion: Lactate, PCT, CRP, IL-6, and PAD2 exhibit diagnostic relevance in pneumonia. Several biomarkers, including IL-6 gene expression, IL-6, CRP, PCT, and lactate, demonstrated excellent prognostic discrimination (AUC >0.95). However, comparative ROC analysis revealed no statistically significant superiority of any single biomarker over the others, suggesting that a multimarker approach may provide greater clinical value than reliance on an individual marker.</jats:p>

8cd514972f04965b968b2d5010a2ca45fd437b93.abstract: <jats:p>Мета дослідження – обґрунтувати дидактичний потенціал генеративних мовних моделей у фаховій іншомовній підготовці та розробити операціоналізовану систему ризиків, яка пов’язує кожну загрозу з конкретною компенсаторною методичною стратегією. Методологічну основу становить теоретико-аналітичний дизайн із двопрохідним змістовим аналізом джерельного корпусу, таксономічним згортанням виявлених положень, порівняльно-зіставним аналізом результатів із різних освітніх контекстів і моделюванням дидактичних рішень. Установлено, що специфіка фахової іншомовної підготовки визначається подвійною вимогою: мовною нормативністю та відповідністю професійно-дискурсивним конвенціям. За результатами першого проходу змістового аналізу виокремлено шість кластерів дидактичних афордансів: генерування фахового входу, формувальний зворотний зв’язок, симуляція професійної інтеракції, підтримка продуктивних умінь, розширення термінологічного репертуару та автоматизація дидактичного проєктування. Другий прохід дав чотирирівневу таксономію ризиків – когнітивно-навчальних, змістово-епістемічних, етико-академічних та інституційно-професійних. На цій основі побудовано матрицю «афорданс – домінантний ризик – компенсаторна стратегія», шестиступеневу шкалу когнітивного делегування D0–D5 та архітектуру оцінювання, що поєднує контрольовані завдання без доступу до генеративних систем, завдання з декларованим їх використанням і критико-верифікаційні завдання. Наукова новизна полягає в системному поєднанні дидактичних можливостей і ризиків у межах однієї моделі та в розширенні структури промпт-інженерної компетентності метакогнітивно-верифікаційним компонентом. Практичне значення результатів полягає у можливості використовувати запропоновану матрицю, шкалу D0–D5 і дескриптори верифікації під час проєктування завдань, оцінювання студентських робіт і формування локальної політики академічної доброчесності у закладах вищої освіти.</jats:p>

title: Taxing working memory shifts the balance from goals to stimulus-response habits
f6ec643f5db85219f3db8d59fd7ce83a4fa503b8.abstract: Despite our familiarity with the concept of habits, eliciting and measuring habitual “slips of action” experimentally in humans has proven to be difficult. A possible explanation is that participants in psychological experiments actively recruit goal-directed control and therefore make few habitual slips-of-action in the presence of stimuli signalling devalued outcomes. In the current experiment we used the symmetrical outcome-revaluation task in combination with a working memory load in an attempt to tip the balance from goal-directed control to stimulus-response habit. During the instrumental learning phase, participants learned to make a Go response to stimuli signalling valuable outcomes (and points) while not responding (NoGo) to stimuli signalling not-valuable outcomes. During the subsequent test phase, the outcomes signalled by the stimuli were either value-congruent with training (still-valuable and still-not-valuable), or value-incongruent (devalued and upvalued). Participants had to flexibly adjust their behaviour on value-incongruent trials where the stimulus-response association learned during training was no longer appropriate. For half the participants, a concurrent working memory load was imposed during the test phase. In line with our preregistered hypotheses, participants showed evidence for habitual slips of action across two experiments, but those under working memory load showed increased habit tendencies (specifically failures to inhibit prepotent Go responses in the presence of stimuli signalling devalued outcomes). This central finding suggests that a working memory load can be used to reveal habits in humans.

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
f171216399a007e7c399c672df322f23f7504b96.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title: The Autonomous Learner; Decoding Cognitive Logic of Generation Z in the Sri Lankan Advanced Level Classroom
container-title: Adhyapana Prathibha
66c36a7cdf6e51d9fdecfc4ac37f940042bdf340.abstract: <jats:p>The Advanced Level (AL) classroom in the modern era is no longer a site of passive reception but a dynamic ecosystem of negotiation and cognitive autonomy. This paper explores the behavioral and cognitive shifts within Generation Z (Gen Z) individuals born between 1997 and 2012, who currently occupy the 17-to-19-year-old cohort in Sri Lanka (Dimock, 2019). Despite geographical, cultural & subject streamwise specificities, Sri Lankan Advance level students are increasingly bridging cultural disparities through digitalization, adopting a globalized "digital-native" logic. This article analyzes the "Authenticity Filter," the "Fast Brain" paradox, and the transition from instruction-following to instruction-making, arguing that modern pedagogy must direct toward relationship-based facilitation.</jats:p>

title: Beyond TAM: a mediated-moderated analysis of perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust as catalysts for AI adoption
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
6da4b5961b80fb182f0f7449a891d8ffaa5aa46f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines customers’ adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Jordanian telecommunications sector by extending the technology acceptance model (TAM). Specifically, it aims to investigate the effects of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism on actual use of AI, while testing customer intention as a mediator and technology trust as a moderator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative approach was employed. Data were collected through self-administered questionnaires from customers of telecommunications companies in Jordan. Using stratified random sampling, 482 questionnaires were distributed, and 438 valid responses were analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling using SmartPLS 4 was applied to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, mediation effects and moderation effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism significantly and positively influence customers’ intention to adopt AI, whereas perceived usefulness has no significant effect. Customer intention significantly predicts actual AI use and mediates the relationships between perceived ease of use, perceived anthropomorphism and actual AI use. However, intention does not mediate the relationship between perceived usefulness and actual AI use. Technology trust significantly moderates the relationship between customer intention and actual AI use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Telecom providers should design AI-enabled services that are simple, intuitive, human-like and trustworthy. Managers should also communicate the tangible benefits of AI more clearly to strengthen customers’ usefulness perceptions and encourage sustained usage.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends TAM by integrating perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust into a mediated-moderated model of AI adoption in an underexplored Middle Eastern telecommunications context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The challenge of AI dependence: exploring its impact on cognitive autonomy and elaboration in creative performance
container-title: Information Technology & People
5d10468ae5a26c2d8ac92ce1ad78fb5842569e0a.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As artificial intelligence advances and its application scenarios continue to expand, human–artificial intelligence interaction grows increasingly close. While artificial intelligence brings convenience, it also raises concerns that it may weaken users' cognitive autonomy. To investigate this issue. This study aims to explore the composition of AI dependence and its impact on cognitive autonomy and specific aspects of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study draws on cognitive evaluation theory and the elaboration likelihood model to construct a dual-pathway model with instrumental dependence and affective dependence as core variables. The model explains the formation mechanisms of the two types of artificial intelligence dependence and their differential effects on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily examines their potential role in the elaboration dimension of creative performance. A two-stage mixed-method design was employed to test the model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Study 1 found that perceived trust mainly had a positive effect on instrumental dependence. Different dimensions of interactivity differentially affected affective dependence and cognitive autonomy. Mediation analysis further confirmed the core mediating role of Dependence. Study 2, a small-sample exploratory experiment, re-tested selected hypotheses and found a possible negative effect of instrumental dependence on the elaboration dimension of creative performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The main theoretical contribution of this study lies in revealing the dual-pathway formation mechanisms of artificial intelligence dependence and the reshaping effects of different types of dependence on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily explores the potential effects of dependence on elaboration performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>

title: Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Causally Supports the Memory Advantage of Reading Aloud
1403e8a8d1a1df5ab3ce67d956e96cf3822ce4bf.abstract: Reading words aloud improves later recognition relative to reading them silently, a phenomenon known as the production effect. This advantage may reflect not only the distinctive sensorimotor information generated by production, but also cognitive control processes that prioritise this information during encoding. Given the central role of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) in supporting cognitive control, we tested whether this region causally contributes to the production effect using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). In a preregistered within-participant study, 40 adults completed three sessions in which TMS was delivered bilaterally to the DLPFC. They received continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS), expected to reduce DLPFC excitability; intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), expected to increase it; or sham stimulation. Participants then read words aloud or silently before completing an old/new recognition test with confidence and recollection judgements. There was a clear production effect: words read aloud were recognised more accurately and quickly, with greater confidence and more frequent recollection ratings, than words read silently. Crucially, cTBS reduced the accuracy advantage for aloud words relative to sham and iTBS. Exploratory receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) and unequal-variance signal-detection (UVSD) modeling approaches provided converging evidence that cTBS reduced the memory advantage for words read aloud. Stimulation did not reliably affect responses to new words. These findings provide the first causal evidence that the DLPFC helps make words read aloud more memorable, consistent with a role for cognitive control in prioritising the distinctive information generated by speaking.

title: Taxing working memory shifts the balance from goals to stimulus-response habits
219b8e86120ef541ec2ab6258272e25a46c32817.abstract: Despite our familiarity with the concept of habits, eliciting and measuring habitual “slips of action” experimentally in humans has proven to be difficult. A possible explanation is that participants in psychological experiments actively recruit goal-directed control and therefore make few habitual slips-of-action in the presence of stimuli signalling devalued outcomes. In the current experiment we used the symmetrical outcome-revaluation task in combination with a working memory load in an attempt to tip the balance from goal-directed control to stimulus-response habit. During the instrumental learning phase, participants learned to make a Go response to stimuli signalling valuable outcomes (and points) while not responding (NoGo) to stimuli signalling not-valuable outcomes. During the subsequent test phase, the outcomes signalled by the stimuli were either value-congruent with training (still-valuable and still-not-valuable), or value-incongruent (devalued and upvalued). Participants had to flexibly adjust their behaviour on value-incongruent trials where the stimulus-response association learned during training was no longer appropriate. For half the participants, a concurrent working memory load was imposed during the test phase. In line with our preregistered hypotheses, participants showed evidence for habitual slips of action across two experiments, but those under working memory load showed increased habit tendencies (specifically failures to inhibit prepotent Go responses in the presence of stimuli signalling devalued outcomes). This central finding suggests that a working memory load can be used to reveal habits in humans.

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
b9ccdb38f6597ed3e62466f34e81e1c68972ba14.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title: Phenylbutyrate improves recognition memory and increases dendritic spines in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus in hypertensive female rats
container-title: Brain Structure and Function
233482833a48c8f54c415c40ac3ebfc26f8516b8.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hypertension and aging are two major global health challenges. They frequently coexist, presenting with aging-related neuronal alterations which are exacerbated under hypertensive conditions. In the present study, we utilized female, 12-month-old spontaneously hypertensive (SH) rats as a translational animal model of combined hypertension and aging. Phenylbutyrate (PB), a compound with reported anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties was evaluated for its effects on recognition memory and dendritic architecture. PB treatment significantly improved both short- and long-term recognition memory, as assessed by the novel object recognition test. At the structural level, PB increased dendritic spine density in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and in multiple subregions of the dorsal hippocampus, including CA1, CA3, and the dentate gyrus. Moreover, PB selectively enhanced the proportion of mature spine phenotypes, increasing mushroom and bifurcated spines in the PFC and hippocampal subregions examined. Together, these findings indicate that PB mitigates recognition memory decline and preserves dendritic spine density and morphology in cortico-hippocampal circuits in this animal model. Our results support PB as a potential therapeutic strategy for neurocognitive dysfunction associated with the comorbidity of hypertension and aging.</jats:p>

title:
Reducing Sampling
Effort for Mapping Air Pollution:
A Two-Stage Framework
container-title: ACS ES&T Air
4ab7e87c78f98030c9083792eb2fa1effa546a03.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mobile monitoring is essential for resolving intraurban air pollution gradients, yet its scalability is constrained by the intensive sampling required to produce stable concentration maps. Here, we develop a screen-and-target two-stage framework to help reduce the effort of mapping hyperlocal air pollution. Using large mobile-monitoring data sets from Shenzhen and Macau, we combined spatially constrained segmentation models with land-use machine learning to evaluate how sampling effort affects air pollution mapping stability. Mean NO2 higher-lower (binary) concentration zone classification agreement first exceeded 80% at 3% of randomly sampled observations in Shenzhen and 15% in Macau. Random selection of whole measurement days required more effort for the same agreement level: 27.7% of observations (8 days) in Macau and 22.6% (30 days) in Shenzhen. Land-use machine learning achieved 80% of the total reduction in prediction error with 25–36% road-network coverage across pollutants, but errors remained high in large unsampled areas. Under the same sampling effort, the screen-and-target strategy reduced road-segment NO2 estimation error by 18–32% relative to conventional uniform sampling, whereas its zone maps improved mainly at low effort (≤20% of the campaign effort). These findings can guide resource-efficient sampling strategies for mapping and mitigation of air pollution in cities.</jats:p>
