title: Integrating AI General Education with Digital Literacy Cultivation and Cognitive Construction in Industry-Specific Universities
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
ed572e57c1cc41bc9396ae2882f5f643647c0276.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence has evolved into a general-purpose technology that permeates nearly every corner of knowledge production and social governance. This transformation is pushing college students' digital literacy far beyond the traditional "digitization" benchmark toward what this paper terms "intelligent-digital" literacy. For industry-specific universities—institutions committed to serving specific industries and cultivating application-oriented talents—the significance of AI general education is perhaps even greater than for other types of universities, because their graduates directly enter the industrial chain. Taking the practice of Moutai Institute as a concrete case, this paper elaborates on the internal logic, practical challenges, and feasible pathways for integrating AI general education into students' digital literacy cultivation and cognitive construction. The core argument of this paper is that such education should be anchored in industrial scenarios rather than abstract theory, and that cultivating compound talents equipped with digital literacy, industrial awareness, and social responsibility requires simultaneously grasping three main threads: technological empowerment, value guidance, and cognitive construction. On this basis, this paper proposes a trinity integration framework and offers actionable strategies from four dimensions: curriculum system, teaching model, faculty development, and evaluation mechanism. This paper aims to provide theoretical reference and practical insights for general education reform in industry-specific universities.</jats:p>

title: Does Bilingual Code-Switching Enhance Executive Function in Children? A Focused Review of When and under What Conditions Cognitive Benefits Emerge
container-title: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
bd62b75a4cfe050f48f813b62ed113b68438e32a.abstract: <jats:p>Research on the bilingual executive-function advantage has produced positive, null, and inverse findings. One likely reason is that bilingualism is often treated as a uniform category, even though children differ substantially in how they use their languages. This focused critical review examines whether code-switching, rather than bilingual status alone, is associated with cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control in children and identifies the conditions under which benefits are most plausible. Eleven peer-reviewed sources were selected from the project's literature corpus to provide theoretical foundations, broad child-level syntheses, methodological critiques, and direct evidence. The evidence does not support a universal code-switching advantage. Direct child studies report a conditional positive association, a null association, and an inverse association; another study shows that the relation between language control and cognitive control may also operate in the opposite direction. Across this literature, language ability, interactional context, switching type, task choice, and age emerge as candidate boundary conditions. The most defensible conclusion is therefore not that code-switching generally improves executive function, but that specific forms of regulated switching may be associated with specific executive processes in particular children. Longitudinal, ecologically valid, and better harmonized studies are required before causal or educational claims can be made.</jats:p>

title: Application Patterns and Educational Effects of Intelligent Tutoring Systems for Memory Learning in K-12 Education
container-title: Applied and Computational Engineering
42f64ebfd1e94c2fcc25240635ee685c92f4bdf4.abstract: <jats:p>It is crucial for K-12 students to find a way to remember the information they have learned, particularly when working with an intelligent tutoring system. In order to learn more about how intelligent tutoring systems can assist them in this process, the literature review was conducted in relation to documents that were published between the dates of January 1st 2018 and August 31st 2026. The methods that were studied include spaced practice, AI-based question creation, visual flashcards, and gamification. Various outcomes were obtained from the studies; the textbooks that were studied on the subject of spaced practice and visual flashcards offered information on retaining vocabulary, while studies examining the art of question formulation provided information about the practice of retrieval and feedback technique. However, investigations into the gamification of intelligent tutoring systems mainly examined how effective the system is in terms of how engaged learners were with the learning material. Therefore, all of the studies were conducted with different samples and settings. In the general sense, it can be said that using computer-assisted instruction properly is one of the most effective methods of memory retention learning in K-12 education, which provides the strongest effectiveness in the area of vocabulary retention.</jats:p>

title: Lower cerebrovascular reactivity in HIV-associated cognitive impairment: compared with normal aging and vascular cognitive impairment
container-title: NeuroImmune Pharmacology and Therapeutics
b7b6013c810a5656beb0317decbaf8ad10b9fd67.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Older people living with HIV (PWH) have a higher risk for HIV-associated cognitive impairment, which may be exacerbated by age-related cerebrovascular disorders. However, the pathophysiology underlying the cognitive impairment in PWH remains unclear. The goal of this study is to evaluate cerebrovascular dysfunction in PWH and investigate its relationship with cognition.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_002">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cross-sectional study included 83 eligible subjects (ages 50–81 years) who completed MRI scans. Cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) was assessed using blood-oxygenation-level-dependent functional MRI (BOLD-fMRI) during a 5 % carbon dioxide inhalation (hypercapnia challenge). A global cognitive measure of Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and a battery of neuropsychological tests were also performed to assess their cognitive status.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Quality-assured CVR scans were obtained from 63 subjects (22 PWH, 41 non-HIV controls), who were divided into 4 groups: 11 PWH without symptomatic cognitive impairment (PWH-sCI–), 11 PWH with symptomatic cognitive impairment (PWH-sCI+), 23 non-HIV controls with normal cognition (non-HIV-NC), and 18 non-HIV controls with cognitive impairment (non-HIV-CI). HIV status was associated with relatively lower regional gray matter CVR in the frontal lobe (p=0.001), parietal lobe (p=0.003), and basal ganglia (p=0.001), indicating cerebrovascular dysfunction in these brain regions in PWH compared to the non-HIV controls. Lower whole-brain and regional gray matter CVR were significantly associated with worse global cognition measured by MoCA in older PWH (p<0.037).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_nipt-2026-0024_abs_004">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings provided direct evidence that cerebrovascular dysfunction is associated with cognitive impairment in aging PWH, suggesting CVR is a promising candidate imaging biomarker of cerebrovascular dysfunction associated with cognitive impairment in PWH.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Conceptualizing cognitive load as motivational cost: a mixed methods perspective
container-title: Instructional Science
d9558edd00cfd5db59203400e7b1047bb082ca47.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Through the theoretical lens of cognitive load theory and expectancy-value-cost theory, this exploratory mixed methods study examines the associations between cognitive load and motivational and affective constructs. This study evaluates the experiences of Ph.D. students in the biological sciences, particularly those involving motivational constructs and costs, and how these costs can be conceptualized as unproductive cognitive load (i.e., extraneous cognitive load). In this study, semi-structured interviews (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 80) were drawn from a separate longitudinal study and coded using a grounded theory approach. Using the qualitative codes, frequencies of co-occurrence were evaluated using Spearman’s rho. Results indicate that common sources of unhelpful or unproductive cognitive load (e.g., via lack of support, guidance, and/or instruction from professors and advisors) are differentially associated with value, expectancy, and motivational costs (particularly overwhelm). Specifically, extraneous cognitive load is significantly correlated with low expectancy for success (i.e., low self-efficacy), subjective task value, and overwhelm. These findings are consistent with the emerging understanding of relationships between cognitive load type and motivation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Hippocampal event updating and narrative relation-map updating during naturalistic memory encoding and retrieval
698e2b8eee695ce669f03dcb8d0284b9861ea910.abstract: Naturalistic memory depends on whether an event can be recalled and how accurately its original memory state is reinstated during successful recall. However, how brain-state changes around event transitions and changes in story relationships relate to these aspects of memory remains unclear. Here, we analysed functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 24 participants who viewed and freely recalled 43 naturalistic narrative events, measuring post-boundary hippocampal state changes and changes in narrative relationships. We found that larger late hippocampal state changes predicted successful event recall, with the effect confined to a specific post-boundary window. Among successfully recalled events, larger changes in narrative relationships were associated with more accurate reinstatement of hippocampal states. The relative associations of the two types of change also differed between memory outcomes. These findings suggest that brain-state updating and narrative-relation updating provide complementary perspectives on memory formation and reinstatement under naturalistic conditions.

                    <jats:p>To observe the effects of intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) combined with hyperbaric oxygen therapy on cognitive function and cortical hemodynamics in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Sixty patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment were randomly assigned to an observation group and a control group (30 cases per group). All patients received hyperbaric oxygen therapy and routine cognitive training for 6 weeks, while the observation group additionally received intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS). Before and after the intervention, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) was used to assess global cognitive function, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to detect task-evoked cortical oxygenated hemoglobin (Oxy-Hb) responses, including prefrontal Oxy-Hb integral values and channel-wise Oxy-Hb
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      values representing cortical activation intensity. Paired
                      <jats:italic>t</jats:italic>
                      -tests were used for within-group comparisons of pre- and post-treatment MMSE scores and prefrontal Oxy-Hb integral values. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with baseline values as covariates was performed for between-group comparisons after treatment. For channel-wise
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      values, a two-way mixed-design ANOVA was used to test group × time interactions, with group as a between-subject factor and time as a within-subject factor, followed by FDR-corrected simple effects analyses for
                      <jats:italic>post hoc</jats:italic>
                      comparisons.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups (all
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &gt; 0.05). No significant baseline differences were detected in MMSE scores, prefrontal Oxy-Hb integral values, or channel-wise Oxy-Hb
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      values (all
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &gt; 0.05). After the 6-week intervention, paired t-tests showed significant within-group increases in MMSE scores and prefrontal Oxy-Hb integral values in both groups (all
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.05). After adjusting for baseline values using ANCOVA, the observation group had significantly higher post-treatment MMSE scores and prefrontal Oxy-Hb integral values than the control group, indicating significant between-group treatment effects. title: Sericin attenuates diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction by inhibiting apoptosis and inflammation with involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
48df7a36ac9af756f805c199855a8b498d557f9c.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) is now acknowledged as a key complication of diabetes, whereas the precise pathological mechanisms remain unclear. Sericin, a naturally water-soluble protein complex extracted from silkworm cocoons, possesses glycemic-regulating and neuroprotective properties. This study aimed to investigate whether sericin could attenuate DACD via the PI3K/AKT pathway.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ)-induced diabetic Sprague-Dawley rat model was established. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 was used to verify pathway involvement. Effects of HFD/STZ induction and sericin treatment were evaluated by analyzing cognitive function, lipid profiles, and hippocampal apoptosis and inflammation markers via Morris water maze test, ELISA assays, Western blot, HE staining, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Diabetic rats exhibited hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and cognitive impairment, along with decreased p-PI3K, p-AKT, and Bcl-2 levels, and elevated levels of caspase-3, Bax, IL-1β, and IL-18 in the hippocampus, while NF-κB showed an increasing trend. Sericin treatment significantly ameliorated metabolic disorders, attenuated cognitive deficits, and reduced hippocampal apoptosis and neuroinflammation. Notably, the neuroprotective effects of sericin were partially reversed by LY294002, supporting the involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sericin intervention attenuates DACD by inhibiting neuronal apoptosis and inflammation with involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Thus, sericin might be a potential neuroprotective intervention for DACD.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Model Agnostic Meta-Learning based Adaptive DecoderA Cognitive Radio Approach

b32b1c6a34f9d1e1c88230734470121e14371d34.abstract: <jats:p>Conventional Deep Learning algorithms have had a significant impact on wireless communication, including channel estimation, signal decoding, power optimization, and resource allocation. However, the performance of the Conventional Deep Learning Model is limited when deployed in a dynamic environment due to slow convergence and the requirement for large datasets. To overcome these limitations, a novel Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML)-based decoding algorithm is developed in this work. The MAML-based algorithm requires fewer training samples and converges faster in new environments. Numerical findings confirm the benefits of employing meta-learning for signal decoding in wireless systems in a real-time scenario, achieving a minimum decoding accuracy of 80% under highly noisy conditions and 100% at moderate SNR. The data required for the proposed model are obtained from a practical setup using the National Instruments Universal Software Radio Peripheral (NI-USRP), and the performance of the proposed model is experimentally verified.</jats:p>

title: Periodic theta and spectral–memory relationships differentiate amnestic mild cognitive impairment from healthy aging
8fab7f13d2f746019f486bac921bb6c17c116d1a.abstract: BACKGROUND Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) carries an elevated risk of progression to Alzheimer's disease, yet no reliable resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) signature has separated it from healthy aging. Disease-related information may lie in spectral power itself, in how spectral activity relates to cognition, or in both. Standard analyses also conflate oscillatory changes with aperiodic background activity. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, we combined sensor- and individualized source-level analyses with spectral parameterization of high-density resting-state EEG from 150 participants (34 aMCI patients, 58 healthy older adults, 58 healthy younger adults) and tested how oscillatory activity related to memory within memory-network regions. RESULTS Both older groups showed higher beta and gamma power and flatter aperiodic slopes relative to younger adults, consistent with known aging effects. The clearest distinction between aMCI and healthy aging was in periodic theta. Patients showed higher theta than healthy older adults and resembled younger adults, an effect standard spectral analyses missed. Source-level gamma and beta power was associated with worse memory in aMCI but not healthy older adults, though only the precuneus beta difference was confirmed between groups. Age was more closely associated with slope flattening in patients than in healthy older adults. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that aMCI is distinguished from healthy aging not by the magnitude of spectral change, which the groups largely shared, but by specific alterations in oscillatory activity and its link to cognition. Elevated periodic theta and the altered precuneus beta–memory relationship stood out most and are promising markers for longitudinal work.

title: Associations between insomnia and suicidal ideation in depressed adolescents: the mediating effect of cognitive symptoms and sex differences
container-title: Frontiers in Psychiatry
ac743d4c2a06801f1eec99ea521f2b809aa0050d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among adolescents diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD), suicidal ideation (SI) may be closely linked to cognitive symptoms and insomnia. However, the potential pathways connecting these three factors remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the mediating role of cognitive symptoms between insomnia and SI, and to further examine whether this mediating pathway differs by sex.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2021 to September 2023, recruiting 332 adolescents diagnosed with MDD and 123 healthy controls (HCs). To assess depression severity, cognitive symptoms, insomnia, and suicidal ideation (SI), we administered the Clinical Global Impression – Severity Scale (CGI-S), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-24 (HAMD-24), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), and Positive and Negative Suicide Ideation inventory (PANSI), respectively. The PROCESS macro (Model 4) for SPSS was employed to perform mediation analysis, examining whether cognitive symptoms mediated the relationship between insomnia and SI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      SI was significantly more prevalent among adolescents with MDD than among their healthy counterparts. Within the MDD group, PANSI scores were negatively correlated with sex, age, and age of onset, but positively correlated with CGI-S, ISI, and HAMD-Cog scores (all
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001). These correlations were more pronounced among female patients. Mediation analysis demonstrated that cognitive symptoms, significantly mediated the relationship between insomnia severity (ISI) and suicidal ideation (PANSI). In the overall sample, the total effect, direct effect, and indirect effect values were 0.657 (95% CI: 0.452 - 0.863), 0.463 (95% CI: 0.279 - 0.647), and 0.195 (95% CI: 0.096 - 0.303), respectively. A sex-stratified analysis revealed a significant mediation effect among female patients, with total, direct, and indirect effect values of 0.734 (95% CI: 0.502 - 0.966), 0.539 (95% CI: 0.326 - 0.752), and 0.195 (95% CI: 0.088 - 0.315), respectively. Conversely, in male patients, neither the total nor the direct effects were statistically significant (confidence intervals included zero), and the indirect effect also lacked statistical significance (effect size: 0.132, 95% CI: -0.064 - 0.345), indicating that the mediating role of cognitive symptoms was not supported in this subgroup.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Adolescents with MDD exhibit elevated levels of SI, which is significantly associated with both cognitive symptoms and insomnia, particularly among females. Furthermore, cognitive symptoms could serve as a mediating factor in the link between insomnia and SI. This indirect effect was statistically significant in female patients, while results for male patients were inconclusive due to limited sample size. Consequently, in clinical practice, it is essential to understand the interconnected pathways linking insomnia, cognitive symptoms, and SI, with close attention to sex differences in the underlying mechanisms. This approach is crucial for enabling more precise risk assessment and targeted intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Understanding danmaku behaviour in esports live-streaming: insights from social cognitive theory

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the digital era, danmaku has become an important channel for real-time audience interaction and communication in esports live-streaming. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), this study examines the associations among viewing motivation, self-efficacy, sense of presence, and danmaku behaviour, as well as the proposed sequential indirect pathways linking these constructs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Viewing motivation was positively associated with danmaku behaviour, self-efficacy, and sense of presence. Self-efficacy was positively associated with both sense of presence and danmaku behaviour, while sense of presence was positively associated with danmaku behaviour. The mediation analysis further identified three statistically supported indirect pathways linking viewing motivation with danmaku behaviour: through self-efficacy, through sense of presence, and sequentially through self-efficacy and sense of presence.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>

title: Gender-differentiated effects of motion-enhanced AI-generated images in instructional videos: a mixed-process study using TAM-related perceptions and cognitive load theory
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
bc566f9cb1b938da7f71b0693c88ea1b882e4442.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    With the widespread adoption of online educational technologies, instructional videos have become a pivotal tool for flexible and efficient learning. The integration of visual aids, such as animations and dynamic elements, aims to enhance the learning experience; however, their effectiveness remains debated. This study examined learning performance and subjective experience when instructional videos presented static AI-generated images or manually animated versions of those images. A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 40 undergraduate participants (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 10 per cell), comparing static versus motion-enhanced presentation conditions across male and female participant groups. Stable Diffusion XL generated the base images, and CapCut was used to add motion; the motion itself was not AI-generated. Participants viewed a 140-s mobile video on mortise-and-tenon structures, completed a 10-item accuracy test, and rated willingness to continue learning, preference, acceptability, ease of understanding, and mental effort. The ANOVA results provided no statistically significant evidence of a main effect of motion on learning accuracy. Differences across gender groups were observed for several subjective outcomes. For acceptability, the gender × motion interaction was statistically significant, but Bonferroni-adjusted simple-effect tests supported a gender-group difference only in the static condition. For mental effort, the interaction was also statistically significant; adjusted simple-effect tests indicated higher mental effort among female than male participants in the dynamic condition and higher mental effort in the static than dynamic condition among male participants. title: Task exposure and stimulation duration modulate HD-tDCS effects on working memory in older adults
container-title: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
fcf28a076713fe10f51d4657b6ebce21f9e1f227.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Age-related working-memory decline has been associated with altered neural oscillations, and high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) may improve cognition. However, responses vary and may depend on prior task engagement and stimulation duration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We examined these factors in a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled crossover study of 39 healthy older adults (65.4 ± 3.0 years). Participants received real and sham 2-mA HD-tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for 10 or 20 min. Task exposure before real stimulation was determined by stimulation sequence, creating less- and more-exposure groups. Working-memory performance and EEG spectral power were assessed during two-back tasks before and after stimulation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Change in discrimination sensitivity (Δd’) showed a Stimulation × Duration × Exposure interaction. Exploratory comparisons indicated that 10-min real stimulation improved Δd’ relative to sham in the less-exposure group but reduced Δd’ in the more-exposure group; neither 20-min subgroup showed a significant effect. Secondary inverse-efficiency analyses showed improved efficiency after real stimulation under less exposure and poorer efficiency under more exposure. The more-exposure, 10-min group also showed increased central beta power following real stimulation. Associations between beta-power changes and poorer behavioral performance did not remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that HD-tDCS effects vary with stimulation duration and prior task context. However, the small subgroups and confounding of task exposure with stimulation order and session position require cautious interpretation. Larger studies independently manipulating exposure and stimulation order are needed to confirm these potentially state-dependent effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From cognitive relief to motivational enhancement: associations between perceived Agentic AI Capability and student engagement in systems development courses
container-title: Frontiers in Psychology
04eec25055c2932d7db3cc4a40bf906875b849e3.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI agents are increasingly emerging as important learning partners for supporting complex problem-solving in higher education; however, the psychological processes associated with student engagement remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in Cognitive Load Theory and Social Cognitive Theory, this study examines how perceived Agentic AI Capability is associated with students' extraneous cognitive load, academic self-efficacy, and overall student engagement in systems development courses. An empirical study was conducted among undergraduate students majoring in e-commerce who participated in systems development-related courses. The results indicate that perceived Agentic AI Capability is negatively associated with extraneous cognitive load and positively associated with academic self-efficacy. Extraneous cognitive load is negatively associated with academic self-efficacy and student engagement, whereas academic self-efficacy is positively associated with student engagement. The indirect associations through academic self-efficacy and the sequential pathway are statistically significant. The findings provide evidence on cognitive and motivational correlates of AI-supported learning while, given the cross-sectional design, not establishing causal or temporal relationships. This study extends the application of Cognitive Load Theory and Social Cognitive Theory to human–AI collaborative learning environments and provides theoretical insights and practical implications for integrating generative AI into systems development education.</jats:p>

title: A Reconfigurable Ferroelectric Acoustic Computational Primitive for Analog In-Memory Computing
c5816f678f094c3857c1d867849269aa299d73cc.abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence (AI) have renewed interest in emerging nonvolatile memory (eNVM) crossbar array technologies for in-memory computing to reduce the energy cost of moving data between processors and memory. Here we report a computational primitive that merges ferroelectric memory and acoustic resonators in a single platform: Ferroelectric memory Embedded in Nanoscale Acoustic resonators (FENA). We experimentally demonstrate over 100 nonvolatile analog admittance states arising from partial ferroelectric polarization switching in lithium niobate resonators. The devices exhibit highly symmetric potentiation and depression characteristics, which directly impact computation accuracy, favorable dynamic range and linearity, and low projected read and write energies after scaling. We further propose a radio frequency (RF) peripheral readout architecture that extracts frequency- and phase-sensitive effective conductance states to offer an expanded state space and hardware-level reconfigurability. System-level evaluation using the NeuroSim multi-layer perceptron (MLP) simulator demonstrates the suitability of FENA for both online and offline neural-network training, with scaled devices achieving competitive 84% and 92% classification accuracies, respectively.

title: Genetic Algorithm-Optimized LQR Control Strategy for Boosting Ethanol Production and Minimizing Control Effort
container-title: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
52dbbd49f6fb39a820e0f2828b8b715ee590c4d9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a novel control strategy for the dynamic optimization of ethanol fermentation using a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) whose gains are tuned via Genetic Algorithm (GA). The fermentation process, characterized by nonlinear and time-varying dynamics, demands advanced control strategies for optimal performance to maximize the production of ethanol and to minimize its environmental impact. A procedure for controlling the bioreactor's temperature is created because it is a crucial component of an effective process. Multiple evaluations conducted using genuine computational simulations are provided to confirm the efficacy of controlling techniques. A GA is employed to optimize the LQR's cost function matrices Q and R, aiming to minimize a composite performance index based on tracking error and control energy. The fitness function evaluates each candidate based on performance of various criteria such as Integration of Absolute Errors (IAE), Integral Time Squared Error (ITSE), Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE), and Integration of Square Errors (ISE). The simulation results demonstrate that the GA-optimized LQR outperforms conventionally tuned controllers in terms of ethanol yield, disturbance rejection, and system stability. This approach shows promise for scalable implementation in industrial biochemical process control.</jats:p>

title: Metformin regulates astrocyte autophagy via the AMPK/mTOR pathway to improve glutamate homeostasis and prevent cognitive impairment induced by cerebral ischemia-reperfusion
container-title: Frontiers in Pharmacology
0a84f3223a9cf2c439070210c4bab96b9af0a968.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury frequently causes cognitive dysfunction, and glutamate excitotoxicity induced by astrocyte overactivation is a core pathological mechanism. Autophagy exerts a critical regulatory effect on astrocyte function. This study aimed to investigate the preventive and protective effect of metformin (Met) against cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion‐induced cognitive impairment, and to elucidate how Met modulates astrocyte autophagy and glutamate homeostasis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:italic>In vivo</jats:italic>
                      , a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model was established;
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , an oxygen‐glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) injury model was constructed using U251 human astrocytoma cells. Each model included control, injury, Met treatment, and intervention groups co‐treated with AMPK inhibitor Compound C or autophagy inhibitor chloroquine. Cognitive function was assessed via behavioral tests. Pathological and ultrastructural alterations were examined by HE staining, Nissl staining and transmission electron microscopy. The expression and colocalization of GFAP, GLT‐1 and LC3B were detected by immunofluorescence. Western blot was performed to measure target protein levels, and hippocampal glutamate content was determined.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Met significantly improved cognitive function in MCAO/R rats, alleviated pathological damage and neuronal ultrastructural injury, suppressed hippocampal astrocyte overactivation, upregulated GLT‐1 expression and reduced glutamate accumulation in hippocampal tissue. Meanwhile, Met activated the AMPK/mTOR pathway and promoted autophagic flux, and autophagic changes were colocalized with astrocytes; consistent results were verified in U251 cells. These protective effects were reversed by both AMPK inhibitor and autophagy inhibitor.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Met pretreatment enhances astrocyte autophagy by activating the AMPK/mTOR pathway, which further upregulates GLT‐1 expression and improves glutamate homeostasis, ultimately ameliorating cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion‐induced cognitive dysfunction. These findings provide experimental evidence for the preventive and protective effects of Met against ischemic brain injury.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
container-title: Nature Communications
d7a3821d1678b618e797e03a0a9974f51c79cd5a.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry.</jats:p>

title: Hypergraph-Driven Robust Vision Framework with Calibrated Explainability for Reliable Skin Lesion Analysis
container-title: Cognitive Computation
bfd291da42a39c40e248b6071b23cf0c2b9bbff6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reliable automated skin lesion diagnosis remains challenging because deep learning systems often suffer from adversarial sensitivity, feature redundancy, poor calibration, and biased learning under imbalanced clinical data. This work introduces a unified framework named RA-HYPER-VISIONNet that combines hypergraph-guided representation learning with uncertainty-aware optimization to improve robustness, calibration, and interpretability in dermoscopic image analysis. The proposed architecture integrates adversarial distribution alignment, intrinsic explainability-guided feature refinement, Bayesian focal optimization, and transformer-based uncertainty fusion within a single learning pipeline. Unlike conventional post-hoc explanation methods, the framework embeds explanation consistency directly into feature learning to produce clinically meaningful predictions. Experiments were conducted on the ISIC2019, HAM10000, and ISIC2018 benchmark datasets for classification and segmentation tasks. The model achieved 97.56% classification accuracy with 0.991 AUC on ISIC2019 and 96.94% accuracy with 0.988 AUC on HAM10000. For lesion segmentation, a Dice coefficient of 94.96% was obtained on ISIC2018. Under adversarial perturbations, the framework preserved stable predictive performance with limited degradation. In addition, feature compression significantly reduced computational overhead while maintaining diagnostic precision. The results demonstrate that integrating robustness, calibration, and explainability into a unified architecture can improve the dependability of AI-assisted dermatological diagnosis.</jats:p>

title: Understanding Advances in Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Over the Past Ten Years: A Scoping Review
container-title: Cognitive Computation
a4c15179eec9d28fd289b67f425079358937b40d.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Computational Cognitive Neuroscience (CCN) is an interdisciplinary field that uses computational models to understand how the brain gives rise to cognition. Although the field has grown substantially over the past ten years, no review has systematically mapped the major advances achieved during this period. This review therefore aims to map advances in CCN over the past ten years by analyzing the most frequently used computational models, the cognitive domains investigated, and the computational tools employed, and by determining the predominant emphasis of the studies, whether theoretical, translational, or integrated. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the methodology proposed by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and reported following PRISMA-ScR. Searches were performed in PubMed, Embase and IEEE Xplore between 24 and 28 April 2025, and were complemented by a supplementary relevance-ranked Scopus search and by expert-informed identification of additional records. A total of 104 studies were included. Recent progress in CCN was found to be predominantly theoretical, with research focused on memory, learning, language and communication, and decision-making. Recurrent neural networks and Bayesian models emerged as the most widely adopted frameworks. Although CCN has advanced rapidly over the past ten years, the field continues to face critical challenges, notably concerning neurobiological plausibility, model integration, limited external generalizability, and a pressing need for more translational research. Beyond the reviewed corpus, the review discusses emerging AI paradigms, transformers, foundation models, large language models, and neuromorphic computing, as prospective directions informed by complementary literature.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Cognitive Decline and Consumption Changes Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults
container-title: Research on Aging
9ee1fcd57afe49de3f3bcc9a464ba98803669df6.abstract: <jats:p>Cognitive impairment is associated with financial burdens on individuals and their families, yet less is known about how families change consumption patterns around the onset of cognitive decline beyond out-of-pocket medical expenditures. Using data from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and the Consumption and Activities Mail Survey (CAMS) from 2002 to 2018, we examined changes in spending during the six years before and after the first onset of cognitive impairment no dementia (CIND) and dementia among community-dwelling older adults. We found that older adults with cognitive decline reduced total spending, as well as spending on food at home and away from home and on non-durables, before and after onset. Out-of-pocket medical expenses, transportation, and housing spending remained unchanged, but there is suggestive evidence of declines in leisure spending, gift-giving, and utility costs. Future research should explore the potential for material deprivation related to these consumption changes.</jats:p>

title: Beyond TAM: a mediated-moderated analysis of perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust as catalysts for AI adoption
container-title: Global Knowledge, Memory and Communication
6da4b5961b80fb182f0f7449a891d8ffaa5aa46f.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines customers’ adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Jordanian telecommunications sector by extending the technology acceptance model (TAM). Specifically, it aims to investigate the effects of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism on actual use of AI, while testing customer intention as a mediator and technology trust as a moderator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative approach was employed. Data were collected through self-administered questionnaires from customers of telecommunications companies in Jordan. Using stratified random sampling, 482 questionnaires were distributed, and 438 valid responses were analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling using SmartPLS 4 was applied to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, mediation effects and moderation effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that perceived ease of use and perceived anthropomorphism significantly and positively influence customers’ intention to adopt AI, whereas perceived usefulness has no significant effect. Customer intention significantly predicts actual AI use and mediates the relationships between perceived ease of use, perceived anthropomorphism and actual AI use. However, intention does not mediate the relationship between perceived usefulness and actual AI use. Technology trust significantly moderates the relationship between customer intention and actual AI use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Telecom providers should design AI-enabled services that are simple, intuitive, human-like and trustworthy. Managers should also communicate the tangible benefits of AI more clearly to strengthen customers’ usefulness perceptions and encourage sustained usage.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends TAM by integrating perceived anthropomorphism and technology trust into a mediated-moderated model of AI adoption in an underexplored Middle Eastern telecommunications context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Are you a positive or negative user of AI? Exploring the impacts of undergraduates' GenAI use
container-title: Journal of Research in Innovative Teaching & Learning
49ee98c7eeacb7dbccf5fcc9ceb17fefa88e08b7.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly becoming commonplace in many academic environments; however, studies examining not just whether students use these technologies but how their usage patterns shape learning outcomes and academic integrity remain understudied. This study begins to address this gap by exploring undergraduates' patterns of constructive or problematic use of AI and their relation to academic and ethical behaviors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This exploratory study used a cross-sectional design employing quantitative data collection methods. A correlation and multiple regression analysis were conducted with college students' (N = 110) self-reports of AI use, academic motivation and engagement, reliance on AI, and digital citizenship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Negative and positive AI use were correlated with AI Reliance. Negative AI use also predicted stronger AI reliance with weaker digital citizenship skills, unlike positive AI use. Notably, positive and negative AI use were strongly correlated, suggesting that use patterns are not uniform on an individual level and may vary by context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results suggest that students may shift between different AI patterns. Future researchers should aim to clarify the causal mechanisms and recruit a larger and more diverse sample to validate and expand upon our findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To our knowledge, this paper is a rare empirical study that explores the relationship between specific student academic outcomes and AI use in distinctive usage patterns: positive and negative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Mapping data privacy at the intersection of AI and the digital economy: a bibliometric review, taxonomy, and research agenda
container-title: Electronic Commerce Research
4771700294a9adc8d5aa2955311b1e6641f61402.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid integration of artificial intelligence and related emerging technologies has intensified data privacy challenges across the digital economy. Although scholarship has grown substantially, it remains fragmented across technical, legal, ethical, and sector-specific domains, limiting a clear view of the field’s structure and development. This study presents a bibliometric analysis and thematic mapping of 434 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026 in the Web of Science Core Collection. It identifies seven thematic clusters and finds that applied and privacy-preserving technical work dominates, while business strategy, trust, and public-sector governance remain underdeveloped. The study extends this mapping with a multi-dimensional privacy taxonomy and a TCCM (theory, context, characteristics, and methodology) synthesis, moving beyond the topic- and domain-specific scope of prior reviews to diagnose where the field is structurally weak. It argues that privacy remains under-theorized as an economic and behavioral phenomenon despite its centrality to digital commerce and sets out a research agenda of economically grounded questions derived from these gaps.</jats:p>

title: Integrating AI General Education with Digital Literacy Cultivation and Cognitive Construction in Industry-Specific Universities
container-title: Communications in Humanities Research
ed572e57c1cc41bc9396ae2882f5f643647c0276.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence has evolved into a general-purpose technology that permeates nearly every corner of knowledge production and social governance. This transformation is pushing college students' digital literacy far beyond the traditional "digitization" benchmark toward what this paper terms "intelligent-digital" literacy. For industry-specific universities—institutions committed to serving specific industries and cultivating application-oriented talents—the significance of AI general education is perhaps even greater than for other types of universities, because their graduates directly enter the industrial chain. Taking the practice of Moutai Institute as a concrete case, this paper elaborates on the internal logic, practical challenges, and feasible pathways for integrating AI general education into students' digital literacy cultivation and cognitive construction. The core argument of this paper is that such education should be anchored in industrial scenarios rather than abstract theory, and that cultivating compound talents equipped with digital literacy, industrial awareness, and social responsibility requires simultaneously grasping three main threads: technological empowerment, value guidance, and cognitive construction. On this basis, this paper proposes a trinity integration framework and offers actionable strategies from four dimensions: curriculum system, teaching model, faculty development, and evaluation mechanism. This paper aims to provide theoretical reference and practical insights for general education reform in industry-specific universities.</jats:p>

8cd514972f04965b968b2d5010a2ca45fd437b93.abstract: <jats:p>Мета дослідження – обґрунтувати дидактичний потенціал генеративних мовних моделей у фаховій іншомовній підготовці та розробити операціоналізовану систему ризиків, яка пов’язує кожну загрозу з конкретною компенсаторною методичною стратегією. Методологічну основу становить теоретико-аналітичний дизайн із двопрохідним змістовим аналізом джерельного корпусу, таксономічним згортанням виявлених положень, порівняльно-зіставним аналізом результатів із різних освітніх контекстів і моделюванням дидактичних рішень. Установлено, що специфіка фахової іншомовної підготовки визначається подвійною вимогою: мовною нормативністю та відповідністю професійно-дискурсивним конвенціям. За результатами першого проходу змістового аналізу виокремлено шість кластерів дидактичних афордансів: генерування фахового входу, формувальний зворотний зв’язок, симуляція професійної інтеракції, підтримка продуктивних умінь, розширення термінологічного репертуару та автоматизація дидактичного проєктування. Другий прохід дав чотирирівневу таксономію ризиків – когнітивно-навчальних, змістово-епістемічних, етико-академічних та інституційно-професійних. На цій основі побудовано матрицю «афорданс – домінантний ризик – компенсаторна стратегія», шестиступеневу шкалу когнітивного делегування D0–D5 та архітектуру оцінювання, що поєднує контрольовані завдання без доступу до генеративних систем, завдання з декларованим їх використанням і критико-верифікаційні завдання. Наукова новизна полягає в системному поєднанні дидактичних можливостей і ризиків у межах однієї моделі та в розширенні структури промпт-інженерної компетентності метакогнітивно-верифікаційним компонентом. Практичне значення результатів полягає у можливості використовувати запропоновану матрицю, шкалу D0–D5 і дескриптори верифікації під час проєктування завдань, оцінювання студентських робіт і формування локальної політики академічної доброчесності у закладах вищої освіти.</jats:p>

title: From disclosure to epistemic accountability: preserving meaningful human control across the AI-assisted research lifecycle
container-title: Frontiers in Research Metrics and Analytics
d5990fe9a3456ccb8623b79ac3aea44455cfc88d.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming embedded across the scientific research lifecycle, while prevailing governance remains centered on disclosure of tool use and the assignment of responsibility to human authors. We argue that disclosure is necessary but insufficient because it does not establish that researchers understood, verified, challenged, and authorized the AI-assisted processes that shaped scientific claims. We define this disconnect as the epistemic accountability gap and develop the Lifecycle Epistemic Accountability Framework (LEAF) as a testable theory of how meaningful human control can be preserved across AI-assisted knowledge production. Drawing on a structured integrative review and critical interpretive synthesis, LEAF links four human-control capacities—competence, contestability, intervention authority, and traceable ownership—supported by evaluability by design, to five lifecycle checkpoints spanning evidence identification, study design and ethics, data processing and analysis, interpretation, and reporting or knowledge translation. The framework proposes that accountability improves when oversight is exercised prospectively at epistemically consequential decision points, documented through an audit trail, and calibrated to epistemic materiality: the extent to which AI assistance can alter the validity, interpretation, or consequences of a scientific claim. Six propositions specify testable relationships among disclosure, epistemic materiality, meaningful human control, lifecycle checkpoints, auditability, and defensibility of scientific claims. LEAF therefore shifts AI research governance from retrospective visibility to prospective, risk-proportionate control. We identify boundary conditions, implementation pathways, and an empirical research agenda for testing the framework across disciplines and resource settings. LEAF's distinctive explanatory mechanism is conditional: epistemic materiality escalates oversight, evaluability enables four human capacities, lifecycle checkpoints interrupt error propagation, and retained audit evidence makes consequential decisions answerable.</jats:p>

title: The Care Plan Compiler as an Agentic AI Framework for Translating Clinical Recommendations into Feasible Patient-Centered Care
container-title: Universal Library of Innovative Research and Studies
737fc0c4fb28af6247d52e56f6b2080ca39e7c71.abstract: <jats:p>A clinical recommendation becomes care after someone confirms coverage, finds a facility that provides the service, arranges language support and transportation, books an appointment, and verifies that the visit took place. When no organization owns this work, it falls to the patient, and a missed service is recorded as nonadherence, even when the failure occurred within the health system. The review examines five adjacent fields, each addressing part of this problem, and develops the Care Plan Compiler, an agentic AI framework that treats the clinician-approved recommendation as a protected source specification and compiles it into a graph of tasks with named owners. A deterministic readiness checker releases a task once all prerequisites hold and classifies any unknown coverage, capacity, or accessibility as unresolved. Feasible plans are compared across a multidimensional burden vector, and a change in context triggers recompilation of the dependent tasks. A synthetic case of diabetic retinal screening illustrates the compilation, and a four-stage evaluation program sets a screening completed within the approved window and verified within 90 days of referral approval as its primary endpoint. The framework moves responsibility for missed care to the system layer where the failure occurs.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence use, entrepreneurial mindset, and perceived work-based learning readiness in higher education
container-title: Higher Education, Skills and Work-Based Learning
dc06affb0475fcac02293e0fa8f0ff94c2a911cf.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) use in learning, students' entrepreneurial mindset, and perceived work-based learning readiness in higher education. It investigates whether AI use in learning is associated with entrepreneurial mindset and perceived work-based learning readiness, and whether entrepreneurial mindset is associated with perceived work-based learning readiness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted with 300 undergraduate students from business and entrepreneurship-related programmes in Indonesian higher education institutions. The respondents had prior experience using AI tools for learning purposes. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling to assess the measurement model and structural relationships among the constructs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate positive associations between AI use in learning, entrepreneurial mindset, and perceived work-based learning readiness. AI use in learning is positively associated with entrepreneurial mindset and perceived work-based learning readiness, while entrepreneurial mindset is also positively associated with perceived work-based learning readiness. These findings should be interpreted as evidence of self-reported perceptions rather than actual workplace performance or behavioural capability development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study has several limitations. First, the use of cross-sectional self-reported survey data limits causal interpretation and may be affected by common method bias or social desirability. Second, the study measures perceived work-based learning readiness rather than actual workplace performance, internship outcomes, or employer-rated competence. Third, the sample is limited to students in business and entrepreneurship-related programmes, which may restrict generalisability. Future research should use longitudinal, mixed-method, or multi-source designs involving students, educators, employers, and workplace supervisors to examine how AI-assisted entrepreneurial learning influences actual work-based learning capability and graduate employability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that higher education institutions should integrate AI-assisted learning into entrepreneurship curricula in a responsible and pedagogically guided manner. Educators can use AI tools to support idea generation, market analysis, problem-solving, project development, and internship preparation. However, AI use should be accompanied by clear ethical guidelines, AI literacy training, and activities that strengthen independent judgement, creativity, and critical thinking. Institutions should also connect AI-supported entrepreneurial learning with work-based learning activities, such as industry projects, capstone projects, employability training, and workplace simulations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study highlights the social importance of preparing students to engage with AI responsibly in entrepreneurial and work-based learning contexts. Responsible AI-supported learning may help students develop digital confidence, entrepreneurial awareness, and readiness for technology-driven workplaces. However, the findings also suggest the need to prevent overdependence on AI and ensure that students continue to develop creativity, ethical judgement, and independent problem-solving. By promoting responsible AI literacy, higher education institutions can support more inclusive, adaptive, and future-oriented graduate preparation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes by positioning entrepreneurial mindset as an important pedagogical and psychological construct in understanding how AI-assisted learning relates to students' perceived readiness for work-based learning. The study extends discussions on AI in higher education by connecting AI-assisted learning with entrepreneurship education and work-based learning preparation, while acknowledging the limitations of perceptual and cross-sectional evidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Indoor Air Quality Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
47b9e68bf232f52679454c3d2fe3aaf90d5ca23a.abstract: <jats:p>To investigate variations in indoor NO₂ concentrations under a subtropical climate, their relationships with indoor and outdoor environment parameters, and ways to improve prediction accuracy, this study monitored indoor and outdoor air quality in a teaching building from May 18 to May 31, 2025. Measurements included NO₂, PM2.5, PM10, O₃, temperature, and relative humidity. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated, and variables with |r| ≥ 0.3 were selected as model inputs. Multiple linear regression (MLR) and artificial neural network (ANN) models were developed and evaluated using R² and RMSE. Based on validation results, the preferred ANN used two hidden layers, with 150 and 75 neurons, and ReLU activation. On the test set, MLR achieved an R² of 0.5975 and an RMSE of 4.8597, whereas ANN achieved an R² of 0.8528 and an RMSE of 2.9389. Compared with MLR, ANN increased R² by approximately 25.53 percentage points and reduced RMSE by approximately 39.52%. ANN also reduced the underestimation observed at high concentrations and improved accuracy across concentration ranges. These findings show that indoor NO₂ depends on multiple indoor and outdoor factors and that ANN captures their complex relationships more effectively than MLR. The results support ANN-based indoor NO₂ prediction under subtropical conditions and may inform air-quality monitoring and forecasting in similar buildings. However, the study was limited by its short monitoring period, incomplete coverage of relevant factors, and limited neural-network optimization. Future studies should address these limitations.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Risk Early Warning for the NEV Power Battery Supply Chain—Framework Development and Case Analysis Based on Public Information
container-title: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
4341daa2a4629a65e7b5d1b2444219817a9c2a8e.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of new energy vehicles has made power battery supply chains strategically important but increasingly exposed to mineral-price volatility, supplier disruption, quality failures, demand changes, logistics delays, and policy uncertainty. This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven early-warning framework through literature review, indicator design, public-case analysis, and scenario reasoning. The framework links five layers: data, indicators, models, warning levels, and management decisions. It organizes signals across upstream supply, internal operations, downstream demand, the external environment, and circular supply. Public disclosures from Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) illustrate how material exposure, supplier performance, customer demand, and recycling capacity can enter the framework. Four warning levels connect model outputs with differentiated procurement, inventory, production, logistics, and supplier responses. The study does not claim unverified prediction accuracy because firm-level time-series data are unavailable. It instead specifies the data and governance needed for empirical validation. The findings show that AI adds value when heterogeneous signals are converted into interpretable risk assessments and timely, accountable actions.</jats:p>

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in High School Science Education: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, Pedagogical Strategies, and Critical Thinking Development
container-title: Journal of Education and Learning Reviews
7ae48f59180fb1d3c9a8abac185c2aa46794f0d3.abstract:
<jats:p>Background and Aim: Evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in secondary science education remains limited. This systematic review examined students’ conceptual understanding and engagement, teachers’ pedagogical strategies and challenges, and students’ critical thinking and scientific inquiry.
Materials and Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, ERIC, Scopus, and Lens.org were searched for peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026. Two authors independently screened 187 unique records (Cohen’s κ = .78), identifying 20 eligible studies. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Framework synthesis integrated findings, informed by Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK).
Results: Seven studies assessed AI capabilities rather than classroom implementation. Only two compared learning outcomes across conditions; none employed a randomized controlled design. Student perceptions and engagement were generally positive, whereas learning outcomes were mixed. A chatbot supporting self-regulated learning outperformed a rule-based chatbot, but ChatGPT-4o yielded smaller gains than peer collaboration. Teachers reported concerns regarding content accuracy, assessment reliability, and instructional readiness. Generative AI matched or exceeded student performance on structured examinations but demonstrated lower grading reliability than human assessors. Evidence concerning critical thinking was particularly limited. Richer reasoning was reported with dialogue-oriented tools or teacher guidance, whereas answer-seeking use of general-purpose tools was associated with weaker reasoning.
Conclusion: Pedagogical structuring was recurrently associated with productive AI use, although causal inference remains limited. A provisional model warrants empirical testing. Priorities include structured tasks, science-specific teacher development, human assessment oversight, explicit AI literacy instruction, school governance, and controlled comparisons of structured and unstructured use across secondary science classrooms.</jats:p>

title: Typicality biases in interpreting unmarked sentences: an artificial language learning experiment on differential argument marking
container-title: Frontiers in Language Sciences
7ca7d7ce71c647ea6fda7be902e5db1f938a3482.abstract: <jats:p>Many languages exhibit differential argument marking (DAM), in which nouns are marked for their grammatical role only in certain contexts. DAM manifests as differential object marking (DOM) and differential subject marking (DSM), both of which are conditioned by factors such as animacy and hypothesized to arise via ambiguity avoidance and tendencies to mark atypical situations. While previous studies have primarily focused on production, this study employs artificial language learning to investigate comprehension of ambiguous (unmarked) sentences in both DOM and DSM, examining whether learners rely on typicality biases for grammatical role assignment, and whether the type of marking they have learned affects their interpretation. Results indicate a strong givenness effect and a potential smaller animacy effect, with no significant differences between DOM and DSM conditions. These findings suggest that typicality biases play a key role in shaping DAM systems—particularly information structure—and that their emergence might be best understood as a communicative phenomenon shaped by listener expectations.</jats:p>

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
f171216399a007e7c399c672df322f23f7504b96.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title: Bayesian Treed Regressions for Estimating Heterogeneous Trajectories of Test Scores in Large-scale Educational Assessments
ad1a679cf6269a4b781711662e48705559a9b3c7.abstract: In large-scale educational assessment, students’ academic outcomes can evolve over time, due to various effect modifiers. For instance, parents’ education level, a common modifier, has been found to have time-varying effects on children’s test scores, leading to heterogeneous academic trajectories. To model these varying trajectories, parametric models like hierarchical linear models (HLMs) are commonly deployed. While these highly parametric methods are interpretable, their predictive capacities have not been rigorously compared to those of more flexible nonparametric approaches. We present the results of systematic simulation studies and empirical analyses comparing traditional parametric models to Bayesian nonparametric models based on Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART). Our findings indicate that BART-based alternatives can (1) achieve comparable out-of-sample prediction as HLMs, after accounting for individual variability over time; (2) provide a reasonable amount of interpretability and uncertainty quantification; and (3) do not incur much more computational burden. This work contributes to the existing social science literature by demonstrating that Bayesian treed regression methods are viable and feasible alternatives to conventional HLMs for predicting heterogeneous trajectories across time.

title: Clinical utility of real-time comprehensive molecular testing in large B-cell lymphoma
container-title: Blood Advances
edd3547d88b874383d838cca20326a2ee1020f1e.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Because of the rapidly evolving landscape of targeted therapies, there is an unmet need for comprehensive molecular profiling to guide treatment decisions for patients with large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). Therefore, we designed a pilot study to assess the feasibility and turnaround time (TAT) of a comprehensive whole-exome sequencing (WES) and transcriptome sequencing (RNA-sequencing [RNA-seq]) assay in patients with LBCL. Patients aged ≥18 years with LBCL were eligible. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues obtained at diagnosis or recurrence underwent WES, RNA-seq, and copy-number analysis with concomitant germ line DNA sequencing. Genomic and transcriptomic data were profiled to define various LBCL signatures, such as cell-of-origin (COO), dark zone signature (DZsig), LymphGen, and lymphoma microenvironment (LME) classification. Among 100 patients enrolled, samples from 71 patients (48 with newly diagnosed and 23 with relapsed/refractory disease) passed pathology quality control and underwent WES and RNA-seq analysis and reporting. The median TAT was 8 days for individual patient reports (range, 6-22 days), with 73% of reports delivered ≤10 days. Applying molecular risk classification, the high-risk event-free survival within 24 months signature was associated with DZsig and LME, but not with COO or LymphGen, indicating the complex heterogeneity of the disease. We demonstrated the clinical utility and acceptable TAT of a comprehensive WES and RNA-seq assay for LBCL managed in routine clinical practice. These findings support the real-world feasibility of using integrated WES and RNA-seq to define molecular subgroups, guide clinical decision-making at the time of initiation of a new line of therapy, and enable biology-based, subtype-driven clinical trials. This study was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05464823.</jats:p>
