title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
607e01bc517c5399388e06837788a54fe973b640.abstract:
<jats:p>The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories  (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution.
We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE).
We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+
The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range.
A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.</jats:p>

title: A neural-network model for finding correlations in astrochemical space
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
421dace86fb494a31f092362923a0cee1c76d657.abstract: <jats:p>The detection of new interstellar molecules is a central objective of astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field over the past decade has been the dramatic increase in both the number and diversity of detected species. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing models, we developed a machine-learning pipeline, in line with recent approaches reported in the literature, to establish relationships between molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in the prototypical dark cloud TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. In this work, these representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17 and 0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29 and 0.59, all expressed in logarithmic units of the column density, together with coefficients of determination of 0.88 and 0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets, respectively. The latent vectors learned by the model represent a rich mathematical object that captures not only the underlying chemical relations but also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory allowed us to identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. Furthermore, by training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond the accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.</jats:p>

title: Towards a new model of the compact triple system łambda Tauri I. Improved periods and preliminary elements of the triple system
container-title: Astronomy & Astrophysics
43cd7848f6594d5caa0166684f329b55f4e7bebb.abstract: <jats:p>We analysed our new radial velocity measurements and photometric observations (covering a time interval of 46838 days and 39100 days, respectively) as well as those from previous studies to derive accurate ephemerides for both orbits of the compact triple system łae. In the case of the inner eclipsing subsystem, we obtained a linear ephemeris of T_ ̊m min.I = ̊m HJD ,2440998.86069(35)+3 = E, improving the accuracy of the previous solutions by more than an order of magnitude. This allowed us to reproduce well all available light curve minima, including the first one recorded in 1844. Furthermore, the period of the outer subsystem, determined from radial velocity analysis, appears to be constant over the interval of available observations, with the corresponding linear ephemeris being T_ ̊m periast. ̊m HJD ,2456822.5(3.6)+33 E,. Assuming near coplanarity of the inner and outer orbits, we estimated the preliminary physical properties of the whole system. We found that the secondary of the inner subsystem is filling or nearly filling its Roche lobe. We used the long-term stability of the eclipsing subsystem period to place a strong upper limit on the rate of the proposed episodic mass transfer to its primary component. Our results constitute a preparatory step for a follow-up study that will also include an analysis of a rich collection of optical spectro-interferometric observations and use a full-fledged numerical model to describe the evolution of the orbital architecture of the system. Particular attention will be focused on determining the inner orbit forced eccentricity and understanding the absence of the apsidal advance of the outer orbit in our present solution.</jats:p>

title: A five-field mixed formulation for the fully dynamic Biot-Brinkman model
container-title: ESAIM: Mathematical Modelling and Numerical Analysis
daf3b1b47b687feb865f05abcf7a6127a66b4d05.abstract: <jats:p>We propose and analyze a mixed formulation for the fully dynamic Biot--Brinkman system, which models the coupled effects of internal viscous diffusion and deformation of the porous skeleton. The classical formulation is expressed in terms of displacement, fluid velocity, and pore pressure. In this work, we reformulate the problem in terms of the fluid velocity, pore pressure, and poroelastic stress tensor, together with two additional variables: the structural velocity and the rotation rate. In particular, we eliminate the solid displacement and the rotation tensor from the set of primary variables. Both quantities are subsequently recovered by a simple post-processing step. This yields a five-field mixed formulation. We establish existence and uniqueness of a weak solution and derive stability bounds based on the Babu\v{s}ka--Brezzi theory for perturbed saddle-point problems, as well as on the theoretical framework developed by Showalter for semilinear degenerate evolution equations. We then develop a semidiscrete continuous-in-time approximation based on stable mixed finite elements. Moreover, employing a backward Euler time discretization, we introduce a fully discrete finite element scheme. We prove that both schemes are well-posed, derive stability bounds, and establish the corresponding error estimates. Finally, we numerically verify the theoretical convergence rates and perform classical benchmark tests to illustrate the robustness and versatility of the method across different domains and parameter regimes.</jats:p>

title: CONCEPTUALIZING THE MULTIMODAL APPROACH IN FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING METHODOLOGY
container-title: Еволюція наукового знання: сучасні парадигми, методи та концептуальні засади досліджень: збірник наукових праць з матеріалами I Міжнародної наукової конференції (м. Чернігів, Україна; 10 листопада 2026)
d6aad0d99fe5718108ef56eab10bfeac152fb7da.abstract: <jats:p>The dynamic shift in the contemporary communication landscape underscores that alphabetic text alone no longer dominates meaning-making in foreign language education. Rooted in the foundational theoretical ideas of the New London Group, multimodality reflects how modern interaction relies on the interplay of two or more communication modes within a single text. When considering foreign language teaching methodology, a mode must be conceptualized as an organized set of semiotic resources-specifically en-compassing linguistic, visual, aural, gestural, and spatial dimensions. Recognizing how these distinct modes operate allows educators to move beyond traditional monomodal boundaries and design interactive learning environ-ments that reflect real-world language use. This changing nature of digital communication necessarily demands a broader understanding of literacy itself. Traditional definitions centered strictly on reading and writing printed words prove insufficient for navigating today’s textual world.</jats:p>

title: Beyond Model-Centric Object Detection: Mitigating Scale Bias Through Object-Size-Aware Dataset Partitioning
container-title: Iraqi Journal for Computers and Informatics
a2bffc37ee08bd944c965234a2e662b5685fd12c.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable object-detection evaluation is essential because reported performance depends not only on detector architecture but also on whether training, validation, and testing subsets adequately represent the object-scale characteristics of the data. However, conventional dataset partitioning often ignores object-size distribution, which can introduce scale bias and produce unstable or misleading estimates of model generalization. This study investigates whether object-size-aware dataset partitioning can improve the representativeness and reliability of detector evaluation without modifying the detector architecture. Two license-plate datasets were examined under four partitioning scenarios: natural unsorted splitting, descending size-ordered splitting, stratified size-descending splitting, and size-aware stratified sampling using strict quantized and hybrid semi-stratified variants. After partitioning, subset representativeness was assessed using Kullback-Leibler divergence and normalized Earth Mover’s Distance, while the nano variant of You Only Look Once version 11 was used as a fixed detector and trained under identical conditions at 640 × 640 resolution for 100 epochs. Performance was evaluated primarily using mean average precision over intersection-over-union thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, supported by mean average precision at 0.50, precision, recall, and F1-score. Size-ordered splitting reduced the primary metric to 0.124 in Dataset 1 and as low as 0.005 in Dataset 2, whereas size-aware stratification recovered competitive values of 0.523 and 0.477, respectively. These findings indicate that dataset partitioning is a consequential data-level design factor and can support more dependable benchmarking for automated license-plate recognition, intelligent transportation, traffic monitoring, and surveillance applications.</jats:p>

title: The challenge of AI dependence: exploring its impact on cognitive autonomy and elaboration in creative performance

5d10468ae5a26c2d8ac92ce1ad78fb5842569e0a.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As artificial intelligence advances and its application scenarios continue to expand, human–artificial intelligence interaction grows increasingly close. While artificial intelligence brings convenience, it also raises concerns that it may weaken users' cognitive autonomy. To investigate this issue. This study aims to explore the composition of AI dependence and its impact on cognitive autonomy and specific aspects of creative performance.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study draws on cognitive evaluation theory and the elaboration likelihood model to construct a dual-pathway model with instrumental dependence and affective dependence as core variables. The model explains the formation mechanisms of the two types of artificial intelligence dependence and their differential effects on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily examines their potential role in the elaboration dimension of creative performance. A two-stage mixed-method design was employed to test the model.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Study 1 found that perceived trust mainly had a positive effect on instrumental dependence. Different dimensions of interactivity differentially affected affective dependence and cognitive autonomy. Mediation analysis further confirmed the core mediating role of Dependence. Study 2, a small-sample exploratory experiment, re-tested selected hypotheses and found a possible negative effect of instrumental dependence on the elaboration dimension of creative performance.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The main theoretical contribution of this study lies in revealing the dual-pathway formation mechanisms of artificial intelligence dependence and the reshaping effects of different types of dependence on cognitive autonomy. It also preliminarily explores the potential effects of dependence on elaboration performance.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>

title: Crosslingual Writing in Language Teaching
9e6426d45d69c974bab1778b2c7e3cd8b90fece6.abstract: <jats:p>Writers who read, think, and write across languages need tailored support to navigate the complexities of crosslingual writing. Despite interest in pedagogical translanguaging and the rehabilitation of translation in language teaching, crosslingual writing remains underexplored as it stands at the margins of established disciplinary domains such as additional language instruction, writing pedagogy, and translator education. This Element argues that crosslingual writing is not only an essential skill for plurilingual communication, but also a powerful tool for language and writing development and deeper learning. Situating crosslingual writing within the trans/plurilingual turn and combining theoretical, empirical, and pedagogical insights from language (in) education, writing instruction, and translation studies, this Element identifies tools, strategies, and digital literacies for AI-powered crosslingual writing. It further explores how crosslingual writing can be systematically integrated into language curricula, offering practical strategies for pedagogical task design, scaffolding activities, and crosslingual writing assessment.</jats:p>

title: Pedagogic Tasks for The Language Classroom
fe4a22b649082c599359c568471c55f598d8057c.abstract: <jats:p>The purpose of this Element is to bridge research and classroom practice by presenting clear actionable strategies for how to design and implement pedagogic tasks from a task-based language teaching (TBLT) perspective. The Element is intended to benefit practitioners in English as a second language/foreign language (ESL, EFL) and world language classrooms as well as researchers who wish to use tasks or who wish to gain a better grasp of the interface between research and practice. We focus specifically on pedagogic tasks, which are approximations of real-world tasks that teachers can readily implement in their language classrooms. The Element is organized around a set of seven key principles that are supported by theoretical and empirical research in the field of SLA and illustrated through examples. Content covers fundamental concepts such as common task outcomes and task types, communicative gaps, task difficulty, scaffolding, focus on form, feedback, task engagement, and assessment.</jats:p>

title: BinauralLM: spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation with large language model
container-title: Journal on Audio, Speech, and Music Processing
19e57fa93b910b6cf942cda62ef61b5a1dc05797.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Binaural audio is a practical spatial audio format for headphone playback and is widely used in immersive media such as games, VR/AR, and interactive multimedia. Currently, binaural audio is still largely obtained either by specialized recordings or by spatializing pre-recorded monaural signals, which limits flexibility for controllable content creation. While recent text-to-audio models can generate the required audio, most of them target monaural output or unconstrained stereo. They provide limited control over spatial attributes such as direction and motion. To address these challenges, we propose BinauralLM, a spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation framework with large language model (LLM). BinauralLM adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, we use a Qwen2.5 LLM to autoregressively generate coarse binaural token sequences conditioned on text and spatial prompts. To effectively couple semantic content with spatial cues, we introduce a spatial prompt encoder and an attention fusion module to produce a unified conditioning representation for binaural token generation. Second, we employ a flow matching model that takes the coarse binaural tokens as conditions and reconstructs high-quality binaural waveforms in the continuous domain. Experimental results on the BEWO-1M dataset demonstrate that BinauralLM achieves superior performance on standard text-to-audio metrics and binaural spatial metrics, and achieves higher MOS scores in perceptual evaluation, especially on spatialization quality. These results indicate that our proposed method offers an effective route to controllable and high-quality text-to-binaural audio generation.</jats:p>

title: Innateness is (still) an orienting principle for language development
d94b3856e42e5d9a204d1345c69ca324c6794baf.abstract: How humans come to acquire language has been a persistent object of philosophical and scientific inquiry, in part because it bears on fundamental questions about the nature of human cognition.Classically, this field of inquiry has centered innateness as a critical component of language acquisition, traditionally characterizing innate capability in terms of richly specified, biologically endowed linguistic structure, such as Universal Grammar. Contemporary theories have evolved considerably from these earlier formulations and now present several differing candidates for innateness in language. Throughout this evolution, though, questions of innateness have remained central to theories of language acquisition, even as the nature of those questions has shifted in response to new sources of evidence. In this Perspective, we consider evidence from three complementary sources of evidence—linguistic diversity, human social interaction, and language models (LMs)—that together inform the question of what children must bring to the task of language learning. We conclude by identifying desiderata for theories of language acquisition that seek to specify the nature, scope, and explanatory role of innate contributions to language development.

title: Bayesian Treed Regressions for Estimating Heterogeneous Trajectories of Test Scores in Large-scale Educational Assessments
eff1fc6350d87a48be91231392d68074af4dbfa4.abstract: In large-scale educational assessment, students’ academic outcomes can evolve over time, due to various effect modifiers. For instance, parents’ education level, a common modifier, has been found to have time-varying effects on children’s test scores, leading to heterogeneous academic trajectories. To model these varying trajectories, parametric models like hierarchical linear models (HLMs) are commonly deployed. While these highly parametric methods are interpretable, their predictive capacities have not been rigorously compared to those of more flexible nonparametric approaches. We present the results of systematic simulation studies and empirical analyses comparing traditional parametric models to Bayesian nonparametric models based on Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART). Our findings indicate that BART-based alternatives can (1) achieve comparable out-of-sample prediction as HLMs, after accounting for individual variability over time; (2) provide a reasonable amount of interpretability and uncertainty quantification; and (3) do not incur much more computational burden. This work contributes to the existing social science literature by demonstrating that Bayesian treed regression methods are viable and feasible alternatives to conventional HLMs for predicting heterogeneous trajectories across time.

title: Peers link conflict-resolution reputation to social and cognitive capacities rather than the capacity to impose costs among Ethiopian forager-horticulturalists
b9ccdb38f6597ed3e62466f34e81e1c68972ba14.abstract: Leadership emergence in socially egalitarian contexts depends on the qualities of individuals and on how others perceive their capacity to use them. Multi-Capital Leadership theory proposes that leaders deploy material, social, somatic, and neural capital to solve problems of group living by providing benefits to group members or imposing costs. Conflict resolution is one important leadership domain. We reanalyse peer rankings of 60 adults in a relatively egalitarian community of Chabu forager-horticulturalists in southwest Ethiopia. Seven peer-raters ranked participants on twelve traits identified as relevant to leadership in contemporary evolutionary theories. A previous analysis averaged rankings before modelling, obscuring differences among raters and treating positions within an ordering as continuous measurements. Here, we fitted a multivariate Plackett–Luce model directly to the individual rankings. This accounts for dependence within rankings and incorporates uncertainty into estimates. It also allows us to estimate consensus orderings and systematic variation associated with rater sex. Male and female peer-raters produced broadly similar orderings, including for conflict resolution. This could reflect actual covariation in participants’ qualities, a shared evaluative schema, or both. Peer-ranked proxies for material, social, and neural capital covaried closely and did not form clearly separable perceptual domains. The clearest descriptive contrast was between benefit-related attributes, including conflict resolution, sound decision-making, and prosociality, and cost-related attributes, including being feared and fighting. Conflict-resolution reputation was most closely associated with decision-making, kin support, respect, and intelligence, and showed no clear positive association with fighting. In these rankings, a reputation for conflict resolution was more clearly distinguished from aggression and coercion than were measures capturing the three capital domains represented in the instrument.

title: Beyond Chemical Fingerprinting: Raman Photonics, Molecular Spectroscopy and  Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Palm Oil Authentication, Quality Assessment and  Transferable Optical Sensing
container-title: Journal of Advanced Physics and Interdisciplinary Science
84b8f03b843f3011a32eba7eff1136cea1cf4e7f.abstract: <jats:p>Authenticity verification and quality control in palm oil increasingly require rapid, defensible measurements across heterogeneous supply chains. This critical qualitative literature review examines the molecular physics, analytical performance, and interpretability challenges associated with Raman photonics and complementary optical spectroscopies. Drawing on journal evidence published between 2020 and 2026, it distinguishes chemically grounded measurement from statistical identification that may depend on correlated pigments, processing conditions, or instrument characteristics. Recent handheld Raman studies demonstrate geographical discrimination of West African palm oils, while machine learning-assisted Raman analysis has reported promising prediction of peroxide, iodine, and acid values. However, high within-study accuracy does not establish causal provenance markers, robustness across refining states, or transferability to new instruments and regions. The review compares Raman, Fourier transform infrared, near-infrared, fluorescence, and multimodal approaches; critically evaluates spectral preprocessing, variable selection, explainable AI, calibration transfer, and uncertainty management; and proposes an evidence-gated framework for deployment. Key recommendations include chemically verified band assignments, hierarchical out-of-domain validation, metrological controls, prediction intervals, standardized acquisition metadata, and reference-laboratory confirmation of consequential decisions. The resulting framework positions explainable spectroscopy as a powerful screening and process-monitoring capability while maintaining clear boundaries between compositional inference, product authentication, geographic attribution, and certified sustainability traceability.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence Assistance with CRISPR to Optimize Drug Development
container-title: Theoretical and Natural Science
d3a234a40b3f1788d998eef39dd6112dabcf3dea.abstract: <jats:p>Drug development remains a costly and time-consuming process since identifying therapeutic targets that are both biologically relevant and clinically effective remains challenging. New technologies including bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, CRISPR screens and AI are enabling new target discovery opportunities, but there are still a number of challenges in bringing the heterogeneous data sets together. This paper describes how AI-assisted integration of these three technologies can improve drug development. This paper explains in detail how Bulk RNA sequencing can detect differentially expressed genes, how Single-cell RNA sequencing can uncover cell-specific expression patterns, how CRISPR screening can identify dependencies of genes in disease-related phenotypes, and how AI models can recognize complex molecular patterns and prioritize targets for therapeutic intervention using these complementary datasets. With AI support and current technologies, researchers could decrease false-positive target identification and enhance drug sensitivity forecasting. This paper suggest a way to improve the precision-drug-discovery strategies. But there are still issues with data heterogeneity and with model interpretability. To address the remaining challenges, interpretable AI models that combine multi-omics, functional genomic, and patient-derived data should be developed in the future.</jats:p>
